reviews.comment:
If you're used to writing essays last minute, this class will be pretty painful, but nonetheless Professor Falek was clearly caring and devoted. 

Grading criteria is pretty clear, she gives many opportunities for feedback before final deadlines, and she helps you structure your time through "progressions" (phases) of each essay unit.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This professor is very kind and super accessible. She will help with whatever she possibly can. However, while the papers are long, you can choose the topic (given a wide selection). Also, there is a lot of homework but you can use the homework when crafting the essay. Her tips on writing are great as well.

Alexandra Falek is honestly one of the kindest and most knowledgeable Writing The Essay professors at this school (especially if you are a Humanities major). Her classwork can get overwhelming, but it is rewarding since these assignments help build the foundations for your essay. Highly recommend her if you actually want to become a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Falek assigns a LOT of little assignments in between the three essays you work on through the semester, but once you get to drafting, you realize that because of the assignments, you already have almost all the paper written. SO kind and really cares about your writing development! If you actually want to learn something, take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class has honestly made me a better and more confident writer. Professor Falek is extremely accessible, truly cares about her students, and offers tons of feedback. It's not an easy class, but it's definitely doable, and you'll be really happy with results in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Falek made my first semsester. When I struggled with deadlines, she was incredibly accommodating, and gave me all the flexibility I needed. She replies to emails quickly and is always willing to make time to meet. This is not to say that the class was easy. But as long as you do the work (even if it's not incredible) you'll do great.

It was very hard to keep up with the progressions (ungraded homework assignments that build your essays), but the fact that this class kicked my behind and called me stupid in five languages is exactly what made me not just a better writer but a better person. My habits changed so much. Prof Falek is so compassionate and kind, highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: if you actually want to improve ur writing and LEARN in this mandatory writing the essay course, I def suggest you take hers. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Always prepared for classes. She teaches the material well, and it is always interesting. Class discussions, even online, were fun and I was even able to get to know other students. It was without a doubt, the most writing I have ever done in anyclass, she requires massive amounts of drafts and writing, but she is always accommodating about it.

She is extremely accommodating and kind. If you ever needed help, she would always find the time to read an essay or talk about the assignments. She was great at stimulating meaningful class discussion and made class very enjoyable and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Probably the best writing teacher or professor I've ever had, but there was definitely a lot of work. She made writing the essay as good of an experience as possible, and she really improved my writing habits and style throughout the semester.

Take any chance you can to take a class with her. Lots of people complain about writing the essay but she makes it so enjoyable. There is homework everyday but the class is set up in a progressive style where you keep adding towards your draft, so the work you put into the homework always pays off. Probably one of the best classes I took this year.

You might hate the process, but you'll love the result. There's hw for WTE of about two pages of writing every two days. It's not fun. But you constantly get feedback so by the time you submit your final draft there shouldn't be any surprises. You wont find another WTE professor who cares more. She constantly checks in and makes sure everyone is ok
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Falek is the best professor I have ever had. She is caring and knows what she is talking about. I really appreciate how organized she is and how she really guided us through the process of writing a strong essay for WTE. Her teaching and questions really get you to become a better + a more aware writer. I could not recommend her enough!

BEST WTE PROFESSOR. TAKE HER. She does a really good job at a rather tedious core class. always gives a bunch of feedback and really helps you develop the essays. attendance is mandatory, she does assign a lot of homework but they are due when the essays are & are really only counted for effort. Just take her.

Amazing Professor. Made writing the essay one of my favorite classes I've taken at NYU. Very caring and helpful, gives great feedback. Gave us very interesting texts to base our essays on. Encouraged independent thinking and different styles of writing. Definitely take writing the essay with her.

Professor Falek is an amazing professor, probably one of the best for WTE. She is not a hard grader at all--as long as you show improvement in your essays and take advantage of the skills she talks about in class, you'll do good on your essays. Alexandra is a wonderful professor. She really cares about the students and wants to see us succeed. Taking her class made me grow as a writer.
Good professor, sucky class. It is writing the essay, though, so you can't expect much better. She does assign a lot of homework, though.

Assignments were weekly and were moderately difficult, but never took > 2.5 hrs. Amanda was accessible and TAs were helpful. Fun and easy A!!

Lecture days would get participation through PollEV, but no other form of attendance. Assignments could be challenging but the lecture slides helped.

Prof. Amanda is very accessible outside class and replies to student emails quickly, even on weekends. She is kind and patient and always answers questions after class. The course has one coding assignment and quiz each week, which is manageable, though the homework can be challenging and the final exam is very difficult (but it is curved).

Amanda is such a sweet professor! The assignments can be tedious for the course, but I believe they are standardized between all the sections, so that is not a reflection of her. You can always reach out for help from her or a TA. If you do practice problems and study in advance for the midterm and final, you will be fine.

Very chill professor. Lectures are not explicitly mandatory but she does surveys to make sure you participate. The lectures where she helps with that week's assignment is not mandatory. The assignments take a bit long to complete (1-2 hours) but is more on the tedious side than difficult. Go to practice sessions for midterm / final.

Strange (in a bad way) - smiling and chuckling when students are struggling on exam, giving hw problems that are unnecessarily hard. Messed up a problem on our midterm, typo made the problem impossible, took majority of most people's time. Examples in class DO NOT cover the hw or test problems. Be ready to self-teach.

Horrendous homeworks, quizzes, and tests. Made an error on the second exam and caused everyone to waste a ton of time. I swear he doesn't proof his homeworks and tests or even take them before he releases them. Some homework problems are made to be absurdly long for absolutely no reason but for random algebra irrelevant to the topic. Don't take.

reviews.comment: First rating ever. Was compelled to rate because this is the worst teacher I have ever had. Have taken calc 3, ODE, data analysis, discrete, never struggled until this. Lectures and gives very few examples. Examples do not cover what is on the tests or the homework. Questions are so obscure that you can't even find them on the internet.

I had Sanfrat for discrete math (&took Linear Algebra with another prof) & Ithe ratings on here miss the point.
Discrete Math &Linear Alg ARE HARD COURSES with all profs. 

Professor Sanfratello was very accesssible during in person & online office hours and his lectures overall were clear. The exams and homework were hard but standard for Courant.

He is underrated. He's not that good but definitely not as horrible as some reviews said. Quizzes are hard. Drops lowest 2 quizzes and 1 HW. Exam 1 is easy while Exam 2 are a bit harder (but he took one question off and gave everyone 4 extra pts). He did kinda read off his notes and poor explaining, but nothing is impossibly hard in this class
Messed up professor teaching a messed up course.

Just avoid him. Jesus. He does explain the concept; however, he assumed that all the concepts you learned just suppoed to provide you a base. And he is asking you to build a landmark on it by yourself. All tough problems you saw are easiest problems for him. No wonder why exams are hard. You will find Q1 a)is easy, and b),c),d)you'll have no ideas.
Extremely hard exam
Second exam was so much harder than the first exam. The numbers were not easy to work with and the exam was super long.
First Exam was really easy, second exam he made impossible without any forewarning
Atrocious exams, no one had enough time for the test. Skips a lot details in lecture that helps make the content intuitive.

He is frankly an insecure control freak that doesn't allow you to do anything besides his way. He requires people to work on the HW PDF. Doesn't sound bad until you get points off for writing your HW answers clearly on lined paper with work shown. When you email him you have to email him in a specific yet tedious format or he won't respond.Insecure

His teaching style is divisive, you either understand him or you don't. And if you don't you are on your own.  The exams were wayy to hard for a pre-calc class with the averages being around 50-59%, he does curve at the end of the semester but really plays with your confidence and those scores reinforced my hatred of math.

Lecture materials were taught well, but exams and quizzes were extraordinarily more difficult that the materials taught in class to the point where students were not taught more difficult concepts that showed up on exams/quizzes. Allowed a cheat sheet, but not enough time on exams. Overall professor was rude and dismissive when asked questions.

Makes ZERO exceptions, lectures fail to explain the simplest of concepts, quizzes are online with a 20-minute time limit, and requires you to do your HW using LaTeX software, which he never explains how to use in class. Went to his office hours, but he was standoffish and didn't seem to care. One of the worst professors in the NYU Math department.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take! Forced to self study and basically teach the material to myself. I have taken this class in high school and yet he still makes it confusing. Passive aggressive, unresponsive, and does not care. Stay away if you can.

I HATE him PERIOD. I wasn't able to access the webassign. Even though i texted bunch of cengage people and they say its the prof problem and our "respected" professor sanfratello respond is: You have to figure it by yourself...thank god I drop his class and you know what, i got placed into cal 3. GOODBYE

DO NOT TAKE HIM IF YOU HAVE OTHER OPTIONS!!
Give two quizzes with in one week (one of them is pop-up), and there's still quiz right after midterm. His grading rubric of polished proof is basically asking you to publish another textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: When I have a better understanding of "passive aggressive"

Just avoid him. Very nice guy, but does not care about you in the slightest. Lectures are irrelevant and goes on a tangent. If you want to learn your better off learning calculus through YouTube. If you're praying for NYU just avoid him since the payment is better off going to a YouTube channel or a tutor since you will need that.

Does not give enough time for exams, even with letting us make a reference sheet to use. Quizzes tended to rely on tricks/manipulations rather than actual computations or applications. He did teach things very straightforward (nice), but in the process omitted the concepts and connections needed to understand the overall concept, and skipped steps.

Engaging lectures (mostly) explained well. I feel like he lectures based on his old notes so he doesn't remember all the things he's lecturing about (so might not answer questions well). He glosses over some concepts he thinks are "basic" or doesn't cover more examples in class but the homework are good indicators of what to see on tests/quizzes.

He seems to really care and his lectures are engaging. However the problem is that he glosses over so many things in class assuming you already know everything. His example problems have giant leaps in the process for the answer which make using them to study useless. HW and exams will only vaguely if at all resemble what he does in lecture.

Please for the love of God ignore the students giving him 5/5. 

Imagine paying 80K a year at school only to get a teacher that cannot properly teach the concepts. He constantly glosses over the basic, important steps to understand the work. You either have to be math genius or you already know Calc

Professor Sanfratello doesn't deserve the amount of criticism that the reviewers are giving. He explains concepts clearly. The concepts can be challenging to grasp at first. Some HWs can take a while. The exams can be a bit of a time crunch, but they aren't that hard.

Absolute legend, he is hilarious and really smart. His lectures are clear, hws are easy, but exams are a bit hard. Make sure to do a lot of practice and go to his office hours. Overall, an absolute star!!!

I don't know why there are so many negative reviews...give this man some credit!! Speaking from someone who has ALWAYS struggled with math, this class is relatively clear and well-organized. Linear alg isn't very hard and there are TONS of resources online, so u can't blame him if u r not doing well. He is a humorous guy who cares about the topic.

The course is OK. The professor is OK. He can explain basic concepts of Linear Algebra. However, Time for test is absolutely not enough, and he do not know how to accommodate student who take this course online. Students wasted 10 min because of him and he did not give extra time to compensate. Number is his HW and quiz is disaster.
Incredibly amazing, except that he is one of the worst I have seen in NYU. Choose him!
bagayalu
Pretty chill guy to learn LA from. Pay attention in class and it is an easy time.

Homework is easy and the quizzes are a little tricky, but the exams are a false mirage of being "easy." You think you studied enough for the exam, but it humbles you. Recitation leaders are more helpful than him. Sanfratello is good person, but not the best at lecturing. Unless you live, breathe, sleep matrices, I would find a different professor.

exam 1 was based off of topics that were not taught in the class yet, he graded the tests even though he knew that the exam questions were wrong. overall not very accommodating. lecture slides are ok, he gives them to you filled out. quizzes are pretty easy. TA's have argued over correct answers with him. if you can take someone else please do.

Sometimes it feels as if the professor of the class has made himself the king of zoom just because he has online exams and proctors them. Unsure whether the professor is proficient in his own material because we are often referred to high school algebra for help. Would not recommend, especially online.
Does he understand the knowledge himself?

His lecture makes no sense since he only teaches matrix calculation omitting the meaning behind it therefore his math class looks that a remembering class. I am not sure if he really understands linear algebra himself or just too lazy to teach in detail.

Isn't great at giving lectures, slides are poor, make sure to take good notes. Definitions/theorems are significant portions of exams, make sure to memorize important ones. Familiarize yourself with proofs and know the general format. Make sure you understand HWs for exams. Quizzes often, but usually on the lecture he just gave. Exam averages: 65s

For his linear algebra, very heavy workload. You're expected to read the textbook word by word, and homework amount is insane.
I had him for online class, the midterm and final exam are terribly difficult compared to the in-person person.
Try to avoid his online class. Tough grading for ONLINE linear algebra.

He is a decent choice I would say. I didn't have any complaints and thus he deserves 4/5. Unlike other professors his classes are bearable to watch so I will give him to that. Class work is normal, not crazy. Exams are fair but the quizzes are hard.

He doesn't understand half of the really complicated topics and his lecture notes are a mess. Towards the end of the semester, the proofs he teaches in class become logically incoherent. I compared his content with a different professor's, let's just say the latter made a lot more sense. His exams are easier though, and plenty of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a normal professor but sometimes can't explain deeper concepts clearly to students. Normal exams but quizzes are hard.
To be honest, his class is relaxed and fun. He is very inspirational! For the group project, if you put your heart into it, you will get a pretty good score. He is a real GEM.

Quite literally the worst course I have ever taken. The lectures drag on eternally, the content is either excruciatingly boring and useless or needlessly complicated. This is a required class, and it seems like Prof Sanfratello is either unaware of that, or is completely insensitive to it. I wish I could rate it a 0.

Every single class theres a pop quiz. Every week you have to do a polished proof and code it into Latex. Every other week you have to do 10 problem sets with multiple parts. He rushes for over content for the quizzes that don't matter and makes the dumbest jokes. Overall not the greatest and annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Sanfrantello is a very solid professor. He is a bit funny and helps you learn. Issue is, since he is new and the homework is from NYU the stuff you learn in class does not always relate to the HW. The problem sets are a lot of work. However the exams are fair but require a ton of self study to do well on the proofs part.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Sanfratello is the new professor here and he is very hilarious. We can get a full mark in quizzes as long as we read the book ( the quizzes are pretty short! 3-4 questions per quiz). He is always there to help me and encourage me to learn discrete math. Listen carefully and you will get great grades! Choose him and you won't regret : )
The course is easy, and I don't listen to him at class. His exams are really basic and not difficult.

Prof Sanfratello is great! His class policies make it very easy to learn well. He lets you use a cheat sheet for the midterms. Homework is standard, and so are the exams. He quite funny, but sometimes makes arithmetic mistakes that can be really annoying.

Lectures are interesting, he is funny, explains material well, and is always open to questions. You may skip a few classes, but he gives a pop quiz almost every time. There are a lot of assignments, but if you understand the material you'll be fine. Also, some quizzes/assignments are dropped so you if bomb a few you'll still pass the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Only covers the basics in class, and makes a lot of arithmetic mistakes. Questions given in HW & exams are far more conceptual and complicated. Doesn't even follow the guideline sometimes on what to expect for weekly quizzes. However, he does allow us to bring in a cheat sheet for exams, and gives out extra credit problems.
The work amount and deadline aren't good at all. Both of the readings for each week are due right in the middle of the week, on a Wednesday at 5pm...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about his work and wants to encourage his students to resonate with the material. Definitely a lot of reading! Weekly responses and 3 total essays. He likes in-class participation but you can get away with not talking much. Really recommend booking office hours to speak with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a really nice guy and the discussions are interesting. But he is a very very harsh grader. And he is not joking when he says you must attend every single class to be able to get an A.

His class felt like story time more than an actual class, he requires reading then runs out of time to discuss it. The discussions felt aimless and I don't think I learned anything other than fun facts, he is a nice guy.

Veerstegh is a super interesting and kind person despite his seemingly intimidating nature. Veerstegh leads the class in a manner that can make rather boring texts interesting. Simultaneously, Veerstegh will assign 3-4 readings per class, and it's very hard to engage purposefully with each reading, which is one thing I would have liked to change.

Boring readings and class discussions, they are always very predictable. I learned nothing from this class coming in liking the subject matter. Assignments aren't tough or anything, very easy and managable workload if you skim the readings. TBH you don't need to read but its obvious when everyone hasn't.

He's a great professor. Can be a little rigid in how he directs the class, but he does really know what he's talking about so the discussions are usually pretty engaging. Lots of reading for homework. He is tough but gives really good feedback and suggestions if you ask him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Adrian asks that his students read a fair amount for his classes. The readings are not demanding but they can be long (though consistently engaging). It's certainly doable if you're remotely organised with your time. Otherwise he's a great professor and his courses are intellectually rewarding, unique and he's always available to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Although Adrian's lectures were somewhat interesting (the class is about sewers and subways, so it's NOT a particularly cool subject matter), I feel like I didn't learn anything from it. I'm finishing the class without knowing anything relevant. If you're an out of the box thinker go for it, but you'll struggle if not. Wouldn't take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would admit that I did poor at writing. It's simply not my interest. But Adrian is very helpful whenever I have problems with essays and is open to all the different opinions. I would not take his class again because I am so done with writing stuffs, but for those of you who also hate writing: make efforts and talk to him, he will understand you.

Assigns lots of reading (he's a literature prof, after all), but very generous grader if you participate and make a real effort. He actually brought us to the library and showed us how to do research, which no one else does. Also, he taught a class with a rat (yes, really).

While some of the readings were interesting, and he was very accessible outside of class, he was not my favorite professor. He forced discussion and group work in awkward ways. Was not clear in his feedback. Attempted to do too much in one class. For a research class, he did very little focus on research.

Adrian is a solid English 101 professor. He definitely keeps class interesting and encourages everyone to share their viewpoints in discussion. Clearly very passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Nice to have a young, energetic professor for a change.

I took Adrian's Gallatin research seminar "Shadow Cities". He is very engaged during class and does give very helpful feedback during office hours. If you make the effort, read the material, and participate in class, you will do well. Course material became a bit boring later into the semester. He also has a tendency to talk AT you not with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Sweet, funny, challenging, brilliant and gorgeous. Just wish he taught more courses.

He's an offbeat young professor who is very passionate about what he teaches and always willing to help. Go to office hours because he's funny, very motivating and unbelievably smart and can talk forever about pretty much any topic. Hope he stays at NYU.

He is seriously smart on an array of topics and can sometime seem intimidating. However, as long as you read, everything will be swell. People tend to describe him as boring and not good at leading class discussions but he is in fact the opposite. He is able to lecture to a class full of students who did read and that's a true talent.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Taking him now for Victorian Literature. Adrian is an amazing, knowledgeable instructor. He always comes prepared and is a great discussion leader. A bit challenging, but you will do well as long as you read, participate and do the assignments. Caring. Understanding. And, yes, the man is jaw-droppingly handsome. If I could... let me stop.

This was easily one of the best classes I've taken. Adrian is a talented lecturer and engaging discussion leader, very generous with his time and willing to accommodate different student interests. Obviously the two negative reviews below were written by the same person. But Adrian gets a lot of attention. That's probably why you're here, right? ;)

Adrian is clearly a new professor and while I see a lot of potential, he hasn't figured out how to engage his students. Classes went over the allotted time (which was 3 hours), questions asked didn't generate discussion, and his prompts were extremely vague. While he made himself available to meet often, the meetings weren't particularly helpful.

Though Adrian is clearly an intelligent student of literature, I was disappointed with his teaching and at times unprofessional manner. Adrian consistently held class late up to a half hour and arrived late to appointments. In class discussions, Adrian asked mainly basic plot questions or closed questions, preventing a range of interpretations.

One of the smartest people I have ever met... awesome lecturer... seems intimidating at first but is actually genuinely kind and sweet. Helps a lot during office hours. And yes I would totally have his blue eyed babies.
Super smart. Looks like a young Brad Pitt. Holds class in the park when the weather is nice. What's not to love?

Do not take him for HBSE. He has changed the syllabus 6+ times throughout the semester, adding new readings two days before class. He doesn't post rubrics and his feedback does not reflect the grades he gives. His lectures are unstructured and often irrelevant. Maybe he is good for research but not for HBSE

Professor Alif reminded me why I came back to academia in the first place: to challenge wicked problems in a way that still centers, honors, and respects those who are disproportionately harmed by them. They are a rising tide who lifts every boat. If you're lucky enough to take a class, just make some flashcards (they'll help w/ acronyms).
extra ordinary teacher that have  I ever seen .amazing experience with them

Professor Alif, is a caring and genuine guy. The best professor I had at NYU. The pop-quizzes are rough but he does his best to prepare you and will spend the time with you outside of class to make sure you understand content. Outside of the classroom he is a true advocate for his students. I personally connect recommend a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Alif is very kind. He respects students' wellbeing and personal life. However, the lecture was bit dry, even he provides a lot of personal experiences to incorporate the materials.

The professor is new to teaching, but he brings a wealth of field experience and personal relevance to the class. You will learn a lot from him. While he is a tough grader, he is very considerate. Be ready to be challenged and to think outside the box.
I think Professor Alif is very smart and inspiring. He is also very enthusiastic about teaching students. I appreciated the class even though I found it challenging!

He clearly cares about students' learning. That being said, the course often felt inconsistently prioritized in terms of engagement versus other priorities in the professor's diverse set of responsibilities.

Good at integrating relevant material. Extremely disorganized and a poor communicator. Often spoke in abbreviations that no one understood. Provided contradictory guidance over half a dozen messages on every assignment. Lectures hard to follow. Every classmate I talked to found his teaching to be inaccessible. A smart person, but a weak instructor.

Professor Ahmed goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material. 
The readings and podcasts he provided were relevant. I definitely gained a lot from this class and feel more confident doing research after his class
Prof. Alif does a great job bridging theory with real practice in behavioral and public health.
Come in ready to learn
He was great!

This professor is genuinely the worst professor I have ever had in my university experience. I'm not done yet but my course just took the second midterm, and the entire class felt that they failed.That's a sign the professor is a failing educator. You could study for weeks with all course material available to you and still fail. Don't do it.

reviews.comment: class is not hard but he is bad at teaching.

Teaches off slides/doesn't work through problems. Lectures don't prepare you for exams. Makes fun of you for asking questions. Lots of time spent reteaching myself every lesson. Exams impossible to finish in allotted time. Overall horrible experience.
RUNAWAY IF YOU DONT WANT TO DROP YOUR GPA
RUN! No reason to take this class!!!
