She is laid-back and an easy grader, but you still have to do the work because otherwise you'll fall behind. Overall, I love Tina and recommend taking any class with her!

Tina is wonderful and vivacious. She makes learning italian much more interesting and has quite a fun class, though it lacks come structure it is very conversation and culture oriented. I loved this class and would recommend it to others looking to become acquainted with the language.
Tina is awesome, take her class. She is a great teacher as well as person. I LOVE TINA!

Tina is an amazing teacher.  You should definitely take her if you have the opportunity. Very sweet and funny..engaging and helpful as well.  Quick with emails and super down to earth.  You're the best Tina!
Tina rocks!  Take her if you can.  Super nice grader and really nice woman.  Will definitely make sure you get a good grade!
She is great, a very good teacher but also a great role model. She is kind, compassionate and makes learning a new language fun.

The material was taught in a very engaging and interesting way and I felt I learned a lot from outside ? the - book teachings. Tina is one of my favorite professor at NYU. She understands how to relate to students  and makes the class fun and engaging despite the boring curriculum.
Very nice, highly recomend
Really nice native Italian professor.  Sometimes a little hard to understand, but she will always re-clarify if necessary.  Easy grader.

A native of Italy, she is very good at the language and its intricacies. Understandably, her English isn't perfect and thus her clarity in teaching suffers. A VERY easy grader, you simply need to study for the midterm and final. Quizzes and "tasks" are almost guaranteed perfect marks. Although she's nice, sometimes she literally ignores questions.
Really good, especially since its an introductory class.  Not bad on the eyes either!
Weird and way too personal and inappropriate in class. Nice enough, but unprofesional.

I could write a whole novel about this class. It was easy? So if you want an easy class, you will definitely get an A. Carley herself, though very kind, can be really tough to work with at times. Instructions are often VERY unclear, and students don't know what to do. Not very helpful whenever asking for help. People in my class were stressed.

Carley truly wants to get to know you, and gives detailed feedback on essays! The classes are overall chill (a little unstructured sometimes) and theraputic. The essay topics are designed so that you could basically write about anything that interests you. If you're examining the sociopolitical state of world the typa gal you would like her a lot.

carley is sweet and caring! you can tell she genuinely wants you to become a better writer and she def helped me in becoming that. participation matters a lot and get ready to share a lot of your own writing with the class, which may be uncomfy at first but you get used to it.

SHE IS SO SWEET. She is extremely understanding. Be prepared to share your readings in class though. But overall so caring and gives great feedback. Has 2 essays throughout the semester but you get feedback from her and the entire class. TAKE HER!!!
If you attend class and do the very few assignments, you should get an A. I dont see how you wouldn't

I loved the welcoming environment the class had, she was really welcoming and lenient on grading the lowest grade she gave anyone on a essay was a B-. Also there wasn't really that much reading that you have to do in the class. The major grade are just 2 essay and participation basically. Must take class!!! Would def recommend taking.

If you like to talk, you'll like this class. Very goated chill prof and very nice too just do your work and you'll do good. Very honest, and you can learn many things about the world. Overall GOAT W Carley in the chat.

Carley was one of the best professors I've ever had at NYU. Truly cares about your progress in writing and allows you to stay true to your voice. She will push you but this class was delightful, manageable, and the assignments were diverse and fun.

Carley's class is great. Its that simple. Not a ton of homework a few big assignments but no busy work. Only 2 essays which are longer but super manageable. She gives good feedback and helps outside of class. You would almost have to try to do bad to get below a B. I love this class honestly my favorite class thus far. Definitely recommend Carley!

Carley is a really sweet woman and a decent teacher. She does force students to share their work and she tends to bring a lot of politics into the classroom, which can make things pretty uncomfortable. But other than that the class is pretty easy and her assignments are generally fun.
I LOVE CARLEY. She is very insightful, patient, caring, and kind. She doesn't grade lower than a B-.
Carley is fantastic. It takes a sec to warm up to her because she's very unique from a lot of professors at NYU, but she's truly one of the greats.
Carley was an amazing professor! The best writing prof. I've had so far. She's helped me improve my writing so much and i've learned to be more confident when I write!

Carley is the most amazing professor. She changed my freshman year experience. I not only learned so so much, but I also wanted to go to her class all the time. It was fun, engaging, and one of the best classes I've ever taken. I owe so much to her for everything she gave me. Please take her class! You will not regret it. I love Carley!
Do not take her class!!!
If you wish to avoid experiencing intense pain and suffering, do not enroll in her course.
She is the best writing professor I have ever met in my life! You will definitely improve a lot when working with her
Wonderful professor! Learned lots about writing essays. She always checked in with the whole class to see how we were.

I really love Carley! As a student not good at writing, she encouraged me to try my best and gave useful feedbacks for revising the essay. Only two essays for the class. Class environment is so chill. There are usually short readings for every class. Although I got B for midterm, Carley gave me A at the end. I strongly recommend taking her class.

AMAZING PROF!!! LOVE YOU CARLEY. I learned so much as a writer and person in this class. Carley creates such a wonderful community and she truly cares. She also gives great feedback and is very understanding.  Take her class. She's awesome.

Carley is an amazing writing professor. I am not a great writer by any means and she really encouraged me and made me feel comfortable. There is little hw and sufficient time for the 2 essays we do in which she guided us through it. 100% wish I could have her every semester.

Carley is an amazing professor that truly cares about her students. She is so kind, so attentive, and the way she creates mini communities within her classes is masterful. I felt comfortable, respected, and valued in her class thanks to her. Taking her class was a transformative experience.

Compared to my other classes, this writing course allowed me to temporarily escape my academic writing and let my creative side loose. The classroom environment feels inspiring thanks to the informal yet academic group discussions and peer review workshops. So grateful for courses like these!

Professor Moore is the best professor I have had during my first year at NYU (and I had some great ones). She is inspiring, caring and compassionate. Her class structure is engaging and she brought readings that were interesting and sparked intellectual discussions in class. I have definitely become a better writer with her guidance.

Carley's great. I took her for both Writing I and II, and overall enjoyed my experience. Participation and discussion are key. Readings can be long, but digestible. Always gives good feedback when workshopping papers. A must-take.

Carley did some kind of magic and somehow made our class into a mini community. For a writing class that was so fantastic to have because everyone was able to write, share, and critique on a deeper level. Will miss this class. Only non-positive thing I can say is that her essay grading criteria was a little vague.
Hands down my favorite professor at NYU so far. We all loved her!!!

I had Carley Moore for Writing 1 & 2 in the LS program. If there were a Writing 3, I'd take it with her too! She challenged me more than any teachers I had in high school, but she also gave me creative space to be a human being and develop my unique voice as a writer. She cares genuinely cares. We need more Carley Moores in this world.

One of the best professors at NYU. Carley gives assignments which are interesting and worth writing. It is impossible to do bad in this class because she gives so much help and advice. She really cares about her students; she is very understanding and is a great person in general. Definitely recommend if you want to grow as a writer.

Carley is the best writing teacher/professor I've ever had and the first one who actually taught me how to be more articulate and write an essay that matters. My class loved Carley so much that we literally once went one-by-one and told her what we liked about her. She's a professor that'll change your life!!

She always pushes you to do the hard thing. It's going to be challenging, but it is deifinitely worth it. Two essays per semester,but she will help you through it; a few small assignment at the beginning, and a blog post during the semester. Everytime you feel like giving up she gives you a reason to stay.  Take her, you won't regret it!

Carley is the sweetest and most dedicated professor. She genuinely cares about her students and wants us to succeed. She introduces the class to a lot of great readings and books that actually help us improve our writing skills. Though the homework sometimes seems to be a lot of work, it all has a purpose. She never assigns busy work!

I love Carley! I took her again second semester. She really works to give you feedback for your essays and grades according to how you take your feedback. If you put in the effort you'll definitely get the grade you deserve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Carley is the only professor I have ever bothered to review on Rate My Professor. She is the kindest, most genuine person. She made Writing such a wonderfully explorative and enjoyable course - I never once wanted to skip. We had to write two papers and a blog post, and her methods of teaching and analyzing made the 8-10 pages easier than expected.

I love Carley as a person and a teacher. She's a generally awesome person who cares about her students. However, don't take her if you're looking for an A. She's a tough grader, and is very blunt when she doesn't like something you write. It can hurt sometimes. THAT BEING SAID, she's a lovely person and knows what she's doing!

Carley is an incredible woman and great teacher.  she is patient but doesn't let people walk all over her.  she gives a lot of freedom in how we write and has so much wisdom.  my writing improved so much over the course of one semester and it reminded me of why I used to love writing so much.

It's like her voice is drowning her face to sleep. Easy class if you can deal with the monotone. Her thoughts are extremely abstract and one has difficulty at times relating the assignments to every day life. Otherwise, a wonderful person.

Carley is an amazing professor. She will teach you things about writing that you will be able to apply to all other parts of your life. She is fun, energetic, and inspirational. If you are dedicated to learning and work hard you will get a good grade.

Carley is the perfect teacher. I initially had no interest in writing, and absolutely no interest in essay writing, but Carley changed that. She is extremely helpful and instructive, and if you are willing to learn, you WILL, you will learn so much and see tremendous growth in your writing.
Carley is an incredible teacher. Her lessons are fun and engaging, and she is extremely knowledgable. It's definitely not an easy A but it will be worth it in the long run. Take her class!
Carley has a great control over abstract ideas.

I took Writing I and II with Carley Moore, and she has taught me more than any teacher I've ever had. The readings and following discussions are lively and interesting, and she gives you leeway to write about what interests you. She will work you had and challenge you, but you will leave her class a 100% better writer and better human being. LOVE!

Carley is literally the best professor I had. She cares about you and she cares about your writing. She wants you to be better and she knows you can be better. She will frustrate you, annoy you, make you work HARD, but the product will be amazing. Her readings are so interesting, and she's so fricken nice. I took her again. TAKE HER. SHE IS AMAZING

She will challenge you, keep you up late some nights, and really frustrate you. some days you will love her, some days you will hate her. But at the end of the day she is a damn good teacher and really knows what she is talking about...you will become a better writer under her and it is worth it.

Carley may come off as intimidating at times, but she's funny, laid back, and wants to have a good relationship with her class. I found her super challenging, but she taught such helpful methods when you put in the effort. Read really awesome articles/excerpts.

Carley is one of the best professors I had at NYU. I had her for Writing 1 & 2 and although they were challenging, it was worth it! You will thank her later for making you a better writer. Participation and effort are all it take to get an "A"!
Wow. This class was bad. She thinks she is really smart, but is factually ignorant and spacey. DO NOT take any class with her.

Although she's a tough grader and her essay topics are challenging, Carley really cares about her students' writing, and only helped me improve over the semester. She's awesome!! Definitely take her class if you want a challenge AND some fun!

Carley is an AMAZING professor! Not only did my writing improve with her class, but I was able to enjoy the topics. The class discussion is both relevant and extremely helpful. If you don't understand something or need extra help, she repeats her office hours pretty much every class. One of my favorite classes!
Now that I look behind, I can realize how much I learned. A lot of work, but one of the most helpful teachers I have ever had.
You opened my eyes! Thanks fore everything Carley!

Carley's teaching style was very hard to get used to at first. But now, I can honestly say that I enjoy her class and she 100% has made me a better writer. She wants you to figure everything out on your own, but she is there to guide you. I reccomend her, the work load is average, and you will improve as both a writer and reader of texts from her.

Awful. Unhelpful and completely out of the loop with all information. Avoid. And if you ask a question it is likely her response is I don't know. How can you lead a class with so little direction and knowledge of the apparent school resources?

Carley is amazing - one of the best profs I've had. I took her for two semesters, and my love for her has only grown. Her classes are fun and interesting, and she has really helped me become a better writer. A lot of essays to read, but most of them are interesting, and it's okay to skip a few of them, but you'll learn they actually help you.
No comment

Carley is great as a person but if she doesn't like your style of writing it's hard to well. I learned a lot from her and how to convey a concept clearly and with plenty of evidence but felt like I came to a dead end with my grades. Make sure you do the reading, it's what your essays are based off of.

I love this lady. At first you'd think she was an evil kindergarten teacher, and then you learn they don't hand out Ph D.'s to just anyone. She pushes you and the end result is nothing short of amazing.

Carley is a great teacher: though you might wonder why she's making you do some seemingly unnecessary work, it always turns out to be helpful and everything you do serves a purpose throughout the course. There are no midterms and finals, but 3 essay requirements per semester, and she's a tough grader. She really expects us to learn and PRACTISE.

My assessment of her has changed the way historians' assessment of Truman did; hated her after I was done with her, but I've come to realize she was very good (though not great). She's wonky, very abstract, and can be VERY frustrating. But the way she gets you to write is multilayered, and more along the lines of creative writing than droll essays.

I had high hopes for this class but Carley successfully crushed them. This class consists of useless art projects and lofty, horribly explained essays and must fit her definition of a good essay or else you will get a poor grade. Prior to this class, I didn't realize there was only ONE way to write an essay. Thanks Carley for killing creativity.

Carley is the best teacher I've had at NYU so far. She makes you work hard, but you will learn so much and be a better writer for it. Plus, her class is really enjoyable and she makes it interesting. She's a great person. I wish I could take her again!
Carley will make you work really hard, and it totally pays off, especially in other classes. I love Carley!

Carley is amazing.  She really wants you to learn the things she is teaching and cares about her students.  I feel like I could talk to her about anything even outside of class.  She'll take time to read drafts and give her feedback.  She is challenging and wants you to do your work but isn't that the point?

Convoluted writing assignments that take several classes (or meetings) to explain. Deals with abstract absurdities like "pebbles" and "ripples." Has specific idea of what she wants you to write but almost refuses to articulate it. And if you can't do what she wants, she condescendingly criticizes you-even though her stance is based on pure opinion.

she is amazing. i use her writing techniques in all of my other classes and the A's just keep coming. I had her as a freshman and now as a senior she will still find time to talk to me and help me out with anything. She also writes great recommendation letters. the most important thing though is how she completely trains you to think deeply.

I love Carley! she will turn you into a much deeper thinker an da better writer. At first I thought she was going to be a hard ass, but she's really funny, nice, and patient. (I am late every time, she has yet to get really pissed) I wish I could take her next semester!
CARLEY IS AWESOME!!!  SHE IS MY ROCK.

Carley was awesome! There is a lot of work in this class, and she is very big on journaling, but it is totally worth it. My writing improved so much. Her grading is more than fair, and she is always willing to help you out, if you put the time in. Would highly recommend her.

She is cool, a bit weird at times, but if you care about her class she will show you how to do well. If you ever have problems just ask her to have a meeting, she is very helpful, but there is a ton of work to do, you will learn but you will suffer in the process :) j/k she is probably the second best professor at NYU, i have yet to meet the 1st :)

I cannot say enough about Carley. She is so helpful and very encouraging. There's a lot of work to do, but I enjoyed it a lot. She's young enough to know what college kids are going through, and she's very real. My writing improved amazingly. I actually made sure that I had her for both semesters. Take her class if you possibly can!
Loved Carley Moore.  She's young and has a good idea what freshman and everyone else are facing.  Learned a lot from her, and she's wonderful.  Take her class if you possibly can.

Carley was great! She made the class fun and interesting, and really encouraged class discussions. Although there is a fair share of work involved, it's totally do-able. She makes herself very available to students who need help with assignments. She's very kind, sweet,  absolutely recommend her!

carley is really great. she gives tons of writing, but makes the writing seem fun. be prepared to write a lot, have work to do every night, but also to have an incredible fun time. im impressed at the how my writing skills improved. REALLY. carley, keep doing a good job.

carley is the best! she gives lots of stimulating exercises and explains well so you are prepared for her writing tasks. her class is pretty laid back yet you get a lot of work done. her class is fun and interesting. carley is super nice, relates to her students, and she loves rock!!!
carley is the best; she conquers the sometimes impossible task of making writing fun, and makes improvement exponential and unavoidable
Carley is great. This class has an intense amount of writing, but somehow, she makes it alright. I would recommend taking her.
Easy A if you participate and just follow along with the class. Definitely the thing you need in the first year of college.
Made complexities enjoyable and was very kind. Participate a little and do the homework for a free A. Midterm and final weren't difficult.

Really nice teacher and the class was really easy. Took complexities: oceans with daniella, which was a new course, and she made it more enjoyable. Just participate a little in class and do the work, and it's a free A.

Jeff Day, what an incredible professor. Please do yourself and him a favor-- don't take his class UNLESS you are serious about the topic. He will invest in you if you invest in his class. He will always make time outside of class to help you with your photography, but he won't sugarcoat it if you need to up your game. Most honest and caring mentor.

Good teacher, engaging class. Has clear views about what he likes and if your work doesn't fit that you'll know. Only flaw is that he makes a few morally wrong comments here and there but it keeps things interesting. Easy A class and a highlight of the week. Will take your around the city and explore

Jeff Day, where do I begin... this man has changed everything for me. He has completely made me rethink the way I photograph and view the world. Cares about his students and gives constructive feedback. Anticipates what you need before you even know you need it. He is a powerful man.

What I love about Jeff is he's not interested in helping you fill a requirement towards a diploma; he's interested in actually teaching you skills that you can use in the real world and helping you grow as an artist. You get back what you put into the class, so to reap the rewards you just have try. I am in Beyond Picture Perfect as well.I love it
I took his class Beyond Picture Perfect. He is funny and has a lot of technical knowledge as well as artistic input. He made me such a better photographer. I definitely recommend.
You can choose him if you like a lot of unnecessary homework and boring class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kuaiii pao jiarenmen
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Foley at the Writing Center was incredibly helpful and kind. He reviewed every word of my essay and provided detailed feedback. During the discussion, he discussed my ideas with me and documented our discussions and give it to me afterward. His  questions helped me better structure the logic of my writing, which I found truly inspiring.

You have so much homework every class that doesn't even contribute to your essay. all of the lectures are long and boring and filled with things I knew since middle school. I can imagine him being a good teacher to someone who needs help learning how to write but if you have these skills already the class is just painful.

Professor Foley's classes were well structured and clear- he always had a concept or idea for us to focus on each class. His feedback is helpful and he created a good atmosphere in the class. Although difficult, I feel that my writing, comprehension, and thinking skills have improved immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dont take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: From the beginning, class was always super engaging and David was passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. He fostered a fun but hard-working classroom environment, which was very conducive to work. He gives a moderate amount of work, less than other teachers, and always gives great feedback. Grading is very fair, great class overall!

You definitely have to put in the work when it comes to this class. He gives really great feedback and he really takes the time to read and reread your work. He makes himself very available if you need any help outside class whether that be with finding sources or figuring out the topic of your essay.

I know this keeps getting said but he changed the way I write. I think he's either a hit or miss professor. It can be quite a bit of work at certain times and it can be a bit repetetive to some people which is why everyone may not like him. However the work eventually builds up and if you actually try in the class essay writing becomes easier.

David Foley changed the way I think about writing. He negotiated a perfect balance between work with specific technical elements and allowing for abundant creative freedom. The homework is, I believe, about the average for this course; but it is RIDICULOUSLY helpful. The class may be a bit dry, but it is worth it for such excellent instruction.

tbh the whole expository writing program does not make a lot of sense. You will barely write like this in your other classes. Professor Foley made this whole thing even tougher. Lectures are boring. He assigns hws every class, and most of them are not what you are passionate about. Grading is ok, but I did not gain a lot from the class.

Foley is a teacher that you must put in the work in order to gain from this class. If you arent willing to write a lot in the beginning then this probably isn't the class for you. Although I will say, his homework can be a little overwhelming but when its time to write the paper, you technically have written a good amount of it beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Foley is a teacher that will force the work out of you. If you are not ready to work ie. write, read and write some more. He probably won' be a great choice for you. Also there were many times when I was confused with the criteria but Foley does conferences for each essay and they were extremely helpful. Overall eye-opening experience of my growth

David is very accessible outside of class and will give you extra hope if you want to It. The homework, although it is more than the Usual, it helps you in the end when you were constructing the essay drafts. Amazing professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Okay heres the deal, yes theres homework but it kinda therapeutic to write in a starbucks nearby. Its not even a lot, all the people commenting are slackers. You can easily finish an essay over a weekend without stressing because he gives really good feedback and individual attention. Sometimes class is a bore but hes GREAT!!!! Pls take

David Foley is a wonderful professor. He gives you good notes on essay drafts that help you develop your ideas more thoroughly. The exercises We do in class are very helpful and they are not just busy, irrelevant work. I have grown so much as a writer in his class. He is amazing. Definitely recommend as a professor.

-will make you a better writer but you're gonna have to actually try -do all the assignments and hit the requirements for your paper and you'll be fine -participate every now and then -bit of a stickler on attendance but if you reach out about illness he's a bit flexible -Nice, but will give you a bad grade if you don't do the work

Go in ready to learn, don't feel bad when he tells you don't know as much as you thought (he's right.) The only way to do well is to participate and do all the assignments. No BSing your way through. Very flexible with late assignments & missing class provided you have a good reason and are participating in class. He will challenge you!

After starting my second semester with a new teacher i realized how much BS work we had to do in his class. The stuff we did in class was for the most part a waste of time. And the homwork can sometimes take FOREVER. I feel like I grew a lot as a thinker, not so much as a writer though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Too. Much. Work. This class is taking up a good 3/4 of my weeks work time and is almost irrelevant to what I came to study here. Means well but just stresses and depresses.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: You definitely need to put some effort into this class but he is an amazing teacher and really helpful. He wants you to learn and become a better writer and critic. I learned so much in this class and really recommend him to any student who is serious about their education and their voice in the world. Great teacher!

Foley is a stereotypical English professor who believes everything he says is incredibly profound and complexly interesting. He is generally known as one of the worst Writing the Essay teachers at NYU. BUT he is a surprisingly forgiving grader. I was stuck with him for both semesters and it was NOT a good time.

Ok, so David Foley is bae. If you actually make an effort and engage yourself, you will grow so much. You need to give yourself to him if you want him to give anything to you. He's witty and sweet and so clever and I am basically in very deep platonic love with him. I have incredible conversations with him, he's amazing, I can't even. Bae, I swear.

David Foley is the worst! I was taking his class while struggling with depression and anxiety and he upped that with his confusing advice and inconsiderate attitude. It did not help having him at 8 in the morning, and he talked down to  his students. He was not very helpful and contradictory. He made us hate an already notorious class even more!

He's well meant, but doesn't teach that well, instead trying to focus on developing the student's thinking. This doesn't work because he overloads the amount of work that he assigns, which doesn't work well if you're trying to develop your writing. Instead you just end up spitting out irrelevant exercises and then failing up your final papers.

This guy is super into his own intellectualism.  Every single thing that came out of his mouth was vague; nothing in this class made any sense whatsoever.  He's very particular about little details that don't matter; for instance he refused to accept an essay because I didn't use the right kind of folder.  DO NOT take his class.

So...he is actually a kind and caring guy. He's pretty flexible, but don't push it. He is SO CONFUSING! My exercises didn't help me get to my final essay. The in class prompts were not helpful. He always asks "what are the implications of this?" and I feel I did not grow as a writer in his class. Everyone pretty much gets some sort of B.
Very good class, loved it. Any professor who will quote DFW on syllabus gets an automatically great rating.
the worst prof ever.... dosent help at all... only attacks your ideas... he dosent even tell you what is wrong... DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS every one hates it
Did not answer questions and was very vague if he did answer anything. Pretty much gave everyone a B
He was a great teacher. He was challenging yet always there to help.
Super super super nice guy, but didn't teach anything at all.

Professor Demaio is a very nice guy, but not a great professor. Every class consists of watching something for 30 minutes, not talking about it, then reading out people's homework. And each homework is just to add more pages to our scripts. Zero guidance on story structure, writing conventions, or how to improve. Frankly a waste of time and money.

DO NOT TAKE HIM if you want to learn. Most unhelpful professor. Doesn't give any feedback, teach tv structure, remember your name or the name of your scripts. He will just show tv episodes for the whole class sometimes and not even discuss why it's good. Nice but DO NOT TAKE.

I struggled to enjoy his class. He wouldn't remember people's scripts or names for the first few weeks and would never really teach us anything about writing a pilot--he'd just play TV pilots and then not even talk about them after. His feedback for scripts was very surface-level. Everyone in my class agrees. However, he's very kind to his students
Weekly writing assignments, but Donald was super helpful and kind to everyone who showed up to class. The assignments were not too hard but just expect to practice writing a comedy sketch each week.

I wish I listened before I took Packard. First of all, his syllabus is so confusing and TEDIOUS. It's on a Google Docs and he doesn't post ANY assignments on Brightspace so you have to keep track of deadlines and upload it on a shared Google drive. I had to do 3 presentations in this class and I had less work in my harder classes. Don't take him!

Was really sweet and made me actually interested in the subject. He gave honest and detailed feedback, which genuinely pushed me to try harder. Quizzes were 20% of the grade, and he allows a makeup, so it's easy to get a good grade. Very helpful in office hours and genuinely listens. Highly recommend!

Sweetest guy ever, but his class has unclear expectations and rubrics. PARTICIPATION IS SO IMPORTANT. He is a tough grader, especially when it comes to essays, but you can go to him to retake quizzes for an A.

Packard is a professor that will spark your natural curiosity if you let him. He's a great professor and gives second chances when needed. Just show up, read, and get the work done. The class has a lot of work sometimes, but it can be manageable.
SOOOOO MUCH HOMEWORK. Lowkey my heaviest and hardest course this semester, Unclear essay evaluation criteria! Gives super low participation grade

he's a great guy and so nice and understanding. only thing is that he doesn't use brightspace and only uses google drive which gets really confusing sometimes. also there is lowkey more work than necessary, like even he admitted he gives more work than any other arts & cultures professor. but he's really funny and sweet

His instructions are so unclear, and half the assignments are literally just busy work. The energy in his class is so depressing that I hop the turnstile in front of cops in hopes that they arrest me so I have an excuse not to come to this class. Hes nice though.

Nice guy, very prepared for each class. However there was a lot of homework and a lot of in class group projects. Have to admit this class kept me on my toes. No final test, just an essay, same for the midterm. Wouldn't take him again because I feel like it's just too much work for a simple class. Good guy though, always willing to help.

bro i don't think he graded my final paper but still gave me an A, the lectures itself were pretty fun (even if I didn't read the material). One of the nicest professors I personally know, and was really helpful during office hours.

Nice guy but instructions are sometimes unclear on papers and assignments, and his explanations do not help. I think he is vague on purpose to let your creativity take over or something. Overall his class is pretty easy. There's lots of reading, but hardly any of it is necessary to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: He's not funny because he is trying to crack jokes, but because he's not great at tech and other things. Sometimes he will get your name wrong on the second-to-last day of class, but I am pretty sure he likes me because he sent me kudos. This is my second review for him cuz I took him twice. I highly recommend! Hes sweet too.

Be ready to read. Each class starts with a discussion based on the materials in the documents, he never uses Brightspace, so all assignments and class content are in the current unit's doc. 

Almost every class has homework that you need to submit to the folder; he doesn't give you any grades or feedback on that homework(feels pointless, right?)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment:
2 papers
3 quizzes(you can retake them outside class)
Cares about feminism and queer culture
if you participate he will help you out. He wants discussion in his classroom. He loves natural back n forth between students without his intervention
he cares a lot about attendance
fair grader and tells you where you lost and gained points
great guy!

I love Prof. Packard. He is actually such a caring and nice professor, and he genuinely cares about all of his students. There are a lot of readings, homework, and group projects, but honestly, it's not that bad. He encourages you to talk a lot in class, and he encourages class participation. But overall he's actually great.

He was very kind and clearly super super passionate about what he teaches! I took him for ACA and came back for ACM. I was having trouble keeping afloat in my assignments and he was very understanding and generous with extensions. The most important thing is to speak up and participate. He really values every contribution. Take him!

I can't seem to understand why his ratings are so low. He is amazing. His grading is very clear and accessible to the entire class. He is a very fair grader who gives in-depth feedback and is always happy to help with any questions. The topics he covers are fascinating and you can tell that he genuinely cares about what he is teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Packard is an awesome guy who I can tell is extremely passionate about his subject. However, his assignments can be unclear, and it's confusing which you actually have to complete or not. I felt like the work was easy though, and he fosters a great learning environment. Three group presentations as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Cares for the class and easy if you put in the bare minimum. There's no midterm or final!! There are a few quizes with one retake, 3 projects that are not difficult, and like 2-3 papers for the entire semester! He is very caring and encourages participations, but can get away without. Clear schedules, lots of reading but easy even if you don't.

Great guy and I liked the queer readings he did of some of the poems but he was a hard grader with papers and a big stickler for attendance. Really valued participation, so if you're someone who doesn't like speaking in class I wouldn't recommend. Also lots of reading.

Professor Packard had various teaching methods. He asked us to watch plenty of movies and brought us to different museums. If you have questions, you can meet with him in person every week. His class has lots of group discussions, so you will definitely improve a lot from his class.

He is nice. His syllabus has so many hyperlinks so it could get confusing. His grading criteria is clear, but his verbal instructions are not. He does not use bright space so that's also confusing. 10/10 good guy. Coursework is not thattt bad. Just take him if you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice person in general, but it was overall an unorganized and confusing course. Most of the day to day homework didn't really relate to anything you were eventually graded on, and it felt like a lot of busy work

He is the best professor I have had so far. He will look over your essays and provide feedback if you ask and his feedback is quite extensive, which is amazing! He truly cares about his students. His workload is not much different from any other professor I have had, however it does get difficult if you let your work pile up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Professor Packard is super nice, but my problem was the appalling lack of clarity in assignments and grading criteria. I really like him, and the topic theoretically, but it was kind of ridiculous how unclear it was on what we were expected to do and where our grade would come from. Seems like he just operates on vibes. Also not the best with tech.
Nice guy but not a fan. Annoying about attendance which feels very gaslight-y since this class was lacking in any real substance.
Great professor!

I love Mr. Packard and I think he liked me too. He gave good feedback and always let us retake tests at home and he is a super fare graded. I heard he races horses with his husband named Gilgamesh and Enkidu. He likes people to be out of the box and he wants people to participate. I didn't read though so i was a lil behind in that which was bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Packard is one of my favorite profs/teachers I've ever had, and I hope to take him again. As long as you're able to articulate any sort of considerate thinking about the media you study in class, you'll get an A no matter the opinion or complexity really. He was so easygoing and understanding and lightened our workload whenever we needed it.
His course has three quizzes, and the format is mostly classroom discussion. It's not an easy A, but if you study well you can get A
He is a great professor. His class is fair and interesting. I will take this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Packard was a great teacher this semester. He definitely has a lot of written assignments, but nothing too overwhelming - plus he is a fairly easy grader. Lots of group work for sure, but overall he really tries to make a (in my opinion) boring class interesting. Sometimes unclear in criteria, but always offers timely feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took his Cultural Foundations class four years ago during my first semester at NYU and he is to this day one of the best professors I have ever had. Super supportive and accessible and I felt as if he was very passionate about what he was teaching us which I loved !!

Professor Packard was one of the more eager professors I've had - really passionate about his teaching. He actively inspired class debate and organized great discussion. He was also good in giving essay and research feedback. Real gem in the LS department; be sure to take his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Packard is a wonderful professor who truly cares about his students. I took him first semester as a first-year year and he was always incredibly supportive. He also introduced me to some of my best friends!

Professor Packard is a wonderful person and professor. He cares about every student individually and fosters a wonderful learning environment. I met some of best friend in his class due to his group project pairings. I would die for Chris Packard. <3

He gives you good feedback on essays, but it is very difficult to meet his criteria. He likes kids who talk a lot in class, even if it's none sense. His office hour doesn't very help. Lots of readings go undiscussed. Many presentations during the semester. Don't recommend for people who want easy A. Participation required.

He's very diverse with his readings, sometimes it's heavy but not too bad. HW is easy and simple. Grades essays/paragraphs through google docs + gives good feedback. One huge google doc of all the notes from the class. He emails back fast and helps during office hours. Light lectures. One pop quiz. Super funny and caring, highly recommend!
He is such a sweet person! I wish he was teaching CFII last semester. Overall a very easy course, and he was never hard on grading. He cares about his students grades. 10/10 recommend.

He's awesome! Taking him again because he is engaging, informative and cares a lot about his students. He does his best to accommodate people that aren't in his concentration either so everyone is included.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Overall, I enjoyed his WF2 class. I advise going to office hours/meetings when you get the chance; he's incredibly helpful and insightful. And the work load isn't too much either. Don't hesitate on taking his writing class!
Amazing, take him and ignore those who tell you otherwise. This is coming from someone who's not interested in doing any more work ever than whats needed to do well.
He is a good professor. His work is easy and he is extremely accessible. His score is way lower than it should be.
Great professor, easy grader and not too much of a work load. Works had to be accessible.

He is a great professor, the review don't give him enough credit. I had him for writing 1 and writing two, and he is such a great teacher. He is a really fair grader go to office hours it gives him an insight in your point perspective of the paper which really boosts your grade.

When I took Packard's class he was really demanding about the work we had to do for the class, it was really excessive. At one point I had an extenuating circumstance and asked for an extension ON A DRAFT and he was so rude about it. It was honestly the worst experience I had at NYU thus far.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!! Do not take him for CF or Writing. He will assign work that is half thought out and unclear. He will make you write a paper after you immediately turned in another paper. Be expected to be given readings that will go undiscussed and serve no overall purpose to the class.
Great professor.

His lectures are a long ramble of nonsense that often times doesn't even have to do with what we are studying in class. We have a huge amount of work expected for every class time, whether it is an essay or a group project, and he takes no pity in you asking to cut some slack and not have to learn about stuff that you didn't even see in class.

Packard cares about teaching but unfortunately, he is terrible at it. His assignments are work intensive and often unrelated to what we learn in class. He assigns us long, technical readings that we don't cover in class and then expects us to know the information for tests. His lectures are long and unorganized and complete bs. Don't take his class

1. How can you assign midterms covering material that was not at all touched upon in class? I teach myself the material in this class by myself. 2. What is the structure of your class? I come out of it more confused than I was entering it.  3. Unnecessary assignments...  - He's a teacher whose hearing his students but not listening to them.
Famous for giving vague assignments, rambling through confusing lectures with no logical organization, and not caring about whether or not his students learn anything
Honestly the worst professor I've EVER had. I used to love writing but he ruined that for me. He's very critical and rude. He gives vague prompts and then grades them harshly.

I personally do not feel like I learned anything in this class. This is for people who do not have a lot of other work because you are asked to interview and crowdsource quite a bit. The assignments are different and interesting but take too much time.
Students find Professor Packard, or as we call him -- Chris, very clear and helpful. He is an attractive gentleman with a delicious moustache. Beware!
Great prof
Very vague about assignments... erratic grading... not helpful when it came to asking questions. Really was surprised to find such a prof at NYU.
terrible teacher, treats you like you are in kindergarten and grades as if you are writers for the New Yorker... not helpful at all... avoid avoid avoid...

One of the best profs I've had at NYU. had him for topics in modern culture (middlesexes).  the class was all reading interesting books and watching interesting movies.  workload wasn't bad.  3 essays. great class discussions.  would take him again in a heartbeat!

Packard tries hard to make you a better writer, but most of his day-to-day assignments are absurdly vague, leaving you with no sense of direction. He doesn't seem to be a hard grader - I haven't met anyone yet who has gotten lower than a B on a paper. He's very nice and very chill, but the vagueness of his instructions drove me insane.
Excellent teacher, don't know why people bash him. He helped so much and his work load is manageable. Highly recommended.
this teacher is bogus! his instructions are vague and his grades are based on bs standards... he judges on how much he likes u, not on the writing! avoid!
I don't know what people are bashing him for, I got an easy A in his class.  If you put in any effort (not that much) you'll get an A.  He wants you to do well
do NOT take him... worst teacher I've had at NYU yet, and I hope ever.

Despite the fact that Packard was vague and awkward, I learned a lot from this class.  He does really push you as a writer, even though most of the time you'll have no idea where he's pushing you.  I'm sure there are much better GSP writing teachers

Packard is great. He really wants the students to do well on essays. He always writes very lengthy and helpful comments on rough drafts. You do have to work hard, but he is very helpful at getting you there!

do not, really i mean it, do not even think of taking this class or any class that has chris packard teaching it.  this guy has absolutely no idea what so ever as to what he is doing, and he has no idea how he grades.  i think he is lost in his own head.  trust me, save yourself so much time and work, take any one else but him!!!
avoid at all cost! worst prose comp teacher!
just don't!!!!!! most people who took his class this semester regretted it!! very unclear about expectations, you never know what to do.

STAY AWAY! worst teacher ever! even after an entire semester nobody in my class knows what it is that prof packard expects from students. he is extremely vague about his expectations and his essay topics are extremely boring. the workload is insane, much more than in any other prose comp II class. seriously, stay away! worst class ever!

This prof always makes him available and accepts your drafts whenever and gives you feedback asap. The reason why people hate him is because he actually teaches and expects a lot from gsp students who arent really at the level. I had a bad grade in his class but learned a lot. v.fair teacher.
just avoid...you have to write a lot of long and uninteresting papers. the professor is never clear about what he expects from you, in general everything just seems very vague in this class.
He has very high expectations

I wish someone had written what I'm about to write now and had spared me all the trauma I went through this last semester.  At first he seems harmless and then the beast unleashes and gets you when you're off guard. He's extremely unclear (if only you knew) and makes it hell for those he doesn't like. His class brings me down, stay away.

Chris is a really nice guy, he's just kind of absesnt-minded. He's super unclear with his instructions and essay prompts/topics, and they are really confusing. I don't think he even really knows what he wants. He's helpful, but it's never enough. No matter how hard you work, you'll probably only get a 'B.' I'd avoid him if possible.

Nice guy, makes himself available to help out. Doesn't lead class discussions well (or at all), picks favorites.  Doesn't seem all that creative re: non-gender studies related material, but his gender studies material is very good.
ehh. boring. has a bad memory. picks fav's. dresses weird. didn't learn anything from his class.
C.P. is nice, considerate and leads conversations well. Don't miss him.

I have never been compelled to write a review on here before, but as a senior I feel I need to leave future NYU students with this: TAKE JOEL DERFNER'S CLASS. I've never met anyone like him, especially not a professor. He is brilliant, so caring, and deeply, deeply himself. I wish I could take this again. He has greatly enhanced my NYU experience.
Joel is the best. Writing your life was one of the best classes I took in college :). The class environment he creates is safe. He is so funny and caring and your writing will noticeably improve.
Joel is the most caring and most entertaining professor I have ever had. He'll win you over with stories about his career and give you amazing feedback on your writing. His seminars are therapeutic.

The teaching was executed very poorly. Most of the classes consist of the professor (who is very nice) reading off python documentation for 3 hours straight. No one learns this way and at times I was losing my mind. However, by the end, I did feel well equipped to use Pandas library. But I would 100% skip this class and self teach instead.
PING PING DING IS THE GOAT
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is very kind and genuinely wants to see students do well. Yes, the course and exams are largely memorizing python library methods, it's a bit dry, but that's the course. The professor is very accessible outside of class and is very willing to help any student.

She does not care about her student. She has different criteria for everyone, some student will get a higher grade for the same answer as another student. Additionally, her lectures are very boring and bland, where she just reads of the board.

Took DMA with her in NYU Paris. Although she is a nice person, she cannot teach. It was like the listening to the Pandas documentation text-to-speech. No slides, no visuals, just Google collabs for notes, homework, and exams. Since exams are not open-note, you have to put a lot of effort in memorizing the syntax for SQL functions.

Taken her dma during summer. Definitely a good teacher, replies email fast, willing to have extra office hour. However, the course is 2.5 hours and 4 lectures every week, so pretty intense since you have to memorize all the codes for exams. She cares students, if you miss class, she will reach out to you though email and trying to help you succeed.

For CS-UH 1052G (algo), which wasn't listed on rmp:
She's very nice. Easier material than in NY but her explanations are nigh impossible to follow and to answer questions she repeats what she just said so you won't really learn. Four exams with HW due right before make it hard to learn from mistakes. Check your exams for significant grading errors.
She does not know how to teach. Learnt nothing.

Many codes and method needs to be remembered. Takes time after course. But she is willing to help you outside the course and grade leniently.
But it just takes so much time on remembering methods for exams, which is pretty boring.
Awful classes with many Python library knowledge which you could learn from Python website documents. The tests are heavily memorizing about all kinds of Python library commands.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had a terrible experience with her. She rarely respects her students and is also terrible at explaining complicated concepts. She also treated some people differently based on their appearances (iykwim)---- you know where the good ratings are coming from
Lectures were really boring and monotone but she grades leniently especially compared to other cs profs.

In the beginning her class did seem organised but close to the midterms we started discussing concepts such as permutation and combinations and as much as she loves to teach this, she sucks at explaining it or understanding students questions.(When I found inconsistent grading with my final she intentionally reduced points to offset the increase:))
Professor Ding might not be the best lecturer, but she is very kind and helping. The course is fairly easy, and she often gives extra credit.
She always gives good grades. While she doesn't mandate attendance, she does ask questions to see if you're there, which adds to class interaction.
Good

The course itself has a certain degree of difficulty, but the grading is relatively loose, there are not many homework, and the exam questions are difficult, but the teacher will only deduct a few points. The teacher's teaching level is relatively high, and she explains the problem-solving method in detail.

The Best Professor. Dominates most econ professors regarding teaching, difficulty of material, and caring about student. Super genuine and accessible outside of class. Dont believe comments about "cannot explain things clearly", basically for hard materials like game theory, if you cannot understand Dilip's explanation, just quit any advanced Econ.

Dilip is one of my favorite professors at NYU. He is truly caring and is extremely good at teaching. Besides being a fabulous teacher, Dilip is a highly-respected economist. Taking his class is such a once in a lifetime opportunity that gives me some taste of what microeconomics really is. I admire Dilip's research so much!

Game theory was interesting but v hard, prob wouldn't recommend unless you're rly interested or want a challenge. Got a 60% in the class and ended up w a B+ (somehow). Prof is knowledgable and happy to explain things in OH but the class gets technical with definitions and lectures can be confusing. Take it only if you're willing to put in the work.
Probably the best, in terms of teaching.

No need pointing out avg.55 to suggesting the prof isn't fair with grade. The final grade's really just about how you stack up with the rest of the class. Heads up, a 70 can actually land you an A range. It's all about the class curve, not just the raw points you rack up. Maybe take a sec to reflect on how many lecture/recitation\OH you've skipped.

Cannot explain clearly about classwork. 
Very hard exams and homework. 
Sample exams are not trustful
Average of one midterm is 55 score
hard understanding of slides
Very boring and slow speaking class

Prof Abreu is one of the pioneers in contemporary game theory. Intuitive content at the beginning but will get much tougher, but he is patient to explain repeatedly. Assignments are challenging but helpful, but exams are easier with a generous curve. However, I don't recommend taking it without solid calculus and probability theory knowledge.

He is passionate and insightful about game theory and is very patient when answering questions. Homework can get really tough but exams are easier with a generous curve. However, I wouldn't recommend the course if you are not into game theory or don't have a solid understanding of micro theory and calculus.
Challenging course materials, hard homework and exams, but he is willing to repeatedly explain during lectures and office hours. Also a generous curve up at the end.

Difficult in terms of the material, but he's willing to repeatedly explain things in class and in office hours. He's patient when you don't understand things. It can be hard to teach yourself the slides without explanation or examples, so definitely come to class. Exams are curved generously and not as hard as the problem sets
unless you're either very smart or very interested in game theory, i would avoid this class... extremely difficult material + difficult to follow slides, and he is not good at explaining it
He is so so, nothing earth-shattering. Wish him luck

Amazing. Material is extremely difficult, but he knows this and encourages questions and office hours visits, even if you ask the same question 15 times. He's extremely intelligent and passionate about the subject, and he genuinely cares about inspiring his students. Problems sets are impossible. Tests are fair (and curved). He's seriously awesome.
Best prof in NYU SPS.

Prof Salvato is the best!! We had so many interesting site visits of exciting brands and cool guest speakers. He is one of the most understanding, respectful, and kind professors I have had. He truly cares about his students and puts effort into creating a comfortable class environment. I highly recommend him to all!!

Great person and professor. Thoroughly enjoyed the course. Took Stats for Business Control and Regression previously - made the first portion of the course easier to understand. Theories are simply - basic stats. Homeworks can be time consuming and on the harder side - but are excellent practice for the exams. Highly recommend
take this class. so chill and easy.

Best professor in the poli sci department! Super interesting and informative lectures. The instructions and slides are clear and easy to understand. The wording on the exams can be a little ambiguous and confusing, and the grading is a bit strict, but as long as you understand the material, the exams should be easy.
Prof. Egan gives great lectures and he is very nice in person. His content about R and statistics is really helping non-math and cs students to learn. Put efforts and Learn hard for his exams.
3 Tests and 5 HWs. Only the 3 highest grades for your HWs count.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Egan is by far one of the best professors in the politics department. I was hesitant in taking POL850 since I'm generally bad at math and coding but he did an amazing job of explaining concepts and did he not expect us to be experts in coding. The class is manageable, test heavy but it is open note. Take him, he loves his job and his field :)

Tough class for sure but the professor made otherwise pretty boring stuff into actually a very fun class. experiences with the class vary a lot based on what i heard from other people, i guess i got a good one.

Prof Egan is so wonderful. I truly knew nothing about anything statistics or computers but he broke things down so well. He really wants you to understand and will do anything he can to help. He is also so funny and kind! If you have POLUA850 as a major requirement and are super humanities-oriented do not be scared :)

content of class was boring and exams were tough but professor egan was genuinely really interested in us succeeding and he was so passionate about the subject which made the class more enjoyable. Explains everything very well and I would barely feel lost in his lectures.

tests are open note, only 3/5 homeworks are graded. attendance is not required but i suggest attending to catch the tips and tricks he gives during class. recitation attendance also isn't mandatory but for homework help it's great, tests are like the homeworks

excellent lecturer who manages to break down difficult concepts. homework is not difficult and you are allowed to collaborate. exams are also open note (with no limit on how many notes you can bring) which makes them even easier. recitation was not mandatory attendance either, and it was mostly focused on homework help.

Very knowledgable - makes coding much easier for people with no experience. Speaks straight off slides and posts them, so lectures aren't that mandatory. Recitation is just extra practice, so not necessary either. Exams all open-note (no tech allowed) and not too difficult as long as you understand the broad concepts. Basic statistics thru coding

Professor Egan is one of the best politics professors I've had so far. He is very accessible through office hours, and is very straightforward when it comes to his explanations. The textbook is not necessarily requires, but he does teach from it. Everything that you need to know comes from his slides and lecture. He makes coding less stressful.
might be the most well organized class i've ever taken. structure makes it that coding is very easy, even for beginners. makes very difficult topics easy to understand.
Professor Egan is an excellent professor. He simplifies complex topics and makes a difficult class about research methods very approachable for someone who has never done coding before.

Professor Egan is my favorite. He is extremely helpful, always available outside class, and very kind. I had him for two classes and would definitely recommend him for POL850 and his other electives. The classes aren't necessarily easy, but you always have the resources you need to do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: i love this guy. he is so so inspirational and caring and truly wants us all to learn and succeed. slides are amazing, comprehensive and easy to understand if you stare at them for long enough. however, tests are super hard since open note and the TAs were evil at times. but prof egan is THE BEST !

Professor Egan is super nice and lectures are great. He always posts the slide right after class and that's all you need for homework and open-note exams. However, the class in general is a logistical nightmare. Feedback on everything is released weeks after the due date. The recitations are USELESS even though they encourage us to attend.

Overall good introduction to R and statistics in politics. Professor was engaging but often came late to class. TAs were also helpful in answering questions but recitations were way harder than the scope of the class. Five homeworks with the lowest grade dropped, which was nice. Exam questions seemed to be worded in an intentionally confusing way.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Maybe my favorite professor I've had. He's so nice and is an engaging speaker. He has really cool dad vibes. The class is pretty straightforward. You can work with partners on HW, open notes tests, and plenty of resources to help you. I was scared to take POL850 but he made it fun & welcoming. I 100% would recommend and would take his class again

Professor Egan is great and I've taken him twice now! Relevant to the world of politics now with also a good basis in history, lectures are informative and engaging. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you get points for participation. Would highly recommend!

I took Prof. Egan's class, US Politics and Policy in 2022 and Beyond, on a whim and I am so glad I did. It was a great course and very relevant. Despite it being four hours a day, five days a week, I felt that the course was engaging. This was thanks to the sheer volume of truly impressive guest speakers Prof. Egan secured. Overall, solid prof.

Professor Egan is amazing. I took Politics and Policy in 2021 and Beyond during January term. We had different guest speakers almost every day. His lectures were very relevant and engaging. He brought in a variety of different perspectives from all different areas of policy. If you have the chance to take any of his classes, do it.

Prof. Egan knows his stuff and seems to enjoy teaching as much as he does research. There's a fair bit of work involved in his class, but lectures are informative and fully prepare you for exams and assignments. Great coursea highlight of my semester.

Good professor. Nice guy, too. Exams can be difficult because they are very specific and you lose points if you dont explain it exactly how he wants it. The pop quizzes are just his way of taking attendance because everyone gets full credit. Dont skip lecture. Study your notes carefully and make sure you understand the material, not memorize it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very dense and boring, completely read off slides, and hard to retain. TAs were not helpful whatsoever. Attended every lecture and recitation , met with him outside of class and still struggled. Midterm and final were ridiculously challenging. Harsh grader, criteria is not clear, he comes off as wanting to help, but wasn't helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Egan's lectures are so informative without being dull and monotonous. You HAVE to go to lectures and recitation though because not everything is on the slides and recitation covers completely different material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's a great professor but even if you know what is going on in lecture as long as you can't articulate it EXACTLY the way they want you to you'll fail the exams. His testing doesn't account for the fact that every student learns differently. If you are a bad test taker and do better in writing assignment this class should be avoided at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a pretty good professor. Definitely attend lecture because the material isn't hard, but it can be confusing from just reading it off of the slides and he does give random pop quizzes (really an attendance check because everyone who takes it gets a 100). The readings will definitely help, but aren't necessary. Exams are pretty hard IMO.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Took his course "Power and Politics in America" in my freshman year. His lectures are/were amazing, he really got me into politics. I stopped working and reading in the middle of the semester because of a variety of issues, and I fully regret it. Would take this course an infinite number of times if possible.

Pat is great. Lectures were usually very interesting. Barely did any of the reading and did fine. Three tests total. As long as you attend class and recitation, tests aren't too bad, although many students had trouble finishing before time was up because there was a lot of material. He gives occasional "pop quizzes" just to check attendance.
Great teacher, very relatable. Tests cover a lot of material, study guides provided

Prof. Egan was one of my favorite politics professors. His lectures are super clear and he's always prepared. The class was insanely interesting and I learned a ton. His tests are hard, but if you go to lecture and pay attention, you can do fine.  He's a great professor and I would take his classes again for sure.
He's the man. Amazing lecturer. Tests were graded a little harshly, but overall great Prof.
Egan and the class itself were clear and informative. Would recommend.

Professor Egan is the best. He is enthusiastic, eloquent and very engaging. All concepts are explained with tremendous clarity and exams are not too hard. One of the most attractive professors at NYU too;)

Egan was clear in his lectures and was very organized. The tests aren't hard, and he curves the grades. However, he(or the TA's?)get picky if you don't word your answer exactly as he wants it. Plenty of readings, but they're easy, and are brought up in lectures. Overall, he was a good Professor, and the class was very interesting.

Egan is the best professor anyone could every ask for.He's super clear, super competent at explaining what will both be on the test and the supplementary materials.He's so organized, posts all the slides, has many office hours and is really accommodating to his students. To top it all off, he's actually a really nice person.Take his class, for sure
Egan's awesome. The tests aren't that bad, aside from the fill in the blank which you can usually infer as long as you study the powerpoints. He's an awesome lecturer and really knows his stuff

He's a fair professor that truly cares about his students.  For majority of his tests you can just know models and read the slides and that would get you a C in his class.  I would totally recommend him for anyone interest in politics.  Great Professor!!
He's very knowledgable and class is incredibly enjoyable! I looked forward to it! The tests aren't difficult if you study the lecture slides and do most of the reading. Highly recommend him!

Professor Egan is amazing in every sense of the word. He really knows his stuff and he really wants his students to learn. While I found the mandatory attendance a bit stiffing, I do admit Egan really cares about his students. If you can, take him. YOU WILL GET YOUR MONEY'S WORTH! One of NYU'S BEST!

Seriously, the "high school" comment is  accurate. He completely stifled any interesting discussion and participation while subjecting us to tedious exams and readings. Thanks, Egan, I'm not a Politics major anymore - but in retrospect, it's all for the best! Peaceee.

OK, so he's a nice guy. I tried to like this class, I really did. But I couldn't help but feel like I was trapped in high school during lecture. There is no discussion among students. The material is pretty basic and abstract. But the exams are pointless and needlessly tricky--really, "fill in the blank" and true/false questions on a college exam?
I really hated this guy.

Class is easy, and the material isn't hard to understand. However, the exam grading is ridiculous and you probably won't get an A even if you understand the concepts because of how you word your answers or because you don't answer the way they want you to. If you've taken other politics classes, you probably won't learn anything new.
Very Funny/Interesting. The reading is heavy, but tests focus more on political concepts than history or the reading. Very clear, organized. Overall- Great.
Great teacher. Great Slides. Very engaging lectures. He really loves stats, so be prepared for that. But he makes it interesting. Lots of reading but not necessary to read everything. Fair grader.

Very interested in what he does, keeps students engaged, pleasure to be in his class. Very responsive to questions - clear explanations. Posts slides, which are useful if you miss class. Lots of readings, not necessary to do all of them for a good grade, but an A is hard to get without them. Overall, GREAT professor.
Prof. Egan is very engaging and his lectures are interesting, organized and thought-provoking. Grading can be tough, but the class itself was nonetheless enjoyable.
Prof. Egan is very engaging and his lectures are interesting, organized and thought-provoking. Grading can be tough, but the class itself was nonetheless enjoyable.

PPA was not my favorite class but Professor Egan made it interesting - he's a very good lecturer. In spite of the fact that he assigns way too much reading, you don't really need to do it. Grading is fair but surprisingly not as easy as you'd guess. Overall, great professor.

The material seemed easy to grasp and understand, but when it came to testing, all comforts went out the window.  TA's weren't very helpful nor really that clarifying.  I regret becoming a poly sci major after taking this class.  Reading was top heavy and redundant.  This is a class where you think you understand, but really have no idea.

Prof Egan is interesting and keeps class semi-worth going. The test are pretty impossible.. between the amount of time and the particular answers he is looking for. The amount of reading is also unrealistic. Still, if you need to take PPA Egan is not the worse but an A is pretty hard to get.
Amazing Professor! Very articulate and always a pleasure to listen to.  He genuinely enjoys teaching and has an almost nerdy love for his subject, which makes for a great class.  Take him if you can!

Egan is one of the best profs I've ever had. BRILLIANT, very passionate about his subject, and funny to boot. His lectures are detailed but interesting; so enthralling I didn't need to take notes, I remembered everything! Curves grades on tests; is very reasonable re:grading. Readings can be dense, but lectures supplement well. Highly recommended!

He's a good lecturer... BUT thinks he's funny, when he's actually kind of annoying. Material is pretty basic, exams can be tough, but in the end grade will work out. (2 midterms, group project, final) Take it if youre looking for a non-challenging class/ easy grade.

Yes, he is a nice guy, engaging speaker, and very knowledgeable about politics in America. BUT, the exams are more like "The Statistics of American Politics" than procedure, history, etc. Most questions come from lecture notes posted on BB and not the 200pp per week of assigned reading. 2 midterms, a group project, and a final.
Great professor. He's very knowledgeable and interested in the subject matter. My only complaint is that he is consistently 10-20 minutes late to class.
Great professor, really fair in grading and assigning work.  Keeps classes interesting; he's a funny guy.
Great professor - well-organized, good speaker, funny, helpful

His mannerisms/self-deprecating humor reminded of Conan O'Brien. He posted all the notes because he genuinely wants his students to learn and succeed by actively engaging us in class instead of just reading off a slide. Grading was fair, and it seemed as if he and the grader were on the same page. I think he was especially lenient on the final.

Although I didn't care for the subject matter, he was a great professor. Good speaker and well prepared with comprehensive Power Points. Taking notes in class is almost unnecessary because he posts the notes on BlackBoard. Then again, it covers quite a bit, though it's not much work is needed because of his amazing notes.

I personally disagree with above statements. He is kind of full of himself and becomes very verbose, loving to hear himself speak. Though he's very engaged in the topic, sometimes ignores subjectivity or lack of substantial proof. However he's very "nice"
GREAT PROFESSOR! Very approachable and helpful! Classes were interesting and helpful for the exams, which were always fair. I would take another class with him in a heartbeat!
interesting and gorgeous!
He is a great professor. He really cares about the subject matter and wants to help his students learn above all else. One of the most interesting classes and one of the best professors at NYU.

I took Public Opinion and Pressure Pressure Groups this fall - he's one of the most enthusiastic profs I've had and is genuinely interested in the topics and helping students. VERY approachable in office hours, very willing to help with assignments. Classes were engaging and explained a lot of the reading subject matter.
will mess up your grades.
Content is easy. Lecture is no help. Exams are notoriously difficult.

Complains he cant write practice exam that is captures what the actual exam is like is that not the whole point of a practice exam is to gauge the progress??? u end up doing well on the overly easy practice, and do bad on real one. Ex wording is very difficult, harder than bio has ever been at NYU, so insanely unfair

Unorganized.although ProblemSets are supposed to be assigned in the beginning of the week and due by the end of the week he assigns them late and only gives and extra day.His lectures are mandatory for attendence yet they are useles when it comes to exam questions and the readings are too shallow for the actual exam yet take up so much time to do

you can tell he cares about the class, but not so much when he writes exams. the wording is convoluted, making it SOOO hard to get an even mediocre grade, I wish he cared as much on wording his tests better as he did for the overall class feel
