This class was filled with many concepts, and the exams were too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The tests are more based on reading comprehension than actual biology and are SM harder than the practice test he assigns on Codon. The median for the tests was often in the 70s, yet he would say good job and never share the mean. Lots of homework, ridiculous tests. Study hard.
you can really tell he is writing some of these, esp after someone writes a bad one

Yes, there's a lot of work in his classes, but you need to learn time management and truly work through his assignments and take advantage of his student hours. A lot of students fake attendance or use AI for assignments and he points out correlations between those behaviors & lower test grades rightfully. It's not easy, but getting an A is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: overwhelms you with an insane amount of work that is very difficult to keep up with. Exams are difficult with not good medians, yet says 'good job' — what? He thinks assigning an insane amount of work will help with the exam, but it's the opposite, it's so overwhelming. It's unfair how drastically different this year's bio is
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures are useIess, exams are often on something he barely mentioned. His questions are worded like MCAT problems. Better study with Campbell bio instead of going to his class, but note that his classes are mandatory and he gives some trick poll questions to see if students are ACTUALLY participating.

Yes, the tests are hard. But he preps us a LOT, so getting a good grade in the class is 100% doable. He's very approachable in office hours and obviously cares (even with 900 students!). POB is not the easiest class, but it's very fair and he gives us many drops and ways to raise our grades. Don't expect a free A, but work hard and you'll be okay.
His exams are way too hard like why is the practice exam so easy and then the actual exam so hard and worded difficulty. Also this is for bio 2 not 1
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Likely the only NYU entry-level STEM professor with any talent for teaching. Professor Plavskin obviously actually cares about TEACHING, rather than just caring about bio/chem/physics/calculus/etc. He really wants the class to do well, and seems especially focused on making sure the median student truly understands biology. Phenomenal instructor.
This professor is the best professor I have ever taken and it's very possible to succeed if you actually try and study
very nice but a lot of work outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very cruel man. He is nice to a very select few and can put on a very good persona. He belittles students in his email replies (if he even chooses to reply). You can get an A easily but beware his ego.

HE'S THE BEST! The coolest guy and a very fair and well respected teacher. The class is definitely challenging but it's a hard science class so it should be. His lectures and slides are very helpful and the online textbook/study platform he uses is great. Very fair policies like dropping one of three exam grades and option to not take the final.

Nastiest grader ever was .01% from a B- and wouldn't round my grade. Test are ridiculously hard for an intro bio class. Lecture information does not match exam questions and everything is application based. ALSO changed the final location and time last minute! You can tell this is his first time teaching... AVOID this class to keep your sanity.

Anyone rating this professor harshly just didn't study enough ngl he was fantastic and I learned so much from this course. The Codons were long but they really did help. You get what you give in this course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing professor. He really wants you to succeed! The class is difficult - the problem sets are really challenging and wordy, and the exams are ridiculous no matter how hard you study, but if you study enough you'll do okay! The homework, except for the weekly problem sets, is easy. Leave enough time for the problems sets every week!!!
nice guy blah blah blah. Exams are absolutely ridiculous and so hard for no reason. Is absolutely NOTHING like other older exams when it was taught by other professors

Professor Plavskin has clear guidelines outlined in the syllabus. There are a lot of assignments, but most of them are easy As if they are completed. He is very lenient with dropping assignments. Try and do well on the first three exams to avoid taking the final. He is open to listening to students and adjusting the course as requested.
Professor cares about students' learning- not your easiest A but definitely possible if you put in the work. Exams are difficult but lectures are great and super helpful in learning the content.

VERY different from reg & AP Bio (extremely lecture heavy). VERY content dense and requires lots of independent work (ULC, practice problems, reviewing lectures). hes passionate and reachable, but exam wording is often confusing and overcomplicated. grades aren't exam heavy, but expect to study a LOT. i spent 6 hours everyday studying for exams.

I had no prior bio experience but still did well because he drops the lowest few homeworks and lowest exam grade. He gives a decent amount of homework and the wording on the exams are confusing so you do have to work for it, but he cares about his students and cares about bio so he will help you (he won't round your grade tho, even if its 0.01 off)

Very good professor, super passionate about Biology. I took AP Bio in high school, so this class was less challenging for me. However, I did have to relearn certain things, as Plavskin dives much deeper into the topics than your typical high school bio teacher. He is also extremely fast paced, so make sure you keep up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The course is formatted in a way that is very easy to understand how to get the grade you wish to achieve. The course is pretty content heavy but manageable if you stay on track with the lessons and lectures. Try to miss out on as a little of the given points such as attendance as possible. Overall, very nice guy and knows Biology well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly, he's literally just good. He's very enthusiastic and loves teaching bio and clearly knows a lot and wants the best for his students. However, his tests are extremely difficult and require a least a day to truly understand one chapter in order to do good on the exam unless your like already familiar with the material.

His exams are extremely difficult and he sometimes include things we have not learned and you are expected to cues to know it. He is extremely petty when it comes to to rounding, an 84.9999 does not round to a 85, so don't even bother emailing and asking. He will ignore you.
ive never been so shocked. hes "nice and caring", only for some time... exams were absolutely insane. made absolutely no sense. theres no reason for exams to be so difficult beyond belief.
Very nice teacher who has great lectures. The exams are hard and require a lot of time and engagement with the material (and even then they're still difficult)

I didn't do good cause I procrastinated but you can just tell that the prof really cares about his students and their learning. Exam was fair and there are many components to grading that  each exam isn't worth too much. The course itself was harder than I thought although I took AP bio cause exam questions are not too straightforward

Professor Plavskin, while very kind and clearly passionate about the subject, writes incredibly challenging exams without providing adequate practice. In order to do well on the exams, you need to be consistently studying, not just studying a week beforehand. But, if you have to take this class, do not worry, you can succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't have any prior bio knowledge and still did well.  Make sure you actually understand what is happening in assignments (especially problem sets) because this class is way more than just memorization, and exam questions require deep thinking.  As for lectures, I thought they were really interesting and I learned a lot from this class!

He's a very kind person who puts a lot of effort into the course. There's a heavy workload through Codon, including pre-class assignments, weekly study path questions, and problem sets. While time-consuming, these can help boost your grade since exams are tough and reading-heavy. Attendance is required due to in-class and recitation polls.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Attendance polls sucked, took away time from actually learning new material. His exams are mazes of word problems, but if you have strong reading skills you can get by without knowing too much bio lol. Nice that he recognized confusing problems and gave back points, responds quickly and actually listens to your concerns. Not an easy A by any means.

While some aspects of the class are straightforward, the exams are a different story. If on each exam the class average (from 600 students) is between 65 and 75 every time, that says something about the professor's teaching and exam structure rather than the students' knowledge. Exams are unnecessarily difficult. Don't take him if you don't have to

Wonderful professor! Very kind and very responsive with emails. He is very passionate about his work, and he's very supportive and accommodating. The tests are pretty hard, but he provides lots of opportunities to do better and to improve. Thank you, Professor Plavskin!

He is passionate, caring, and genuinely wants you to succeed. You will learn a lot of fascinating information about biology and will come out knowing a LOT more about the material. With that being said, his exams are challenging and I believe they are harder than what is expected in an intro level course. Be prepared to study and put in effort.

this was his first year teaching PoB I and it showed. He's nice but he forgets that many of the students in his class don't have prior biology knowledge (A.K.A. not great at explaining harder topics). That being said, he is a very generous grader and super lenient about dropping exams and homework which was nice!
After talking his class I want to change my major

I loved Professor Plavskin! He is good at teaching and gives students so much wiggle room since so many assignments get dropped. Yes, the tests are hard, and questions can be super niche, but it is NOT impossible. I haven't taken a bio class since my freshman year of high school, and I did well in the class.

His exams are pretty bad because he asks a load of useless information to test whether you analyzed his 500 hard to understand/overwhelmed with bad diagrams slides. Syllabus policies were loosely followed (ifykyk). Let's be honest, the good reviews are because he's a man... If this were a female professor, there'd be review bombing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took in 2023. Definitely a challenging course, but looking back, definitely a good course. Keep up with the homework, show up prepared, and ask questions. He gladly made time to explain things to me over and over. Make the most of this course, because it prepares you well for research and advanced Biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had no bio background and I could've earned an A if I locked in. the exams are hard. possible to get an A if you really try. Very content heavy but not a huge workload. He's a good professor. if a questions on an exam, a very similar question came up in class/tutorial/codon/problem set. No surprises. drops tons of hw + 1 exam. POB 2 next!

He responds to emails fast and well, and his lectures are almost always very interesting. However, the exams are so difficult in conceptual understanding (ie, many scenarios) and unclear in wording. His lectures require polls, and he always makes them go too fast. I would only take this class if you are already REALLY into biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: POB1 is harder than the average intro class.. but an A is NOT impossible. He drops a lot of grades, gives points back when there's confusing questions on the exam, he's accessible via virtual and in-person student hours, he records and uploads lectures, his accommodation policies are clear-cut, etc etc. it's a VERY structured class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: some ppl are reviewing him without considering how insanely difficult his exams are... its great that yall are getting it but so many dont, not because the material is hard but because he cant word anything properly. theres always a mistake and it feels like a maze to get to the correct answer.

He is very passionate about Biology but his exams will take you OUT. Theres no reason the exams have to be this hard. I've poured everything into this class and still have yet to succeed... Its draining

Guys. He's a good professor and all I think that he is very smart and knowledgable but his exams are so hard just get ready to cry a bit and deffently study in advance :). This class is for sure a very advance biology class and Im sure they made it hard so they can wed out some students because again there were a lot of people in this class.
He has so many drops which make it easier for students to get a good grade!

He seems intimidating but is really caring and passionate. Fought for my life on exams but he gives plenty of resources to study, has office hours twice a week, and pretty fair in terms of grade impact. People have cheated on exams so it's understandable why he is strict for them. Never taken AP bio but passed--he's strict, but fair. Kind too!

Was WAY harder than I expected it to be, but with enough practice (like a lot) you should do fine in this course. The professor cares about his students, but tests tend to be harder than what's offered as practice. (I also have no past bio experience so I'm not biassed and it IS possible to excel in this course without prior knowledge)

This class was far more difficult than I expected, and I'm unsure how someone with limited biology experience can excel in this course. However, Professor Plavskin is incredibly caring, understanding, and passionate, and he was a great professor. 
His exams are not easy, and the course feels unnecessarily difficult for an intro to bio class.

It seems to be that the ratings are heavily skewed. Those who are getting A's have a huge superiority complex over those who are struggling. (By the way if that's the case,  develop compassion and empathy for the fact that not everyone learns at the same pace.). Admit that his exams are too tough for an Intro to Bio course and get over yourselves.
People should not be complaining this much. Prof Plavskin grading criteria was really clear and his exam were easy as long as you watched the lectures.

He's a very enthusiastic professor-- most people here complain about the exams, but the exams are pretty standard as far as college-level exams go (and his test prep problems are really similar to the exam). He gives many assignments outside of the exams that boost your grade, so you can get a good grade if you do the bare minimum.

Guys we are so creative here 🤣. 
Prof. Plavskin is definitely one of the best during my four years of college life. The syllabus is cleverly weighted, so just completing all the homework and get medium in exams can guarantee you a A-!
Difficult exams. A lot of content covered in the course as well. You do need a strong foundation in biology in order to really succeed in this course.

exams are 50% of your grade and the wording could not be any more challenging. i feel like he expects us to know how to read more than how to know biology. hes very nice and cares about biology but doesnt care enough to word his tests appropriately
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His exams? As a freshman, theyre NOT for freshman. They are worded SO BAD and make absolutely no sense... and theres no curve! so if you get a 79.99999 he will give you a C+ its so ridiculous, if his exams werent a mouse trap and a maze maybe students would actually excell in this cource...

Tests aren't too bad as the other reviews say. Just solve problem sets and watch lecture notes and you should be fine. Very passionate and generous professor, often gives dropped assignments and bonus points.

exams were hardish, but similar to tutorials/problemsets, so manageable if you study! anyhow, i do not tolerate plavskin slander! he's a great professor, super passionate, and his way of teaching is super compelling and makes you properly think rather than just memorize. if you're pre-med and complaining about him, reevaluate your career options...
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a professor, he is really passionate about what he does. The Codon pre-class readings, Study Path, Flash HWs, and Problem Sets are all super helpful. The exams are pretty difficult, but I do think it's essential because they get you to think rather than memorize. Some of the questions can be super nitpicky, but the tests are totally doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: his exams... good god. they are in no way intro level.

Best prof ever. Highly structured class with curated, paced pre-class assignments, problem sets, and practice questions. Not hard to succeed if you keep up with content and adapt your learning strategy.
Genuinely cares about our scientific thinking, growth, and the bigger picture in addition to content. 
10/10 would take a million times again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Eugene is a very caring professor who clearly wants u to succeed in the class. He records his lectures and balances the grades so that you have some wiggle room for doing badly on the exams. With that being said, you need to engage very well with the material on the exams if you want to do well. The exams are very very difficult!! Study ahead!!!

He definitely cares about the subject. Going to lectures is pretty essential, but sometimes he rambles about unnecessary information for the exam. However, I would say he is kind enough to post his recorded lectures if you miss any. His exams are hard, ngl. You should definitely study at least a week in advance if you want an A (for most people).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice guy but his exams are evil. Lectures are not engaging and contain so much information that he rambles on and on about. Makes POB much harder than it should be and his exams test you more reading comprehension than it does the material.
exam questions are pulled straight from hell

Guys I fear we are losing the plot. This class (and the exams!) are objectively not difficult. Plavskin's lectures cover everything that he tests on, you just need to take a little bit of time to go over it and think logically. That's literally it. He's also very nice, clearly very knowledgeable, and is accessible to ask questions.
Great professor who is obviously engaged with the material, interesting lectures and exams can be a bit tough but are pretty fair if you study enough.
i dont know how to put this into words, but get ready to cry. never thought orgo could be easier than POB

this is insanity. he will teach u like youre in elementary, and then exam u like ur albert einstein. he will respond to emails, but dont be fooled by his "niceness" because once u walk into that exam room, just know youre DOOMED.

Horrible exams do not reflect the difficulty of the things taught. Very disorganized with his lessons, which makes it hard to follow him. Makes intro-level material more difficult than it needs to be. Nice when asking questions, but be prepared to put in a lot of work. Every time you walk into an exam, get ready to enter the tarantula hawk!!!!!!!
interesting man to say the least
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He needs to chill out
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Plavskin is very caring and he really cares about making sure people understand the material. However, even if you understand the material the exams are very difficult. But he does drop a lot of assignments and one exam so it kind of balances out. You just have to put in a decent amount of work. Just do the Codon assignments and you'll be okay

I have no clue why Prof. Plavskin's rating is low. He is AMAZING. He is very caring for his students and wants everyone to understand the material. He is incredibly passionate about biology, and will answer any question with no judgement. The exams are tough, but if you understand the material you can absolutely get an A.

this class is straight from hell. The exams are so difficult compared to the previous POBI professor - they are beginner graduate level and make you think outside of the box which is helpful but his material is not enough to cover all that.
Midterms are hard. They cover materials that you do not see anywhere in the class. He's a chill professor, but his tests are just brutal. That's it.

What he teaches in class and what he assigns for homework does not help with the exams at all. Exams the problem sets are tough. The problem sets have strict grading, but the exams grading aren't as strict. The topics are hard to understand because he overloads you with many different topics that shouldn't be taught in first year biology,
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about what hes teaching and it is obvious to tell he is passionate about it (which makes attending lecture nice). 50% of our grade is attendance, homework, and pre-class assignments, and the rest are 4 exams (lowest gets dropped).Only thing is that the exams are hard (questions aren't things we've seen before).

Honestly not bad as a professor, but his midterms seem so different from actual content. Make sure you really understand the class content as the tests are lowk worded differently. His codon prepares you for lecture but he covers so much more in lecture so actually pay attention. You do have a loaded week with this class but it can be manageable.

i personally think his usage of codon is really helpful and he's always been very accommodating and helpful when providing resources and guiding you towards the right answer. very nice guy in general and anyone who thinks he sucks just has a pea brain and i hope to god they never become a doctor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Guy is hella chill these bad ratings aren't indicative of him. 50% of the grading is literally homework and easy assignments. The other 50% is exams and one is dropped. So long as you put the work in and listen to him(not cramming the week before the exam but actually doing codon over time) you're chilling

Good luck, the midterms have nothing to do with what you are learning in class. I would say that he is a good teacher and very smart he just isn't teaching the right way for you to succeed in this class. I would say you really have to work hard in this class and cry a little bit.
Awful exams with no resources given, and he will make you hate bio.

A great prof who cares for students and is very passionate. He provides helpful resources and gives back a few points for questions that most of the class got wrong. His exams are way too hard for an introductory class. There's 3 midterms and a final, you can drop one. It's doable, but be prepared to study LOTS on top of your other work (esp GCI)

Professor Plavskin is an AMAZING and WONDERFUL educator and I mean it! His lectures are very very interesting, very clear grading criteria. There are a few short assignments and a problem set (a little bit challenging) due each week. The class is very well organized and very well planned. He knows what he does. Amazing person!
Amazing professor! I never cared about science or bio before, but his class made me super interested in the subject and want to pursue it more!

One of the BEST professors in NYU. He's caring and very clear about what you should expect on exams. Just pay attention in class, study outside a bit, and utilize the resources he gives you and there's no way you'll get anything lower than a A- or B+.

Very caring and passionate professor with decently fair exams if you actually put forth an effort to study. I didn't take any previous AP science courses, and still succeeded. The online learning tool Codon is super helpful, and Plavskin utilizes it beneficially. Problem sets (homework) are harder than the actual exams and kinda unhelpful/useless.

Passionate about biology and clearly knows his stuff, but that passion doesnt translate to effective teaching. Doesn't teach in a way everyone understands. He spends too much time talking about his biokogy hobbies instead of exam material. His tests feel like grad-level exams. Slow to respond too. Take AP Bio or another bio class first for B+ min.

It's literally so hard. He's actually nice and very passionate about biology but he expects you to have prior knowledge about chemistry and I have none so I'm struggling it's just a lot of work and a lot of studying on your own time!

his midterms are soooooo difficult
there are molecular bio and developmental bio questions in pob 1
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
hey eugene plavskin 
whats going on???
great professor, cares a lot about his students and breaks topics down very simply and clearly puts a lot of effort into content both in and out of class
Difficult Exams and Content heavy lectures with high expectations

This course is hard. It is dense with material and the homework assignments take a long time. Dr. Plavskin is incredibly enthusiastic about his course and it shows in his teaching. His office hours were many hours long, and he stayed until the last student left. If you are willing to put in effort to learn difficult concepts, I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very difficult class.Coding assignments are useless,exams are difficult,TA was not helpful.Eugene is great however it is clear he purposely makes the class difficult since he knows bio majors are forced to take. Avoid if you dont want your GPA to tank.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! Stats Lab assignments are so useless and he makes the exams so difficult for no reason. If you're thinking about taking this to fulfill your bio elective... don't.

this rating should not be as high as it is, the number of false cheating accusations made has to be a world record and the "code" he uses to "catch" people is almost certainly nonsense The focus on R coding is totally useless to the majority pre-med class. He's charismatic, probably why his rating appears as good as it is, but its a trap. stay away

This class is dense in content and it will be quite difficult for you if you're not a biology major, especially if you are not familiar with the concepts of genetics. But trust me, you will learn a lot in this class even though it's heavy on stats + bio, and also coding in R, but it will be rewarding.

I learned so much in this class, and Professor Plavskin really knows what he is talking about. Although it is a lot of info and R assignments take a long time and can get draining, there are drops and both Professor Plavskin and the TAs set aside a lot of time outside of class to help students, please take advantage of it. Do every practice problem
Focus on his lecture material. R is difficult unless you go to recitation. Growth bonus is available
Eugene is an amazing prof! Cares a lot for his students and is very welcoming of questions. I had him for Biostats and ATB: Genetics and Genomics, and he was great for both. Take his classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Clear, concise lecturer that wants you to ask questions so you understand. Grade comes from R assignments, preclass quizzes before every lecture, 2 exams and a final. Exams aren't the easiest but are generally fair and based on quizzes and core concepts/problems went over in class. TAKE HIM FOR YOUR QUANTITATIVE REQUIREMENT BIO MAJORS!!

Lectures are easy to understand. And 45% of grading comes from R homework which is good (can ask for help and try ChatGPT :)) and bad (too heavy: each time about 300 lines of coding). Fair exams and give extra credit when needed (curve the exam reasonably). Caring and really accessible outside of class! Have great feedback for every HW.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I highly recommend this professor and his courses. He will teach his ideas and opinions very carefully. In this course, he will divide a paper into several paragraphs, and then let students show their own understanding and the logic shown in the paper. The assignment is a small paper twice a week. You only need to write one page of this paper.

You will find classes very enjoyable. Most classes have consisted of political discussions and debates on AI ethics. Really helps think through ideas in an engaging way. Projects are also engaging and well connected with real life issues. Definitely a more modern approach to teaching.

She's great!! Always allows us to express our opinions in class. I don't believe she is disorganized; she's been pretty understanding. Work-wise, it's not a lot, just readings and annotations, and a few essays sometimes, but they are pretty easy to do. Participation matters a lot; part of the grade is based on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Just Take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's okay. The class is often disorganized but very chill and somewhat laid back. She gives readings almost every class. Don't take her at 8:00am though, you will find yourself very annoyed. No exams, no midterm just a few papers across the semester (roughly 3-4 but every spaced out so it's not too bad).

The class is definitely laid back but I wouldn't consider it disorganized. It's definitely an easy A if you show you somewhat care about the pieces you're writing. Heiser is very caring and definitely wants you to do well

Heiser is a chill prof. 2 papers (one short and one 8-15 pages) and a presentation on the final paper. One page responses to some of the readings and discussion posts sometimes. Easy class based on discussion, so for a good grade you need to participate.
She was good prof. Wish she emailed earlier. Her grading criteria was very unclear. She was kind and understanding. She loves personal essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very easy class-- if you're already confident in your writing and want an easy A, I'd take it, otherwise I would go for another professor. There's a lot of small group discussions, but in general the class is very laidback. So long as you submit your essays on time you'll be fine!
Erin is nice and caring. But if you want your tuition to be worth the money, don't take her. Easy A, but only because her class is like a middle school English class.

Heiser is a great prof, easy A but her rubric is kinda hard to follow. She doesn't really "believe" in grades so its hard for her to outline what an A, A-, etc. looks like in her class. She is super nice, the only reason I wouldn't take again is bc during discussions she tends to put others opinions down if they don't align with hers

She's the GOAT, really. She's so nice and understanding of what college students go through and have to do that you will never feel overwhelmed by her. Her topics for essays are always interesting and she helps you A LOT. Highly recommend her, she will make writing class truly enjoyable and you will look forward to her class during the week, trust

Professor Heiser is by far the easiest Writing professor I have ever had in my life. If you are looking for an easy A, she should be your top choice. Don't get me wrong you won't learn anything, but the class is very easy.

This is an easy A, but it won't help your writing in the slightest. Readings are inconsequential to your grade, though online participation functions as less of a conversation with peers and more so just busywork. Essays offer you a little too much in the way of creative freedom, contributing to a general lack of clear grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: An excellent professor who cares for her student. Love her!!

Literally the worst professor Ive had in my college experience. Take her class if you want to waste your money. I learned nothing from her. Didnt help me improve my writing at all. Felt like a high school class for an NYU price.

I took her for both writing 1 and 2. She gives good feedback on your essays. and you can talk to her before the essay is due to see her opinions. It matters to talk in class and participate in group discussions. Also there is group workshop for every essay with 3 to 4 classmates. She prefers personal stories in your essay.

Wants people to participate but will ignore raised hands to tell her own personal stories and share her own opinions and take up half the discussion (not in a way that keeps the conversation going but in a way that distracts from the students ability to participate). Do NOT take her if you actually want to improve your writing. Not helpful at all.

I learned how to express myself through my writing and take risks, which previously I could never confidently do. Writing has become a possible profession for me, when at first, I hated it more than anything. Professor Heiser was open to meeting whenever we needed to, and gave comments that encouraged us to push ourselves.

Expect you to participate, but she talks about her personal feelings a lot and wonders why no one is discussing. Also, I have no idea how to meet her essay criteria. I try to meet her standard of good participation but still got poor participation grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class is mostly discussions based on the readings or whatever she feels like talking about. TBH showing up to class is very optional. Grade is composed of a few papers that she allows peer grading on. Reasonable grader.
take her
she was the easiest writing prof ever. She does not assign a lot of work though. show up, participate a bit in class, submit your hw and youll get an A

Easy class. simple. Professor hates assigning a lot of work because she's "busy' lol. But, hey, I didn't mind... you get 4 absences before u begin to be penalized. Not a tough grader, very nice. She is all about women's rights, to the extent that it gets annoying.
Erin's alright. I did not really find her feedback helpful.  She only gave 3 essays. She's kinda lazy.

She was often late to class and when she canceled class often she would notify the students at most a half hour before class is scheduled to begin which honestly is not enough time especially when you are a commuter and the train goes underground and you have no service or you have to leave your house an hour before class begins to be on time

Erin is a really nice professor & chose a lot of interesting topics for the class to look at. Her class is VERY discussion based, so the more outgoing you are, the better. Even though her class lacks some structure here and there, I would definitely recommend her for writing because her feedback is pretty motivating. Plus, she's a big Buffy fan.

She is truly an amazing and inspiring professor. The class is very low key and comfortable. It is discussion based and participation is very important. She is super helpful and the topics she choses for papers are actually interesting. A must have for writing I and II.

Let this example speak for itself: for an entire semester, the first thing that she lets us do in every class is a kindergarten-style "can someone tell me everyone's name in this class?" and we go around. But as of week 10 out of 14, she, herself, still doesn't remember the names of some of my peers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Has a lax grading system if you just submit everything (which isn't much) and show up, pretty much guaranteeing at least a B+. 

1-on-1 meetings are pretty nice. Clear she knows what she's talking about and wants to be constructive, but it really doesn't come through in class.

Had her for an early morning, but she often felt passive aggressive.

not AS BAD as the 1/5 comments claim, but she's definitely NOT a good professor in almost any way. like sure, you can get by pretty easily, just do your homework. but her personality... she treats you like INFANTS, and there's ZERO enthusiasm in class (she SOUNDS enthusiastic, but never successfully produces anything that's worth any enthusiasm).

She was my first writing professor, and I found her class quite engaging. Doesn't give you too much homework, but requests submission two days before your actual class. I found her quite interesting, even though the way she explains homework or an essay can be quite confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Don't understand the negative reviews. If she's confused by what you're saying in class/thinks it's shallow she'll question you on it, but she isn't passive aggressive at all, just honest and direct, and she's always respectful and cares about students (she even brings in food sometimes). All the in-class writing exercises were rlly helpful too.

She's quite hypocritical. Not a terrible choice like you'll be fine but if you can take someone else, do. Her instructions are weird but she's pretty hands off when it comes to essay writing. She's very strict about her attendance policy, but if you always show up you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Emily was nice but I was often confused by her class. She used Brian Eno's creativity cards to help us with ideas which was awesome. It felt like she hadn't made up her mind with how the class was going to be taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: God I hate this woman (and I got an A!). Unbelievably rude and snarky to students. Her class may be technically easy in the long-run but her instructions feel like deciphering ancient texts. Also, her essays somehow like aren't graded on the quality (mostly) so uhh it's really hard to want to put in the work to write something actually good.

She is definitely a strict grader, but I don't think she deliberately gives students a hard time. She is just really specific with what she wants. If you pay close attention and work hard on every assignment, you would find all the assignments manageable.

She is kind of bipolar but is very nice in the end. Her classes are fun and you can get an easy A if you submit the HW. She got us free movie tickets and brought donuts and different stuff to class. She might have favorites in class but you are never sure. I would take her again, personally I really enjoyed her classes despite some random moments.

Take this class if you want somewhat of an easy A but you will be miserable for the entire semester. She is very passive aggressive and gives confusing directions. I got low grades for every assignment but somehow I ended up with an A.

Runs class in a questionable way and has clear favorites. Only redeeming quality is the grading policy - it is basically impossible to fail as long as you go to most classes and turn in the assignments.

easiest class this semester, she had a fair grading system where everyone started with an 85 at the beginning of the semester and could increase their grades through bonus points from assignments etc. she credits students for trying their best which i appreciated a lot throughout the semester. would recommend taking her for an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An acquired taste. Very bipolar personality - one class she's fun then the next she's in a bad mood putting students on the spot. Lots of participation but never seems to like what we had to say. It was unclear what she liked to read so I never understood the grades I got on my essays. I didn't learn anything from her only my classmates tangents.

There are definitely times when it's questionable with how she runs the class or asks her questions to the class for discussion. However, she is a pretty fun teacher and she grew on me a lot by the end of the semester. Try hard on your assignments and you'll enjoy them better bc she gives a lot of freedom with your writing (encourages risks)
avoid her at all costs

she is the most cruel teacher I have ever taken, one time she said that I was the worst writing in the world by calling me a disgusting disgrace of a person who should never touch a pen or a keypad again. I feel so discouraged by writing, and as a former dramatic writing major at Tisch I feel sad to ever write again. I am now a sophomore in film.

Emily is definitely an acquired taste when it comes to whether or not you'll like her. She does have favorites and if you're not one of her favorites the class might not be as enjoyable. But the grading criteria is very clear and if you make the most out of it, it can be a relatively chill class. If u just do the work and you'll at least get a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Often shuts down the person in the class, doesn't like questions, and makes students seem like they are at fault for not understanding things. We do not learn much in class and discuss our assignments too much.

She comes off as nice (esp in the beginning) but became very irritable in moments and has a judgmental demeanor. She isn't too harsh of a grader in my opinion (EXCEPT WITH PARTICIPATION! I don't know anyone who got above a C in that). Her feedback on assignments and rough drafts is horrifically vague and unhelpful, and I don't feel I learned much.

AVOID HER CLASS. She is very unclear in her assignments and gives difficult, broad, and unhelpful feedback. She has a stringent attendance policy and is very curt and passive-aggressive with students she doesn't like. She gave me a C- in participation after only missing 2 classes over the whole semester and participating in ALL class discussions.
She is very kind as a person and a grader. Genuinely an interesting person who is honest and cares about what she teaches. I liked her a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She gives very confusing commentary that is often unclear and overall vague. She is overall a nice person, but doesn't connect with students on a real, meaningful level.

Emily is a great teacher. She is strict in classes. We read lots of materials in and after class. Attendance is required for her class. There will be homework after every class. But she really have great teaching content and clear feedback after every essay. Her goals are clear and if you fulfill all requirements, you get good score.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Emily's like a friend to us than a teacher. She's interesting and inspirational as a writer and teacher. Although her assignment description is sometimes vague, I can always reach out to her after class by email. She can always be the choice that opens the door of college writing for you.
She is kind. However, she gives vague and confused comment. And she normally did not provide unanimous comments on your work.

Emily is totally a great professor to take for international workshop 2. Because this is a small class. As long as you are willing to answer her question and communicate with her, you will get good grade.
Not as bad as other claims. If write all three essays, 100%B.

Emily was very clear in what she expected from students because she had clear grading criterion for each essay and explained them well in class. My writing skills improved a lot, because she structured her class in an organized and reasonable manner, presents useful skills to be applied in your essays, and gives very helpful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Stone always has a mindset that she is always right. She dismisses every single opinion as wrong before taking a look into your argument (especially in an editorial assignment). She always comments that our essays are not deep enough and judging by all the other people who rated this professor, this wasn't unique to me. very condescending.
Emily is nice and caring. But for the essays, it's hard to know what she likes and hopes to read. Lectures are good but not related to the essays.
You need to write in the way she likes in order to get a good grade. Also, I don't like the way she teaches. She treats you like a middle school student, which makes me feel stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Emily Stone clearly has her own "outstanding" understanding of how an essay should be structured. Yet whether this system of standards is truly objective or valuable is debatable. Apparently Stone knows that all her students are idiots that she has to pay efforts on. So a minimal B score would be the best gift she could give.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Emily was very friendly, but she can be a tough grader. Be ready for weekly assignments and to participate in class. The worst part was that she isn't great at giving feedback on drafts of essays so make sure that you ask the questions you want answers to.  The majority of your grade is based on 3 essays that you write, so keep up with work!

He's so chill the class is a bit long and was kinda late so it wasn't that good for my schedule besides that it was easy there's a lot of reading but no one ever read and the exams were easy one take home final and one midterm in class

Overall, I enjoyed the class! It was interesting, particularly for those interested in law/politics. Professor Gioia had an abundance of stories that, coupled with lectures, made it easy to stay engaged. I do wish the structure of the class was a bit more grounded, but I learned a lot, and there were quotes said that I will forever remember.

Clearly thinks he is above this class, usually does not provide feedback but when he does, it is harsh and he is not open to listening. Funny guy with  interesting stories, but still. We were graded off of three things, two of which we never got back. Syllabus wrong, readings barely mandatory, easy to get away with little work. Easy, but annoying.

Professor Gioia is a really really really impressive person and his lectures (more like storytime) are amazing. However, he's like entirely inaccessible outside of class (WILL NOT RESPOND TO EMAILS) and he made us buy like 6 books that we didn't use and now I'm just stuck with Abundance by Ezra Klein forever. Really wants you to think about it!

This class has a great opportunity to be amazing, but it feels like Prof. Gioia does not really have time for his students. He is definitely a well accomplished and smart guy, but he is so busy with other stuff that this class feels like an after thought. the syllabus is wrong, he is hard to reach, and does not know our names :( graded off 3 things

Very caring and driven professor / attorney / former city council member. The classes are scheduled for 150min but he lets you out 10-30min early, especially when we have movies to watch for homework.
You can also find almost all the required books at Bobst or the NYU library online database. Participation counts, and please answer his questions!!

Loved this class! It's really mind-opening and he poses questions about real-world policies that really get people contemplating. He does random cold calls so you gotta do the readings, but the class's graded only on the two exams and final project (all take-home). He brings up a lot of stories too, which are pretty interesting to hear about.

I loved this class as a FYSEM! I think it opens up your mind to thinking like a politician looking at real-world problems and being able to discuss them intellectually. This absolutely spiked my interest in public policy and really got me thinking about hard questions we need to think about. Side note: He will cold call so be prepared

Honestly he is one of the best professor I have ever had, his lectures were also very engaging and interesting. His assignments were all from the content of his lectures and I learned a lot. Plus he has very interesting anecdotes and is very knowledgeable about politics. A top notch scholar, Gioia is a great choice for a future professor.

Professor Gioia squarely fits the "prone to tangents professor" vibe. However, if you're interested in politics or public policy, those tangents will often be a joy to listen to. He's a very engaging professor, and everything said in lectures typically is relevant to class. Very open to changing assignments if needed. Great prof, would recommend.

His 2:30-long lectures are a drag, but Mr. Gioia tries to keep it lively with vids and anecdotes. He is very well-connected and will often tell stories of X politician or CEO, and he offers so much insight for someone interested in the field. Very little homework and commitment but you can learn a LOT by just listening in class and asking questions

There's literally no graded homework. Your two grades are the midterm and the final project. The readings are short and you can just skim over them without actually reading it. Gioia seems nice and likes to hear himself talk (a true politican). The class is interesting and relaxed, if a little boring occasionally. Overall, a definite GPA booster.

Gary rules. He's been in the NYC studio recording industry for decades. He's exactly the sort of person you'd want to learn analog recording from. You get out what you put in. He'll show you how to work any gear in the studio. Has lots of stories and opinions/guidance. Keep an open mind and learn what you can. I'm tired of these low effort reviews.
He is a very chill guy, though you pretty much have to learn everything yourself, but the work is easy. His stories are pretty interesting.
only thing i learned in here is where all the bathrooms in the steinhardt building are

bro this man yaps like there is no tomorrow. you will learn MAYBE one thing by the end of this class and that's being generous. if you want to learn? there's no chance of that in here. if you want an easy A? this is perfect for you!!!
Old school guy, very knowledgeable but you have to listen to weed through the babble to get to the good stuff. Enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

Though sometimes clueless, he does offer a lot of great insights into the recording business. I have to say the first few classes are hard to sit through, but when you get to know him, there is a lot of great pieces of little stories with a lesson in them; not the greatest teacher, but there's a lot to learn from him if you want to
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I've never written any rate my professor reviews, but I would do it for Gary. The most lovely professor I've ever met at NYU. He is the reason why I believe the educational system needs reform. He makes me wanna learn, and has hope to be someone that I would want to become in the future! Easy A. Don't listen to the hate comments lol so not true

Useless class. His style of lecturing involves him blabbering on about whatever he feels like talking about that day. Stuck in the past, topics mainly include things that may have been useful if you find yourself time traveling back to 1980. Waste of time and money, dont waste your time at NYU like I did with this class.

A fine man. But he opens mouth, I close my eyes. So many of things he put in the test are in the text book, which he barely mentions. Instead of sticking to a ppt or something, he just blabbering on about whatever he feels like. We have to figure out everything in studio by ourselves.

Amazing and informative lectures, which he incorporates hands-on learning to quite frequently. Very simple homework and recording projects, though tests can be a bit daunting. I've learned more from this professor than anyone else teaching Music Technology, strongly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Filadelfo is one of those professors who has no patience for academia and bureaucracy and just wants to impart his vast knowledge. He breaks things down fairly simply and is just a really fun dude. Highly recommend taking his class and his tests are very easy if you've been paying attention.

Gary's hilarious. He has a lot of experience and a lot of stories to tell. Explains the material very clearly and doesn't give out any crazy projects; doesn't make you buy any software/equipment either. Quizzes are pretty easy so long as you study. Really laid back guy; very accessible outside of class.

Awesome! Gary's lectures are amazing and he's willing to explain anything that you have any questions about. Hilarious guy, homework is easy, tests can be tricky but nothing too bad. Totally worth it for everything you will learn.

One of the best teachers I've ever had.  He has a very charismatic way about him that brings the subject matter into an incredible new dimension for his students.  His ability to aid students through the thought process of recording is unbelievable.  I learned more in this class than any other.  If you can take one of his classes, do it.

Gary is the man! I've never had a teacher before who could make the subject matter so interesting and thought provoking. Plus he knows how to inject some humor into lessons and make the students think through things in a logical manner. Highly recommended.
Doesn't teach ever and every single human being cheats on her tests - kids who don't study or come to class at all get As. Was probably the only kid that didn't cheat and got an A.

The worst teacher I have ever had. Impossible to follow her notes and lectures. Makes simple topics difficult for no reason. Is not available outside of class. Uses chat gpt to make exams. Exams make no sense compared to the notes and practice problems. Avoid if possible!

Literally run in the opposite direction. The lectures are impossibly hard to follow, she doesn't follow her own syllabus, she is not accessible outside class, the homeworks are ChatGPTd, and her notes literally make no sense. Worst professor I've ever had especially for a math class. Expected more from Stern.

Do not take this professor, lectures are not useful AT ALL. You will end up having to teach yourself all of the material. The class is very disorganized and she is not helpful at answering questions. Please take a different professor if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: she's a bad teacher. Does not teach. rely on yourself COMPLETELY. Boring lecture. Does not answer questions correctly. You have to teach yourself everything  genuinely.
She's not very good at teaching
This is the best professor I've met at NYU. She's very caring towards students, has excellent teaching quality, and is incredibly knowledgeable.
Basically, work on your own.

Please do not believe the positive reviews (I am pretty sure they are fake!). I did not miss a single lecture and still did not learn from her and had to self-study throughout the semester. Yes, I did get an A but it had nothing to do with her teaching. I took AP Statistics in high school and had to depend on the previous knowledge to get through.
You have to teach yourself.

Many many problems with her explanations, teaching materials, and the TA. Many errors were found in her slides, which she didn't even recognize as errors. Take her if you love skipping classes and learning on your own. Lectures are not useful at all.

Very bad at explaining things, unorganized lectures, and a lot of issues with her TA. I would definitely avoid her at all cost. I took AP Stat in high school (I already knew all the lecture materials), but she confused me so much that I got worse at Stat. Please avoid her. I'm being serious and I am usually happy with all the professors.

Good luck if you didn't take statistics before college. Her lectures communicate information terribly and she does not know how to answer simple questions. Exams are relatively easy but you need to do all the preparation and learning yourself. Final exam was ridiculously difficult and came out of nowhere in comparison to first two midterms.

Absolutely the worst professor I've ever had and I'm being generous. DO NOT TAKE PLEASE. Lectures are unintelligible even when I'm the only one paying attention. Heavy on notation she doesn't explain. Tests are not too hard except for the final. Laughable teaching skills.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

As a business major, I found STATS 103 incredibly useful. The course made stats feel practical, with clear examples from marketing, operations, and finance. Concepts were well-explained and tied directly to real data. I feel much more confident analyzing data and making business decisions. Highly recommend!
Super nice professor but wasn't always the best at explaining concepts. Tests are extremely hard but the class is curved so as long as you study relatively hard you'll be fine

Nice and simple class, I only study for two hours before the exam to complete an official "Cheat Sheet" (yes, you are allowed to bring summarized notes to attend the exam). Not much work to do and few assignments can be done in less than one hour for each of them. 
Overall a good choice if you can self-study, the hardest chapter was already removed
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very kind person, but not the best lecturer. Classes are often disorganized and she throws notation at you without adequately explaining anything. Final and midterms are very similar to the practices. HWs are easy and collaborative, but be aware of the pop quiz.

Super nice, but beware of these reviews. Lectures are confusing and notation-heavy, and she hesitates to complete sample problems. If you didn't take stats in high school, you will struggle. Attending class is no use. She writes equations on the board, copying the notes from a paper she holds. Tests and pop quizzes were easy until the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: oh boy oh boy where do i even begin. these other reviews are fake, don't listen to them. how someone can give her a 5/5 is ridiculous. she struggles to grasp basic concepts in statistics, much less teach them. i can honestly say I learned more about myself in this class than I did about statistics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No idea what is being taught in class. Only notation and no explanation. Do not take unless you want to learn everything by yourself
a
Organized and great lectures.
Prof. Chen is very willing to help students. She explains clearly.
Great!
Organized, easygoing , and attentive! I received outstanding grades in her class. While some exam questions might be challenging, they serve as bonuses for those who attend every lecture. :)
This professor is grading generosity, even when the material can be tough! A very kind professor.
Her organization and clarity make complex concepts easy to grasp.
Stats was surprisingly interesting. Prof made complex stuff make sense. Quizzes were hard but fair. Would take it again!
Prof. Chen's Stat 101 is fantastic! She's super clear, organized, and kind. Makes stats less scary. Highly recommend!

I took her class fall 22. If you don't know what to believe between really good and really bad reviews, go to albert and check feedback on her stats class from previous semesters. You will see that evaluation of her class is way lower than other professor for same 6-credit stats class. Also the TA was really bad at explaining concepts.

Her lectures are okay. Pretty much the exact same thing as covered in the "required" textbook. Very powerpoint karaoke. Her tests are all over the place, though. 1/3 of the class got a 100 on the midterm, while the (uncurved) final had an average grade of a D. The test itself didn't actually have enough info in the question to be possible to solve.

If you're not very intuitive or have not taken stats before you will not do well. She mainly reads off the slides and the proofs she tries to do in class are very confusing. The exams were not like the samples and the class average for both midterms was in the 60s. The really good reviews are very suspicious

The worst class I've ever taken. She explains concepts too deeply and confuses everyone. Her final exam was nothing like the sample. People were actually crying while giving it. DO NOT TAKE under any circumstance.
Professor Chen is very articulate and she explains concepts well. She is very nice too.

Hope you guys know what I mean, but those good reviews are VERY SUSPICIOUS. She basically reads off the slides, her pronounciation was hard to understand, and the final was nothing like the practice sets. I suggest people to take their stats class from different professor who actually tries to make their lecture interesting.
The lectures and review sessions are very helpful!  Professor Chen also takes great efforts to explain things in her office hours.  She is very caring and willing to take our feedbacks.

Great lectures! Professor Chen offers a lot of extra stuff beyond the textbook and slides to help us understand. The first midterm was challenging but I am glad I get a good score!  It really pays off to attend the lectures, especially the exam reviewer session.  :)

Professor Chen's lectures are great! She is very nice. 

The negative statements below are not true. Maybe they are rating a different professor. I took the class in Spring 2022. According to her syllabus, the minimal grade is C and no A-. She showed the statistics of the midterm scores in class and there is only one or two 100 scores.

Worst professor ever had. I largely suspect that the previous responses are all written by herself or by some bots. She literally just read from her slides all the time and reiterated the same concept every class for at least 40 minutes. She's not a good teacher. Tests, especially the final, were totally different than the assignments she gave us.

Professor Chen is caring for her students and explains problems very thoroughly. Some concepts are challenging but pay attention in lecture and you will do fine. If you have questions you can find her in office hours and she is patient and very much willing to help out and discuss concepts in depth. She's also responsive to student feedback.
Prof Chen is clear in her logic and her lectures are well-organized. Weekly homework can be challenging but are not too crazy. Exams are similar to practice ones but harder, but generously curved.
Professor Chen is great! She is articulated and explains concepts clearly. I learned a lot in this class.  Highly recommend her for 6 credit stats!

Professor Chen's class is amazing. I learned a lot from her. I took the 2-credit statistics class, so the content could get dry and repetitive sometimes, but she made her lectures very clear and easy to follow. The Stern curve made the class somewhat hard since everyone understood the content very well, but the class is still very doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is not an easy course and takes a lot of efforts, but Professor Chen is very clear on the materials. Everything is in the lecture notes. Well organized. She provides sample exams and emphasizes important concepts which are helpful for the exams.

Lectures are very well organized, they cover everything you need for this course. It is important to go to all the lectures since she usually emphasizes the important concepts that will appear in the exams. Three exams. Sample exams are provided for exam reviews. They are very similar, but the real exam will be harder than the sample exam.
Professor Chen is a great professor, she will try her best to explain to you when you have any question. If you have any confusion just go to the office hour.
This mans New Balance game is so strong. Rocks a different pair almost every class, would 100% take again.

Sal is AWESOME. He not only cares about his students but cares about the work you're putting in. There are a extra credit opportunities if you just ask him and he is so accessible outside of class, which not many are. The readings are sometimes dense but all interesting topics. I recommend choosing a presentation on something you like.

I still rave about Media Events and Spectacles to this day. My favorite MCC class I took at NYU and by far the most engaging lecturer. Sal cracks jokes, is extremely knowledgeable, and is a great example of what an MCC class should teach you. I wish I had taken his Fame class as well. Fair grader, easy to get an A if you just listen to lectures.
Horrible teacher
An all-around great professor with lots of experience. He's very jolly, take his Spectacles class!

Took Media Events and Spectacles with SJF this semester and had a great time. Lectures and content are very interesting, you can tell he cares a lot about his students and the content. One of my favorite things about him is that he encourages his students to think critically about the text and not just take it at face value.

Sal is great! He's so kind and funny and really clear in his lectures. He shares material for every class (presentations and any readings), gives out study guides, and makes it hard to fail the class, really. He just wants people to learn and have a good time. So sweet, a gem of the department.

He's a good professor, but when it comes to politics he (a liberal with Marxist opinions) is antagonizing. He is VERY close-minded regarding opinions that differ from his. I'm pretty conservative, so class was dreadful for me because I was shunned most times when I inputted my opinions. He spends lots of time complaining about politics every class

Prof Fallica is great. This class is interesting, especially if you are interested in politics. He says a lot of awkward dad jokes and isn't the most tech-savvy sometimes, but he is super sweet. The class is also pretty easy and straight forward

Prof. Fallica was probably one of my favorite professors at NYU! He is very knowledgable, clear in his lectures, and tries to make people feel comfortable. He's super understanding and can definitely be talked into giving students an extension if they show they're serious. Loved him!

Sal is the best! His topics are genuinely interesting and he opens up the floor to discussion frequently. There's several papers due throughout the semester but they aren't long, and are about the readings. Some readings are hard/dense but he'll really lay it out clearly in lecture. I really enjoyed his class and he was VERY supportive and positive

Very nice professor and a caring guy. Class consisted of lots of papers (4-6 pages biweekly) but no exams. Writing these papers takes time but he is an easy grader so getting a A is pretty easy. No need to participate in class or do the readings. Just be aware that there are a lot of papers, so if you don't like writing maybe choose another course.

He is a great and passionate teacher. Very easy going and kind. He is a little old school with teaching. The grading criteria/prompts and assignments were very unorganized and hard to keep track of because he just has you email him. Fun class and very understanding as a professor. Would take him again.
Love this professor. He is passionate about teaching, values your opinion and treats you with respect. Reasonable work that was actually quite fun to do.

Prof. Fallica's class was always driven by thought provoking, open-ended discussions that made you think for once, instead of passively listening and being lectured to. Sal values your thoughts and appreciates questions you raise or findings you discover. The workload is very reasonable and he is accessible for office hours. He is also very witty.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I love Sal! He is very passionate about what he teaches and genuinely cares about his students. He gave us a pizza party at the end! Just a midterm and a few short papers. He ended up taking out many of our assignments on the syllabus. Readings are very short. The class is an easy A but you will learn a lot from his class.

Sal is the best! It's rare that you find a professor who cares about what students think- he gets it. If your midterms pile up, you may even talk him into an extension. He wants the class to be engaging, highly recommended!

Sal is awesome. He's really nerdy and its hilarious, but he is an extremely knowledgable professor and the classes are pretty interesting for the most part. There are quite a few writing assignments, but they are not bad at all. That's that I liked a lot — they were all short. He's nice to his students.

The best professor I've ever had. I took Sal Fal for Political Communications and Persuasion/Propaganda. If you are looking for intellectually stimulating courses that are also very easy to get A's in, Sal's the man. SERIOUSLY, TAKE HIS CLASSES!!! SAL'S GREAT! Keep in mind that he makes jokes about conservatives, but still grades us all equally.

Sal Fal is an incredible instructor. He is a democrat, but is very open to right-wing comments and discussions. He makes class thoroughly enjoyable. The outside reading won't hurt you if you decide not to do it. I would HIGHLY recommend taking any class of his. He is so, so good at explaining things and very, very intelligent.
Sal wants to inspire students. He is great at transferring knowledge.
SalFal is incredible so personable and will help you with his class and any other problem you could have- amazing

I LOVE Sal Fal. He is one of the most gifted teachers i'd ever known. He Thought me 12 grade english in Malverne High School and i stll remember most of the vocabulary words. I cant wait to start school at NYU, i Pray i have you as a teacher again.

This is one of the best professors I've ever had.  He is knowledgeable, fair, sincere and helps students excel and think critically enabling them to love media in all aspects. Truly amazing professor, I wish him the best everyone I know enjoyed him as a professor, although we all agree he is much more deserving than that title itself.  Best always!
One Word: Folks

Execellent teacher. Really knows his stuff and is very entertaining. He takes dry material and gets you to want to learn it. Gives a fair amount of work and grades very fairly (that doesnt mean easy, that means fair).  Take his class if you are looking for an education with some fun mixed in.  Thanks for the great class Sal.
great guy, well organized, lectures are great, discussions better, great sense of humor, would definitely take a class w/ this prof

This was one of the best professors and best classes I've taken at NYU!! Prof. Porfirio was a great professor and cared a lot about his students actually learning + understanding the material. All the experiments were well-taught and were interesting. 100% would retake!
An amazing professor. Genuinely cares about his students. Will help you succeed. We need more professors like him at NYU.
Super chill guy with grading and extensions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing person! I love his lectures and I love his One Piece shirts.
the worst...

For a core math class, the content is pretty doable. Flek however struggled to communicate and answer questions for most of the semester. He would often cancel class and due to his injury, was gone for 2 weeks without notice. Other than that, his quizzes and exams are exactly like the example problems in class. He's very chill and posts everything.
Teaching style is ahh

prof flek is a kind soul and has been dealing with some health issues this sem, leading to last-minute cancellations. However, I didn't find them super disruptive. concepts were clearly explained and also accommodated Zoom lectures + recordings.

Class was cancelled a few times on short notice, but the professor handled it so well that it felt like a surprise break, not a problem. T/F questions were tricky, but everything else came straight from homework/slides and was very straightforward. He explained concepts clearly and pretty organized. I got a B and would still take them again.

Lectures are not engaging and cancels class a lot because he seems to be in a bad health shape for some time so I can sympathize a little. I bombed a few quizzes, but he gives a lot of practice for exams and I did really well in all three. the linear algebra's not bad. take him if you're able to learn stuff well on your own.
Class was extremely boring, he cancelled class a handful of times as well. speaks in a monotonous voice, wouldn't recommend, though the Linear Algebra is pretty chill.
bud wouldn't bump me up like less than half a point, because he doesn't curve. Easy class, takes answers from GT practice tests, which he gives to us to study.

Midterms are chill if yk how to solve all the ex. problems on the lecture slides. Similar questions from the lecture slides/homework packets are on the midterms. Final had a few tricky T/F questions but you should be alr if you memorized the ones from the homework packets. Quizzes are very straightforward and simple. Easy A if you study 1.5 hr/week
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lectures are very example heavy. If you can solve all the example problems in class without help you'll do fine on exams. Very easy grader and gives massive curves.
Cancel class last minute
Hes kind of unremarkable, not to obad or amazing. Youll be fine taking him for intro math

Free txtbk but not needed to do well; slides are almost the same as txtbk, informative w/ great examples. Missed class w/ late notice. Idk if this is normal since we had to ask & remind him but he uploads slides & recordings. Very late grading, but I heard there were issues w/ TAs. In my exp, did not reply to emails quick. Still, easy HWs and exams
Horrible professor, very unorganized, teached off slides, and missed a lot of sessions so he had to rush some and make us learn it ourselves. Easy class though.
He often miss classes, cancel lectures because of "personal issues". Very irresponsible.
He missed class a lot which peeved me off but he's a decent guy. I appreciate the review classes before the tests.

Barely comes to class and then ends up recording lectures (but publishes them sunday at like 10PM). Pretty disorganized. When he DOES show up tho, he's good at explaining concepts and good at teaching. dk if he's accesible outside of class bc he hasn't rly mentioned. 3 Exams (none cumulative). Quizzes every monday online. HW every tuesday.
Canceled a significant amount of classes. Released the exam grades almost a month later they were taken. Did not communicate enough. His lectures were fine. Records and posts them which are helpful.

There is a lot of coursework, but that is just the structure of math classes at NYU. The midterms were comprehensible after reviewing over the past written homeworks, lectures, and textbook. A lot of people didn't show up to class and did badly, but that's not the professor's fault. Communication will vary, sometimes classes will be cancelled.

The first half of his lectures are basically the exact same (sometimes more in-depth) as the pre-lecture homework, I found it rather useless so I just got done with other work.
The second half of the lectures was pretty useful on the other hand, going over examples in depth step by step.

Don't quite understand why he got such low rate on Rate my professor. He is very caring and accessible outside of class and he is generally kind to you. His midterms are not very difficult if you review slides he posts and go to his office hour for help.

Super nice guy but he is no fit to be a professor and it shows. I have never struggled with math my entire life until taking this class. I believe in my particular class at least 10 people dropped the class after the first exam. This guy screwed up my academic career.
don't take his class unless you want to spend more than 3 hours on the assignment

The second class I take with professor Flek. If you listen carefully, do homework and go to his office hour, you will get a relatively good grade. His tests can be a little bit difficult but almost all of them are based on the lecture slides(use the same method but different numbers)
Flek is a very run-of-the-mill math prof. Ended up teaching myself most of the material. Take this class if you need to fulfill a requirement but don't expect sunshine, rainbows and lollipops.
Not a good lecturer and unfair tests. Also doesn't give a generous curve. Do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice, accessible, and patient professor. Kind of quiet and awkward. However, his lecture is the most boring one I have seen so far. The lecture content is basically watching him doing calculus questions for 75 minutes with some explanation. I often fall asleep during lectures. Moreover, calculators are not allowed for exams.
Sweetheart and does not make you feel stupid in his explanations to your questions.
sweet and flexible. He is also very understanding. If you asks questions he explains it well without making you feel stupid. Patient
