This class is impossible to pass if you did not thrive in mathematics previously. If you're struggling early on I suggest you find a tutor as the nonexistent curve will not save you on the midterm. I withdrew after the midterm, as it was clear I could not cut it lol. Lectures are too quick and tests don't feature material covered in class.

don't really know why he has a low rating here. His lectures can be boring, but it's super clear and he actually makes math make sense. Had him for both basic algebra and calc1. If you do the weekly homework and actually understand it, you'll have no problem on the tests. fair grading system, but not so good curve. i would take him again

Very accessible and quick to respond to outside of class. But lectures were very boring and by the end almost no one went to class. Midterms were much harder than what he taught in lecture. He also didn't curve while the other calc prof's do. I took AP calc in hs and still struggled in his calc 1 class just due to the difficulty of the exams.
Not a good prof, boring lectures and midterms are difficult
DIdn't like this class. Not to mention, the other math teachers curved better, but his lectures are boring and his midterms are super hard. He didn't curve one of them. Take another professor.
While his lectures are clear and he records his classes and can be watched on Zoom, his midterms are absurdly difficult compared to the material taught.

There are 2 midterms worth 20% each and final 25%. He curves midterms, and I haven't taken the final. Online and paper hw every week really help with understanding the material. He posted the slides and recording of class, use them! Also, post-previous exams to study from, are very helpful. Exams are 10 MC & 5 FR. A good professor for pre cal
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tests have content that was not taught in class. Do not take if you did not take calculus before.

This class is so frustrating, there is so much homework and it is all so hard. This entry level math course consumes all my time and the exams are only 15 questions and just so stupid hard. Maybe the entire NYU math department sucks but this class is not an exception to that rule. I genuinely feel like they want me to fail or something.

You pretty much have to teach yourself everything because he just reads off the slides. Attendance was really light in the last few weeks because he posts the lecture slides after class so there's little incentive to actually go to class. His office hours were really helpful but he only had them once a week so I have to go to tutoring each weekend.
Organized class structure, clear lectures and quizzes are easy. Theres lots of hw, but its good practice. Would take this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: hes fine. you really have to learn everything on your own bc he just reads definitions and examples off slides. lots of homework but it is good practice. he makes mistakes relatively often in class

Professor Flek is honestly a good teacher. He just reads off the slide yea, but if you have any questions he will answer them, both in class and outside of it. He was very accessible and is generally kind to you. Homework could be overwhelming, but if you need help, he will help you. Definitely recommend him, if you want a good math professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of homework, but good practice. He also teaches very fast, but is very accessible for office hours. The exams are not worth too much, which helped because I winged the final.

THE BEST MATH PROFESSOR. Clear lectures. Good feedback and answer your questions clearly. Significant amount of hw, but he does that to help you practice. At the end, you will thank for hw because the exams are based on that. He curved all midterms. I became more confident in math after his course. Math is not easy, but he makes math easy.

He is quite kind, but you should only take his class if you are very confident in your math abilities. Exams are difficult, but they are curved. You will often have to go online to teach yourself the material.

Flek is really good if you already have a sense of the course you are taking. For me I've already taken Pre-Calc in HS so I didn't have to grind very hard in his class. His lectures are very easy to follow and he answers most questions. Plus he drops a lot of grades at the end of the semester.

Professor Flek explains things well during class and is patient when giving feedback and corrections. He always makes time during class to answer your questions. His work may seem like a lot, but math always requires practice so it's basically inevitable.

He is a great professor. He always explained to detail what you got wrong in exams, and is open to meet up to discuss topics we might not understand. He gives two homework weekly, but they're very easy and you can always ask for help during recitation or office hours. Overall, the class was good. Really Recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Weekly homework was alright, some problems were challenging. He spoke in a monotone voice which made me want to fall asleep especially at 8am. Exams and quizzes were pretty fair. He answered emails within a reasonable time. Overall, decent average teacher.

This prof was very helpful, he did assign a lot of weekly homework but are not hard to do. He curves exams a lot, which is very helpful. Always posts the slides and records lectures. Brightspace is very organized, with the class and quiz schedule there along with the syllabus, helpful links and others there. Overall good professor.

Assigns an insane amount of homework. The class had to do over 100 problem questions of Hw over the weekend on the first week of class. He does not give us any time to write down examples before moving onto the next lesson/slide. It was impossible to keep up. I wish anyone taking this class the best luck. Youre going to need it.

Very average professor. Basically reads everything from the slides. Sometimes confuses himself. Homework is fine but exams are way easier. Grading is super slow. A nice person tho, patient when answering questions. Only take him when you are confident at your math ability.
Flek's lectures are pretty clear and he responds to emails very quickly outside of class, so he's accessible. His exams are pretty difficult, but he did curve up the second midterm exam immensely.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Flek was an adequate professor but never stopped to take questions and didn't really teach- he just read off the screen and did some problems without explaining much. I pretty much had to learn everything on my own. Not to mention the impossible homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very confusing professor, frequently had to cancel class and at some points would not show up to our class without warning. Difficult to understand him lecturing, often would quote our textbook word for word without further explanation. Nice at office hours, but found myself more confused after every lecture. Exams took more than a month to grade.

Professor Flek is a really nice professor. I took AP calculus in high school and did well in the class and on the exams, and expected this class to be an easy A. However, the exams were pretty challenging, but Flek is super helpful and good at explaining things. He's a great professor and I would recommend him.

Professor Flek is really great! He walks through all the material, equations and problems clear and slow. If you attend classes you can understand everything. The workload is not heavy and the exams are also not hard. All the materials in the exams are covered in class. Overall really recommended if you are going to take Cal I!

I'll be honest: F CALCULUS. But Flek is not bad. I wish he taught a course I actually liked, because I'd give him a 5/5. He teaches in a straightforward manner and is very accessible outside of class. He does not make you feel inferior for not knowing how to do math. He is understanding. If you put in effort, he will take that into consideration.

His class is fine, he teaches mostly pretty clearly but he has a very monotone voice and isnt interesting. Exams are straightforward to the material. Homeworks are very light and manageable. It's easy to skip class since its a large lecture and no one notices, but beware of slacking off because it bit my butt in the end. An okay choice.
Not a hard class but average is so high and messing up once can kill your shot for an A. Stern curve so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad curve, If you mess up 1 test you lost your shot at an A. Group project is ok but random attendance, would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Only 2 quizzes (both of which were open-note). Group project and in class participation/attendance heavily matters so make sure you don't miss class. Truly the best professor I have had at nyu. Take her for an easy A
The best professor ever, GOAT of Marketing department.

Responsible and caring teacher!  BEST prof I've met
Whenever students have questions, she patiently takes the time to explain. Also she thoughtfully recaps the previous lesson, helping us deepen our understanding
She said she will always open notes for exams, cuz she said we can search when we work after all, so why not be kind to students!

Prof. Hogan might seem strict at the beginning because she spoke fast and sounded uncompromising, but actually she is nice. She appreciated all our opinions and respected everyone's voice. Her weekly journal assignments seemed tough, but she graded them quite leniently. I got all A's on the assignments and got an A in the end.

She is one of the kindest, passionate, and inclusive professors that you will ever meet! Her syllabus literally has all the details, dates, explanations for the readings and assignments. Class is more discussion based but often among small groups/partner. She really values hearing your experience and connections to the lessons. 100% worth it!

Great professor! Her classes are very discussion heavily but you will be fine and if you contribute regularly you will get an A in participation easily. She gives the clearest rubric on everything and is just so nice and kind. She is fair and friendly to all students but it is hard for her to remember your name if you have a foreign name.
weird......

She is awesome and knows her stuff. Fast engaging lectures and no tests but definitely homework. I love that she is outspoken but sometimes it was sometimes overwhelming with the amount of correct political terms. I was never bored though.

Easy A if you just pay attention and participate in class. She really cares about students, pay attention and respects their opinions, and was the first professor who remember my culture on name preference. One of the best prof and highly recommended.

This lady is the epitome of the woke mind virus at NYU. She polices the language of students and even deducted points from my work for not using the most up to date politically correct terminology. If you take her class, simply use every liberal buzzword and she will give you great grades. As a POC, I also felt like she has a white savior complex

Would definitely take the course again! Clear grading criteria, inspirational lectures, and she truly cares about her students. She reads your response and gives thoughtful feedbacks. The workload is not very light, but the readings are not long, and as long as you pay attention in class, you will be fine.
She's really nice! While I was not a big fan of turning the cameras on during certain times in class I did learn a lot.
very good prof
Very organized and easy grading. would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Elizabeth is an amazing professor who cares about her students and their future as academic writers. While the class is difficult and is more strictly graded, she makes sure that you are set up for success in future college classes. Personally, I did not enjoy the material of the progressions, but she was always there and provided great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: very fair and accommodating + super organized and structured. content is not super interesting for first two progressions, personally. homework is pretty easy, takes

Elisabeth made this class fun and enjoyable! 2 papers make up 70% of your grades but are relatively easy as you choose your own topics to write about. She makes you go through peer feedback and one-on-one meetings to check in with her. She is very caring and open, please ask for support when you need it. Short readings, little homework and amazing!

Very fair class, always show up prepared to class as your participation and what not is a good part of what brings your grade up if you don't do as well on the essays. Very easy to talk to outside class just shoot and email and see will provide feedback or help you out. They care about student well-being and make it simple to ask for extentiontime.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Elisabeth is an accommodating professor that will help with anything as long as you communicate. Sometimes her feedback on papers can be given close to a deadline and a bit nitpicky about concepts and structure. That being said, I would still take the course again, she genuinely cares about her students.
Gives clear feedback, very little homework. Only two papers and was always open to meet outside of class/help you with your work. She's very lenient with giving extensions.
She has a very understanding perspective on students' busy lives and her feedback is very clear. Her essay assignments are open-ended and students can choose to write about topics that interest them.

I didn't have prog Fay for a class but went to her for my writing center appointment. She was AWESOME. Gave so many really good and thoughtful feedbacks, and was able to hold a conversation with me that guided me and gave me inspiration on things I was stuck on. Highly recommend her for the writing center!

AMAZING!! I had her first semester freshman year, and she is such a caring and funny professor. Extremely accessible outside of class and always gives very precise and helpful feedback! Her assignments were very clear and always helpful for the final essay. Definitely take her! She is probably one of the best NYU professors; I would take her again!

The absolute best professor I have ever had. She's incredibly caring and understanding of her students. And considering that it's a writing class, her lectures are actually so useful and helpful. Gives incredibly helpful feedback, as well.
Amazing professor, only two 6-8 page essays and annotating short readings graded by completion. Very accessible and helpful professor when helping formulate essays.

Elisabeth is hands down one of my favorite professors at NYU. It is required for me to take Advanced College Essay and Elisabeth made the entire experience extremely comfortable and enjoyable. She is super open-minded, kind, and truly cares about your academic growth AND personal well-being. TAKE HER CLASS!

I loved her so much. The reading is heavy, but the content combined with her helpful feedback will really help improve your writing. Get help when needed, participate, and you'll do great! I would highly recommend taking her class especially since it's usually required!
Elizabeth was a fantastic Writing the Essay professor. I genuinely loved the class.
Elisabeth was perpetually peppy and engaging, even when the energy in the room was at rock bottom. Her advice was constructive and helped me significantly as a writer.

Take this class. Elisabeth is hands down one of the most caring professors I've had the pleasure of having so far  at NYU. She is always willing to go out of her way to help students who come to her for help, whether that's setting up an office hours appointment or granting additional extension hours on top of the ones given to every student.

Elisabeth is truly amazing, and I could not recommend taking her class for WTE/ACE enough. She was able to make a class as dreadful as a required writing course entertaining and somewhat enjoyable. She also is extremely caring and is always willing to make accommodations to meet her students' needs.TAKE HER CLASS, you won't regret it!

Amazing is an understatement to describe my time in Elisabeth's class as a student! She is so sweet and understanding, and the work was thought-provoking. I can genuinely say that walking out of this class, I feel more confident in myself as a writer, and she was always willing to help out. If you can take her class, please do!

Elisabeth is one of the most caring professors I've had; she is extremely understanding and respectful of students' time, even has a "grace period" on almost all due dates for this reason. The class is engaging and makes you think, and her feedback on essays really does help you improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Definitely recommend taking Elisabeth's class! WTE can easily be a dreadful class, but Elisabeth's class is so well organized that the workload doesn't feel overwhelming at all. She's very caring, understanding, and super accessible to students during and outside of class. I wouldn't say this class is an easy A, but it's definitely obtainable.

TAKE THIS CLASS! She is so aware of students' needs & gives great accommodations  she lets you rewrite a paper at the end of the semester, and is very understanding/generous with extensions. Feedback is clear & I def improved as a writer. If you do the assignments, follow her feedback, and go to office hours once or twice, you'll get an A.

Great teacher! Cares about your writing and is understanding towards her student's workload. She definitely grades your writing so it is not an easy A class but as long as you do the work you should be fine.

Elizabeth is a very understanding professor. Probably one of the nicest ones in my whole career in NYU. She specifically adjusts her leniency when noticing a student is really struggling and is super nice and cool. Leaves easy to read feedback on essays and there is no chance of a bad grade if you do all the work and attend class. Would recommend!

Take this class!!!! My favorite professor as a first sem freshman during COVID and online learning. Went out of her way to make accommodations for students and really made them felt seen/appreciated. You will have to work hard on essays but if you put in the work and address her feedback you will do well.
The class (WTE) can be a pain during drafting and editing, but she provides the tools to make it much simpler (and better.) Your writing will improve.

Professor Fay is a true gem. I was going through a lot during my semester in her class and she was always SUPER understanding! Leaves very clear comments on your work and structures homework in a way that you are not writing your entire essay the night before. The class is quite a bit of reading but it's expected from a writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is SO nice and caring. She gives out a lot of optional extension time for papers throughout the semester with no penalty and gives great feedback. I would definitely recommend taking ACE with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Fay prepared students for essay writing with many guiding exercises. She provided feedback for all of the exercises and drafts and made you think about issues in a deeper way, questioning motivations and cultural expectations / norms. She made expository writing enjoyable and interesting. Take Professor Fay if you can!! She's great

I've taken two of her writing classes and can honestly say she is the best. I've heard of tough professors, but Elisabeth is very fair and straight forward. She has helped me grown as a writer. Her class isn't difficult, you just got to put in some effort and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved Elisabeth Fay her classes were great and super enjoyable. Classwork is manageable and she's really good about not letting anything build up. I wouldn't say its an easy A, but if you go to office hours and take her comments to your work seriously you can do well. She's really accessible and always responds if you ever need her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a good choice for WTE. The exercises she makes you do before writing an actual essay are really helpful, and she's good at meeting with you out of class. It isn't an easy A, you may think you're a good writer and end up with a B+/A-, but it feels satisfying, and as if I've learned something from the course.

She gives good feedback on your essays, and as long as you put in a lot of effort into your papers and show improvement, you'll receive the grade you deserve! My writing really improved while taking her class, and I totally recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Bit boring, monotone voice. But he seems respected and knows what he is teaching. Very easy class, easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TRUST if u need an easy A take this. its all memorization & tests are all mcq. recitations are so unnecessary bc tas just reteach lecture but theres attendance so go. theres a group project u present in recitation but otherwise theres basically only hw graded on completion & midterm/final

The consensus is true, and the class is very easy. He does just read off of slides, but he is a really nice guy and the material in my opinion, was actually interesting. Attendance is not required. All the required material is in the textbook, but honestly, just go to recitation. Would take again, whether for an easy grade or for genuine interest
such a nice, chill professor. i would def take him again- the most stress-free class u can take at NYU. hes also really nice to talk to after class. offers a ton of XC too
easiest class i've ever taken, weekly hw graded on completion, just review key terms for tests, and the rest is common sense

Gollwitzer seems like a nice guy, not a very good lecturer. The content is regurgitated from the textbook word for word, and he's pretty hard to understand. This class was also graded based on a group project and two exams, so not a whole lot to go off of. That being said, if you review before the exams, it is a super easy A.
Very easy to do well, just make sure you do the hw and pay attention in recitation and you're good

Professor Gollwitzer is a very fair and kind professor. He is very knowledgeable in his field and explains things in a way that is easy for his students to understand. The final and midterm were both very fair. I would highly recommend taking his Social Psych class he was great.
Such a cool guy. Take him!
i love peter! hes a funny guy, and i recommend getting to know him better after classes.
easiest class of my life, my goat

Dude. This guy. He was so boring.I've never rated a professor for being too boring but this guy takes it. Went to 3 lectures total, did well in the class. Just read the McGraw Hill and don't go to class. All lecture he just regurgitates the textbook. Honestly take him for an easy A, guy just doesn't seem to care about teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures can be dull, but the topics are interesting. Lecture slides aren't on Brightspace, so take good notes. I did well on exams by studying notes or sometimes the textbook. There's an easy group project in recitation, and attendance counts for credit. Overall, it's a simple class, and I recommend it!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were a bit boring, but overall an easy class and he clearly cares about this subject a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I only went to two lectures but I still got an A. The Professor had a faint voice which you can't hear anything. THE MOST BORING CLASS EVER IN MY ENTIRE COLLEGE CAREER
The class had a lot of potential, but his lectures were not very exciting. You're only graded on two exams and a group project. The content of the exams is always weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gollwitzer is a knowledgeable professor in his research/in the field but repeated everything we read in the textbook for homework. The class was disorganized with dates and assignments being changed. It's an easy A if you do the work and study for the midterm and final. Only graded on the midterm, final, a presentation, and a little homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want a GPA booster class, I recommend taking this class. As reiterated by a previous comment, if you want to truly learn I don't recommend taking this class. The professor reads from a script/slides not made by him and although I can sympathize with his injury this semester, the second half of class was overall unorganized.

Pretty chill class tbh. Alls I did was read the textbook and study the day before each exam. Gave me a ton a time to sleep in on Mondays and weds considering lecture was online. Take if you want an easy A and have more difficult classes to worry abt. But if you want an engaging lecture environment with an exchange of ideas you should avoid

Zoom lectures where prof just read the textbook review slides - so if you take the class you're paying $100 extra to read textbook on your own or go to lecture and get a summary of the chapters. TAs were awful and so disorganized. They assigned group projects last minute because they didn't want to read individual papers but told us last minute

if you just want a good grade, take his class - its an easy A. if you value your education and want engaging/not boring lectures - don't go near. he's a smart and nice guy, just some people don't have the personality to be teachers. its a shame bc the material would be so interesting if he gave it life and didn't read straight from the textbook.
Really cool professor. Lectures are straight from the McGraw textbook slides but he goes into his own research and experiences sometimes which I found interesting. Tests were very easy.

A lazy prof. Mandatory $100 textbook which also provides the quiz grades. He even uses the textbook company's slides for lecture and can not post them on brightspace because of copyright. And then he reads those review slides, which are word for word from the textbook in the most monotone voice. I hated him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class can be skipped as the lecture slides are copy & pasted from the textbook. Relatively easy class--the only thing that upset me was paying $90 for McGraw.

Prof. Gollwitzer has a reputation for being quirky, but that is exactly why he is immensely smart and inspiring. He is open to lots of ideas and is extremely knowledgeable. Don't expect the usual PPT slides and organized handouts. If you are lazy, don't take the course. If you are willing to work hard, he is a wonderful, caring and fun prof!
He's a talented researcher, but I don't think he cares much about teaching. Very relaxed and chill in a way, but I wish he put in more effort in another. TA was extremely helpful and available.

Gollwitzer is pretty boring, and although his intentions are probably good, he doesnt seem like he puts in any real time or effort on teaching and preparing lectures. He uses the slides from the text book and sometimes rambles off with incomprehensible stories. His German accent can be hard to understand when he speaks quietly or rambles off.

It's hard to understand him, but you can do well just by reading the textbook. The TAs were awesome!! Attendance is mandatory, because you have to write a response for every class. He gave us 4 quizzes, which counted for one midterm grade, and an 80-question final. 3 papers, ranging from 1 page - 6 pages. Overall, I recommend him!!

He's not really hard, but it's stressful. You will NEVER know what your grade is. He doesn't talk about modernity. It was chemistry. Changed syllabus/grading 3 weeks before the end. SO disorganized; nobody knows anything about our assignments or what is expected. He just wants to see u care, so have a general idea of readings, talk A LOT, and pray.

He is a really sweet guy, and he's very educated on what he's talking about; however, he strays completely from what Global Works classes are supposed to be, and instead, we spent the semester learning about Biomimetics and AI usage. He is super disorganized and it makes it kind of stressful on students. But he will do what he can to help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Please. Please. whatever you do do not take this professor. He is the most disorganised person you will ever meet. I nearly cried at multiple points throughout the semester because he randomly created an announcement that I could not make head or tail of, the night before the class.Very unclear assignments, cannot stick to his own syllabus,

A knowledgeable professor who brings a lot of energy to the classroom. You really need to love the subject matter to keep up with him. There is some reading involved, but not an overwhelming amount; it's not like 1,000 pages a week. While he is a tough grader, he is also understanding and offers students a chance to improve their work.

He is a chill and nice guy, but sometimes the course just gets really unclear. Whether its about the grading, or due dates, or what he is saying in his lectures. 
You can take the course and do okay... its just average.

Very chill guy and the content is pretty interesting. However, it took forever to get prompts and even longer to get grades. I only got 3 grades from him (w/ very little feedback) despite how much we did. Lectures are long, but survivable. This class is not worth the unnecessary stress was caused by his lack of communication and organization.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Terrible, rude, and uninformative.

He was a really nice and down-to-earth guy. He was just a really tough grader, and assigned really difficult assignments, with very UNCELAR directions. He also takes a while to post assignments and by the time he does you have a few days to complete them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Unclear Grading scale, Does Everything last minute. Don't take him unless you have to. The only upside is he gives entertaining lectures
shi

funny, passionate, and nice but all over the place! he pulls assignments out of thin air and takes forever to grade! added on to my stress during the semester especially with two 10 page papers given to us a week before they were due. if you really love philosophy take him. if not, DO NOT!!!

Readings are extremely long and time consuming as well as last minute 10 page papers before breaks. You will not know where you stand in his class as he does not grade anything until the very last second. Lectures are dry and disengaging. I still do not know my midterm or final grade in his class and it is already the second semester.

reviews.comment: Might be easier than others, but no consistency. If you care about philosophy then take his class, otherwise avoid! He's silly, caring, but hard to follow and all over the place. No clear assignment schedule so might randomly have a quiz or paper. Returns grades months late or not at all. Time consuming and long papers. No motivation to be there

reviews.comment: submttd big assgnmnt sept22 n received grade dec10, class based on abstract concepts, impossible 2 understand if ur doing things right until he returns grades 2 late(@ very end of sem). makes it impossible 2 improve, lectures dry, boring, not attention grasping, confines students to ither getting it from the start or never understanding the class.

reviews.comment: -not a good professor. if you actually want to learn something , dont take him. he goes off topic all the time

reviews.comment: Unless you're really into philosophy and like to read tons, don't take him. He was nice but I didn't understand what was going on the entire semester. We didn't really have many assignments and the goals of the class were unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want to have some laughs in class, then definitely take this class! If you want to know your grade, what is going on, and what you are being graded on, then you should steer away.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His grading scale is very unclear, somehow it's a B or C. The midterm grade may be an A, and the final and final grade becomes a B-.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Aside from the negatives, there are many bright sides to taking his courses. He is a very forgiving grader, and dropped our two lowest assignment grades from the final grade calculation. The course content is also very interesting, but active participation is required if you want to make the most of it. He is also passionate about what he teaches.
He is a nice person but his class is disorganized and boring. It was an easy A but I basically learned nothing in his class.

I took him for liberal studies core classes twice and he was such a fun teacher. He assigns a lot of readings but he goes over all of it in class and you only have a few hw assignments the whole semester. And most importantly he's a super caring and passionate teacher. If you raise your hand and answer a question he gets so genuinely happy.

Professor Mahootian can be disorganized at times, but his lectures are amazing. His lectures are funny, interesting and he really tries to be likeable by students and encourages you to ask questions otherwise you would feel dumb asking. Papers can be extensive, but he is open to answer any questions you have and provide you with feedback.
Worst professor I have ever had. EVER. So disorganized, mean to the students, and took so long to grade I had no idea how I was doing until 2/3 weeks before the semester ended. DO NOT TAKE.

Professor Mahootian is a wildly intelligent man, you can see it in the way he speaks. However, he is incredibly disorganized. He often went on tangents in lectures, changed due dates or assignment criteria, and was very slow to grade. I didn't have any knowledge of my standing in the class until he released midterm grades and the same with finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took his Science of Tech class. The reading material and his views on the philosophy of technology are fascinating (if you're interested in that sort of thing). He's flexible w/ assignments, easy to talk to, and genuinely interested in what he teaches. Only negative was his unclear grading criteria (although his grading was lenient and flexible).
Okay, Prof. Mahootian's class was all over the place. If you are an organized person, avoid his social foundation's classes. Is he passionate, yes, but I am not entirely sure what we learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: As a 4.0 student trust me: the worst professor you will ever come across. Complete inability to speak coherently and extraordinarily late to grade anything. It's almost impressive how his prompts can be interpreted in at least 4 different ways due to his horrible grammar and misuse of words. No regard for student interest, rambling on for hours.

Mahootian is such a genius and seeing himself get lost in his own thoughts is one of my favorite things about his class. Studying and following instructions will get you a good grade and he's always available to talk outside of class if needed. A super cool guy that will talk to you about anything and is very funny/lovable

This man single-handedly my first semester GPA. This isn't a class where you can work hard to get an A. If you aren't good at philosophy, even if you're willing to learn, you won't get a good grade. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rambles. Completely philosophy based. If you aren't good/into that do not take this class. One of the hardest classes Ive ever taken.

His lectures are convoluted and he goes on many tangents. Had three graded assignments total the entire semester: a 20 point quiz and two longer essays. I was not able to get any feedback on my last essay, he didn't give any comments. I have no clue why I got the grade that I did. He is passionate about his class, however.

The paper I submitted in the third week of the semester was returned to me with two weeks left in the semester. This made it impossible to know how I was doing in the class. The only written assignments we had were the first paper and a 10 page final paper. Being graded on two things makes it much harder. I would give him a 0 if I could.

Super intelligent. laughs at his own jokes, can't bring the class to match wits with him. You can just be on ur laptop when he talks in class he wouldn't care. But u'll see he's actually a genius if u keep up with him. Super layback too, flexible with deadlines. Very openminded and caring. Only wrote 2 papers and a worksheet for this class

It is hard to follow Prof. Mahootian's thoughts during his lectures. Although he is incredibly passionate when teaching the class, and genuinely cares for his students, understanding the course material is often confusing. There is an incredible amount of reading for his class, and the text is usually very dense, and dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Farzad is interested and knowledgable in the material. BUT his class is confusing, grade boundaries no clear, and he discusses too much heavy content all at once so you leave the class confused and overwhelmed. Grades aren't really known until the end. If you take him, go to office hours for extra help!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Loved him. Tough grader and rambles, but so sweet. I used to love going to office hours just to talk to him, he's so brilliant! He lets you rewrite papers and take quizzes you miss. The final is a take home. Work hard, go to office hours, and you'll get an A.

I did not like it at all. Lectures are very dry, texts hard to understand. I did not learn anything useful in his class. He might seem funny at first but it is really hard to follow his thoughts. So think twice before taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The best SF teacher. Loved the class material and he really knows how to teach well. Interesting lectures too.

He's super passionate about philosophy and what he's teaching, which is great! But as the other reviews have said, his lectures tend to just go on and on and you'll realize that you have no idea what he's talking about anymore. His readings are also a pain in the ass at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very passionate about the course, however difficult to follow. The coursework is relatively unorganized which makes it difficult to complete his often vague essay prompts and test questions. Very easy to get lost in the course's material, doesn't need a lot of effort but demands attention. Very nice and funny guy and available during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is a really passionate man, but is extremely confusing. He provides no clarity on the lectures, rambles incessantly, and takes months to return a paper. Although he is cool and funny, I would never, for the life of me, take this awful class again. So many papers. Very harsh grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: i really do appreciate how passionate he is about philosophy. however, his lectures are extremely confusing and he tends to ramble on and on, jumping from topic to topic without clarification. sure he's funny and entertaining, but i wouldnt take his class again if someone paid me! going to class is a waste of time cause i dont understand anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor Mahootian is really nice and cool, but he is a tough grader - he looks for very specific answers. One thing I did really like about him was that he was always open to help me during office hours with correcting my answers and you could rewrite every single essay to get a better grade. But beware, he rambles on and on in class!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Philosophy of physics/chemistry/sciences (he was a philosophy/chemistry major and references science in class often), philosophy of religion, epistemology. If you don't like writing about these things and/or can't write coherently on these topics, this is not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You either love him or you don't. While he is funny, passionate, & knowledgeable, I did not enjoy his class. His bi-weekly reading quizzes are so specific. His essay prompts are too vague & he is a really harsh grader. However, he does lets you resubmit. Also, if you are not the slightest bit interested in philosophy this is NOT the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is an amazing teacher! very inspiring and fun. Highly approachable and understanding!

He's very confusing. He might be a funny guy, but he's not that great at teaching the material, if there even is one. Half the time, I'm completely confused by the class, no matter how hard I read the text. The essays are also really open - as in you can literally write about anything and everything and that's not a good thing in a freshman class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: good guy; gotta meet him in office hours if you like the philosophy of science. I see a lot of people who arent too into Plato and Phil though so if you not interested in philosophy, you probably wont enjoy the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's a fun guy and a good person, but can be very confusing. His lectures can be hard to follow, but he is easy to approach and will try to help you whenever you ask for it. Yes it is confusing, but that is the case with all SF class. With Mahootian the time you spend in the classroom would be entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's really confusing, but so is the work. If you want to do well in the class, do the readings and go to his office hours if you don't understand them. He gives quizzes a lot in the beginning but then stops after mid-terms. He's super helpful, but you have to ask for it. Not a lot of papers, the tests questions are often taken right from the HW.

Professor Mahootian is one the best professors I've had at NYU. His discussions of philosophy were outstanding, the work is relevant and balanced. His lectures are entertaining, interesting, engaging. We started Day 1 by watching Monty Python's Meaning of Life. You'll love class with him. And if he's still doing Tea & Philosophy, do it.

Yes, the class is confusing, but that's the material, not the professor. Mahootian is honestly one of the more helpful professors I've had this year. He really wants you to succeed. If you're having trouble on an essay, go to office hours, and he will help you SO MUCH. He even allows revisions. He's truly a nice guy & is very passionate.

He is an intelligent man who is passionate about his subject. However, he is very CONFUSING. There is A LOT of reading assigned. He tends to talk about the material as if you already know what it is. You must READ CAREFULLY because he gives QUIZZES often. His essay prompts are COMPLICATED. He's also a HARSH essay grader.

He's a little kooky, but very intelligent. Lectures can be dry--I didn't pay attention most of the time. The class is super easy though, and the content itself is pretty interesting if you're into philosophy.

Cool, interesting guy but his lectures are extremely confusing. He talks about the material as if you already know it therefore doesn't go in depth and assumes you understand everything, making it easy to get lost and feel inferior for not understanding.

I was confused for 80% of SFI. You go over confusing philosophical topics and most of the professors explanations are even more confusing. Not a bad professor just hard to understandnot very helpful. The essay prompts are beyond confusing. Just trying to figure out what you are expected to write is almost harder than writing the actual essay.
Without a doubt the worst teacher I've ever had, and that's saying something.
Just don't.
Do not take his class if you know what's good for you!!!!!!!
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS! He may be nice and funny but the readings are incredibly confusing and he doesn't help much in explaining. Clearly plays favorites and also grades unfairly.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!! Mahootian is "funny" for the first day but he uses this as a trap. He's passive aggressive and doesn't let you go to the bathroom or use laptops in class. He picks dry, difficult readings and assigns hard essays. He will grade you poorly if you don't use flowery language/agree with him. Totally useless class.

He's hilarious!  Loves to make jokes and have some fun in class, he gets bored simply lecturing.  However, his SciTech class was pretty difficult considering the concepts.  He's very understanding though - a good professor to have overall.

Professor Mahootian is an incredibly engaging teacher. Although he often goes off topic, he is always bringing up different topics and theories that are not in the textbook. You need to be genuinely interested in the class in order to really appreciate what he teaches. So long as you work hard in the class, you should be fine.

This professor is the funniest and most interesting. You have to see him in office hours, talk to him in between classes, and raise your hand sometimes. If you make the effort and put yourself out there, he will reward you. However, he is super paranoid about computers, so look up every once in a while so he isn't suspicious of you. HE is the man!
Completely useless class. I only go to class  for attendance. Can't care to listen if he doesn't care to grade fairly. That's all I have to say

At first, I thought his class would be good because he's goofy, friendly and tries to be funny. However, his class has become completely useless. He's all over the place, picks the driest texts (which I think he likes just because they confuse and bore everyone) and always gives last minute flowery assignments.

His teaching style places emphasis on actually getting the kids to learn, through discussion, not merely regurgitate a textbook. I love his class, it's pretty easy but also enjoyable if you try to participate!

Farzad's really nice, goofy clumbsy, but a poor prof. He also teaches philosophy & spends most of class lecturing on material that doesn't relate to class. When you ask simple questions it takes him forever to respond. It's very difficult to understand what he wants in essays, etc. and his responses are convoluted. Not a hard class, but a lot of BS

Dr. Mahootian is an extremely nice man. He gets off topic very often, but he's always talking about science or philosophy and always with a smile on his face. Very approachable, also. He was very unorganized, but he really likes what he does, and he wants everyone to do well. Don't be afraid to ask him questions and to go to his office hours.

Not a good professor. A nice guy who used to work at NASA, but not clear or interesting and not really an easy A either. Found myself waiting for class to end every time. Going to his class three times a week was dreadful.

Really, really hard class; left every class completely confused and frustrated. Not a science person? Avoid Mahootian. Gets off topic VERY easily, and ends up talking about things not in the curriculum, which he decides to add to the test. Takes on much more than he can handle.

Seriously, Mahootian is the best. He's funny and weird (in a good way), keeps you engaged and makes you REALLY think about things. Had him last semester for HOU and this semester for SFII. You really do learn things in class and he really values what you have to say--it's refreshing to have a professor that actually cares.

I had Professor Mahootian for History of the Universe. He could get off topic really easily, but I always left class knowing something new. The midterm and final weren't bad at all, especially if you paid attention in class. He worked with students who needed it, and overall made a class that would have sucked really cool.

Extremely passive aggressive and restricting. Doesn't engage with student views much or encourage a lively classroom environment. No technology policy, no bathroom breaks, feels like a prison. Unnecessarily nitpicks every little thing done and tries to be tough and strict as possible. Class is disappointing& boring despite having so much potential
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor assigns a good amount of reading before classes, and participation matters.

This will be one of the easiest classes you will take. She is a super easy grader. You have 1-2 readings per class but you can get by by just skimming it. Each class, you basically get divided into groups and have to use the reading to answer questions.
racist and biased against students. impossible to communicate with. gives vague feedback and grades harshly. gets and gives no respect to her students. avoid taking at all costs

I don't understand her at all. You can get C's on your papers, ask her for feedback which she won't give, then she'll give you an A at the end of the semester for all the pain and strife she caused. She gets super bugged about notification sounds during class so you can't have a phone or laptop during class. You also can't use the bathroom.

Don't take this lady. She is extremely passive aggressive and so strange. She won't let you have an opinion that differs from her's and she will not answer your questions if you need help. Hardly accessible outside of class (5 minute office hour appointments) and she grades papers randomly even if you do well on the HW. No bathroom during class too

Galal is the easiest grader i've ever met. she'll give you 100s on every single assignment, you bearely have to do anything. She's a bit anal about class, you can't leave to go to the bathroom or be on your phone or computer. But the readings aren't that hard and they're fairly chill. Take her, your GPA willl thank you :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class consist of heavy discussions within smaller groups that are assigned. The main grades are participation, a group presentation, individual presentation, midterm paper, and final paper. She is an easy grader but there are a lot of readings involved. Lectures are heavily discussion based so it could get boring at times with the 30+ pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This is probably the worst professor I have ever taken during my academic career. She is extremely disorganized, can't follow her syllabus, and has difficulty remembering her words and rules. She wanted to be tough so bad that she did not give students a space to grow or be heard.. it gave identity crisis. Don't take this professor.
genuinely cares about his students and is super funny. very passionate and knowledgeable. love this professor

Really cool guy, super passionate about both the subject matter and teaching. His accent (Scottish) was difficult to understand at first but it got easier as the semester went on. Found his lectures engaging. Strong recommend.

He is very knowledgeable in linguistics, but he ends up info dumping during lectures. His passion for the topic and personal annotates about this children's language develop makes class interesting to learn. Although it is recommended to read the textbook, I still got an A just by attending class and reading parts of the textbook.

The topic itself was a bit challenging alongside with homework, but he answers your questions pretty well. Tests were a bit hard but quite similar to hw, and you get to make your cheat sheet. Although the exams were a pretty time crunch, he gives extra credit in hw and exam to make up for. Overall pretty chill/decent class. Recommend.
Prof. Thoms is super passionate about linguistics and does his best to engage students to enjoy it as well. The class was a bit dull for me but that was due to the subject matter and not Prof. Thoms
great and caring professor. homework is a little hard, but he is very caring and reachable. good class. Just take it!
Funny, sweet, and very knowledgeable. Our resident Scot in the NYU Linguistics Dept. What more can I say?
A cute, interesting professor. Very caring. If he speaks SAE, I would be understanding better. But overall good.

I took a really interesting intro to linguistics class with Gary. He's a very smart, laid-back guy with a great attitude. Common feedback about Gary's teaching though is that his Scottish accent can be hard to understand at first, so just try not to sit in the back.

Take Professor Huang if you can! He's easily the best teacher at NYU. He wants everyone to get an A and lets you rewrite your assignments until they're perfect. The classes are super collaborative and full of cool guest speakers, and topics are taught in an engaging, but not preachy way. Would absolutely recommend.

Best prof I've ever had. You need to be persistent in seeking out help if you need it, but he's extremely knowledgeable and generous. Flexible on deadlines and understanding when life happens. You'll only learn if you read, participate, do homework, but as long as you hand everything in its an easy A.

This professor is very easy and usually stops grading about halfway through the course. I also took him for Sports and Society and he did the same. I received grades for the first two assignments but after that, nothing else was graded. There is no final. He does not teach much; most of the class is guest speakers.

i love mike as a person. he cares about you and will help you with navigating the journalism world. but, as a prof, it can be frustrating sometimes. he's super busy with his other job - doesn't always have time for his students. pushing back deadlines, not grading things, ect. i haven't received feedback since march. no idea what my grade will be.

Took his Sports Reporting class. He's an amazing professor who goes above and beyond to ensure success for his students. Hosts weekly meetings with every student to revise their drafts til it's an A or A-. Super understanding when we go through shit, and lenient with deadlines. Well connected and really experienced in the sports world. MUST TAKE.
She is very friendly and caring. She makes the material interesting and easy to understand. I have never liked coding, but I find myself enjoying her class.

Quiz: Hard - Very little practice and quiz topic is unclear beforehand. HW: Not difficult & helpful office hours. Exam: High avgs. Many very specific definition questions worth 12-16%. go to review session to know which slides to copy to cheatsheet. Textbook: mandatory as the prof only has a few practice questions per slideset. Prof doesn't use it

I often couldn't understand what she was saying within the first 3 minutes of class. There's zero consistency between the lectures, quizzes, assignments, and exams. The test scope is vague and arbitrary, making it impossible to practice effectively.
No curve at all — I scored above average and still ended up with a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Incredibly un-engaging lecturer. Fell asleep every class so just stopped going (attendance not graded). Gives attitude to students. Impossible weekly quizzes but only 1% of grade each. Exam isn't hard, 2-sided cheat sheet so can cram the night before and get by. Take if you want an easy-ish class but prepare to teach yourself everything.
easy lecture, impossible hw and quizzes

Her weekly quizzes are much harder than what we learn in her lectures. Some of the material on the quizzes aren't even taught in her lectures, which makes them hard to prepare for. But the curve she gave was generous and I heard she was easier than many other CS101 profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a fine person, but she don't really know how to teach CS 201. I think someone is correct, she assumes that all the students have already known everything, so she usually cover the slide really quick. Her quiz and homework, and test are very tricky. For example, she asked the name of 3 conditions in the quiz.

Unclear grading criteria, and very unorganized. She seems like a good person, however I had a bad experience with this class. Final was suddenly changed to take home and no feedback was given on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Have a good experience with her in computer graphic, super lenient with grade!!!
AVOID AT ALL COST. Unclear lecture + impossible exams and quizes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
No feedback was provided on all the quizzes and midterms taken.

She speaks and writes scribbles on the blackboard during the lectures, and the handwritten lecture notes are hardly readable unless (perhaps) you've taken notes during the lecture and compared them. Good luck if you are designated to take this course during her iteration.

She makes you fly blind in this class. In one case, we were given a 30 minute window with only 20 hours notice to be able to look at our midterm. Most of the semester we had little to no feedback for our assignments so it was hard to know what we needed to work on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUN!!!!! She's the worst professor I've ever met. She assumes we know everything and refuses to give a curve even avgs of tests are quite low. Extra credit only works for those whose grade is around the next letter grade, u may gain nothing to finish the extra credit perfectly. If u want to suffer a whole sem and mentally break down, choose her.
Assignments and class material are sort of on the difficult side, but she is extremely lenient with grading. Would highly recommend for Computer Graphics

She assumes that students know everything. The assignments and quizzes are manageable, yet the exams are very challenging and include concepts that she rushed through last class. The absence of curves, delayed return of exam/assignment grades, and no response to emails contribute to a less than optimal learning environment. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The BEST professor throughout my CS undergraduate journey! She provided me with crucial support and encouragement, for which I am deeply grateful. I highly recommend her course! Wishing her all the best!!!

Very average class. Looking back I care a bit more about the material than I thought I did during the semester but it's not a super interesting topic. Some weird timings on projects and tests (a pop quiz the class before the midterm exam, seriously?) but otherwise a generous grader and always willing to help.

One of the most boring and unhelpful professors ever. Lectures are horrible and she assumes you know everything and are a total genius after she explains something poorly once. BUT the homework and exams are super easy if you review slides, and the actual work portion of this class has been nonexistent. The work is easy she just sucks at teaching.

Definition of a mid prof. Assigments are short, easy, and sparse which is good. There are 4 pop quizzes which aren't bad if you are paying attention and doing minimal studying (they're predictable). The content can be tough but that isn't her fault. She made CSO one of my easiest classes even though she isn't the best, and I am grateful for that.

She's fine person, rally really nice and patient for the questions. BUT!! She does provide any feedback on assignment, exam, quiz, especially the pop quiz!! She do knows every thing about the content of the course, but she've assumed all the students had known everything, so she don't teach anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a fine lecturer, and clearly knows the information that she is is teaching. However, she provides minimal feedback on assignments and none on exams, does not answer her emails, and takes almost a month to return exam grades. She even mutes students while on Zoom so as to "avoid distraction." She's fine, but wouldn't be my first choice.

Professor is a nice person. However, her exam is too much HARD! Java basic is not hard at all, but she likes giving exam about the concepts she didn't interpret clearly during lecture. Sometimes the confused and hard concepts she quickly went through in the last lecture will appear on the final exam.... !! No exam example questions!!!

Professor Kayar is good, but not amazing. She's very kind and a lenient grader. However, I don't think her teaching is the best; it gets the job done but I was often confused and had to study on my own to understand what she was trying to explain. I would still take her since she is a nice knowledgable lady.
really nice and very accessible by email outside class. willing to answer any questions you have
Great professor, very patient and caring during office hours, and gives out clear lectures.

Solid professor - had her online. Slides had good examples and were generally easy to follow, although her explanations might be a little vague. Might not be too responsive to her emails. I recommend familiarizing yourself with Java basics before going into the course. Assignments and tests sometimes vague, but those answers are very open-ended.

A great professor who is both caring and knowledgeable. The recordings of the class are posted onto Brightspace, but you're better off just going to class in person because it's much easier to ask questions that way. Weekly assignments/quizzes are manageable and exams are fair.

Professor Kayar is a great professor, super helpful and willing to set aside one on one time to help you if you are struggling. She has clear lectures and homework assignments, and very fair exams. Lectures are supplemented by the textbook, but not a requirement to read the textbook to succeed in class

70% no reply to your email. Not accessible at all. Different policies toward two sessions but she still thinks she's fair enough. Also, strong accent. If you want to take this class, get ready to learn by yourself and hope you will not encounter any problems for the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The grading rubric is very clear, and you get graded on completion. If you do all the work, then you get a B in the class, and you can do 3 extra credit assignments, such as going to the writing center or attending an event outside of class, and writing a reflection to get an A. Such an engaging and easy class, totally recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She does give quite some work however the class is labor based meaning everything is based on completion and you just have to do 3 bonus assignments which can be like going to the writing center or reflecting on the course. She's very sweet and accessible you can tell she just wants you to be a better writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Truly a kind professor who just wants her students to become better writers. Yes, there's a lot of work, but it usually isn't super challenging.

LOVED HER. I took her class twice and would take it again if I could. She really wants you to learn and use your creativity rather than a hard grader. She is very understanding and picks great books to read.

Class was contract graded, assigns a heavy workload but she's super sweet and actually wants her students to succeed. You have to meet with her multiple times during the semester. Very seminar style, you have to talk.

Genuinely wants her students to improve, be engaged and enjoy what they're writing about. You get an A just for doing the work. You chose your own final project topic + she has individual meetings during the semester to give feedback and just check in. Mandatory reading and can be a lot at times, but the texts she chose were always interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's super nice but don't be fooled the work load is not worth it. Unless you love English and writing I suggest you take any other writing class. TOO MUCH WORK!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Listen to the other posts, dont take her unless you want to be wasting all your time on a mandatory writing class. So much homework (LONG ESSAYS) and readings, and presentation FOR A WRITING CLASS... Expects you to participate and is not lenient with grades. Just save yourself the energy and choose a different professor....

This was probably one of the worst professors I've taken at nyu. She is very inflexible and assigns so much work. I don't think the other reviews are genuine because they are completely false. I would highly recommend avoiding her as a professor if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not sure where these other reviews are coming from.. Srsly taking another professor would've been so much easier. So. much. work. If you listen to the reviews be prepared for so much extra work that you could've avoided by taking another professor and still receiving an A

Professor Hendrickson is a really caring professor. There is a lot of homework but she was willing to remove some of the assignments and adjust the syllabus. It's a pretty straightforward path to getting an A as long as you follow what's on the grading contract. Class discussions are always open and welcoming. Definitely recommend taking her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't listen to the 5 star reviews. TAKE ANOTHER PROFESSOR. She give SO SO much more work than other professors. She has grading contract for B, but to get an A is SO much extra work that you could have gotten easily with another professor. Sure, take her if there are no other professors left and the ones remaining have horrible RMF ratings.
Professor Hendrickson is very caring and allows students to share their opinions without judgment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Hendrickson is an amazing professor who really cares about her students. Her grading criteria is great, she has engaging readings, and discussions in class. The prompts for essays, discussion posts, and creative responses are very clear so there is never any confusion. She goes in the direction that her students want. Extremely genuine!

Really good and responsible professor. Take her if you feel okay with contemporary Latin-American Literature. Sometimes in-class discussions can be a little dry but overall it is pretty good. She really tried to get us into multiple writing genres. Just don't forget about the discussion posts.

Professor Hendrickson is by far the best professor I've had. You can tell that she really cares about her students and places emphasis on guiding them through the class. Participation is very important, but she creates a very welcoming environment, so it is very easy to participate. I would highly recommend taking Professor Hendrickson!
Smart, caring, clear, helpful, accessible, and patient. Most well-rounded professor of all time.

Zhao is an amazing teacher and works through problems with students in recitation and is always happy to answer questions outside of class too. With his capabilities he should be in charge of the lectures too tbh. Very kind and patient guy, do whatever you can to get into his section!
I am naming my first born son after Hong Zhao. He is the man, the myth, the legend! Helped me get an A in Orgo 1.

I know other people love him but I didn't have a good experience. Was always very pessimistic and condescending. Would laugh when I asked questions and always said things like “you should be doing this in your sleep by now” about concepts we were all struggling with. Didn't love that, he explained things well though, after laughing at you
So kind and willing to help, explains very very complicated concepts in a succinct and easy to understand way. Take Zhao for Orgo recitation if you can. He is wonderful!
Take his class cuz he's one of the most caring and intelligent professors. He is the reason that you will pass orgo!

Hong is truly a gem within the orgo dept! Please take him for either recitation or lab!! Super lenient and fair grader and his explanations to difficult concepts are amazing and have helped me learn so much. He's a super nice and easygoing prof.
Super nice and caring professor! Highly recommend him to everyone who is taking orgo :)

The absolute best recitation leader you could have for orgo. He goes over everything that will be on the quizzes and makes sure we all understand the material. So patient and explains things very clearly. Had a near perfect quiz average because of him. Absolutely recommend!

Professor Zhao is the best recitation instructor for orgo, (great combination with Weck) he goes over all the materials that will be on the quiz, and hold extra office hours before each exam. Would definitely recommend taking him at all costs.

Zhao and Weck is the best combination for orgo 1!! You can understand everything you don't from orgo lecture after going to Zhao's recitation. He makes everything clear and simple, and makes sure everyone understands the topics before moving on. Best recitation instructor.
He is the most nice and best professor! Like he is the reason you will pass orgo.

Dr. Zhao is absolutely wonderful! He is by far the best professor I've ever had. His recitation reviews are amazing and he helps clarify all the dense course material from the main lecture. He genuinely cares about your well-being inside and outside of class - his office hours are a game-changer!

Prof. Zhao is one of the best chem TA's I've ever had. He's accessible via email, and answers things clearly and patiently. He's always willing to help no matter the question and it's important to feel comfortable asking questions in Orgo. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Zhao is the kind of professor you want. Explains all the concepts clearly, including the key points + some more difficult concepts with plenty of examples. Doesn't get too theoretical with orgo, focuses on the stuff you need to know. Understanding and kind, always patient with questions. A generous grader. His office hour is at a bad time, though.

Actually, a wonderful professor! I'm happy that I had him for my first semester. He is so understanding. There are only three examinations throughout the semester, no attendance requirements, no participation points, and no quizzes or exams.
Hong is the best prof/TA I have ever had. He's super nice and always there to answer my questions. He is not just a teacher but a friend :))

Zhao is an insanely good teacher who you must take to learn Orgo. Labs are the easiest to follow I have ever seen & super interesting. You must register for his recitation because it's too good! He breaks down all the concepts and always answers questions compassionately. He is very funny and you can always tell he knows what he is talking about.
Actual god tier at teaching, maybe the best i've ever had. He's so clear at explaining complicated subjects and is super accessible during office hours. just a great dude

Not gonna lie, prof. Zhao is definitely one of the best professors I have ever taken. He explains super well and will upload all his lectures in a summarized version as well. He gives practice exams that have the exact same type of questions as the regular exam. Prof. Zhao is very approachable and caring, always open to questions and suggestions.
Honestly goated lab instructor, if you're reading this Hong good shit.

Hong is an amazing recitation leader! Only graded on attendance/completion, and he essentially just walks the class through the worksheet. Super helpful for reinforcing the material learned in lecture. As a lab professor he can be a little scattered, but he is in charge of all of the TAs. he is good at answering questions and very helpful!
amazing recitation leader for orgo. weekly problem sets graded on completion not accuracy, basically gives you all the answers. take him!

reviews.comment: One of the greatest. He doesn't use PPT but notepad instead, so you could review it on zoom if you miss the class. The class does not require attendance and does not have anyhomework. Exams are easy since it allows you to bring a one-page note with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Hong is by far one of the best lab instructor for Orgo. He gives excellent feedback on your post-labs and is lenient with the grading, but you still have to put in the effort. In addition, he helps you go over lecture topics during lab, when the experiment takes time. Definitely a solid choice for people wishing to pass the lab component!
Hong is super clear and chill. Probably one of the best ORGO TAs. I'm taking him again for ORGO II
Best Organic Chem TA ever! Take him if you can!
He is so sweet and caring! I have him this semester as my TA. Get him if you can!

Hong was my TA for organic chemistry. Such a great guy; always helpful and an easy grader (he had the highest average out of the TAs). I understand so much more just because of him. I also loved listening to his experiences doing lab research. He made orgo lab so much more enjoyable. Overall an amazing guy. Get him if you can!

Younger guy, very nice, cares about his material. Two essays, a midterm, and a final. Content was dense at times, but was never too bad for anything contributing to your grade. Took this class and International Economics in the same semester - similar content, liked the cross over. Highly recommend!

Considering the fact that I have no background in economics, this class was taught very well and I learned a lot. He's great at explaining dense topics and the case studies were super interesting/relevant, especially the last few weeks (populism, climate change, MNCs, China). he was helpful in office hours / email too.

This was Professor Hai's first semester teaching undegrad students since he earned his PHD, and he is already one of the best professors in the department. If you are interested in how economics and finance influence politics, take his course. He is a great lecturer, includes relevant topics, and the textbook he assigned was very informative.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you participate in the lecture discussions and do the readings, you're gonna love the course. He tries to get good discussions going in class, the grading for the midterm and final essay is kind of all over the place though
His feedback is kinda unclear but if you manage to incorporate it, it's an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think Halperin was a decent professor. He values participation and will let you know in the midterm check if he wants to see you participate more. The more you participate, the better grade you get on the essays. As long as you participate and do assignments, you will get an A in 60% of the class. He cancelled class or ended early multiple times!
I had no idea what he was teaching or saying in class because of his accent. He has a very strong accent and is the worst at teaching. Just choose a different professor INDEED.

One of the worst teacher ever in my life. He's definitely a very tough grader and he has a lot of expectations from students. He also takes participation very very seriously. I would definitely not recommend at all ever because he barely or never gives A in class. In fact, no one received "A" in the first exam. Never take this class!!!!

Provides clear explanations and breaks down what he means by each requirement in the syllabus. Really values communication and participation in class. Definitely attend office hours with the TA for helpful advice on essays and to talk through ideas. Be prepared to speak about texts every class and specific when writing essays & thesis statements.

Like all other commerce and culture professors, he is a tough grader but overall a nice professor. Make sure to participate and actually read the assigned books and watch the films and you'll be fine. Interesting discussions in class and he'll even break down some questions if no one raises their hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters
