reviews.comment: Uninteresting lectures with barebones slides, doesn't post important information online, doesn't respond to emails, doesn't give feedback on hw past the second week of class, barebones and unhelpful notes on essays, and grades harshly
Not super engaging, really lecture-heavy, and tough grader. The amount of work however is very doable.

I enjoyed this class. While there are a couple of discussion boards and in-class worksheets, he keeps you engaged. The readings are relatable, and he makes it a comfortable environment to participate in.

His class is nearly entirely discussion-based, and how interesting it is depends on how many people participate. Your grade is based on essays, participation, and assignments graded on completion. He only gave at most 2 A's per essay and his grading requirements can be very pedantic.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He yelled at me in class multiple times and doesn't care about your life. He refused to give me an extension even if I have Moses center approved letter.

Very tough grader. The similar effort I put on another course would get at least an A-. Lecture is really boring he needs to figure out how to improve it. His slides look like they are from the 90s. But I guess he is a fine person though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting conversations in class but extremely hard grader. Didn't give any feedback on journals and doesn't really help during the writing process of the essays. His comments on essays also don't make sense all the time and seem very subjective. Did not really improve as a writer from this class. Also was not accommodating for religious things.
Dismissive, unprepared, and clueless
Amazing lectures but he is a difficult grader. I doubt he gives more than two or three As per exam/paper. I feel like I learned a lot

solid straightforward class. pay attention in lecture because main points will end up in the midterm/final (which are heavily graded). you have to write a lot/overemphasize points in the papers to get a good grade. nice guy but hates phones and lateness
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: STS2144 Ethics and Tech. Do not take him. The guy takes a useless woke required course way too seriously. For a subject that's supposed to be a GPA boost. Utterly useless. Unclear grading and his lectures are very unnecessary and boring. A waste of time. Nice guy but what does that matter if it helps no one.

Course material was interesting and he explains it in an engaging way, but your grade is really dependent on the midterm exam and final paper. He's a tough grader but he makes the class interesting, for written assignments you really have to over-explain your arguments or he takes off points
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst grader on papers and provides vague feedback. Reading heavy and overall just boring lecture, not engaging would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Halperin was very kind and very accessible. He wanted every student to be successful no matter what. He loves participators so make sure you participate.
Professor Halperin is very responsible and is willing to help you during office hours. However, he is a harsh grader.

Big ego, unclear feedback, no rubrics for assignments, no online syllabus, unrealistic expectations, (especially for people new to journalism) and the thing about getting one grade for the whole semester is true.

I respect Professor Hochwald; she cares deeply for her students. However, you either understand the advice she gives or you don't. Prepare to focus on this course, as there will be a lot of trial and error when writing your first stories. There are last-minute print jobs, outdated resources, and no online resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved her class! She didn't have favorites, the whole class felt fairly equal and participated greatly in discussions. You do have to do a lot of outside work and reporting. If it's your first journalism class brace yourself to jump right in, but as someone who had a bit of prior experience, it was nothing crazy & great exposure to the field!

Overall, great professor that knows a lot, so be ready to intake a lot of information fast. I was able to learn A LOT. Weekly deadlines. You WILL HAVE TO interview people! If you're ready to get engaged and out there, this class is perfect. Lots of fun conversations and events! 10/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Learned alot, but tough grader. Once you get your first grade, you will recieve that grade for the rest of the semester. Provides little to no explanation on it, and is not fair. Has favorites and treats them differently. Dont take her class.

She was great at introducing different types of writing, and really pushed us to go out and do our own reporting which was a ton of fun. I greatly improved my writing and reporting skills in this class. 
Her feedback wasn't always the best, but she helped me find a passion for journalism and learn more about New York City. Definitely recommend.

This summer class proved invaluable as a journalist. Hochwald's real-world expertise made a six-week course into a richer experience than a full semester. Field trips to interview businesses, politicians, and a Food Network editor were transformative. I highly recommend her comprehensive journalism education catering to all levels of expertise.

Kind-hearted! She loves when students reach out. If you're thinking about expanding your network and getting more opportunities in journalism, she'll love to help you. Her classes are very dynamic: she invites different guests ranging from social media managers to politicians; and she also takes students to different field trips. Take her class!

BEST professor I've ever taken in NYU, period. In a semester, she transformed me from a total noob in journalism to someone comfortable reporting and writing journalistic pieces. She really paved my path and ignited my passion in journalism.

Professor Hochwald really taught me how to write as a journalist. She does a lot of hands-on teaching, and is very encouraging of us to go out and do reporting. Gives good feedback on your weekly stories. Can sometimes give impossible deadlines (ie a story in an hour in class) but overall is very caring of her students and taught me so much.

Yeah, don't take this class. Got an A, but at what cost? Worst professor and class at nyu especially for starting off in journalism. Made me want to switch majors. Don't know why she's allowed to teach. Don't believe the 5 stars.

Got an A but hated this class. Don't believe the good reviews. She tells her favorites to go on here and post. Tough grader without explaining her logic. Unnecessarily difficult assignments that don't help you grow. Has the biggest ego ever. She also said I treat everyone well, "even prostitutes." Um, why do you have to say that if you do?

I absolutely loved Hochwald's JOUR 101 class. A lot of the work done is real-world experience; you are taught the basics of interviewing and are expected to interview someone every class, (this may turn away some people, but I loved the experience). Also be prepared to write news stories every class, your writing will greatly improve as a result.

I took Professor Hochwald's class during the Summer session, and I have no regrets! She is a caring and devoted professor. Her course was challenging but the knowledge acquired from her assignments is so worth it. I got out of my comfort zone, and would have never done so without her care and encouragements. The best professor in the department.

I took Hochwald over a year ago and it's one of the worst classes I've taken at NYU in any major. While she seems okay in class, she truly doesn't have any consideration for outside issues students may be dealing with. Also, she's a tabloid journalist and her feedback made me a worse writer. Assignments were busy work and her grading was ridiculous
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: dropped my journalism major because of her and retracted all my journalism internship applications because she killed any interest I had in a career, so that sums it up.

Don't believe the good reviews about her- I'm pretty sure she writes them herself as she literally told us in class to please go & give her a good review on rate my professor which means she knows this page exists and frequently looks at it. They all also say similar things. But she's fake, harsh, gives no good advice at all, and has a massive ego

Professor Hochwald was hands down the most life changing professor I've had! She was my first journalism professor and the class was my first to present a challenge (to be honest), but one I was excited to take. Professor Hochwald was constantly there. She answered all my questions quickly. She pushed us all out of our comfort zones! 100% recommend

Professor Hochwald was a great professor. She was a tough grader, but as you progress over the semester, you can see yourself improving as a writer because of her feedback. Would definitely recommend anyone to take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Hochwald is the worst professor I had at NYU. Her class made me switch out of journalism and I blame her singlehandedly. Unnecessarily hard, doesn't give feedback or constructive criticism, just gives out bad grades and says your writing needs to get better - alright, how?? She doesn't tell you. Would never recommend her. SEEK ELSEWHERE

I loved this class! Prof Hochwald was extremely accommodating of the online situation and of my lack of journalism knowledge. She was always available for emailed questions and live edits, showing just how dedicated she was to helping us grow. Her experience allowed us to interview several fascinating special guests and get real industry insight.

Professor Hochwald was the most uncompromising, unaccommodating professor I have had. She is extremely inflexible and even when a pandemic started in the middle of our course and we all moved across the country, she did not change her already extremely tough standards. I would never recommend this course if you care at all about your mental health
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Hochwald is sincerely a great teacher. I took the class in the Fall of 2020, so we were online, and the course was perfectly tailored for it. It was clear that she really wanted us to still have a good experience even if we were online. I will say, make sure you're ready to write, you do a lot of it. Class isn't easy, but well worth it.

Professor Hochwald has left an amazing impact on both myself and my academics. She always made sure her class was positive and enjoyable, while pushing you to do your best. She makes such an effort to keep in touch with students, so willing to write letters of rec, and genuinely cares about her students' success both in the class and in the future.

I took her class in 2017; it gave me a great foundation for my journalism career. We gained real-world experience reporting in the field, spending some classes going out in different parts of NYC to do man-on-the-street interviews and quickly write up stories. Class exercises were fun, and Prof. Hochwald is helpful and really cares about students.

She thinks so highly of herself but she is not a good teacher at all and most of the people in our class did not like her. She clearly has favourites and gives them As. It's so clear who she likes and who she doesn't. Worst journalism professor at NYU. Doesn't give helpful feedback and grades harshly for no reason

Professor Hochwald simply cares about the success of her students. Sure, there is homework, readings, and a final exam. And yes, the work is challenging. But the work is not challenging to the extent of inability. If you pay attention, do the work and ask questions -- not only will you excel in this course, but you will become a better journalist.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Hochwald is a phenomenal journalism teacher. She will give you all the skills you need for basic writing and reporting by just having you go out and learn by doing! She has amazing connections and I learned so much from her as well as the guest speakers she brought it about what journalism is like as a career. 100% recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Hochwald is one of the best professors at NYU. She is such a caring, funny, professional journalist who you can learn so much from. Anyone who is interested in journalism or wants to learn how to write professional articles should definitely take her class!

Lambeth is one of the best professors I have had at NYU. She gave our class lots of real-world knowledge to actually be able to find work, and she brought in some amazing guest lecturers pretty often. The class was really about growing and developing as a journalist-style writer and it was super eye-opening.

Prof. Hochwald is the best! We had courses go online this semester due to the pandemic, but she still managed to make everyone excited for class with PHENOMENAL guests and fun work. Definitely feel like I'm ready for a job in journalism, and this was just an intro class!! if you want an internship or journalism connections, TAKE HER CLASS

If you are serious about becoming a journalist, you need to take Prof. H's class. She's an EXPERT and has lots of connections. We took a trip to Hearst and met the EIC of HGTV along w/ many other successful journalists. She also cares about her students' success. Her feedback improved my writing/reporting skills so much! Best class I've ever taken!

Professor Hochwald is great! I expanded my knowledge from 0 to 100 throughout the semester. She is definitely a tough grader, but once you get a hang of the formula, you will do well. This course requires effort and passion. If you're up for it, take her class! You will get an incomparable insight into her field.

This course definitely expanded my knowledge of journalism and pushed me to go out and get actual experience reporting. While the grading was tough, professor Hochwald was readily available to meet and discuss ways to improve our writing going forward. It was very useful to get real life experience and do man on the street interviews.

Professor Hochwald encourages students to work hard and step outside their comfort zones, which certainly proves results by the end of the semester! I was first intimidated at the prospect of weekly reporting and interviewing, but throughout the course I found my confidence and writing skills significantly improving! Such an influential professor!!

Professor Hochwald is by far the best NYU jouralism professor I've ever had. Although the class is a lot of work, you will significantly improve your writing skills by the end. Prof. Hochwald pushes you outside of your comfort zone with weekly writing assignments and interesting in class lectures. The class is hard but extremely worth it!

Prof. Hochwald's class is for ambitious go-getters who are looking to improve their writing/reporting skills-- fast. You will be challenged, pushed outside your comfort zone and sometimes, very stressed. But you will come out of the class with refined writing & interviewing skills. (Don't be late to class, participate & reach out if you need help).

Professor Hochwald is one of the few professors at NYU who's truly pushed me to be a better writer. She's a tough grader, but your work will be so much better for it. She's also extremely accessible and genuinely cares about seeing her students grow and succeed. If you want to really get something out of Inquiry, take the class with her.

Professor Hochwald is a diligent, intelligent professor who doesn't beat around the bush. She teaches by throwing you into the fire of on-the-street reporting, and if you're okay with that you'll thrive. The courseload is occasionally heavy, but never overwhelming, and the material is up-to-date and always engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Hochwald is very good at what she does. Although sometimes her class may feel challenging, it is ultimately worth it and her grading is always fair. She genuinely cares about her students' growth as writers. As a bonus, you also get to go on cool and relevant field trips if you're in her class. Would recommend!

She grades tough just to grade tough. I got an ok grade in the class but had to work twice as hard for it in her 101 class then I did in my advanced Journalism courses which seems excessive. The news quizzes are impractical for people with busy schedules and frankly the course was a bit boring except the field trips
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's awesome. Very professional. Cool field trips and tries to push you out of your comfort zone. Great introduction to the world of professional journalism. INSPIRING! Made me want to be a journalist. Lots of assignments though, you really have to be interested in the subject. But she's a fair grader.

Professor Hochwald is FANTASTIC! She really tries to push her journalism students out of their comfort zone, which is exactly what a lot of journalism students need! She works very hard to emulate real-life journalistic experiences and does so very well. She is also a very fair grader. I learned SO much from her.

Professor Hochwald is not only a great Journalistic Inquiry teacher, she is also a working journalist who knows the business inside and out. Her in-class assignments make you work under deadline and she will always push you towards your best work. After you take her class, you'll know how to write a variety of articles, interview better and edit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The reason why I loved this class and the professor was due to the improvement I saw in my journalistic writing. Seriously, she will push you to go beyond your potential and I'll forever be grateful for that because now I am interning at a great publication. The skills you will learn are vital to your journalism career. Awesome guest lectures, too!

Professor Hochwald really helped me become a better journalist. She pushed us to go out of our comfort zone, for example interviewing random people on the streets. She also had a lot of connections in the industry, especially in the magazine industry. Definitely the best class I had last semester!

She was an amazing teacher. It was one of the only classes that I felt I actually learned something. There was never a dull class, she even invited professionals in the field that were truly inspiring!

Professor Hochwald was an amazing professor and really pushed our class to write quality pieces. She was extremely helpful, attentive to students outside of class and challenged us to do our best. I would 100% recommend her for journalistic inquiry.

Professor Hochwald explains things clearly, and with credibility, as she's a successful practicing journalist. She's extremely approachable and contributing in her class never felt intimidating--she incites easy conversation. I'd definitely take another one of her classes in the future.

Hochwald truly gave applicable journalism tips, especially if you're going into the magazine industry. She also has amazing contacts and experience and is always up to give feedback. She was always easy to reach through email and makes it her goal to see her students improve. Only complaint was clarity in assignments, but she improved my writing!

Professor Hochwald was a really great resource for me! She always made herself available, really cared about her students and had a lot of experience to draw from. She focused on learning applicable journalistic skills in class rather than focusing on small details. She's also just a great person!

THE WORST INQUIRY PROF ..do not take her class. she is so dumb, NYU has so many better professors to offer. it's a shame they waste the money on this lame prof with such little to offer. you will feel you lose a few more brain cells each day.

Lambeth wasn't the best teacher. Her comments and assignments weren't very helpful. I don't think she really taught me anything new. We had a lot of speakers share their interviewing experiences but most said, "You'll have to find out what works for you."  I feel that we wasted time.
Journalism classes are workshops and you get what you give. Lambeth offers top notch connections if you can figure out how to use them.
wasted a lot of time, seemed to forget specific instructions and was generally very unclear on assignments and presentations... She tried hard but I would not take another class with her

An excellent teacher! Encouraging, knowledgable, intelligent, professional, personable. Class was dynamic, assignments were fun, guest speakers were interesting. I loved going to this class, and my writing improved. Give this lady tenure!
No Comments

The best journalsim prof in the entire dept.willing to help you get JOBS gives CONTACTS she is the BEST A+ you have to work but it's all about helping you get the best grade she's also taught Magazine Article (another great A+ for her there)

The class was excellent, and the topics were interesting, but the TA was a VERY harsh grader. Would take it again if it was a different TA. And participation PLUS participation matters. They deduct an enormous amount of points if you only attend and do not participate.
My favorite professor at NYU. If she has a class open TAKE IT.

her lectures were good, covered lots of interesting topics. took this course because it fit my schedule and i knew nothing about the middle east, but learned a lot that was surprising and relevant. it totally matters who your TA is.

(CORE-500 Cultures and Context - Middle Eastern Cities)
The class was excellent, and the topics were interesting, but the TA was a VERY harsh grader. Would take it again if it was a different TA. And participation PLUS participation matters. They deduct an enormous amount of points if you only attend and do not participate.

The day we read and had a philosophical discussion about TikToks and memes, I was like, oh my god, this is the best. That's what MCC classes should be about! Also so cool that she let us do media-based projects and held virtual galleries to share. Great class.

Copy and Collage was interesting and fun. I love that she gave us a mini art history lesson, made us read, watch and listen to bunch of stuff, and gave us wide possibilities of creative and hands-on assignments. This was a great way to end my time at NYU, and even though it was good on Zoom, it made me wish we'd been live.

this was the first class that made things real and made me realize how interconnected everything in the world is; also learned some useful stuff that i'll always remember. class includes some good visits/trips; response papers; open flexible final projects. she seems like she'd be mean and tough but she's super chill
one of the few times i did a group project in a class and got something out of it. tough subject matter but she knows what she's talking about and she makes it interesting
awesome professor. i miss her!

grad seminar: we read an entire book every two weeks - great experience. laid back atmosphere in seminar yet informative. i'd never realize that the 2.5 hours flew by. she is also friendly, super generous, and humble.

Helga is by far the best teacher I've ever had in my life. She made me think and question like no other professor. I was both unlucky and lucky to have her as my teacher my first semester at NYU because she set the bar so high for all my future professors. I can't stress how much I learned from her and would highly recommend her to anyone.
hilarious. smart. friendly. funny. knowledgeable. intimidating. different.

she's different. she'll push you, she'll make you grasp, she'll overwork and overload you, there will never be enough time to discuss the millions of things that come up. but it's totally worth it. especially by the end, or much after class is over, you'll remember what she was trying to teach you all along.

Helga is the best. There are a lot of readings, some of which are dense, but they are informative and enjoyable. Her lectures are amazing. I wish I could listen to her lecture for hours on end. Friendly, hilarious, intelligent - one of the best professors at NYU.

Helga was extremely passionate. Most of our class was not too informed on international issues since we thought it was a Comm. class and she took the time to catch us up to speed and really cared about what she was teaching. Highly recommend her! Very helpful when you reach out to her.

Any class she teaches you should take. You'll come out so much more knowledgeable than you imagined, especially about current global events. She knows her stuff, extremely passionate, knowledgeable, down to earth, quite funny, and helpful if you ask. Readings and assignments can be hard but interesting.
Great professor. Great class.
Great professor, very knowledgeable as well as entertaining. No exams, but lots of reading and a ton of writing. The class was harder than I expected but I learned a lot.

awesome prof, makes interesting and controversial topics so much fun. brings in tons of examples from media that challenge stereotypes. she's tough but also understanding and super helpful. accessible too, although may not seem so when you first meet her. totally recommend her no matter what she's teaching!
extremely knowledgeable and funny too. great prof and great class
Great Prof., Very accessible and helpful.
she is so cool!!!!!!!!!!!
No Comments

At the end of the course, he gave us graduation chords from Amazon. His favorite students got "better" ones than everyone else. These students are conservatives, btw. Easy class, though. His rhetoric is just Thomas Sowell x 10 and his teaching is so nonsensical that it's easy to figure out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He verbatim quotes Thomas Sowell during his lectures and is a "libertarian," but is ridiculously conservative and of course, close minded. This was an easy A for me because I just started writing and talking (low-key memeing) like a conservative, but if you don't know how to do that, don't take this class. Very lecture and reading heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All of the other ratings here pretty much have him spot on. He is extremely close-minded and grades his papers in that way, meaning if you disagree with his views you tend to score lower. But even aside from that, he is EXTREMELY unclear with regards to the assignments. By the end of the semester he had completely undermined his own syllabus. AVOID

Awful professor, opinionated, not compassionate, and is not willing to listen to any views which dont align with his own. Im someone who sticks to classes but i HAD to drop this and based on the other reviews im glad i did. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR

Stay away from this professor. I dropped his class after a couple of weeks and I am so glad I did. He said that humans are individualistic in nature, and I asked about collectivist societies. He said, "What about them?" and then proceeded to make fun of me to the class. He also made fun of other students when they asked questions. AVOID

This is by far the WORST class and I strongly advise NOT taking this course or any course taught by THIS professor. The negative comments below are correct! He claims to be a debate master. However, this is not accurate and he will not listen to any comments that do not align with his Extreme Right sided views. Life experience isn't enough. RUN!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: These reviews are a little exaggerated. Proff has a ton of life experience and knows what he is talking about. I have appreciated his perspective on the topic. However, it is challenging to be in class because he doesn't really allow his students to disagree with his perspective or even argue with him. The work itself is doable and not too bad.

Do not do it. Every time I leave this class I am so frustrated that I cry. He just rants for 75 minutes about his own poorly evidenced opinions and if any student tries to argue something he says, he shuts them down, despite being a "logician" that "loves debate". If I never have to hear the phrase "we are HUMAN" in my life again I would be lucky.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This professor lectures and tests on personal views and does not follow the literature on poverty. Grades essays in a format that will allow you to pass if you agree with his viewpoints. Exams are old school on paper/pencil. If your essay is not to his liking politically it will be graded poorly. Even though it is the argument you like to make.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is one of the most pointless classes Ive ever taken !!! Sometimes Im not even sure that the professor even knows what hes talking about . He just rambles on and on about nonsense. I dropped this class after a few weeks because I was genuinely confused and he has unrealistic expectations. Do yourself a favor and run as far away from this

STAY AWAY! Classes are extremely intense, and he has extremely controversial, and frankly problematic views, which are concerning when it comes to a topic like poverty. Does not allow you to critique his views, and doesnt seem very compassionate either. Dropped class after 2 weeks.

I ended up withdrawing from his class after a month. He approaches everything from a logic perspective and leaves no room for emotion, which is bound to come up when discussing poverty. He tears apart the authors of the readings he assigns, but does not allow you to critique his own views. Has VERY controversial views on the causes of poverty.

The exams (60% of your grade, all free response) are super heavy on memorization of facts, places, things, and years. And that information is nowhere on the slides (usually just pictures), so you better hope that you have good notes because the grading isn't lenient. I and several of my classmates had the worst exam grade of our life in this class.

Course is not very organized, but workload is nonexistent. All you need to do is memorize the names, facts, and significance of archaeological sites and a handful of important concepts covered in lecture for the exams. A few chances for extra credit. Very light, but not an easy A as you still have to study. Overall a decent choice for soc sci core.

Not very engaging, and the lectures are essentially just images with no captions, names or dates that he will expect you to memorise and discuss in detail on exams. The course itself is not very well organised and professor provides very little framework to think about the VAST amount of information you are expected to internalise.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A kind, knowledgable, + accessible professor. I think he is a quiet lecturer who is not super engaging. Try not to skip lectures since he goes over a lot of info that's not on the slides (they're basically just pictures). A *lot* of memorization, tests weighed 60% of final grade and I spent quite some effort studying. Don't take if you want easy A.

Prof Iovita is clearly an expert in his field, but he forgets that he's teaching an intro-level class with students who have no idea what he's talking about. Harsh grader on tests and expects you to remember a tiny details. Also the textbook covers a lot of material that you need to take notes for. TAKE HUMAN EVOLUTION BEFORE TAKING THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My least fav class of sem. He spoke so quietly & lectured the whole time. Said we needed no pre-reqs but each week would talk about how we should already know things he was referencing. Final paper is on nothing he covers, it's 15 pgs of research on anything. He's nice, but all the readings are very data heavy. Don't take unless you're in anthro
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: IGNORE OTHER REVIEWS, unless you're reading for the drama. This is one of the most interesting, funny and help professors at NYU. He is passionate, caring and more than willing to work with students.

Professor Iovita is incredibly knowledgeable about the subject, and his lectures and discussion classes reflect this. The readings assigned are very interesting, but do require engagement. Additionally, Professor Iovita is generous with his time and his office hours are very helpful. Overall, this class was fascinating and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof Iovita has a deep command of the subject matter, and the time he takes into preparing for lectures--even online ones--really shows. There's a steady stream of work--you can't coast, but the work pays dividends. He draws connections between the big questions in the field--which are big questions about life--and the reading for each week.

It might be bc we're online, but it was really disappointing, I would've thought a class on migration would be a lot more interesting. It was an endless cycle of reading 4-6 10pg papers, writing a response every week to them, and a lecture/discussion about what we read. There's also two 10 page essays as a midterm/final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: The class wasn't super hard, just go to lecture and pay attention you should be fine. However Radu is the most egotistical narcissistic human on the planet. Seriously very rude, never want to interact with that dude again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The midterm was 30% and final 40% of the grade (30% for lab) which makes this class very difficult because your grade relies almost entirely on the exams. He was new to teaching Early Societies and Culture so I think thats why, however he's very enthusiastic about what he's teaching and I never dreaded going to his lectures

Okay prof. The class really isn't AS hard as other people are saying - you just need to go to every lecture and pay attention/take notes and actually listen to what he says. The tests are stressful, but not impossible (and he's very generous with grading). Didn't even touch the textbook - didn't need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I thought I'd wait until after the final to post. This was ridiculous for an intro course. It's not that the material is that difficult to digest -- it's that Radu gives no guidance in terms of what to study. His tests are practically impossible to prep for, and 2 exams  70% of your grade. The TA's are great. He's unhelpful. I did well, but no.

If you're not an Anthro major, don't take class with Radu. His lectures involve quite a bit of rambling, he's non-specific about what'll be on the midterm or final. His TA's are wonderful. But unless you want to memorize an entire textbook and half a semester's worth of lectures for a test with 14 questions on it, take another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Radu seems very passionate about his field, but for a non-anthro major taking the course as a core requirement, it could be intense at times. Go to lectures... the tests are almost entirely on the material covered in lectures (and the slides he posts won't be v. helpful since there are few words). TAs very nice, and little weekly work, just tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR!!!! would take it again if I had the chance. Can tell he's very passionate about the subject matter and knows a lot about it too. Always added a layer of depth to the lessons and course!
he is the best professor

Professor Isikara is very understanding. He explains concepts very well, and I have learned a lot from him. He makes sure that class is not an added stressor. The quizzes we have are online, our assignments are group ones, and the exams are reflective of what we do in class.

Great professor, explains everything well and sets students up for success
Has a good personality as well

Professor Isikara was super understanding, and tried to make the best of online classes. He gives extra credit and does everything he can to make sure his students get As. His assignments mirror the midterm and final, so studying those and participating almost guarantees an A. He is very smart, but his lectures can be kind of slow and boring.

Great Professor. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches and genuinely wants students to understand the topics and concepts. Quizzes, midterm, and final are online. If you have to take econ in LS, TAKE HIM!!!!!!

My favorite course yet! I loved how Prof.Guney teaches orthodox economic theories prefacing and post-facing the assumptions, and even implications of economic assumptions. Many other economic classes often end up technical-heavy, but he facilitates discussions of social welfare and environmental justice––which I appreciate a lot! Learned a lot.

Great prof. Explains everything well, takes the time to answer questions, always reachable, and tests are online. He is relatable but very professional, explaining concepts super clearly. Make sure to just listen in class and everything will be clear after his lecture.
He's a great professor. Midterm and final were online, and he gives students options for extra credit. Take him.

Professor Isikara is very passionate about his subject. If you do not may attention during lectures you are screwed but he makes sure that his lectures are very interactive and engaging and if you genuinely have an interest in Economics and want to take it with a professor who cares take his class. The Midterm was very long but open note to be fair

Super great, he does take home test and quizzes as well as giving a week for assignments that are done in a group. Really recommend if you need to take an economics class, participation and effort goes a long way with him.

Took Intro to Micro with Isikara. Explains concepts really well, and tries to make content more interesting by bringing real-world case studies and issues. 

Assignments aren't particularly difficult, and if you do the readings/pay some attention in class, workload is totally manageable. 

Very solid class, would def recommend.

Professor Isikara is a great professor. He truly cares about the things he teaches, and wants the students to understand it. He has a very interesting socio-political approach in economics. Overall, if you need to take economics in LS, take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Isikara is one of the most caring and understanding teachers I have had at NYU so far. His lectures are clear and provide great resources for outside class material access, including copies of all slides, lectures, and Zoom recordings. I highly recommend you take his class if it is an option! He works hard to make sure his students are ok

I really enjoyed taking microeconomics with Prof Isikara. Prof Isikara gave wonderful lectures that put a social and historical spin on economics. The class involves four group projects, which were very accessible and fair, as well as open-note quizzes and exams. Attendance and a little participation is important. Highly recommend.

Professor Isikara is the best professor I have ever had at NYU! I never thought econ would interest me but this ended up being my favorite class. He is so knowledgable and really cares about your learning. It's social and political approach to econ but I found that this approach made it more interesting.Take his class! I wish I could have him again

He really cares about providing comprehensive, engaging lessons. Microeconomics isn't always a fun subject but he tries to make it enjoyable for students. He takes time to explain concepts and ask for questions, sometimes the format/working of the quiz questions can be confusing but if you put in the work you can easily succeed.
the best teacher ive ever had at NYU, must take him because he's such a nice instructor.

I absolutely loved professor Isikara. The class really is designed to ensure that students thrive; he WANTS you to learn and get a good grade so he will go out of his way to make sure you do. Theres 4 group assignments (which are very easy), 4 multiple choice quizzes, midterm and final exam. Everything is open note. Definitely take him

Really nice guy, lectures are super straightforward, and he explains everything really well. He's clearly designed this class for students to do well in, just read the textbook (for your own sake if you are interested in econ) and you will most definitely get an A in this class. There is a midterm, final, 3 online quizzes and 4 group assignments.
What an incredible professor. If you have the chance, take him! He opened my eyes to a completely new type of Economics and made the class interesting. I wish I could take him for all four years.

Absolutely wonderful teacher. One of two profs I've had at NYU that's a 10/10. Truly passionate, cares about making his lessons interesting... if you want to start economics, and if you like participating, please take his class, because he's incredible.

Awesome guy. You can skim the readings, he goes over material a lot. He loves to relate textbook stuff to current events/progressive economic ideas, which makes class really fun; engage with him for sure. Exams/quizzes are fair, but questions are not too easy, you do have to prepalso, the time limits are the hardest part, make sure to go quick.

The prof gives a nice and interesting textbook with paragraphs corresponding to lectures, so it's enough just to either listen or read. He is nice and accessible. 4 quizes, 4 group projects and that's it, the exams are similar to them and graded not strictly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Isikara is one of the best professors at NYU! The course guidelines were clear right from the beginning. He makes sure each and every student understands the economic concepts clearly. Very caring, an easy grader, and makes the subject extremely interesting! One tip: The more you participate in lectures, the more fun you will have!

had him for my intro to econ LS course. All in all, excellent professor. Wasn't too fond of econ in HS but he really takes the time to introduce what many would consider as an otherwise tedious course to learn. Just participate, actually study with a friend or something and DO THE EXTRA CREDIT. As long as you work, you'll get an A.

He is honestly the best professor I have had at NYU. He is always available to talk to and really explains everything so clearly that you dont even need the textbook. He will make you work your ass off for a good grade and his homeworks/quizzes are hard/fair.

Course has very clear guidelines and assignment/quiz/exam dates are charted out from day one. Easily accessible through e-mail and office hours. Participation matters but can come in the form of forum posts, speaking in class, etc. Exams, group assignments, and quizzes all open note and fairly easy. Lenient and kind. Don't need to read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easily one of the best teachers I have ever had. Super caring, always accessible outside of class, and an amazing person to have a conversation with. Readings are optional (but if you've never taken econ like me) they are SUPER helpful when following the lecture. Because its blended he grades on participation, but office hours satisfy that. study!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course material itself is not too hard, but he makes everything clear and understandable. Love the amazing analysis and "rants" he goes on in class about the defects of capitalism. Learned more than just boring textbook economics, he gave many relevant outside examples. Helps the student see the world of economics from a different perspective.

She gives you a decent amount of work but she is a nice teacher and it is fairly easy to get an A. I revised one of my drafts in like 30 minutes and she gave me a 92. You will have to read out loud and talk to others tho.

Tough grader, but amazing professor. She really cares about you and has good exercises to improve. Attendence is mandatory, but if you're actually sick and usually go to class she'll let some stuff slide.
I took her over the summer and she was an amazing professor. She genuinely cares about the students and tries her best to be understanding.

Great Professor, she was very kind. There will be a lot of group discussions, but most discussion topics are very interesting. If you tell her any concerns with your essay during your meetings, she will help you tremendously. Like every writing class, be prepared to read. She gives enough time for assignments. She has the best style of clothes!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The assignments given are simple and help build up towards your greater progression; however, they may be quite lengthy. Whatever effort you put into the exercises, she will notice and keep it in mind. She is very accessible during office hours and offers good feedback. Attendance and assignment completion is considered in your final evaluation.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you put in the work, class becomes fun and the homework becomes very straightforward.
You need get get an 96% or above to get an A in this class. Lenient but also strict at times. Very emotional and takes things personally.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Classes were much more interesting than my other writing professors, but she is a really tough grader. Isn't explicit about what she wants. There is an insane workload, and I felt like a literature major by the end of the semester. She offered a lot of extra credit though, and I think most people got Bs and As.

Don't know why she gets such a low score. She definitely deserve a five. Reasonable workload and fair grading. Care about students very much and would accept late work if the accuse is reasonable. Love this professor!!
She is nice and accessible Outside of the Class however she gives lot of homework. Could give better feedback. You need to work a lot if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think Professor Im is a great Expos professor. She cares for students and gives meaningful feedback. Her class was not boring because there were many discussion periods with your groups about your readings and essays. Also, she had a clear grading chart of essays and assignments. Lastly, she gave a total of 3 extra credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a responsible prof, but is really strict in grading. It's impossible to get an A in her class. Normally, we get a B -. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, but she has so many assignments to the point where you start feeling like you are majoring in English with a minor in entrepreneurship. She's also a super tough grader, so do the ECs and get as much feedback as possible. What's super cool is that she is willing to write recommendation letters for everyone at the end!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took the new pilot course for entrepreneurship with her. Let's just say she's a VERY tough grader, which you can especially feel if you had a wonderful professor in EXPOS-UA 1. Don't rely on her initial draft comments!! How much ever encouraging she might seem initially, she ends up being rough on your final grade (always go to her office hours).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professors I've had so far. She is helpful both in and out of class. She often holds office hours to talk about essays. She offered extra credits twice last semester, which is very important in a writing class. She also offered letters of recommendation to the entire class at the end of the semester.

I thought I would have a hard time based on the rates. But it turned out that Professor Im is awesome. She put high expectations on students and I really learned a lot. She cares students and meeting with her is very helpful. Plus, she would give extra credit once or twice per semester.

Jeannie has a bad rep, but I actually thought her class was ok. Yes, you'll have to turn in papers but she outlines her grading criteria clearly and the reading isn't even that bad. She's nice and cares about her students, and even offered my entire class rec letters. If you're choosing between her and the other "bad profs" definitely go with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Im is one of the few best professors I have come across in my freshman year. I love how she challenges her students to become best writers. Of course, she holds her students to a high standard, while at the same time showing them the best route to achieve it.

Has high expectations for her students. Comments on papers are clear and helpful. Assignment (class/hw) instructions are sometimes vague, but she doesn't mind clarifying when asked. Conferences are extremely helpful. Rarely gives extensions for assignments, but will make an exception if you're struggling. Her "talking down" attitude is nonexistent.

Didn't like her at the start of the semester; Noticed she talks down to students and she's rude. You get used to that. The assignments are specific and extensive, however, if you do them correctly it entails everything she would want in the final essay. Meetings are very helpful, she'll tell you exactly what she wants. Work with the writing center.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She talks down to you, is unclear what she wants in the essays and good luck trying to get an appointment for office hours. Her writing classes are her priority, not this class. I have no ideas how my grade is determined. She is nice though.

When I first signed up for this class, I thought I Was going to have a bad time based on the reviews. However, after taking WTE with her first semester, I was completely wrong. Her assignments and essay prompts are clear, and is very willing to help if you want it. I am assuming the other reviewers did not take this class much seriously.
she is very tough and unfriendly. I would not recommend taking her class

She might be the worst professor I've had so far. Her approach in lecture and writing critique is layered with pretension. It gets even worse because, if you start running into problems (like people do), she begins to become very dismissive. Stay on her good side or else she won't even try to help you in class. Just use the Writing Center for help.

Although it often seemed like she was talking down to the students in my class, she honestly made me a better writer. She helped me on every essay and I was able to raise my grade drastically. GO TO THE WRITING CENTER for every essay if you can because they're sooo helpful. (I wish I had before the end of the semester)

It sucks that you have  an assignmentdue  every class; however,  that is not Jeannie's fault. She's a great teacher and has helped my writing improved. She's not rude, more like sarcastic. People have forgotten to turn in assignments and she'll still grade it. She's intimidating but you'll learn alot talking to her. She also brings treats!

This professor was not clear on what she wanted, but wasn't very helpful in getting us to that point. She expected a lot from us (for example assigning us to watch a 2 hr. film 2-3 times on Mon., with a 12 paragraph response due Wed. during midterm week). Overall not a great professor, not very polite. Knows what she's talking about but not helpful

In my experience Im isn't an easy grader, but she's definitely clear on what she wants and grades fairly based on those principles. email-wise her response isn't fast, but were helpful. Grades depend on what you put into it and how well you follow the instructions. Also, her criticisms can be super blunt borderline rude but be sure to follow them!

Firstly, this professor was amongst the rudest I've ever had. Furthermore, she often refused to explain vague statements or prompts. Her grading was tough, but it wasn't as arbitrary as other WTE professors' policies. She never responds to emails regardless of the circumstance. I would strongly recommend searching for a different professor.

While everyone complains about how hard this class is and how mean Professor Im is, she is actually a really good teacher. My writing has improved tremendously and that is saying a lot for me. TIPS: don't fall asleep in class, she will call you out. do not be obnoxious, she will hate you. pretend that you have interest and she will like you.

She's not helpful at all.  Very rude and totally ridiculous.  By the end of the class everyone stopped trying because they felt pleasing her would be impossible.  She is very pretentious and an unnecessarily harsh grader.
She is a very self-righteous teacher and continually gets mad or frustrated when we do not know answers to her questions. She is not an encouraging teacher and I would really not recommend her.

Professor Im is tough but my writing has improved a lot. She really appreciates students who contribute to discussions. Don't be sarcastic or funny in your writing--that's not the point of this class. If you don't like to be picked on, don't talk in class for the first two weeks. ALWAYS GO TO CLASS or else she will call you out publicly.

Very challenging class, but I have to say my writing improved so much. This class definitely is worth the money and she plans out each lesson very carefully. Take from Prof. Im if you actually want to learn something.

This Professor is not helpful or understanding.  Her instructions are vague.  I still do not understand what she wanted from my writing.  I spent tons of time on this class and only managed a C+.  Before this class I had a 3.86.  Take any professor but Jeannie Im.
This professor is not understanding , has poor manners and is not helpful nor clear.
Pretty self-righteous lady. Take a different WTE teacher. She's tough for no reason and used to be a TA for Renzi.

Really not that bad. Fun lecturer, but be organized in this class and make friends. Also, getting a good TA means the world! Ece Gurleyik was a tough grader! But really not that bad, just be organized, know deadlines, take notes, and you'll be fine. The tests are MCQ, not much writing heavy.

Professor Ali is a fantastic lecturer whose main shortcoming is the slides to match, get ready to listen well and take lots of notes. The readings are pretty technical and not as relevant as the lectures themselves. The only complaint I have is her attendance policy, however it isn't unusual.

if i can give a 0 i would. no study guides, no real slides (js pictures that did not make sense AT ALL if you don't take notes of every word she says), basically you cannot survive this course if you are not a good notetaker. TAs don't even know what is happening most of the time, and everyone is just confused about what she wants. AVOID HER.

The worst teacher I have had at NYU so far. I do not think she knows what she is talking about half the time and her tests are impossible to study for. No study guides, and literally anything she rants about in class could be on the exam. No class have ever given me such anxiety.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: having taken Ali for both History of Media and her Inquiry Seminar, i can say the latter is definitely where she shines. she makes herself accessible outside of class, gives helpful feedback on projects, and is really quite hilarious during class discussions. a far better experience definitely don't write her off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do NOT take if you want to keep yourself sane. Talks like Eminem rapping and expects notes based responses when she rewords her sentences 5 times. And EACH explanation is a new one. Words her exams like she wants you to fail. Question would be about the most random thing she mentioned in lecture. Makes you giggle but, preferably, save yourself.

Prof. Ali is quite humorous, and I can tell she genuinely loves teaching. But honestly, her teaching style feels pretty chaotic to me... I don't think she's a very organized professor. I only managed to survive this class thanks to having a great teaching assistant.

Honestly, I was really surprised by the negative reviews. The class gives you a solid foundation for the major and Professor Ali is enthusiastic, funny, and genuinely kind. I didn't study as much as I should've, so my grade wasn't what I wanted, but she really puts in the effort. PS. Don't listen to people who fail the class; they're just salty.
I walked into this class hopeful and walked out questioning my entire academic life

This course felt chaotic! The slides are just some pictures, so you must create all the structure yourself. No study guides for any exams, including the cumulative final. MC questions are vague with multiple plausible answers. Recitations don't help. Heavy workload but unclear teaching. Run as quickly as possible

Lectures are extremely disorganized. The “slides” are just random images with no structure, and nothing on Brightspace is helpful. Exams are very detailed, yet no study guide is ever provided... Readings barely matter early on but become essential for the final. Expect unpredictable tests and unclear expectations...
took during the summer so it was pretty fast-paced, TA grades all the assignments and takes off points for lowkey no reason, super lecture heavy and she kinda just makes the same jokes everyday

Just awful. Does not take any late work even if it's one minute. Went to her to review an exam so I could improve for the next one and she said if she were my TA she would have given me an even worse grade. Lectures consist of photos and that's it. Also speaks like she narrating a movie??

RUN FOR YOUR LIFE. The material itself isn't hard, but she makes exams unnecessarily difficult to understand. She has no empathy for the students and doesn't take student circumstances into account. Missing an assignment puts you in a worse position than literally failing exams. Does not accept late work AT ALL. She straight-up gives you 0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ali can be funny yet she shows no respect behind close doors. Both me and my friend went to her office hours and she literally traumatized us into depression throughout the semester saying how horrible we are. She only do that to certain students she like and some students told me they paid her an insane amount of money so she changed their grades.

Has a way of talking that is so confusing and completely unclear, genuinely impossible to follow. The TA's carry this class entirely. Midterm and final exam essays are tedious and memorization heavy. Unfortunate that she's the only one who teaches History of Media & Comm
As long as you take detailed notes and pay attention to the examples she gives in lecture, the class is super approachable and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is NOT helpful. Her lectures are mostly just her yapping and hopping from one irrelevant topic to the other. You can't properly take notes since her slideshows provide no context. And despite my best efforts, she's never given me an A+ due to her EXTREMELY picky and biased method of grading. And zero extra credit assignments. Just horrible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly don't let the reviews scare you. I was going through the trenches the semester I took her class but she was extremely understanding and honestly let me off the hook way more times than she should have. Her class was rather enjoyable and the assignments were a nice change of pace from the usual essays we have in MCC.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's not as horrible as the review says she is!!! Yes, there's no bullet points or words on her slides, but that ensures that you actually pay attention to what she says in lectures. Just write down everything she says in lectures, and she also gives you the questions for the exam in advance.

Professor Ali is incredibly cold and unsympathetic, honestly evil. I missed a deadline by two hours due to my terminally ill dad being hospitalized, and she gave me a zero. Later, despite approved absences, she failed me for attendance. I had As on everything else. Avoid her if you expect basic empathy and human decency.

I think she changed her curriculum since last semester because previous ratings don't match my class experience. I found this class so interesting. Workload is not bad and exams are open-note. The lectures are very entertaining but her slides are literally JUST pictures... take detailed notes bc there's no way to re-study.
class was incredibly boring. ali herself was a funny person but the lessons were a drag. be prepared to do your readings because that's what you're going to need for the exams
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ali was one of the best professors I had here at NYU, she was very kind and caring and understanding outside of class. She knew my name and always checked in with me and is very funny. Her lectures were good but there is always stuff to takeaway from it. Just sit in the front row and you will definitely pass with ease.

Isra Ali is getting coal for Christmas... 
Lectures were done without a microphone and only vague images on slides, so if you were in the back of the class you were screwed. There were 3 exams based on memorizing and regurgitating info from lecture and readings since questions were given in advance. This course left me and my friends frustrated.

Lecture's are SO hard to follow! You never know what's important and what's a tangent. THE SLIDES DON'T HAVE ANY WORDS!! So you have NOTHING to go by if you zoned out for a second. You MUST use only lecture examples in the exams so the lecture is essential but it's literally so hard to pay attention. Also if you miss over 3 classes points are lost
RUN!! NOT A PROF U WANT IF U GET TO PICK
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: your grade in this class heavily depends on your TA! Prof Ali's lectures are unorganized, fast paced, and hard to follow, but the class was interesting overall. I'm not a fan of the lecture-heavy exam content (you have to cite lecture examples), but it wasn't the end of the world.

The worse professor ever, if you miss lecture you will get so behind. She somehow expects us to know every single thing in exams and doesn't make what she wants exactly clear. IF YOU CAN AVOID HER PLEASE DO IT FOR YOUR MENTAL HEALTH
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Make sure to pay attention in class since the lecture slides are super vague. Can tell this professor really cares about this info, it's just super boring sometimes. Your grade will really depend on your TA, but tests are manageable as long as you take the time to prepare and pay attention to lectures and readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While the lecture's aren't well structured, professor ali is a really sweet professor who's accessible outside of class and is willing to help if you're struggling. The exam questions are given to you in advance and it's easy to prepare for them even if you've missed readings or course material. The slide's aren't very informative so take notes
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't get how she hasn't been fired yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dear prof, humble yourself. You're not nearly as good enough of a lecturer to teach 200+ students lets be fr. Every single time you speak, I wonder what in the actual world you're trying to say. If you're going to be genuinely terrible at public speaking, then at least make your exams based on other stuff, not just your lectures.

Professor Ali clearly is a knowledgable person but she is a terrible instructor. Her lectures are hard to follow and she often goes on tangents. Her "slides" consist of literal screenshots of tweets or single words with no explanations or content. Your grade in this class is reliant on your TA so pick wisely. Studying for her tests is a nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I went to her office hours but I didn't learn anything at all. She expects you to know the materials before you go find her or else she's just gonna ask you a bunch of questions and expect you to know the answers to them. She won't teach you afterwards but tells you to go back and read the assigned readings again.

I changed majors because of this class. I genuinely wasted so much time and energy on both her and the course material. She doesn't have proper slides, goes on irrelevant tangents, is not lenient, and does not seem to care for her students. I would highly suggest avoiding any class taught by her for your sanity. So not worth the headache and time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Unironically one of the worst educators I have ever encountered. Horrible lecturer, no shows her own office hours, and when she does decide to grace you with her presence she's unhelpful. If given a grant I would dedicate hours of research to finding out if she and her TAs possess kindergarten level literacy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: no lecture slides or notes, nothing, very bad
Prof Ali is kind and her social media practicum was not difficult; I stopped doing the reading halfway through the semester and was fine.

maybe i'm biased because i had TAs grade all my assignments but ali's class was really enjoyable. it wasn't easy but her lectures are fun and she's pretty good at responding to emails. the tests were hard. it was 8 questions beforehand with 4 of them being on the test and each answer had to reference 2 readings and 2 lecture examples.

Genuinely terrible. She is nice and funny sometimes, but she grades so inconsistently and horribly. She is all over the place, and nothing she teaches makes sense. She goes on rants, and doesnt stay on topic. Doesnt give good feedback, except 'good work'. Doesnt seem to care at all. If you want to take this for an easy A save you're time.

Prof. Ali is an amazing lecturer, she is able to keep her students engaged into the lesson. However, just be aware that your grade in this class will be very dependent on your TA, as they do all the grading for the 2 midterms, final, and a couple other assignments. Easy class to do well in overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ali is funny and charming at times but not super lenient & genuinely impossible to reach outside of class. Lectures are interesting most of the time but make sure to take notes because exams are basically about regurgitating information from class and the assigned readings for homework.
i promise she's a great prof if you don't take her for the required mcc lectures

really love prof ali i would take her again if i could. hers is the only class i take notes in because her lectures are so engaging. the exams are a lot to prep for but they really make sure that you know the material so i appreciate it. she's so smart and doesn't speak that fast. overall very knowledgeable professor who enjoys teaching love her sm

strict about attendance but she's really understanding and caring about genuine circumstances when one misses lecture. Easily accessible in office hours and fun lectures. The exams are really easy with questions given in advance out of which 4 come on the paper. Overall, she's really sweet and chill just go for lecture and you'll be fine

Professor Ali gets a bad rep, she is not a bad lecturer the only thing is that she does talk fast, however, you can just tell her to repeat herself and slow down. the tests are pretty straightforward with 6 readings and 6 class examples for 4 questions in 2 paragraphs each. The ta's did most of the work but history was way better than intro
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Someone send her this site link because she needs to entirely change her teaching style. She is the WORST professor I've had at NYU. Lectures are boring with no substantial material. No clear instructions on assignments. Leaves students feeling more confused and offers no clarity in office hours. straight up AWFUL. please pick a new profession

Awful professor! Talks A LOT without saying anything. The whole semester was her talking about unrelated things. Gives no clear directions for Final project. I went to office hours multiple times and left more confused. Should stop teaching atp.

Usually easy to get a good grade but she is so confusing and I don't think she even knows what she's looking for. Everyone in the class is always lost because she changes the directions for things constantly and it seems like she's just making up random things as she goes along.

I was a little worried because of some of the other reviews, but I did NOT need to be! Professor Ali explained the material (which could get complicated) in a way that was clear and easy to follow--and she was also really funny, I loved her stories and illustrations from personal experience. Grading criteria was always clear as well.
was so afraid to take her due to such terrible reviews. so glad I gave her a chance because she is such a gem! hilarious, accessible outside of class, and her TAs were all fantastic.

i had prof ali a few years ago and would mot have given the same rating, but this time around she easily became one of my favorite professors. caring, understanding and knowledgeable, and more important unpretentious unlike many other academics.

Awful. Every class she just asks about our weekends and talks about nothing. Her lessons cover nothing and have no basis. She assigns readings but does not even acknowledge or talk about them during class. Her paper instructions are poorly made and she has the strangest assignments. Should be an easy A class but is made weirdly complicated.

Awful. For 30 minutes she just asks us about her day and then covers no topics during class. She doesn't assign homework or talk about the readings, but just expects us to know about them and write about them despite never acknowledging them in the first place. Also just really strange and weird assignments. This class is a joke.

Lectures are boring and never related to the readings. On a usual week, there are "expected" readings that can be up to 90 pages long (i doubt anyone did them, but you need to skim them and quote for papers). No guidance nor good feedback for grading and every grade is either a 100% or a 20% with literally no in between. Prof is also pretentious

One of the worst classes I've taken. She talked in circles all class and the assignments are extremely vague to the point of having no direction. When you ask her for help on the final project she's passive aggressive, rejects every idea and will make you even more confused. Plus sides are she doesn't care about late assignments or attendance

A completely different teacher in-person than online. Was not a big fan of her history of media, then took her for social media practicum and inquiry seminar in the same semester and she was excellent. flexible with due dates, easy grader, and gave great guidance feedback.
You can always send your drafts to Professor Ali before submission. Gave me very detailed feedback. go to her office hours before submitting your work, read the prompt carefully and you'll be fine.

Prof. Ali gets a bad rep from when she taught History of Media but she's one of the best MCC profs out there. She is obviously incredibly smart, classes, lectures, assignments are all planned and organized. She is super accommodating and funny (at times cringe but all good-hearted). Good feedback AND ON TIME!!! The class is also very interesting!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I loved prof ali so idk why there are so many negative reviews. social media practicum is graded by few assignments + a final project but they're all for completion so it's an easy A. as long as you raise your hand once in awhile to ask questions and show up to class semi-regularly she'll love you. i genuinely thought she was funny and caring!

She'll play videos for half of the class, and the other half she'll lecture off the top of her head without any notes -- literally just rambles. Don't ever really know where she's going with lectures, there's not really a main point. Tough grader, her essay prompts list 10 different instructions and you don't really know what the main idea is...?

I wanted to like Ali, but she ended up being angry with the class and started grading harshly. My conference with her was unpleasant for no reason, it seemed as though she wanted us to understand her course the way she did - impossible in a few weeks. The material is interesting but I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Does not respond to emails, very tough grader, insane workload that does not consider students' other commitments. Very lecture heavy- zone out for two minutes and you'll be completely lost. Had to withdraw from class two weeks before semester ended to make sure I didn't get the F. Taking again with a different professor.

Professor Ali was one of the harshest teachers I've had at NYU. Her lectures are very unorganized, she goes off on tangents, and overall does not present the information in a clear way. She also has an extreme attitude if you upset her in any way, often times being very passive aggressive and rude. She can be funny at times, but that's about it :(

For History of Media and Comm, You have to go to every lecture because you can't miss anything... she expects you to remember every little thing. I went to office hours to get my midterm back and she was rude and passive aggressive. Thank god for my wonderful TA! Do well on the final. Be specific! When we moved online, she made the final longer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Only cares about her own business. Never reply to students' emails. Never read your papers and only gave u tough grade. Never give suggestions.

Professor Ali is not as bad as some of these ratings say. Maybe it's different in an in-person class, but online and asynchronously, she makes History of Media & Communication a great experience. There is a lot of reading but it really helps and prepares you well. Her lectures are so funny and she has great energy. She made this class so fun.

Idk why there are so many bad reviews, I literally never watched the lectures or did the readings and I still got an A. Sure you've gotta do some more skimming come exam time but in an online asynchronous course that's easy. I thought her lectures were quite easy to understand, especially compared to other MCC profs. And she's super nice and fun.

Professor Ali's lectures unnecessarily go off-track, making it hard to pay attention. She also does not mention any of the concepts by name making it hard to go back into lectures to find what she's talking about, despite saying that she explicitly mentions the theories and examples. Does not make it clear whether we are learning theories or not

Her lectures are dense and convoluted, and she often will drift off-topic. This is usually not a problem in an engaging in-person class, but in a pre-recorded video, the lectures become far more difficult to get through. Often felt disconnected from the assigned readings. She is also a needlessly tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The online lecture format was great and easier to follow because there was a transcript below which made it easy to find things to talk about for the midterm and final. If you watch the videos, take really good notes, and do the assignments ontime it is not difficult to get an A. the lectures are really interesting and I truly learned a lot.

I personally loved Professor Ali! she did a great job of keeping recorded lectures engaging and fun (sometimes a bit cringe though). If you pay attention to lectures, take good notes, and actually do the readings class isn't hard. there is a 5 part project that honestly seemed pointless and weekly forum posts but both are just graded on completion

I took History & Social Media Networking with Ali. History: the class is a lot of work BUT it was my favorite MCC class - def worth it. SM Networking: much easier - do the readings and engage & you will do great. Not too much work at all. Also, the smaller class size makes the dynamic super fun and engaging.
Loved the class! Prof Ali was open to students discussion, not a harsh grader at all.

I really don't know why Ali has bad reviews, I thought her lectures were really interesting.
