He takes his lectures very slow so it is comprehensible! He is very educated in the subject and he treats his students as his very own. He grades fair and understands everyone has their ups and downs. I highly recommend taking his class! It is also important to attend PTE'S!

You will only comprehend this class if you've taken AP Chemistry in high school. If not, you will be on the verge of passing or failing. In lecture he only goes over his class notes, but yet on the exam it's questions based on quantitative questions. Exams are not multiple choice, therefore getting a good grade is impossible.
Not hard at all, and I used to hate chemistry. Practice exams in Bobst are all you need to prep. Recitations are helpful, but only depending on who you get. Overall, pretty easy class.

Halpin is the easiest professor in the chem department at NYU. He is super fair with grading, and really helpful in office hours. For the midterm and final just do the practice exams in Bobst and you should be fine; most of the questions on exams are exactly the same but with different numbers. Take his class!
Perfect professor. Best man at NYU chem

Great Professor. Very clear, very helpful, loves chemistry with a passion. Will do anything he can to help his students. He spent a LOT of time helping me even though he has so many students. He really opened up my interest in chemistry and is the best teacher I've had so far.
Excellent professor overall. Kind, helpful, and committed to his students. If you're not a strong chemistry student, he really will take the time to help you out. Highly recommended.

Really great professor. He definitely cares about his students and it's clear that he wants them to succeed. He loves chemistry and wants his students to truly understand the subject, which I love. But maybe I'm biased because I'm a chem major lol. Exams are difficult but very fair. Grading's a little crazy though. I recommend him nonetheless!

He is a great, great teacher. First of all, forget all the stuff about him just reading the notes. He doesn't do that. He add lots and lots of examples and details to whats already in the notes. The notes are simply outlines. He just wants you to do well. All the negative reviews are from people who don't do the work and complain when they do bad.

Prof. Halpin clearly knows a lot about chemistry.  However, it is virtually impossible to reach him at office hours.  The one time I went, just to get a form signed, I had to wait an hour and 45 min in line to see him.  Which proves how clear his lectures are (being that so many people need to come for extra help).
he was great and it was not at all a hard class. He has been teaching this course for so long, its like second nature to him
He's really sweet. Tests are easy if you do the homework problems he gives. Truly the best professor I've had so far.

Overall going to lecture is pretty much useless but it is mandatory because he has a device that keeps track of attendance. However, Halpin cares about his students a lot and wants them to succeed in his class. I screwed up royally both semester on at least one test and ended up with an A-. Great Professor!

No doubt he cares a lot about helping students learn. The exam averages are around 75 in a class of 600 people, but he drops your lowest exam if you score a certain % higher on the other ones. The problem is attendance is mandatory. All he does in lecture is go over the exact same material already found in your notes (which you must buy).
Don't expect the class to be personal with 600 people. Halpin's notes are helpful. DEFINITELY take the practice tests. Halpin's an okay guy.

Halpin's lectures are extremely helpful and informative. He is truly passionate about Chem and tries to engage his students as well. My only complaint is the iClicker he uses to take attendance, since many students come in a minute too late and are marked absent. But the class made me much more interested in Chemistry.

Now a student of Jones, I sorely miss Halpin. Just go to lecture, follow the notes, and do his practice exams (don't use the textbook). He hardly throws any serious curveballs (unlike Orgo). As long as you nail the math, you should be perfect for every exam and get As. TAs grade very fairly and try to give as much credit as you deserve.

Very easy class im taking it right now and am acing it. His exams aren't hard its just that most NYU students are good at only memorizing facts so when it is necessary to become applicative and calculate they struggle. Class Avg about 75-78, To do well just work on practice problems and disregard too much memorization just learn the general concept

Halpin is absolutely amazing because he loves what he does and genuinely wants you to like it too. Hilarious jokes, personality, and an all around great professor. If you study notes and do practice problems for the tests, and do the other things, you will have no problem getting an A. I love this class!

Halpin was awesome, he most definitely cares that he students know the material rather than memorize the book. This approach to teaching is reflected in his tests which are very hard if you do not actually understand the material but rather memorized how to a problem. Awesome prof all around, and has awesome corny jokes.

Halpin's seems genuinely interested in getting students to understand chem. Tests really are difficult, but the final grading at the end it definitely fair.  If you want to perform well in this class, do a million practice problems, and get to the point where you can do them without your notes.  Tough class, but doable.

DO THE WORK AND READ THE TEXT! You will fail if you don't. He basically reads over his lecture notes in class. Drops the lowest test if you do something like 15 points better on the 2 others. Pretty hard tests, I recommend you ace the 1st one (if you just want to pass the class and don't care about the A) because it's by far the easiest.

I found this class really hard. But maybe it's because I took it in the summer and it's only 6 weeks long. You really need to keep up with textbook readings and homework to do well. If you miss a few readings/homeworks, you're done for. Keep up and you'll do fine. I don't recommend that anyone take this class over the summer. You'll need time.
Great Professor. Learned a lot from him.

Most awesome professor at NYU. Excellent teacher, totally fair with grading (drops the first exam as long as you do 25% better on the next one). Exams are tricky but just do a million practice problems and you're golden.

super cool professor who really wants you to do well. he's so nice in office hours! the lecture is really boring and 600+ people, plus you MUST attend because he uses the CPS system, which sucks.  TAs tend to be horrible, and quizzes are a ****.  the sample exam usually has nothing to do with the actual exam, but he drops the lowest exam grade.

Halpin is adorable and amazing! You can really tell that he cares about his students!  He prints out the notes so that you can just follow along in the notebook.  It makes studying so much easier!  LOVE HIM

Halpin is a funny lovable guy. His lecture notes basically eliminate the need for note taking (as well as eliminate the need for the textbook, though its a useful resource). Even though the lecture hall has ~400 students, he tries to encourage questions. He wants everyone to do well and is passionate about chemistry.
he is an absolute cutey! you'll fall in love with him! he really wants you to succeed. lecture notes are a concise version of the textbook.

i am in love with John Halpin. He obviously loves what he does and it really makes the class a lot more interesting. plus he's just lovable. halpin demonstrates why nyu needs fewer research scientists as professors and more teachers. this class will really teach you a lot and if you read his notes, it's not even that hard.

Halpin is the best professor I've yet to have at NYU.  While his lectures are a bit dry, he actually gives you all the lecture notes, so there really isn't much note-taking at his lectures.  He's very knowledgeable in his field and is very clear and concise.  His jokes aren't bad either.
He is amazing.  He is the best professor I've ever had.

halpin is awesome in many ways! but what is most most most amazing about him-he drops ur lowest grade! basically you can get a 2 on the first exam and still get an A in the class! get hold of old exams not the practice exam, do problem after problem and you'll do fine on the test..start studying about 2-3 weeks in advance and that A wil be yours :)

If you want to begin with chemistry, you definitely SHOULD CHOOSE HIM! His lecture is crystal-clear, and you will find his lecture notes (actually you do not need to make notes during lecture) extremely handy except that you have to pay for $200 txtbook & CPS device, youre gonna love his lecture
rate my professors won't give him the chili pepper I want it to.

Amazing, amazing professor, I loved him. Made Chemistry understandable. Never had to use the textbook. The best professor I've ever had. One thing I didnt like were the length of the tests. There was never enough time to finish. LOVE HIS SARCASTIC JOKES

Halpin is a wonderful teacher. His research interest, as listed on the chem dept URL, is chemistry education. If I ever become a teacher, I will adopt many of Halpin's techniques. A fun guy and a great instructor overall.

I love Halpin so much - made chemistry make sense, and you really can't get a bad grade if you get your act together after failing an exam. Exams aren't even that hard if you go to lecture. Lectures are concise and he clearly explains what he wants from his students. Homework also really helps in learning the material.
Prof. Halpin is amazing.  end of story

AWESOME PROF!!!ACTUALLY CARES ABOUT HIS STUDENTS! EXTREMELY FAIR, GIVES ROOM FOR IMPROVEMENT BUT EXAMS ARE PRETTY TRICKY AND YOU HAVE TO KNOW THE MATERIAL THROUGH AND THROUGH TO DO WELL...LECS ARE BORING AND HARD TO STAY AWAKE IN BUT EVERYTHING IS IN THE LEC NOTES SO NOT A PROB IF U HAPPEN TO CATCH SOME Z'S DURING HIS CLASS..LIKE EVERYONE ELSE LOL

Halpin is one of the best professors I've had at NYU so far. He's super organized and announces everything ahead of time so that students can plan assignment and study time. He's very fair and reminds students when assignments are due. Although he can be a little tricky on exams, he does his best to prepare students ahead of time.

Awesome Professors. The best on the Pre-med track. Unfortunately, it's all down hill from there. He's helpful and super fair. Everyone loves him just look at the facebook group dedicated to him, "J-Halp is more ballin' than you are."

HALPIN rocks my socks! He is very helpful and accommodating. while he admits he can seem like an old grump. he really isn't and does everything to ensure that you do well! exams are not easy, but very do-able if you do the work! very time-consuming course though!

Very helpful! If you just do the practice exam (repeatedly) you'll do fine in his class. Go to clinic AND recitation. He's awesome in office hours too. Love him. Awesome jokes and quotes. Unintentionally funny. basically, he's AMAZING. Celebrity citing if you ever see him on the street.
Halpin is awesome!

Prof Halpin knows chemistry and therefore is able to explain the concepts well. Just use the lecture notes to study. I only used the textbook for the homework and read barely any of it. The essays he had us write were rather simple but the tests were somewhat tricky. This class will require effort but if you enjoy chemistry Halpin is a good choice.
Halpin's class is straightforward and fair. He is dedicated and helpful. He works closely with the TAs and does everything he can to help you succeed in his class.

I LOVE HALPIN!  His lectures were my favorite classes to go to, and he's a really nice guy.  He's very accommodating to his students.  He's just so great overall (he's tough, but fair).  Definitely recommend him.
Very very helpful. He definitely cares about his students and loves the subject he teaches.
Fair teacher, but hard to talk to.

Halpin is wonderful and I think every premed/engineering misses him after gen chem.  He cares about students and does everything he can to make sure you do well.  People who do bad on his exams are just lazy-- if you put even a little effort you can easily get at least a B-.

Halpin loves chemistry! Although I often fell asleep in lecture b/c of his monotone voice, I think he is still a great teacher. His lecture notes are a great help and he is a very fair grader. He even drops your lowest midterm and extends deadlines on chem essays.. he does anything to help out the student!
amazing prof, loves the subject and encourages you to come to office hours
very fair grader, easy A but only if you study and do all the required work

Sigh, one more semester of corny jokes and that soothing voice that did make me fall asleep multiple times. He's a great guy though, has the most organized class I've ever taken and it is possible to get an A if your not adherently prone to stupid mistakes on exams. Great class though cuz Halpin loves what he's doing. Tough if u dont like chem.
Excellent at teaching but Tests are difficult!!
If I marry a man like John Halpin, I will die happy! Please future Gen Chem students, go to lecture every time, learn about the beauty of chemistry and fall in love one corny joke at a time...
I found him incredibly patronizing.
he's got a good sense of humor, and he loves chemistry. he's always really fair. he makes it really easy to do well in the class by offering a lot of ways to do well.

J-Halp (as I like to clal him), is an amazing professor.  Yes, his voice is soothing enough to put you to sleep, but he really makes you learn.  Go to recitation and clinics and do the practice exams and homework and you'll do well in the class.  He wants you to do well and will try and boost your grade as high as possible
I really liked Halpin.  He works all year round (including summers.)  He seems to always come across with interest even though he has taught the same stuff forever!  He is a very reasonable guy too.

Prof. Halpin is one of the greatest teachers ever. He knows the subject well, SO organized, and he can help you with questions you have (office hours). Definitely do the practice exams and the packages from clinic. Weekly quizzes are hard, but come from lecture notes. Hw isnt graded on correctness, so get a 10 on every HW and it'll will help.
He can teach
Great teacher, VERY EASY. Just read his notes and do his practice exams and this class is an easy A for sure.
Very structured and organized teacher.  Has frequent office hours and hold review sessions before each exam, and has practice tests for each exam which directly reflect the actualy exams.

I took General Chemistry 1 with Professor Halpin and I think that his class was moderately easy as long as you understood his (very clear) notes and DID the practice exams before the test.  The only difficult part about this class is the recitation quizes, which can be made easy my studying his lecture notes beforehand.
No Comments
No Comments
Halpin was great
Loves what he does. Excellent professor. Really wants every student to make it, and his grading policies reflect that.
not happy with teacherbad guy, im a chem major, many other teachers in the department are better than halpin.

Amazing professor!  Really puts a lot of time and effort into helping his students learn and understand chem.  He gives extra study sessions before exam.  Exams can be hard but fair!  He's a fair grader and you just need to do your work and you'll be fine.  Can't complain with this professor.
Very difficult material, but he is a superb teacher.  He is especially nice and cares a lot about students.  He is very understanding.
The reason why I dropped out of Pre-Med.  Brilliant professor, but his test (to me at least) never reflected actual in class problems.  Failed miserably.

Prof. Halpin is a stellar instructor.  He is organized, fair, and can explain the most difficult concepts with simplicty and clarity.  His notes have come in handy in every science class I have taken since Gen Chem.

Excellent teacher, explains well, elaborates if asked, overall helpful.  Holds Q&A sessions before tests, and tests are pretty easy if you pay attention.  Even gives you all the notes before class, so just read through them with him and add on extra notes.  If you know some chem, don't need lecture.

Great teacher - he really tries to help you out. His tests are sometimes tricky, but as long as you do the homework and come to lectures, you'll do fine. He does his best to try to get you the highest grade you can get - even if you bomb on a test.

You need to invest a lot of time studying for his class in order to do well. He is a great professor-very straightforward and clear. As long as you do all the work, it is very possible to do well. He is also a very fair grader.
really nice guy. make sure to go to recitations and clinics or you won't know how to do anything on the tests. study hard, but he's very fair.
He is a cool guy. He is very fair. You might have the tendency to sleep in his class though.

True, his lecture voice can be monotone but other than that he is truly an AWESOME professor.  He responds to questions both quickly and informatively.  I love how his lectures notes and previous exams are availabe - both are great study tools.
No Comments
He is a great teacher, always willing to help, and he goes at a pace that everyone can keep up with. He makes class interesting with his chemistry jokes.

Prof. Halpin has a great teaching style. His notes are very helpful, but like he always says, it's true that you will NOT do well in the class unless you make sure to do a lot of studying on your own.
Halpin's notes are great.  You need to invest a lot of time into the class in order to do well.  His jokes are cute.

Can be tricky on tests, but provides practice exams and lecture notes and works closely with T.A.s. You can always get your question answered from someone. Responds to emails quickly and is willingly to help you any way he can
Genuinely the best prof at NYU. I took her for writing as exploration. She really cares about students, fair grader, clear rubrics, lots of time to complete assignments.

Totally the best professor I've ever met. The course is easy, you only have to finish one essay during the semester. A few readings after class. She is kind, caring, giving feedback patiently. You can talk to her without any pressure.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take her!!

Prof. Chavoshan was so inspirational and taught me so many important things during Bridgerton. She is nuanced, she is aware and she is interested in learning with her students. She has never talked at us and rather beckons us to add to what we already know. She is fantastic at giving feedback and has made me a more aware person.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took her for WRCI over the summer and she was great! lectures kept me engaged and easy A. Midterm/final is one paper and she gives feedback during the step-by-step process. Had some breakout room talks but nothing too serious. We had weekly posts based on the articles we read-prompts are very clear! highly recommend taking her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her online for WRCI, and she organized the course very well. She made her lectures as engaging as they could be online and was very clear with her class expectations. Most of the grade was one big project, which she gives good feedback on step by step, and the rest includes attendance, discussion posts, and a small presentation.
Very helpful class and makes writing better and also helps international students with writing assignments in other classes. Very nice professor.
she's great
Adorable, funny, intelligent! I am constantly impressed by his technology skills.

Goofy dude who is a bit too into the class material given that it's common sense, but success is heavily based off of participation and the passion you show for the class. Grade is group-dependent but you individually control ~60% of final grade so just try to yap and smile and all will be well. Always go to feedback meetings after presentations
As long as u participate and follow his conventions its a free A

The greatest C&C professor of all time. My only regret is not being able to take him for B&S. Participation matters heavily, but he is generous with grades and the class is fun. While other kids were busy reading 2000-word books, my class was watching great movies and having nice discussions.

Prof Schenkler is the goat.

All you have to do in order to get an A is to participate once every discussion and do well on the 3 essays. He will give out 100% to everyone that follows his criteria (which he states multiple times in class). 

Ended the class with 100% on everything, while not reading any of the material.
Nice professor that will give you feedback but lectures were quite boring but there's nothing that can be done about that

Despite the positive reviews, Schenkler has clear favorites in his class. He frequently makes mistakes while grading essays, such as claiming my evidence doesn't exist in the book while it does. He judges your answers to discussion questions and would take his bad attitude out on the class sometimes. I didn't enjoy taking this class.

What a guy. Hands down one of the best writing professors at Stern. Classes are engaging and organized in a great way. Understands we are busy and doesn't expect us to read everything on the syllabus. Gives weekly journals with great feedback and the essays (although tedious to write) are pretty easy to score well just follow the rubric. 10/10!!!!!
Professor Schenkler is a great teacher for commerce and culture. Grading is very clear and if you write the way he likes, you will do fine. Highly recommend.
Easy A
Has clear favorites. Don't take this prof if you have other tough classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Overall solid professor. Make sure you participate and be prepared by doing all the readings. Raise your hand in class and contribute meaningfully to class discussions.

Professor Schenkler was a very solid option for Org Comm. Had very clear grading criteria that were easy to follow for both presentations and written assignments. As long as you follow his instructions clearly & participate in class you will receive an A.

Kind guy who makes participation in discussion-based classes open and easy for everyone. Classes are always interesting and engaging. Very fair grader. The B&S course is underwhelming from a learning standpoint, but this is universal for all B&S professors. Good B&S teacher choice to help develop your writing a bit, while still enjoying class.

Overall, great guy! Loved coming to his class every Monday and Wednesday. As long as you do your work, participate and ask him for help whenever you need it, you should have no problem ending the semester with a good great.
Second worst professor ever. The most regretful thing is choosing him. The rating tricked me.
Good professor but worst experience this year. Would not have chosen it again.

Very good professor for Commerce and Culture. Clear guidelines for your writing and great feedback on individual assignments. Encourages participation and makes it easy for everyone to contribute. Somewhat strict on certain aspects of writing, but if you get those issues down, you will succeed. Definitely better than other options available.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Schenkler is the best professor I have ever met at NYU. He is like an inspirational mentor for me, and I believe he is the one for the rest of the class. All my classmates appreciate his works and comments. I would like to take his class one more time.

Prof Schenker is very old-school. He's been at Stern forever and is very respected. But, he's very particular about his grading and giving out As. A lot of his grading is based on how much he likes you, so go to office hours. Just know that getting an A won't be super easy, but his class isn't super hard.

He is very attentive to individuals and gives you good feedback on your papers. If you put in a good effort, he will notice. Participate in class discussions! Also can be sarcastic/make funny comments
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor definitely would take again
Really Great at improving your presentation skills!!
Prof Shingler really wants to help you improve your presentation skills.  He is dedicated and takes the time needed to analyze your posture, speech, etc
Hard to get an A, but makes it really easy to get a B+. He talks a lot and the class was pretty interesting.

Funny (sometimes sarcastic) professor.  He values participation a lot. He likes his students to think outside the box, so if you stick to the obvious, he won't give you  a good grade (obviously). He pays individual attention to his students and is very dedicated.
intuitive, but a harsh grader. if you are intersted purely in intellectual discussion regardless of your grade, take his classes.
hard grader, but he really helps you learn individually in the class.
Has favorites. Get on his good side.  Great at teaching, sucks at grading, and has an abrasive, in-your-face personality.

Very good professor - willing to help, focuses on individual improvement, always interesting.  He can also be mean, lets his mouth run, and insulting.  Despite that, his class and how he teaches is well-worth the anxiety.
Be ready to consume a lot of media and film, class conversations will be fun and interesting. Yet I don't recommend because of how all over the place everything was.

Very disorganized and not that open minded to personal opinions in class. It's also difficult to meet her outside of class hours, and she will send readings to do before class very last minute. Shes kind but the course overall didn't feel stable and consistent with the syllabus.
goood gooood goooood
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Langer is very educated on books, paintings, and movies. When it comes to discussions, she loves for students to be engaged. Her writing prompts will get you thinking about things you hadn't considered. She's a very nice and understanding professor. There are a couple of readings and movies, and you might need to purchase books.

Prof. Langer's course stands out as one of the most fulfilling and engaging parts of my first sem. Despite other reviews, she created a safe and encouraging space where I felt comfortable sharing my opinion. She was easily accessible and patient when working with students. I never witnessed her 'shaming' anyone, so be mindful of online reviews.

Prof. Langer is very easy-going and a fun person to get to know. The class itself isn't too difficult and feels fairly casual rather than strictly academic. 
I enjoyed that we watched many films throughout the semester. Professor Langer also offers many opportunities for extra credit.
Overall, this class is a great option for a relaxing course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Niceish person, bad prof. Very disorganized, late to nearly every class and office hours/meetings. Grading feels arbitrary; taking her direct feedback doesn't improve grades on assignments. Assignments are posted late and in random places. Heavy reading load at times, but most of class is just watching movies. Long grading times. I learned nothing.
did not follow the syllabus and always showed up late and unprepared to every class. not very accepting of other viewpoints. don't take her.

Honestly to speak, she is amazing. Her class/lecture are splendid and full of respect. She is a very responsible person. If you have any questions, just go to find her. She will be there waiting for you.(Although you are introvert person, that will not too hard, she has good self-control.）A fair classroom, and efforts will surely be rewarded.

I took Professor Langer for both WRCI102 and WREX101. She was very understanding and one of the nicest professors I've met. She assigns great books. In class, we'd discuss the assigned reading, go over anonymous papers for feedback, or work in groups on activities. It's easy to do well in her class, and she was always reachable when needed.

Wonderful professor! Prof. Longer picks out wonderful, diverse books and readings plus, facilitates great class discussions. Her essay prompts are fun, creative and she always gives a more research based option for more technical people. Also provides detailed feedback. Great person and teacher. Would highly recommend!

Feedback on essays is not helpful. Gives a million paper handouts to hold onto. Sometimes posts hw on BS, sometimes on email, nothing is ever in the same place- just completely disorganized, and teaching methods seem very lazy. Not hard to get an A, but if you want to improve your writing, do not take her.

So mid. Nobody does the reading for her classes and she is extremely disorganized. Good person but just simply couldn't care less. She is always late to class, is late on the syllabus, takes months and months to grade, and misassigned us a paper she never even graded.
Best professor I've ever met. She is patient, caring, and nice. My writing skills improved a lot through her lecture. A lot of chance for extra credit!

I had Langer last semester, and she was phenomenal. Not only did I fall in love with reading again through the texts she assigned, but I learned so many different writing styles through them. Any student who doesn't have the biggest interest in writing, I advise you to take her. she You will become a better writer and broaden your outlook on life.

All I learned/read from this class is book about the first homosexual man in this world and BLM and female rights, but nothing about writing. I support all of the things above but I wish to learn more about writing, given that the class name is writing 2. Learned a lot about political correctness but my writing skills did not improve by a tiny bit.

Good professor, unfortunately she is a little disorganized and not reliable over email. But if you participate enough, pay attention and actually do the work, class is an easy A. She does get tougher and the work does get more grueling in the 2nd semester for Writing Critical Inquiry. Overall a solid professor I'd take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I seriously loved this class. If you have the chance to take her, DO IT! Her assignments are fun and homework is not rigorous. She is a very easygoing and personable teacher. She cares deeply about her students and completely gave me a new outlook on creative writing. Participation is very important to her but it is not difficult to get involved!

She is kind and funny and gives a detailed feedback if you ask for one. Participation matters you had better speak one or two times every class. The grading criteria is not always clear. You can get a first draft 95 and a final draft 80 after revising according to her feedback. She does not follow the syllabus and makes the schedule confusing.

I had Professor Langer my spring semester for WRCI. The course material was very expansive and allowed creative freedom when choosing topics to write about, all very interesting. Professor Langer cared about making personal connections to the students and their educational success. Loved this class!

I had professor Langer for my fall and spring semester (two different classes) and LOVED her. She genuinely cares about her students and went above and beyond last year to host classes in person. She ALWAYS wore a mask and was flexible and understanding with students regarding deadlines/workload. She's an insightful professor & an amazing person.

Professor Langer is very disorganized when it comes to planning out the class, it is also very unclear what your grade is going to be until the very end of the semester because she does not put anything in gradebook. The readings are boring and the class discussions drag on. She is a very sweet lady but boring when it comes to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly boring in lecture and as an online student I didnt feel that she gave me the chance to engage with the class as my other professors did.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tough grader--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Langer is a great woman who tries to make the class engaging. Throughout the semester, we read multiple books, poems, and articles (some of which were not discussed in class). There were very few major assignments other than the midterm, final, and short essays. She's also very responsive. It's tough however to know your true grade till the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Langer was late (even when we had online classes) and very unclear in her assignments. She takes forever giving feedback and her lectures are not very interesting. She assigned light homework and readings frequently. She made it easy to participate in class and the 3 essays were easy. The topics discussed in class were somewhat boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Super sweet lady. I took her Writing I class and she was incredibly helpful and always accessible. We workshopped all of our papers in class and she is very clear with instructions and due dates.

I didn't realize just how awesome of a professor Langer was until my second semester writing class. She's organized and gets to the point with engaging stories that contribute to an overarching theme. If you take the time to go in and have her give comments on your essays, and you apply those comments. You'll become a better writer and an A student
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Writing 1 was a drag having Professor Langer, even if you make the corrections she suggest on the 1st draft you still might not even get a B. she will give you unnecessary readings and make you print out your own copy everyday before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her teaching style is great. If you ask for help she won't hesitate. Edits on essays are based off of the rough draft itself (in terms of quality and length).
Great Professor, I miss her so much.
The professor is indeed a good one. She attempted to get to know everyone in the classroom to teach everyone in a special way. Thanks to her, I enjoyed my first semester in NYU.

Professor Langer really knows how to train her students into reading, writing and thinking with clarity, precision and grace. You get as much out of the class as you put in. If you want to improve your writing in a manner that is beneficial for the rest of your academic and professional career, definitely take her. (Also makes great jokes)

I loved being in Professor Langer's class. I found the topics that she taught to be relevant to my interests, and I loved the discussions we had in class. As a result, the papers were fairly easy and fun to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The class is pretty interesting but she's way too tough on grading. She assigns a bunch of reading homework thats unnecessary. If you want an A you're better off taking someone else's class.

Very nice person with interesting discussion topics.  I really learned a lot and cultivated my opinions from this class.  She is very disorganized and often posts homework at the last minute.  She can also be a harsh grader (if she finds something she doesn't like, she'll take off a lot of points).  Willing to help but rambles a lot.

She is a great writing professor! Often unorganized, but her discussions are really interesting. She listens very well to all the ideas. She is pretty lenient with her gradings. Her topics are really interesting.

I LOVE HER! She is so helpful and awesome. She's really nice and it's mostly a discussion class. She's very lenient and chill about deadlines and grading. She is very sweet and can be funny, too. I am taking her again next semester. As long as you show up and read the stuff, it's a total breeze. She's also there for office hours all the time.
Her class is really interesting. Her topics give us so much to talk about. She is my favorite professor so far. The reads were short and interesting. I just loved her class!!!

The class itself was okay. She seems to talk a lot and the daily freewrites are tedious. Towards the end of the semester she started to assign bigger workloads as if she was trying to cram information in. I also feel like she likes certain people and not others. For the most part, it's an okay class. Nothing great, I suggest taking someone else.

I found professor Langer to be mildly helpful, any writing class is bound to help you just by the experience, but I felt a little awkward in her class. She seems to have a very specific idea of what answers she wants to her questions and she knows exactly what kind of interpretation she wants you to have. She's okay, just a little narrow minded.
Her class is a little boring but she is an awesome person and thus, an awesome teacher!
she's awesome

A very nice woman. She tries to make the class interesting but sometimes it doesn't work. Personally, I loved the discussions and when you participate, it's like brownie pts. She doesn't make it too clear what she wants from your writing, but in terms of workload, it's good. Beware the workshops--totally pointless and unhelpful.
It's a pretty easy class. Very research based. Can be boring. Langer is nice and gives easy homework. Not the most amazing class, but it's fine and wont add very much to your work load.

she is a little tough on the grading. she started giving me better grades, saying how much my writing's improving. not sure if she does this for everyone. i honestly don't think she improved my writing THAT much. very nice and willing to help whenever. gives clear, helpful comments on the papers. sometimes asks stupid questions during discussions.

She is a nice person but grades kind of strictly.  We wrote about four different topics w/four main essays.  It's not too much work and she's pretty friendly.  She didn't help improve my writing that much though.
He is a really cool guy with easy to follow lectures. His assignments can be a little cryptic, but he clears up any difficulties when asked. Very amazing professor.

Amazing professor who is very good at teaching. He recognizes the changing landscape of technology and coding, and shapes his class to reflect current trends, also being a very respected professional in his industry.

Loved his teaching, also could use ChatGPT on the final which was clutch. I think it really depends on your TA because she was the one who graded all my assignments. He's very approachable after class and as long as you put your face in his brain, he will grade well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: panos is one of my favorite professors! He often brings pizza for the whole class and is very knowledgeable. Straightforward and will give you what you need to succeed.

Great guy, especially if you get him warmed up in his office. He is extremely passionate for his work, and if he feels that you are interested in learning the topic in depth he can spend a lot of time with you.
Nice guy, really passionate for what he is teaching. I wish all my other professors were as engaging as Panos

great guy, funny greek accent, and interesting class. he is enthusiastic about the material, but the class is so broad that we never get deep into the material. interesting group projects, boring individual assignments
No Comments
panos really knew what he was talking about and was always willing to answer questions. He has a great sense of humor and a funny greek accent. I would definitely take him again.
He is a great professor. He can explain. Although the materials in this class is difficult to understand, under this professor, you will be able to know what it is.
Panos is a great teacher. He really knows what he is talking about and he makes every effort to be available to the students. I enjoyed the class, even though I was not interested in the topic.
just take anyone else

Where do I even begin. He uses slides from another professor and then is confused by the content and tries to figure out what is going on. Hates having to put in extra work (ie review sessions). He talks back and judges students on their questions. The midterm was nothing like the practice midterm/work, included content we learned in later units.

He is very kind and has a sarcastic sense of humor (that apparently everyone takes seriously). The subject is difficult, for me at least, but he is very understanding. I recommend going to office hours where it's a lot easier to clear up any misconceptions, and he was especially helpful after the first midterm.
Great sense of humor.
Nice dude, doesn't budge on his rules no matter what. Tests way harder than all the practice/hws, Class test average was a 62.5. Make sure to lock in on time management or else you'll get cooked.

Ignore all the other review, Jung is the GOAT. Boy oh boy where do I start. Every class, a smile comes on my face. He brings joy to my day and is the only 11am class I would ever wake up for (I typically wake up at 2pm).  Although our class average on the midterm was a 63, he is still the GOAT for the W curve. I love you Professor Jung

This guy is not it; pick literally anyone else. He's lowkey just a yapper. If you have a hard-to-pronounce name, beware. He won't call on you for participation. Hates actually having to host office hours and review sessions (sad that he "misses out on lunch"). Not as funny as he thinks he is.
utilizes peak word salad during lecture, nothing from lecture/practice exam actually ends up on the real exams. run fast kids
GUYS RUN RUN AS FAST AS U CAN
Good teacher to help you improve your discipline.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Read this and read this carefully shes honestly the most vicious TA you can have. She gets off on holding power over you as a TA and abusing it. Don't ask her questions, try not to interact with ner. But majestically when the lab professor comes around she's an ANGEL (to him)! She will grade your quizzes and lab reports as if you owe her money.

Way overhated for some reason. Super accessible and very helpful outside of class. She will call you out on mistakes, but for good reason and she really does her best to teach. She's slightly better as a TA then lab instructor but her method of being very critical of her students helps you improve a lot.

Read the reviews about her before last semester, got super scared. She is actually AMAZING, if you put in the work, ask her what you can do to improve, and actually care, she is a great prof. she is also great in recitation as a teacher and as long as you put the effort in knowing the material. she's very smart and over-qualified for what she does
I think she's just misunderstood, she may get annoyed if youre not prepared

Martinez is one of the worst TAs you can have for Orgo lab or lecture. She is an unnecessarily hard grader and doesn't care about her students at all. She's only there to mediocrely do her job. Her lectures are blunt and rushed and she is very condescending and rude when asking questions. She doesn't want to be teaching but she does like chemistry.

Your typical arrogant orgo prof. A lot of lecture notes/problem sets do not accurately reflect the exams and her extremely condescending attitude to anyone she deems to be unworthy doesn't help much. She curved generously at the end but keep in mind that the midterm averages would consistently be in the 40s and the mean final grade was a 58 lmao.

Prof Martinez can be unapproachable and condescending in both class and OH, but I think she means well and just wants people to take her seriously. She will deny any curve until the end of time despite half the class failing but ultimately curved generously. Overall, she is brilliant and passionate but has trouble connecting with her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: under the mask of condescending attitude and a big ego, she is actually very helpful to students and even help me print my cheat sheet. Gives good curves. I literally thought i am failing this class but i end up getting a B+, this makes me like her a lot lol
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Material is a lot, but Martinez finds a way to make it fun, and not too stressful!

Dr. Martinez CARRIED me in Orgo, lab and recitation. As someone who was slow to grasp the concepts, her office hours were a blessing. She's cheerful and explains ideas clearly. While she can be a tough grader with the labs, she is overall a kind and patient mentor who genuinely looks out for her students and gives thoughtful feedback on our work.

She lectures really well, the material is just very challenging. She is very misunderstood, she offers help whether it's with lecture or with long term plans involving your career. I only had her for recitation, I cannot vouch for how she grades in lab. All I heard was she took 5 points out of 10 for someone not writing the experiment title.

She's great for recitation because she can teach well, but again, very condescending at times. Avoid her for lab because she's an extremely harsh grader. In general, avoid ppl like Martinez and Ramdular for orgo labs because they harsh.
Avoid her if you can. she makes the class hell

Orgo is a hard class, so don't go into this expecting it to be like Gen Chem lab. Read the procedures carefully and try to understand what you're doing. Dr. Martinez is very responsive and helpful during class even though everyone is asking her questions. Very helpful with post labs if you reach out. If you're self sufficient, you should be okay.

For someone who can teach, she is extremely condescending in everything she does. Her grading is petty. Not harsh, just petty. Some of the reasons for taking off points are clearly forced, to keep post-lab averages low. Again, good at explaining topics, but if no one's comfortable approaching her, then what's the point of being good at teaching?
I wish I listened to the reviews beforehand. She is a good at teaching and is smart but incredibly condescending. She is a harsh grader, even if you get the answer right. Just take another TA.

she's def a harsh grader but other than that i think she's fine lol i don't rlly think she's condescending... she's been passive-aggressive to me once or twice but tbh lowkey deserved on my end lmfao. but yeah personally for me i don't think she's condescending she was very nice to me even tho i messed up in lab a LOT

Extremely passive aggressive and condescending when you ask her anything. Absolutely brutal grader and takes pride in having consistenly low post lab averages. Be sure to do well in lecture to compensate for your grade in this portion.

This LAB section nearly kills me. Ruin my Life, Ruin my college 
A TOTAL waste of TIME. Hardest grader. God bless students in her section please .

Never had a lab instructor this horrible. Feels like she just wants to get out of there as soon as possible and doesn't actually care about her students. Don't bother asking her questions. She's condescending, demeaning, and makes you feel like you're wasting her time.
Horrible lab teacher. Takes so many points off on post labs for unnecessary small details that other profs would not. She made the entire lab section a drag by how hard she grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will never know if you understand what he teaches because you have no practice exam. Hw is the only way of checking your understanding but it's not related to exams.
He can't explain the concept well and he has no practice exam. The only thing you can do is review slides and hw, but it actually not relate to the exam.

when students ask questions, he struggles to clarify concepts in a way that actually helps. The exams feel disconnected from what is taught in class, making it difficult to prepare effectively. Grading is also very harsh and does not reflect students' understanding of the material. I would not recommend this course unless you want to suffer a lot.

He just wrote the equation and theory on his mac, even though they are not making any sense for me. And the midterms are really difficult, those questions have no any relation to what you learned in the lecture. If you dont want to get B or B-, RUN!!!!

He is an awful professor. Only 5 out of 50 students in class actually listened to him. I deeply doubt he knows the material he taught. He cannot explain the concepts or answer students' questions. Most of the time, he silently wrote formulas on his iPad (or more precisely copied the formulas from textbooks). He is not responsive after class either.

This one is also off topic. His son Joseph gave me some nerds. they were scrumptious. Thank you for raising your son well. I rate you in your ability to raise children 5/5. Job well done. Truly job well done
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very good class.  He related the lectures material to real life finance.  This class helped me get an internship at a major firm. Hope to take a class he teaches
Interesting material discussed in this class Learned alit during lecture. Enjoyed interacting with him
Great lectures.  Learned a lot in the class.
love him

The whole course is basically to read the textbook and do the confusing homework and exams. He may be trying very hard but has no teaching skills. Often cornered by questions and horrible handwriting.

Really enjoyed this class.  The homework were very relevant to learning the material.  The lectures were interest.  It was great to have a class that applies mathematics to real world problems.  He was very responsive to emails and office hours. I hope I am able to take this professor again.

Professor Cerniglia did a very good teaching this courses. He balances teaching the mathematics along with the underlying financial concepts.   He communicates well and responsive to questions.    Homework are challenging.

If you are a math major with no interest/experience on finance, you might avoid this course and Professor Cerniglia for the following reasons:
1 involves many terms about finance
2 He will avoid math induction and the specific step. Not interesting
3 Not easy A
4 In his hw/note, many definition are blur but his email response is slow

Cerniglia is a kind individual. He chats with students a lot about course materials, internships, and future plannings. However, he is not that a good instructor since he is an adjunct one. He makes mistakes on the board, in the homeworks (challenging) and in the exams. Moreover, he does not explain the ideas behind materials, which could be tough.

Mr Cerniglia is an outstanding teacher. He blends both finance experience with a strong understanding of mathematics. His classrooms communicates the core concepts clearly. His homeworks are challenging and useful for understanding the material. I really enjoyed my experience in the class and would highly recommend hoim.
Grades are actually impossible, teaches work not on the slides, unavailable consistently

Do not listen to the negative reviews. If you do not like long classes, don't take a 2.5 hour class. That is the only option for her course at NYU. She always let us out a solid 40 minutes early and if you show up, the lowest you will get is a B. She is a very kind and knowledgeable professor who I wish taught more classes at NYU. She was great!

I disagree with the negative reviews. Very straightforward clear about what you need to know for the exams, and exams are open book. She is very accessible and encourages questions during lecture, so our understanding is partly student-led. Honestly my easiest class of the semester because I tried.

Unhelpful lecture slides, speaks in really confusing ways, and lots of readings that she doesn't even cover in lecture. Very abstract and theory-based class, so know the case studies very well. The final exam questions made no sense and just sounded like a word salad of the key terms we learned this semester.

reviews.comment: Schlesinger was the worst Professor I had at NYU. Extremely boring three hour lectures, many homeworks and readings, and never stayed on topic in lecture or gave any extra info than what was already online. She is extremely biased and unprofessional when grading. I hope she never teaches another student again. Good luck if you get stuck with her.

reviews.comment: Generally speaking, the grading system is quite fair, and it's not difficult to get an A if you read textbooks, listen to lectures, and spend some time preparing (open notes). reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly I understand all the ratings on here. If you had her during the Spring 25 semester, when our class went online without prior notice, it did suck. But overall if you go to office hours and ask any questions, she will answer them. I was able to get the entire layout for the exams by asking her during office hours, which helped me get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor! Lectures were most useful if you took active notes. Never did readings and crammed for both exams. Gave midterms back and feedback at office hours going over what exam sample responses should include. Also went over case study/theory analysis relevant to exam questions. Most people on here just didn't make the effort to go to OH.

honestly i thought jayme was great. she was dense, but lectures were organized by the first half explaining theories & the latter focused on the case study based on  the readings. if you know how to write 5 paragraph essays with a basic thesis statement you will get an A. Use readings as evidence. i heard ppl didnt do readings, so they struggled

one of the worst profs in the politics dept

Bad lecturer and harsh grader who gives no feedback on any assignments

reviews.comment: her lectures were incoherent and half the time she would ramble, making it difficult to stay engaged. she never gave back the midterm which was 40% of our grade and didn't explain how to do better on the final- despite it being the same format. worst politics class i have taken at NYU by far, do not take this course if she is teaching it.

reviews.comment: While the professor herself was nice, there was no feedback and she was a harsh grader.

The grading rubric was given to us after the midterm which was also very useless and generic. Goes on tangents a lot in class and u only have the readings cus the slides r so useless. Don't take her.

reviews.comment: Interesting subject matter and lectures aren't too bad. Heavily dependent on your midterm and final. You don't get a study guide or any guidelines to go off of. Lectures can be a little long and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really nice professor and the class material was engaging. There are readings every week that are mandatory and will be tested on through attendance quizzes. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No study guides provided beforehand for midterm and final, nor does she hand them back so that we can individually review. Commentary not provided, even of the bare minimum. As another review said, she does lose her train of thought and go into tangents. It would be nice to have a professor who could come into lectures prepared. Also got an A
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very boring class and unclear expectations

GOT A. Difficult to understand, speaks too fast, and is scattered in thoughts, going into tangents straying from lecture plans. Slides have minimal info insufficient for review; quizzes/midterm/final exams are hard, overly broad/conceptual essays; stacks of complicated reading; harsh grades; no feedback. reviews.comment: She is very nice but her lectures were hard to follow. Does not provide what will be on exams and beware of pop quizzes for attendance which she also grades tough. Overall good class, but would not take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor's lectures are extremely unengaging and scattered. The slides are minimal so they're useless in trying to make sense of her lessons. Grading is harsh and she gives no feedback to tell you what you need to improve. Terrible professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schlesinger is nice but not the most engaging or clear lecturer. Attendance is taken on 4 pop quizzes that are, unlike what she describes in the syllabus class, based entirely on readings and are graded rather harshly. That said, be sure to actually do the readings and take notes on them. Overall this was a pretty average politics class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor did a fantastic job at teaching us US Foreign Policy. I would highly recommend her to anyone considering this course. I read the other negative review of her on this site, and in my opinion, that student is dead wrong. Alas, this is subjective, though I believe this professor gave captivating lectures and was great to learn from!
Grading felt inconsistent, and feedback was minimal, so it was tough to improve

Getting help was also difficult- questions were either brushed off or answered in a way that didn't really clarify anything. Grading felt inconsistent, and feedback was minimal, so it was tough to improve.

The class is challenging, and the teaching could be clearer. Lectures don't always explain the concepts in an easy-to-understand way, and the examples sometimes don't align well with the homework. The homework itself is difficult, and grading tends to be strict. Exams are also often harder than the practice problems provided.

Tough class and the teaching could be clearer. Lectures don't always make the concepts easy to understand, and the examples don't always match the homework. Homework is challenging and grading can be strict. Exams also tend to be harder than the practice problems.

Tough class but great teacher! Teaching style uses lots of examples and helps work out problems with us in class. Homework is difficult, but always available for office hours and recitation practices with a very similar problem set. Homework is graded very easily and tests are very similar in difficulty to homework.

Support beyond class time was limited, and building a meaningful connection proved challenging. I would not feel confident seeking mentorship or a recommendation from this professor. By the end of the semester, many students were relieved the course had concluded. If given the option, I recommend choosing a different instructor.

Support outside of class was minimal, and establishing any real rapport was extremely difficult. I wouldn't feel comfortable depending on this professor for mentorship or a letter of recommendation. By the end of the term, most students were simply glad it had ended. If possible, I strongly suggest selecting a different instructor for this course.

This guy made my econ experience at NYU worthwhile. Patient, answered all my emails, and showed me grace when my mom was ill. He also wrote me a letter of rec for law school. Can't say enough good things about working with him, and during our last class, all of us thanked him for a wonderful experience. If you have to take this class, go with him.

This is the best econ prof at NYU. Prof. Scianimanico uses guided notes in each lecture to make sure you have all the information you need to succeed. He is very accessible outside of class and even outside of his office hours. Although most of your grade is exams, he explains everything that is going to be on the midterm/final before you take it.

Jud is a great director. He's really great. It's just that his lectures were a little boring and repetitive. I wish he had spoken more on directing different types of actors, and how to direct certain genres. But he's a really charismatic person, and a great connection to have.

He's witty and caring, and even helped me and some of my friends get a connection for one of our film endeavors. Great guy, but the lectures are repetitive and can get boring. Some lectures are randomly extremely helpful, but most of the time it's the same ten things being covered again and again.

Appreciated Judson as a prof but absolutely could not stand his lectures. They went on for so long and rarely anyone even payed attention or showed up. He's passionate about his craft which is inspiring, but I couldn't tell you half the things we talked about. I raised my hand maybe twice the entire semester.
Judson is awesome and so passionate, performance strategies lecture is kind of a pointless class but his personality and presentation style makes it at least bearable.

Hypothetically an interesting topic but his lectures are useless and annoying. Keeps the class going for much longer than necessary and everything covered in class could be said in much fewer words through a slideshow. Mandatory class and its bearable and not much work for an A, but lectures are painful.

Every class with Judd is like watching a TedTalk, both because he's a good lecturer and because his lectures go on for way longer than they should. It's repetitive, but he's chill. You'll watch good movies.

I had him for lecture. He is a really sweet and supportive professor. He is very passionate about his work, but I wish we could cover more content in class. What you learn is important, but I just wanted more! If you have any questions in class, he is always willing to discuss. I wish I had him for something like recitation!

I only had him for lecture, but they were a lot. The class seems like it would be super interesting, but after the third lecture it becomes clear that this class is not. I think it could be, but this professor rambles on and on and on about the same thing every lecture, and loses a lot of the classes attention.

Had him for recitation. Gives really good feedback on our directed scenes at the end of the semester. Very knowledgeable about his craft and thorough when explaining what could have been improved upon. Also, the fluctuations in his voice are very theatrical and it's fun to listen to.
Slides are jame packed with information, and imagine a text heavy course with someone who is very monotone… It just isn't helpful. I wish there was a different option available as far as professors.

imo she's not bad. everything that she said was on the exam was on the exam. don't need to read the textbook, it's rly just her slides. this was also my easy class so idk bc the exam average was in the 65-75 range.

Not the best at teaching the course. She reads off the slides and doesn't give any great examples, or clearance of the lectures. Her exams and homework questions are very tricky. Very stressful course.

Honestly, I'm disappointed with NYU. How they have kept this professor on for so long is beyond me. She doesn't know how to teach the subject. Although she is very knowledgeable, her lectures are extremely boring and do not prepare you for a test. The class average on test is an D to F. She is doing something wrong, should be investigated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Everybody does poorly in this class. It is a waste of money, time, and effort and will lower your GPA. Find another professor for this course.

You're provided with class slides that include notes prior to class. You definitely need the textbook for this class because she cannot explain things well and is condescending when you ask questions. She takes attendance almost every time, so show up. You also need to purchase the iclicker. Try to take a different professor if you have the option.

Boring lectures that are just summary of the textbook. Always fails to explain questions well. Takes attendance almost every time, so show up. Just remember the really detailed stuff. All about memorization.
Dr. Lancaster fails to give useful feedback and speaks to students in a condescending manner.
Good class, but a bit boring.  She is a smart professor and cares about her students learning.

Kurokawa is amazing! Don't be put off by her sometimes sarcastic or not soft manner - she always means well and underneath it she is an amazing teacher who has passion AND knows the art of teaching a foreign language. She is homework, participation, and quiz/exam heavy but by the end of the semester that work will show in your Japanese skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Take it if you love her bad attitude and being treated harsh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kurokawa sensei's classes made NYU such a wonderful experience for me a few years ago. I took this class on a whim as a graduate student and thanks to her class, my interest in Japanese language was born. I'm studying for the JLPT now, and I really owe it to her class. Be prepared to work and memorize hiragana/katagana before day 1!

She's pretty nice, but also really strict. You have to participate EVERY class, which is expected for a language class. If you get the answer wrong she might get annoyed, but if you do the homework and memorize grammar structures you should be fine. Very strict on attendance. She's kind and cares about everyone. Exams are a little difficult.

She may look strict, but she is super nice! She's very clear with the grammar, if you want a great grammar learning experience, choose her! If you listen in class, and you do the review sheets carefully, you will definitely get a good grade on the test! The work loads are manageable.
Very good professor, you can really learn something from her class. She is very patient.

I've taken several teachers' courses and Kurokawa is definitely the BEST Japanese language lecturer in the department in terms of personality, course structure, and teaching. She is caring and funny, talks very fast but pays attention to the words she uses to make sure you understand what she says, and she tries to engage everyone in discussions.
She is a nice teacher but a lot of workloads. But as long as you did them, you are fine. I really like her

Kurokawa-sensei is one of the best professors at NYU. She is super engaging and makes zoom class very fun. I think she is also very hilarious. Going to her class was one of the few highlights during this semester. Unlike other professors, she also replies to emails really quickly and follows up with you. I think I'm going to take her class again!

I took her post-adv. special topics course "Japanese for your future" and she was great. She made sure to incorporate everyone's interests in terms of how they intend on using Japanese in their future. I assume at post-adv. grading becomes more lenient, and she's open to student input as well as going the extra mile to help you. Highly recommend!

Kurokawa sensei is truly great! You would definitely get a good grade if you passionately participate in class discussions, and prepare well for exams and oral exams. She is accessible after class, so you can ask her questions or practice spoken Japanese during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A lot of workloads, super stressful. She is always annoyed at you if you don't get the answers right or get everything right LOL. She seems to hate students in general. Her class is a nightmare, which makes me not even want to visit Japan. Just don't take the class. Biggest regret in my life.

Kurokawa sensei is one of the best Japanese instructors at NYU. Taken her Intermediate 2 and Adv I. If you follow her lecture and do homework you will be fine. Go to her office hour and she will go through your essays word by word. Even though she is a little bit strict, she is open to students' ideas and gives well-organized lectures. Respected.

She does not respect the students and has a really bad attitude. There is an electronic version of the textbook. However, she does not like students to use iPad during class. Although she had tutor session for those who got bad grade for test, she blames on you for the most of the time which is very disrespectful and irritate you.

Classes are really helpful, and they cover exactly what you are expected to know. Show up to class consistently and put in reasonable effort on the assignments and the class will not be difficult at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is one of the best professor I had. Definitely accessible. If you go to her office hour she will help on refining every line of your essay. If you want a good grade just go to her officehours and put more efforts on it.

Kurokawa-sensei is a fine teacher. She truly cares about the teaching of Japanese and really wants her students to succeed. The issue comes when they do not. She has a tendency to get annoyed and frustrated by students who ask questions she deems unworthy, or who don't seem to understand despite her extra help. Okay class, just be careful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Kurokawa is probably my favorite Japanese teacher that I've had so far; She might seem a little intimidating at first but her classes become very lighthearted and entertaining. She's a great teacher and she is ALWAYS there to help if you ask for it (at the appropriate times ofc).
Good, kind, and helpful.

She was a really helpful teacher. It was difficult at times because the lessons were carried out at a very fast pace. But other than that, she is committed to the class and her class was overall fun as well :)
Kurokawa-sensei is decent enough as a teacher, if you can get around her unpleasant personality. She seems irritated with her students most of the time. Try for a different teacher.
Kurokawa-sensei seems a little strict and old-fashioned, but she is actually pretty funny and nice! Very helpful and encouraging.

This class is very homework heavy which is the only annoying part of this course so I don't understand all the negative reviews. At the start of the semester he repeated multiple times that this course will get more difficult and you will have to teach yourself some things. The assignments are quite literally all called "self paced xyz".

reviews.comment: He can barely teach, takes months to grade, and tests are worth most of the class grade.

reviews.comment: Professor is very awkward but he was nice. He teaches through PPT and then asking us to code a little ourselves in class. Just ensure you review the HWs and common CS quiz/ exam questions to practice coding and prep for the exam.
