reviews.comment: RUN THE OTHER WAY. I took this class because I had no other choice, and I can understand why the previous reviews were so bad. Doesn't really teach and only rambles to himself in class (keep in mind, I came in with zero coding experience). Ended up self-teaching with ChatGPT and asking CS major friends for help.

By far one of the worst teachers I have ever had. The homework does not reflect what we learn in lecture, and he does not grade work until the end of the course, meaning you have no feedback on how you are doing until AFTER you've taken your final, worth 35%.
Nice guy but not good at teaching. Lectures are extremely tedious and unhelpful. Minor mistakes on homework result in large point deductions.

Teaches horribly, material is difficult enough, and all the assignments and homework are impossibly hard compared to the material that is taught. Everyone in the class is equally as confused and average test scores are low. Indicates how great he is as a teacher. For this class you just have to self teach everything.

Absolutely downright catastrophically bad; socially hindered with severe awkwardness that can feel rude at times, grueling lectures that have no engagement with students, and enough coursework to guarantee you have no time for any other course. Teacher has a horrible reputation throughout the department and it's recommended you take someone else.

Prof is definitely shy but literally you can ask him questions about everything and he's SO helpful. Always willing to put in the time and effort needed to explain things and make sure u get it. Also his exams aren't bad if you just pay attention

Avoid this professor! He will take attendance seriosuly and teaching mostly by reading slides. He gives complicated examples on class that nobody can follow. He also gives very long and hard homework. You might need to study something extra from the syllabus to complete them. His test is nothing related with the homework and on the easy side.
not a good teacher, cannot teach at all. a good person, but he's just a bit awkward.
He is a genuinely nice person, he is simply not a good teacher at all.
A kind and generous person.  But he expects you to learn, which maybe some people don't like.

Don't understand why his ratings are so low. His teachings were satisfactory, though I learned more in the online modules/assignments than his lectures. He is a very kind and caring person and had a generous curve on his exams. Takes feedback greatly, and made the final a lot easier after realizing the midterm was a bit difficult

I ended up dropping the class because of how bad my midterm grade was and how little of a curve he gave. He is nice but makes tests so insanely hard, and most students just stop showing up halfway through the sem. Most people who had him will tell you his class was the worst, just avoid

He's a great person but not a good teacher. He releases retrospectives. He asks students for lesson feedback and check in with them if they have any questions. 
Has high expectations on students, would extend the material by "too much."
Assignments were very unclear. Had to ask for a lot of clarifications. 
Exams were really tough, too.
Sucks at teaching, socially awkward doesn't get to know his students at all. Don't take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most useless and boring class

It's his first time teaching right out of grad which makes sense why he is super disorganized and not a great teacher. And, for an intro course, expects too much from students and isn't very flexible especially with office hours. All his assignments have mistakes and aren't clear. He's not a bad person just not a good teacher. Also kinda awkward.

okay guys when i say hes disorganized like its so bad i literally cannot do these assignments because theyre worded so poorly and he is so harsh on grading and he literally changes the criteria in the assignments HOURS before its due... please explore alternative professors for this class especially as an intro class tis so bad

Never checks attendance or gets to know your name. Midterm and problem sets are very poorly worded causing lots of confusion on what was expected. The entire course is essentially self taught through modules but that is standard across all intro to comp prog classes as well as 30% midterm 30% problem sets 30% final and 10% module quiz/participation

His instructions on the assignments are so confusing and I needed to ask many clarification questions. The grading is extremely unclear. He is very kind and caring, so that somewhat makes up for it. But I would not take him again.

Dr. K is the real deal. While he focuses on making sure you understand the textbook concepts, he equally cares about ensuring you learn soft skills. If you show up on time, participate, and ask questions, you will be halfway there. Not only is he my professor, but he is also my faculty advisor. I now have a lifelong mentor in Dr. K.
Alot of research and readings. Group projects are expected. He is very passionate, respected, and inspirational. There is a field trip and alot of guest speakers.

Dr. K is a wonderful and inspiring professor who delivers amazing lectures and makes every class genuinely fun and engaging. The course material is incredibly interesting and valuable, and he truly cares about his students both academically and professionally. I have learned so much from him. One of the most rewarding classes I've taken.

With Dr. K, you'll learn the foundations of business and apply it to the hospitality and travel industry. But most importantly, you will learn how to be a more disciplined person by learning about essential soft skills. If you put in the work, it is guaranteed you'll learn valuable lessons about yourself as a student and as a future professional.

Best Professor ever, cannot recommend enough. He is so engaging in class and not only good at explaining the content but also teaches life lessons. He is very realistic about the society and gives great tips and advice. Very inspirational professor.

Dr.K is simply amazing. His classes are always so fun and engaging. He really cares for his students and is ready to help you. You will learn so much from him. The class is not difficult as long as you put in the effort. Easily one of my favorite professors!

Dr. K is the professor you hope to get at NYU. His passion is contagious and his industry experiences bring the classroom to life. On top of class visits to Google HQ or the UN, every class was insightful and inspiring. He truly cares about student success — always approachable, endlessly supportive, and genuinely invested in our growth.

Dr. K is an incredibly passionate professor who genuinely cares about his students' success. His classes are an excellent way to learn about Business and offer valuable life lessons. I recommend taking his class.
Dr.K is a really great professor, you should take his class, it is worth it. He has a great passion to teach which made the class really interesting and engaging.

Dr. K is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about business and marketing, making every lecture engaging and insightful. He genuinely cares about their students' success and is always approachable for help. I highly recommend taking their class!

Dr. K is an amazing Professor! Truly cares for his students, wants the best for them, and will push them to do their best. I genuinely thought that this class was fun, interactive, and very informative. His teachings about life and the business world are so meaningful and valuable. I would certainly take him again!!!!

Dr.K is one of the most amazing professors here at NYU. His lecture is amazing, and he cares for his students so much, which helps students make their future endeavors successful. Just keep your focus and try to understand what he is saying. Then all good! I highly recommend taking his class and also want others to get an impact from him, like me.

Dr. K is a very kind professor.  He wants us to succeed in life and is well-known in the industry. He teaches many life lessons along with the curriculum. Exams are challenging but not impossible if you study and read the textbook. It's not an easy A; work is required.  But you will learn. I enjoyed my experience with Dr. K.

Dr. K is a great human being and a great professor. He is hilarious, engaging, and inspirational. I have taken away so many life lessons from his teachings and advice. He truly cares for his students and the school. He places a deep focus on networking and encourages students to utilize as many resources that NYU has to offer. Read the textbook!

The best professor I have had so far in SPS NYU. Class is exciting, he's super funny, cares about your personal life and personal career more than your grades. Priortizes your understanding of the concepts and really cares for his students. Don't be afraid to ask questions in class, and make sure to participate! Offers immense support if needed.

Ok to be fair I love Dr. K. Such a respected professor with clear grading criteria. It's just a LOT OF WORK. I am repeating, A LOT OF WORK. Participation matters very much along with weekly group presentations. I love him, I think I grew a lot through his class, but it was stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very passionate about his career and caring for his students. He is a great professor and is willing to re-teach content to students. Mid-term and final are difficult, and they count for the majority of your grade.

Dr.K is a great professor. He is enthusiastic about his topics, and he is a very flexible professor with students and their time. He takes care of students' careers and gives excellent advice and feedback about the course and the students' career life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. K is amazing! He really knows how to engage you in the class. He understands your skills and try to elevate them along with other skills he thinks you need to achieve to become a leader in your field. His class is fun and energetic, there is no room for boredom there. I learned a lot!!

Professor Karaburun has high expectations for the class, but his enthusiasm for the subject makes you want to perform to the best of your ability. His class is well organized, the assignments are well defined and the class discussions elicit dynamic class participation. Take any class Dr K teaches!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good amount of team work makes the class engaging, professor actually tries to teach and cares about students, will make time outside to class to meet if students need help.
His teaching style can be hard sometimes. However, you will learn a lot. During his classes, you will also receive  few carreer and professional advices which are always welcome.

Avoid at all costs! While she does have a clear criteria, the workload is difficult, especially the last project, which will take up much of your time. reviews.comment: Although this class is straightforward in terms of concepts, her exams are difficult and her projects take a immense amount of time for no reason. She has a great structure of the course but her teaching and grading are the worst compared to other professors. Avoid if can
Mental breakdown!!! But have to admit this professor teaches clearly.

A very challenging professor with difficult exams and long projects. Only take this class if you're serious about cs and actually wanna improve. Otherwise, take an easier professor.

Don't take, otherwise you'll end up struggling throughout the course.
She somehow makes the class extremely stressful for no good reason, whether intentional or not. The teaching style will probably suit high school students more to be honest.

Reviews are not harsh. Projects require 30+hrs of work (you'll still do bad). Lectures and concepts seem simple but exams are rough. Pointless recitations. She expects 6-8 hrs of studying outside of projects a week. Could not recommend less. She's cold. RIP your GPA. You will become a good coder, but out of pain and suffering.

Clear lectures, but exams are much more difficult, testing things you thought were trivial. I recommend doing the practice sets and slide deck questions/examples. Professor is pretty good compared to other data structure professors. You really do learn a lot. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thought I would get a awful grade since it is a tough course and I didn't take the prerequisite course Basic Algorithm, but her lecture is extremely inspiring and useful so I paid some effort and got back on track. I end up getting an A despite the fact that I gave up half of the points on a couple of homeworks and got a B for the midterm.
Can't believe she can make data structure so difficult.
Sure she makes you a good coder. That'll be your consolation prize when she tanks your gpa after spending countless nights writing her projects. Do not be fooled by her 5/5 here like I was

I truly do not understand how this professor has a 5 on this website. If you truly believe this is accurate then I truly believe you will get an F in this class by looking at the star distribution. I truly don't understand why doesn't Joanna buy herself a punching bag instead of pulling up to CANTOR-200, as all of us could have better lives.
Pay attention during lectures and properly spend time to understand the concepts and this class isn't as bad as everyone makes it seem like it is.

Joanna's class develops a strong foundation in computer science that will help you with the rest of your computer science journey. Took this class 2 semesters ago, and I'll say this, if you ever want to work at FAANG or any other big tech/quant company: take Joanna's class and push your capabilities. Work in the present to succeed in the future.

Yeah the projects are hard but that's why programmers get paid a lot lol you can't get a job and cry about doing a big task or project. This class is NOT for the weak but Joanna will help you learn and get you HIRED. If you're not cut out for this workload, don't go into CS. Data structures are the foundation of CS and one day you will thank her.

Most of these reviews fooled me... Joanna is a BAD professor. Ask anyone in my Data Structures class, and they will say as much. Her teaching skills are awful in a REALLY intense class, she grades harshly, and her recitation leaders are equally bad. The ones who say she's the worst? - The 15-20% of us who got above a B. She does not prep you 4 CS.

you will become a good coder in this class but at the price of your gpa and your will to continue learning cs. Take anyone but her. Has one of the strictest grading policies of any professor I have taken. Her exams are HARD and very unforgiving and her projects will take you an insane amount of time.

People are too harsh. Projects are difficult, but they prepare you to become a good programmer. I have cried over this class but everyone giving a bad review is bitter. I've learnt a lot and the projects are useful. Joanna is a very good lecturer. I'm a humanities major and not great at CS but have done well in the class. Quizzes aren't that hard.
The review below this

Very harsh grader. Her assignments leave the university's tutors confused. Very easy to mess up her quizzes/ exams and a couple bad grades can bring your grade to a C. Is very knowledgeable but comes off as condescending if you ask for help. Take someone else if you haven't coded for your whole life
I had to drop my minor due to this course. If it was another professor, I know the outcome would've been different. If you learn through example, this is not the professor for you.

She is by far the most difficult CS professor I have encountered at NYU. Her lectures are structured in the sense that they are not appealing to all learning types and it makes it difficult to learn things. Very little example code, or explanation on how to execute the concepts. If you learn by example, this is not the professor for you.

Took Joanna last semester, out of 5 CS professors I have encountered thus far, she is the best one if you want to learn. I think she delivers material very well and is very engaging, the stuff she explained really stuck with me. Her quizzes are tricky though, a couple of missed questions and you're getting C, but she did have a curve at the end.
Best class of my life! Amazing lecturer and fair exams.

Prof Klukowska is the most serious prof ever. I recall her laughing only 4 times that semester(spoiler): 1. 8 rabbit=rabyte 2. Little vs Big Endian 3&4. Mock at others and me kindly for being dumb. She is very caring and answers all of your question, but she likely won't make you love CS. She is most helpful if you are already interested in CS.

Regardless of my grade, I can say prof K's lectures are very well organized, insightful and she's always willing to help, only if you ask her first. If you want to learn, take her class. If you are just looking to get through data structures with a good grade, take another prof. Would be very helpful the sooner you get used to her testing style.

simply not a good professor. quizzes and midterm are difficult for no reason and her answer keys almost always have at least 1 mistake or more. a very theoretical class with lots of useless "trace the output" like questions rather than actually writing/designing programs. take bari if you can. gl.

Aside from CS102 being a complete waste of time to begin with, Klukowsa makes sure it's as big of a waste of time as possible. We have the midterm in a few days and have so far covered Linked Lists in lecture. But not extensively at all. Nor have we applied them in any context. Four 30 min quizzes are 24% of ur grade and class avg is an F.

Don't take a class with her unless you know all the material already. Posts problem sets where the instructions are useless then spends 40 minutes each class explaining what she wants. When you try to reach out to her for help she actively avoids you. She does not even grade assignments and her auto-grader makes mistakes. Dont take her class
joanna is a good professor. projects get difficult by end of the year so make sure you start them early. quizzes and tests were harder than the projects for me personally. no curve.
Class isn't easy but you really learn. She cares a lot about the subject. Reminds you why the subjects are worth learning about

She is extremely condescending and unapproachable. Projects are horrendously difficult, quizzes and exams are much more manageable. Extremely rude when people asked questions during class. She teaches as though she would rather be doing anything else.
the GOAT

Prof said she won't curve, but she ending up doing huge adjustments, pushing everyone's grade up.

Great professor to have if you actually want to learn a lot. HOWEVER... her projects and quizzes are hard. We actually need to learn the materials. The professor is supper accessible during office hours.

Joanna is useless to me. She is rude and condescending in class and that makes her absolutely unapproachable for me. So far all assignments have been graded incorrectly you can never really be sure of your grade. She doesn't believe in curving and dropping grades. reviews.comment: I love Joanna. I have had the greatest computer science experience with her in Data Structures, and highly recommend for everyone to take her.

I adore Joanna. Took her for DS, and even took 8am just to get her again for CSO. Her lecture explanations are always crystal clear (go to them!). Start the projects early and they are no problem, spec is detailed on expectations (plus she is very active on Piazza). Tests are super fair, never any surprises - but they will test you thoroughly.

This is by far the toughest class I've taken at NYU and Joanna as a prof. certainly doesn't make it any easier. super great lectures, learned so much from her, would highly recommend. do as she says and you'll do great.
best comp sci teacher

Although Joanna is a relatively tough grader, you will ultimately get a higher grade with her than with another professor (e.g. Bari). Amazing teacher, she even takes questions from real CS interviews. One of the questions discussed in class was the exact same question I was asked in my internship interview. Personally got an A-, highly recommend.
Very difficult to get an A. Great lectures, test heavy, pop quizzez.. take Bari if you can  hes more chill. Shes a solid choice otherwise.

I have to say she's the best cs professor ever. She explains everything super clear and knows the class material very well. I took both Data Structure and CSO with her. I learnt a lot. reviews.comment: she does not curve at all.

reviews.comment: Joanna is a solid professor. Even though she's a pretty tough grader, her expectations are really clear. Projects can be long but she teaches very clearly so that you know how to apply the data structures in the projects. TL;DR - she's tough but you learn a lot.

reviews.comment: Go to class and take notes, you will learn so much and she explains things clearly and in depth. Adhere to her spec for projects or your grade will be wrecked; if things are not clear, ASK questions. Her exams are super fair, make sure you understand concepts and do not rely on solely memorizing code.

I honestly didn't think that she was too difficult as a professor, exam average is 80. She is very fair. Take the time to review the material on your own time and it won't be too bad. Make sure you're very thorough and efficient in all of your projects from the start because everyone gets wrecked on the first one.

She's highly recommended and now that I took her Data Structures class I know why! You will learn AND work hard. I recommend forming a study group in the class for studying purposes. There is no group work except in recitations. She only teaches CSO in the Spring semester. Most of the grade (65%) is only the midterm and final. She doesn't curve.

Despite that, she did an amazing job being thorough with the material, and is a professor that I genuinely like to go to her lectures.  TAKE HER 500% if you have a choice between her and anyone else for either 201 or 102!

An excellent lecturer, makes classes interactive and remembers the names of her students. Does pop quizzes if she sees attendance drop. Her exams are long, but she's up front about the material on it. She loves to assign stuff, so don't wait until the last minute to start something.  She's worth the effort, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Joanna is a fantastic lecturer, extremely organized, and very helpful. She gives so many helpful resources and they are all extremely clear and concise. Read everything she posts! I will say, even though this is true for every CS teacher I've had, I wish she / the graders gave the assignments back earlier so you can get feedback quicker.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: If you're serious about Data Structures and really want to learn about it, take Joanna's class! She makes you learn more about knowing an algorithm rather than memorizing the code. She can be challenging, but she is one of the best teachers you will ever have. Her office hours are extremely helpful too.

I had Joanna for 102 as well and honestly I think it was a joke compared to 201.  201 lectures are just way more rushed and difficult to digest. Also, pop quizzes are weighed pretty heavily (almost 10%) despite them being quite luck based (there were only 3 of them and who the hell can always be caught up in a class like 201).  She's helpful tho.

Joanna is so solid. Her accent is both understandable and enjoyable (Polish-like tendencies) so I recommend lectures in a major way. I'm not gonna lie, this professor is gonna grade you. Her pen is a weapon and you have to battle it. Buy the book fam, save laundry quarters for a couple months or something, I don't know your life, but it's worth it
Super easy A, definitely take her. Jokes aside, easy A if you actually study the lecture notes and do the practice questions from the book.
Her projects are one of the simplest compared with other professors since all you need to do is implement classes and not start everything from scratch. Her tests, though, are difficult

I took the class before this in the curriculum with a very easy professor that made me think I was a coding genius, put Professor Klukowska kicked me into reality. She is really one of the best professors I've ever had, and I've learned more from her in 2 months of this class than in any class I've taken before. Take her take her take her!

She really goes into the algorithms of how things work and is big on visuals. Not much coding in class, and even then it is pseudocode. She cares more about your understanding. She is really nice and always there to help. Just do not be afraid to ask questions and work enough to get an A

I had Professor Klukowska at NYU this semester, as a freshman. Her class was a perfect introduction to Java and Computer Science, and I'm so glad to have her again in the Spring for Data Structures! Her class isn't easy but it's so worth it once you have those "ooooh!! OOH!!" moments. She's always available and there for her students. 1010.

Joanna is by far one of the best Computer Science teachers I've had. Her notes are clear and she provides source code for every problem. Exams are really straightforward  they test whether or not you've done the homework on your own. If you listen in class you will do well.

She is a helpful professor. The programming projects are a little bit tough if you pursue extra credits. The homework is manageable. If you want to get a high grade, read her lecture notes and complete all of homework.

She's a friendly and nice person, and is very helpful and understanding during office hours. Lectures are pretty boring. Perfect Comp Sci professor. Not incredibly easy, but you will learn obscene amounts from Kapp. He truly cares about his students as well as the course material. Very approachable and encourages everyone to go beyond his class. I wish I could switch to comp sci major =/

Just do yourself a favor and take his class. You won't regret it. Craig Kapp is one of the most helpful and genuine professors I've had at NYU. And did I mention he actually teaches you the material? And that he cares about whether you understand or not?? Just take his class already.

An amazing professor. Classes are interesting, and homeworks are extremely helpful. Attendance is mandatory (sign-in sheet). Lessons are very organized; all materials are posted on the course website. He's approachable and dependable. The best of the best!
He inspired me to change my major to compsci and he is now writing letters of recommendation for me. Phenomenal professor and person.

Very organized slides. Very organized curriculum. Consistent teaching method. Homeworks are useful and he drops the lowest one. Exams are fair. Always tries to show practical applications of the course as well. Very solid overall.

Professor Kapp is the best professor I've had at NYU. He made me want to switch my major to Comp Sci and I'm not a computer science person. His lectures are so clear, his powerpoints are amazing, he posts everything to a blog, and he grades extremely fairly. I have not a single bad thing to say about him. LOVEDDDD

Craig is a brilliant and enthusiastic professor, and overall awesome guy. You'd be remiss to not take one of his classes. He is extremely friendly, chipper, patient, and engaging. Some people are just born to teach, and he is one of those people.

Best professor at NYU. Very good at explaining concepts. Always prepared for class. Very willing to help and an overall great person. Only negative is that the homework assignments can be quite lengthy and time-consuming.
Great teacher. Makes the subject easy to understand.

He's a phenomenal teacher. He's challenging, but it's easy to maintain an A in the class. He's very approachable and shows interesting applications of the coding he demonstrates in class. Definitely take his class!

Truly excellent professor, one of the best I've ever had. I had no prior knowledge of computer programming but he explained all of the concepts so well and made the subject accessible. Exams directly correlated with the material taught in class. Does everything he can to help you learn. Highly recommended professor & class.
Don't hesitate to take one of his courses. Does everything he can so that you learn the subject, and goes out of his way so that you succeed in the class. Always nice and helpful.

It was truly a pleasure to be in Craig class. He is well organized, intelligent, kind and extremely helpful. He has a great personality, as well. You can't help but love the guy. I recommend taking this class, even if you aren't a computer science minor/major.

Great teacher and person. He takes attendance and there is a homework assignment once a week. However, Intro to Comp Programming was my favorite class this semester. Kapp is super organized, extremely smart, and really helpful. You won't regret taking his class!

Professor Kapp is the best professor I have ever had. He explains everything with the upmost clarity, is always willing to help you out if you have questions, and is extremely laid back. As long as you do the homework, the exams are simple as well. Overall, highly recommended.

The best! Very cool guy, explains very well, provides lots of examples, tests are fair, HW is fair, helps with HW,really nice and approachable, even inspired me to be a CompSci major. Gives plenty of study guides and by far this has been my favorite class and professor at NYU.

Craig Kapp is the best professor I've ever had. It was an absolute pleasure to be in his Intro to Programming Class. I've learned SO much and, suddenly, comp sci feels accessible for someone as humanities-minded as myself. He's a great professor, really helpful, super nice, laid-back, funny, an awesome guy. who made programming feel... do-able. :-)

He is the best professor I ever had at NYU! Extremely organized, exam questions are very fair, some extra credits available to boost up your grades, and very very helpful. There is no reason not to take him. Although there is a hw almost every week, it really helps you to practice what you have learned in class. I love the class.

Craig is an extremely helpful professor.  His methods of teaching far surpass the other intro to programming professors.  In this class, I learned a lot about programming in python and made many programs.  To keep it short, I don't think that there could have been a better intro to computer programming professor.

Craig is an amazing professor and is highly recommended. Super down to earth and friendly and willing to go out of his way to help any student in the class. The course itself doesn't go into any one topic in extensive detail but it is an excellent overview to a variety of computer programs and an invaluable foundation to have for the future.

Lori was my Practicum Advisor. She was always very accessible and provided the information I needed. She helped me find 2 great internships and was very supportive and attentive. Lori was a big part of my education and I appreciate her!

Amazing! Always available and really understands the challenges at practicum placements. She helped me to see things in a more positive light and just take what I can from my placement rather than focusing on the negative. It really turned my experience around. I am very grateful. NYU is lucky to have Lori.

Lori is awesome! So caring and supportive. When I wasn't happy in my placement, she helped me find a new one. She always listens and understands my concerns. I am very lucky to have her as my practicum advisor.
She's a terrible practicum instructor she should be fired. Everyone has so many issues and she doesn't care about the students only pretends that she does. She just cares about keeping her job .
Not helpful at all.
avoid this class at all costs. getting an A is impossible and her expectations are unreal. she grades freshmen like we're grad students.

reviews.comment: Lots of work. Would not take again despite grade. She's a nice person but not a good/reasonable teacher.

Super hard grader, every other prof is easier cause it's supposed to be a beginner class. Her lectures are really boring and the class is not science-focused like it claims to be. You'll regret having her...

reviews.comment: If you need this course for a requirement, choose almost anything else. Despite the name "Scientific Inquiry," the content has little to do with academic science. Instead, it focuses on an anthropological approach to social issues such as gender roles and disability stereotypes rather than the scientific method you'd expect.

reviews.comment: go to her office hours and meet with her at least twice for the big essays to make sure that she likes it, if you really care. do the readings because she gave a few pop reading quizzes. don't know anyone who got an A in the class.

reviews.comment: She is a really tough grader like I think only 10% of the class got an A and she is really strict about being on time and attendance. Really pay attention when you schedule draft conferences because that was the most helpful thing she does all year.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is such a hard-worker who gives very helpful criticism on writing exercises that can help you fluorish on final essays. She answers emails on weekends and is very available by appointment, so there's no reason not to do good. You don't have to be the best writer to get an A, just work with her and apply everything you learn in class in writing

A clinical professor who takes her required writing class way too seriously. Obsessed with ethics but lacks the self awareness to realize its unethical to make her students work 4x as hard as other teachers teaching the same class. Approx 10% of class is on track for an A. 

Avoid if possible.

The class itself is pretty challenging, but Professor Liston leaves incredibly detailed feedback on all assignments, including exercises and drafts. Structure of the class is nice too, the homework prepares you for the final essay. Only downside is the insane amount of reading, but you'll get that with a lot of professors for expos courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: In my opinion, the course difficulty has little association with professor ratings. The professor is a very nice person who is genuinely interested in the topics she teaches. Her feedback is detailed and helpful. Students definitely need to commit substantial time & effort. This course helps greatly in critical thinking & writing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Liston is a kind person, however, her coursework is heavy. She gives essays every week but does give helpful feedback on them. Lots of work. Hard grader, but a nice professor.

Probably the most stressful and unrewarding class I've ever taken. Prof isn't even a bad person, just know that your painstaking efforts will not be acknowledged in this class. Only recommend this class if you're majoring in writing/humanities area
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Most likely the hardest course you will ever take in NYU. Prepare to write essays every week and be graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I felt like she was really tough in class. Lowkey is kinda sweet if you meet one-on-one but idk. Maybe it was more about the fact that the class is boring and she doesn't make it fun. I don't regret not dropping the class but I wouldn't take it again.

While my writing did improve a lot, often times I would receive comments on what I could improve after submitting the final essay that had never previously been mentioned in draft comments. Luckily these did not seem to substantially impact my grade, but I wish I had the chance to fix what was mentioned in them beforehand.

reviews.comment: WTE with Professor Liston was life-changing- the quality of my writing improved by more than I ever thought possible. But let me make one thing clear- previous reviews who say she is too tough of a grader are absolutely wrong. She makes you work for your grade, as she should. As long as you put in any sort of effort in you will be FINE

reviews.comment: very nice, lectures are actually interesting if you listen and he's very knowlegeable (just seems boring because he's monotone) & pretty easy class, readings are long but you can get by just reading the ones needed for reading responses + essays

One bad thing is the AWFUL final paper deadlines, but overall fascinating class

reviews.comment: One of the best profs in MEIS & NYU no doubt. Neg reviews bc he doesn't parrot mainstream narratives ab Israel & the ME (stay mad). He has a wealth of knowledge and I'm v grateful to have taken his class

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and class! My favorite at NYU. Prof. Lockman is a giant in the field and obviously extremely knowledgeable. Take all the classes you can with him!

Prof. Lockman is super knowledgeable about the Palestine-Israel conflict and his lectures --albeit dry--are easy to follow and break down the conflict really well, but the amount of readings & essays is beyond excessive. Our TA was nice, but recitations weren't too useful, since they discussed readings, which most people didn't do.

reviews.comment: I promise you I am here to help you: DO. NOT. TAKE. THIS. CLASS! Professor Lockman is incredibly knowledgeable/smart, but I believe he is biased to the material he teaches, he's not open to hearing the questions of students (you're scared to ask a question), a final exam (some core classes don't), BORING lectures. Not worth your work or time.

I took Professor Lockman's Imagining Palestine/Israel class. It was BY FAR the most interesting and fulfilling class. My TA was amazing and very easy to communicate with and reach out to. Professor Lockman really knows his stuff and the assignments and reading are nothing out of the ordinary for a Cultures & Contexts core class.

reviews.comment: Prof is nice but most of your communicating will be with TA but that is fair because core classes are usually quite large in size. The class is heavy in content but okay in workload, although the general course is really interesting and stimulating.

I took this class because I was casually interested in the topic, and saw that Professor Lockman had a high rating. I'm not sure if it's because of COVID, or if most of the past ratings were left by students who were very interested in the topic, but this semester was horrible. Lots of readings, dry lectures, harsh grading. Avoid for your own sake.

reviews.comment: This class really opened my eyes in terms of Palestinian and Israeli conflict, but was the worst core class I took. You have to write four 1000 words essays that have really complex prompts and should be much longer.

reviews.comment: This class was the bane of my semester because of the heavy and complicating content and the workload. Prof Lockman is clearly very knowledgeable on Middle Eastern history and politics, so you will enjoy his class if you are truly interested. But it could definitely be recognised and made easier given it is a type of core requirement.

Only take this class if you are PROPERLY and TRULY interested in the middle east history and politics. It will be too time consuming, challenging and stressful for a core class. The TAs grade harshly and the curve is high.

reviews.comment: I took this class because I'd heard about the israel conflicts but knew nothing about them. I couldn't even tell you who the Israelis were or who they conflicted with. But I wanted to learn more. The class taught me much more than I expected and I have an informed opinion now. Awesome prof, great lectures. I learned so much and vouch for his class.

Professor Lockman knows his history, and it shows. Every lecture is filled with a wealth of information, and he is obviously passionate about the subject he teaches. Some students have called him biased. Coming into this course, I was casually pro-Israel. But once I learned the facts, my opinion on the issue shifted to match reality. Thanks Prof Z

Prof. Lockman knows his stuff and is clearly passionate about his field. A respected historian, Lockman is at home lecturing and his class is always enjoyable. Although his personal biases are well known, his teaching hews only to facts and students are encouraged to explore their own perspectives. Readings can be a lot but are generally useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great professor that I highly recommend. Very clear, organized lectures that were very thorough but also very interesting. For a history class that could easily be hard to sit through it definitely was not. Not biased and very clear that actions made aren't the actions or opinions of all people.

Lockman is a very nice professor and does care about the eduction of his students, however his bias towards the material made me and many others dislike the class. Overall, the class load is not difficult, however listening to him is often frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took the PZI class with him and loved it. Lockman is a very intelligent, caring, and approachable professor. The course itself was challenging yet interesting. if you study for it, you'll get an A.

PZI was such a great class. I'm so sad that it's over. I looked forward to every lecture and recitation. The work load wasn't too bad--five response papers, two midterm essays, and a final exam. All were very manageable. Highly recommend taking this course, even if this isn't a subject you have a lot of interest in.
he is a great teacher, great person. I owe him a lot for my intellectual development

Had him for "Palestine, Zionism, and Israel". Professor Lockman's lectures are extremely interesting. Two essays (bring your thesis to the TA for a good chance of a good grade), 5 500 word response papers to the homework, and a final exam. For the final he gave us a study guide with terms and essay topics. Put in the work, and you can get an A.
Lockman's a great guy. Interesting class with a great discussion. Matt, the TA, can be a tough grader, at times, but led an interesting recitation. Highly recommend.

Great Professor, and very interesting class. The readings were engaging, and the lectures were organized and informative. Work-load was average. If you do the readings and show up to class, you should be fine in terms of grades. You'll walk out of the class with an abundance of knowledge. Good stuff, good stuff.

Professor Lockman is a gem. He cares deeply about the historical issues he has devoted his scholarship to, and it comes across in his teaching. Very approachable (though not the chattiest man) and a wealth of knowledge. Challenges his students to move beyond grandiose statements into real thought. Take him if you have the chance.

"Palestine, Zionism, and Israel" was one of the best classes I took at NYU. Professor Lockman's lectures were clear, rigorous, and engaging. He is very open to answering questions and meeting with students outside of class.

Very Modest, knowledgeable, respectful and JUST. One of the best profs that I've ever known. I truly enjoyed the lectures and discussions in his grad course; intellectually challenging and fulfilling.

He's incredibly  knowledgeable and a really interesting lecturer. I took a class about something I knew nothing on and at the end of it feel really confident about the subject. A lot of reading, but most of it does enhance the discussion. Take his class!
He is a great professor, a pro in his field, a great adviser for graduate students, a great reader, very helpful, down to earth. The best professor you could possibly have.
Great teacher. Really informed in his field. Not extremely organized but if you're interested in the Middle East you should definitely take a course from him.
sooooo much unnecessary homework & not that clear on feedback for essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Schnairsohn is nice and will actually make you feel like you improved at writing without being unfair at all. Your grade is basically only dictated by your essays, but he gives great constructive feedback on essays, and the grading isn't harsh. The homework/lecture work aren't graded but it will actually help you write the essays a lot.

Leeore is a very chill prof, lectures are fun and engaging, its just that you have to participate a lot. As for the progression essays if you read the rubric and go to office hours he will give you helpful feedbacks. Sometimes his feedback might be confusing but you just have to talk to him a lot. If you do that you will get a pretty good grade

His lectures are interesting and enjoyable sometimes. lot of class discussions where he encourages ppl to participate. His workload is a lot and time consuming so don't take him if you're looking for a easy writing class but if you dont have a choice, get your planner ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting enough, class time was enjoyable. Following his suggestions does not result in a better grade. Not an awful teacher but for sure avoid if you have other classes to focus on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Leeore was a tough grader but clear about what was needed for a good grade. He was engaging and genuinely passionate about the material. His feedback on essay drafts was incredibly helpful, and he clearly cared about his students' success.

reviews.comment: You feel like you learn something, but you actually learn nothing in the class. Writing, knowledge, and confidence are lowered after the class.

I can't tell if he is an intellectual or a pseudo-intellectual. Good guy, but not a good teacher and grader. He thinks his answers and ideas are the only right answers in his class. He will try to make everything harder than it is and confuse everyone in the class. It's better to avoid him. He will tank your GPA and work-life balance.

Also, pretty sure he's a zionist, and he makes it very apparent that no view besides his own is worth speaking on.

Professor Schnairsohn's class is easy if you pay attention, write well, and do the homework. Class discussions are also very interesting. If you want to challenge yourself and genuinely become a better writer, take him.

He lacks a diverse point of view on world problems; he decides what is right or wrong based on his views as a Caucasian man. He cannot communicate without being passive-aggressive, i.e., "These lines are so close together it hurts my eyes," which is funny because my paper was, in fact, double-spaced. Old grumpy man, do not take, seriously, don't.

TBH he doesn't know what he's doing in the lecture, he seems guiding us to think, but sometimes the conversation will go to some directions of nonsense, and he WAS NOT TRYING TO STOP at all. Bro seems daydreaming during the class. He appears to be a listener lol, but you wouldn't want to waste your time on listening others yapping, SO DID HE.

Very abstract thinker. A lot of his lectures are pretty interesting, easy to get engaged with his lessons. He was a very interesting perspective in things. Nice professor. reviews.comment: Lots of essays to write, lectures are bearable but the grading was waaaaay too unclear, says you are a good track but then gives you a bad score, very high standards for writing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly he is very disjointed. His lectures are interesting, a little obsessed with Herzog, but often entirely unrelated to assignments / the unit. His grading is unclear and very vague, he tells you that you're on the right track and he still gives you a poor grade. Very heavy workload, long busywork assignments due every Mon and Wed. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool guy but a bad lecturer. He's obsessed with Herzog and his bear movie. The workload is intense, with assignments due every three days. The comments on the essay are vague and provide little guidance for improvement.

He may be pleasant in class, but his workload is ridiculous—2–5 tough essays weekly. His grading is vague, with previously not mentioned critiques on final essays. He doesn't even read your work before conferences, wasting half the time reading and rarely finishing. If you want improvement or an easy time, avoid him at all costs!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He was way too obsessed with the Herzog bear man documentary. I would avoid going to class because I didn't want to watch any more of that documentary. He doesn't actually read over any of our homework and gives bad advice during one-on-ones. He never gives specific feedback. Harsh grader. He also wore open-toed shoes during the summer.
Good teacher. Lots of assignments, unclear grading. Very passionate, but thats a double edged sword.

but he a harsh grader and gave a lot of reading despite being aware of the demographics of the people taking his class, being people who don't care about non technical writing. Also, his topics were really weird, and he didn't know how technology worked despite being pretty young. Avoid this guy if you can if you like your GPA/sanity

Leeore truly cares about his students and will work with them if they communicate with him. He's passionate about writing and film and stuff, and he notices when you participate and put in effort. It's a writing class so there's a few writing assignments, and some feedback is whimsical. Ask him what he means and try. He'll notice and reciprocate

The teacher assigns a tremendous amount of homework. Do not take this professor if you can. By all means, attempt to take another professor because you will be stressing yourself out throughout the semester when trying to keep up with assignments. Imagine completing a three page essay in 2 days and another one that is due next week which is 5.5-7.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: interesting lessons, not so clear and harsh grading criteria, confusing and unclear feedback. if you want an A, you will have to work for it.

Good professor in the sense that he actually promotes critical thinking and thoughtful discussion, he's definitely left me with more interesting perspectives than most. but he's not-so-great in that his grading is unclear and inconsistent, and his feedback is equally vague/abstract. you rly need to meet with him a lot to understand what he wants

He gives entirely too much work and gives feedback that even when you follow, does not translate into good performance. His feedback is very abstract and hard to follow and so are his instructions. Especially if you are taking him for research based Expos, he makes it abstract to the point where it feels like overly demanding creative writing.
There're a lot of assignments, but most of them are not graded, and his grading is fair. For me, the feedbacks are not super useful for revising. The classes are somewhat interesting.

Sometimes there is a lot of homework, especially for essay drafts, but they are doable if you manage your time well. Essays are tough but he gives fair grades. He gives great feedback and his classes are enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Schnairsohn is good at lecturing and presenting, but quite harsh when it comes to grading. The grading structure is very heavily skewed towards essays (90%). Homework is not graded but mandatory (your essays will get a 0 if you miss a HW). I didn't learn anything new; he's not a bad option if you're just trying to get EXPOS credits.

Professor Schnairsohn makes you work for your grades, but he grades very fairly and works really hard with you to develop your writing and thinking. He was a great professor and as long as you listen and participate, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hes a great teacher and has a very interesting teaching style. However, his class isnt an easy A. He'll make you work for it and will let you know of his expectations during conference. Workload kinda heavy as well but his exercises do help build anticipation for the progression essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He can be relatively ambiguous when it comes to feedback, but going to talk to him about your essay and its flaws will almost guarantee a B+ or better on the rewrite. His focus on helping students find "intellectual problems" is very helpful for future essays you will write. Classes are also very entertaining.

Class either makes you understand something or leave you with questions. Every paper I've turned in so far came back as a C+. With the comments he made & going to the WC, a rewrite came back as a A-. He's very critical on grading making sure the essay meets his standards of having flow and logic. Avoid if you want a writing class that is calm.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely ambiguous. No clear grading criteria; you'll get comments and a lackluster grade but you won't know how to fix your writing. Asks questions but doesn't give answers. Doesn't give A's, makes you feel uncomfortable (very awkward) and doesn't help improve writing style. Doesn't help with writing structure at all and gives no direction.

Professor Leeore is a great EXPOS professor and he clearly outlines his course structure and what he wants from you in the class. His comments are super helpful when writing your essay and his lectures show that he is truly interested in what he is teaching. That being said, you need to do that work in this class to get an A, but it's worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Writing the Essay in 2015 and feel like Leeore scrambled up my writing style with the abstract structures he wanted us to use so badly that my writing became worse in this class and took years to finally correct. Maybe if he was better able to teach these structures, my experience would've been better, but I got nothing out of this class

reviews.comment: Very unorganized. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Tough grader, but really learnt a lot and in end, it was worth it.
He is friendly and his lectures are interesting and engaging. However he expects a great deal of work and grades very harshly

I really hated him when I handed in my very first paper because he said everything was wrong about it, but after multiple conferences with him, he really helped me expand my ideas and take them in the right direction. GO TO ALL HIS INDIVIDUAL CONFERENCES!!! He's super helpful one on one and will go through every detail in your essay to help you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Tries to make you write and think outside the box, so if you write in a contrived structure and you aren't interested in breaking out of it, avoid. If you want to expand your thinking, take him. Some say he's a tough grader, but I got an A+ on my first essay, so if listen to his comments and put in some effort, you def have a chance of doing well
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Seems like an open minded teacher but there was so much writing in my opinion. Everything I wrote, he'd tell me I was wrong. In this class, opinions can be wrong. On my 8 pg essays he would stop at pg 3 (thesis location) and tell me I'm wrong. Each time I rewrote it and he told me it was wrong again and left me with little to no guidance.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: The best professor I've ever had in my life. He taught me how to write with an unlimited mind

I had him a while back, but I have to say that he's helped me grow insanely as a writer and his class was one of the best experiences for developing analytical skills. The class isn't hard if writing is your forte, it's more the way he pushes you to think. 10/10 would recommend, a truly truly valuable experience

Professor Schnairsohn has a unique method of teaching and I really enjoyed his class. He really awards creative writings because he wants you to be adventurous with your writing. During conference, tell him what you are trying to do and he is willing to help. I learned a lot from his class and would definitely take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. He's really nitpicky with grading and basically will give you bad grades just for disagreeing with you. I went to 3 different Writing Center tutors who all said my last paper for the class was amazing and that I did not need to change anything. I handed that same paper in and he gave me a C.
My writing definitely improved, but it wasn't easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Leeore is a hard grader, but he truly wants to help you develop your writing style. By the end of the course, you will feel that you received tons of helpful feedback to refine your voice as a writer. If you show your interest and dedication to his class, he will be willing to help you 100%. He's intimidating at first, but softens up.

Worst class I have ever taken; Avoid him for Writing the Essay at all cost, ESPECIALLY IF YOU'RE PREMED! To be fair, he's a cool guy and he shows interesting videos in class. But he never tells you what he wants on papers and won't accept any views that aren't his own. He also doesn't take essay rewrites, unlike EVERY OTHER WTE CLASS AT NYU -_-
Best course I've taken so far.

His class is definitely difficult, like any Writing the Essay class. But I would definitely recommend taking another professor if you can avoid him. He never tells you what he wants on papers, so you have to read his mind. He VERY RARELY gives A's and doesn't take essay rewrites. He shows cool videos, but they haven't helped my writing at all

I found past reviews of Schnairsohn to be incredibly accurate. It's an incredibly difficult class but your grade will accurately reflect the amount of time and effort you pour into these papers - definitely helped me refine my writing skills for college. If you're looking to learn - even if you may have to sacrifice your grade - take his class.

Unless you are a future Nobel-prize winning author, Writing the Essay will be a challenging regardless of which professor you get. That being said, I'm glad I got into Leeore's class. His anecdotes and lectures will eventually make sense you start the drafts, and we watch interesting films. Make sure you attend his office hours if you need help.

This class was extremely challenging and the professor always seemed to want us to read his mind for how the texts should be interpreted. I honestly have never worked this hard in a class and gotten such a low grade. I have to give it to him that occasionally we watched cool videos, but class was mostly confusing discussions that got us nowhere.

If you look for traditional class bounded by a rigid structure, don't take his class. Leeore uses very unusual, yet interesting analogies to help you understand the course materials. With Leeore, it is always about having your own voice and thoughts. He will not tell you what a text means because he's only interested in how YOU interpret a text.

I took WTE linked with Renzi's Text and Ideas, and I didn't think this class would be so difficult. It's a lot of work that requires papers full of substance and not your high school bs. It was nearly impossible to fully please him or understand what he wanted from your papers. However, I learned a lot and don't regret it. It was very rewarding!

Awesome class-- I was truly disappointed for the semester to end. Great teacher, a little hard to understand what he wants at first, and it's next to impossible to get an A in his essays, but he always starts great discussions and brought great insight, making this class I was dreading turn into one I'm sad to end.

He has very interesting writing exercises that not only help you develop your writing skills but also thinking skills. Weird analogies are funny. Interactive. Fruitful class discussions. Great use of multimedia. Gave us chocolates on the last day of class. Easy to share your ideas with and work with. Meaningful Class!
it won't let me say anything

frequently went off topic and talked about romance in his life. if you treated him as a friend you would probably enjoy the class more. but honestly i did not attend his class and just memorized the slides as he word for word said to memorize and study the slides to the point you knew the order. very straight forward and exams worth 75% of grade

This professor frequently went off-topic, spending class time ranting about personal dating experiences and political opinions instead of teaching the material. Worst class ever!!

Really funny professor and easy class. Extra credit questions seem random but are easy to answer if you watch the lectures. All readings are optional. Professor Reed comes across as standoffish, but he usually enjoys interacting with students -- he's just direct. You can debate/discuss controversial topics in weekly Ian Unchained calls.

3 exams with no drops, so you need to ace every exam to get an A in the class. Tests are easy if you memorize literally every single slide. You also don't have to show up to lecture since he records all of them. But make sure to watch them because he throws in bonus questions. Start studying 3 or 4 days before the exam and you should be golden!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love love love this class. Graded on very easy exams that come straight from the slides. Tests aren't proctored so it's easy to cheat, but his class was really interesting so I still attended lectures. Highly recommend especially if you have a otherwise heavy course load

He makes his lectures interesting and engaging. There are 4 online exams and your lowest grade is dropped. Exam questions are basically all multiple choice and the content comes directly from the lecture slides, making it easy to study for. I never found myself stressing over this class.

The class is based on three exams and one assignment, which is tough if you're not a good test taker. Professor Reed is accessible outside of class, but not accommodating at all. He seems not to care about his students, especially their well-being in the course, which is odd, considering he is a psychology professor.

LOVEDDD abnormal psych, just attend lectures and memorize the highlighted info on slides, and you'll get an A. Don't listen to these other reviews, they didn't go to class. Extra credit was easy if you ATTENDED CLASS.

Professor Reed is knowledgeable, hilarious, and an expert in the field. I wish this class were in person, but the online lectures were just as engaging. This course covers all areas of psych with a focus on clinical. Lecture is not mandatory, but I strongly suggest going because it's really interesting. 4 online exams; drop 1. Go to Ian Unchained!

Material is really interesting but the prof is not the best. The tests were based on ALL the slides. My study guides were at least 80 pages of information. The extra credit questions are irrelevant. Also as much as I hate homework, your grade is just based on the tests.

We don't get to take a look at our exam after everyone's finished but we get to request re-grade if we got valid reason, which is so confusing because how can we come up with a valid reason without looking at our exam. Also, the extra credit questions for exam 2 are for example, his routine before bed that he mentioned at some point of 8 lectures.
Need to read and memorize all PPT, too long and complicated, with lots of data and subtle points. Plz do not take this.
WORST CLASS HONESTLY. DON'T TAKE HIMMMM
WORST CLASS HONESTLY.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're a psych major, you NEED to take his elective "Sex, Evolution, and Human Behavior," full stop. Absolutely fascinating class that completely changed the way I view psych and people. It describes *why* we have certain behaviors, not simply *how* those behaviors unfold. Easy class as well with very fair exams based on lecture material only.

Reed was a good and funny professor. Attendance was only mandatory for test day. I never came to class and still got As/A-s on my exams. The QDAFI's are so easy as well. Highly recommend this class cause there are 3 exams and they are all pretty easy and it's all multiple choice. Just study the slideshows and you will be good to go!
My favorite professor during my time at NYU.

Ian's classes are always fun because of his lectures. He's knowledgeably and relatable, but the exams are simply too much. Having solely multiple choice exams based off hundreds of pages of slides for 90% of your grade with no study guide is borderline unfair. Makes things way harder than they need to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ian is an alright professor. Not the most respectful to women, not the most accurate about scientific evidence/interpretation. His lectures are engaging, but he isn't the best at facilitating discussions. When answering questions, seems like he's more concerned with proving that he knows what he's talking about than actually answering the question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ian is an excellent professor. His lectures are well-structured, and he is very funny. We were assessed via three exams (four with the lowest grade dropped), the exams were quite easy. I imagine that the negative reviews are from people who didn't bother to study, and studying for this class involves memorizing the slides. Very straightforward.

this class was not terrible at all. best advice is to just memorize everything that is highlighted in the powerpoints, if you do that you will be golden. i started making flashcards like 3-4 days before, memorized through repetition, never attended lecture and did very well in the class.

Ian is such a funny guy. Supper chill. Very knowledgeable man. His class was super interesting and engaging most of the time. Tests cover about 5 chapters each. Honestly, it's not bad, I never spent more than half a day studying for his class. If you know how to study properly then it's easier than studying every little thing in his ppts.

WORST CLASS HONESTLY. He always crammed five, 60 page slides into one 50 question exam and it was so hard to know what to study for. I was thinking psych would be so easy but this class just made me even hate the idea of becoming a psychiatrist.
Extremely funny and as long as you read his slides, you are set for the exams.

This was an in-person class for fall 2024, would not take again, make sure to take the online one. Too much people, 90 percent test (4 total pen & paper scantron test), and 10 percent recitation homework, no make up test/extra credit, no curve, def not a easy class like people said, not accessible outside of class, do not offer re-grade.

AMAZING. Class was so enjoyable since he was just so funny and makes pop culture references all the time which made his lectures even more engaging. Tests were fair, in my opinion, as they mainly focused on content covered in slides. Also brought a fart machine to our last class?? HAHA
Inflexible and rigid with poorly worded questions, I wouldn't recommend taking this Professor if you want any sort of reason when it comes to grading exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Avoid taking abnormal psych with him. Despite its reputation as an easy A, the class is far from it. His ambiguous wording leads to trick questions, and he responds condescendingly when challenged. Nearly 93.33% of the grade comes from 3 exams with no drops. An interesting subject overshadowed by poor teaching style.

Ian is a funny guy and clearly very interested in what he teaches, making for a fun class with good information. However, the grading is structured around 4 exams worth 90% of your grade which is crazy. The exams are also 100% memorization-based multiple choice questions, so it can be daunting trying remember everything.

Ian is so great, he's hilarious and so so smart.  He cares a lot about what he's teaching and its really clear that he does.  Ian Unchained is awesome and you should totally go, it's a good way to learn more and develop a connection.  Super test heavy though, I suck at memorizing, which is all the tests are.  Thats the only bad part about the class

What a guy. He's funny. And he's really smart. You can tell he knows a LOT about what he's teaching. The lectures are kinda a lot sometimes, and they can get a little long. REALLY test-heavy (3/4 tests are graded for 90% of your grade), but if you study and pay attention in class, it should be easy. Love this guy.

Professor Reed is clearly passionate about what he teaches and always finds a fun way to do it. I took this class in Fall 2023, and it was online. The class is very lecture-heavy, but attendance is not mandatory. The questions on the exams were multiple-choice and fill-in-the-blanks, and everything was taken from the lecture slides.
Best professor ever! Never went to class, didn't study, still got an A. Recommend.

Ian is a really good guy, he makes his lectures easy to understand and his lectures were fun, not super heavy material. Abnormal psych was not difficult as long as you memorized the key points he highlights from lecture slides. 3 exams and one QDAFI is your grade. Many get As because he makes it easy to pass and focuses more on you learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Take this course if you have a really good memory. The exams are in person now.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Reed is an amazing professor and is clearly very passionate about psychology. The exams were also very easy, as he would make presentations with the material we needed to study on them and share them with all of the students. I would 100% take his class again, or any class that he teaches.

This is for his Columbia Course: Highly recommend! Received an A+ and didn't attend a single lecture after the first exam. He records all lectures so I just watched them when it came time to study for exams in 2x speed. Very effective and so thankful for that since it was an 8:40. Required a lot of cramming though!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easiest class I have ever taken in my life. Interesting topics and he's a chill dude. Couldn't recommend enough.

Lectures don't require attendance. He lacks in communication and not accountable for projects/exams. One exam, worth 30% of our grade, had MC, SA, and T/F. Despite spending 75 minutes on it, he curved the total from 50 to 41 points, citing his TA's reluctance to review SA responses. This ambiguous grading is unfair, making each error more costly.

Passionate about psychology. Full of himself. Shut down almost every student question because they weren't phrased well enough for him to understand. Extremely easy exams, they were online and open note, so no need to attend the class or study. Made fun of "PC" people who wanted safe spaces because they don't work, no need to be rude imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely the easiest class I've ever taken. Attendance is not mandatory and the class is online. I didn't learn a lot but I learned a little for the tests. There are 3 exams and 1 article summary, those are the only assignments as readings are optional. The professor is kinda like a fun YouTuber. Very encouraging on student participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is funny. He uses his own slides, so no textbook is required. I took this class online and all the exams were online too;) Also, the lowest exam will not be counted toward the final grade, so it's pretty easy to get A. The recitation was useless but it was mandatory....

Professor Reed is amazing! He is funny, kind, and extremely approachable. The tests and article summary assignment are pretty straightforward...Definitely take him for Abnormal Psychology (or any class for that matter)!

This is my first time ever rating but I just had to. Professor Reed (he likes to go by Ian) is the funniest, sweetest most chillest professor at all of NYU. If you can take any of his online classes DO IT!!! Trust me. Ian is FABULOUS ABSOLUTELY FABOO!!! I cannot stress this enough TAKE HIS CLASS!! You won't regret it.
love ian hes funny, i always went to lecture and rewatched them on 2x before the exam while taking notes and i did very well

Best. Professor. Ever. 
Prof. Reed is so good at getting his material across and giving relatable examples to help the material stick. Honestly very easy class if you pay attention during lecture. Don't listen to the bad reviews, he clearly cares alot about his students. Tests are taken 95% from slides and 5% from understanding. Easy A.
Top-tier professor, he's very smart and cares deeply about his students.

I took two abnormal psychology(online) and clinical psychology(in-person). You can really learn many things from his professional experience and his explanation of the lecture. He always have recordings, so I watch them at flexible time. Tests are not hard if you review the slides. Helpful, Knowledgeable, and Professional professor. I love him!

Loved this class so much. If you are contemplating which psychology courses to take, I strongly suggest anything given by Professor Reed. He is very erudite and kind and puts his all into his classes. He is an excellent instructor and super knowledgeable, and you will benefit tremendously from his classes. Great intro into evolutionary psychology!

Reed's lectures are scintillating, clever and material is laid out wonderfully. You will learn so much about the nature of psych. disorders -- info that will stay with you long after course is done. Cannot recommend enough: not only is subject matter fascinating and insightful, the prof genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed.

Ian is one of the BEST psych professors in NYU. I've taken 2 of his classes & learned so much. Lectures are clear & he highlights the important points that he will test on the exams. If you take the time to watch lectures & review material before exams, you'll do well. Sweet & genuinely cares about his students and the material. 100% recommend!

Interesting class. recordings are posted so you can always go back and view them. exams are online and open-book. Questions are specific but you have access to everything. I transcribed slides so answers were easy to find during exams. Besides the take-home (which he ended up giving the class extra points, thankfully!), it was an easy class

Lecture slides and recordings are available to students and the exams are straightforward. There were 3 exams and a short article summary. He is very accessible outside of class. Take this class if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ian is a great professor and a funny guy. His lectures were really interesting and exams were very straightforward, so you'll be fine as long as you review the class slides. He also posts recordings of his lectures in case you need them. And if you're ever confused or just want to talk, he's super accessible outside of class. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: As a non-psych major, I got out of this class what I expected. Clear grading, straightforward exam questions from the slides, and learned a wide-variety of topics. If you aren't able to memorize a lot, his exams may be difficult for you. Reed as a person is okay. Came off a bit arrogant and condescending at times, but the content is the same.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ian is one of the best professors I've ever had. Not only does he make jokes during class, but you can tell he truly cares for the students and is passionate about the class. All the exams are based on the lecture slides so during the lecture you don't have to panic if you missed something he said. The exams are a breeze if you review the slides.

I'm not even sure what my grade in this class is and depending on one take home quiz (25%) I could drop from an A. I don't understand how the take home has so much weight vs the A average I have from all my exams. This class was unnecessarily hard for the class that it is. Professor also voices his "controversial" opinions as facts. Avoid.
