reviews.comment: Deciding to take a course with Professor Reed? DO IT! An A is very attainable - all exam material comes from the lecture slides which he posts. Engaging lectures w/ thoughtful stories and details from his experience as a therapist. If you found him or this class difficult, I am offended that we go to the same university.. do some soul searching

Ian was a fair and nice guy who really only quized on what he said he would. He likes to joke and is extremely open to feedback, and is very reachable outside of class hours. Take a chance and try this course out.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ian is an interesting and chill person. He likes to share personal stories during his lectures. While his stories are interesting, I feel like he spends too much time on them. I wish he could spend more lecture time explaining the actual course material. His tests are extremely SPECIFIC and you really have to memorize A LOT of material for them.

if you're a psych major, TAKE THIS CLASS. Very genuine, caring, always available, especially via email, fair exams, engaging material. Loved the class, loved the professor. 1000000% recommend. this is coming from a  psych major whos graduating this year. no other psych class tops this one: material wise, professor wise, and exam wise. TRUST.

His lectures are so interesting, he is very honest and nonjudgemental, willing to talk with you about anything. 

The class is super straightforward, if you attend class and review the slides you're good for the exams. 

Very reasonable, open to feedback. Which is why I don't understand the hate here, if there's an issue, just communicate with him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes I've taken at NYU. He makes the subject matter so interesting and very clear. The class is lecture heavy, and you need to be good at memorization for the tests. He really cares about students and the quality of his lectures and class. Totally recommend, fantastic professor and super fun class!

I found the course/prof engaging, but wouldn't recommend for all learning styles or if you prefer more conceptual qs or essays. Something to consider: exams are MC, and we quickly go through 35-50 slides per class, so studying heavily involves memorization of quite a bit of material. Prof is willing to answer qs and posts slides/lecture recordings.

I really enjoyed taking Ian's class. He's a great professor, provides clear expectations at the very beginning of the course, and doesn't test on anything that isn't on the lecture slides. He zoom recorded each lecture and even emphasized accessibility by allowing students to attend remotely. He's hilarious, open, and honest. I highly reccomend

By far one of the best professors I have had. Professor Reed is so accessible, responds to questions/emails quickly even on weekends and is always willing to help and clarify doubts. Lectures are super fun, he is extremely funny and candid and a very good grader. I would definitely recommend taking this class!

Ian is solid in what he teaches us during his lectures through his experiences as a psychologist. As a psych major, I am glad I took Abnormal Psych. I got to learn more about the nuances of disorders, which is important to understand to accurately diagnose in the future. I am grateful for the effort he puts into this class. Thank you Ian.
For electives, I did not learn anything that makes me motivated . But now I know note taking means nothing if there are no class participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His tests simply feel like assessments of memorization. If you're good at memorizing and efficient at test taking, this course will be a breeze and an easy A. If you're more about conceptual understanding, this class will be slightly difficult to get a high grade because it is more about specific information rather than the understanding of ideas.

He is a very interesting and knowledgeable professor. The exams are not too difficult and are basically based on slides and what he has mentioned in lectures, so if you study hard and review, you will get a good grade in this class

Professor was very passionate about the topics.  Did not try to trick students at all on assignments, and made it clear what you would be tested on, making studying easier.  A lot of stuff to remember but if you study you will do fine and there aren't other assignments taking up your time.  Really interesting material too.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor always attempts to exclude his opinions when answering questions. While the course is solely exams and a final assessment, all of the course slides are readily available in brightspace and the recorded lecturs as well. Exams don't have tricky wording or misleading questions. The objectives of the course are clear and achievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor! His classes aren't too difficult as long as you put in effort. He repeats the same thing many times and answers any and all questions in class. You definitely would benefit more if you are actually in class live, though it's not required. He gives out his phone number so that students can reach out and get prompt responses.

As long as you attend class and pay attention, you'll do fine on the exams. I didn't have to memorize anything. Lectures are really entertaining and prof Reed is a refreshing departure from the echo chamber that NYU can feel like sometimes. Exams aren't too hard- again, all you have to do is attend lecture and pay attention. Would recommend!

I loved Ian but it's also true that the text questions are hyper specific. One line on the slide can be on the test and you have to be prepared for that. e.g. xx is more common in women of x profession, T/F.

Sex, evolution, and human behavior is definitely more difficult than abnormal psychology (he teaches both).
I would give him a 5 for PSYCH-51 + in general but no slides were provided for PSYCH-300 & what made it even harder was the specificity of qs/answers. Abnormal psych is doable (all mcq) but don't take evolutionary psych if u want an A.

Professor Reed is one of the best in the psychology department at NYU. Lectures are concise, easy to understand, and engaging. Exams are very lecture based and attendance is not mandatory so long as you pay extra attention to the slides.

Classes are lecture heavy but Ian's humor and personal anecdotes make it very enjoyable and memorable. There's three exams and a short paper, and there is a lot of memorizing but the exams are quite straightforward so I'd say it still is very fair and reasonable. Overall great class and highly rec!

Like this class a lot so far. Lecture is funny and materials are interesting. Exams are straightforward, although sometimes challenging for me cuz it asks specific questions with sometimes vague wording. A more generous cut-off would be more fair in terms of grading as the exams are now in person & close-book. But Prof. Ian always deserves a 5.

Ian is a good professor and his lectures are great. I have taken his other classes before and I always loved them. However, his tests are so much harder now as the questions are way too specific that you have to know not only the concepts but EVERY SINGLE WORD.

Ian is one of the most interesting professors I've met. Lectures are detailed/contain a lot but are all easily translated into the exam material. Studying involves time but he also encourages you to listen rather than take notes so just pay attention in class and you should be fine. He isn't trying to trick you - he's on your side. Highly recommend

Ian is one of the best professors at NYU. The exams are online but in person. He is extremely understanding and has let me reschedule exams due to family situations. He even highlights the material that is going to be in the test. Highly recommend!

This class is one of the most straightforward classes that I have taken this semester. All the exam content is straight out of the slides, and the professor highlights stuff that might be important for the exams. Also, the exam questions are all multiple choice.

I wasn't a huge fan of the class. I understand that everyone is entitled to their own opinions, but as a professor teaching potential clinical psychologists, I think that he taught the class a lot of his own (sometimes inappropriate) opinions as if they were objective facts. For the tests make sure you can memorize information but it's manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Ian is one of the best professors I have had at NYU. He truly gets the struggles students face. The class is made up of 3 multiple choice exams (30% each) and an article summary (10%). Every single question on his exams comes directly from his lecture slides. He even highlights the information we should know in a different color. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Reed used to be an excellent professor. However, he changed!Although his lecture is still attractive, and he is keen on interestingly explaining terms and research papers, it is way too hard to get good grades on exams. Exam questions are really tough and confusing. I felt like I was doing a word puzzle.Hope there can be a curve to boost our grades

Ian's class is EXTREMELY difficult. Grade for the entire class is based on three exams (30% each) and an article summary (10%). He asks EXTREMELY specific questions and there aren't many questions on the exam, so there's a slim margin for error. 

 Not very accessible outside of class. Class average is below a B- even with studying all night. Avoid
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ian's literally a gem at NYU; his lectures are very straightforward and his exams are exactly what's on his lecture slides. He takes out questions if everyone gets it wrong on the exam, which helps boost your grades. Each exam is non-cumulative, so this course was a breeze if you came to lectures & listened.
The tests are tooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo difficult!!!    Avoid this professor at all cost if you don't want to study 4 days stayed up late and got an B.

The exam used to be open book so it was an easy course, but for this semester it is a closed book exam. There are in total 4 exams, 3 midterms, and 1 final. Although the exam is not cumulative, but there is too much information needed to remember, which for me is too heavy for an elective course. But Professor is good and nice and cool.
The true goat! Wished he taught more courses in undergraduate.
One of the best professors I had in NYU. Well-taught class. Highly recommend.

This was my favorite class as a freshman at NYU. Prof Reed is amazing!! 
Take intro to psych with him as a psych major (it's great to take as an elective course too).
The lectures were SOOO good! We learned quite a bit but also had fun. Recitations were not hectic which was great because other classes I had were hard.
Take this class with him :)
Any class taken with Prof Reed is a great one. You won't regret it. I wish he taught all my classes. Also I hate mornings but I WILL get up at 9:30 am for this man. Lol.

As long as you review his ppt carefully and know where you can find all these concepts, you will get an A. Yet you can still learn a lot from his lecture. The best intro class ever. Broad topics that can help you find your major and interest.

Final grade consists of 4 exams (non-cumulative, open note) and recitation assignments. Since it was online, I didn't even go to class, just took the exams with minimal studying. Honestly though you should go to lecturesthe few I went to were fun because of how funny and caring he is. Insanely understanding and easygoing.

i wish his class is in-person because he gives funny, amazing, and inspirational lectures for sure. As long as you watch all of the lectures, you are good to do the exams. It's def not that hard and the materials are interesting to learn too.
Excellent professor! His exams are straight forward based on his lecture slides. Hes a really funny and caring guy and I am definitely taking another class taught by him.

Ian is the best professor I have had. He is truly passionate about psychology and loves talking about it. I had to fight to get into this class (bc the waitlist was 80+ people) but it was worth every drop of sweat. He is able to make lectures informative and also funny. He truly wants you to learn and really cares about you as a student. TAKE HIM!
I never thought psy lectures could be this interesting.

So far the course was a breeze and it was mainly due to his exam style. While it covered the topics discussed with in the lecture and his notes, it was not cumulative, meaning that the Final Exam did not include information from the beginning chapters of the textbook. He was super funny and easy to get along with. Take him!

If you take his class seriously you will get an A, but more importantly you'll actually retain what he teaches because he cares about teaching the subject instead of just academically stratifying kids. He's passionate about psychology and it shows. Great professor, great classes, and most importantly a great guy. NYU needs to pay this man more.
God. nuff said

Super cognizant about the difficulties of being a student, especially during the pandemic. Outstanding, inspirational lectures! Reed is an amazing professor that truly loves his work, and it shows. Grade is based off mostly exams, which are almost too easy as long as you pay attention to lecture (don't even need notes!).
Super engaging, creates a great learning atmosphere even online. super knowledgeable and a great guy.

Teaches interesting material that's applicable to real life and always makes lecture fun. 4 straight forward exams make up 80% of your grade. No midterm or final, but you're required to do 7 hours of research participation (which basically entails doing some surveys, small tasks, etc.) Overall, a fun easy A as long as you pay attention in class
He's really an amazing guy and teacher. He's caring, considerate, and super funny. He understands what college students go through. Take him asap

He's an absolute gem. He really wants you to learn and be able to apply what you learn in class to your everyday life. He's totally hilarious. He doesn't believe in cumulative tests, so it makes exams a lot less stressful. Everything you will ever need is provided in the lectures, you will never be led astray or tricked.
He's the best, wish I showed up to more lectures. Funny guy and I would definitely take another class of his in the future.
Excellent Prof in NYU!! The topics are really interesting and related to your everyday life. He said everyone should take it because it is going to help your life and I totally agree with it.
Great professor! He's kind, funny, has good music taste, and is obsessed with How I Met Your Mother. Lots of lectures, tests are very straightforward and easy.
Best professor at NYU
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: It's really apparent how aware he is of what it's like being a college-student. There's no surprises, he tries to be as clear about what is required as possible. You only have to study the lecture slides to succeed in the exams (there's 3 midterms and a final, all multiple choice). Good lectures. I learned a lot & the topics are interesting.
Professor Reed is intelligent and caring. If you try hard, you will do well. You will also learn a lot. I highly recommend this class.

Professor Reed is very passionate about what he does and really has his students' best interests at heart. He's really just a solid guy who loves what he does and that reflects itself through interesting/memorable lectures. The course is fair, lectures are fun with pop culture references, and he's just a caring, funny, quirky guy. Highly recommend.
Took for evolutionary psychology, and he was great at explaining the material and structuring the class with understanding. Greatly appreciated him.

Does a good job of explaining the course material  which is already interesting but can get dense at times. His tests get progressively harder after the first one but they are pretty fair. Just show up to lectures and review the slides/notes beforehand and you'll be fine.

just take anyone else honestly, cause her grading is so tough... did all the work and she still managed to give me bad scores

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Tariq as my lab instructor because of Rate My Prof, I should've listened to the sub-5 ratings. One of the best, if not the absolute best, in the chemistry department.
She was very helpful in recitation and always can explain tough concepts.  At first, she might seem scary but after that she is very sweet and funny.

Had Tariq for recitation, she likes when you come with questions and wants you to describe your question IN THE CLEAREST way possible. However, she is very helpful and lot of gaps in my understanding were filled in.

Had her for lab and taking her again next sem. Super nice and helpful, and is a fair grader for notebooks and labs. She helps a lot during lab as she is very knowledgeable about chemistry, and she is available during lectures on Zoom if you need to ask questions. Heavily recommend
best everrrrr
If you try you will do well
She is very nice when you get to know her. She's very knowledgeable and won't mind if you ask many questions. Gives good feedback and helps before recitation quizzes.

Dr tarik is easily one of my favorite NYU professors ever! she is amazing and always willing to help. One thing i admire is her ability to answer every question, no matter how dumb it may seem because she truly wants you to do well. Take Dr. Tarik if you can! I highly recommend her :))

Dr. Tariq is a very knowledgeable professor for any General Chemistry or Organic Chemistry. I had her for Gen. Chem. II Laboratory, and the only thing was that she is on the harsher side of notebook grading. For post-labs she is hard, but since the labs are completed in the lab, she will give great guidance on how to answer the questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took this professor for 2 semesters for lab and she is the kindest person I know. She does grade strictly but this will help the students improve and learn better. She gives good feedback on how to improve and will go out of her way to explain concepts to students when they don't understand them.

Dr. Tariq is very nice. She is super helpful and kind and is willing to answer any of your questions. She is a bit of a tough grader in lab, but she does it to make sure you understand your information.

She may seem scary, but she isn't at all!!! I love Dr. Tariq so much, she is tremendously helpful in recitation and in lab. I had her for gen chem 1 and 2 and she is also a very caring person. Don't let these reviews scare you off, she really is great once you get to know her.

She is awesome. If you put in the effort she will guide you to a better grade. Take her if you ever find an opening in her class. Her sections are gone within seconds. I am still on the waitlist for gen chem ii with probably 20 people ahead of me

reviews.comment: Love her. Was able to joke around with her like she was a friend. She's a tough grader but makes sure you understand and learn the material. Take her if you want to learn SOMETHING from genchem! Not for an easy A.

If you're someone who needs specific explanations for concepts, I think you'll love her. She's valid and funny if you get to know her, very helpful too

don't understand the hate against her - if you put in effort she appreciates it!! Tariq explained things really well, and matches your energy. if you gave nothing you got nothing tbh. she's always open to questions and explains things very well tbh. PUT IN EFFORT AND SHE WILL TOO. reviews.comment:
Really tough grader. You and your friend could have the same EXACT answers and she'll take off an extra 10 points because you didn't word it the way she wants it. (true story)
Not helpful during labs and is not accessible. Yes, she is very smart, but I think she sometimes forgets we are still fresh out of high school.

She was not my lab instructor but helped me so much. She took the time to answer all of my many questions and explained each one sincerely whereas my own instructor only said right or wrong and never bothered to explain. Regretted not being in her section. I hope I can get into her section for orgo next semester.

not really accessible outside of class
doesn't understand grading structure well&disappears to find answers mid-class when you ask certain questions
expects a lot from YOU-know things from lecture/to be on top of stuff, but doesn't deliver herself-disorganized deadlines, lastminute/late emails, doesn't seem to want to teach, only answers when asked

Mehrin is Meh

This course was very helpful for me. The readings and reflection assignments helped me better understand myself and my goals, and I feel more confident going through the recruiting process. I also found the networking tips really useful and practical. Be prepared for weekly written assignments.

Mirza is one of the best professors I've ever had. This course taught me how to improving my resume, portfolio, building confidence and connections. I've already started using these skills in real life. She guided me when I felt lost and helped me find new directions. She is patient, understanding, and always encouraging. Highly recommend!

This is one of the most important classes in my undergraduate. Two years later, I am still revisiting Professor Touseef's materials and sometimes I invite others to do some of these exercises I've once experienced. You have to put in work to receive a good score, but nothing too harsh since the class is about personal development. Take it with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This course has been instrumental in the growth of my overall confidence professionally. I have learned how to better communicate my ideas in and outside of the workplace, without doubting myself. Touseef helps students to narrow their focus on what they personally value and want to improve upon, tailoring her feedback to individual needs.

A lot of homework and reading, but highly useful and directly related to the midterm and final. Learn from lectures on how to be professional in the real world. What I'm most grateful for is the positive, supportive, and friendly atmosphere she works hard to build in class, which has helped me grow and gain the confidence to express myself.

Her class was super insightful and her lessons still help me a lot with networking and job hunting. I found the job interview exercises, salary negotiation exercises, and cover letter/resume workshops to be super helpful to me. I would totally recommend this class to anyone struggling with navigating the job search process.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class does have a fair bit of reading, but it is very easy. The homework seems like a lot at first, but all of the questions are on the midterm/final, so if you take them seriously, then the exams are free. The most important thing I got out of this class was becoming more confident in myself. Made my worries about career prep go away.

Gives great insight into how the professional world works and in which ways to navigate conversations surrounding a more creative career. Very homework heavy but manageable. Great feedback overall and you can tell she's truly looking out for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, but some interesting guest speakers. The negotiation class and how to do outreach was helpful in giving some ideas on how to do this effectively.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Touseef's class was engaging and I highly recommend her class for those having to take Professional Practices for Creatives. Participation and interacting with your classmates matter for the class but they're not all that difficult. Her lectures were insightful and practical, like her lesson on how to negotiate your salary and benefits
do not take this class

gives way too much homework that doesn't seem necessary. has no knowledge of the recent design / creative industry where I would not apply any of her feedback to my design portfolio. doesn't really seem to care deeply for her students and only talks about herself and her achievements. also no laptops during a 3 hr lecture class.

One of my favorite professors at NYU. He very obviously knows so much about what he's teaching and is super enthusiastic. The lectures were mostly discussing the readings and the historical context as well as answering student questions. Super nice guy too.

Took Greek/Roman Mythology, fantastic class, learned so much
- Lectures are dense but interesting, note-taking is critical (lecture slides are just pictures)
- Graded mostly on 2 tests and mini writing sessions that he mostly warns you about
- Read as much as you can
- Really funny guy, lots of stories, fun class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had by a mile (in my senior year). Super entertaining lecturer, you can tell he lives for this stuff and he's obviously deeply educated on it. You cover literature, history, geography, topics of gender relations, war, and trauma, plus he provides free tickets to plays that help you learn the material through performance.
overall, entertaining class. prof makes the class very engaging. he tells you everything you need to know about the tests. can clearly tell he is passionate about his subject.

Took his greek & roman myth class. AMAZING lecturer with so many stories and experiences to share. Will tell you exactly what to study for the exam. I'm pretty sure the TAs were grading everything, but the exams were not hard. You only really need to read the classical texts to succeed in the class. DONT SKIP LECTURE

I've enjoyed Classics&Social Justice! He requires that everyone asks two questions every class, but I think he realized that there are simply too many students and not enough time for that. Ask a few questions and you'll be fine. Only thing is he is very vague about the final requirements. We're a week out and I have no idea what the assignment is.

I really like Prof Meineck. His stories are great, the lectures are full of good information, and he really knows his stuff. Which is why it's a bummer I have to write this. I had a death in the family during finals week and asked for a SHORT extension on my final. Meineck asked for proof (obituary, funeral notice, etc.) Was slightly traumatizing.

Prof. Meineck was a really great and entertaining lecturer. The class was graded on one research paper, a midterm exam, and a final exam. Weekly readings but they weren't a lot of work and all you really needed to do was pay attention to what he was saying. Extremely smart and informed prof. that I felt lucky to get a chance to learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: An excellent lecturer. Knows so much about his field, and wants you to know it too. Will throw so much information at you. Has high expectations for papers, of which he assigns few and on which he gives little guidance, so start working early!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get ready to be rocker, because Peter Meineck is here with a bloodlust. People were literally crying in the midterm. He then proceeded to write an email torching the entire class for doing poorly when... he provides literally no preparation for exams. Even if you really like Greek mythology... it's more than likely really not worth it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am unsure why so many said Professor Meineck did not care about the pandemic! During lecture, he always encouraged us to take care of ourselves (recognizing the pandemic). When you participate, he takes your words and gives great insight. His lectures were hilarious. Try to get Dr. Kim Adams as your TA! She is very helpful and constructive.

He's not a great prof. Doesn't teach how to write papers and is all about greek tragedies to the point where it's boring. This is Expressive Cultures: Performance and we only did tragedies, not music, dance, film, etc. Only reason I didn't give 1/5 is because Kim Adams (TA) is the best and really helped my essays. If you need to take him, have her!

Professor Meineck is so far my favorite professor in the Classics department. He is so enthusiastic with his materials. He offered tons of opportunities to improve your grade, extra credits by going to a zoom theatre, and he reads your paper drafts and gives really helpful suggestions quickly. The readings are all basic if you are classics major.
Not considerate about the pandemic or disabilities at all
he assigns way too much work for a core class. reading and writing assignments are kinda ridiculous sometimes. wasn't understanding of the pandemic at all

reviews.comment: Amazing insights each lecture. Even if you knew a thing or two about myth, he just allows you to think of myth in new ways. Do the reading for yourself, it will plant fresh ideas each time. Amazing lectures. Amazing prof.
It seems to me that this class would be better if Meineck made us finish the books we read instead of spending so much of the class focusing on staging mythology.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He is my favorite professor I've had so far! The tests are based on the plethora of reading you have to do but you don't want to miss his entertaining lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Took Classical Mythology with him. Amazing lecturer. Makes a big lecture class feel very small. Really cares about the subject and knows a lot about it. A good amount of reading, but interesting reading. Difficult tests though.

The class is a lot of reading, so make sure you are interested in the topic. Meineck's lectures are great and teach you a lot about Classical civilizations and their culture. There are two tough tests and a research paper.

Professor Meineck is HILARIOUS. I hated missing any of his lectures because I loved his stories so much, he's had such an interesting life and it was the best lecture I had that semester because I got to hear from him. He makes the subject so interesting, and the accent is a plus. Such a great class, just pay attention and you're fine with tests.

Meineck basically is a Greek Hero, in the best possible way (friend calls him "Pallas Meineck"). Tells stories that may not seem relevant at first, but are. Doesn't retread the reading in class, so make sure you do that on your own time. Always brings a new insight, even if you already know the story. Tough, but very fair with grades

He tells good stories in lecture, and the tests aren't graded too harshly. But he went way off the syllabus - a difference bigger than just 1 or 2 classes, so couldn't keep track of what to read for when.

I highly recommend going to lectures.  They're not very informative, but the main reason I liked this class is because of the awesome stories he tells in class.  Tests were really difficult, lots of reading (but it's only plays and short stories), and one 10-15 pg research paper.
Simply put: I loved coming to lecture everyday and I was interested in the material and the readings he gave us.
Fun class! But maybe should be retitled Peter Meineck's Story Time. Nevertheless, I learned a lot because I had never read these plays before. And his stories sure are interesting!
Awesome Professor! Very knowledgeable about material, and made everything interesting and funny. His personal stories were pretty funny too. I highly recommend this class.
He likes to talk about big concepts in class that are hard to take notes on, but his exams are very straitforeword. Sparknotes were key for this class.

He is extremely knowledgeable, funny, provocative, and captivating. He's got an awesome accent. I loved him, and now i'm taking his ConWest that he's designed. Its going to be amazing: Conflict and Resistance. Get him!
eh. he's okay
One of my favorite classes of all time.  Prof. Meineck is brilliant and captivating.

he is the greatest teacher ever...i could listen to him for hours on end and he makes the classes fun and interactive. its a lot of reading but its good stuff and is like one of my best classes this semester

He is brilliant in every way..and not hard to look at for an hour.  This class was VERY hard though...and required more reading than I did in all my other classes combined that semester. Bloody ****, but knew his****.

Well, I'll confess that he's a bit of a pompous ass, but his classes (when he is able to arrive on time) were entertaining, though somewhat off-topic at times (Staging Shakespeare's Comedies should really have been "A History of All Comedy EVER," but oh well.)

Yes, he is a genius!! Everyone, take "Staging Shakespeare's Comedies"! He knows everything since he's an artistic director of a shakespeare company. And he has a sexy english accent and he's really funny, even tho he maintains a serious face. Oh and he just got married and he's wife is soooo pretty.
No Comments
man is a genius

Teaches a lot, exams are quite tough, assignments are not easy but you learn A LOT. I also appreciate how he connects what we learn to the outside world, making it seem far more relevant. He definitely cares for students and want them to excel both in and outside of hte classroom.

He is a very funny and is able to work with his students well. He grades really late though, got my semester grade a day before winter break ended. Takes a long time to grade and goes very fast with the lecture slides. Makes the midterms and finals extremely hard but curves a lot (like a lot!). Homework take forever to complete and be graded.
He'll really try to make sure that, even if you're behind, you can catch up and not lose too many points.
He's kind and kinda a cutie. His assignments are not cute though, but he is super helpful during office hours

Spent a lot of time on his class ngl, but the prof was very kind and helpful in answering questions, and was very flexible a particular case where I needed an extension because of various personal issues. Definitely treats students like human beings, which I really appreciate; something that some of my others profs don't do sadly.

Assignments are definitely difficult, but you learn a lot. I quite enjoyed the lectures, he really tries to make them interesting. I also think he's a very generous grader when it comes to the final grades; I was expecting to get a B in the class and ended up with an A-.

Overall, if you put in the work, your grade will turn out alright in the end.

Mihir is an amazing professor! He uses cartoon characters to make the class more fun. Assignments may seem tough at first, but those questions are practical and can be applied to different life situations, which is really useful and beneficial for future study. Mihir's class is inspiring and he always shows how interesting Computer Science can be.
He wasn't the best at teaching and his exams were difficult. the assignments took forever to grade and the final exam was very difficult.
The class was okay. Assignments were a bit difficult. Classes were funny. Takes a long time to grade assignments.

Genius in Python, but be prepared for tough assignments that push your limits. Unconventional teaching style may not be for everyone, but fosters growth. Supportive and dedicated, brings Python to life with creativity. Hard work pays off with invaluable knowledge gained.

Mihir is a brilliant professor, and has very creative lecture and assignment style. There were a few lectures where he explained for loops by singing songs in class which were particularly memorable. I'd say that his assignments are quite difficult and time-consuming, but I feel like I have a much stronger grasp of Python because of them.

Mihir is undoubtedly an expert in his field, however the assignments and exams he gives are notoriously difficult. This is supposed to be a beginner class yet the assignments he gives are ridiculously complicated that even the class tutors complained. Avoid if you can!

Mihir knows his stuff, but the assignments he gives are horrendous. He thinks that the beginner in Python should be able to do much more than what they are capable of. He gives barely enough time for the longer ones and his exams are terrible but the assignments will kill you. If you can avoid then avoid.

Definitely one of the most stressful classes ever taken. Homework was hard but not worth a whole lot grade wise. He will lie to you about only giving you a small curve but the curve is massive trust me. I got away with doing minimal pre-lecture work and pay close attention to class and hw. Love the prof tho gives good lectures.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A great professor for a tough course. It's a lot of work, but he ensures to keep lecture information valuable, and it is all relevant to what you will be tested on. Hard, but fair.
He gave a bad curve for final grades and he doesn't teach well. He just shows a problem and the answer, barely reviewing the steps that lead you to the answer.

DON'T take him as your Discrete prof. Nice person, but man, he goes way too fast in lectures. Very hard to keep up with; not the most helpful when trying to understand which specific areas I should practice for the exams. If you're a math nerd, you'll love him. If you're taking him just for credit, good luck... don't take him, ruined my semester!
I am not able to get 4.0 even in the first year of college....I am cooked. X_X
Bad Midterms, His slides are not great and doesn't teach that well overall, I personally just self studied the whole thing

He often uses videos from Selin Kalaycioglu. Just take her if possible. Prof Leingang is for the ones who love math. 

Only nice things were that he is very supportive of trans folk and I had kind TAs who gave a lot of credit on FRQs.

His reviews sum it up: most will struggle, only few will soar. LOTS of hw. Can't stress this enough. LOTS of hw, but they help you learn. Not very helpful in explaining concepts. Not like other math profs (beware). Records/posts all lectures. Can join on Zoom. Attendance not necessary. Difficult exams compared to other profs. Friendly enough dude.

Poor at explaining topics and his slides can be hard to follow. I learned a lot more about this course by myself rather than his slides that he speeds through. There is a good amount of homework but it's spread out somewhat to where you can manage it. I would say the course isn't even that bad, but personally I had to teach it all to myself.

if you are bad at math AVOID 100% !!! super hard. while he is a nice guy himself, lectures make no sense and he DOES NOT CURB even tho the average is always 60%. only good thing is he has a bunch of assignments so like if u pass fail it u can get away with DOOK scores on midterms and final. never take this class if u r not good at math tho horrible

You get pre-quiz, post-quiz, in-class poll for EVERY single lecture! Also, he has homework sheet every week (also counts for grade). Totally 2 midterms and 1 final, which is graded HARSH, the mean is about 60% and this man only curved slightly. The content is way over scope (lots of niche theorem), I would never take him again.
good professor, pretty kind and caring about his students. tests are surprisingly difficult, averages are very low. doesnt seem like we're quite prepared for what's on the exams in class.

He's an amazing person and lecturer. Everything is so organized in lecture. A lot of work tho, you have quizzes before and after lectures. However, they are super helpful. Lecture is proof heavy, and a lot of definitional questions on exams, and some of them are tricky. Amazing professor! Take him if you love math!
he's a good person, but needs to slow down in lectures
The exams average are all about 60, and he gives almost no curve. Run!
F this mf he ruin my whole semester

reviews.comment: For the people who say Calc 3 is easier than Calc 2, it is not. I personally would not recommend the YT videos he has in brightspace. Instead, learn a bit about the general topic on your own, then look at the textbook. Sometimes, trying the WA can also help. Put a genuine question into the pre lecture survey. Finish assignments a day before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: He's great at teaching and very nice. He actually answers questions on the discussion boards & he gives pre-class surveys where you can ask more questions. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class hit me like a truck, but professor Leingang was great. He's very passionate about math and energetic in class. There is a lot of homework to help with practice as well as weekly quizzes that I tried my best to prepare for and didn't do very well. He does have a lot of office hours which can be helpful if you have a specific question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Very passionate lecturer, but forgets that students are not going to pick up a concept as quickly as he thinks. Pure attendance not graded, if you want participation points you have to actively participate in class and go to office hours. A lot of work outside of class, exams are exactly like practice/homework. Very responsive outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Has a MASSIVE ego. Very unapproachable and does not offer help on HW. Weekly quizzes that and other bs in the class that feels like "busy-work" rather than actual learning. 5% participation grade is graded subjectively...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Leingang is the best professor at Discrete Math I've seen! You can attend the morning class via Zoom and he'll still count your attendance. The lecture typically starts with a funny poll, and the contents are interesting and easy to follow. The course is well organized. Take him for Discrete!
The course is not extremely difficult, but he assigns a lot of pointless tasks that makes it very painful.

Tends to lecture beyond what is necessary to understand Calc 3 which can be confusing but exams are reasonable. Spends time getting to know each student and will notice the effort you put into the class.  Slideshows and brightspace page can be overwhelming but are useful if you don't take notes. Posts everything after or a bit before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is fine person, he's lectures are fine and interesting. I think most of the time he covered much more than the text book, but sometimes there are also ocassions that he didn't cover the textbook. That's a little bit tricky. Also he suppose you to spend a lot of time on this course. I think he is a teacher between ok and good.

This guy is a dry but fine lecturer, but has an enormous ego about his teaching and his courses. He expects people to commit an insane amount of time to the course. Assigns so much work—all small, but annoying and not helpful—due daily, even on Sat. Can't ever seem to get a break from this class even though in reality it's easy stuff. Strict tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment:
I don't know why this guy is getting paid.

Do better Mat.

Decent instructor, lectures were pretty clear and easy to follow. Only issue is if you don't understand on the first explanation, he wont break it down but just expect you to understand it. Quizzes before each class are kind of annoying but its not too bad. Weekly quizzes every other class as well.

his lectures are just whats on the textbook. he assigns a quiz before each class GOING THROUGH THE MATERIAL FOR THAT CLASS, and the entire course is literally just read the textbook chapter -> do the quiz -> go into class and learn what you just read. at the very least he simulcasts lectures on zoom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
One of the worst subjects to learn in my life!
And the worst teacher I have had so far.
Spending more time figuring out how to get rid of him instead of how to study for this course.
The class is literally a bomb.
I really wanted to like this professor. But I end up feeling stupid in his class instead.

Meticulously organized. Always posts some enrichment material after lecture on Brightspace. Goes above and beyond the textbook at times, although lectures mostly regurgitate said book. Unfortunately has a tendency to neglect struggling students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: he is good person, but his slides are useless
Definitely take his class

Slides are useless and his way of explaining Calc 3 makes this subject 10 times harder. Lots of workload and homework is hard and useless. Relied on youtube to understand this subject otherwise I would definitely fail this class. Exams are extremely hard so be prepard. Generous curve though.

He explains everything very well and clearly, and he is very responsive and caring. But he is a tough grader. 4 quizzes per week, strict grading criteria of polished proof, and seldom give full participation grade.

2 post quizzes and 1 written hw per week is a lot but it actually helped me a lot to understand the material way better. The lecture would not make sense if you dont put time into the textbook readings and exercises. The class itself is fun but is indeed challenging since it is so different than calc or any other math classes ive taken before.

No doubt that calc 3 itself is really hard.. Prof. Leingang actually tried to make the dull material more fun and more engaging in class. Weekly written homework + weekly in-class quizzes + 2 midterms and 1 final. Not hard if you are interested in math. DO go to his office hours; he replies email very fast (within a day normally)

Tough grader, Too many slides, Online quiz before and after each class, Very fast homework deadlines (quiz due second day after each class), Very heavy exams: multiple choice, check all that apply, true/false with justifications, and free response and they are very challenging. Be prepared to put in intense amount of work if you take him.

organized class but a lot of work. lectures are boring and grades really strictly. he doesn't really answer questions and just gives u a shrug when u ask. definitely more organized than some of the other discrete profs so wouldn't be a bad option for a required class but be prepared to put in a lot of work. accessible outisde of class
His lectures are inspirational, diving deep, and also very hard. His course involves a lot of professional mathematical knowledge and lets you have a profound understanding of every aspect.

I found his course more frustrating than educational, and I think there's much room for improvement in teaching methods to make the material more accessible and the assessments fairer. The assessment methods were tough, with frequent quizzes and a strict grading curve which shows off his math talents instead of helping students learn effectively.

This semester has been extremely tough due to the way the course was taught. While he is knowledgeable in math, the teaching style didn't work for me. The lectures were complex and felt like polished long essays, which made it hard to understand new concepts. It often felt easier to learn from the textbook than to follow the lectures.

His lectures are organized and he keeps all the materials organized but the lecture is copied straight from the textbook without elaborating. He also does not answer questions and rarely provides useful feedback. If you love math take him, otherwise avoid.

he seems like a nice person but he just cant teach. He reads off the slides and repeats everything out of the textbook. The polished proofs are graded very heavy and the midterms are very hard. The homework is very time-consuming because we have to code them on latex and he assigns 4 quizzes per week. I'd avoid him tbh.

Very accessible if you have any questions but is not super lenient. Grades the polished proofs are very hard but the weekly homework papers and the post quizzes are decently easy. Midterms are a bit tricky and the questions are hard the understand in the writing section and the MC section is a bit hard. Other than that, not bad.
He is a nice person, but a tough grader. His grading criteria is stricter than that of any other sections. If you want to challenge yourself, then take his class. Otherwise, avoid.

Second semester having him, this time for Discrete Math. Very heavy exams - multiple choice, multi select, true/false with justifications, and free response questions. Very tired of them. There are online quizzes before and after each class. If you take him, be sure to get ready to work for this or Calculus III.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tough grader
I get all A except for this class. If you want to get a good grade, avoid this professor at all costs. Four quizzes per week, an extremely tough grader, and a lot of homework.

Not the worst, not the best. There was a lot to take in for Calculus III. The course itself was also difficult. Midterms were heavy as it had all sorts of questions. Also makes us do pre-quizzes; they were annoying but only requires us to ask a question to earn full credit. Overall mid professor, but a nice person.

He was cool. Super funny if you like dry humor. The content of the class we quite heavy but he explains everything fairly well. Not a bad choice for a Discrete Math Prof. One con was the pre-quizzes due before class, but luckily they force you to learn and they're graded by completeness. Had a lot of office hours and was very responsive by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not the worst professor out there. He's pretty fair about grading. Class is pretty dry as it's just a regurgitation of the textbook, so you can get by the whole class yourself with the assigned readings. He is very organized so there won't be a problem with that, but if you aren't on top of your schedule, it'll be a hard time for you.
The hardest I have ever worked for a C. Never have I done so much homework for one class. Upwards of 5 hours every day. Avoid if you are able.

He truly cares for his students, and provides fair exams. He explains concepts clearly and in a manner that's easy to understand. He gifts you with a strong foundation in Calc and in Maths in general. He will challenge you, and patiently explain to you until you understand. He, inspired me to pursue Maths. Don't hesitate to take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Harsh grader but caring and wants you to succeed. If you attend his office hours regularly you will be fine.

Truly wants to get to know you as a student. Helpful during office hours throughout the week. Lots of time is required/effort to do well in the class if you aren't naturally good in math, but he sees your efforts. Super rewarding because you'll learn a lot. Exams are created super fair if you keep up with material from slides/past exams he posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Super caring and friendly. The friendliest professor you will find at NYU.
Only tests on whats taught. Very accessible and passionate guy. I love him
You will do well on his class if you figure out the content in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: Avoid at all costs. Extremely condescending and doesn't listen to student feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is a good professor and nice person, but he is a really tough and strict grader. The rubric is not clear at all, I got points taken off for not assigning pages when turning in works on gradescope, not simplifying fractions, or didn't put fractions into decimals. Also assigns heavy readings that make going to lectures pointless. 4 quiz per week.

A lot clearer in lectures than previous math instructors. He has a good vibe and tries to get to know his students. I took a medical leave and he was very understanding and flexible with me as I got back on track. Course material is challenging but he explains it in a way that makes it as easy as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lots of assignments, lots of reading, some jokes. Passionate about math and educating. Repeats the entire textbook reading in lecture plus worksheet problems here and there. Personally, one of the classes that drained me the most.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's super nice & chill and I had him over zoom. Just look at his slide and understand the material, most test material is from slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Leingang gives different kinds of assignments to help improve all kinds of learning skills. Discrete math is definitely difficult, but these assignments help a lot. They improved my ability to write proofs and learn from textbook to a huge extent. Attendence is not mandatory, but you will do much better if you really come to class.

Bad studying habits aside, this class is definitely manageable. MATHUA120 can be dry since it's mostly getting familiar with mathematical language, but prof Leingang made it interesting where possible. He's really tolerant and understanding, so I can imagine enjoying his class a lot more for another math class (like calc). I would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Leingang is best suited for individuals who are truly interested in math. That being said if you are looking for an easy math class where you rinse and repeat formulas, this is not the class for you. I think many of the bad reviews are biased by the difficulty of discrete math, not Professor. No one is just immediately great at proofs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Could you imagine a 10%-weighted group project damaged my overall letter score from A to B+? My points lose here are the same as those lost at the other 90%... Overall, he's not an unacceptable guy, but be careful that you'll face a bunch of tiny homework that only counts 3% and DIFFICULT midterm 3. Kind of a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Leingang was a nice lecturer. Those who participated all thoroughly understood concepts. He has a lot of small assignments (more so to check understanding) and is really good about helping students and applying concepts. Honestly, I have no clue why some of these other ratings are so harsh to him.

Pretty good professor. Good at helping to understand the material, is accessible, and kind. The workload can be sometimes heavy but is def manageable if you manage your time correctly. Test are hard but fair. Weekly quizzes are not as hard. There are also some easy A assignments he gives that allow you to boost your grade too.

Prof. Leingang reminds me of a grade school teacher. He marked attendance, graded participation, had student do Do Now questions at the beginning of lecture, and remembered every student's names. He manages to make the complex concepts of Honors Calc III digestible. However, midterms and weekly quizzes were rather difficult.

He's an okay teacher. He's bad at explaining things so I used Youtube and the textbook to learn. Lectures were just a repeat of the book. Even when I asked for help I usually left more confused :( . But you can tell he cared because he always gave help. HWs are due every fri and quizzes every mon (so time-consuming). Exams were pretty hard.

Class reminded me of my hs classes tbh. Encourages group participation and has mandatory attendance. As for the guy himself, he has a pretty dry personality and seems to try to apply what he learned in psych 102 to his interactions with his students. Also felt the need to mention that he drove an electric car.

This professor gives very clear explanations to even the most complicated concepts. His classes are very organized, strictly following the syllabus. Grading is a bit strict but definitely fair. Homework are carefully selected, very entertaining to work with. Definitely don't regret taking his course.

Like his class in general. He is a kind and easy-going teacher. You may also learn a lot about math if you take his class frequently. Homework is not too much. The only frustrating thing is that Latex is a mandatory requirement, which costs lots of time.

Leingang is a great teacher, and if you're some one who likes math, you'll find the class quite fun. (Discrete Math). Weekly quizzes are straight from the assigned textbook problems,HWs will usually be from the book but must be coded on latex (time consuming). Exams are easy! I've heard that he' s really tough on his hon calc 3 class though.

I had Prof. Leingang for Discrete Mathematics and he was not the best at teaching. He went incredibly fast and expected you to know the complex material after a 30-minute talk about it. His lectures are entirely based on the textbook so going to class is the same as just reading the book, negating the entire purpose.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took honor calc3 instead of the regular calc3, which is by far one of my most irrational decisions. Leingang is a tough grader, even if you attend every lecture you still couldn't get full credit of participation. He has great passion in math especially geometry, which means he expects you to be as passionate as him to attain his standards.

Very respected and teaches great. You can tell he is passionate about math and teaching and really knows his stuff. But avoid him unless you are okay with getting a B-level grade after spending 20hr weekly on this course.

Honors Calc III is a lot more about the conceptual than the practical, so be prepared to study calculating examples on your own in the book. However, Leingang does a good job of getting weird concepts to be understandable. Hard-ish weekly quizzes and homeworks, so study up and learn LaTeX. Make sure to participate and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Leingang is a seriously underrated prof. Sure, he gives a decent amount of work and he makes you use LaTeX, but if you go to class, do his homework and pass his quizzes, you'll be in good shape. For a lot of profs this is NOT true. Not to mention he really cares. He'll go out of his way to help you and puts so much effort into teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof Leingang teaches well but taking his course isn't the best idea because he gives a lot of homework which requires writing tedious LaTeX code. There are weekly quizzes. The lectures, quizzes and homework are entirely based on the book. But he experiments with his exams and gives challenging questions. He does curve his exams which is helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really tricky, I only suggest to those who are able to give up on everything else in their semester. HW qs are very interesting, but you budget most of your week to be working on them, quizzes are every other class. Exams are definitely tricky, but he curves them up quite a bit. If you want a real challenge, take this class, otherwise don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is smart definitely. However what he taught in class is exactly the same in the textbook. Gives lots of homework and requires us to use Latex. Although I love coding, the homework process is tedious and time-wasting as you actually can complete it way faster if written homework allowed. Midterm is standard, but every weeks' quiz is annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Easy class if you've already taken at least Calculus AB. Hard class if you haven't. Lectures are half-baked and studying the webassign questions is your best chance at doing well on quizzes and exams.

He was such a fun teacher. He had a lot of fun with the subject he taught. Even though he would let out the occasional corny joke, I still laughed. He's the epitome of a dad. He was very helpful with feedback and made sure you really understood it. He was very accommodating with office hours. Had him for Calc I and II. Would recommend
Lectures were always very well planned and structures - his notes were abundantly clear and were always followed by practice worksheets and in class exercises. Homework was challenging but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: I admit that he is a very smart guy, buy he regards himself a genius. Sometimes His hand writing can be illegible, and  he talks  too fast. Homework and midterms are tough. Don't recommend to take his class if you are not interest in calculus.
Very clear in his explanations but gives ridiculously tough test questions.

Great professor, but he gives extremely challenging exams and homework. Somewhat of a tough grader. He speaks really fast and assumes previous knowledge in Calculus, so if you don't have a strong interest or foundation in Calc, you will probably have a hard time.

Leingang is definitely one of the smartest and most friendly professors I have had so far. Lectures are crystal-clear, and office hours are helpful. However, his major downfall is assigning ultra-difficult problems on both the written assignments and midterms. I would only recommend him if you're really into math or wanna tackle difficult problems.

He went to univ of Chicago and Haravard so he knows he math and knows how to make diffcult problems. Test and quiz averages are often below 70%. Weekend webassign proofs are difficult and take hours. Calc 2 is not a required course for premeds. I recommend taking a more useful math class or an easier calc professor so you can balance your classes.

Quizzes every week, but he drops the lowest 2. The homework is ridiculously hard, but he grades pretty leniently and drops the lowest grade. Grading isn't too bad. Just pay attention and take good notes.
In class: this is how you integrate. Exam: find the total perimeter of an infinite ever-growing fractal in series form. What even.

The class structure is awesome. You learn the lesson through clear examples and then do a worksheet about what you learned/harder examples. Quizzes and exams are really straightforward. The only draw back is he does written homework through web assign so you have to scan in your work to your computer.

Flexible, committed, and knowledgeable. Requires participation - which is kind of difficult for a calc 3 lecture. If you are there to learn and work hard you'll do fine, he is very understanding and helpful.

By far the best professor I have had in all of my years at NYU. He is extremely intelligent, approachable, and caring. He wants all of his students to succeed and understand the material. He does an excellent job of explaining the concepts and getting the class involved through worksheets. You will leave this class being amazed with him knowledge.

I do not know how he got his PHD from Harvard. He is not good math at all!! He can only cover what text book says, but cannot explain anything complicated. Even though he is nice and approachable, he is not a genius in math. No wonder he does not do any research now, simply teaching calculus....

His teaching techniques makes sure you learned the material before you leave class. After he teaches a section, he hands out worksheet to do then he calls on someone to do it on the board and goes over the answer. He is excellent, funny, and answers all questions.
take him if you really like math and really GOOD at math!

Professor Leingang is one of the best calc professors ever.  He's clear in his lectures and uses worksheets to get students involved.  He's dorky and quirky in an adorable way.  His tests/quizzes aren't unfair or extremely difficult.  I learned a lot from him.  Highly recommend!  Do whatever you can to get in his class. :)
Best. Professor. Ever.  --> Take him for the upper level Calculus Classes and you will not regret it.  You get the grade you deserve and he does everything he can to help you learn.

He's a smart guy, but his downfall is that he teaches straight from the powerpoint, so if you don't kno how he got from step 1 to step 2, you'll be pretty much lost as to how he got to that answer. My class did horribly on the final, therefore the curve was pretty generous, although he doesnt curve all the time..Prior AP Calc is a must to get an A

Intelligent and clear in lecture. Class, however, is HARD. Especially calc2. Very concept heavy. Seems more geared towards math majors than anyone else. Webassign (online hw) was torture. So was written hw. Had to do proofs for hw in calc2! I say avoid, there are prob easier profs out there

Leingang is an interesting character. He is nice he does the "this is my favorite calc class joke" in every calculus class. He does the tree strech when ppl are falling asleep in his class. He is a very nice profesor . But calculus itself has concepts that are hard to grasp or easely undertand so you will need to do use the txtbook alot
Take him if you're really good at calc. And I mean REALLY.

I recommend him if you have taken AP Calc in highschool. Otherwise, he is really conceptual and you'll have to teach yourself most of the stuff. He uses webassign for homework (in addition to written hw) and that's basically death. If you know calc, you don't have to go to class. Not the best, but at least you can understand him.
nice and funny guy. expalins things well

If I had never taken AP Calc in high school I probably would have done terribly in the class. The professor is a nice guy but he moves through topics quickly and spends too much time on proofs which confuses everyone. If you've taken calc before, this class will be a breeze. In my opinion, all quizzes and the midterm/final were easy.

He's brilliant and funny. Reminds me of Ted Mosby from How I Met Your Mother. He is the head of Calc Prog, so he writes the finals. But both the final and midterm is hard especially the conceptual word probs. He cares about his students.Very helpful and approachable. He would respond to e-mails. There'll be quizzes. But again, brilliant,choose him.

He really knows his stuff. Powerpoints are very clear. Spends too much time on origins of proofs and deriving them. All we want to know is how to get the right answers! The Web-Assign is extremely time-consuming but you can't avoid it. HW is graded strictly and the quizzes are short and a little tricky. Just a midterm and final. Best CalcI can get.
His lectures are very interesting and he is very hot;)easy A without worries
His class is interesting. It's not hard to understand and the quizzes are easy.
I have had friends telling me that they hate him. I dont, but the class is not easy. Word of advice, take Harvey instead. His midterm is so much easier than this prof's.

I liked his powerpoints - saves a lot of time and easy to review later for exams. hated Webassign - hwks are very time-consuming and not necessarily reflective of exams. He's no Jaime Escalante, but the man is very passionate about teaching calculus. Go see him during office hours and get to know him.

Matt spends too much time on concepts, and not enough time doing problems! His tests are hard, but with a LOT of work you can get an A. The TA's are really helpful, though. He teaches everything on a powerpoint; i personally hate that. On the bright side, he speaks english and makes the final for all sections. Good Luck!

Funny guy, approachable, wants to get to know his students. I personally wasn't too big a fan of his teaching style, since it involved too much theory and PowerPoints. But if this is your second go-around at Calc 1, I'd highly suggest him, because he does give you a deeper understanding of the material as promised.

Leingang is truly an amazing professor. If you have to take calc, make SURE you get into his class! he made calc lecture somewhat interesting, and has great powerpoints that he posts that you can study off of later.also, he's super funny!

Leingang is an amazing professor. In a class of 200 students, he actually takes the time to try and get to know everyone personally. He tries to make the subject material interesting and sometimes he incorporates his daughter which is adorable. He assigns 1 homework per week and he has a midterm and a final. He's awesome! Don't hesitate to take him

Seriously I found him to spend wayyy to much time dealing with concepts that were irrelevant. He is so much harder than the other professors and his midterm is by far harder than other professors. Plus you can't argue with him because he is head of the department. He is a smart and nice guy though

Leingang is the deputy departmental head for undergrad math. He writes the final for all classes, so if you take him, you'll be used to him for the final where others won't. His teaching is very fluid, but he spends far too much class time covering theory for its own sake without demonstrating how to apply it to exam-style questions.

He'll make you hate calculus. You can tell he's very intelligent and knows what he is talking about, but he makes concepts too complex and wastes time deriving proofs you'll never need to know again instead of doing examples. Overall, fairly decent teacher. Quizzes are easy. Online homework each week is tedious, but thats all calc 1 classes.

I really enjoyed taking Calc I with Leingang. Though I didn't get a very good grade, that was not his fault by any means. Makes lectures really interesting: interjects math-history and even pop-culture trivia in them while not losing sight of teaching important concepts. Really friendly and approachable. Highly recommended!

Makes the final for all classes, but his midterm is the hardest, as well as the quizes. Hw is the same for all calc classes so there is no way to avoid that. If you're good at calc and understand the material he presents you should get at least a B+.

He is a really smart teacher who knows what he's talking about.  he's very into theories of math which can be very boring!!!  if you are a hard-core math person, then take him.  one good thing about him is that he makes the midterm and the final for all calc classes.

Professor Mayya is someone who seems to mean well, but is not good at teaching a class. He tends to go on weird tangents and be very hyperspecific in what he tests on out of the mass of content he teaches. Wouldn't recommend.

honestly, mayya might be one of the worst professors ive ever had. bro's lectures were a pain to sit through with how he'd drone on and on and the tests were about rote memorization rather than learning. would never recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved Mayya. Very chill, kind professor that cares and wants you to genuinely learn! I learned a lot of cool fun facts about how computers work and would definitely take his class again!
great guy. teaches very well and honestly is very clear. wants you to succeed

great prof, you can tell he genuinely cares about his students. youre allowed to miss up to 6 classes before it starts to affect your grade. during lectures he makes everything super easy to understand. i never had any prior knowledge of sql but now i learned it! if you just show up to class and pay attention, then easy A
Amazing professor--very kind and genuinely passionate about what he does, a feeling that permeates the room. He is a great guy and cares for his students.

Prof Mayya has been one of the best and most caring professors I have ever met. He cares about students and is willing to elaborate on knowledge points and grading criteria. I enjoy taking Info tech with him. I am not a super "technical person" but have no problem learning SQL or other areas. Highly recommend. You won't regret it.

I highly recommend Professor Mayya's section of TECH UB 1! He is incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the material and explains challenging concepts clearly. The course content, SQL, Network Effects, etc., are also pretty useful. Grading is fair, and he is super accessible during office hours and genuinely wants students to exceed!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is extremely content heavy with SQL in the mix. Final Exam/Quizzes are really tough theoretically. While the content is extremely sound and super useful for a good foundation, the exams/quizzes did throw me off for a loop. Not only do you need to mug up but also understand the logical explanation. However, Prof Mayya is super kind!

Professor Mayya is a great professor who is clearly very passionate about what he teaches. His lectures are very clear and if you listen during class it should not be a difficult class. He is very accessible outside of class for office hours and willing to work with students and listen to new ideas.

Prof Mayya is a rly nice guy and is super passionate about the content & teaching. The SQL is so helpful and I've held onto it for my resume and even in job interviews. His infotech class is pretty applicable and interdisciplinary so it connects with other Stern courses too. He makes everything clear/fair and efficient, which I appreciated.

Prof. Mayya is great! His lectures were clear and engaging, and I learned a lot from the class. It's structured so that no assignment or test is weighted too heavily. He's also easily reachable outside of class, which is super helpful for some of the new concepts, and he's a very nice guy in general!

Great professor, and definitely recommend taking Professor Mayya! He was super accessible outside of class and gave great feedback to succeed in his class. He always does his best to address any concerns you have, and is supportive all around! Just make sure you are keeping up with content and follow up if you need help in any areas.

reviews.comment: Professor Mayya was one of the best professors I had at NYU. Very unhelpful and pains me to this day that I paid tuition for this class that barely ever met because he would replace classes with optional office hours. He does not care about your learning.

Took him for business simulation. Very tough grader. quarter of the class dropped out or opted for pass or fail after he announced that the course will be "curved" only top thirty percent can get an A or A-. Don't think anyone got an A in the class.

He was ok, I didn't love the class but it didn't negatively impact my life. The lectures aren't interesting but the information is easily accessible. reviews.comment: Professor Narayanan is a great choice for Intro to Marketing. His lectures were pretty involved, with many case discussions and opportunities to participate. This class was very interesting, and the professor did a good job facilitating discussion about cases and topics. Some of the lectures were a little dry, but overall a good experience. Workload is light, most of your grade is 1 exam so make sure you do well on it (50%) and make sure you also do well on the case write-up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sometimes I wonder if he curved my ISP grade wrong. He docks points for not including things in your papers that he made sound optional before. He is a tough grader. I scored higher than the class on everything except the exam and ended up with a B+.

Professor is a nice man but the instructions for each assignment are not clear at all. An extremely tough grader and class lectures don't help with assignments. He expects way more than he lets on, don't take class unless you want to hurt your GPA lol.

Class was not what I expected. Class material was not helpful in writing the major papers for the class. Tough grader and expects a lot.

reviews.comment: What a G. Very sweet. Quite engaging on the subject matter, though his lectures could stand to be more linear. HW is very easy: very interesting, one reading a week or less. Only 2 papers: both require significant effort and critical thinking. IMO, the difficulty of the exam + midterm is MORE than compensated by the light volume of work.
Sunder is the best! Had a great semester. Learned a lot (he explains so clearly) and enjoyed myself. Assignments were not too hard and he gave us all an extension for the strategy report.

He's a caring, funny professor. Highly recommend him for EMI, he made the content easy to understand. He is very straightforward about the grading, only problem is that only 30% of the class can get an A and everyone else gets in the B range but that might just be Stern rules.
