The homeworks can sometimes take a lot of time, but the grading criteria is very clear and if you read the instructions carefully, you can do very well. The exams are very fair and lectures are very clear
He's generally a nice guy but his tests are just so hard. He did give some extra credits opportunities.

Well versed in his field; however, there were 4 programming assignments every week and not too many tutoring opportunities. Average on both midterms was around the C range, while the max was an A, if that gives you an idea of the difficulty. This class actually made me realize I don't want to do computer science, haha.

Professor Versoza is the reason I pursued a CS career as a non-major. His lectures were super clear & entertaining. He was always there to offer assistance. He was patient and truly wanted to see you succeed. He offered plenty of opportunities for extra credit. His assignments were sometimes a bit challenging, but never felt pointless.

He gives a lot of homework each week that feels never-ending. He is very nice but his lectures can be redundant. The exams were difficult and he does not curve more than 1-2points depending on the class avg unlike some of the other professors.

VERY practical content for AIT. Long weekly HW but again very practical and helps nail concepts/theory. Plenty of deadline extensions & extra cred. Lectures move fast and demos imo aren't super engaging. Can study on your own and do fine. Tests nuances and specific stuff on exams. Final project is an awesome chance to add someth to your portfolio.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: One of the better professors at CAS that knows his stuff, and is very dedicated to teaching students. His lectures were very informative and interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 100/100. Prof. Versoza is amazing. He is probably one of the most dedicated instructors of NYU. The course was difficult (tonnes of hws) but it helped me learn technologies which are widely used in the industry. If you're a CS major, don't graduate without taking this course.
AIT is hands down one of the most useful classes I have taken. Joe is lit! He really cares about his students and knows the material so well.

(AIT) It's not an easy A. He's not very friendly in office hours; best time to talk to him is right after class while he's still pretending to be nice. He gives so much hw without any breaks, even while we were working on the final proj he gave us hw. Assignments and exams were not easy. Time consuming class so do not take with other hard classes.
AIT was actually pretty okay with homework, and imho it's very doable. Comes off as a bit pretentious tho.

AIT - With a homework every week, it is a dependable heavy workload, but it is so worth it. It was one of my favorite classes I've taken - you learn a ton of useful material. The reason he gives you assignments every week is so that you actually understand the material he is teaching, and the grading is fair. Take the class if you have time for it.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: SO much work!! 12 pages of hw due every week is unreasonable, especially if you are taking any other CS class. Look at an old syllabus! He is a tough grader and his lectures are not interesting. He gives you coding demos and expects you to follow, even if it is a new topic. No hands on coding in class, except for the last two classes.

Versoza's class is the best experience I've had in the CS dept; it's built around tight feedback loops, from the fair but non-triv hw to the lectures (most of the teaching is done through live demos); he can effctvly take the temp of the class and backtrack organically when necc; the class seems designed to teach everyone w/out patronizing anyone.
Versoza is cool and a good lecturer but gives a lot of homework and the midterm was hard. Although final was easier. Take the class if you want to learn JavaScript. If you want an easy A don't do it.
Loved the prof, amazing teacher. Could explain python to a toddler

Took his undergrad data management, and after midterm, he said he's giving average B-, which made me so worried, so I'm writing this review for future students taking this course. His lectures and notes are clear, and there will be tons of materials if you're not a web minor or not on this track. You'll learn, but you need a big and strong heart.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: AIT is a very very hands-on and intense elective, especially if you've never learned Javascript (and HTML/CSS). Hard to follow lectures, so be prepared to learn everything on your own outside of class. Slides are directly related to the hw though, which form the foundation for the exams. Very useful class though.

He actually knows what he's doing and will teach actually useful full-stack skills. Be prepared for a lot of homework, but for the most part, they're manageable and the tutors he's hired are super friendly and accessible. Lectures can feel rushed because he's trying to squeeze in a lot of material in a semester.

Joe was always super clear during class and super fun! He really cares about his students and makes an effort to make homework/projects fun. For Python, don't bother buying the textbook! Do the online modules and homework.

Happily dumping endless hours of weekly homework, offering pathetic quantities of extra credit, expecting perfection on a test that the TA's don't understand, and refusing to curve the class grade, Professor Versoza is lightyears from encouraging students to pursue programming professionally. Joe needs to reconsider his curriculum and beyond.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He quickly learns students names which eliminates intimidation in a class of unfamiliar people. Complaint: his exams do not show accurate representations of a student's skills. Programming heavily relies on continual test runs which a hand written test doesn't allow for. Sometimes, in attempt to let you figure it out, he fails to properly assist.

I had Versoza for Python and Intro to Comp Sci, and he's the reason I'm a CS major. He's extremely clear in his lectures, provides very good resources, and his assignments were always lengthy and tough, which is incredibly helpful. He emphasizes the importance of working hands-on with code, which reinforces the material incredibly well. Great prof.
He is clearly smart, but is not a good teacher. His method of teaching is reliant on giving you an enormous amount of teeth grinding work. Also he talks way too fast.

Joe is an amazing professor, especially if you're just starting out with Python! Lectures are extremely clear and fun and homework assignments are also not hard. It's a shame he doesn't teach Intro to Comp Sci or I would definitely have taken his class!
Gives Lots of homework and focuses on too many details at exam. He has some sort of weird smartness that he would like to show off.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lots of homework and difficult tests
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. Gives a decent amount of homework, but it's very effective at helping you learn the material. Clear lectures and slides, always available and willing to help, and grades very fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Somehow feel the professor overpraised in rmp. Really good for learning but really give assignment more frequently than other professors, and somehow repeating. Understand that practice makes perfect but feel a little bit unnecessary, as least from my point of view. But still I see he is a good instructor.

Didn't open the textbook once. Uses students in higher levels of CS as graders and tutors. They hardly give you the help you want when you go for tutoring or ask questions in class. Two days a week: one class for lecture, one class for in-class assignment (where we worked on HW). HW due every week.

Hands down the best professor ever. I came in this class thinking I'll take it for a semester, but Joe made programming so interesting I'm considering majoring in it. He's really approachable, funny, and cares about his students. His exams are fair and he's an easy grader but homework might be a bit overwhelming. Please take him if you can!

Best Computer Science professor I've had. He really makes the material engaging in a way I haven't had with any other professor. I wasn't sure if CS was the right major for me at the time but his class definitely helped me affirm it. Easy to reach and helpful in every regard to the curriculum.

Professor Versoza was a great teacher who was very organized. He made Python very clear, and provided numerous resources  to improve our knowledge of the language. It's important to look over his review powerpoints because some test questions are fairly tricky. I will definitely take him again for CS101.

prof. versoza is everything a professor should be. his lectures and ppts are very clear, his homework questions are challenging and comprehensive, and he prepares you very well for his exams. (and he's a very generous grader). he doesn't take attendance but i recommend you go to every class because you get a lot out of them.
Love this guy. Will be looking forward to taking him again. I definitely recommend him. He makes everything pretty straightforward and clear.
Clear, pretty engaging lectures, everything posted online, lots of assignmentssome EC can smooth over some rough exam scores. Definitely recommended.
Tried emailing him 3 different times and he didn't answer any of them.
Very good teacher, teaches clearly, gives fun assignments, and likes to use cute cat examples! He is helpful, easy-going and you will learn a lot from his class.
Joe is awesome! Super clear, helpful and a great guy. Wish he taught all my compsci classes.

Joe's lectures are extremely clear and fun. If you go to class, the assignments are a breeze. He makes it very clear what he expects you to know for exams, and he doesn't try to trick you with his exam questions. Easily one of the best professors I've had at NYU.
Joe Versoza is easily the best professor I've ever had. He's clear, concise, organized, and funny. He goes above and beyond to ensure his students know the material and are prepared for exams.

Joe Versoza is an awesome teacher. He is super organized and I can not recommend him enough! The home work is moderately difficult, but if you ever ask him for help you won't have any trouble. Also, he prepares you really well for his midterms.
Many pop-quizzes. Really hard.
This professor really likes to use pop-quizzes to force students show up, and he'll still go ahead with the quiz no matter how many students are actually there

Prof Waldinger is ok. His lectures are clear enough and he gives you good notes. That being said, his exams are really hard - the class average for the two midterms was around a 55. But the class is graded on a curve, so if you beat 20-30% of the class, you get an A no matter what actual numerical grade you get.

The class itself is super hard. The professor tries to make it simple by outlining everything but the second half of the course is impossible to understand. You cannot attempt the HW problems without help and the exams are harder than the HWs.

Pros:
1. Organized lecture notes
2. Fair exams that look like HW
3. Super clear lecture and office hour sessions

Cons:
1. Competitive curve 
2. Some derivations on lecture notes skipped many steps, might take some time for you to figure out step by step
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: yes, he's difficult and harsh. but honestly, he's harsh bc he cares. he humbles you to prepare you for life (beyond operating systems). the ppl that complain about him are ppl that just want an easy A. if you put genuine effort and time into it, you'll be fine and you'll learn a lot. he's a great lecturer and is very charismatic
If you already know all the material you'll still do poorly. He won't teach you anything, and won't grade you justly on what you do know. Makes everything so hard and enjoys putting people down.
Bad teacher, makes things very very difficult to understand

This class is already difficult by nature and he seems to try and make it harder for students to understand. Lectures are generally informative but the amount of work he assigned outside of class was ridiculous and made it impossible to have time for any other classwork.
If you're confident in your skills, you definitely shouldn't miss his class. The labs are tough and he grades strictly, but he's the best lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
By far the best lecturer I've had at NYU. Walfish is big on understanding the material and not just knowing it, and it shows. If you read and understand the textbook before each class, you will get the most out of the lectures.

And if you really put in the time, you won't find the exams that bad. There's also a huge class curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i learnt a lot from this class. if you want to become an expert in OS, take him.

This one is a tough grade, because on one hand he is a great lecturer, is very funny, and is very accessible to receive help from, but on the other hand his grading style feels far too stringent, with the average of the first midterm often falling below 50 or 40.

Only take him if you are serious specifically about becoming a systems programmer.

Amazing professor who's very knowledgeable in this field and uniquely able to explain hard topics clearly. That said, only take this class if you're passionate about CS and not in any other hard courses. Exams are weighted heaviest by a lot. If you start labs early, go to office hours, and study religiously for exams, this class is very worth it!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He actually made me realize how not very intelligent I am! Good luck!

Don't take it if you already have tough courses. 
This course will probably take up all of your time and energy. However, if you do exactly as he says (do his readings, homework, and labs diligently), you will have a great time. 
It took me a while to figure out why he does things the way he does, but it makes a lot of sense now.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: RUN! Take anyone but don't him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely poor at teaching. His notes didn't go into details at all and besides the notes, all materials on operating system he provided is the textbook, which was long, vague, boring and not helpful. And he even said that some of what textbooks said was wrong. So why didn't he prepare his own materials? He didn't want to help students at all.

Michael is so far the professor with the best lecture skills I've ever met. His lectures are impressive, humorous, and inspiring, and he is a very knowledgeable and friendly person. But yes, CS202 is itself an extremely difficult topic, and he does provide tough labs and exams. So if you want scores, avoid him; if you want to learn, pick him!

Yes, CS202 is a hard class. The mean of exams are usually 50/100, and requires ACTUALLY understanding the content to excel.

However, if you are willing to put yourself through the (possible) pain of using your brain, and put effort into the labs, you are going to get the BEST lecture you r ever going to get at NYU, and a solid OS understanding.
I don't know, if you can't teach a class without assigning ridiculously long readings multiple times throughout the week, maybe you shouldn't be teaching certain topics/classes!

Hardest class I've taken at NYU. The tests were incredibly difficult and he expects you to have a deep understanding of every single concept.

He's incredibly smart and a good professor (though probably overqualified), but sometimes overcomplicates things to flaunt that he's smart.

Prayers to anyone who has to do lab4 in the future

The best professor I have ever encountered, extremely knowledgeable, classes are fun; although at times challenging. But OS is supposed to be this way. The exams were butchering, but curving can help at times. You end up learning a lot during the course, and if you are enthusiastic about learning, this might be the best class you end up taking!
Very difficult topics and lectures, insane workload

OS is just a hard course, it's the first required NYU class that forces you to write non-trivial amounts of code. But I found Walfish to be a very good professor, great lectures and you learn a lot of useful cli tools while working on the labs.
You learn a lot.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He will answer all your questions and is EXTREMELY knowledgable. You won't get by blindly memorizing stuff for the tests (which is what I liked). You have to develop a deep intuition by doing the labs and such. If you like hands on programming and solving problems you'll enjoy doing the labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Extremely difficult course, but just as rewarding when you finish it.

He covers a lot of content way too quickly so just rewind through his zoom recordings.

Exams are insane but if you study hard for the final and do the labs properly you will do well; the averages are very low.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely difficult and overrated in terms of how good of a lecturer he is. Yes there's a lot of reading; labs are extremely difficult and so are tests, which btw the final is worth 45% of the final grade. The class is not as incredibly meaningful as people would lead you to believe. But there might not be a better option, sadly. Prepare to suffer.

Super messy slides, a lot of things you ask him will receive the reply "its policy". Really hard class with extremely hard labs and really hard exams as well. Really egoistic imo, still treating his lecture class like a high school class. Slides and explanation is all over the place. Overall bad experience and horrible mistake taking his class.

DO NOT TAKE. Assigns an unfathomable amount of reading before every class, if u don't u won't understand anything in lectures. Labs require far more time/effort than one can possibly devote. Exams ridiculously tough, worth majority of the grade. odd policies on student collaboration. By far the most stressful college course one could possibly take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Recommended only if you're genuinely interested in learning about operating systems. The labs can be challenging, but they hold significant value and provide thorough instructions. Words can't describe the incredible satisfaction when you use your own "ls" program (lab2) to examine a disk controlled by a disk driver (lab5) that you've written.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: STAY AWAY. Walfish's lectures are extremely unclear, as he expects students to understand deep technical concepts without clearly explaining anything. Moreover, his notes are so messy and unuseful. He is a major red flag on how he treats his students and he is extremely rude in his communication. His hw/labs are very challenging and stress inducing

Bro got the messiest lecture slides I've ever seen. He does explain stuff thoroughly but there is so much jargon that figuring out what you actually need to know to succeed is pretty unclear. He's also a stickler for integrity which is fine but he takes it too far to the point where its just annoying.

Best CS Professor in Courant, responsible, and really cared if we truly learn something. He is so well-organized and everyone could learn so much from his lectures. Though his exams are difficult, do not worry. He curves a lot.
Very nice professor
Easy A.
He is an enthusiastic lecturer who teaches REAL stuff. Start early on the labs and use the office hours, and you will be fine.

One of the best professors in CS dept! Yeah, his class is hard. He really taught me the difference between knowing sth and understanding sth. Exams are tough, but there will be a huge curve (my frind got an 50 out of 100 in the final and still got an A). 

BTW, Walfish himself is bussy, but his 4 TAs are amazing and are always available for help!

Professor Walfish is awesome but get ready for a tough class. Some say dry, I say fascinating. Its assigned to use the textbook but I never opened it to be honest (lost a couple points but nothing too bad). 

Labs are intense and SERIOUSLY START EARLY. Space out working on it as when you get stuck you can utilize Campuswire and come back to it.

His cs202 is definitely not an easy class, but you have to really know and internalize those stuff as a computer science major student. If you are a minor or just want to code without knowing what is happening under the hood at the same time get a straight A in CS, avoid. If you want some challenges and are eager about CS, then his course is for u.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best CS class have taken at NYU

Professor Walfish's advantage is that he taught us a lot of knowledge and equipped us with prerequisites of being a real computer scientist. His disadvantage is that the course is too challenging. If you want to puruse computer science in the future, his course is a good option. Suggestion: Pay attention to class notes he wrote.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Instead of answering your question cordially, he would find ways to put you down in the name of the policy and integrity. Just a very rude and condescending person in the name of justice. He also enjoys assigning hard homeworks, and prohibit communication between students. Terrible and stressful learning experience overall.

His lectures felt like the user manual of some ancient OS--super detailed yet painfully boring and heavy on memorization. He likely had no real world experience, and his antagonistic, antisocial nature deprived his class of any humor or analogy. He practiced grade deflation because he wants "the best student" to stand out at other people's expense.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The most painful class I have ever had over my entire life, but the pain is totally worth it. I felt like a learned A LOT in this class, not limited to OS, but also the courage of facing seemingly unsolvable questions. Btw even though the material is hard, Prof. Walfish is super logical and well-prepared.

Easily the most difficult CS course I have taken at NYU. I don't regret taking OS with Mike though, I'm confident that this class will set me up well for any systems-related course I take in the future as well as interviews. Do note that this class might be a big hit on your GPA if you are not typically a top 10% of the class student.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would not recommend Walfish unless you have BOTH a perfect GPA and are extremely interested in OS. He does not care about general ideas as much as getting every small detail PRECISELY correct, which makes the exam, assignment and lecture difficult. Throughout the semester, he also threatens harsh punitive measures over petty things. Not friendly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took Operating Systems. Material will be hard to keep up with (whether due to difficulty, quantity, or lack of interest) for a lot of students; I found myself doing a lot more backtracking than I do for other classes. Exams were difficult. That said, Mike is strict but well-spoken and caring about his students, and you'll definitely learn.

Not as hard as everyone makes him out to be, but you need to do the work (as you should anyways). He runs a tight ship in class which keeps everything moving forward, course and info/schedule organized very well, you always know exactly what you have to do and he delivers information very efficiently. Take him if you want to learn.

"Days never finish. Master got me working. Someday master set me free." The lyric of Eric Cartman's slave song best describes this class. He is a good person, and his hyper-organized and prepared. But it averages to about 20 hours of study per week outside of class. If you are not really interested in backend Computer Systems ideas, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a fan of his lecturing style. It's much more worthwhile to go through the assigned readings than to rely solely on his in-class musings, which unfortunately oscillate between too general for what you need to know and too specific for the edge-case, niche (useless) material. The class proves useless when actually attempting the labs.

Most intensive class I've taken at NYU. He knows a lot + doesn't mind correcting himself. He was a bit too much for me sometimes, class had lots of readings and very complex (time-consuming!) assignments. Exams can include general-knowledge stuff he might have just mentioned in class. Great class nevertheless, you learn even if you don't want to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had been straight-A until taking this course. Mike covers much more topics (such as computer security) than other professors. Needs to read a lot of PDFs before each lecture. Exams are very difficult - you need to remember every detail, including those not covered in lectures but only appeared in the corner of your textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tough grader--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Worst class I've taken at NYU. Extremely tough grader. Doesn't give partial credit on labs (that are very difficult & time consuming) & exams are difficult. Lectures are very fast paced & hard to take notes on. Was not accommodating at all during coronavirus & punished people for being in non-ideal living situations. Avoid at all costs.

No laptops: keyboard sounds are distracting. Lectures too fast for handwritten notes. Weekly HW, biweekly Labs (5 total, hardest was building my own OS), lots of readings. Exams extremely difficult. Finals worth 50%. If there are other profs to choose from, choose them. If 1 of them is Panda, dont take (they coordinate so sections are the same).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His OS class was the hardest class I've taken at NYU, but also the best. It was my lowest grade this semester, but also the one I'm most proud of. We finished the base curriculum a month early and were able to even cover distributed systems and security. Your GPA doesn't matter enough for you to miss out on this class. 100% must take.

The hardest professor you may ever have. But every minute of the metaphorical pain will be worth it, you will come out a much better programmer and a deeper understanding of systems. If you're considering graduate school, his classes are a must-take purely for the experience. You need good (excellent) fundamentals in C and x86/x86_64 assembly.
Long homeworks/labs, but very great professor. Definitely by far the best professor I have taken at NYU so far, but also by far the most work.

Walfish is very articulate and knows the material  well. He does an excellent job verbally explaining the content. Having said that, the class is incredibly difficult. The amount of homework and labs is unreal, even excessive. The exams require super detailed knowledge. Very hard class.

For the love of your life, please avoid. The only good thing about his class are his explanations. Other than that, this class is hell. The workload is super intense. I barely had time for other classes. Furthermore, he is such a tough grader.   Briefly, this class is so annoying and hard that I had to consider counseling after finishing it.

If you love your life then avoid this class. Michael Walfish is one of those professors that could not make it in the real world and therefore takes it out on innocent undergrads. He will give impossible amounts of readings and assignments without actually teaching you how to do them. The average grade on the midterms and finals were a 56.

Knows a lot about the topic and will explain in office hours, but the best way to get a decent grade is to skim the textbook before lecture. Used an old version of the textbook, pay attention in class, and it will be fine. Slow to respond to emails but easily accessible in office hours.

Incredibly difficult to understand as a lecturer. Often goes on long tangents about unnecessary material that doesn't appear on exams only to skim past important topics. Slow to respond to emails, and lectures often left me more confused than simply reading the textbook. Clearly a smart guy -- doesn't know how to teach. Exams are difficult! Beware!

Prof Winawer is a really nice and caring guy, but his lectures are just too boring. I think all the good reviews are because the class was online, it's not anymore. This class is definitely one of the harder psych courses. Not an easy A by any means. This review is not to hate on the prof as a person, but serves as a warning for future students.

Lectures deliver unhelpful material in long tangents. Gets through material slowly, not able to finish material that will be present on test, in which additional lecture videos are assigned to make up for his poor lecture delivery. Overall nice person, but very frustrating to have as a professor. Too much detail on superfluous information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The semester is not over yet, but do not take him.  Lectures are so unclear and he goes on so many tangents, he is not very responsive, lectures go over things not on the test (for half of the lecture too), tests/quizzes are impossible.  Very inteligent guy but is just not good at teaching to students, and focuses on unimportant things.

30% quiz, 20%final, 50% 3drop1 exams. He curved to meet the around 40% A standard so it really was nice of him. 1% ec added if complete pollev. He's lectures were fun, shows lots of visual/auditory examples to help us understand the concepts. But lectures itself wont get you good grades. Be ready exams are a bit hard.
Amazing professor, not a difficult class if you do the readings

(PSY53 - PSS) Prof is kind and understanding. His grading was lenient; 1/3 exams dropped, 4/12 hw assignments dropped, extra credit, & 80% credit on late hw, which went against his original rules. If you have any special circumstances, he is rlly helpful and will find a solution. Attendance isn't mandatory, & he posts all his slides and recordings.

Course: PSYCH-GA 2245 -- fMRI Lab

Overall, Prof. Winawer is a nice person and able to explain challenging topics fairly well.

However, he has a serious grading problem, in that he does not do it. Our first assignment was due in Feb; we never got feedback for anything. It is now 1 week after final grades were due and he has not submitted them.

The lectures can be boring but the class was easy. He drops your lowest exam and 3-5 quiz grades- all open book. His curve is insane (I had a 120% in my quizzes after getting 6/7 on most). Exams are based on lectures and readings (make sure you read). Allott proper time for this class, stay on-track (with COVID it's hard) & you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He curves quite heavily. 3 quizzes and 1 Exam were dropped. He is an absolute sweetheart who tried his best to make the class work through remote learning. Absolutely take him but be ready to read and pay attention in lecture cause the exams are not easy, open book though. Recitation and lecture attendance was not necessary.

Jonathan is one of the kindest, most human professors Ive had. Hes pretty chill and lectures arent so bad - sometimes the material was really complicated though. There are short weekly reading quizzes, take 3 drop 1 exam, & a final. No study guide given. He responds quickly to forum questions & emails. Perception was a good class to take online!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Best professor. I was so sad that he doesn't teach this year. His perception class was just amazing. I didn't even read the textbook and only showed up at the recitation and the lectures. And I didn't even take notes. He made things so clear that all you need to do is listen. He also replies emails in literally seconds.

Professor Winawer is a really considerate and nice guy. Lectures can get a little boring if youre not interested in the material but the class is overall not too bad. 30% of your grade comes from the quizzes in recitation which could be an easy A if you read the chapters before class. You could drop one of the 3 exams.
Professor Winawer is very smart and will make difficult material easier to comprehend. I highly recommend this course.

Winawer is such an understanding professor. He curves both the quizzes and the exams! You can drop 1 exam and 3 quizzes. Read and you will ace the easy quizzes that really help your grade. The exams question can be challenging, but he really helps you out with the curve. Work hard and you'll get at least an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Take him! I truly enjoyed his class and learned a lot. One of the most interesting psychology classes I have taken.

I really enjoyed Winawer as a professor. There were weekly quizzes for our semester, based on the textbook chapters. The textbook itself is not a difficult read, so it was feasible. Also, he helps your grade out with both the quizzes and the tests because the material definitely requires deep understanding (yet is manageable).

Really one of the most insane classes, it covers so much so be prepared to keep up on the reading and learn fast. Go to recitation so you can get credit for the easy quizzes which comes out to be 30% of your grade (really helps out). All the tests are insanely specific, he curves every test because its almost impossible to get an A on the first try
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: He's pure excellence! I would highly recommend him. He's so passionate about the subject & willing to help if you see him during office hours. He's very understanding & wants everyone to do well. Your grade is determined by 2/3 best exams & 10/11 short assignments. You also can earn up to 5 points for extra credit if you go to class. Good luck!

This professor is amazing! I can't believe not more people have rated him because he's so understanding. 3 exams (including the final) and he drops one. He records his lectures so if you missed something in class, you can always rewatch it on nyuclasses. He gives up to 3 extra credit points added to your total grade. Overall, amazing class!

Winawer is such an awesome person and if you go talk to him then he will definitely help your grade. Tests are fair but some questions can be challenging and straight from the book. Do the extra credit and listen to online lectures!
okayish-fair grader but the mandatory readings spike my cortisol. also heavy workload

The teaching style relies heavily on having students repeatedly read aloud in class. Small mistakes result in being asked to reread the same text many times in front of everyone, which can feel discouraging and stressful rather than helpful for learning or confidence.

The classroom environment often feels hostile rather than supportive. I found the professor's feedback style to be demoralizing, which made it difficult to participate without fear of being singled out. I usually love studying Chinese, but the teaching style here made me dread class. Waking up in the morning started to feel like a nightmare.

She literally doesn't care about her students. Has a humiliation kink and is a general bully. Thankfully dropped this class before the add/drop deadline, but prayers to everyone taking her class right now.

did not hate her lectures, but did make me not want to come to class sometimes. cold calls on you sometimes but can be condescending. will not budge on late work or absences (even excused ones). hard class with lots of work, but can be easy if you try.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Syllabus is clear on grading.

Can be very condescending and sometimes just repeats students' mistakes back to them (ie incorrect tones) without providing additional help/context; made 2 people cry in class bc they asked for clarification/misunderstood assignments that were poorly explained.

Wish we were taught more vocab common in novels.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: professor did not let me go to the bathroom during a test. Even though it was an emergency. Even though she had our phones and backpacks. I had to turn my incomplete test in before sprinting to the bathroom

I see none of the other reviews have included this, so I will. Her class policy states that you automatically fail her course if you have 8 unexcused and EXCUSED absences. I saw 2 classmates beg her at the end of the course to be more understanding, one of whom has pneumonia and missed 2 weeks of class. Workload heavy, heart of ice, steer clear.

I had to return home for a week due to a sick relative. I emailed the professor beforehand but returned to find my grade had been docked by a letter. My grandmother passed away that week, and when I tried to explain, she said, "Your lack of preparation will not sway how I grade this class." An awful professor, and an even worse person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great Professor, Amazing Lectures, Learned so much from her class. Take her if you want to learn about Chinese Poetry.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: overall the class is decent because you actually improve at reading and writing in chinese. however, be warned that the workload is quite heavy as you speed through around a lesson per week. professor is funny at times, but sometimes she would put people on the spot.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: she's a very caring, funny, and cool professor, but the class is hard as shit. tbh this is not a class for "advanced beginners". better off going to chinese 1 if you actually never learned to write chinese. homework and quizzes every week actually made me braindead, not her fault all the accelerated chinese classes are like this.

There is a lot of daily homework, but Shao Laoshi's class was very informal and she clearly did want us to learn. You can only learn as much as you're willing to work for in Chinese, but Shao Laoshi made that process much smoother.
You will do well in the class if you participate and do the homework. The professor really wants everyone to do well! super recommended

As with any language, how good you get and how much you improve is almost always entirely up to you. Shao does a good job trying to facilitate that growth, but it's still largely up to you to actively learn and practice the materials provided. Classes are chill and non-formal, a truly stress-free environment.

Profisn't considerate with people with disabilities and having traditional + simplified words on the same powerpoint is confusing. But also when she goes over the homework sentences, it is too fast to write it down if youre wrong on something, especially for non-natives. Wish it could be written out for us so we can take time to digest the meaning.

Professor Shao is great, i think NYU has great chinese teachers, and she is no different. I had her for advanced chinese 2 and i think she is a great teacher, she is pretty thorough and yes there's a lot of work but thats expected for this level. She is very eccentric & vibrant & really wants everyone to do well! very funny too!

I loved this class. Though the workload was a lot a times, it definitely made learning Chinese much smoother. Prof. Shao made the class environment fun and interesting, so learning new words or phrases easier to remember. Highly recommend making quizlet sets to help study.

(Advanced Chinese II) The best Chinese teacher ever. So funny, super caring, wants you to do well. Yes there is a lot of work BUT it's not hard to do, you just have to take the time to do it. She wants you to learn. Probably the best/most effective Chinese class I've ever taken. Quizlets for the vocab on account Emma_Iridondo.

It's a pretty tough course, there's homework and something to do in class more or less every day. Attendance and participation is required, but I suppose that's to be expected of a language course. As long as you put in a bit of effort every day, you should be okay. Homework isn't terrible most the time, just time consuming.
Nice experience overall
I didn't learn anything in class. The instructor would refuse to use the definitions given in the textbook and make her own up that didn't make sense. When we asked her to clarify, she was unable to.

Classes can either be engaging or dry depending on whether we are engaging with the text or learning new vocab. The workload is fair (weekly quizzes, oral recordings, occasional written prompts). Make sure to follow. her. instructions--and you'll have a decent time in her class. She cares for your progress and wants you to do well!
Unorganized and poor control of the classroom. Gets angry at students when they pronounce a tone incorrectly (it's a language class). Very discouraging behavior.
She is a kind, caring, and funny professor who explains things well and keeps classes interesting. I enjoyed my class with her

Had her for Elementary Chinese for Advanced Beginners and I think everyone did well in her class. She gave a lot of work but she's a light grader so it wasn't really a problem. Would've taken her again for Intermediate Chinese but she was teaching at 8 am.
super easy and nice!! she's really caring and engages in conservation with you. plenty of extra credit opportunities as well.

Shao laoshi was the best! I was worried about learning Mandarin Chinese but she made learning really easy and fun. If you actually take the time to do the homework and study for quizzes, you'll get an A for sure.

SHE'S THE BEST TAKE HER. She's the funniest professor ever I spend half the lecture laughing @ her jokes. Her lectures are amazing. She explains things really well, gives plenty of examples. Graded by lots of different things so it's easy to get an A even if you do badly on a couple things. I love her so much one of the best profs I've had at NYU.

Shao Laoshi is amazing! She is super sweet and will always help you out if you're feeling lost in the class, and offers tons of resources to practice Chinese. As long as you're polite towards her, participate during class (she is very strict about phones!), and study a normal amount for her tests, you will do well.
don't want to take her again..

Confused as to why his rating is so low. Did these people get the right guy? Super inviting of in-class participation. You don't have to be a genius-- just participate. Read the required texts! You will have such a better experience in class as you'll be able to understand his witty jokes. Overall great professor. Wish I could take him again.

No idea why he has anything less than a 5. He is super warm and open to answering all questions even when they're obvious and is very reasonable with readings. Only 2 essays and 2 exams (midterm and final) and he really cares about what he is teaching so he makes it interesting and does a great job explaining the more complicated texts. Take him!

Steen is a great professor. He's obviously passionate about what he teaches and will give you an A if you put any effort into his class. You can get by reading a few of the readings as long as you focus in class. He cares about attendance and will give you an attitude if you skip. He's really awesome, understanding, and funny though. Take him!
Prof Steen is great! He is super nice and funny. Lectures are engaging and the class is very easy if you do the readings. Take him if you can!
Took him twice. Readings were easy and there were only two papers online. Really easy and good person.

Avoid him if you can. Lectures are inspirational and he does analyze the texts well. However, he is condescending, doesn't reply to emails, and lacks empathy toward students. His grading system is weird and subjective, as only certain students he likes receive good grades.

its a lot of reading like the other text and cultures classes, but they werent boring reads. theres only 2 1200 word essays, a short 2-3 minute presentation (not for a grade tho), and the midterm/final are just 2 really short essay prompts. pretty much a good teacher and class structure overall. id be down to take him again if i had to
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very understanding just don't take it for granted because he will get annoyed. Easy class just do the readings, participate, and turn your work in on time and you will get a good grade.

The content in his course is interesting, it's obvious that he makes an active attempt to engage the students. His grading scheme is fair and his feedback is very helpful. Additionally, he is very understanding and in no way uptight. All of the readings/content are accessible online and his lectures explain the text in an engaging manner.

so difficult and stuck up. he was not understanding at all, is so anal about showing up on time no matter how much you participate. he grades harshly, even if you know what you're talking about. Ignores your emails... overall the worst professor I've had.

Really didn't like him. All these reviews seem accurate. He demands 100% effort and enthusiasm for a class that is very much a requirement- meaning no one actually wants to be there, especially an 8am. Work is fine, he just makes it so so so much worse. Avoid if you can. If you can't, you'll be fine- you'll just wanna rip your hair out.

Stay away if you could. Steen is one of those professors who thinks his class is the most important, and acts that way. Work is manageable and not hard, but having to listen to him talk for 3 hours a week is cruel and unusual punishment. I got an 84 on a paper and emailed for a better grade and he delivered with an A, take that as you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: idk how this rating is so high. In the beginning his class is tolerable then just takes a turn for the worse. Material is extraordinary boring but he expects 100% attention and excitement-  unrealistic and destructive. 8AM and he was upset participation wasn't through the roof. Work isn't that hard just super boring. Good looking guy though.
major tweeeeeek. fine class. would not take again. not so hard but lost patience for our man Jonny Steen.
This class was very interactive. The readings were interesting. Professor Steen is a very understanding teacher and his essays were fun to write. Would really recommend taking this class!

To him for ACM, an easy A! Do the reading and the discussion post, and try to participate when you can. He's very understanding and gives extensions when asked. 100% recommend 2 papers, midterm and final short easy
Great professor! Learn a lot of stuff while not worrying too much about the grade

Professor Steen is the absolute best!!!!! I had him at 8am and I am not a morning person but it was still by far my favorite class! He makes everything super interesting and has great analytical skills. Not too much work, just participate and show you care about the material and it won't be hard to do well!
BEST!!
Steen is so friendly and he is funny. He cares about your performance and pays attention to your improvement.
Just show up every class, participate in his class and put efforts on the assignments that he asks you to do, it is not hard to get an A in his class.
He's truly one of the best. Take him if you can! He is encouraging and caring, and he analyzes texts really well.
He is one of the best! Definitely choose him if you are here.
He provides great feedbacks and papers for tests aren't that challenging.
Super nice guy and a great professor. Not a ton of work either, but the texts we read are mostly interesting, and he analyzes them really well. Take him!
Talks about latest and coolest stuff in ai
Knowledgeable professor
If you do all of the work you will get an A. Professor is pretty knowledgable in this subject, you will learn a lot from him.

Put "Respected" tag becuz he is sort of a figure in colit & EA departments, but he really doesn't care much about students. He yaps whatever comes to his mind for the entire 2hr45min class, no engagement with students, no dicussion of readings. If you truly want to learn something, I advise you take someone else's class like Rebecca Karl.

His lectures meander unpredictably through the global humanities, which could be very edifying, but his breadth of expertise is clearly much narrower than his breadth of focus. I only noticed this when he started talking about 16th century Dutch paintings, and spoke a few generalizations that were very incorrect. We rarely get to the topic.
Prof. Zhang is very friendly and caring, but lectures were so boring. I could never make it past 5 minutes without dozing off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are very, very dry. He does not really seem to know what he's talking about; even if you try to pay attention, you get distracted by how many times he says "um" during one lecture. There is a lot of reading; be prepared to read up to 300 pages a week, on top of your other classes. Recitation is required and sometimes much more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good lectures but can be quite boring. He also never responds to his emails, which is very frustrating.

Fascinating professor, so knowledgeable and well-versed. His teaching of literature also encompasses history, film, politics, philosophy, and more.  You will learn so much no matter what your major is!

Professor's lectures were pretty relaxed. His focus is on poetry, and we read a lot of it. In recitations the focus was on the history of China. Prof. Zhang's lectures are sometimes boring but if you pay attention, you will get something out of it.

Professor Zhang is an awesome guy! I was in a lecture of 170 so there wasn't much 1 on 1 time, but he was very clear. He has a wit that forces you to laugh or smile. His lecture is comfortable and the work is stimulating while moderately challenging.
IRRESPONSIBLE AND ARROGANT
He's a good guy, but his World Cultures China class was a bit of a mess.  Don't take it if you don't have an interest/ability in interpreting poetry.

20th Century Literature in Translation...sounds like a hard lit class, right?  Nope.  Easy film class.  It was SO great.  Zudong would just chat about films he liked, and then the whole grade was class participation and a final paper analyzing one of the films we'd talked about.  He's brilliant and yet kind and tries to challenge you (and he's hot)
My favorite prof at NYU. Very intelligent and well spoken, an expert in his field.
Very intelligent, easy to talk/relate to, challenges his students, encourages all perspectives. (Not like most intellectuals in their ivory towers...)

Brilliant professor whose courses have a lot of offer if you know what you're in for: theoretical emphasis with socio-historical leanings and a lot of revelations that make sense at the time but leave you with more or less indecipherable notes.

Zhang really screwed a whole class. Syllabus said Modern Chinese Fiction but he decided to teach Post-Mao Intellectual politics. Actually, he didn't teach at all. It was obvious he never prepared for class. He let his sychophantic grad students do presentations (none of whom can speak english clearly), and skipped 2 of our 12 classes.
He is a nice professor and really teaches us algorithms that are useful in job interviews, although they might seem hard.
Could you please teach some useful stuff for exam and homework during the lecture, rather than teaching nothing and letting it become a self-study course.

Don't believe that this class is well designed. The lecture slides and the homework assignments are very different. The slides are too simple while the homework requires way too much thinking. There is no room for failure. There isn't enough practical practice questions from the slides or recitations to be prepared for the midterm or final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If Prof Xue was teaching in New York, I would be a heroin addict. His lectures do not correlate with any of the exams or even the homework. His homework is so hard, and there is little to no practice at all. I would never recommend anyone to take his class because he is so hard.

the worst experience i've ever had taking a course. professor is very inconsistent with everything. expectations for homework and exams are completely different and aren't explained beforehand. expects ability to mathematically prove algorithms despite never teaching us how. grading was 25% hw, 30% midterm, 45% final. would never ever take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not take this professor ever again. Lectures are tedious and difficult to follow, super math heavy, doesn't really explain anything clearly. Grading is (25% HW, 30% midterm and 45% final exam) and inconsistent, partial credit is hardly given. Exams are super hard and he is not lenient, course felt like a self-study course. Would avoid!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very caring guy, but awful professor. course expectations are not clear at all, he wants different things on the hw/tests and does not tell you his expectations. i lost many points on exams and homework because of that. he does not clarify complex concepts well, and his lectures are so math heavy and abstract. do not recommend

Professor Xue have a in-depth understanding of algorithms and he explains the concepts pretty clearly. However, the course is graded only by homework and exams, which are all very challenging and graded harshly. He expects you to be well-versed in proofs and mathematical methods.
Prof. Xue has a solid background in Data Structures and Algorithms. His lecture is not that easy to follow but he is nice in office hours.

Professor Xue is very tough. One big problem is the inconsistency among his lectures, homework, quizzes and exams. His lectures are pretty tedious and hard to find key points for his quizzes and exams. It is said that he once even made ICP too hard that he was complaint by peers. Don't choose his course unless you're super confident with CS.
final accounts for 50% and grade very hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although he is patient to answer questions, he knows next to nothing about homework. Also, his lectures are too easy that there is a huge gap between the lectures and homework, you cannot count on him to work out the homework assignments. However, his TA, Sven, is super handsome and always willing to help.

Professor Xiao is an extremely knowledgeable professor who cares about her students. She is receptive to questions and office hours and is very friendly. The workload was relatively light and she grades very fairly, allowing flexible deadlines and credit back with test corrections.

I enjoyed taking professor Xiao's class, she is a fun and encouraging teacher. You do get a decent amount of hw but it is based on completion. The class itself is not easy for sure, you take 3-4 unit tests, one final on top of an end-of-the-semester project. However, she grades fairly and prepares you well. Just show up and try your best!

Professor Xiao is an excellent instructor. While the workload was heavy — especially if one is less proficient in the language than what is asked of the course — effort is rewarded accordingly thanks to her clear grading criteria. If you are willing to put in the work, you are guaranteed to do well!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Though there's lots of HW and some tests were difficult, as long as you try and put effort in this class, you will do well. Xiao Lao Shi was an amazing prof.

If you show Xiao Laoshi you want to put in the work and get better, she'll take care of you. However, since Advanced I only meets twice a week and covers a lot of ground, you have to be independent and practice outside of class. That's not a flaw with her, just the nature of the class. Extremely kind, motivating, and accomodating. Highly recommend.

She's a great professor! She takes the class seriously and expects students to as well, so be prepared to put in effort, but if you do she will work with you to make sure that you're able to succeed. She's very accessible and accommodating with student's schedules and provides plenty of opportunities to make up for missed work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: overall fine, but she was very dry and in class only read aloud her study guide with grammar structure examples (all in chinese). shame bc the one time we had a supervisor she actually taught well. also wasn't too accessible, but she was a nice grader and gave 20% back on tests so if you do the work then your grade should be fine

Hanyu Xiao is AMAZING!!! She is incredible at language teaching, never in my several years of studying Chinese has a teacher pushed me so far so quickly. There's a lot of work in the class, but she doesn't try to trick you. If you do the work you will do well in the class. Her main goal is to improve your Chinese, and she really does.

Shes amazing! really wants to see u do well, and is accessible outside of class. gives extra credit which is great. Really caring! However, she KILLS you with work, I did 4 group projs & 4 individual so its a lot. She makes u work for your grade, but if you pay attention & practice youll be fine. WIsh it was a little less work but solid choice
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: unprofessional

Xiao Laoshi is one of the smartest people I've ever met. She has a PhD in linguistics and uses it efficiently to further your knowledge of the Chinese language. She is also extremely knowledgable in Chinese/linguistic history, which is extremely helpful at this level of language learning. Lots of tests/quizzes, but she'll make sure you're prepared!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Xiao is one of the best Chinese teachers that I have ever had. She truly cares about her students and their learning. I looked forward to going to class every day. If you want to improve your Chinese while also having fun, I would highly recommend taking a class with Professor Xiao! Grading is fair.

This is my second semester taking class with Xiao laoshi and she is hands down the best Chinese professor I've had in my life. Even though the material in Advanced I and Advanced II is really tough, she explains everything very clearly so you understand how to read, write, and comprehend complex Chinese sentences easily.

Couldn't imagine a more dedicated and passionate teacher. Take this class if you really care about learning Chinese. With Xiao Laoshi, you will learn fast and she will lead you to have great tones/pronunciation, written form and understanding of grammar, providing an excellent foundation. Her high intelligence doesn't make her less approachable.

Xiao laoshi is incredibly smart, talented and understanding. She makes sure that everyone in the class is on the same page and is really committed to helping each student learning mandarin. She is simply an amazing human being both in the classroom and outside of it. I highly recommend taking her class!
She deserves more than one review! Hands down best professor I've had. Very funny and stylish, too. Her lecture is usually the highlight of my day.
Xiao laoshi is a great professor. Lectures are very clear and make heavy use of the textbook. Attend lectures and do the homework and you'll be fine.

She is genuinely one of the best professors at NYU Shanghai. She truly cares about her students and creates a safe, supportive, and non-judgmental environment. She is kind, understanding, and warm-hearted, with such positive energy. You will never regret taking her class.
She's an amazing teacher who genuinely cares about her students. She's very understanding, so don't feel the need to hesitate to talk to her. Any course you take from her, you will learn a lot.

Easily the best Chinese teacher at NYUSH! She speaks primarily in English for intro classes and uses slideshows so it's easy to keep up even if you fall behind. She was pretty strict on attendance but as long as you go you should be good. If you see her as an option in the course catalog, sign up and you won't regret it :)

Grades are determined by TFs with three essays and two take-home exams. Readings are heavy but you can skim.
Great 400-level Anthro course with her! Clear on what was expected and very kind. Material was engaging and interesting!!!

The lectures tend to be unengaging Grading is largely handled by the TA. Recitation is mandatory, with weekly write-ups and two presentations. While it's a challenging course, it serves as a valuable and rigorous option for fulfilling a liberal arts requirement
Great 400-level Anthro course with her! Clear on what was expected and very kind. Material was engaging and interesting

Professor Zhang is a gem! Her class introduced me to a field I was completely unfamiliar with and I enjoyed it. She's very knowledgeable and has a passion for what she does. Grade is completely based on your TA. 2 writing assignment and the midterm and final are take home papers. A lot of readings, but the lectures help clarify the concepts.
It's generally an easy class. Grades are determined by TFs with three essays and two take-home exams. Readings are heavy but you can skim. Tara Mitra is an extremely nice TF.

While attendance is not mandatory, Prof. Zhang's lectures are very engaging & genuinely interesting material. Your grade is entirely determined by the TF, but all of the TFs this sem. were very knowledgeable & facilitated good discussion in recitation. 1 extra credit paper opportunity & very generous extension policy (5 free late days)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Lectures are boring and you don't need to attend. Readings provide more info that you will use on 2 full papers (3-5 pages) and 2 take home exams. 1 ethnography, it's really easy. 

Basically graded by TA. Recitation is mandatory, with weekly write ups and 2 presentations. Not a sexy class but a great easy fill for liberal arts requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: lectures got a little boring at times but overall super interesting + amazing readings + we watched 3 very nice films in class! grade was based purely on essays. midterm + final was a take-home essay (48 hours for the midterm and ~5 days for the final.

Grade depends on TA but Professor Zhang is a great professor with great lectures. Her class is reading heavy but they are all engaging and interesting reads that are provided for you. Overall essays and tests are easy and lecture/info given are vehicles for success. Guidelines and grading criteria are also very clear.

Professors Zhangs class was super interesting. Shes one of the best professors Ive had at NYU. The class is reading heavy but the readings are all provided and super interesting. She gives out a lot of info in lectures. She doesnt just read of the slides and makes them really engaging. We had a take home midterm, 2 essays, and a final.

Eloquent lectures, easy to follow. good office hours Straightforward papers, only a total couple assignments for the semester. Papers are graded by TAs- recitations are chill show up and get participation. Prof Amy did asynchronous lectures this semester (fall 20) for remote learning, idk if that's subject to change in the future.
Amazing professor. Adapted to mid semester remote learning change extremely well. Thoroughly enjoyed her class. assignments, communicate with TA/participate, and youll be fine!

Prof. Zhang does a great job with organizing and explaining her main topics and themes in class, but not in the presentations, so you have to go to class to get all the information. As long as you pay attention to lectures and skim the readings, you'll do good in class. She and the TAs also do reviews of the readings before a midterm/final.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Zhang is so nice! I took her last year for Anth and she was a real gem! However, your recitation professors are the ones who grade you. 3 papers, 2 exams. the midterm and final are based on stuff from the lectures. vocabulary, and a free response was on the midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Super chill guy and lots of fun activities in class. Gives out free food, free cash, and free life advice (not in a bad way) at a lot of times. So sad that he only teaches M&O.

Sal is the best prof I've had at NYU. Lectures are incredibly engaging and involve cash and snack prizes. He really makes you want to come to class and teaches the concepts in a really easy to follow way. Grading is fair and he gives good feedback. Also bought Pop Up Bagels on the last day after final group presentations. TAKE HIM!

One of my favorite professors I taken at Stern! Class is always fun and the lectures include activities that always keep you invested. Exams are easy and he makes sure to not overwhelm you with work. Take his class if you can!

Probably my favorite professor that I've had at Stern. Lectures were super engaging and filled with activities to get everyone involved (many included cash prizes and snacks). Super easy to talk to and really made it fun to come to class. Can't recommend him highly enough!
Best professor I've had. makes the course content engaging and is very fair and respectful. 100% would recommend taking a class with him

Best professor I had at NYU so far. He is so nice and makes jokes all the time. He made us play games and do fun activities. I get that Stern grading policy is annoying. He actually made me want to go to his class every week. He always brought pastries, coffee, etc. Always available outside the class and responds to emails fast.
Really sweet guy. Super accessible outside of class and makes classes engaging and fun. His millenial humor is top tier LOL. 100% recommend. Genuinely cares about each one of his students.

Sal is an amazing professor I just don't understand how getting an A- and an A for both midterms is still not enough for your grade to be in the A range. Provided that the group projects and individual paper went well too. LIKE, WHAT DO I NEED TO DO?

grading: individual (75%) and team work (25%) 
readings are all online case studies, podcasts, newsletters, etc. 
two case analysis options 
two organizational research assignment options (2%) REQUIRED 
*arrive on time and be engaged*
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Sal provides engaging classes and many opportunities to participate and work with others you do not usually sit with or know. After all, you do not get to choose who you work with in a work setting. 

Very flexible, gives halftime breaks during lectures, understanding, chill, and replies to your emails ASAP.
Amazing guy! Gives out cash prizes in class
Conceited, and not well prepared
No Comments

Despite having a A average the entire semester, I got a C+ on my final.  I e-mailed him, and he never re-checked it or explained anything.  Too bad he was completely unhelpful, because it was a very cool class.

the class is very informative, and prof affron knows so much about what he is teaching about. i like the films he picked for class, but the grading was a little harsh, especially if you have no background in cinema studies. affron doesn't grade papers or tests, they're graded by a grader, who was ve
Professor Affron is a bit wacky but his classes are fun. He choose some pretty bad movies for the course though and he is a harsh grader. Still, his class was enjoyable.

Super nice and you can tell he truly wants to get to know the students personally. He gives good feedback on what you could improve on and super responsive when I needed help with an assignment! 10/10

Alfo was my TA for Cultures and Contexts Italy. He's super nice and understanding, and makes recitation enjoyable. I suggest speaking up during discussion and writing more than 2 pages for your short papers. I also suggest not doing all the readings, but only some and using them in your short papers. Do this, and an A is easily manageable.

He is my favorite TA I have ever had. He tried to make it interesting as possible. Took time out of his schedule to accommodate us with any of our questions. Would look over your essay if you asked. He really wanted to get to know us personally and was very passionate about his studies! I highly recommend!!

She is my favorite teacher in the Department of Sociology of Education at NYU Steinhardt School. She not only organized interesting activities in class to help students to have a good understanding of complicated and abstract concepts in sociology, but she also provide supportive meetings after class. All in all, you will learn more from her class

She is nice and the course in general was inspiring. However, if you are not the type of people who feel like speaking EVERY SINGLE CLASS, then don't take this course. Otherwise you would get a B- for participation even if you attend every lecture. BTW, she is really a tough grader on essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great prof that deeply cares about students. Lots of reading but she goes over it in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Agyepong is my favorite professor at NYU. She is hardworking, talented, and caring. I looked forward to her class every week; I hope I can take more of her courses in the near future!

Dr. Agyepong is very kind and funny, she really made the course material accessible to us. Would have appreciated more feedback on assignments and less pressure put on participation because the discussions could feel overwhelming with so many people trying to contribute, but the lectures were really informative.

Professor Agyepong is absolutely amazing. You will learn so much with her as your professor and you will not regret taking any of her classes. She is extremely caring and understanding; something every professor should be during a pandemic. I wish I could have her for every class, she was easily one of my favorite professors.

As a black student in a school like NYU it was very important for me to see a teacher like me. There were other students in the class of different races and ethnicities and I think we can all agree that she is absolutely fantastic. The course work was light, midterm and final are simple but the discussions were worthwhile, Learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super nice person but you learn nothing. Would not recommend his classes - he can make it seem like he's talking about something for 2 hours and then you realize nothing was really said. A waste of time.

Gustavo is an amazing and caring professor who creates a safe environment for all students. Learned a lot about myself in this class and was able to step out of my shell and create art I usually wouldn't. You don't have to know tons about art to take this class, you're introduced to new themes and artists.

I am struggling with understanding what is the point of this class. He is like a fish you try to grab but keeps slipping out of you hand. The other students find him nice but boring but I am notsure he is nice just invisible. Linked to are other classes, which are so far great. One is hard but a great professor and TA. Other is easy as pie.

He makes you think and reflect more and be a better artist, but if you want concrete projects or learn about art history, perhaps this class isn't for you. The assignments are quite abstract which makes it fun.
Took for A&C 2 and it was fantastic. Exams were heavy memorization tests, and the course generally had lots of reading, but I learned a lot. Would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor McCannon is a lovely professor, who really does try to make class engaging and discussion-based. While it may feel like a lecture, her little jokes and discussion prompts do make the difference. She is a bit hard to get a hold of, though, and does take forever to grade things (but you can talk to her at office hours).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were very boring and never answered emails. Takes forever to grade papers and when she does she nitpicks. Unprofessional and would forget to upload assignments. She is a nice person but overall as a teacher I would avoid.

I fell asleep in every one of her classes. Her midterm and final require you to remember every little aspect of her lectures including photo and audio. Her papers are niche and she doesn't finish grading them ever. She is a harsh grader. You either learn or drown. The reading is dense. If you put your head to it, though, you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This professor is a nightmare  Also she looks incredibly closely as essay for any mistake and penalizes you harshly for them. Will take ages to reevaluate and won't even change the grade. Finally, she gives no test guide while having ID's in her tests (could literally be on anything you've discussed), so I'd suggest you run away while you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of reading, but you don't need to do all of them to do well on the exams. I think the key to succeeding in her class is taking notes and paying attention during lectures. Only two papers, not too hard. Overall would recommend. Amazing personality and lectures are extremely engaging. ALSO, she offers EXTRA CREDIT!!!

I really liked Professor McCannon. Her lectures were interesting, and I gained a lot from them. However, she's a really tough grader and is unresponsive to emails, but there is an opportunity for extra credit. As long as you participate, you'll be good.
Does not reply to emails. I have been ghosted. This makes me extremely sad. There is a lot of work outside of class as well which one again makes me sad.

I would pick another professor for this class if you could. The unclear grading criteria makes it very difficult to get good essay grades. Pretty zany professor, outgoing but that doesn't matter much when you get low grades. If you want an engaging class that you can get an A in, find a different professor

Rushes through the material, never elaborating or exploring any work enough. Makes it impossible ever truly to understand anything. Tough essay grader, A- and below. Difficult, purely memorization-oriented exams that no clear study guide is given for, and you must rely solely on class notes. Not an easy or rewarding class. Avoid if possible.

Amazing professor, so engaging and funny! A lot of readings but as long as you can identify different authors/styles you're golden. Had her over the summer so it was a condensed syllabus, but like any class, as long as you put in the work you'll be fine. One of my favorite classes so far!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Had her summer 2023. Complaints are true to an extent, but absolutely not as ridiculous as some are making it seem. Office hours scheduled via e-calendar, just talk to her end of class if you need to email about it. Ask for any extension 24 hrs before and it's a default yes if no reply. Exams are a lot but my study group put in the hours and got As

She has the sweetest personality and makes silly jokes in class. If u think that that wont help u, ur wrong bc sometimes her attitude was the only thing getting me through the day. Her midterms/finals are questions that the students basically create so the difficulty of the exams are determined by the classes knowledge of the content. Love her

She emphasizes taking notes as her exams are very high school-esque fact-based. If you take decent notes you can get an A. She is a relatively easy paper-grader. I thought the course was easy if you knew how to make a quizlet for the midterms to memorize the facts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: One Word For Anyone Who Want To Select Her Course: Runnnnnnn!!!! It is not just about hard work& time! not accessible after class (almost never reply to emails or phone calls or texts), tough&strange&unclear criterions, heavy work(2 papers, 2thread weekly, 2 exams) in 2 months, go through about 7 books in half semester, almost no feedback.....

The only content we have is a syllabus, that is constantly inaccurate. No clear instructions at all. For summer class, while other teachers cut down the syllabus, we have exactly the same work load as the Spring and Fall classes. Grade not hardly but weirdly!!!!!!!!!!!!!! No clear rubrics tooo

Claimed that her rubrics were "in her head" when asked about grading guidelines. Exams were memorization based to the point that our class considered not taking it and going to the Dean.
