Claimed that the grades of papers are based on the performance of peers. Other reviews should not be this positive, she was a nice person but a terrible professor.

This is too much factual information to remember for a college-level class. Unclear guidelines and due dates. We have to take notes without knowing what is important for the test. Not inspirational at all. We should be practising critical thinking, but we're not. Can NYU provide more options for summer courses, please?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There so many things to do during the class. The midterm is heavy and difficult. The paper that she required us to do is without guideline, she is a really tough grader. Never take this course again! Never!

Prof McCannon is one of those professors that could get you to intently listen to a lecture about dirt. While she does assign a hefty amount of reading, her lectures encourage you to do the work. Her exams are difficult, but she grades fairly and offers extra credit. She encourages participation, and grades based on how much you participate.

Very knowledgeable and chooses interesting material, but is completely unreasonable with the amount of stuff she expects you to memorize and is chaotic with guidelines, deadlines, and feedback. As long as you go to class and take good notes you'll be fine, but if you miss anything you're doomed. A lot of reading. Would take again, but not an easy A

Though Dr. McCannon is a passionate professor who clearly loves what she is teaching, her grading style is somewhat nonsensical and confusing to experience as a student. I never received feedback that explained why I didn't get an A. However, she facilitates a good discussion and is very knowledgeable, so.. take at your own risk.

McCannon is super passionate about Arts and Cultures. If you are in Liberal Studies and do not want to go into Liberal Studies for the rest of your life DO NOT TAKE HER. Her tests are niche and heavy, for the exams you have to memorize all of her spoken lectures (she does not post notes). She grades harshly on writing too. Would not take again.

She is a nice lady, but the thing is she hardly ever gives you feedback, I didn't get my first assignment's grade till the last class of the semester. She is nice but can't change my mind about never taking her class again.

The professor's lectures are amazing! The best that I have experienced so far. She is so lively that she can make any text seem fun. It's just that she's a bit disorganized and doesn't give a lot of feedback. Nevertheless, she is such a great professor, and its a 100% clear that she loves what she does :)

Prof. McCannon was great and very understanding of COVID struggles, but there was still too much asynchronous work in ACC for me. She explains tough things very well and is responsive in person and during office hours, but is hard to reach over email and doesn't really give feedback unless you ask. But I really enjoyed her overall.

One of the best LS professors. She knows how to talk about art and culture naturally without getting weird about it, like some white professors inevitably do. Loved her classes and readings, but personally assignments were difficult to grasp. Spent lots of hours wrestling with papers and I didn't have the time to submit something satisfying.
Professor McCannon is so kind and makes class not feel so stressful. She gives us clear ideas on what tests and essays should have. Shes amazing!

I had her for "Approaches to Global Studies", but I'm not sure which course code I'm supposed to put. Anyways she's a very understanding and down to earth professor. Her weekly readings are straightforward, the presentation was pretty easy, and there's a midterm and final paper but it was not hard. Make sure to show up and do the work on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is hilarious and her kind of lame jokes are what kept me awake at 9am. Honestly, she's not really a harsh grader at all but I will say that you MUST attend class and take notes on what she says; a lot of the stuff isn't in the assigned reading and the exams are mostly made up of what she mentions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: McCannon brings lots of energy and a clear passion for her work, but I often felt bored in the class, because the pace was very slow. I wasn't sure what to study for when it came time for midterms and finals, however she was not an extremely harsh grader. Obtaining an 'A' is not impossible, but definitely one of my tougher classes this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's not the most inspirational teacher, but she is passionate about what she teaches. She's very well educated and tries her best, but she fails to make the CF material enjoyable or engaging. If you slack, you'll get the grade you deserve. You get what you put into the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: McCannon is one of the best professors in LS from my experience. She is funny, caring, professional and cares about what she teaches and her students' work. I was never bored listening to her lectures and her assignments are all very interesting. As long as you read and follow instructions, the classes aren't hard at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Quite honestly the best teacher or professor I have had in my entire educational life. She genuinely cares about her students in all respects. We are real people to her, with different lives and with different understandings of class discussions. Her paper topics are clear and fun to write. Take her by all means. I cannot recommend her enough,

Professor McCannon's classes were an academic highlight for my freshman year. Her lectures are super engaging and very interesting. She is very energetic and has an AMAZING sense of humor. I took her Cultural Foundations classes for both semesters, which was the right choice. I found her grading very reasonable, but there is lots to keep track of.

LOVE Professor McCannon. She's a fantastic lecturer, and her conversations are engaging with the whole class. She has a great sense of humor as well that makes even the blandest topics interesting. Two warnings: don't skip bc her exams are based off of a lot of class discussions, and DEFINITELY go to office hours for papers bc she's a rough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great class. Makes you work hard for a good grade. She's tough on essays and exams but she is always willing to give feedback on drafts and conducts helpful review sessions for her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved her! She was so nice and really wanted to make sure everyone was interested in the course.  While the books may be boring, she talks about them in class in a way that is easily understood by everyone and makes them actually seem interesting! There are blog posts that are due every week, they can be tedious but do them - they help your grade

Came on here just to rate her. Absolutely incredible professor. Clear and detailed lectures that keep you engaged, fun and creative projects, and you truly get a lot from the class if you pay attention. If I could have her for every class in college I would. TAKE HER.

McCannon made the material come alive in CFI. She helped students pull out themes in the art and literature, which helped us to understand what goes into analyzing the culture. The essays are pretty easy if you talk to her about your ideas beforehand. The midterm was good, too, if you took detailed notes. You don't really need the books in class.

The best thing about Prof. McCannon is that she has this policy where if you need an extension, all you need to do is ask for it 24 hours before the due date and it's granted. It's very useful. If you can, take her for CF
A wonderful lady, take her if you get the chance, she's everything you could hope for in a professor!

She is very nice, and makes you feel very at ease in the class. She tells you EXACTLY what she wants from you in papers. The semester just began about a month ago, but I already know that I like her, would take her again, and would most certainly recommend her to anyone taking cultural foundations 1.

Professor McCannon is one the best and most inspirational professors I've ever had. I absolutely hate the cultural foundations classes, but with her I was excited to go to class every day. She makes the material really interesting. I never missed a class bc I liked it so much! Take notes in class because that's what the midterm and final are about!

Funny, caring, and fun. We played with building blocks in one of her classes to better understand how roman bridges were made. Her lectures are boring if you don't participate but she's super nice and helpful

McCannon was one of the best teachers I have had. She is an amazing lecturer and  really loves her subject. She makes things clear and really makes you think. An inspirtational teacher I loved her so much I'm taking her again.  She's fun and intelligent, and really makes going to class worth it. If you want the best CF around, take her

Wonderful prof! Afrodesia is funny and her classes are ALWAYS interesting. Definitely take notes; copy everything on the board and you'll be good for the midterm and final. City Treasure assignments were interesting, but not necessary. Keep up with the weekly blog posts! Harder grader on papers than I expected.

Took both CF's in Paris and had a great time. Although I feel as though I didn't retain a lot of information AFTER the class (but who DOES?), I enjoyed the class while in it. McCannon is also one of the most helpful and nicest profs I've had at NYU. Mumbles a bit, but very open to questions and comments. Does fun activities
Be at class, that's all the midterm and final is about. Ask specifically what she wants on essays. Shmoop the readings. everything's g double o d good

BRILLIANT Professor. Speaks 7 languages and runs marathons with injuries. Is possibly one of the most interesting and great professors I've ever come across and I would recommend taking her class in any situation.

Honestly a great professor. Class itself was difficult due to the amount of work involved, but you end up learning a lot. I actually really enjoyed blocks and clay. Specifically, I thought the "City Treasure" assignments (which send you around the city looking for cultural influences) were a nice tough. Great prof, just be prepared to work.

She's honestly a great professor. Very competent, very specific as to what she wants you to know and what you need to get a good grade. Straightforward and she is really quite kind too. She teaches in a really fun way too!!

Afrodesia is a delight. Not only is she a competent and worthwhile professor, but she takes an active interest in her students. While she may not allow students to get a 4.0 without any work, she rewards diligence and effort.

Alrighty heres the deal: shes hilarious but difficult... You have to put a lot of time into getting a good grade with her (but hello, this is college so duh). Shes really intelligent and totally into the material, but she isn't always clear in her expectations. Oh and COPY ALL BOARD NOTES.

Do not take this class, unless you want to spend your entire life doing homework and silly assignments about uninteresting topics. There is a ridiculous workload, and while she tries to appear nice, she grades impossibly.  I cannot wait for this to be over, and I feel terrible for all the people that got stuck with her again next semester.

Well intentioned, but horrible teacher. We spend class looking at "10 Signs to Tell if Your Guy is in a Bromance" to study Gilgamesh, play with building blocks, and tons of other activities that waste time. She also mumbles a lot. A nice, somewhat dorky lady, but don't take her if you want to actually learn anything.
Amazing woman, very interesting class, but unreasonable workload.

McCannon is absolutely awesome. She is fun and approachable. Also, the key to acing her finals are to pay attention to what she writes on the board; copy EVERYTHING she writes down, study it, know the general plot and importance of the books and you'll be fine.

I don't know why her rating is so low on here. She is an awesome teacher! The homework load isn't that much. You have to do a blog pretty much once a week which isn't too difficult especially since you can usually do them without having to read the books. All in all I'm very glad I took her this semester and would recommend her to everyone
Favorite professor this semester. It's a difficult class, but totally worth it. She is really funny and relatable. Makes lectures interesting and fun. I would definitely take her again, if I could!

Her class definitely requires a lot of work. The lectures are never boring. She is very animated and demonstrates all her points clearly. She knows what she wants and lets you know. Of course with such a great lecture there is the harder work. She is a hard but amazing professor. I enjoyed her class very much.

I really liked McCannon. She's clear during lectures, yet always manages to let her goofy side show. Tests require a bit of studying but the essays aren't bad at all. If you like ancient history, you'll like this class and have a good time with McCannon.

Afrodesia is seriously one of my favorite professors. She makes the class entertaining and wants you to enjoy the class and understand the material, and, since the class is mostly discussions, she really tailers the class to what the students are interested in. Essays & tests are hard, but if you pay attention & study you'll be fine. Take her!

Oh my god, I can't wait for this horror of a semester to end. Literally the Worst: completely irrationally when it comes to grading papers, biased toward her own faulty opinions, unclear about everything! I dread going to her class and seeing her (pun intended).

Afrodesia is AMAZING! But that's only true if you're really into this subject. If not, then she's still an interesting teacher and makes class entertaining. The work load can sometimes be a bit above reasonable, but you can easily get away with not doing all of it. So long as you engage yourself in class then class is really really fun. A+ for me

She's not easy, this much is true, but she is a fantastic teacher. As long as you go to her after class and make sure that your essays cover the material in an appropriate way, you'll do fine. The midterm and final are sometimes difficult, but as long as you read the books thoroughly and study enough you'll o well.
Hey, I may switch out of my current cf class cuz of a time difficulty and may take mccannon's. Can anybody tell me more abt her class/personality/grading style. Any feedback is greatly appreciated!
She's very cool, one of my favorite professors in fact.  However, I agree with the first two.  She is very hard, and I felt like I didn't know anything that was on the midterm.

What do you guys mean. she is so nice and makes class fun. I would not describe her as hard. just the blogs are annoying but they are so simple because everyone can see eachothers work. duuh. she gives essays like anyone else but are straight forward. the only thing is that she isnt helpful for quick after class questions, only office hours. easy A

guys shes a nice fun lady but her midterms are brutal. her finals are impossible and her essays are so unfair. the only good thing in that class are the occasional jokes but other than that its unbearable. I am serious, do not take her. she is a king and nice lady but gives so much readings and such hard tests.

seriously, i did really really well on both papers, the final, and the midterm (like B+ and up) but somehow still ended up with a B- also never missed a class so participation wasn't the problem. she thinks shes funny but shes not and expects too much- especially on papers. do not take her.

Very understanding and available for any questions. Breaks everything down into easy parts. In recitation, attendance was asked for but not really needed every time. Wrote feedback for legit all the discussion posts (twice a week btw). If you participate and do the basic work you'll be fine.

Not the best structured class but Elisa is very nice and understanding. Even if you completely suck at spanish I don't see how she could give you a bad grade. Very easy homework, participation in class, quizzes, exams. Even the pop quizzes are generally expected. Just do the homework and be ready to get called on and you'll be good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Elisa was one of the best teachers I have ever had. Extremely helpful and style of teaching is incredible. She grades pretty easily and if you pay attention in class, this course is an easy A!

Great Class. You learn a lot and at the same time its not overwhelming. Its a great alternative to the other language courses because its much less stressful. She's a very welcoming professor that makes the class very enjoyable.

She's the best. Doesn't feel like a class - super fun and lighthearted. But you definitely learn a lot and the best part is that she doesn't go only by the book. We watch movies, videos, have debates, read stories, write scripts, etc. Definitely recommend Hindi if you want something less stressful (but just as rewarding) than Spanish, French etc.

She's such an amazing and sweet woman. If you're not already somewhat exposed to Hindi (e.g., knowing a similar Indian language, watching Bollywood movies), you may have some trouble keeping. However, I thought she was an amazing teacher having already had minimal exposure. I was surprised how quickly I learned to read and write in a new language!
Easy grader with a thick accent. Tough if you've never taken Hindi- but easy if you have some knowledge. The substitutes are all trash so you want her in class.

Very knowledgable and knows what he's doing. Well-structured class/ lectures. Learned a lot in this class and it's been absolutely fun for me. Need to do the reading for quizzes but he will let u know when there is one. Definitely not an easy A but participate in class n follow the feedbacks ur gucci

He's a fair professor and though he's a somewhat harsh essay grader, his feedback is helpful. It can be a bit lecture heavy, but it's a text-dense course so no ones really holding it against him. Aguirre is a nice guy, just raise your hand (participation really does push your grade up) from time to time and take notes, and you'll do great. GL!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Juan Aguirre is an amazing professor, and one of the best I have had at NYU. He is very knowledgable and passionate about what he is talking about. He answers questions thoroughly and it is a joy to come to his class every other day. The readings can drag, but READ. He is very lenient on attendance as long as you don't pass 6 absences.

Honestly, there wasn't a lot of work for this class, but the readings were beyond boring. Most of the classes, he lectures and it isn't really too much you need to pay attention to except which passages he goes over and the common themes around those passages. Essay grades are harsh but fair, and the group project was graded pretty easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gives a lot of work and is harsh grader. I sincerely believe I deserved a higher grade in his class for the amount of effort I put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Aguirre is a kind, thoughtful teacher with a deep understanding of the course material. He's very reflective and critically analytical and encouraged us to follow suit to the best of our ability. My only complaint would be that at times the course felt disjointed in that the assignments didn't relate to most of what we did in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: dr. aguirre seems like a chill guy trying to be more professor-y, yknow? he has a great sense of style, and is funny and amiable when he lets his guard down. the rest of the time he's more serious (but never mean). although i liked him as a person, his style of teaching didn't really click with me  it was more lecture-based than other LS classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof is a great guy, super knowledgeable and nice, but the grading is ABSOLUTELY HORRENDOUS. The TA was absolutely diabolical and gave almost no concrete feedback on anything. ID's and exams were difficult and referenced readings we barely talked about. Super nice guy and interesting class, but do not take if you value your gpa.

Absolutely horrendous structure to this class. Grading between both Bekemeyer and Radney was extremely stringent. While Bekemeyer is a great guy, and a great lecturer, tests were absolutely brutal in this class. ID's on tests were referenced MINIMALLY in readings, and less than 20% of the class ended with an A. Avoid, avoid, avoid!
Very interesting content, but the grading is tough. Took the course as an elective, but it was definitely not a GPA booster.

Bekemeyer was great, but the structure of his class was questionable. The grading system was uneven between him and his TA, resulting in class-wide grade discrepancies (lower than grades for many other public policy electives). There was never a clear consensus on what exactly they were looking for on free-response exams. Better structure needed.

Prof. Bekemeyer is very knowledgeable and passionate. However, the course often forayed into an incredibly broad survey of American history. This made studying for the two tests overwhelming. Him and the TA were the most stringent graders I've encountered in any history course. Take a different course if you are interested in maintaining your GPA.
He seems like a nice guy but the class structure and grading make it hard to do well

Grading in this class is unequal between professor and T.A.; numerical grades are considerably lower compared to other history classes at NYU. Interesting lectures, but a heavy focus on background content vs. the readings and applications to policing. Worthwhile course if final grades will be curved; stay away for GPA if not.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Take this class!

Such Dad energy! I took his Cultural Perspectives on Mental Health class and absolutely loved it! My major has nothing to do with psychology or CAMS and I still found myself looking forward to this class week in and week out. He's a very caring, engaging professor who is clearly very passionate about the course and it resonates.
Doctor Reliford is such a gem. Hands down one of the best professors I have had so far at NYU. He truly cares about his students and lectures are always fun and engaging. I highly recommend him!
He's very knowledgable in his field however his grading seems very subjective

Professor Reliford is a gem! He is very kind, intelligent, and open-minded. Cares very much about his students. Cares about students' well-being, especially during the pandemic. Cultural perspectives on mental health class is graded based on 3 papers, one research presentation, and one final cumulative exam. One of the best classes at NYU!

biggest waste of time ever, but it's a required LS class so I guess you were wasting your life to begin with. prof uses chatgpt presentations, syllabus, and grading. the audacity is genuinely stupefying. content is extremely shallow, basic, and worthless. Since he teaches using the answers chatgpt gave him, you should just use chatgpt as well.

Professor PAN is a very sweet and funny professor, however the class is not very engaging. As someone deeply passionate about philosophy, history, and cultures (especially within antiquity), I suprisingly dreaded attending this class. No tests, but mid-terms/finals are 3 5-8 page essays due within 7 days. Also, graded by AI but he's a fast grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So. Much. Readings. For sure lecture heavy, he talks about interesting things from time to time. If you at least do spark notes of the readings you should be good for the lectures because he does explain majority of the key things in class. If I absolutely HAD to take him again I would. He is a very fair grader and gives great feedback I will say!

lectures give me a headache with the amount of questions he asks. lots of reading that no one completes, completing the readings will take you hours each night. however, he does give good feedback on papers. I honestly dread going to this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: very chill professor. his lectures can be dull but workload is really minimal and grades are generally good
The pace of the class is too fast, which makes me feel it's quite difficult to follow. The class atmosphere is also very serious.
He has quite a lot of homework and a lot of reading context. Try to avoid it if possible.

The classes are very serious and dull. There is a huge amount of reading. If you don't read carefully, the consequences will be very serious. There is a lot of writing, but the grades are not very high.

Professor Ngomo is the absolute goat. I wish I could take his class during the actual semester instead of during the summer. His lectures are heavy but the way in which he presents the information is so incredibly intriguing and helpful. I love the way he answers questions; very direct but informational at the same time. Love this guy :)
strict about attendance but not about the readings. You have to participate.

His course is super interesting! You'll learn a ton from him. He'll put himself in your shoes and help you understand the homework problems. He'll also give you more time to finish. And the test is not too hard at all.
Good Professor. The exam is take-home.

Looking back PAN was one of the best professor I have had in my undergraduate career. Not a lot of work other than writing which he gives the answers to in his lectures. He likes different perspectives when writing. Also very accommodating whenever I had an issue just emailed him and he'll try to help.

Attendance is mandatory but Ngomo will not report your absences unless they affect your grade. He is chill & will give you extensions if you need them. He assigns MAD readings but goes through everything in class. As a student just trying to finish the LS curriculum, his class is amazing. Exams are take-home and easy & he gives a week to submit.

Professor Ngomo is easily the best professor I've ever had. He very clearly cares about his students both in terms of learning the material and in terms of grades. No coursework needs to be purchased, and he's extremely accessible outside the classroom. I absolutely would recommend him to anyone who needs to take GWM.

I enjoyed this class a lot! The lectures were engaging and I felt like Prof. Ngomo cared about his students. As long as you participate and show that you are trying in the class you will do fine. Beware of the research paper at the end of the year and plan accordingly. Overall, the content was interesting and I would recommend taking this class.

FAVORITE PROFESSOR OF ALL TIME. HES AMAZING. If you listen and take notes in class, the midterm&final are going to be easy. plus 2 essays but all are fairly graded and there is no strict guideline. All out of class exams. This professor is so fair, so nice, so funny, and EXTREMELY smart & inspiring. TAKE HIM & actually go to class bc he does care.

He is a great professor. You just needs to write a lot. You will not feel interested in his lecture if you do like philosophy but he do not care about that. Do not have to participate but needs to show up because he sometimes do pop attendance.

Overall extremely fair grader and a nice guy. Midterm and Final are take-home, and he posts slides of class lectures to ensure that you have all the information you would need. Only downside to the class is that there is a lot of reading, yet he provides all of the texts on brightspace so you won't have to purchase anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Ngomo is the goat no cap

A genuinely interesting class taught by the funniest professor I've ever had. Prepare for sitting around and debating the ethical implications of very specific and very absurd hypotheticals. Two take-home tests, one policy proposal, all graded pretty leniently. I really loved going to these classes and I recommend him strongly.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took him for GWA freshman year and thought I'd take him again for GWM. Unfortunately, while P.A.N is an easy grader and not strict, his lectures were very draining. He assigns a lot of reading which most people don't finish, so classes are dull. GWA was super interesting, maybe it's just the material, but GWM was not worth taking with him for me.

Class is incredibly boring. Nobody ever does any of the readings because they are extremely long and class discussions have nothing to do with them. He is an easy grade but the class is still challenging cuz of the amount of writing you have to do. 15 page midterm, 20 page final and then 2 essays.
hes a goat no cap

I love this man. There was a lot of discussion so it wasn't so boring and I felt like I learned a lot. His essay topics are interesting and give you room to be super opinionated. He was really nice, sometimes interrupts or misinterprets what you say, but was otherwise a gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I love his lectures. Solid and insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Ngomo is super nice and a really wholesome guy! He grades easily and posts class lecture notes online (read these!!). The content focuses on philosophy and religion and the readings are ancient texts, so it can get pretty dense, but his lectures help a lot with comprehension. Pay attention and do the readings and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ngomo provides an exceptional first look into the development of political theory. His expectations are very clear, and he tends to give good grades to students who participate in class. The entire class is a discussion. Quite a bit of reading, but nothing too crazy. 10/10 highly recommend!

P.A.N. is an AMAZING professor. The professor genuinely cares about you and wants to see you do well. He is flexible with deadlines if you talk to him. Two-take home tests and a short paper. Show him that you are making an effort and care about the class, engage in class discussions, and I promise you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, great class. Only trouble is sometimes he drones on a bit and ends up repeating things. Tests and the paper are super easy.

Took his class in the Summer, one of the best. He really wants students to succeed and give them the chance to do so. He even shared his cell phone number with us. Political Theory is a boring subject, but he makes it fun. Also, he makes students vote if they want to do exams in the class or take-home. RECOMMENDED!
PAN is a great professor. You can tell he is passionate about the subject matter and he does his best to help you understand the material. He asks really interesting questions.
Great lectures! Very smart man though a bit too much self deprecation
Remarkable teacher and very approachable. His passion is contagious. Cracks a few jokes
Highly competent teacher and exciting as well. Good Classroom atmosphere overall
Love this guy, has a great command of language and political philosophy.

Nice guy, but he certainly did not bring the classics to life. For our summer class everything was take home, but the 3 hour lectures were sleep inducing. I had to do a lot of extra work to understand everything.
Attempts to teach the class, and always asks good questions. He also tells a  joke once in a while

pretty good recitation leader for political theory...he encourages alot of discussion and asks provacative questions...makes you think...although he is a tough grader, for the first essay nearly EVERYONE got a B+ no matter how good your essay was...

AMAZING PROFESSOR!! He is such a seasoned, well-connected veteran in his field and brings in industry professionals to speak basically every class. The stuff you learn in this class is genuinely useful for your career and you can feel the passion he has for media literally radiating off him each class. Take it!!!

Professor Cohen is an excellent professor. The content he taught was engaging and insightful. There are readings assigned for this class, but as long as you do them, you will do well, and this will help you in class since it is mostly discussion-based. Overall, I learned a lot and appreciated the readings. I would recommend this class.

Easy coursework, but impactful stuff. This class was mostly discussion-based with minimal homework apart from readings (which were all really interesting). Aaron is very kind and is always willing to help when needed. I highly recommend this class!

Aaron is a great and interesting professor that really cares and the class was genuinely enjoyable. Class is largely discussion-based with thought-provoking conversations that gave me new perspectives and had real-world relevance. Also hosted some really insightful industry speakers. Highly recommend, show up and participate and you will do well!
He is an interesting person but not necessarily a good professor. He is very disorganized and not clear about what he wants. There is no way to know how to get an A in the class.

He is not the greatest teacher, but wonderfully connected to the tech business. He brings in a guest speaker from big names in internet media almost every week. The reading quizzes are kind of a pain, but not hard. All you have to do is show up, put in some effort into the minimal amount of work, and you'll get an A.

Hes very passionate and is good at getting you interested, but he is so incredibly disorganized. He wants to be that "special" professor to you and be approachable out of class and help you with your career, but NEVER makes a real effort. He reached out after the semester encouraging students to contact him, but when I did he never once responded

He is enthusiastic, dynamic, and passionate about the subject matter. The class hosts a high-profile guest almost every week. I recommend reading the assigned books to join in on the class conversation. If you are apprehensive about expressing your opinions in public, this is probably not the class for you. Otherwise, go for it!

Aaron is one of the most inspiring teachers I've ever had. His teaching allows students to think beyond the course material, providing them the tools necessary for the "real world."  In taking his class, I was introduced to countless opportunities to further my studies and career. In general, class is informative, applicable, and interesting.
This class is a great foundation for basically every field. Professor brings in great speakers that gives the class great insight on how powerful the Internet is in every career path.

Really wonderful class- Aaron really cares and wants you to do well. Show up to class, pay attention, read and ask questions and you will no doubt do well. He just wants you to learn and be engaged without being stressed or grade-obsessed. I highly recommend! Warning: class is not super structured which may be a problem for some but I loved it!

Aaron has a very loose structure to his class, and sometimes you're not going to know the "right" way to do an assignment. This is only because he wants you to learn things on your own, like in the real world. He is a very intelligent man who inspired me to think outside the box. I look at the Internet very differently now. Totally recommend.

I really liked this class.  He can be disorganized at times, but the content is very interesting.  Also, it is really easy to network with some of the guest speakers in the class.  Readings can be long and boring at times but the class itself was fine.

don't take this class. he is very disorganized, changes the syllabus at the drop of a hat, and you get no clear instructions on assignments that count for 30% of your grade. the weekly quizzes are ANNOYING. he's very condescending and unapproachable. on the other hand, Amanda (TA) is amazing and helpful.

Incredible professor with incredible knowledge, incredible experience and incredible connections. Will hook you up with a plethora of internships through people he's worked with as CEO of multiple startups. Teaches highly relevant and interesting info. Must-take.

This class will change your views on the internet. Professor cohen is like no other. While the class is demanding with the reading, you read things you're interested in. One of the best classes at NYU. Cohen lets every speak and is all about the back and forth between students. Special guests such as Tumblr Founder, Coursekit Team ETC was unreal!

Great class, even better professor. I stumbled on this course as a non-MCC student and fell in love with it. Amazing speakers come in plus internship hook-ups are great. Recommend this class to EVERYONE REGARDLESS OF MAJOR!

Aaron is definitely one of the best professors I've had at NYU. He is inspiring and passionate and I'm so glad I took his class. He sees students as individuals and gives them that respect. He pushes you to think and the grading is fair. I loved this class! TAKE HIM!

Aaron's class was fantastic. If you want to learn from a true entrepreneur working in the new media space, take one of his classes! His no-BS attitude is great, and theories are presented without the usual stuffy academic tone.

The Greatest Professor at NYU isn't a Professor, he's a CEO(...****) and is a resounding illustration of why the best teachers didn't study teaching and we need to break through teacher's college collusion and backwards pay-scale processes to let the experience speak for "expertise."

Now taken 2 classes with Aaron: The Business of Media and The Rise of Internet Media. Both amazing classes that lead to a full time paid internship in a film office running social media. I knew nothing about tech, media, or business before these classes and am now very confident in my knowledge. Great teacher and great classes. Highly recommend

Rise of Internet Media should be a mandatory class for media majors. Fantastic and interesting class with a knowledgeable professor. Do not miss out on this class! The internet isn't going anywhere, so we all need to know where it came from and where it's going to go. Great opportunity for networking with all the guests and pertinent readings.

He is a really good teacher. Grading is fair and not harsh at all. He knows his stuff and is very enthusiastic and down to earth. You will learn a lot and be happy to go to class. My favorite professor so far at NYU. He is also an entrepreneur and might offer internships or you can bounce your ideas off of him.

Had Aaron for Business of Media, his teaching is a bit unconventional but as a media business person he knew what he was talking about. Class was discussion based and much more 'real world' applicable than many other classes I've had. Lots of speakers and opportunities for networking.

Prof Aalai was a delightful person to see every week. Hilarious, witty, and charismatic. However, she does not do any slides or a formal textbook so you really have to pull your weight to be there every class. She can also get off-topic during her lecture. Overall not a class where you will learn breakthrough information, but good for beginners.

She made developmental psych so enjoyable. Great, engaging lectures; amazing personality, clear grading assignments/criteria; fair and clear exams. Truly a joy to take her class and have her as a prof. One of the best psych profs - the other profs should learn a thing or two from her amazing teaching. Take her class!!

One of the best professors I've had. You do need to go to class or have someone send you notes if you're absent but the exams are soo easy. The readings are interesting and modern and theres no textbook.

Prof. Aalai was amazing, and I would absolutely take her class again. She makes every part of the course interesting and shows real caring for her students. If you keep up with the readings and quizzes you'll be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Aalai gives interesting lectures that are infused with relevant anecdotes and examples. It's clear that she's very passionate and enthusiastic about what she's teaching and that she's receptive to students' input. I'd recommend taking thorough notes during lectures to prepare for the open-note quizzes.

Dr. Aalai was amazing! You can tell that she's passionate and knows a lot about her field, which made the class more engaging for me.The only caveat was that she doesn't do slides, but if you need them, the TAs upload their own slides, which reviews the material we covered in class. She also has recorded lectures. Highly recommend!

Dr. Aalai is a great professor, but she is so busy that it can be hard to get a hold of her. Class is based on 2 tests, ~6 online quizzes, and recitation attendance. Dr. Aalai is very fair and interesting person, however her class can be hard to focus in bc she doesn't use slides and often spends long periods of time answering students questions.

Professor Aalai isn't bad, she's just not particularly engaging. She 1) doesn't use slides 2) doesn't use a textbook and 3) goes off on tangent all the time during her lectures. I don't think I've ever found it as hard to focus as it was in her class. Fairly doable course, but not the most exciting.

Dr. Aalai's class was the only class I genuinely looked forward to. She lectures without any slides, so she doesn't talk AT you. There is a quiz every couple weeks and one midterm and one final that are all MC, so the fact that I wasn't stressed about the workload made the class more enjoyable! My favorite class ever!

Loved this class. Was apprehensive at first given the grade is only made up of recitation attendance, quizzes, and 2 exams but quizzes and exams were so easy (all MC). Will say lectures were not accessible as Aalai would speak to the class without any slides (had to take really thorough notes to remember what she was saying). TAs were amazing too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Love Dr.Aalai, and TA Savannah is so supportive and nice!

This was Prof Aalai's first time teaching a class at NYU so, it was a little disorganized, but it's better now. Attending lectures/paying attention is important. Weekly quizzes excluding exam week. The exam was 50 questions from the quizzes. Recitation attendance is required. 25% for Midterm, Recitation, Final, Quiz. Very nice & flexible if needed.

Knowledgable, passionate about teaching psychology. She is very energetic and I enjoyed her developmental psychology course. Attendance is not mandatory but matters because no slides and only oral lecture, but the lecture is organized and clear, if you keep up your attendance, the exams are fair.

Dr. Aalai cares less about teaching course material and more about discussing her own opinions. Class consists of debating a few research papers that she finds interesting. Don't dare to disagree. Better suited to those who are interested in paying thousands to have philosophical discussions rather than actually learning applicable information.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Christie's stories about his time in government really elevate the class material, and he makes the classroom environment very engaging. He's also well connected and will always help you get the contacts you need. Took almost an entire month to grade papers and post final grades on Albert

One of those teachers that has so much to say he ends up on tangents a lot (in a good way). Textbooks but if you don't do the reading it makes no difference. A Republican but he's aware of his audience so it's never overbearing. Genuinely loves teaching. Make sure he knows your face and you'll get an A. Never gives grades though so that's annoying

Interesting course on the presidency, great content and the professor has many unique stories because of his personal background. Very caring professor. The only concern is that we never received any grades back except for our final grade. Seems tough to get a A but relatively easy to get an A-.

Took his math modeling last semester. Great lectures and he's good at using examples and explaining things. If you are still confused about how to do the homework, attend his office hour and he'll explain everything to you. Super nice and helpful.

I see both sides. Yeah he's disorganized and rambles about random stuff. But when he actually does teach material, he's pretty clear and good at it and tries to break things down to be intuitive. He seems to not care too much about exam grades. In conclusion he's just a chill guy
take math modeling with Rangan plz
Best Math teacher in NYU. If you attend his lectures and did every homework, you can get A.

Most disorganized class ever. We probably got through half the topics on the "syllabus". Half the lectures are just random stories. Never answers emails. Very bad at time management. The final was a mess, last week of classes he assigned a take-home practice final, a take-home final (length of 5hw), and an in-person part of the final.
He is the goat
Trust me, He is the best!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

the BEST professor ever!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
interesting lectures.
He is the best professor I have ever seen in NYU!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!11

You can learn a lot from Rangan's class if you choose to learn. However, if you choose not to learn, you can still get an easy A if you do every HW. Really Chill professor. If you have choice and don't choose him, you definitely will regret!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

You can learn a lot from the class if you choose to. Just do the work and you will get an A, at least during the semester I took his math class. Yes - you need to know some basic ODE / Matlab skills but he posts his own code half the time and you can get 90% of what you need from that.

Professor Rangan is an enigma. Towards the end of most lessons he starts talking about dinosaurs or life on Venus, or the statistical improbability of the existence of a megalodon. Despite lacking a syllabus, it was otherwise organized. Nothing was too difficult assuming you've done calculus and linear algebra already.
Best professor. Greatest guy. Highly recommend!!
if you have the chance to take ANY class with this professor, definitely do it enough. best math professor I ever had

He's a nice guy, great speaker. But those of you unaware should know: he doesn't actually teach Calculus, so you won't learn calculus. He just teaches whatever, and then gives you a grade. No joke. Some like this. Most of us will unfortunately leave not knowing calc 3.
Don't take this guy: no syllabus, doesn't explain anything well, doesn't reply to emails. Gives grades arbitrarily without reason. Terrible.
Rangan is absolutely terrible. Don't take him if you want to retain your sanity.

This man is a legend. I wish his math modeling class was twice as long. Easily one of the best professors I've ever had. His class gives you the freedom to actually focus on understanding the material and putting things together rather than just aiming for a grade. He's a pleasure to listen to. Keep up with the homework and you'll do well.

Professor Rangan is the best instructor I had for a math class in my entire life. He emphasized problem solving and frequently went over problem sets in class before they were due. His exams were a compilation of unaltered questions from the problem sets and open note. He often draws pictures to help his students visualize the concepts. Take him.
Avoid

The way this guy teaches is GOLD. You do not learn anything the other professors teach. He spends the lecture telling hilarious stories and teaching graduate level applied mathematics and physics. His class is easy with all homework being for completion, no quizzes, no midterms and a final he writes that is straight off the homework. Take him. :)

In this class, you'l learn everything except for calculus. I now consider myself an expert on board game-playing neural networks, the different methods of transporting giant stone statues, and the various parasites that infect seagulls, but I do not know how to take a derivative.
professor rangan is a math god. everyone received a's in our calc 2 class because he taught so eloquently. what a legend.

aaditya rangan is so hilarious that my chest hurts from laughing so much during the lecture. he always keeps his lectures clear and concise, and always tells really funny stories. overall, he is a solid guy. he does not follow the book at all, but instead teaches us real world application. there is minimal homework and open note tests.

Rangan is rather hard to assess. If you are taking a fundamental class like calc13, don't take him, he teaches 100% diff stuff. If you're taking an advanced class, and you have some idea about the content, this guy is enlightening - he will give you so much field experience and intuition it's awesome. If you're looking for easy grades, take him.

i truly believe that aaditya rangan is a straight up legend. his class is supposedly way easier than those who have mutiara sondjaja or vindya bhat. he has only note tests and exams, with ZERO quizzes. tests and exams are OPEN NOTE and legit come straight off the hw. hw is graded for spot graded for completion. he is simply sensational

Professor Rangan is breath of fresh air in the calculus sequence. He is remarkably clear and concise in explaining the concepts he covers. He teaches differently than most professors, so you will never use the textbook nor have any web assign. We took his final instead of the departmental one. His final was open note and straight from the homework.

Professor Rangan is a true gem. His lectures are always clear and concise and he does a remarkable job of explaining the real world application of the concepts that he is teaching. Homework is graded for completion and there are no quizzes. The exams are straight from the homework and open note. We took his final instead of the departmental one.
aaditya rangan is a straight up legend. his calc lectures are so clear and concise. his exams are also open note and come straight from the homework. bless nyu for such a wonderful professor

-as long as you show up to class, you will receive an a -unlike other teachers, rangan has no quizzes and all of his exams are open note -tests are straight copy and paste from his homeworks -i highly recommend him, especially if you are interested in statistics and natural sciences because tries to tie in real world applications to the course

This was a stressful class. He teaches as he likes to. He doesn't cover the topics that other professors usually cover. He doesn't have a syllabus or grading criteria. It's very unorganized and conceptual. Homework is hard. But tests and grades are very easy as long as you understand what's going on (which is hard for some people)
Very easy class as long as you show up

Caution: This is a math class unlike any other. He teaches intuition about the topics on the syllabus. CONCEPTUAL. That's not for everyone. Some survival tips: NOT an easy A class. Be able to GO WITH THE FLOW. Don't buy the textbook. TAKE GOOD NOTES for the open notebook tests. Form study groups (find a friend or two). Enjoy the stories. Good luck
sensational

Professor Rangan has to be one of the smartest Professors I have ever met. There are definitely times in which I feel lost, but he's always willing to explain himself. Expect a large amount of homework and long nights. The textbook isn't really useful for those assignments so the best recommendation would be to take concise and good notes.

Rangan is the best instructor I've ever had! I took his Linear Algebra and Scientific Computing. He knows how to motivate students and clarify hard concepts and theorems. He also gives great grades as long as you spend time thinking about the problems. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!

This course almost covers all the fundamental fields of maths, from algebra, calculus, possibility theory, stochastic process and numerical analysis. Homework, although carefully prepared step by step by professor, is somehow challenging. Fortunately, there is no midterm and final, which makes everyone a little surprised.

He did NOT teach us anything we needed to know for Calc II. He taught everything conceptually and graphically and I left that class not knowing how to solve a single equation. I got an A. He literally counted the dept final as a quiz and made his own final to get away with it. Now I'm behind in all of my chemistry courses bc can't do the math

Seriously, if you have the chance to get Rangan and you don't take him, you're a fool. He is by far the best Calc professor in the whole university. Some professors grade generously, but teach terribly. Some professors teach extremely well, but grade like Satan. Rangan is a fantastic teacher (you will learn SO much) AND grades generously.

Don't miss out on a chance with a wonderful professor! He is one of those professors who will make your time @ NYU worth it. Really friendly, grades generously, and cares about your growth, mathematically or otherwise!
Take him and thank me later.

Love him. Probably one of the most interesting teachers, made calc 2 a piece of cake (that is for math people), he would tell you EXACTLY what his test is going to comprise of. Hates the calc dept which is more than justified. Has useful insight and his class was a lot of fun. DEF TAKE HIME !

GREAT PROFESSOR! Didn't follow the syllabus and hated the department but taught real-world, useful applications of the material. Also, gave his own tests that were much more analytical and concept based.  Also told really ridiculous stories to lighten the mood through our 2 hour lectures.

Prof. is there for you, when you ask. Shares personal stories and is funny. Attend lectures to get a good midterm grade, memorise dates, etc. Expectations regarding the paper are unclear, but you learn to think for yourself and grading is fair!

Prof. is funny and helpful, replies to emails quickly. Midterm is tough indeed, but counts only 20% towards final grade; you have to memorize dates, attendance to class is useful as he asks things which are not in the slides. Grading on the paper is fair; little guidance and unclear expectations, but you learn to think for yourself!
very bad teacher boring and unclear classes  tough tests  bad grades + doesn't explain why  not helpful at all

Doesn't matter how well you do on the test since your grade is entirely based on the paper, with your midterm and final ending up to not matter much at all. He seems like a nice enough guy, funny and replies to his email quickly enough, except his grading on the paper is the harshest I've ever seen. Avoid.

Extremely unhelpful and unclear as to what he expects re: papers, assignments. The midterm for this past spring 14 was strictly memorizing dates-- very little comprehension of themes in his class was necessary. Would avoid 100%.

Stay clear. Unless you like writing papers at a 300 level standard in a 200 level class with very little guidance, this is not the class for you. Gurwitz is a nice man and can be pretty funny at times, but his expectations are not clear. What is expected of you isn't clear and students use to grinding out numbers in other classes will be stumped.

Predictive Analytics is naturally a difficult course and requires a lot of studying. It can be extremely stressful if you have a heavy courseload, but very rewarding when you're able to gain such a deep understanding of meaningful, important topics. If you're struggling, just go to office hours and you'll be fine. He wants you to do well.

One of the most egotistical professors I have ever met throughout my college experience. He doesn't explain concepts very well, throws equation after equation at you expecting it to stick and then moves on immediately. Just overall terrible at teaching. If you can avoid him, I would advise you to avoid him like the plague.

Exams are hard and you need to stay on top of the material for quizzes. It's a tough class but you really do learn a lot, so it's worth it. He's a really good professor and gives tons of extra credit, like 5-10 points on each homework and 25 on the last. Just review the material weekly and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, lots of extra credit opportunities. You will need to keep on top of material weekly to do well on the quizzes and exam, but he is helpful during office hours.

It is definitely a hard class, but you will learn a lot. The professor is caring, and always willing to help during office hours. The exams are long, but not hard. If you paid attention in class, and on the materials he provided, you will do just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hard conceptual lectures with long coding HW(he expects you to do without going through in class/any hints). 3/4 of the material overlap with FML, but quizzes and exams are much harder including math proofs and niche concepts (he barely touches in class). Long exams you just can't finish NO CURVE at all you could understand everything and get a B-
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good prof. Gives additional materials for u to understand the topic. It is a hard class and be expected to have quizzes every class, exams are time-consuming rather than hard. Homework is long, but it covers data analysis all the way through machine learning, you get to implement algos from scratch for example pca, k means algo, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He has pop quizzes that make up about 10% of your grade (NOT on the syllabus & random). He introduces a lot of material and doesn't go into much depth but I also wouldn't say this class is useless. There are several extra credit opportunities. Not very hard, but take it ONLY if you plan on going to every class. I wouldn't take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: goes through material pretty quickly and its hard to keep up if ure not on top of it. gives pop quizzes to enforce attendance which is pretty annoying. i don't personally think he did a great job explaining the intuition behind certain topics but that could just be me being stupid. the main thing i remember from class is that he worked at google.

I do not really recommend this course. He takes attendance randomly and has pop quizzes that make up 50% of the homework grade (this is NOT mentioned in the syllabus). The exams and quizzes are harder than the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was my second time with Dr. Ahn and I have to say, I strongly dislike her teaching style. She uses the same colors on her lecture slides that are so boring and just spills info on the slides that makes it hard to take notes. This class is lecture HEAVY, and they are boring lectures. The class is 1hr40min and we get no breaks...do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is so sweet and king and she puts so much effort and love into her classes. Not that hard of a class if you listen in class, there are a lot of assignments and you have to sing for two of them two. But its kind of fun and I learned a lot. Cool class and I love her.

Professor Ahn is one of the kindest professors I've had and she has a genuine passion for music history. While the class packs in a lot of content, the professor made it more bearable and she helps her students to the best of her ability. There are only a few things that make up your grade but it is definitely a doable class.
Really nice guy. Always willing to talk about movies, art, books, music, and theatre. Barely gives any homework. Super easy grader. Made this horrible class actually really fun. Highly recommend.

The class itself is terrible, but there's no way to change that. Aaron's a really nice guy and a fairly easy grader. He doesn't always give a lot of feedback unless you ask for it, but if you do, he's pretty helpful. He's a good guy and a good teacher but he needs to have more classroom discussions cause otherwise everyone just spaces out.
Just an awesome, down-to-earth, laid-back, funny dude. Good teacher of the class nobody likes.

I don't remember THAT much about his teaching technique. I think he tried a lot to explain difficult writing concepts (kind of successfully). Lots of good class discussions. I know he has a dry sense of humor and is a TOTAL hipster (but not in an annoying way).

Many ppl don't like him, but I really liked his class. Not having him 2nd sem was a bit harder. His movie knowledge was so interesting! I always wrote down his suggestions. Sometimes his directions were vague, but in the end he made me into a much better writer. You just have to be willing to put in a ton of work into your essays and exercises.

Aaron can't teach a class. He would give vague directions and then act frustrated when you couldn't understand what he wanted. He sucked at leading class discussion and I didn't learn anything for an entire semester. Avoid him if you can.

I did pretty well in & liked HS English but WTE was more about thinking. Always interesting,but hard. Wish I had done better/had more time on some of my essays--usually by the time I turned them in I felt like I was just getting started. Aaron was cool teacher-unexpected humor & knew lots of cool film & music.

Aaron Balkan is the worst writing teacher I have ever had. He doesn't take much time to focus on the individual student and does not tell you what he wants. He is very difficult to learn from. If you can possibly avoid this professor, do so.

Aaron was the man.  He's a really great teacher and really tries to help his students both in and outside class.  I had him for the first semester of writing the essay and had no idea why people thought it was a bad class because I loved it.  This semester when I don't have Aaron, it really does suck.

Aaron is a cool dude.  To be honest, I liked him a lot better in retrospect.  He knows his stuff and he is pretty reasonable.  He has a cool, though dry, sense of humor and he is very relatable, especially to film students.  If you have him, check out his website aaronbalkan.com.  Make a comment about one of his films or poems to earn some points

He has a wry and sarcastic sense of humor that can come across as mean, but it's alright. Really, the problem is that he's vague, vague to the point of confusion about what it is HE wants YOU to do. I'm willing to accept that I need to improve, but I'd prefer to be told HOW.  He's a good teacher when reveiwing one-on-one, but too abstract in class
aaron is awesome
Aaron Balkan has a wry sense of humor, knows his stuff, and is passionate about writing good essays, which helps when the material can sometimes seem kind of dry. A very good prof.
No Comments
No Comments

hard grader but fair. this course has a bad rep, but I found the things aaron said about writing to be inspiring. you have to want to challenge yourself though, and be willing to accept that your writing is not already perfect
prof balkan is uncomfortable with himself and it shows.  always deferred to higher ups.  got a god grade by haunting office hours.  must force him to give out decent grades.
No Comments
the class itself is tough, but balkan makes it enjoyable. my writing definately improved. a good guy.
he's a nice guy. not too bad, just not so good at explaining. but i feel that's more that course than anythign really. not a terrible professor in my opinion.
he's terrible.  he has no idea what he is talking about.  dont take him.
Super helpful and genuinely nice. Always willing to support students and quick to respond to feedback. The workload is very fair. Great professor overall
