reviews.comment: Easy class. Clear lecture, easy exam. TA Aria was GOAT.

(Discrete 2024) Misleading syllabus. Reads directly from slides. Not much point in going to class... except for mandatory attendance, or you get points docked. You will be forced to solve problems in front of the whole class, or get points docked. This class managed to be both boring and anxiety-inducing simultaneously.
took analysis with prof. it was very easy.  prof explains well and is accessible

FOR CONTEXT: this is for MATH-UA 325 (Analysis), not 120.

Terrible professor. He had no idea what he was doing. His proofs were often wrong in class and we had to correct him. Midterm was abysmally hard (the avg. was a 38%) and had nothing to do with anything we did in class. His TA graded everything and pretty much taught the class. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved professor Bou-Rabee a lot! He is a really caring professor and his lectures are very clear. The exams are tough, but if you attend lectures you see some pretty similar stuff on them.
Lectures are usually pretty clear and he seems to care about our understanding.  His exams are hard but def attend lecture as some questions are exactly what we did in class!
His exams are tough, but If you love mathematics, go with him.
Really tought prof, gives 3 tests worth 20% each. Test are created by the prof and really expect you to think outside the box while taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Amazing guy but the only reason I gave it a 2/5 in terms of difficulty is cause I am so bad at this. But he's really nice and checks in all the time and emphasizes reaching out and being accessible. More of a my thing than his
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice and easy going, knows his stuff, gets to know you, super accessible, always willing to go over to help.

Honestly such a kind and easy-going person. Makes class fun and engaging and honestly cares about your concerns and experience. ITP graduate himself so he knows how to help. Gets to know students personally and puts an effort to help. Classwork is straightforward and hes more than happy to help with concerns. Hes willing to curve ;)

His classes and grading are super straightforward and transparent. He's always open to helping outside of class and being accessible. Attendance is mandatory but its only once a week and he's SO understanding. Classes are informative, funny, and he creates a comfortable atmosphere. Assignments are easy, never overbearing. Just communicate with him.

Ahmad is the nicest prof ever. He's one of the few profs who genuinely care about their students and WANT them to pass and do well. I've had profs at NYU who know their field well and leave the students to self-study. But not him, he does everything he can so my class did so well. Highly recommend, everyone does. Respectful, funny, knowledgable.

I'm shocked he doesn't have more ratings! My entire class agreed he's by far the best professor they've had - not to mention his experience. He's so so SO understanding, and although attendance counts due to the department rules, he's always so quick to respond and caring if anything comes up.

Prof Elkhouly is a cool guy and is clearly passionate about the material. The tests are all short answers, but people generally do well on them. Strongly recommend, the class is pretty low work and the teacher is able to engage the whole 180+ person class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy A,
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUUUN as fast as you can, waste of your time, your money, your everything. He doesn't curve!! Even he gives out extra credit, but he is so unorganized, and unable to catch up the syllabus and he doesn't care about it.

He is a nice person but a horrible professor. He is just extremely unorganized, our syllabus is not detailed or informative at all, and he never gives detailed instructions for projects and extra credits. We are a few chapters behind, and he doesn't seem to mind. IMO his exam was really easy, but it's everything else is terrible.

NO, just no. He is unorganized in the lecture, has no homework so you don't know what you should learn and prepare for the exam. The textbook he asks to read is just unorganized as him. He is trying to waste everyone's time in this course. And basically, he doesn't teach anything related to urban economics.

Easy A. He gives an opportunity to gain 10% extra credit on your final grade & the midterm/final mirror practice exams. He takes intro concepts & reframes them in terms of Urban Econ, so if it is repetitive. The difference is that you get to take the definitions u memorized last sem and think about them critically - what a 200 class is all about.

He gives you chance to earn about 10 extra credits, which weighs almost 10 percent in the grade. As long as you put your effort, it should be an easy A and he does teach you a lot of life meanings. Btw, he doesnt curve which means you just need to behave yourself well. He really wants everybody gets an A in his class.

I found it a real privilege to take urban economics with Professor Elkhouly. He is a great teacher, who is extremely passionate about economics and teaching it. He doesn't want his students just to memorize equations or facts, he wants us to truly understand the material. He is a breath of fresh air in the economics department. A++ would take again

The only reason why I give a 2 is because he gives out extra credit. Other than that, I dont know how to praise this guy. He is late for class very often, I remember once he was late 40 mins for a 75 min class. He doesnt honor his promise and leave all grading to his TA, and take all the credit. The class has 200 students yet he has only one TA
At the end of the day cares about his students. pretty easy grader, class is fair and you just need to put the work in.

Enthusiastic about teaching, clear and interesting explanation for the economic problem. He says that he doesn't curve which is pretty good because you can get what you deserve finally. Go ahead and pick him.

Very philosophical, lots of why this and how that which gets you to think about why certain economic phenomenon occur. However, he does go on tangents often and reads from slides. Lectures get boring. He is late very often, disorganized and the TA does all the grading. He has POTENTIAL doesn't deliver (which is unfortunately all that matters.)

THIS IS THE MAN. He doesnt want students to just memorize boring stuff. He actually helps students think as economists. He shapes the way we think by asking why, why, why, digging down to the principles of economics by helping us become better thinkers, therefore learning the class material much easily. He deeply cares about his students. Great pf
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Those comments are sick. Professor Elkhouly is so much passionate about teaching. He is a nice person. I think he did a good job in teaching. I pretty enjoy his lecture. It is a pleasant experience.
He made the prestigious nyu econ a community college level. It is such a joke that he is allowed to give and grade any paper here at NYU.

He is a chill person. But he is not a good professor. I do not think he understands economics that well. All of his understanding is qualitative instead of quantitative. I think his style or caliber is simply good enough for high-school level economics or intro level economics, absolutely not for the 200s or 300s. Not sure why NYU hired him?
The definition of academic disaster. He is incapable of basic quantitative reasoning. The exam is like all short answer questions to which he does not even know the correct answers.

Im sure hes a nice guy but he just is not a good lecturer at all. He repeats the same info and kind of just reads the PowerPoint every class. There are also only three grades so no homework and no review for tests he also said he makes up the test so no past exams to use for study as well. Just not a well-structured or organized class

Our class is Urban Economics, and it feels like intro. He reads off of the slideshows and drags it on.. a lot. When I say that, I mean we are on the same slideshow for 3 classes and "review" information for 2/3s of the class. He also did not give us much prep for the exams at all. The class has no homework so we have no clue what to prepare for.

Aharoni is a great professor and if you can take his class you should. His assignments are fairly straightforward and easy and grading is very lenient. It's pretty hard to not get an A. Just make sure to participate in class, especially when there is a guest speaker.

Professor Aharoni is one of the best profs I've ever had. His stories from his time as an Ambassador helped enhance the course material and lectures and make things interesting. Participation is really important, and he heavily values it, so just make sure you speak: he gives ample opportunities. The papers were graded very very easily

Took Idos diplomacy to marketing class and absolutely loved it! The professor brought in guest speakers from the field for each class and was always willing to talk to students in his free time. No major assignments outside of the final paper (mine came out around 25 pages) but its worth it!!! Such amazing experience!

Weird grading criteria. You gotta actively participate in discussions, both comments/opinions AND questions, to receive a decent participation grade. I did, but only received an ok grade. Grade report & comments on all 3 required essays are only available after the course has ended. No immediate feedback on class performance during the semester.

Dr. Navarro is one of the most experienced TAs in the organic chemistry lab. He helped tremendously by measuring out compounds and setting up for us while the lab lecture was going on. If you are unsure about why you received a certain grade on the postlabs, it's very easy to get feedback from him which helps to improve in the class.
Pretty rude
Great professor. He has a great sense of humor which makes class fun. His grading is straightforward and fair. You get exactly what you put in. Take him if you can!

Abel is a very kind person however, I would not reccommend him for orgo lab. There are other instructors who are more lenient with their grading, rarely gives above an 80 on labs, I would take somebody else if you don't want to drag down your lecture grade with lab.

He is a very nice guy. Always helps you set up your stuff and answers your questions very nicely. But he is a VERY harsh grader. Very hard to get higher than an 80 on a lab report, even after checking it with a tutor beforehand. Also he just doesn't give 5/5 for safety ever, no matter what. But he is very very nice during the lab.

Regardless of what I did, he would always give me the lowest grades for technique/safety even when others did things more egregious. Even when I felt good about an experiment I knew I'd be a scapegoat and get the lowest points on safety and technique in the entire section. If he knows you from prior, you're good. Sadly, I didn't have that leeway.

Navarro is a tough but fair grader. For lab he is very helpful and will explain concepts and skills if you ask. He'll help you with the experiments and clearly wants to be there helping you. He's a very good lab ta and I would absolutely take him if he is open. He'll help you learn and make orgo lab a much more enjoyable experience.

Navarro often helped us prepare parts of the lab set ups or distributed materials during the lecture portion of lab so that it was already done by the time we got to working on the experiment, so we could skip that while other sections still had to set up. A bit of a tough grader though and wants very detailed observations in the lab notebook.

Upon taking organic chemistry this semester and finding out Abel had limited reviews, I was skeptical. Turns out, I could not have made a better decision. Not only can you relate to him on a personal basis, but he takes the time to help you understand the material. Grades are respectable when compared to the rest of the lab sections.
He was my lab instructor and was really helpful and will assist you if you need it. Somewhat of a harsh grader but very forgiving in lab.

Absolutely crap professor. Very tough grader. And don't give a damn if you are doing good in class or not. He just wants to leave and earn the money. Don't take the course with this professor because you will was te your money or damage your gpa. Don't believe any of the positive feedbacks. They were probably written by himself
Good prof, but lots of group work. pray you get a good group
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Abelson was great. She is very caring and understanding once you get to know her. The class wasn't hard at all as long as you show up and participate. Most of the grade is based on group presentations that are relatively straightforward.
she focuses on your growth and is invested in your learining One of the best teachers at NYU

She consistently added extra credit assignments which are great for boosting your grade if needed, but she would add a lot and say nothing until the end of class and then get mad when we didn't know what she was talking about. Be prepared for favoritism and for the group presentations. There are about two main group presentations and chap readings

Loveeee her. She can be intimidating at first but such a sweet professor once you get to know her and really cares about her students. If you make an effort and participate you will get a good grade. Take her!!

This class has two big presentations that make up most of your grade, so it may not be great for shy or anxious students. The exams are easy and straightforward. One exam was blue book style, but she was not a harsh grader. There are many extra credit opportunities. Participation matters, and if you are not paying attention, she will call you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor tends to *allegedly* favor the boys. Excessively praises the boys in the class and never compliments the girls. If she thinks you are not paying attention in the class she will try to embarrass you/call you out. Very presentation heavy. Hard grader when it comes to presentations but soft grader when it comes to exams.

Professor Abelson is a very sweet and caring teacher. She definitely pushes you to do things outside the classroom to broaden your knowledge. She is very understanding and is a kind grader. There are lot's of  extra credit opportunities and the midterm and final is mainly based on the end of chapter questions.

She cold calls and REALLY cares about participation. She definitely has a tough love mentality, but she pushes you to grow through it. The course itself is very easy and presentation-based with fair, easy grading. However, she doesn't do much actual teaching—students teach the class through presentations.
"can i kms?" i ask every morning before going to class

If you're taking her class expect to present over and over again. She gives decent feedback on every presentation you do so you actually do learn how to present well. The final presentation is worth more than the actual final so if you aren't good at public speaking good luck. But, if you are it's easy. She's also really nice if you get to know her

Now that I look back, Dr. Anna Abelson was a solid professor. I really hated how she wasn't clear about gradings, homeworks, and class schedules... But I liked how she gave solid feedbacks. Participation matters very much.

Teaches nothing. Many mandatory outside lectures (some are extra credit, some are mandatory). Students do all the chapter presentations and she barely taught anything. Unclear criteria in Hw. Easy exams (she gets most questions from the textbook). Take her if you care about grades but don't if you want to learn something. Two projects.

In the beginning, professor Abelson was a little intimidating and scary. However, once we had more classes, the class environment became more engaging and exciting. She is very passionate about the tourism industry and provided our class with solid networking tactics and useful skills for the real world. I would take another class with her.
Abelson is the best just participate do well on the final project and your good she is extremely accommodating

She is definitely a terrible teacher. Barely teach in class, but rather ask random students questions. We have to learn by ourselves. Also, students are asked to do many presentations. Please avoid her if you can.
She is very nice and straightforward. You have to read skift or other articles everyday to share to classmates and her

reviews.comment: It took me a while to enjoy her class but I improved SOOO MUCH because of her. It is true that she is demanding & WILL push you out of your comfort zone, but you will benefit. I have developed a lot more confidence in presenting & teamwork. Participation is essential for an A (final/midterms don't matter as much). For passionate students, take her!

Professor Abelson is one of the best professors at NYU. She is very knowledgeable about the tourism industry and compels her students to truly educate themselves and be interested in tourism as a whole. reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Abelson is a very well connected professional in the tourism field. The course consists of a group project, mid term and a final. She requires you to participate in class. Every class is discussion heavy. If you don't participate, she will pick on you. Although it's a bit scary, but it's very good practice! Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Easy professor, you can learn a lot in her class. However, she picks on her student for discussion so make sure you pay attention in class and be prepared for each class. The assignments are fun and fair

I really love Professor Anna's course. The course mainly contains a midterm, a final, an individual presentation, and a group project. Instead of merely focusing on slides and textbooks, Professor Anna communicates with students in a caring and relaxing way. She often raises some interesting topics, and the class atmosphere is good!

Skipping class is not worth it in Prof As course. She uses the textbook as a reference but you learn through classroom conversations. By the mid-term youll feel like you have learned nothing, but in reality, you have picked up many concepts of tourism w/ out realizing it. She organizes the course so students will ALWAYS understand basic tourism.

Professor Abelsons course contained 2 tests and a group project. Every week you are assigned chapter readings, but as long as you go to class and participate, then you should have no problem passing. Homework includes, weekly Twitter posts about real-life events. Prof. wants to see all her students succeed and will answer any questions!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class is really easy. A lot of what we learn is common sense. Abelson is a pretty good professor, but make sure you go to class because she will call on you to answer questions if you missed the last class. If you did miss class than make sure you read the textbook.

There is a midterm, final, two presentations, and a research paper. I haven't taken the final yet, but the midterm was not very difficult. Both presentations and the research paper are done as a group project with was awesome and made doing the projects more manageable. Make sure you stay up to date with Tourism current events!

The class isn't set up as a traditional lecture style class, which I really like! Instead of Professor Abelson talking the entire time about the textbook reading, she assigns groups to each chapter and has them present the important details. There is also another presentation/research paper, but it's really interesting and not too difficult.

Good prof, but she means business.  There's not much warm interaction, and she basically only lectures and there's j out much personality. Her exams are pretty hard, but there's a decent curve. Lots of readings, and 3 assignments worth 15% each. Great class to learn hands on experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Abascal is a good professor. However this lecture is 3 hours long once a week and is incredibly hard to sit through. She is good at explaining it though. There are only 3 research projects and a few pop quizzes. She and the TA are lenient graders but it takes a lot of effort on these projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Abascal is a really nice teacher. She illustrates every concept clearly and makes sure everyone get it by using understandable examples. But the lectures are heavily based on readings, be prepared to read a lot. There are 4 quizzes count for 10% of the grade, she won't tell you when to take them, unless you attend every lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Research Methods is a fun class because you get to basically study whatever you're interested in, and she is an intelligent person and good professor. The only issue was that she just wasn't very friendly. She's not the kind of professor you bond with and want to keep in touch with after, but maybe it's because she's new. Not hard class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I would take her again. She just seems a little bored in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Abigail Joseph is a great professor! I felt that she cares about us learning and understanding the content. Her office hours are also really helpful. She really appreciates participation and cultivates a really welcoming class environment. She gave very clear feedback on essays, and if you don't understand something she's willing to elaborate.
kind and understanding, minimal homework. go to conferences with questions if you want guidance on papers.

FYSEM Historical Fictions:

Very nice professor, will definitely make the time for you if you ask for it. Participation is key. She's very nice and sometimes is too nice to criticize your writing. Meet with her often to get the best out of your grade.

Tip: Always choose the creative writing options, they seem to be graded easier.

Professor Joseph is very sweet in class and can be fun to talk to as a person. As an instructor, the class was organized and I knew what I needed to get done; however, she was such a tough grader that it was hard to increase my essay scores. On top of that, she did not really offer office hours and her feedback was not always informative.

She didn't seem that interested in teaching. Caught her on her phone a few times. She gave face level comments on essays, like she had only decided to skim through it. Overall, she was okay, but I would not take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is so sweet and helpful. Every class at the beginning of the week, we have a class debrief and everyone just gets to know each other. She also shares parts of her life too, so you really feel connected to her as well as the course. She gives good feedback on your essays and fosters an environment so everyone can share and voice their opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Abigail assigned readings for almost every class, most of which were interesting and easy. Not much workload. She took a lot of time to give back feedback and corrections, which made it hard to know what she was expecting for the following drafts. I would recommend her if you want to improve your writing and have a tight schedule (minimum workload)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Really wonderful prof. I cannot recommend her enough. Homework is light, and classes are largely discussion based. Only two essay assignments for the semester, and a final project which can be in the form of an essay or video essay. 
For context, I am a generally good writer, which may impact my perception, but you will not regret choosing her!

Abigail is very nice and caring. I had the class online so unfortunately, it was hard to collaborate with my fellow classmates. I could tell she tried her best to make the class entertaining and collaborative, but at times it was a little boring. She always has a clear agenda for class and some of the art we discussed was interesting.

I felt Professor Joseph would grade based on her opinion and not on actual writing techniques or style. If you don't agree with her stance on the readings presented, it's likely you'll get points off for it. Having it online was even worse as there was little effort to push collaboration in our class.

She's always cheerful and patient despite how awkwardly quiet the class can be. For EXPOS: Art in the World, Class material is pretty straightforward. Homework, for the most part, was pretty light and not graded. As long as you wrote something you're good. She gives good feedback, and as long as you follow it you can get a decent grade.

She's very knowledgeable and tries to make the class interesting. If you have a class that doesn't participate the class will be extremely boring. Despite being a tough grader, she gives decent feedback.

inspirational, knowledgeable professor; chooses thought-provoking texts and makes a required writing class fun; takes into account your effort and grades fairly, but is tougher than other class profs; only 3 short readings/essays; always available; truly cares about your ideas and subsequent classwork; wonderful prof choice for 'writing the essay'

Professor Joseph is pretty difficult, However, she appreciates the effort you put in so if you sign up for her open hours and go prepared, she will give very good feedback and will point things out to fix. She is a very fair grader, but a critical one as well because she seems to have very high standards. Just work really hard

She's very intelligent and tries to make a pretty boring mandatory class interesting. However, her feedback on essays is very lacking. If she says you need to improve something, it doesn't mean that you need to tweak it, it means you have to spend a solid hour plus reworking the idea. Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: It's a difficult, mandatory class for most freshmen, but Abigail definitively makes this notorious requirement much more bearable and interesting! Possible reading materials are especially eclectic, including both influential, classic texts by "dead white males" and lots of modern, progressive, and insightful texts by writers of all kinds.

This is your typical writing course so there is going to be quite a bit of essay writing. However, Abigail is extremely helpful with her writing conferences and gives you good ideas and helps you revise your rough draft. She's respected a lot and you can tell she's very intelligent.

I really enjoyed my semester with Professor Joseph. She made class interesting, and she made a required course a little more bearable. The content is still difficult. There's really no getting around that. But Professor Joseph uses unique and interesting examples in class, and her office hours are open to ask for assistance.
She actually gives less homework as compared to other WTE professors. She's not super clear but if you approach her, she's definitely willing to sit down and discuss your essay her.
I think she's a good professor being forced to teach a very annoying, standard, mandatory class.  I'm sure she would be an even better professor if she taught a better, more interesting class.
I really like Abigail. She's super smart. People who don't like her tend not to be.

She's very sweet, nice and approachable. She tries to get the class talking by asking questions. If your class isn't that involved is going to be quiet and boring. Her assignments/homework aren't that bad but for your main progression essays her feedback is horrible and even the corrections she does give aren't very clear, making it hard to do well

she is not very helpful and only agrees with everything that people say instead of adding anything further. moves her hands too much. it gets annoying sometimes. she lacks clarity in her assignments and lessons. have a great semester (sarcastic) i definitely would not recommend her

Class wasn't very stimulating and very lecture heavy. Did not provide adequate feedback. Concepts were not explained thoroughly and I did not take away anything from the course. Additionally, expect professor to say one thing and end up wanting something completely different. Definitely had favorites as well so try hard to get on good side.

Bearable but really boring. Teacher is nice and helpful but that is the best thing about the class. The material is very surface level and if you have done any internship in retail or fashion etc I do not recommend this class as the material covered would not get you past day 1

Honestly one of my favorite professors I have taken at Stern. I learned SO much from her and from the course content of Retail Strategy. Everything I learned directly applied to my job in makeup retail and clarified and taught me so much. She is so kind and engaging and everyone in the class wants to impress her. TAKE HER!

The best there is. So lenient and will always help you the best she can. S&S has a lot of rules and restrictions, but you can get away with a lot with Gay -- she will help you find ways to execute your story, to hell with the rules if need be. She really cares about all her students and you can feel it. Hilarious too.
Picks favorites

Course requires 8h+ attendance/day&16h+/week. I attended all shooting sessions&carefully completed all assignments. I didn't attend some morning lectures because the prof wasn't really doing anything. Everyone is asleep or working on their own stuff. I got C- w no further negotiation. Course length doesn't make sense &people need sleep to survive.

She is a Dynamic Life Long Learner! Prolific Writer, Story Teller, Director, Producer, Filmmaker & Editor, dedicated to the Performing Art's.

I became a SAG/AFTRA Member in 1978.

I was very Blessed to be Cast as the Lead in her Film "Fragrance" at UCLA! in 1981!

Great Cast and her attention to detail was above and beyond My expectations!

Whether you are inexperienced or experienced, Gay is the professor for you. She will be there if you have difficulty understanding the tools, she will take care of you if you are overwhelmed or stressed, and she makes a  difficult, 7-hour twice-a-week class feel easy and fly by. I never had a more sweet and understanding professor.

Gay is a real gem. I strongly recommend you take her for studio. Especially during pandemic times, she is so flexible and kind. She is more than willing to talk with you outside of class either about your work or about school/life in general.

If you want a teacher who genuinely cares about her students, take her class. Extremely caring and kind and fosters an atmosphere that makes even the least enthusiastic kids want to show up first to class. An overall joy to be around. If you get a chance to take her class, you're beyond lucky.

Gay was there for our class for the entire semester. She was available to contact at all times, which is great when you're trying to make a student film. She'll be straightforward with you about your production and will do everything in her power to help you make your film.

Gay really knows her stuff when it comes to pre-production. The pre-production colloquium I took was really easy, since it was pass-fail, but Gay was determined to teach us as much as possible and not waste class time. We watched a lot of student short films and she told us about the flaws and successes in each production.

I had Gay for Intermediate Narrative production and now she is my go-to advisor for everything. She is so awesome and so nice and she seems to know a bit about everything. She is genuinely one of the most caring professors I have ever had in my entire NYU experience.

Professor Abel-Bey is one of the best teachers you'll ever have at NYU Tisch.  She truly cares about her students and she will help you anyway she can to achieve what you want with your films. I totally recommend her class!

Very knowledgable, but needs to make her lectures more interesting. Pre-Production Colloquium needs to be revamped in general (we spent two classes watching a doc by a director who was suppose to come to talk to us but never did).  She's approachable though and if you have a question about production in general she will give you a thorough answer.
Just a great lady.  Took her for many more classes.  Very accessible and friendly.  Do the work and she'll appreciate it and be helpful with it.  Easy grader as well.

Although the professor puts focus mostly on presentations and interrupts you during the presentation to ask questions, only ONE thing matters. Your participation and your confidence!!! It is very crucial for you to be always ready to answer the questions asked by the professor and the participation is mostly not voluntary.
clearly not what I expected and.. honestly he does not really teach anything. you just have to study on your own.

Professor Abdulhaqq is a very great teacher. He focuses on using real life examples in order to teach versus just reading out of a textbook. There are group presentations almost every week, but don't let that intimidate you. I learned a lot from this class!

I cannot recall a more apathetic, boring, or incompetent professor in recent memory. Acevedo does not care about her students' physical or mental health and does not care about students' accommodations/disabilities. Her slides plagiarize the textbook and her course has no structure. Her study guides are full of irrelevant information, avoid!!!

read off slides every lecture, never able to answer student questions. rarely tested on general concepts from class but useless specific information that would be like in a small corner of the slide that she never addressed. she would put stuff on the test that wasnt on slides, then would claim that she talked about it in lecture when she didnt.
Questions went unanswered. This was my most anticipated class of my undergrad career and I wish I had a professor that simply knew more about it and didn't just read off the slides.

didn't like in the beginning but warmed up to class and teaching style. recommend taking notes on the physical slides, bc the slides tend to not make so much sense so you need to elaborate on them based on what she says in class. a bit difficult but not impossible. textbook helps. class ended up being really really interesting in terms of material
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I loved this course - I learned a lot about linguistics. The most important thing for students to understand is that they need to come to class prepared to discuss all the questions and thoughts that came up for them in the readings. Class is what students make it - Professor Achino-Loeb is there to guide students' self-generated conversation.

The class is pretty straight-forward, in that there is a reading each week and discussion during the class. The professor gives feedback on everything, though the weekly assignments are primarily to show you read the material. She guides the discussion but for the most part the in-class conversation is dominated by students. Overall, I enjoyed it.

I had a really great experience in her class. She opened my eyes to a lot of aspects of language and globalization that most people don't usually consider. The readings were all great, and she was extremely passionate about the subject. She gave a typed page of her comments back for every essay, and her discussions were always thought-provoking.

I would never suggest this professor to anyone. She demands that we lead the class discussion, but as soon as someone tries to bring up a topic, she'll cut them off and go on her own tangent. If she doesn't agree with your argument, then it's wrong. Her feedback is completely unhelpful and often confusing, and her essay prompts are pointless.
Very helpful, willing to discuss papers. She is extremely knowledgable and presents interesting ideas in the class.
I learned a lot from this class regarding the politicization of language around the globe. Lectures and readings were interesting and informative, and good feedback was provided.

She was always willing to help.I found her full-page typed comments with essay grades the most thorough I ever received from a prof. Class dialogue was consistently high-level, and the curriculum was definitely interdisciplinary (including films). Started course with no knowledge of linguistics but ended up using class material in my colloquium.

The course Prof. Achino-Loeb taught has honestly become an integral part of my perception of reality as a whole. I often cite the course text, which she wrote. And because of how understanding Prof. Achino-Loeb was, I earned the appropriate credits needed to graduate after passing my colloquium.
The interdisciplinary ideas that Prof. Achino-Loeb presents are on the cutting edge of the field

Has many requirements that are not listed on the syllabus, requires students to meet as a group for NON-GRADED work, seemingly unable to make efficient use of technology (cannot print PDFs, does not HAVE blackboard for the class, emails to "group leaders" every week instead of email the class). Moody grader.

Unclear Professor. Class goes around in circles, so she acts as if there is a distinct answer to the class. Favorites are pretty clear in the class. Not available for most of the week to talk bc she isn't a full-time prof. Very late with grading. Ultimately, I hate her atm.

The entire grade is basically 3 assignments (none of which I have gotten grades back for even though the class finished last week). There are many readings but she barely touches on them in class so no one ever did them and the entire 3 hour class was just her talking to a wall. It was pretty easy but not stimulating at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took Gizem for IAD this summer. She clearly cares about students and would go above and beyond to inspire them. Readings were fun and heavy, but the discussions under her lectures made my efforts worthwhile. She is also super accessible and is always willing to stay around for a little while after class for questions. Take her if you can!

Def one of the best profs I've had here, incredibly accommodating and accessible, if you talk to her she's always willing to help. Final grade was based on three things, participation and a 2 page research proposal each 30% and the final 10 page paper was 40%, but as long as you skim the readings and actively participate in lectures you'll be fine.

Gizem is a great professor and person and cares about her students. The class was very interesting and she fosters an environment for open discussion. There is a good amount of reading and there aren't many assignments you are graded on
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kindness professor ever!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took her Foreign Aid & Development in the summer. Caring Professor - would go the extra mile to make sure students are doing well in the class. Straightforward assignments (4 short papers in total). As long as you do the readings, actively participate in discussions, and go to office hours, youll do great in the class.

Interesting reading selections but lectures are dry. Graded by a few things (1 short paper + final exams: 3 short essays). Doesnt really provide feedback on your work. Final exam questions are kinda weird and poorly phrased. But shes a nice lady, very reachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Acikgoz for POL-UA 994 Revolutions during Summer Session I. She is truly nothing short of a gem! She is incredibly kind and so knowledgeable! The class was ready reading heavy and discussion based so it was pretty nice + relaxed. Make sure to utilize her office hours when it comes to the papers (proposal + finals) and you'll be fine.

She was amazing - all you really needed to do was complete the readings, and meet with her as much as possible about your essays (midterm and final). She will tell you exactly what she wants for your essays, you just need to follow her instructions. Prompts are straightforward and the most simple answers, as long as your sources are right, will ace
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Gizem is wonderful. I've never felt I was great at math, but I did well in this class. Lectures were once a week and long, so I had to force myself to focus, but if you do, she'll give you homework hints. She really wants her students to succeed. Take her class!

Great class if you need to fulfill a math requirement or you want to take a politics course. If you took AP Stats, do not bother showing up to class. The lectures online will guide you through the homework and you can independently study for the exams. The professor is very kind and helpful if you need assistance.

Gizem is an absolute goddess. I'm an IR major and was worried that the QR would hurt my gpa standing. I had to work extremely hard and devote some effort, but I ended up doing well. She is always there for office hrs, and ultimately wants everyone to do well. Midterm and final are easy if you spend time on hw (25% of grade). Recitation  MANDATORY!

I am NOT  politics student. I took this class to fulfill my QR requirement. As a non- math person, this class was okay. Lectures are insanely boring but you don't have to attend since she posts her powerpoints.  You CANNOT miss recitations though.  Overall, an okay course. Not bad if you have to take it.
Best professor at nyu, period.
A total sweetheart. Really enjoy the class and her dedication to her students is amazing. Take her.
Helpful, caring, and creative. Every class is a blast.

BE CAREFUL! The exams were clear and straightforward but the homework's and lab projects are graded quite harsh. The home works are nitpicked to an insane degree, especially if you have Mai as a TA. It was clear she enjoyed taking points off.  The lab project is said to not hurt your grade and has a high minimum grade. All lies.

Gizem is the best professor at NYU!  She will literally get to know everyone's name in a class of 100+ She makes everything clear and relevant.  The class is amazing, homeworks are easy and worth a big chunk of your grade which is great.  You can't help but love the class and her daily enthusiasm; and I got an A which is very very achievable

Wonderful teacher. Took her for Quantitative methods in Political Science, MUST GO TO recitation because you work on a Stata project. She's very clear and doesn't try to trick you on the midterm and final although you have to study really hard. Got an A so it's doable

Gizem is absolutely wonderful. I'm a politics major that isn't great at math as a general rule, but I looked forward to her class every day. She is SO sweet, SO helpful, and will do whatever it takes to help each student. LOVED her. Definitely take this class.
Whether you are a politics major or a IR hopeful, take this class! Her lectures are clear, precise with a reasonable amount of work. Learning to use Stata is also a plus.
Amazing. So dedicated to her students.

BEST, SWEETEST and KINDEST prof at nyu period. Will stay hours beyond her office hours to help students, emails beyond 12 AM, and so passionate about each student not failing. This class is basic stat for pol sci but its worth taking this class just for her. Also Michael is awesome and knowledgeable. Everyone will agree...she deserves a a prize

The best person in the world. Will be there for you always and will make every class so much fun even though its math. Exams are easy and final project sounds intimidating but you do it on recitation. Take Michael as a TA!
Hands down the absolute best professor at NYU. She's super nice, approachable and really wants everyone to do well. I'm not interested in statistics, but this was my favorite class because of her.

Very knowledgeable and accessible outside class. In lecture, he often speaks quietly and the pacing can be slow, so it's easy to lose focus—sitting close and taking notes helped. Homework is demanding. You'll learn a lot of linguistics and his teaching methods are strong. Grading felt fair; there's one curved midterm and a significant project.
GOAT Professor, must take his NLP course

Would Recommend taking his NLP.
Somewhat flexible about grading, and understand how import it is for us. HE IS ON OUR SIDE!
Exams are easy, almost unchanged for years, but it covers a lot. REMEMBER TO SHOW YOUR WORK!!!
Lecture is heavy, just feed it to GPT for better understand.
As long as you pay some attention to it, this course is Easy A

The lectures are painfully boring and monotone but the professor is very kind and caring. If you're looking for a modern NLP course this is not it (it's more computational linguistics than anything related to AI/LLMs). Easy HW, 1 midterm, and no final exam, just a final group project. However, disorganized and unclear requirements.

Okay yes the lectures are not good (at all) but you'll be fine: 5 coding assignments that are honestly more annoying and tedious than they are hard, 3 short answer homework assignments, no quizzes, one midterm and a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Reads the slides on the board in monotone voice, hard to keep up with.
Some of the least engaging lectures I've ever experienced. I found it nearly impossible to pay attention, ended up figuring out most of the material on my own time outside of class.

All he cares about is linguistics and shows no understanding for anything computer related. Deadlines are constantly delayed, nothing gets graded except for the midterm. During the midterm, I saw majority of the class was sitting in the back taking pictures of the test and asking ChatGPT as I was leaving the room. Don't waste your time and money.

The professor was excellent, delivering lessons that aligned with NYU's high academic standards. The course was challenging but manageable with consistent effort. The teaching style encouraged deep understanding, making the hard work worthwhile. Overall, a rewarding experience for those ready to put in the time and effort.

Okay, this class is very easy to fall behind and get lost in the material. The only way you can succeed in this class is if you actually know how to code in Python and have been doing so for years. Meyers is a very nice guy, very chill, and sometimes funny but you will find yourself disliking the class. Very hard and overwhelming midterm :/

you don't learn anything from lectures, after the first week only 1/3 of the class showed up. professor meyers always seemed confused and I learned everything on my own. compared to other teachers for this class, his homeworks and midterms were unnecessarily long and complicated. i wouldn't take this teacher

Homework is like 50% of your grade. This class is a free A. He sucks at lecturing so you can just dip after taking attendance and read the slides on your own time since that's what he does anyways. I can barely hear him. He gives us ~45 min each class to do hw and ask the TA any questions. The slides have hints to hw but hw is still time consuming
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Sure he is open and very flexible with deadlines, BUT even with prior python knowledge, his "reading off slides" type of monotone lectures became intolerable and I lost track after midterms.
I basically had to self-teach everything.

I completely understand that he might be a bit difficult for people who haven't coded before. But his homework policy is so lenient that I wish blessings on him and his family. The midterm was a bit more difficult than I expected but the homeworks more than prepare you for it. This class is chill and he is pretty decent in lecture. goated prof frfr
not a very good preofessor just reads his slides and is slow with reading. id ont think he understands how to explain to beginners who have never coded before
Great class.  Take him

The course focuses on the fundamental aspects of NLP, emphasizing linguistics rather than modern models like BERT or GPT. The professor is genuinely nice, very responsive to emails, and always willing to help students. Additionally, there are no strict deadlines for assignments, allowing you to manage your time effectively.

I know a lot of students came to this class expecting him to teach some transformer or gpt stuff. No, everything you will see is like 20 years ago. Also he's lectures are so boring, I stopped attending after midterm

absolutely awful lecturer. basically just reads off his incomprehensible slides at lightning speed and calls it a day. i'm sure he is an amazingly smart person but he seems to have no interest in teaching. if i had known he would be this terrible of a presenter i would not have taken his course

prof meyers is really smart and willing to help his students. HW is mostly programming, and i am not the best programmer so they were really difficult for me. it was a great experience to explore my interests in NLP. however if ur not into NLP this class will be extremely boring. i feel like i did below avg and still got a B so he curves generously

Dont take him if you have no programming experience. He can't teach. Teach yourself python and THEN take his class bc he will just confuse you and you won't learn basics from him. He is a nice guy though. Kinda quiet and awk but nice and approachable.

The lecture slides are clear and shown in detail. The group project was given half a semester to accomplish. Choose his course if you need some experience on research. Btw the midterm is easy to prepare if you understand the slides well.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Best professor ever! You'll learn a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guy can't teach for his life. Do not take this class if you actually only have limited computer science experience. The only people who will do well in his class are people who already know how to code and have been coding since middle school. He knows his stuff but he absolutely cannot teach anything.
The professor is caring but his lectures are dry. Homeworks and exams are mostly relatively easy.
Lectures are very dry as he just mostly reads off the slides . Final Project specifications really unclear and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
NLP is not a hard class, but you probably aren't learning much. 
There's a midterm but no final, so expect the second half of the semester to be very filler/slow. 
There is a final project though and its open-ended but most options are tough.
He spends lots of lectures reading off presentations. Lectures are recorded though.

Though Professor Meyers is lenient with due dates and exam policy, he's disorganized and unclear in delivering lectures and giving homework instructions. He assigns 15 mins in lectures for us to work on homework problems, which is inefficient since these problems may take several hours. He always gives irrelevant answers to students' questions.

This guy is literally the worst professor I've ever had at NYU. Firstly he is extremely unclear about his grading policies. He also refused to give a student an A when they've achieved beyond the normal A's cutoff for CS major. Totally unreasonable. The fact that his lectures are super boring makes it an extra drawback. Avoid him at all cost.

Lectures are confusing so you should only take it if you're prepared to spend a lot of time in office hours. Each homework took an entire day to complete but he is lenient with due dates. Instead of a final exam there's a group project which seems nice except you have to write a 6-10 pg research paper and the requirements are unclear.

Very interesting lessons, with amazing and interactive guest speakers! He's super nice and caring and easy to talk to. Though the grading on the midterms and final was a bit ehh, super specific for no reason. Just be sure to REALLY study.

reviews.comment: Professor Brown was great. He clearly cares about the topic he teaches and makes complex topics easier to understand. The midterm and final were online, in class, in a lockdown browser (but since we had to write a lot, it made it easier). You don't have to read the books to write the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: he was good, a little strict but i really liked this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: honestly really chill class, engaging and funny professor, interesting subject, just study the few days leading up to the exam and it will work. do need to study tho

Need to read 2 books per semester. Lots of papers and weekly readings (that you don't have to do). But still feels like A LOT for the Cams class. Attendance to lectures is also mandatory. But really nice guy and cares a lot about what he's teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: It is 100% lectures with quizzes, essays, and exams. Dr. Brown is not accessible outside of class. You can only get help from the TA, but even the TA will say that he is not available. He grades ambigously and I had to debate grades for every project.

He's a little strict but it's very obvious this is a class that matters a lot to him. In a few classes he's talked about his own experience working with traumatized children. I felt bad because barely anyone participated. His assignments are also writing-heavy but on really fascinating books! His midterm was difficult for me but his final was easy!

Dr. Brown is a caring professor who is highly respected in his field. He's accessible outside of class and gives excellent career advice/guidance. Class grade was determined by weekly (~10 MCQs) quizzes, three papers, two in-class book club assignments, and two exams (midterm and final). Follow study guide because you will be tested on specifics.

He's a funny guy who is pretty understanding. The grading can be a little bit harsh sometimes, but not too bad. You should get a good grade if you pay attention. The class is pretty easy as long as you do the readings and pay attention in class. I 100% recommend it if you are interested in childhood trauma studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I recommend this class! Just study and read carefully.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Discussion post required for weekly readings, but are only a paragraph or so and can be easily done without having to read everything thoroughly. 2 exams that are specific, but as long as you study the slides you'll be fine. Final project was very open-ended. Takes a while to give back midterm grades. Nice, funny guy.

IMO, Prof Brown does way too much for a CAMS class. He meticulously keeps record of attendance, takes months to grade the midterm exam, and expects a lot from students. However, it's not a hard class. Readings are important, but aren't that bad. Participation is also quite important, and he locks discussion posts after the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Brown is a nice and kind person. However, his lectures are very bland, despite the fact that the course material is interesting. He responds to emails super fast. The assigned readings are very inspiring.

Professor Brown is an amazing professor and person. He is caring for what he does and for everyone. Class was easy with a few papers, weekly online quizzes, group assignments, a take-home midterm, and an in-person final (all very easy). The content is interesting and important. I genuinely loved the class and learned a lot.

Adam was my favorite professor I've had as an undergrad (coming from a senior). His trauma class was taught perfectly. He gave clear warnings at the beginning of lectures and went over material thoroughly and was always open to answering questions. Definitely take this class if you are interested in PTSD and CPTSD. Could not recommend more!

Great class. Truly learned a lot. I'd encourage every person to take this class with Brown. If you want an A, do the readings. Don't just skim, actually read them, annotate and try to absorb the information. This helps when completing the weekly quizzes and on exams. Also reviewing the slides. Class is packed with valuable information and stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Just don't take LOVE ACTUALLY. This class asks you to read over 200 pages of a book each week and the exam question is very very detailed (like one sentence in one book). Prof. Adam is great. I give him three stars because he is very hard to find outside the classroom. If you email him, he will only cc ta and my ta is very slow.

He's great! I took his Trauma class, and he managed to make long lectures really interesting and engaging. He uses a variety of powerpoints, videos, and discussions to keep us all awake and listening. The papers aren't difficult, and the exams are easy as long as you've been paying attention in class and reading the assigned articles.

A great professor who makes long lectures engaging through the use of breaks, powerpoints, videos, and more. Has book clubs throughout the course to connect the topic to modern adaptation. Encourages discussion and question asking even with over 100 students. Is an easy grader for assignments, but exams are challenging and very detailed. Study.

TAKE THIS CLASS! Adam is clear about what you're graded on and deadlines are given at the beginning. Midterm/Final study guides were extremely helpful. Group project is not as intimidating as it seems. Child trauma is a heavy subject. If you can't handle it, would not recommend BUT Adam does a good job of keeping things light (within reason).
Turn in your work on time and you'll be fine. Lots of reading but quizzes are easy. Brown is really chill and incredibly knowledgeable in his field.
When the Nightmare is Real/child trauma psych. Really interesting class, used visuals and great examples to make it all very comprehensible. Readings were kind of long, but you can just skim them.

Professor Roddy is a fantastic lecturer and a caring mentor. The criteria for grading was clear and always consistent. Besides attendance, homework is graded generously and the final project is really what determines your class grade. He makes intimidating material very easy to understand and he's very funny!

Professor Roddy is awesome! I knew nothing about coding at first and struggled, but he was always patient and willing to explain things multiple times. He's approachable outside of class, genuinely wants to help students, grades fairly, and has a great sense of humor with lots of stories. Take him !
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Such a fun class! I was delighted every day that I stepped foot into this lecture. Truly you must take him as a professor if you want the true NYU experience. He is also HILARIOUSSSS and a joy to be around and takes the content seriously, but makes everything engaging for his students. If he taught all classes at NYU, I would be there immediately.

Take him! Even for people who don't have interest in computer programming or writing codes like me learned a lot. He is funny, having clear ideas not to lower down grades but teach some real stuff. No tests, but assignment weekly+final pre/paper. Not too much workload, no pressure. Just do your work and show up, the TA is awesome.

Amazing professor, first time I felt very engaged in the class during my time at NYU. There is a lot of readings and material from lecture you need to study, but besides that the class is a breeze. Def take!

PROF COX IS AWESOMEEE. Best core class I have ever taken. The material is so interesting and she truly cares about students beyond class. She makes an effort to go outside the classroom and take us to see dance. She prioritizes our own mental health and wellbeing as well! Prof Cox is literally the best professor you could ask for!

Had her for Anthro of Black Dance. The course is reading-heavy, but they're not difficult and are summarized in recitations. Her lectures seemed to be a little all over the place at times. I got lost at times, but I feel like the midterm and final are not difficult if you pay attention most of the time in class.
Prof Cox is very passionate and knowledgable about what she teaches and makes the lectures highly engaging. Its not difficult to do well in this class, just engage with the material well!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Usually I don't trust bad reviews on here, but she is really not a good professor. Not necessarily difficult to do well, but lectures are tedious and I didn't learn anything new about the constitution. Slow to grade, unclear on expectations, very disorganized. Avoid if you can!
She uses the Socratic method for teaching and bases her tests off of them, which I believe to be ineffective for a class with around 100 people in it. I cannot recommend her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my favorite class I've taken at NYU! It's not a class for people who want to zone off and still do well and participation is important. The class discussions and activities, the cases she chooses, and the points she raises are all insightful and engaging. The exams are not that difficult as long as you study and pay attention in class.
worst prof ever.

I had a really great semester taking Prof Garcia's SCOTUS class. Her grading is fair and she is open to criticism. I actually liked the Socratic method, and thought it was cool to hear from my peers. She is clearly very intelligent and cares a lot about her students. If you go to class and pay attention, you will get the A! Would recommend to all!

Prof as a person seems nice and smart but I did not like her style of teaching. "Lectures" are just conversation with the few loud people in class (bc of so-called socratic method), and I'm not paying 90k tuition because I care about their opinions. Not a fan of grading system: 30% Midterm 1, 30% Midterm 2, 40% Final. TAs disorganized & grade slow.

very nice and passionate about the class, but you have to attend lectures because there is no other component of the class used on exams. the tests are barely difficult if you study. i'm gonna miss her tbh
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors of all time. Don't listen to the other reviews - if you don't show up to class you will be cooked. Professor Garcia is old school, meaning she puts in a lot of weight on those who show up and participate. If you can't grasp this course I would seriously consider choosing a different path other than pre-law.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really not as bad as the reviews say lol. she basically tells u in class everything that is on the exams. exams r hard, but if you listen to what she says to study then you'll do good. it also depends on the TA that grades it. she gives XC at the end, it helps a lot. advice: ignore what others are studying and only study what she says. take notes!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She never lectured, was unorganized, and didn't seem to care about her students at all. Your grade is made up of all tests, and the grading seems arbitrary. There is no incentive to go to class because you never learn anything, yet the grading is harsh. She also only picked on the guys to speak in a class full of women. Do not take this class.

The material itself was not hard, but classes were largely usless- as there was no productive instruction or lecturing. I ended up not going to class after the first month except for exams and still scored high enough to get an A through self studying. TA's were unorganized and slow with grading- it took a month to get an exam back

Awful teacher who turned class into an unproductive conversation between the five most talkative students under the guise of the Socratic method. If you can teach yourself the material, you might like this class since I skipped 5-6 times and still got an A. Idk why others are talking about the TAs since we never really got to know them at all.

Grade is made up of three exams, and grading was very dependent on your TA (one only gave out B's, the other always gave out A+'s). Garcia is clearly knowledgeable and wants everyone to succeed but teaches unconventionally. To her credit, she was very adaptable like she gave us 20% worth of extra credit to compensate for TA grading

Class was a mess- no guidelines and the use of the Socratic method meant no actual lecturing was done- leading to little learning during class itself. The grading was harsh as well- the entire grade was based off of 3 exams with no proper way to access your progress throughout the course- do not take!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She seems nice and very intelligent, but is just terrible at "lecturing," if you can even call it that. The sole use of the Socratic method is infuriating, especially when 100+ people can't predict what she wants the class to say.

Clearly a smart person however does not know how to properly run a class. Extremely disorganized and graded purely on three tests that you will have no idea how they are graded or what she is looking for. Lectures are sometimes engaging but mostly bad and she makes students feel stupid when they speak in class. TA's particularly bad in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is extraordinarily disorganized and has no leniency whatsoever. The only grades in this class are three exams (Test 1: 30%, Test 2: 30%, Final Exam: 40%). There are heaps of reading assigned, no test outlines given, inaccessible office hours, and a lack of clarity throughout the course. Trust me. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's nice but a horrible lecturer
easy grader and nice person, but this is the most boring class i've ever taken

Horrible lecturer for when she does actually get around to it. Likes to pose questions to class, even though it is far too big for that type of teaching to be helpful. When she does ask you a question, constantly cuts you off; she should've just kept speaking anyway. Ridiculous amount of reading with very little of it actually applying. Do not take
Extremely disorganized and a terrible lecturer. The tests and quizzes aren't too difficult.

About 8 reading assessments (online, open book), midterm and final w/ study guide. This course was fairly simple/easy to complete. It kind of felt like APUSH all over again, but with questionable debates amongst classmates. The guidelines for exams/structure of course changed because she listened to feedback, but hard to keep up with at times!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Takes so long to grade stuff. Literally had to wait almost 3 weeks for ms girl to post the grades. Bores you to death with her lectures
Professor Cournane excels in making complex theories understandable and engaging. Her classes are fun, filled with activities that help you understand otherwise dry materials.

I took this class she taught with McElree and it was very unenjoyable. Prof C is a great lecturer and really knows what she is talking about, however, in conjunction with the poorly teaching from the other professor as well as the general lack of time management, I do not recommend taking P27. I would, however, take a class just taught by Prof C.

Professor Ailis is so kind, knowledgeable, and interesting! You can ask/email her about anything and she'll respond. Recitations prepare you very well for the weekly quizzes and the final project at the end.

I took her Language and Mind class online. It can be a bit boring and hard to follow for non-linguistic majors or if you're not particularly interested in the subject, but she was a good lecturer and her class was easy enough to follow. She clearly knows a lot about her field.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you are taking First Lang. Acq. as a linguistics major then this class will be a breeze. There are 2 hws, a midterm, a final and a project. Exams are fair. The project isn't horrible. There are weekly readings, but Ailis lectures almost directly from the book so you don't have to do them. She's very smart, nice, and approachable. Loves questions

First Lang Acq was a really fun class. If you're a linguistics major, you get some extra room to breathe b/c the psych people have to learn IPA stuff and what morphemes are and w/e. I would have liked more assignments and more feedback, but it was a solid class. The midterm was very short and very specific, but the final grade composition is good.

Ailis is a great teacher! She made all classes interesting and engaging. It was her first time teaching at NYU and she did a great job. Though I believe this class is an easy A, you need to work hard for your grade. There is no midterm. However, be ready for a final exam, a short paper, seven online quizzes, and two short assignments. Great class!

She's very nice & genuine. If you write about something that is important and meaningful and is compatible with the content it's an easy A. Only two papers and a presentation for the entire semester... but a LOT of readings. She goes through each reading during class so I wouldn't say it's completely necessary, but participation helps boost grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She gives 100 pages to read each week with an optional extra 100 pages that are not optional at all, dont let the optional fool you. All of this doesnt even matter to her, she chose your grade the moment you stepped in her class and will grade you accordingly. She does not like minorities and people who speak an opinion opposing hers. Dont take
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, extremely knowledgeable, learned a lot from this class.

What an incredible professor! Rita explained psycholinguistics to the class in ONE lecture, and before that I wasted a whole semester trying to understand it in Brian McElree's class. That said, she's a great teacher. What an asset to NYU.Very fun class, lots of reading, but you'll learn tons. One of the best psych class I took @ NYU! I miss her!

She does want her students to think, yet she stifles what everyone has to say with some research that SHE has conducted already.(sometimes missing your point completely) She has a huge ego. I certainly wanted to learn and work and didn't expect an easy A, but she was very reluctant to help and listen. She has biases towards some students. MusicPsyc

I loved this Professor. The students that complain about her are most likely "idiots" just because she wants her students to "think" she is hailed as this horrible professor. I really enjoyed her class and I learned a great deal. Take this class if you are not afraid of learning by working and are not in it for an easy A.

She is a great person, but lectures are boring, and there's no space for debating philosophical topics; the focus is on how they are argued. I am a good writer and have all A's in humanities classes. Beware
really good prof, lectures entertaining even if material is dense and difficult. pretty easy grading, exams were not too hard either. readings can be skipped, lectures provide what you need
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Aitken is great! SO sweet and always accessible for help. Deadlines are pretty fixed but imo, they're super generous so even if you can't get an extension you'll still probably finish on time. I was a bit scared to take the class bc she was a new teacher without a rep, but I am so glad I decided to take it bc she is such a gem
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: prof aitken is really great! granted how the thick material and readings are, she makes it very comprehendible. super open to help, office hours were always so helpful. lectures were sometimes really hard to stay engaged in, but i think thats just a product of zoom. she generally made philosophy soooo much less daunting, and workload wasnt crazy

What a grumpy old man!  He's so mean and bitter all of the time I actually began to dread class in preparation for what mean things he would say to me. However, he did improve my Spanish skills and understanding immensely. He was very smart and had a good sense of humor.  He really made Spanish class an awful experience three times a week.
Terrible professor, one of the worst I've ever had. I hated going to class every single day.

Native spanish speaker, but not at all helpful. He came to class sick and grumpy when he came at all. I took Adv. Grammer and Comp. from him, and basically had to learn the material from the book. The class was a disaster
Always late, never organized, frequently incomprehensible.  He has managed to offend, annoy or scare almost every student in the class.

I think few people realize that his class is supposed to separate the wheat from the chaff. He expects a little discipline, to be sure, but my grammar was pretty much flawless by the end of the semester. An A is not impossible if you make an effort.

The absolute worst professor I hope to have in my college experience. Often came to class late, impossible to understand, often canceled or rescheduled class, ridiculed students, didn't explain or answer questions. One of the reasons I am not studying spanish anymore. He said he was retiring at the end of last fall, but apparently he's back. beware

Prof. Aiello is a terrible professor.  He is probably the worst professor in the Spanish department because there are some good ones.  The best advice I can give to a student who is taking Spanish is to never take a class with Prof. Aiello.
I didn't know Satan taught Spanish...
One of the worst teachers I know.  He is extremely unorganized and should get it together!  He needs some happiness in his life; he seems so miserable.

While Professor Aiello may seem intimidating in class, meeting with him in person is much different.  He's very kind and helpful and wants you to do well in the course.  The workload is heavy, but you can get by without doing an exercise or two.  Focus on the papers and tests is necessary to do well

He has good days and bad days.  He's definitely a moody person, but he's good at teaching and really knows a lot.  I was lazy and never came to class with the exercises done and he never cared.  He even gave me chances to turn stuff in late.
Professor Aiello was extremely helpful and hilarious.  He was extremely knowledgeable and his mood swings aren't that bad.  He's very nice especially during office hours, very hospitable.
Though at times quite serious, Prof. Aiello is a very knowledgable guy and as long as you do the work he is actually usually pretty hilarious and likeable.
professor aiello is very smart and very fair. as long as you make an effort and participate, he will reciprocate.
don't take any classes with him!!  he's impossible to understand, and very moody, and class is not fun at all.

class involves 4 exams that involve the readings, so get ready to MEMORIZE. she does put a lot of resources on brightspace on what you actually need to know, so lecture is kind of just repeating that. overall nice lady and did offer to help people in separate office hours just for exams.

She's super interactive and passionate but she repeats herself and rambles a lot. No power points, just lectures and readings. Your grade is based only on 4 exams, making this a hard class if you don't test well. Made tests purposefully hard, but you receive exam prompts a week in advance to prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
LOTS OF READING - at least 50 pages of reading for every class. 
Also a write ups on the assigned readings for every class for 20% of your grade.
Not much teaching more of a discussion driven class. Very unclear criteria for assignment and vague feedback.
Pay attention and put the effort in and you'll guarantee a B.
