Dr. Ally is committed to her students' success. She provides individualized attention to each of us and support us as needed. I would most definitely take another class with her in the future.

I am not going to lie, this class was hard. She pushes you to do more and think outside the box. This is probably the hardest class I ever took but I was satisfied with the things I learned. Would love to take this professor for another class in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Ally is tough but her lectures are enjoyable. She makes things easy to remember. You would expect educational policies to be dry but she somehow manages to make this boring topic interesting. She will not disappoint you.
I have been actively trying to take as many of my classes just with Prof Alon.the difference between him and others is next level. He knows so much and actually worked! Can we have an MS in Prof?!
Profs classes are great. I keep thinking about them. Easily the best prof I've had

Last class in CF. Prof is the best I have had. He could teach all the courses. Some of the classes I took didn't make sense, till he explained it again in class. He's normally on-campus and not online. The slides were amazing!
Great professor, made me enjoy networking to a much higher level than I expected.

I had Prof for AppSec. I worked hard in this class and learned a lot. I have taken two classes with Prof Alon, and they are my top 2 classes of the entire program. Ranking 1 appsec,2 networking, 3 netsec (Mak). I wish he taught all my classes!

This is a hard class but prof made it fun we even had a guest speaker! I looked up prof Alon, he has done so much. I liked how he had examples for each part of class on how to use the concepts, other classes stay so sciency with profs that never actually done anything except research. Prof Alon does both. Best I have had at Tandon.

Easily my favorite prof of my entire ms and maybe even undergrad. I learn every lecture from prof. He also respects effort, if you work hard he helps you. first class in a while I feel everyone got the grade they deserved. met people i've been in class with for years, ha, first time we connected was this class.
This prof Alon is one of the best I have had. I was worried after the first course and then had him for my 2nd. looking forward to taking him again!

Hands down the best professor in the program. I took his summer networking class and couldn't wait to have him again for AppSec. It's incredibly hard work, but the course is so wellstructured and his lectures are phenomenal.He explained why assignments may take time and how it was worth it, i love the transparancy.Would take any class Prof teaches
Just wanted to drop in, I took Prof Alon this summer for networking he is so good I hope to take more classes with him.super clear and shares the reason for things including nyu stuff
I just finished my summer term with Prof Alon. I loved his class! My previous course was so so, so this was great, got me excited about networking again!
Best Prof ever! Take any class if the instructor is Prof. Alon!

Best class I've taken in grad school. It was tough but made learning fun again after some dry courses. Assignments were clear, and Alon is really fair about grades and extra credit, no favorites, which I appreciated as someone who doesn't speak up much. Got an A. Super proud of it. I graduated since, but was thinking back on this course!

Just wrapped up my midterm for this class and am on track for an A. Prof Alon is really amazing, I plan to take AppSec with him too since that is a hard class. I had to study really hard for the midterm, but the lectures and readings really helped. And the practice exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Not gonna lie, Prof Alon is the GOAT. I'm fresh outta undergrad and honestly wish I had him back then. The class moves fast, but he makes it make sense and actually gets you hyped to do the work. I'm usually lowkey lazy but I've been putting in effort?? Wild. So glad this is anonymous! 10/10 would take again

Prof Alon is such a change from the previous course I took. I was thinking of stopping the program, and this course got me excited again! The book used in the class is okay, but the lectures are amazing! Just so incredibly good. I wish I had him for all my courses, he could teach them all! A lot of reading, quizzes, and exams, but it's all doable

I am in the summer class, and it's a packed class, but the lectures are so good. There are things I never thought about before that are making sense to me. I am looking forward to learning more! Quiz has been easy, and the assignments are not too bad!

Prof Alon is awesome, my favorite professor in the program. I took AppSec as my last course and left on such a highlight. I had to work really hard to get the grade I did, but I learned more in this course than several of the others combined! His lectures kept me focused, and everything just made sense how he explained it. My previous course didn't

Prof Alon gives out a ton of practice problems, which really helped! He's super fair and upfront about what it takes to do well. If you keep up and follow his advice, you'll be in a great spot. If you don't put in the work, it'll show. dead, this is not a procrast course

I took Networking with Prof Alon last Summer, it was one of my favorite classes in the program, and I saw he's teaching AppSec in the Fall, so I signed up. He really knows Networking, it was a ton of work but he kept it fun! Just awesome in lecture!

Prof Alon is really amazing, the class was hard, but not in a keep-busy kinda way. Everything we did, felt like I could apply it at work. He's super passionate and that kept me going! I wish I scored better. No cap, it was my mistake, I didn't study for the first exam...

By far my favorite professor. The course is intensive, but fun! This may not be popular, but I appreciate that Prof Alon made sure no one could weasel their way into a better grade - everything is laid out clear. I kinda enjoyed the reality check some students had that they actually have to study. I had to work hard in this class and loved it!

I can honestly say I have not had a better professor in the entire program, Prof Alon is so good! I took Crypto prior and didn't understand a lot of concepts, in one of his last lectures he discussed some concepts that finally clicked for me. He really knows his stuff, and explains it all in a simple and practical way. I love his examples!

Prof Alon is one of the best professors I have had during my entire master's program. It's noticeable just how far above many others he is in his knowledge base and teaching ability. I am actually pumped at the end of his lectures!

This professor makes the subject matter easy. This was my last class of the program, and by far the best course I have taken. He just teaches better, simply put. I didn't use the video modules at all, they were so boring. Different people ran them. The lectures with the actual professor were awesome! Do not skip this class, best one I took!

Wow, my appsec course was easily the best course I took in the entire program. I was taking it for the second time, and Prof Alon's version is so much better. I actually understand it now, and am excited again, I was really turned off after a few bad courses. If he teaches anything else, I will come back as alumni. This was my last semester at NYU!

I took networking and was trying to find other courses that he teaches, shame I took appsec prior with a different instructor! Prof. Hillel-Tuch is amazing, I ranked him as easy, but that's only because he makes it easy, the material is challenging, but he takes the time to break it down and digest. Grading is very fair put in effort, do well.

Just joined in to say that Prof Alon is by far the best professor I have had in my entire cyber fellows experience. The differences are sometimes night and day! I wish he would teach every single course in the program, he knows them all and ties his lectures to courses of other instructors, even reminds us what past assignments to look at! Love him

Just finishing AppSec with Prof Alon. He is so incredibly good, I really loved his lectures. This is not an easy class if you are unprepared. He makes his lectures accessible for topics we may not be familiar with and is also really funny, which makes it fun. Labs are hard, quizzes are on the labs. Do the work and you'll be fine, no coasting.

I took computer networking last summer, and it was amazing. It was summer, so lectures got condensed, became longer, but Prof Alon made them so fun, you learn something knew regardless of your skillset. I came in with over a decade of work experience, and there were things he covered I never properly understood before or knew to ask. Truly stellar!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easily my favorite professor of all the instructors in my program. He is so good at explaining complicated concepts and being non-judgemental in the process. You feel safe asking questions. Even with a large class, it feels personal. I wish he taught each class! He  will support you if you do the work, happy someone ok pushing back on the slackers!

Prof Alon is simply one of the best professors I had in my entire program. I wish he taught all the classes! Some many past courses didn't make sense, and in a lecture or two for App Sec it all does. The material is not easy, and the labs are involved, but they're fun and he pushes us to self-troubleshoot. No coasting, it's the real deal!

He is so good. It's a night and day experience for me between this professor and other instructors I have had in classes before. There are courses I took before that I did not understand all semester, and he explained literally their entire syllabus in a single hour lecture. The class is hard, you'll work your butt off, worth it

Taking Appsec with Prof Alon, and it's been amazing. Though the material is tough, he makes it accessible and engaging with fun examples. His lectures leave you thinking without overwhelming. Super fair and approachable, emphasizing effort - work hard and you will do well, don't coast. Wish I knew he also taught Summer Networking,Id take his class!

I had Prof Alon over the summer for computer networking. Ended up with a B+ but that was more on me, I decided to try and go on vacation while in class. The lectures were awesome, he was a breath of fresh air from some of the other classes. He made hard topics easily understood. This was an intro class, but he also teaches one of the capstones.

I had Prof Hillel-Tuch for Computer Networking over the summer. He is soooo good! Created lot's of extra credit opportunities, and made them clear right at the beginning of the semester. Helped alleviate my stress! The material is challenging, but he makes it really fun, his lectures are amazing. Will find other classes he teaches just to take

The professor is easily one of the best professors I have had at NYU as well as undergraduate. He is kind, caring, and very passionate about ensuring we learned and understood the material but also do well in the class. The course material is at the graduate level, and he creates a clear path for all of us to succeed. This was super appreciated!

The whole course is listening to his lectures, which are clear and engaging. Two exams, and helpful recitations. If you have an understanding of the readings and the goal of the course, you will do great.

Professor Appiah was an amazing lecturer. He is extremely knowledgeable about so many topics. Often when speaking lectures can drone on a bit but if you raise your hand he will stop in the middle of his sentence to address you. Make sure you go to office hours at least once, even if not to get guidance for the course then to pick his brain.

Inspiring Professor who is able to communicate ideas clearly from a wide range of sources, I especially enjoyed participating in the conversations we had in our supplementary classes with the TA. I gained valuable new perspectives and insights to inform my ethical perspective, and the work was very manageable.

Her exams are so hard and she assigns so many essays. I took this class as a core requirement and never in my life have I studied so hard for an LS course. I'm shocked I made it out alive. The readings are insanely long. If you want to take her to learn go for it. If you're taking her class just to fulfill a requirement, CHOOSE ANYTHING ELSE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is very annoying and irritating to work with, and her expectations for students are often unrealistic. Her exams feel unnecessarily complicated and frustrating, which adds stress without improving our understanding.

taker her if you care about the topics of the class, do not take her if you are just taking the class because it is a requirement. There's a lot of reading and she will cold call. Shows favoritism. A bit arrogant and thinks she knows everything. Interesting lectures though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Despite the reviews, I still chose Dr. Apsel as my thesis advisor, and never regretted it—my thesis won the outstanding thesis award thanks to her guidance. Even if it didn't win, I would have felt the same nonetheless. If you aren't willing to put in the work and can't take constructive feedback, that is a reflection of you, not the professor.

The class is interesting and she is knowledgeable.

Heavy workload
Syllabus is confusing and assignments are unclear.

Bizarely vindictive, often interrupts and goes off on students.
Does not excuse absences (doesn't matter hospital visit, etc)
Requires attendance at talks outside of class time.

You will learn a lot, but it is a painful semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very sweet lady. Very passionate about what she teaches. A LOT OF READING, but you can skim through. She will cold call at the beginning of semester but later on its more if you want to add on to the discussion. Essays prompts were very in depth, and she wants you to write the facts and implications rather than what you think.

The syllabus WILL be changed constantly and you're playing roulette on whether she even sends the readings. Expect essays (usually 3-4 pages) every week alongside a minimum 250-page reading. Not accommodating either plus the extra credit is tedious. The only good thing is that her exams match the study guide. The lectures are ok on their own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: A lot of readings. Pays attention to certain students over others which can be good or bad; tests are very straightforward but overwhelming with many questions. No clear grading criteria on essays. Will cold call but you can pass.

I took International Human Rights with Professor Apsel and was very impressed with her class, her ability to explore heavy topics such as genocide through an academic lens while still preserving the empathetic nature we should have when talking about such atrocities allowed for very interesting class discussions. Do the readings and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr Apsel is really great! Shes definitely tough though and can be really blunt, especially when telling you your answer is wrong. But she is really sweet. I took her for Global Violence and there is reading to do every class but its super interesting. The midterm was rough though but no final exam-only paper and she is willing to help you out!!

No discussion is chill in this class. You go in prepared and participate, or you hope she doesn't call on you. SFI and II were doable as a non-philosophy person and while it's very difficult and frustrating, you learn something. She's a caring professor who doesn't grade too easily or harshly. A lot of work, sometimes brutal, but you survive (A-).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Definitely one of my favorite professors. Engaging lectures that are thought-provoking and filled with passion. The short essays were a great way to wrap up each topic as a comprehension checkpoint. Because of this class I see the direction I want my career to head! Because of her, I feel more excited than ever to pursue a career in human rights.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Apsel was my thesis advisor, but was very dismissive & from the beginning of the year there was hostile air. I asked once whether I could come earlier for her officer hours & she stepped very close to me & stared me down, almost as an intimidation tactic, to tell me no. I was shaken the rest of the year & regret not having changed advisors.

I took Apsel for SFIII. Her class may not be an easy A, but it is truly worthwhile. She truly cares about the material and incredibly passionate about human rights. She facilitated really great class discussion as well. Will miss this class.

I would not recommend her to be your professor for classes higher than social foundation I or II. She may be a nice lady for office hour, but her class is absolutely demanding and challenging. Lots of reading (if you actually read), huge amt of work and the deadly exams (ask like 15 or 20 questions in one short essay).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is awesome but too many textbooks to read. She asks for a 2-3 pages assignment almost every other week. She is very rigid and very tough grader. She is kind of teacher who has been teaching for 30 years... Anyway, hard work is required.
Absolutely adored her. A little harsh but fair grader. Learned a lot. I'll miss her class.

I honestly loved Professor Apsel. She is so sweet and kind, and genuinely interested in making sure our experience in the class is worth while. If you study and do the work, she gives A's. I've taken a lot out of the class this semester and I think she's done a great job teaching us the information.

The class is very broad, but does not go into depth on any subject, which is terrible for papers, tests, and development of students. Discussions =professor trying to relate the topics that we are discussing in class. Sounds good in theory, but she merely asks question & offers no guidance, aka "What is humannature? yeah, you guys think about it."

A very insightful teacher...very smart and knows her stuff...yes she can be very hard on papers but if you put the effort you will get the A. Her midterm and final is very easy...given study guide...and she is willing for you to learn. Please take her :)

Apsel is smart, and if you care about the material i imagine that she would be great, but since the course is a mandatory freshman class for LSP, i don't recommend her, she is a hard grader and will not sympathize with you.

Professor Apsel is extensively knowledgeable about the subject and you learn a lot from her lectures. You must read the material to be prepared for her class in order to follow along with the lectures and participate. She is a very fair grader and the papers are manageable if you know the material. I absolutely recommend her class.

She's not the most interesting in terms of personality but she actually makes you learn.  She's a hard grader on essays so be prepared for that, but overall - I enjoyed her class and got a lot out of it.  I'd definitely recommend her if you're willing to put the time in to read because you'll learn a lot.
I took this class expecting her to be an extremely hard grader, but I was pleasantly surprised that her grading was fair on both essays and exams. She is really smart and knows what she is teaching.

Very difficult and not helpful; I turned in a paper that she lost and she claimed she never got it- I wasn't allowed to turn it in again. I did well in the class but it was very hard- reading and class participation are extremely important.

Absolutely adore her! She is extremely smart and passionate about her subject. You have to participate, and I'm sure you can get by without doing the readings, but you should so you can participate. Very fair grader. Take good notes, and listen to her, and you will do fine. would love to take her again but shes off next semester! =( LOVE HER! take
She is very helpful if you go to office hours, go to class & pay attention and you're fine.

A VERY sweet woman. Kind and interested in her subject. You need to read the texts. Tests and essays are easy (she tells you everything you need to know). She will warn you the day before when she plans to call on people in class. This is a rewarding class.

I had her for social foundations, she's one of the most intelligent women I've ever encountered. I will admit to sometimes falling asleep, but not for lack of interest, it was because sometimes when she gets intense she whispers lol. Very thought provoking and thorough.

really boring and likes to pick on people on class, need to do reading and don't rely on her notes on the board, take your own.  tends to wander and never finishes thoughts or discussion question , very disorganized but very nice and helpful and likes participation.  essays and tests aren't bad because hse basically tells you exactly what she wants
my least favorite class this semester.  EXTREMELY boring, basically a note taking course.  also, you better do your readings-she puts people on the spot.    can be nice, but try to aVoid if you can.

her class is really boring and shes HUGE on being on time...i was 5 min late and she pulled me aside after class to scold me..pretty nice otherwise, if u pay attention (i recommend adderall) ull be ok..her test and essay questions are pretty vague tho, other than that shes really smart and u can tell shes really passionate about wat she teaches

She assigns a very heavy work load in the begining to try and weed people out. If you're not completely obsessed with the topic or if you don't plan on becoming some kind of human rights lawyer it's probably better to take another class. Mere interest isn't really worth it. She's very intelligent and helpful but doesn't make class very exciting.
No Comments

I LOVE Dr. Apsel.  She's a great professor, has about a bajillion degrees, is very helpful and nice.  Her classes are interesting and well-taught.  She'll help you with anything you need, inside and outside of class.

Very Nice and is concerned about students, which i was very impressed with.  However, I really didn't like being put on the spot.  Take good notes and pay attention.  Good Luck with the writing assignments

Dr. Apsel is one of the most amazing teachers I have ever had. She is extremely intelligent, knowledgeable, and a dedicated teacher. She is very helpful but will make you work hard for an A: that's why I liked her. Dr. Apsel will also aid you in whatever way she can if anything in her class inspires you to research it further.
She's a sweet lady and expects you to do the reading. Tough grader, but definatly recognizes the effort you put in. If you go and talk to her she will listen and be very honest. I love her.

Just do the reading, and take really awesome notes in class and you'll be fine. Write down EVERYTHING - even the stuff she doesn't write on the board. And don't be late for her class. She's a good teacher. I like her.

Conducts class in charismatic, vibrant, energetic manner. Keeps students engaged through frequent discussions. Some texts straightforward, some require in-class analysis. Occasional pop-quizzes. Grammar, cogency, and analytic depth prioritized in papers.

Not the worst, she just is a little confusing in class at times and does not explain concepts too well if you did not do the reading. Recitations are online. I would say take her if there is not a better option. She is ok. Exams were fine too as open note,

her exams are about as difficult as they get. they become more theoretical and not so much practical application of concepts that are taught. her lectures are also not the most helpful but if you don't attend, it's hard to learn the concepts because the slides aren't self explanatory. you really will have to put in the work to get a good grade
Don't recommend for anyone new to accounting she is no help

Accounting is a class that is only difficult because of the curve. But because Klein is not the most engaging lecturer (and free homeworks), the class averages on exams are the lowest of any accounting class (low-mid 80s) while the tests are still very easy! Great professor to take if you want a safe curve

Nice lady but a lackluster lecturer. Unclear, imprecise, and unorganized. Terrible whiteboard usage, writes confusingly. Generally overcomplicates simple concepts and makes you believe they're more challenging than they are. I learned more from YouTube than from class. Fortunately, the material itself is easy, and her tests are fair.
April is a good professor, she presents boring material not in a boring way. Could be a bit more helpful outside class though.

I was so surprised that Professor Kleins rating was not higher. She has made accounting fun to learn and shes extremely engaging. I have really enjoyed this class and it is easy if you pay attention and read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I think she is really cool, and her class is interesting with interactions, and knowledge is really useful. HW is annoying, but it's not her fault. If you are taking intro to Financial Accouting, I think Prof. Klein is a good choice. good luck

Really rude and gets annoyed with questions/remarks by students. The material isn't all that difficult. Klein finds a way to make it so, however. Tests are generally on the harder side vs homeworks and practice problems, there are much better accounting professors out there.

The Pros: Very knowledgeable, has clearly put time/effort into figuring out how to TEACH this stuff. Lectures are clear and effective, lecture notes are comprehensive and online HW (while somewhat annoying due to bad UI) are doable/helpful) The Cons: she is very very 'new york' and can come off as abrasive. don't be late, don't interrupt her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Not sure why she has a subpar rating. She's funny, approachable, and generally level-headed. Makes the course more interesting than you'd expect (accounting is still boring tho). Tests are tough but if you do the right practice problems you'll do fine. Most people end up in the B range. Chegg is a must for the hw - the online system sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I did not like this professor. Very harsh and just a rude person in general

The class is fun. Professor Klein is very engaging and really wants you to learn. She always puts an effort to make the lectures and materials interesting (since financial accounting is NOT generally a fun subject). I really enjoyed her class. And if you study hard, you will do fine in the exams.

One of the best teachers at Stern! Her lectures make sure you 100% grasp the hardest concepts and incorporates interesting real-world cases. If you do the online homework, take good notes, crunch the hard problems and practice often, it is a guaranteed A. She also invites you to take a look at her research papers.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot of people think Klein's class is tough, but you'll do fine if you study the textbook, attend her lectures, and take good notes. Tests are open-book and open-notes, and I found a lot of answers in the notes I took in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take at your own risk. She assigns very few practice problems which are often not truly reflective of her tests which makes it very difficult to study. You can try asking her for help, but odds are she'll just end up getting annoyed after 5 minutes. DO NOT RECOMMEND.
Terrible class. Tests on nothing you learn in class and just based on how smart you are. Did not learn much.

Professor Klein has her moments. She could be in a good mood or bad. She doesnt use a textbook for FSA but gives you powerpoint slides instead. I genuinely learned a lot and found some of the stuff she taught interesting but damn...Her test are extremely challenging and do not reflect really any of the stuff she gives you. Good Luck.
Not recommended. Decent lecturer. Material is simple but tests are harder than anything gone over in class or assigned as HW.
Great teacher. Makes the material interesting. Very comical too. Material is annoying. Decent amount of homework. Tests are very straight forward and open book.

At first, I did not like Klein. She has a strange sense of humor and can be rude but is very laid back at the same time. She genuinely cares about getting students to learn the material, though I was a bit bored at times. Midterm was surprisingly difficult (exams are LONG), but the final was much better since I studied more. Not bad!
Tries to make accounting more fun than it ordinarily would be...and it works...usually pretty helpful if you go to her 1on1....fair grader...overall nice lady and very good course
No Comments
A genuine, bright, and delightfully laid-back muther ****er.
She is unfriendly, unhelpful, yells at people who ask her questions, is very temperamental, and is constantly PMSing. Yet she is clear, and you will understand her.
Clear, patient, passionate and motivated to see students succeed in French. Clever woman and also wrote an awesome book. She enjoys helping students and will go out of her way to help you.
One of the best professors I've had. Very passionate and helpful.
she's an awesome teacher. her class rocked my world.
He is the person who really cares his students and what they learn. Would recommend him to any who want to study real stuffs and commits to become a scholar.

Karl is such a kind and knowledgable professor! His lectures are engaging and interesting, attendance is mandatory and participating at least once in class is expected. There were many papers, but he grades fairly and is very lenient with due dates and extensions. Would definitely recommend!

Really engaging class, pretty much entirely class discussion on the hw readings. You can get away with not reading everything but should atleast skim. Assignments are kind of vague and a bit confusing but not hard. I learned a lot in the class and felt challenged in my thinking, prof is enjoyable and super knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took intro to science and society with him. He was super funny and kept classes interesting even though we were online. Allowed us all to speak very freely and genuinely listened to his students. Definitely challenged us a lot intellectually as well. Very candid and interesting professor overall.

I took prof appuhn twice - once for c&c renaissance Italy, then a year later for t&i nature! There's a reason I took him twice- he's great! I have never thought so much about nature in my life - and now I actually think about it frequently! The class isn't easy, lots of reading, but there's no denying he knows his stuff and is very welcoming/nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE TXTS&IDEAS NATURE. dry lecture,uses absolutely no media, reads from paper on desk. His sentences are convoluted, reflction of mental gymnastics req'd to make meaninglss connctions btwn txts. Humor and enthusiasm, yes, but class is impractical, purely theoretical, exhausting, no greater signif. Inclass essaytests. timewasting, tough class

Best professor and best course I've ever taken in my 4 years of studying at NYU. He has such a gripping way of presenting the material. Listening to his lectures, you won't believe an hour and fifteen minutes have passed! I think Renaissance Italy is not one of the "easy" cultures &contexts u can take, but definitely definitely worth taking!

Prof Appuhn was great-- he really transmitted his love of the Renaissance to his students. He always makes himself available for a few minutes after class to answer questions about the material. He also went the extra mile to help me out via email when I was curious about a subject discussed in class. A lot of reading, yes - but it's worth it!

A very great teacher who genuinely cares about how you do. Makes the C&C requirement doable and fun! The class is set up in that you write 4-5 essays, the midterm is an open note and the final is take home. All very doable 10/10 recommend

Amazing lecturer and was my favorite professor, initially. He graded a few of his students' work, including mine. I didn't get any essays back with notes, just a grade online. I can't improve without feedback. I also haven't gotten back any grades in a month or so. Everyone else has. Emailed him, no responses. Told my TA; she gave me BS excuses. TF
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Texts and Ideas Nature is insanely difficult. Will significantly lower your GPA. Tests require you to know every minor detail about every text read. Papers expect you to be a historian, not a student writing a history paper.
His lectures are crucial to understanding the readings and usually are super important in writing the papers. Lectures are great and very engaging. Technology  ban is a bit of a bummer though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Texts and Ideas: Nature. Lectures and material are great. Papers and tests are extremely difficult.

Appuhn is the man, plain and simple. He's an absolute natural at lecturing, and you'll be blown away by the depth of this course. I took Renaissance Italy with him, and he really knows his stuff. You'll have to do ALL the readings to get above a B though. And the tests are downright scary. However, he's best teacher I've ever had in my life.
Made class interesting, very smart guy. Not an easy class but still laid back. Grading a bit tough but he offers lots of feedback
Extremely knowledgeable and offers great critiques of papers (very clear- tells you exactly what you did right and wrong). Doesn't take any BS but if you respect him, he respects you. Funny too.
Karl Appuhn is simply the best history professor at NYU. His lectures are entertaining. Took Pre-Modern Science, The Renaissance, and Environmental History.

Grading's a bit tough, & he expects you to write papers based on reading often before discussion of the  matters in class.  If you have the chance you MUST try this prof- he's also helpful/interesting to talk to if you can catch him at a free moment.

Grading's a bit tough, & he expects you to write papers based on reading often before discussion of the  matters in class.  If you have the chance you MUST try this prof- he's also helpful/interesting to talk to if you can catch him at a free moment.

Prof. Appuhn is BY FAR the best professor in the history dept. at nyu.  He is extremely interesting and attentive, always available to meet and discuss your progress outside of class - truly a great person of high moral character. Took Pre-Modern Science, The Renaissance, and Environmental History of Early Mod. World with him. Highly recommended!

Probably best lecturer in the history department. Very articulate and eloquent guy but is completely unpretentious, and always keeps sense of humor in his lectures. Relatively hard to get an A, but relatively easy to get a B/B+. Definitely recommended.
He's a brilliant prof. He really teaches you a lot, but doesn't test on your capacity to memorize facts, but to understand the concepts underlying the material. Best prof I've ever had!

This guy is all right, but he's a really hard, and I think a little bit unfair grader. The classes are interesting, but he spends a lot of time giving you the biography of the scientists when you can't use any of that information on the exams. It's all about the theories and you'll spend all this time trying to memorize facts that won't help you.
Prof Strickland is great. She does a good job of getting students to participate and is able to pull smart points out of students who sometimes are not that smart. I could listen to her all day.

April should be a kindergarden teacher...She is smart but its annoying how she says everything everyone says in class is interesting or good, when it may be completely irrelevant or repetitive. She's nice for sure, but really not cut out for teaching at nyu. In anthro of Media, we spent the entire class talking about Facebook...even when unrelated.
So great! I don't know if she's teaching again, yet I loved her class. Highly recommend.
April is great, very helpful and smart. This was one of the best classes I took at NYU. Highly recommend.
I loved his classes. He taught me SPA01 and SPA03. Great teacher and a nice person!
This guy is really great. You can tell he likes what he is doing. He encourages participation through nice class discussions. I highly recommend him!!!
excellent classes, great energy!!!!
Marco is the freakin bomb.  He is the best professor on the face of this planet. I hate spanish but it was the best class Ive ever taken. He is a funny one and he rocks!

This was my second time taking a class with professor shehata. She is such a kind woman and really wants her students to understand the material. She brings in guest speakers to talk about auditing in the real world. There's no midterm, but instead 5 quizzes, a group project, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Extremely passionate and knowledgeable about accounting. Makes it easier to learn a boring and difficult topic. Not my favorite class but since it is a requirement, glad I took it with her.

Great prof. I did kind of bad in the start of the semester so fell behind quickly. This is the type of class where you actually have to pay attention during lectures. I figure I could just doze off during class and self-learn the stuff by myself like I usually would with most other classes. Wasn't the best choice I made, and kind of regretted it.

First of all, really knowledgeable, experienced professor who knows accounting very well, also teaching. If u want to learn sth for accounting, definitely recommend. However, exams and work are annoying. I will say a really professional person who look very warm and helpful, but also know students a lot. Not easy
So so lovely. An awesome person and teacher with a great heart and a real passion for what she teaches. Will always recommend!!!

Professor Shehata was amazing. I learned so much from her lectures and she was great at engaging students. Super sweet and always willing to help after class or during office hours. Would definitely recommend. some people say the curve is bad but I feel like the curve was similar to the other PFA classes
I really enjoyed the class. Would 100% recommend.
Best teacher hands down

Professor Shehata is excellent! She really wants to see her students succeed and understand accounting. I definitely recommend going to office hours so that she can get to know you and to make sure you understand all of the concepts in class.

I would say Shehata is great overall. One thing that you should keep in mind that the competition in the class is usually pretty tough, which makes the stern curve tougher. However, if you plan on pursuing a career in finance you need to know accounting and this class drills it.
Debit on the left, Credit on the right

Prof. Shehata cares a lot about the subject and you can tell how passionate she is to teach. However, the Stern curve can definitely be tough and push you down a letter grade. To do well, I recommended reading the textbook for the homework, while for the tests I recommended thoroughly going through the slides but the tests are not too difficult.

The best PFA professor, in my opinion. Yes, you will need to put in the work because of the curve, but GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!! It helped me so much because she literally doesn't let you leave until you understand the material. Interestingly, I don't even want to do accounting/finance, but I still enjoyed the class.

Prof. Shehata REALLY loves accounting. You can tell by her lectures and by the effort she puts in her class. She  explains everything super well, and does a great job. The curve is kind of brutal, but her tests are pretty straightforward so if you put in the effort, you can definitely get that A.
I dont even take her section of the class. But her review videos are the only things keeping me sane. Goat.

She's a good professor. The main issue was that the textbook was meh and didn't help much with reviewing. Also, be wary that this is the only section where you cannot take a single reference sheet for the exams (which make up 75% of your grade), so you'll have to cram in a sea of boring entries, rules, and tedious calculations. Bubbly prof though.

This is for Accounting and the Blockchain This has been my favorite 2 credit course offered at Stern. You can come in with no knowledge about blockchain stuff and still come out with a great understanding of the fundamentals. Presentations are super easy to understand and there is a speaker every class. 10/10 would reccomend!

Auditing had 4 quizzes, 3 software asgnmts, 4 case studies, 4 discussions, a group project, & a final. Everything but the group project was short. Don't bother reading the txtbk. I learned a lot & you can tell she loves her job. She seems to genuinely care about her students & her lectures are fun. I wish I could take her for every class.

GREAT PROF!!! Really cares about her students and makes accounting fun. HOWEVER, beware that the curve in her courses are ROUGH. Top 25% on the last midterm was 97%. Also, it seems those interested in pursuing accounting take her class, therefore, overall the student body is better at accounting.

Professor Shehata's lectures are super engaging & explain concepts very well. I took her for both PFA and Accounting & the Blockchain. For people who are interested in taking Accounting & the Blockchain, it is definitely very fun and I really enjoy the topics she teaches; however, the workload for a 2-credit class is a lot, so be aware of that.

The absolute BEST. Prof. Shehata is a fantastic professor and an even better person. She literally makes accounting FUN! Never thought I'd like accounting, but she genuinely inspired me to change career paths. She has a wonderful and bubbly personality and truly cares about her students. You should absolutely take her as your professor.
I had Shehata for accounting and auditing and she was great for both. One of the really rare professors who just loves her job and it shows!

Great professor in terms of how well she teaches. She goes into a lot of detail to make concepts more understandable. HOWEVER she is the only PFA professor that does not allow open-book/cheat sheet and the curve for her class is brutal (because a lot of people do well). So be prepared to study hard and in depth for her class if you want to do well.

She is great but the curve is too bad. Worst curve among all other sessions. All other classes are curving up but we are curving down. The median of midterm 2 is 87, unbelievably high. Would have chosen Kim.

Incredible professor whose genuine passion for accounting is evident from her lectures. She manages to make accounting fun and easy to understand and is incredibly kind, caring, and engaging. Would highly recommend.

She was really engaging the entire semester and tries her best to make accounting somewhat interesting. She gives a good amount of practice and her exams aren't surprising. There's homework due almost every week. The hardest thing about the class was the Stern curve because everyone does so well.

Every other PFA professor at Stern has open-book exams. But with Professor Shehata, you need to memorize how to do every problem instead of understanding what you're learning. Great class if you enjoy spending hours memorizing stuff from her slides. I had to make ~100 flashcards before each exam. Not a great choice if you want to have free time.

Shehata is an absolute unit! Best professor I've had at Stern. She is extremely fun in class, provides tons of resources, and makes herself available all the time if you need help. Tests aren't very hard, and homework is quite manageable too. The Stern curve will totally screw you over, though. That (and my questionable work ethic) ruined my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Shehata is undoubtedly one of the greatest professors/teachers Ive had in my life. Her clear love for teaching makes learning a tedious and boring topic such as accounting fun, and incentivizes students to want to do good in her course. If you are struggling, go to every office hours and show her that you care and you cant go wrong.

Overall Professor Shehata was an excellent teacher. I highly recommend taking her if you can get into her class. She is very good at explaining different topics and is helpful during office hours. ACCTUB-1 is a difficult course and you have to be very well prepared for the exams.
Best professor
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I would def recommend Prof Shehata's class. It was sometimes hard to pay attention to the lectures, but I was able to understand the material by reading the textbook. The textbook homeworks are easily to get full credit for. I did well on the exams by making detailed formula sheets, and the curve isn't as bad as other accounting profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Shehata is very nice and a good teacher. Lectures are sometimes boring, though, and can occasionally get disorganized. If you fall behind even a little, you'll have no idea what's going on when she's doing problems in class. Also, the curve is pretty brutal, and her questions are often worded awkwardly, so be careful. Still, very good professor.

This professor makes something as boring as accounting fun to listen to, her energy is great. I loved having her and would have her again! I don't understand the complaints about the curve, not much she can do about that. She's not making exams so easy that one mistake puts you to B+ tho. Don't need to read the textbook, but you should participate.

Professor Shehata really cares that you learn the material, but you pretty much need to prepare for class by reading the textbook material before showing up to the lecture. Her lectures are more like worksheets to test your knowledge than purely trying to teach the concepts. Overall a great professor, but the class is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She's not a very good lecturer. I wouldn't recommend taking her class - she is an extremely harsh grader, and the curve is brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly, I have no clue why the ratings are so high. Maybe its because its online classes. The online version sucks. She goes too fast. Her slides are NEVER in the correct order and it takes a few min to find the slide shes talking about and then shes already moved on. Just circles everything on slides without info. I hate accounting.

Everyone at Stern loves Shehata, but I hated this class. There is a ton of content, and it's not really presented in a way I found easy to understand. Exams are very hard, and the curve in her class is insane. Impossible to get an A. This class made me truly hate accounting. As much as everyone recommends it, it's not for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very thorough and good at explaining concepts. Does a good job at making accounting exciting.
Always motivated for class

An amazing professor. Makes accounting easy and interesting to learn. The only problem is everyone does so well (since she's such a good teacher) that it's a pretty steep curve to get an A. One of my favorite professors at Stern.

Great professor and human being. Handled the mid-semester shift to Zoom very well. You can clearly tell she cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants everyone to do well. Pay attention in class, do all the homework honestly, and you won't have to study much to do well on tests.
really great professor!

Professor Shehata makes all of the material clear and provides a variety of resources to make sure that her students are successful. However, since she makes everything so straightforward and clear, the curve won't do you any favors.
Gem of a woman. Will help you do well. All you have to do is try and this class is an easy A. Do the homeworks and the smartbook assignment and you will know the material 100%

Professor Shehata is the only accounting professor you should take. She turns the boring subject of accounting into a somewhat interesting topic and that by itself is extremely impressive. Also, if you have half a brain you will do well in this course
Great professor! Very energetic and cares about the material / teaching it well. Easy to follow course pack with detailed slides. Lots of practice exams that resemble the actual exams.

TAKE HER!!! Cannot stress this enough. This woman changed my life! She brings so much excitement to her classroom - I've never had a dull day in FA (shocking, but true)! Her grading is fair and always sees when students are trying their hardest. Go to her office hours and get to know her too. She cares so much about her students. YOU'LL LOVE HER!!!

She is awesome!!! There is a reason why she is one of the top 50 professors in the country. Her lectures are spectacular and she makes FA interesting. She actually inspired me to change my major. She is so accessible outside of class and is willing to help you.

Amazing professor!! Explains complex concepts very clearly with lots of great examples. Very accessible outside of class if you need extra help or practice. Highly recommend and would definitely take again!

Hands down the best professor I had my freshmen year at Stern. She is an amazing teacher - makes her points very clear. She made me like accounting. Go to class every day and participate -- you'll get an A. Don't mess up on the homeworks, they're electronic and you get multiple tries.

I love her. You can clearly tell she loves accounting, and she is so amazing at teaching it! I took this class for like 2 days last semester before I was dropped from the waitlist and that teacher made it seem so hard. Choose Prof. Shehata- she makes it seem much simpler and easier and she's very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Challenging but definitely worth it. You learn so much foundation in this course

Professor Shehata is one of the BEST professors you can have! She makes the classes super interesting and it's amazing to see how much she cares and provides help outside her lectures. Hands down, one of my favourite classes. Definitely take her

Taking this course changed my career projections and actually changed my life (no I'm not being dramatic).Professor Shehata is hands down one of the best (or the best) professors I have ever had. I found the class incredibly interesting, especially with the care she took to ensure students took in as much as possible. TAKE HER, TAKE HER, TAKE HER!

The best the Stern Acct dept has to offer. TAKE HER. SO nice and explains concepts until they are crystal clear. Participate. She will help you until you understand and never makes you feel bad when answering questions wrong in class. Exams are fair and her review guides are accurate representations of the real tests. Makes boring material exciting

Awesome professor! Accounting starts off easy, but gets fairly complicated at the end. Prof. Shehata presents even the most complex topics in a straightforward and engaging manner. You will do great if you pay attention during lectures and put in the work to truly understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Very good teacher. Tests are fair based on what is taught and homework. Very inspirational, she really cares and believes in her students.
Very good teacher. Very understanding. Take her.

Professor Shehata is pretty decent. She does her best to make the subject enjoyable. However, she doesn't allow any sort of cheat sheet for her exams, so you pretty much have to remember everything, which is really tough. Her homework assignments are online through Connect, which are really long and boring, and you don't actually learn that much.

Her lectures couldn't be much clearer.  Her class is easy to understand and she gives periodic quizzes which help students stay on task.  If you're even the slightest bit interested in accounting, she also has the ability to get you hooked with her enthusiasm and relevant real-world articles that she shares periodically.  I recommend her 100%.

SHE IS AWESOME. no really.. let's be real.. accounting isn't that interesting. shehata does her best with an otherwise dry subject and works really hard to present information in a CRYSTAL CLEAR way. Financial accounting is one of the first business classes students take at stern and she bridges the gap and introduces the topic really well. TAKEher
she's FANTASTIC. she really really cares about her students and always presents information in a clear, concise way in class!! if you work hard, it'll pay off. TAKE HER TAKE HER
She is amazing!! exams and quizzes are straight-forward and she covers everything in class! and she's funny and helpful!

Prof. Shehata is one of the best professors I've had at NYU. She actually makes accounting interesting and easy to learn. She used to work at PWC and stopped to raise her baby, and I basically want to be her. She's that awesome.

Agile was the CS course of my dreams.

Taking it was simultaneously one of the best career decisions of my life, one of the most instructive experiences I've ever had, and one of the easiest high grades I've ever gotten.

Prof. Bloomberg's courses are the future of CS education. NYU promote this man before MIT recruits him, lol.
Prof is solid.  A lot of BS from students but he deals with it.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The course is a mess. The professor insists on using Discord, but graders and tutors reply slowly, if at all. All classes share one chaotic channel. They keep talking about rules, yet changed group selection to random for one person. The grading is unfair. I'll never take this class again.

Prof is lowkey hilarious but doesn't play around—expect to actually learn Python. He keeps it 100, mixes dad jokes with deep dives, and makes sure you don't just vibe, you thrive. If you're down to grind and want a prof who's both chill and big-brain, this class slaps.
Take this class.  You finally learn to make real software.
Challenging but rewarding class. Professor is super engaging, makes lectures fun. Definitely stay on top of the group projects - they can get tricky. unstuck ai was a lifesaver for exam prep!
Recommend this course
Straightforward.  You get as much as you put in.

Earned an A in both Agile and Software Engineering classes, but he ignored my emails and DMs when I asked if he wrote recommendation letters for grad schools, thinking our project-based courses meant more interaction. If you don't write them, just say so—no need to leave students on read.

Bloomberg is strict but kind. You work with the same people on the same project for almost the whole semester.  It's basically an internship where you learn in trial by fire.  Hardest part is learning to deal with teammates who are slacking... Bloomberg helps you avoid team conflict as much as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hands down the most useful CS course.
I learned so much
One of the most honest nicest professors.  Knows his stuff and likes to go off-script.

TBH, I wasn't a great experience to take this class during summer session I. The workload felt overwhelming for a 6-week class, especially when you're juggling multiple classes. He tends to answer the same questions over and over, which often goes off the topic. Maybe his in-person class during the Spring or Fall sem would be a better option.

Prof Bloomberg was great at getting concepts across, but his lectures will usually get sidetracked either because someone asks an unrelated question or another topic arises. I still learned a lot though. His grading is really harsh. On the final, I made a small mistake on a problem set but got the entire problem set deducted from my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Straightforward class.  Bloomberg is easy and helpful.
the only course in CS where learn real skills
Take if you enjoy carrying free riders

agile is solely based on a. your group mates and b. ur knowledge of web development prior to joining the class. you should go into this class knowing a good portion of web dev or it might be tough to learn everything on the fly. the weekly gradebot constantly miscalculated grades, so clarify your grades w him, especially the final grade.

This course is very useful and enjoyable if you are 1. fine with group projects and 2. have some prior experience with web/software engineering, but not much. Covers useful tools used in software engineering, lectures are more like introductions for you to start learning by yourself. Grading is in general easy but make sure it's the right course 4u
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You do one big fullstack project over the course of a semester and couple quizzes here and there. Very manageable and grading was lenient.
Super sharp and funny.  Nicest prof in CS.
Awesome
Incredible prof in the cs department, the best cs prof in CAS I met
Nice to first learner Pretty good online lectures, hw and quiz are not heavy.
Take him!!!! Really nice professor!
Caring and gives really great feedback, contents relatively easy. You learned, you get an A-
Lots of extra credits so Easy B+ and A-
amazing lectures, exam and quizzes are online which are pretty easy, gives great feedback!
Easy A  Just take him

The whole class is one big group project. Every week we checked in with our project with the TAs and were told it was looking great. When we submitted the final version, we got a 32%(!?). It's one thing to have high expectations, it's another to string students along into thinking they're doing well and then drop a bomb on their grade at the end.
Easy A. He is so nice!

reviews.comment: Great course.  Gives students every opportunity to get an A by providing tools to allow students to grade their own work before submitting it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Bloomberg is very smart and takes his time to dive deep into the course topics and always had interesting thoughts on any questions I asked.
Very funny

Professor will give you a very subjective and unpredictable grade for the quality of your group project, which takes a great percent of your overall grade. There was no grading rubric for this quality evaluation, and he didn't show the mean or median quality grades of all groups. Very Unfair for project quality grading!
A lot of classes are project work (self study/ group study) without teaching anything, so most people chose to be absent on those days. Totally waste of time and tuition

He sends emails every Monday to release your current grade, which is very messy and contains a lot of errors. Every time students have to report those grading errors to him and course assistant, and wait until next Monday to check the updated grades on emails. You can't check your grade on the course website.
Prof. Bloomberg teaches to the good students in the room.  This is great if you care about learning.

Straightforward class, quizzes, and exams, but projects can be confusing without clear grading / instructions (graders are usually chill). Generally doesn't seem to care about his classes and students, can be condescending at times. However, he does teach highly relevant tools, libraries, skills, and frameworks. Mixed bag prof, wish he curved more.

He made changes to the instruction of assignments on the day before the deadline, which means if you do the homework early, you have to do it in another way again!! He only respond to some questions on Discord, and ignore many questions which might be more important and urgent.
Caring, funny, cuts through the bs.  Wish all professors were like this.

Need to self teach most things. Great opportunity to work on group projects. Highly recommend if you have web-app/JS experience or want some. While he is accessible outside class the tutors are not much help and your grade depends a lot on your group and the project you are working on. Expect some late night debugging. Overall, Great guy and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only course in NYU you could learn tons of engineering knowledge, do recommend you to take if you want to learn some

At first, the course seems to be teaching some trivial, not so useful material. However, if you seriously go through all the quizzes and materials, you do learn a lot about engineering a software and group work.
Amazing professor. Would take his class again.
Very knowledgeable and accessible outside class.  I wish there was more time to learn from him.

Professor Bloomberg is a great professor! If you ask him, he enjoys going deep into all kinds of interesting side topics that give you a real understanding.  I was lucky to get in off the waitlist... register early because his classes are really popular.

With Prof. Bloomberg, what you see is what you get.  He lays out the entire semester for you up-front, tells you exactly how you will be graded, what you're expected to do, and how to get an A.  Even though he doesn't take attendance, students who didn't come to class didn't do well.  Those who did come to class all got As.
The worst. the whole course is a shitshow. My biggest waste of tuition fee.
The worst professor ever. Pissed every single day taking his class. He just never cares much about his classes.

If you read the bad reviews carefully, you will find out Prof. Bloomberg is being blamed for a lot of things outside of his control. He is a very kind person with broad interest. He provides generous feedback, gives out interesting (though not always crystal clear) lectures, and helps students to establish interdisciplinary and practical skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: The prof isn't bad, but due to the structure of the class (a large group project) the course lectures feel pretty decoupled from the work students will have to actually do. Given the scope, I understand that not all topics can be covered in depth, but I found myself searching for more resources to supplement my learning that simply weren't there.

Maybe he's an expert in coding and he is knowledgeable, but he seems to have no interest in passing the knowledge to his students. He barely mentions the knowledge in the quizzes and the instructions for assignments are vague. This is a disaster. Hope he would see my words here and do something about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think that Professor Bloomberg likes or enjoys teaching. It is clear that at least for 101, he is there to get paid. There are multiple choice quizzes and assignments for comprehension. The assignments are optimized my being graded by automated tests he programs (another way he sort of avoids teaching/knowing students)
He does not teach effectively in class and the whole class is confusing.
Everything is beautifully laid out on his website, with clear grading criteria and due dates. The workload is medium, and the content is valuable. You can't go wrong with Prof. Bloomberg.

Clear syllabus, topic schedule, and grading criteria. Weekly quizzes (super easy), assignments usually every 1-2 weeks that take 3-5 hours to complete. Midterm and final exams are fair (easier than the homeworks). Only con is that his lectures are a little boring and when you ask questions he often tells you to just "go back and read the slides."
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Super nice guy - he's always willing to discuss and debate just about anything.
Great professor. Very organized and clear. Super helpful... when you ask for help. Recommended for anyone who likes ideas.

I just got an offer for an internship yesterday because of what I learned. After 3 years of CS, this is the first course I've taken that teaches something useful. Prof. Bloomberg is clear that he expects students to work, and he rewards those that do. You get to choose your own project, so the work is hard, but rewarding.

Course: Agile Dev. If you have no prior web dev exp with MERN stack, AVOID unless want to self-study for 4 months and work with trolls in group pj. Lecture is absolute joke, only terminology, then expects you to know everything and start coding. 0 support, arrogant & vauge to questions usually. Grade: A tho cuz I wrote tons. But, AVOID, dont try!!!

reviews.comment: Great Teacher!! Absolutely hilarious and funny! He is also a pretty good teacher and knows code well. Loved him!!Take him if you love code.

I had Amos for Web Design. HE WAS AWESOME. My grader sucked...I had all of the appropriate criteria; however, I lacked extra ***subjective*** dedication. I had an 89.67, I asked if there was something I could do for an A-, he liked me so much he rounded to an A. He's awesome if you show you care! Don't be afraid to fight with the grader... ����
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He makes you work for your grade. Exams can be much harder than the practice tests but he will curve it if the average of the class is low. His lectures are very dry and it is hard to pay attention but they are very informative and helpful for the exams and assignments.

This is an intro-level python class, while he loves give students heavy homework, making me feel overwhelmed. There are 4 lectures per week for this class, which is fine for me, but he also set 4 quizzes a week for every lecture, and the quizzes are 20% for the course GPA, which sucks. He usually make big mistakes in homework and even in exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amos has his unique style - not for me though. His homework usually required you to read ahead what we about to learn and take off a crazy amount of points when bugs are found. (MANY of my classmates went to tutors He doesn't seem like he is invested in the class. I didn't get information when asking his questions and gradually was demotivated.
Amos is ok, lectures can become a bit boring, but he does not seem to care much about the class...

Bloomberg makes you work for the grade and you have to do textbook reading to do well in the class. In my opinion he didn't effectively teach the material, rather he presented it to us with all the info but a lot of self teaching is required for this course. Homeworks require a lot of self learning beyond the basics taught in class. Tough exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Bloomberg is a must take for Java! Even though he is probably the hardest professor in that subject, he teaches the course in a very efficient, organized, and effective way. Class is very textbook heavy and tests are difficult, but this course will prepare you for future Comp Sci courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Explains concepts clearly and in detail. Textbook is not necessary to do well in his class, but do pay close attention during lectures because MC questions have multiple answers (no partial credit for correct answers) and require you to recall obscure info. Practice questions are also recycled and don't reflect the exam. Know your CS concepts well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I mean this: Agile with him was the worst class I've taken. Lectures are dry, exams are oddly worded multiple-choice Google forms, and he blindly grades everything using scripts. For the group project, you have to make a web app and learn to do so on your own in 2 weeks via YouTube. There's absolutely no effort put into teaching this class. AVOID!!
Unfair exams, that's it. Open coding questions are very vague.

Be ready to teach yourself. Homework require you to do work based on the chapter that is covered in the lecture after the due date, which makes it kind of pointless to go to class. But that forces you to read the book which helps with understanding the material well. Entertaining homeworks, easy second midterm (repeats questions from first one).

If you are a cs major student, you should definitely take his class. His lectures are super interesting and inspiring so that you won't be distracted by other things. Be prepared to work hard for midterms and final cuz it is not easy to predict what he would test you, but if you done your readings and pay attention to his lectures, you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: As the negative comments have revealedif you are taking CS just because everyone is taking it, don't take Bloomberg. You have to be really engaged to be successful. But it doesn't shed from the fact that he is a fantastic professor capable to make the material interesting. He will let you to make up for your mistake if you work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thorough textbook reading is a MUST in order to do well on the exams. Homeworks are graded rather leniently, some will push you to the tutor center. Tests are not that bad, 30 multiple choice and 2 code writing exercises. Repeats mc questions sometimes. Not a bad class, Bloomberg makes you work for the grade.

Amos is overall very solid. Pros: grading is decently weighted on the hw (which is easy), and he will curve exams. Cons: exams are tricky - only 30 important multiple choice questions. Lectures are often slow. You need to take notes in lecture - obscure things he mentions are on tests. It's not difficult at all to get an A- with moderate effort.

Bloomberg's class is pure torture. He talks about random stuff and his ability to teach is close to zero. He is unable to keep students attention and listening to him is an experience from hell. Unfortunately, I couldn't say that I learned or understood a single thing in his lectures. He makes a dry subject feel like the Sahara. Stay away from him.

Mixed feelings about this class. Lectures are boring but you have to pay attention because the exams are really tough. A big portion of your grade will be homework, which is relatively easy, but the exams are seriously tough. Readings not necessary for class but I would suggest studying them for midterm and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Made me decide to no longer be a computer science major. His practice tests do not prepare you for the exam. I would recommend taking a different professor if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Amos is overall a very solid professor. Pros: grading is heavily weighted on the hw (which is very easy AND graded leniently), gives lots of extra credit, curves 1 letter grade. Cons: exams are tricky - multiple choice w/ MULTIPLE answers, lectures are often slow/boring. It's not difficult at all to get an A-/A with moderate effort.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Amos is a solid choice for intro to web design. The lectures can sometimes be a little dry, but he spices things up with sarcastic jokes. The projects are super easy to get 100 on. The tests are more difficult. Class average for the midterm was 70%. If you attend lectures on a regular basis, you can get at least a B with minimal effort.

The tests in this class can be a little tougher but overall the course is not hard. Amos is a good lecturer and teaches things quite well with good in class examples. His tests are weird because you have more than 1 answer and you have to circle all the correct answers to get the question right so beware. You will learn though so take him!
He is a great professor who has a good pace in class and gives easy exams.
A brilliant professor! He taught the content very well, had a good pace with material, very responsive with questions.

Excellent professor who is dedicated to pedagogy, and driven by a genuine joy of computer science. Although the coursework can be burdensome, he is an incredibly fair grader and will help students who show initiative. An A is totally achievable if you put in the work. Generous with extra credit, textbook is hugely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A very helpful and informative professor, although he didn't seem like it at first. Hard to reach him by email which gave the impression that he didn't want to talk to students, but it turns out he's actually rather helpful and approachable in person. Do the homework yourself and really understand the concepts because the exams are difficult.

His lectures are kind of dull, but they can be helpful if you pay attention. He loves taking questions, so that's good. Just go to him if you have questions. The tests seem hard at first, and then if you get the essentials of the python, the tests will become so much easier. He can be a nice choice, and CS is interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hes a solid choice. Very clear and thorough and available outside class. However, his exams are very long and often dont test the material in a way thats considered and effective. This leads students who lose focus after a while to do worse in his exams. If youre reading this Amos, and I bet u are, test concepts that dont require much writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Bloomberg gives a very informative presentation of the course material and clear instructions. His handsome look and great personality make it very hard to skip even one lecture. It was also a great time chatting with him during office hours. Exams are reasonable and he replaces lower early exam scores with the later ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all costs!

Very caring and kind. You learn mostly by doing your homework. He's always willing to help and wants you to know the material. His tests are kind of weird.. Some of his exam questions are structured ambiguously and he doesn't give partial credit, making it fairly difficult to get 100.. overall good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy! Always willing to help you out after class and has office hours pretty frequently throughout the week. His lectures aren't the most exciting thing in the world but he does a great job of teaching relevant material. Exams are basically just rehashed homework questions so, if you can do the hw you should be fine.

His class is fairly easy but his tests are sort of hard. Average for first test was 75 and second one was 70. Def one of the harder web design professors because of the way his questions are structured to have multiple correct answers on a multiple choice and you have to get them all to get the question right. Never went to lecture got a B so eh.

Challenging class for an intro level course given the difficulty of the assignments, but he challenges you to make you a better programmer and coder. His tests and assignments are a little vague sometimes, but he has very clear and engaging lectures.

The class is very easy to follow, with very little work.  There are 10 coding assignments, which we spend class time starting, and 3 tests, which we practice for in class.  For homework, there are online lessons, which are really easy to understand, and then short online comprehension quizzes. In general, if you pay attention, you'll do well.
Gives pretty bad feedback and doesn't care about students.

No required textbook, gave us links to online reading instead. Homework every other night, but if you took notes and followed along in class it was easy enough, though I did seek help from the class tutor. The midterm and final varied wildly from our study guides and I did not feel as prepared as I wanted to be. Otherwise a great professor!

Attendance & textbook not mandatory but lectures are very clear & informative. Go to review sessions before exams because he tells us what we should know/skip. Questions on exams are much simpler than class examples. Homework makes up most of the grade and they're straight-forward if you go to class and keep up. Friendly & helpful in office hours.

I took Intro to Programming because I thought it would be a good minor to go with a business degree. Literal worst experience of my life. Spent hours every week on the assignments and it was only Bloomberg's kids getting extra help every week. The average grade in this class is a C not an A-. Don't expect a curve and don't expect to learn anything.

Lectures and homework are pretty informative. However, he'll pretty much shut you down if you need help unless you're a girl or unless he thinks you have potential in CS. Had to study a lot on my own. Tests are pretty difficult and he only curved the class by 1%

Professor Bloomberg is a good professor and gives you a chance to do better on your second midterm, but you learn mostly through the assignments rather than in class. He's a tough grader and doesn't give partial credit, but is very helpful and has a great sense of humor. It's a great introductory class for Comp Sci minors/majors. Tests are tough.

He's pretty good at teaching programming but ultimately you end up learning both through his lectures and through the assignments and self-modules.
