It's really all about learning in lecture and trying to think in a logical manner that helps you make it through Python. He's a great professor and very nice if you need help.

Amazing professor with a great sense of humor. Exams are very reasonable and not difficult at all if you show up and pay attention in class. He makes lectures are fun and interesting. Highly recommend taking any of his classes.

I have no idea who everyone else had as a teacher because that was NOT Amos. If you are planning on taking Database Design, take it with Deena Engel. I repeat. Take the class with Deena. I learned more from the tutors than I did from Amos. Avoid his as a teacher at all costs.
OK professor. Not too enthusiastic or interesting. Gives very tough exams far different from the practice material.

Physical Computing was a great introduction to a topic which is basically nonexistent at the undergrad level. The professor is clear and grading is very fair. If you go to class and do the assignments you should easily be able to get an A.

Cannot say enough good things about him. Assignments can be difficult, but they are always enjoyable. Midterms and final are straight-forward and over the basic information learned. Super understanding and helpful if you ask for it. Hope to take more of his classes.

Took for intro to web development. Came in as a complete newbie but left feeling pretty comfortable with basic HTML CSS and photoshop thanks to him. Always to help and will try to get you an A. He's also hilarious. 1010 would take again

AMAZING professor. Highly recommended! He teaches very well and makes the course super interesting. Homeworks can be a little hard but they are fun to do and they really help you understand the material. Exams are multiple choice, fill in the blanks and 2-3 code writing questions. If you study his notes and do the homework, youll get an A/A-.

Great professor, teaches with great clarity and patience. Has a great sense of humor. Exams are all multiple choice and are subject to a flat curve if the class had trouble with it. Homework is also offered with extra credit in case you need the grade buffer. Gives students every opportunity to get an 'A'.
Great professor! Clear lectures. I recommend taking his class.

One of the best professors I have ever had. I was brand new at programming and became extremely knowledgeable at several programming languages before the end of his class. I cant say enough good things about Amos.
Love this class. The professor clears up the course material remarkably and firmly. with Whatever the reason to take this course, you won't regret to have taken the class ever, never!
Kind of a by the books guy. I've a friend in the other class who had it way tougher. If you get the chance to take web design with AMOS then take it.
Excellent instructor. Very knowledgeable. Learnt every track for becoming a web developer from his web development intensive class.
Great teacher! Clear, good notes and easily approachable.

He is an excellent professor highly recommended. He gives real life examples all the time and he teaches you more than you should know. If you take another professor you are seriously stupid. I wish I can take his classes over and over again. And I will take his courses, if he teaches what I need to take
Excellent professor. Anything not understood will be clarified. Challenging hw, but midterms were fair. Grading was also very fair.

Challenging, yet helpful teacher. While going to lectures are not mandatory, he definitely makes it worth it. While homework can be very challenging at times, he is helpful in explaining, and even helps with parts of it in lecture. Midterms are short and usually easy, but he is a tough grader, and will catch your mistakes.
Really solid professor. Thorough explanations and a very fair grader.
Good professor and will help those willing to help themselves. His tests are easy and he'll show you how to do some cool stuff in Python

Amanda was an unique experience for me. I've never had a teacher I genuinely disliked. For one, she's so particular about words' meanings that she should have her own dictionary. This wouldn't be so bad if she didn't make you feel slow if you're not on her wavelength. Unless you're of that very select few that can mesh with her, avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: she is an incredibly tough grader, no one in my class got higher than a B for writing assignments. insane amounts of reading before every lesson, participation matters A LOT and also she is v strict about ai checks. people in class got accused of ai use pretty occasionally even tho they had solid proof that they didnt. wishing yall the best of luck
She's tough, but I think fair. Knows what she's doing for sure. You'll get a lot out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Respected

reviews.comment: How much she likes you in class heavily depends on how much/well you participate in class. Sitting doing nothing will actively hurt your grade. She is also very bad at explaining assignments, genuinely everyone in my class had no idea what we were supposed to write about because her explanation consisted of re-reading the assignment description.

AWFUL. Makes her class feel longer than it is and clearly ruins everyones mood just walking in. She feels over qualified and makes students live up to an unreasonable standard. The strictest professor I have had and will try to subtly degrade you. Tough grader and cannot stand absences or tardiness, thinks she's the only class you are taking. FYSM
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amanda (yes, you can call her Amanda) was my prof 2 years ago and while the experience was positive, I came here to say that I've been working with her in the Writing Center since then on other stuff and my impression of her has only gotten stronger. She can solve ANY writing problem and she always has a relevant life lesson to offer

I just started today with my new prof for the spring and it made me realize how much I already miss Amanda. She's so animated and passionate and invested and like how cool is it to learn from a professional writer? My schedule didn't match with hers this semester but I will def be visiting her in the Writing Center.

Amanda is a feminist diva who leads with confidence, knowledge, and expertise. She won't edit your thoughts. Instead she'll help you convey them. I will never forget the AMA where she answered all of our questions about college and art and life. She treated us like adults and held us to a high standard and I am really grateful for the experience.

While Amanda is very smart and talented, she has the ego to match. She can be condescending and passive-aggressive. She is very particular, with a strict no devices rule and odd pet peeves. The GOOD thing about this is that if you're willing to play by her rules, you'll be fine. I ended up with some work I really liked. Though if you can avoid, do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bad Bad Bad. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She allows zero electronics(all paper and pen except for homework), gives hefty assignments, and deducts points if she sees a device without warning. She tries to be nice but ends up tearing up students when their ideas don't match hers. She's VERY rude,sensitive and says she is open to other opinions but is not and expresses her political ideology
She is smart but has weird pet peeves and will pick favorites and grade accordingly. The class was still engaging and she had some fun assignments.

Rudest and most condescending Professor I have ever met at NYU. Was quick to drop her class. Enjoys humiliating students. Avoid at all costs and for your own mental health. You can get just as much out of many of the other professors in this departments. Just plain rude and unlikeable.
She's the worst, period. Had her last semester. Avoid at all costs:)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amanda is an unreasonably harsh grader for the little amount of instruction she gives you. She's smart and talented, but expects her students to already be thinking like her before they walk in the door. GPA killer, there are much better options.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amanda is honestly one of the most passive aggressive teachers I've ever had. She treats you like a high schooler in the worst way possible, like we're babies that know nothing. She rude and makes bad jokes. I learned basically nothing from her class.

Generally very rude to students. Very unhelpful. Will not answer questions from students over email if she thinks the information could be found *somewhere* else or considers the questions stupid. That includes questions asking for clarification about an assignment or specific citation formatting questions. Slow to give feedback on first drafts.
Amanda was a joy to have as a professor. When my cat died, she gave me a week to recollect myself. Great person, and even after graduating, we still get coffee.
Professor is very particular about lots of things. Beware of lots of work. She will lecture you on mistakes you make.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I had at NYU. I made a mistake and was on her bad side for the rest of the class. Her exercises were unnecessarily tedious and did not help me grow as a writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you are engaged, you will do well. Amanda values voice, creativity, and curiosity. She made a required class extremely enjoyable. I learned a lot.

She is not considerate of her students. If you think so otherwise, have fun failing. literally. If your zoom camera is not on, shell put the class on hold and wait for you. Casually flexes her awards as if she doesnt care Do anything wrong and shell make you feel like a failure I try not to eat anything before class, otherwise I might throw up

As long as you show her you are working hard, she will recognise the effort. She may appear cold and her feedback is not so constructive but she will do her best to help. Amanda cares for her students and she wants the best out of them.

Amanda is scary and mean. She does not play around and she is extremely punctual. She basically told me that my draft doesn't qualify as a draft and that I should go to the writing center. She makes you want to cry and give up on your dreams and think that you suck at writing.
Worst professor I've ever had at NYU. No empathy. Brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amanda is a queen, don't even read the other reviews. She's kind of cold at first but once she warms up to you/your class she's really wonderful. Yes, she's tough, but her class is always interesting and you can tell she's really rooting for you to succeed. Also, don't show up late or make up excuses for late papers as she'll immediately hate you.

None of her feedback is ever helpful, because she'll just find other things wrong when you fix it. She decide early on that I was a horrible writer and no matter how often I went to the Writing Center she continued to give me the exact same grade on every paper I wrote. She's just straight up mean and awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Great guy

Very structured, Amanda encourages her students to "play with language" and explore their abilities as writers through her class discussions and various writing exercises. She sets a high bar for her students to strive for. Amanda truly cares about her students and provides them with the tools to progress. A class for those serious about writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Amanda Yesnowitz is an inspirational and respectable instructor. She facilitates group discussion over class materials, but doesn't put up with students who disrespect other students. Not only does she teach essay writing exceptionally, but she understands academia within the context of the art world. Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Completely turned my writing around. I'm not a good writer, but her love for language is infectious. Her passion for writing brought out my best work. Not to mention that she is an extremely talented musical theatre lyricist. Very stylish and nice to look at. I would definitely take Amanda's class again if given the chance.
love her. the class sucks but she's amazing

writing the essay art in the world sucks to begin with and I don't think ANY teacher could solve that issue. But Yesnowitz works with a tough course and tries to get her students to make the most out of it and I love her for that. She's a difficult teacher, but her spirit in class and work ethic makes it worth it

Amanda is a tough teacher, but genuinely wants her students to excel. She does not give too much work, only one writing exercise or a reading per class. She is a tough grader but respects students that put in work and improve throughout the semester. I love her!!!

Amanda is a tough-cookie on the surface, but she is genuinely passionate about what she is teaching. She wants each of her students to succeed, though it can be difficult to perceive at times. She does have a bit of a cocky attitude, but in the end, at least I knew I had a confident teacher. Show her you care and she gives you the utmost respect.

It's her way or the highway. Also, she has "yes" AND "no" in her last name. That's never a good sign. Even if you write a paper that you believe in and has clear evidence, if she doesn't personally agree with it, she will shoot it down. All of her feedback is geared towards changing your paper to something she wants to hear.

Smart, but mean. Yesnowitz knows what she's talking about, but she creates an absolutely detestable atmosphere in the classroom. She makes a bad course worse. At the same time, I do have some respect for her. Her exercises improved my writing. But she could have done that without making everyone miserable
She is not helpful or understanding at all. While I did learn a bit over the semester, I only learned how SHE likes essays to be written, and not how to become a more proficient writer. AVOID.

This class is not to be taken lightly. Punctuality is key. AY is very strict about her rules She is very clear as to what she expects tho, so if you stick to her guidelines you are golden. Exercises help and the atmosphere in classalthough tensecan be helpful if you use it wisely. Very self driven class. Read texts,participate & turn in all work.

Amanda is truly the worst thing to happen to my academic career.  She is mean, judgmental, condescending, and the opposite of supportive or helpful to the students.  She will only allow you to meet with her for two 15 minute sessions the whole semester, no exceptions.  She is the worst teacher I have ever had, and made me hate writing so so much.

Do not take this professor. She is rude and judgmental, and she will hold a grudge against you for any mistake. She doesn't care if you have a good reason to miss class, such as illness, and will not accept late assignments. Nor will she accept assignments over email. There is no leniency in this course. Either be perfect or hate this class.

I tried to give Amanda the best rating I could, but there was nothing nice to say. She is a awful teacher. Her assignments are unclear, and wont accept any questions over them. She refuses to accept emails, and, is extremely unforgiving. If you slip up once, be prepared to never live it down. Please avoid he at all costs.

Amanda is easily the worst teacher I have ever had. She is self righteous giving little validation or respect to the opinions of others. She is inconsistent with her method of teaching: advocating messy thinking and expecting clear and developed ideas in preliminary writing. Seeking help is useless. Its clear she does not like her job at all

I was ready to bash her on this, but there's not a rating on kindness. She's a wicked, selfish, fake and pretentious woman, but she is really clear about what she's looking for in the writing. She won't grade you well, though, if she disagrees with your argument, no matter how well it's supported. I hate her.

Amanda establishes a negative atmosphere among her students, all the while praising herself. My best definition of her would be a very opinionated and passive aggressive woman that immediately picks her few favorite students to adore and creates a personal bubble that keeps other regular students at the helm of her superiority complex. Worst Prof
Honestly I was scared to go to her class from her stigma but she is an incredibly sweet and intelligent person. She really taught me how to become a better writer. She not easy though

I graduate at the end of this semester. After four and a half years at NYU, I can safely say that Amanda Yesnowitz was the worst professor of my college career. An accomplished writer, but not teacherly at all. Unsympathetic and egotistical to the point where these qualities render anything positive about her and her class mute.

This woman is nothing but evil. I loved my first semester of Writing the Essay and got A's. She made my second semester hell and was nothing but disrespectful to everyone in my class. I did the work, I was polite, I worked to form my writing to her liking, but nothing worked. She also kicked a friend out of the class. AVOID HER.
yeah...don't do it. she picks favorites and is just not respectful of her students if you're not one of her favorites. She's condescending and harsh-she can't empathize. worst first semester ever

Amanda is a nice person, but a useless teacher.  She is very opinionated and set in her ways, she is an extremely harsh grader and has high expectations for her students. She is not helpful in comments nor conferences, and is just over all horrible at teaching WTE. Many of her discussions are interesting but irrelevant to essay help.

Amanda is a nice professor, definitely has her favorites. She not helpful at all while conferencing, and is a relatively harsh grader (depending on how much she likes you). Amanda also likes people to be on time and not tardy to class. Overall, she is cool, but isn't inspiring.
Essentially, she's Carrie Bradshaw. Consider yourself lucky if you get Amanda for WTE.

Amanda is a very good teacher. Her writing exerises prepare you well for writing the essays, however, she is rather unhelpful when it comes writing to the essay itself. Her written and verbal feedback is often vague and useless. She is also very opinionated and will debate with those who disagree. She has very high standards and expectations.

Amanda is proactive in her work and teaching. We have had very interesting conversations in class. She promotes a warm and cohesive classroom environment. She is interesting and fun to listen to. Her methods of teaching are unconventional and full of personal zest. Overall, I enjoyed her class. Fresh, challenging, mind provoking, and an experience.
Amanda is the best, nicest teacher i have ever had.  She's so sweet and really helpful!! I wish i could have her again!!

I actually had a pretty good conversation with her in our one and only writing conference that was completely unrelated to my essay and to writing in general, but regardless, she's an unhelpful teacher who blatantly encouraged/praised only two of the students and refrained from giving me helpful comments on my papers.

Amanda is truly amazing!  She is super sweet and very helpful!  She gives clear directions and tells you exactly what she wants.  She can be opinionated, and this turns some people off however, her opinions are interesting and worthwhile to listen to.  It is obvious that she is very intelligent and passionate about her work!
No Comments

Challenging but rewarding.  Amanda makes you work for your grade (but you'll be glad you did).  Interesting views on art...lots of great discussions so far.  She knows a lot about good writing and is very clear about what she wants.  She offers many useful tips.
very sweet and helpful
Amanda is an energetic prof and provides many practical ways to improve writing skills. Her love for the  English language is surprisingly infectious.
i always got the feeling that she didn't like my writing, and therefore i couldn't get above a b- in the class. very subjective and picky picky picky. didn't learn a thing.
The worst.  No help at all.  Can't look you in the eyes.
Everything drives her nuts.  including her own voice.
My most inconsistant and confused teacher ever. Don't try to learn anything in this class. Annoying. I couldn't stand her.
She is a very nice professor! The final project is interesting, and I really enjoyed the topic I chose.

Amanda was one of my favorite professors. She really ensures that you are heard during class conversations, and she makes it easy to participate. The nature of the course allows for group projects and personal assignments that allow you to apply media theory to topics and themes you enjoy. This helped me really retain information and media theory.

amazing professor! was hesitant because of the ratings but she's caring and clear about her expectations. as long as you show up to class ready to learn and participate this class will be an easy A for you. readings every week and discussion posts but nothing too difficult. interesting midterm and final project topics! I would recommend.

Amanda is a great professor who wants students to have a genuine interest in the culture industries, allowing us to apply our personal interests to projects and assignments. Lots of field trips, overall an easy and meaningful class.

I have never had a professor be so disrespectful and passive-aggressive in my time here at NYU. The way she grades the assignments makes no sense, she doesn't upload slides, and she has been flat out rude to her students multiple times, both in and outside of class. She is also very retaliatory toward those who do stand up for themselves. Beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: extremely unreasonable and super hard to communicate.
Amazing professor
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Pierce was an amazing professor who truly cares about her students and the course. If you have the chance to take her class, don't think twice you won't regret it.
Amira is honestly very caring and understanding. She is always open to extensions and has a straightforward grading criteria. She offers many extra credit opportunities to boost your grade.
I normally hate english, but professor pierce genuinely made this class enjoyable. Not sure why she's rated so low. one of the best courses just do your work, show up, and you'll have a good grade.

I took FYSEM-UA 900 (Betwixt and Between: Liminality). It has a grading contract, so if you do 3 extra credit assignments you get an A. I highly recommend taking this course, not just because it's an easy A but because the work was interesting and Amira is genuinely so kind. It's obvious that she loves teaching and cares about her students a lot.

(FYSEM-UA 900: Liminality) Very long, boring, and unorganized class. Amira clearly cares about her students, but it seemed like she was unprepared and she was learning with us rather than teaching us. She uses a grading contract where you get a B from doing all your work and can only get an A by doing 3 extra credit works, which are time consuming.

She is definitely a great teacher. She really cares about her student and is being really nice to us. She now grades on a new contract where you can definitely earn an A by your hardworking.Well organized classes and moderate workload. Some reading materials are confusing and hard to understand, and that is the only problem I can find in her class.

TAKE HER CLASS!!! A+++++++teacher. Best writing prof at NYU. A fair amount of work load and an equitable grading system. The learning process has been enjoyable. Offered multiple extra credit assignments to make up for grades.

I just graduated, but I'm coming to RMP to write Prof Amira a review, because looking back on my time at NYU, she was one of my favorite professors. This was my first class where I felt like I had an original thought that I was eager to write about, and it came from an office hour with her. I've got more to say but too few chars. Very cool person.

I agree that she is definitely underrated. She really gives me useful advice during our conference, and if we are not prepared during the early conference in the week, we can schedule another conference with her later in the week to discuss the essay. She is super nice, and the extra bonus is not that hard.

She is so underrated at RMP. I think she is the best writing professor. She is informative and helpful. Writing can be hard, but she would provide extra credits to boost your grade. Although there are many works, you do actually learn things from her class.

Amira is a kind, flexible, and hard-working professor. The lectures/assignments are carefully thought out and the grading system GUARANTEES a B+ if you complete each assignment. 
Amira cares deeply and integrates multimedia sources into her lectures, is always eager to meet outside of class to discuss progress, and asks deep, pertinent questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Piece is very caring and gives great feedback. She makes class super engaging and is hilarious as well. She gives great feedback on papers and meets with students before the drafts are due. I would highly recommend.

amira is really caring and engaging. not much hw and honestly, you don't need to put much effort in those little hw and exercises as long as you do your main essays properly on time. she's lenient on giving extensions. she's not lenient on grades, however, she gives really detailed feedback and you'll get an A towards the end of the course.

Prof Pierce is the best writing professor and perhaps also one of the best professors I have ever met. She might assign you a lot of homework, but you should always know that she is always there to help you overcome difficulties. If you want to success in her class, use her office hours well.

Professor Pierce is definitely not an easy A, but its totally possible as long as you go to class, do the work and take advantage of extra credit or revision opportunities. Pierce was one of the most caring and kindest professors and she really does want to see you succeed.

one of the best professors I met at nyu! she gives homework basically every class, but that's pretty normal for the expository writing courses. if you show your hard work, you'll receive a fair grade. office hours help

Writing the Essay with Professor Pierce was definitely a TOUGH class, but I found that the challenge was what I needed in order to improve as a writer. Ask her to read over your drafts because she gives great feedback. Sometimes the homework can be tedious and confusing, but as long as you put in the effort, her grading will be fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Her WTE class scared me so much based on what I had heard about her reputation. In all honesty, the class was a lot of work and definitely was the hardest class of the semester. She gives good feedback though which is good for improving your writing.
She is really kind. Professor Pierce cares about her students and tries hard to make the class interesting. I would definitely recommend taking her class.

She's nice and cares about what her students are thinking, changing her way of teaching based on the students' needs. Participate in her class, you will learn things.  Each homework assigned will be related to your essays, so try to think of the main theme of your essay as early as possible. Try not to be late or skip class. Not an easy grader.
She is so nice and not such a tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I was enthusiastic about writing at first. After taking this class, i did not learn much, yet felt writing is burdensome.
I choose Pierce for my writing sessions. She was immensely helpful and is bent on helping students no matter what. She also gives really good ideas.
Hard class
she struggles to convey what she expects from her students' works. She is also a very hard grader, most kids get Cs in this class.
Not helpful. Not clear in what she expects.

Pierce is a very charismatic professor however, she struggles to engage and convey information to her students. She is very helpful and is willing to help your writing but is very unclear on what she wants. In addition, she is very proud of keeping her C average in the class, despite the effort put in.
Gives a lot of assignments but is often unclear on what she actually expects. However, I think she's making an effort to remedy this.

Expository Writing is a confusing class and sometimes Pierce struggles to fully explain what she wants her students to do; however, if you ask for help, she will do her utmost and is in fact very useful.
There was a lot of writing in this class but I definitely learned a lot. She's nice, personable, and really helpful if you do the work.
I'd try to look for an easier wte teacher. She's a tough cookie. Not at all an easy grader.
The class is fairly challenging and she is not an easy grader, but she's a good teacher and keeps it at a very intellectual level. She's friendly and personable, as well.
She seems like a sweet teacher but she gives impossible hw assignments every class and takes pride in having a class avg of C no matter how hard you work.
Literally the best professor ever, and helps you with class registration like, a lot! She's so nice and relatable!
i'd give her a 6 if i could
literally so nice, such a good advisor 10/10 i could tell her anything

Amanda's the best. She's the perfect social worker - super empathetic - and an amazing professor. She truly makes spaces for everyone's experiences, and she made a large class feel smaller. The lectures were sometimes boring, but she brought in personal anecdotes from her work that made it more engaging. You'll miss out if you don't take her class.

One of my favorite professors this semester. She invites guest speakers to the class, and provides helpful lectures to get to more familiar with resources around you. The class atmosphere is good, and everyone shares his or her ideas freely. Take her lessons!
One of the best professors at NYU. Her classes fill up quick for good reason. She actually cares about students and likes to be a mentor.
I love Professor Nieliwocki! She's an amazing social worker and advisor! I totally recommend her for any classes she teaches. I hope to have her in the future if possible!

Write what she wants to hear (you get a generally clear idea of that via classes).
Go to her office hours each time before the essay and change according to her feedback (talk to her after class to get extra feedback)
She's a tough grader and I had to work so hard for the grade, but get on her good side and participate.

Overall, an amazing professor. Grades are determined by how dedicated you are to the readings, participating, and attending the class. I would say her grading is tough. If you go to her office hours, she gives great feedback for your essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera seems to be an ok professor who is passionate about what she teaches, but her grading is quite unreasonable. Even when going to office hours and speaking through ideas to get specific feedback, she still finds ways to bring down your final grade.
Amazing professor and really cares if you understand the concept and readings .

OK prof with interesting classes. 3 papers (1 per unit) - she does cap the grade on the 1st paper to do a gradual evolution. Grades rather toughly. Get on her good side from the beginning by participating. She is a rather average/slightly above average prof so idk why there seems to be sm hate in rmp.
Extremely biased, isnt open to your opinion and cruel grader. Avoid her at all costs.
She can be a harsh grader, but you will learn how to improve your writing skills. The readings are engaging, but if you're someone who doesn't like to participate, earning an A will be challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Rivera wants you to participate in her class and I strongly believe if you attend her and the TF's OH you stand a better chance of getting a good grade. Constantly show interest and participate in what is being discussed.

My class had a lot of participation so discussions were always interesting. As a teacher, I think she is underappreciated. She is definitely a tough grader but so is every C&C teacher. Super sweet person and I recommend going to office hours, if you pay attention you can learn a lot about how she wants you to write. TA was great too
DONT TAKE YOUR GPA WILL TANK

Boring as can be. Learned about nothing other than how to yap about what she wants to hear. hard grader. You don't really learn any material just see how business affects culture. She is nice in person but not when grading. No one really talks in class. Go to office hours and get her to like you (helps with grading)

She is so specific about how she wants you to write the essay, and even if you do that, it's somehow still not up to her standards. Seminar type of class so be prepared to discuss the book/movie each day. PARTICIPATE. There's a discussion post and journal every week, but they're easy A's. Sweet lady, but hard grader.

Paper grades were on the brink of the next letter by some decimal amount, which seemed purposeful. She has  specific ideas about what students should write in each paper, but be warned she'll only read one paragraph of your draft, so choose wisely. Ask the TA for more help, or just follow the ideas on her slides.
P.S. She says "right" a lot.

The only reason I got an A- was because I kissed up at the very end and put my literal 100% into the last essay. She wants very specific things and will give you a B if it isn't what she wants. Her in-class discussions are confusing and sometimes she leads the class in a strange way that is received in silence because everyone is confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
"right"
once you realize she says this word, it is super distracting and you also can't improve on essays and also doesn't give good feedback at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is nice but has specific ideas that she wants students to bring up which limits students' abilities to come up with their own points. She talks over many students or will reword their points in order to get conversations going in a specific direction but it feels like she disregards the student. Grades very harshly and takes a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think she is under appreciated. She is not the most lenient grader, but if you show up, participate and discuss ways to improve, she is very accessible and open to helping everyone.

Rivera is a great person and if you put in the effort to participate in class discussions, show initiative, go to her office hours and in general build a relationship with her your semester will go really well. She is a tough grader, definitely not an easy A.

Tough grader. Feedback on essays don't really make sense. On the last essay, I showed her my outline during office hours and she gave some comments on it. She told me to change some parts and to add some parts. I implemented them for the final essay, but in the feedback she told me to write about something completely different. Weird...

She is nice but marks meh. In my 3 essays, there is little (0.1pt) or no improvement. Also didn't publish grade breakdown at the end of the semester. She does give good feedback if you ask, also pushes you to analyze. She is flexible on deadlines tho, if you're a bit late and email her she won't take marks off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Rivera is a decent choice for a writing professor. She really challenges you to analyze texts thoroughly by facilitating class discussions. Classes can become quite dry sometimes though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: definitely dont take her class. other professors are much easier and actually grade fairly. you barely improve on essays and if you do maybe by like .1 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I cant say much about her grading style, as she eased her grading system due to COVID, but overall, shes a fair grader. Shes really nice too. Her class can get a bit dry sometimes and the essays you do in the class is often just professional essays. In general, her class was about urban centers and I think that was very interesting indeed.
Took his class randomly as an elective, but was amazed when it quickly became one of my favorite classes of all time. He's super engaging and listens to student feedback very well.

For ethics, hes great to take at the end of the day. He often lets students out early or has films related to class topics. Overall, he's also extraordinarily compassionate and understanding. He almost seems uniquely in tune with the issues Tandon students face. He cares and feels like a respected friend rather than professor. Offers extensions too

He's funny and an amazing professor. He makes crazy jokes and make sure the lecture is engaging so students don't feel bored (although I had him at 8AM). If you want a free A on top of your other hard classes i would suggest you take him. He doesnt give out weekly assignments, you really just have 3 essay assignment throughout the semester.

I had a great time being part of his lecture. He doesn't give out much assignments and definitely not a tough grader. The topics he goes over sometimes might be a bit weird at times though. But overall an amazing professor.
He is literally the best, I wish I could take all my classes with him.

One of the best professors at NYU. He is very caring, and you can learn a lot from his class. If you want a class that helps you take a break from all the difficult classes at NYU, take him. Show up to class and pay attention. The papers are a bit confusing, but if you ask him, he is very understanding and can help you out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is one of the most funny and kind teachers I have ever had. He really cares about his students and wants them to do well. He's so chill about the assignments and is really understanding. Take him! And treat him well!
An easy A where you actually learn at the same time! His class was a lot of discussion and we watched movies from time to time. The assignments are also not that difficult. Just show up lol.
Super chill guy will super chill assignments. If you just show up to class you're bound to learn some interesting stuff. Totally recommend taking him for ethics!
One of the best humanities professors at Tandon

Great, easy going professor. Genuinely interesting topics. Not much technology. You don't need to do the readings. Understandable and approachable. Minimal effort class, you can tell he cares about his students. Accommodating, overall great teacher and guy! You get a fun final that other professors wouldn't give. Would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Andrew is a good professor, he really cares about our thoughts and adjust his lectures.
Really great professor. Highly Recommend!
Really great professor, super understanding, easy to do well. Highly recommend!
GOAT! Very humorous teacher, his jokes are interesting.

Andrew is such a wonderful and knowledgeable professor. He really cares about what he's teaching and even brought in guest lecturers. He's super engaging, funny, and chill. He assigns a lot of reading but is open to our opinions on what we read, so the readings gradually became more interesting. I hight recommend any class he teaches.

Still halfway through the class. Wanted to feedback in case anyone is thinking of taking the course in the summer. What makes Prof Mims great is her experience in the CSuite a number of times. She covers academic material, so you have to read and stay up on current news. It's like being mentored every week for a leadership role. Do the homework!

Really liked the open sharing of professional experience that made some of the material come to life.
Working on teams is important, which I don't like, but it drove the point across that we work on teams out in the marketplace and learning to do so is important.
Great mentoring advice in the middle of lectures.

Participation is important and being prepared about the readings. A lot of class dialogue with students and the professor about topics. Professor shares her experiences and knowledge with class which is good. A lot of reading.
Participation matters as does having an opinion. Great class topics and case studies. Lots of reading. Great professor- best class of the 2 years.

Really great professor! Tons of actually business and C-suite experience so her cases and examples were very good and relevant. Inspiring to see a female minority make it so high up in business and academics. Great class. Recommend taking this course.

Do not take Professor Mim's class if you don't want to learn how to be come a critical consumer of the news, all things leadership and the world around you.
Do not take Professor Mim's class if you don't want become a more practiced public speaker. 
Basically, do not take Professor Mim's class if you don't want to grow.
She's great.

For the first half of the semester, she was extremely strict and graded things harshly. Her delivery and tone for her feedback/lecture were also combative, making for a tense environment. After the midterm, she improved a little, but still, this is a tough professor! You will learn some interesting things, but beware.
great professor，hard exams

I LOVE PROFESSOR BONEZZI SO MUCH I DON'T THINK I'VE EVER CRIED AT THE END OF A SEMESTER BEFORE. Take him, he genuinely is so caring and does his best to get you the best grade possible. He def gives girl dad energy and you will love him. TAKEHIM!!!!! you won't regret it
Professor Bonezzi truly cares a lot about his students learning. He is incredibly helpful and pushes students to participate during class. I would recommend him to anyone interested in marketing.

The best. He's the kind of professor you actually want to stay in touch with after the semester. Thoughtful and humble, with a lot of heart, but also sharp business instincts and strategic insight.
The course and exams are very manageable, and you learn a lot. You'll walk away with a solid, structured understanding of marketing. Highly recommend.
One of the most caring profs. I was so lucky to have him. He prepares you for the real world
Go to class and take basic notes and you will do great on exams. Only tests what is talked about in lecture. Most caring and kind and understanding professor.

engaging lectures, very chill! exams are lengthy, but doable with studying. lots of group projects but he's very understanding about people not pulling their weight. stretches the curve as much as he can. I completely failed the first midterm and still got an A. highly recommend for non-stern students -from a non-stern student

fav professor, gives girl dad energy. lots of group projects but from experience if someone isn't holding their weight hes super understanding. midterms are lengthy so def study & homeworks take a while to complete. class is basically all lecture & he says participation matters but i only spoke twice and still got an A albeit i attended all classes

Tests are pretty hard and I was below the cutoff for both of them. However, he stretched the curve much as possible and somehow I ended with an A. The 4 assignments are also pretty tough but overall if you put in the effort it is possible to get an A, but mostly matters on your group!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only 4 assignments + a semester long marketing project. Honestly learned a lot and really nice guy. Before grades were released, thought I was cooked bc the exams are a lil hard, then he mentioned how he stretches the Stern curve as much as possible to really help everyone and I ended with an A. Would def take!
Awesome Professor, really cares about students. Pay attention in class and you will do well. There are a lot of group projects which is slighty annoying but there's no final exam.

I took him for consulting capstone - he is the best professor for this course. He is extremely realistic in terms of how hard it is to work with a client and how subjective the case you receive can be. He doesn't care too much about grades and more about his students getting through the course. He is a great professor to come to for advice!

Professor Bonezzi is an exceptional educator who brings a unique blend of humor and genuine care to the classroom. His lectures are both informative and entertaining, making learning an enjoyable experience. While his tests are lengthy, they are not overly difficult.

This professor's classes are highly enjoyable and engaging. Through his course, I have gained a solid understanding of essential marketing principles. While the exams can be lengthy, they are not overly difficult. Additionally, the professor is compassionate and attentive to his students. I strongly recommend taking his class.

The homework can be very heavy but it's doable and you can work in teams. A lot of what he teaches is useful in an actual job and the homework really gives you a taste at what marketing in the real word is. If you want a useful course I suggest taking his class. Very funny and super approachable. He was nice to give me points back on my first exam.

Professor Bonezzi is of course very knowledgeable about the class content, but his passion really comes through as well. The course was well-structured, material was articulated in a manner that is easy to follow, grading was fair and appropriate, and the professor is available for one-on-one meetings and assistance when necessary.
Really good. Definitely cares about his students and does a very good job to create an interesting learning environment. Not TOO difficult. Fair grading. Basically everything you can really ask for.

Be prepared to do lots of work outside of class. Professor Bonezzi has great lectures that are engaging and insightful. But the class is homework heavy with 4ish assignments (taking 6-10 hours each) in the first half of the semester and a semester-long group project.

Professor Bonezzi is one of the nicest, most caring professors I have had at Stern. Homework assignments are time-consuming, but since there are only 4, it is doable. He genuinely wants to see his students succeed and very willing to help out students. Slides are easy to understand and tests are very fair and based on the material he covered.

Andrea is by far the best Marketing professor at NYU. There are basically 4 HW assignments and one group marketing assignment that you work on throughout the semester. You definitely have to know what you're doing in class in order to do the HW. But he's the best, he explains everything clearly, and is extremely flexible and caring about everyone.

Professor Bonezzi is one of the most knowledgable and caring professors I've ever had! Although this class (online) was homework/group project heavy, and you definitely need to study the slides on your own outside of class, I still learned alot from this intro course.

I would not take this class if I were you. It is definitely NOT an intro class. The lecture covers a lot of material and there is never time to go through all of it, so you will find yourself studying all alone. The group projects are at least 10-15 hr work per week and there is a lot of excel. Yes, you learn, but not an easy class. Very though gra

Well, it's hard to understand that he has a rate at 4.9 out of 5.0. Though he has great ppt that help you understand new concepts, you have to learn those lectures by yourself, since he might not be able to go over all important concept, and his homework is pretty hard like one project with over 10 hrs work every two weeks. If you have time,its ok
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IT IS WAY TOO MUCH WORK. I don't know if the prof increased the course load because of covid, but each assignment takes HOURS to do, and he ensures that there is one due every second week. Assignments range from 1000-3500 words and include huge presentations and excel sheets (for an intro class!)

Professor Bonezzi is a super caring professor. Hes always available to talk about anything, truly a great professor that ACTUALLY cares about students. The class itself is very practical. All slides he use are very easy to understand. Tests are not bad and after this class, you will have a solid understanding about marketing! Definitely recommend!

Prof. Bonezzi is a great guy, very helpful, entertaining and clear. His lectures are very well structured and so are his slides. He gives you a very good basis in Marketing. Tests are pretty long and homework can be very hard. The group project is not so bad cause it involves a lot of creativity. I would absolutely take him again!

Very helpful guy, clear and simple lectures, easy tests that follow the slides posted online. The few assignments, however, are impossible if you don't know what you're doing and the group project makes or breaks your grade. You definitely have to work for your grade.

Bonezzi is a great guy and always willing to help. That said, he (or his TAs) are tough graders on assignments and on the final group project. Tests are an easy A, but the project is worth more of your final grade and you will work on it a LOT. Readings are  unnecessary and participationattendance is a big part of grade.
Amazing professor; goes out of his way to help and the class isn't tricky; just read his PPTs and you're set
Interesting, passionate, and probably the best professor I've had at Stern so far. Really into helping his students, will provide adequate time to discuss your own problems and concerns
One of the best professors. He really really cares about his students. He is helpful and funny too. Just take his class no matter what

One of the best professors I've had. Cares a lot about helping any way he can. Makes himself available all the time. The class is very straightforward. Midterm/final are 15% each and they are straight off his PPT slides, no curveballs. You study and you get an A. The mkt project is very interesting as well. A bit of work involved but it's an A.

Great professor. Responds to emails extremely quickly, and if you have in-depth questions he asks you to call him at his personal number -- sometimes even as late as midnight. Although the class itself isn't hard, he makes it interesting and engaging. Sad he isn't teaching any other courses.
Very helpful, very clear, but a lot of group work. Really sucks if your group mates don't care or arent as hardworking. Overall, great professor.

Great class, could not recommend a better Intro to Marketing class.  Very manageable workload.  Interesting cases that are applicable in the real world.  Most of the information on the quizzes and final exam are based on the power point slides.  Definitely Take!!!!
Awesome professor! Definitely one of the best classes in Stern and very applicable to real life situations. He is funny and very helpful, the classes are mostly based on powerpoint slides.

GREAT PROFESSOR! Lectures are interesting. Will help you if you need any questions and does a great job of making himself available out of class. Grades are based on participation, case studies (which he lets you do in groups), and tests which are very fair.

Excellent professor. I have never learned more from a class than I have from his. I have frequently applied what I have learned in his class. He is extremely clear and explains things very well, with good examples. Very engaging. He always makes himself available to help students. Tests aren't easy, but if you go to class and study they aren't bad.

He's awesome. Entertaining, funny, very helpful, and bases the class almost entirely on his slides. The quizes are a little bit difficult but easily manageable if you study and pay attention in class. I recommend him 100%.

He's a great professor. He's very kind and understanding, but also very clear and easy to understand. He'll help you if you need any questions and does a great job of making himself available. You couldn't ask for much better in an introductory level class.
I love this class so much. The exams aren't hard if you study a fair amount and read. Amazing.

Such a fantastic professor! Graded on 4 essays and a 2500-word final paper. It is a bit of work, but his enthusiasm and cheerfulness make the class worth it. You must participate in the class to do well. Would recommend and willing to take againn

I LOVED Prof Needham!! Took him + Stephen Gross for C&C and they were both amazing. Lectures were very engaging and he loves cracking a good dad joke. Obviously cares a lot about the topic and his students and does his best to make every class interesting. Not too much reading outside of lecture and 3 short essays that make up the grade.

Cultures & Contexts with Andrew and Stephen was a great class. 3 essays (reasonable difficulty but somewhat time consuming), a midterm and a final. Available for office hours for help. They had us choose between the last essay or the final exam instead of doing both at the end, which was a reliever. Overall would recommend.

Prof. Needham is AMAZING!! You can tell he actually cares about his students and the material he's teaching. He's kind, quirky, and cracks lots of jokes. Took him (with Prof. Gross) for my Cultures & Contexts requirement and I highly recommend #dreamteam. Midterm and final were easy. Plus we had weekly readings/discussion posts. Take him!! :)

Professor Needham is phenomeal. I had him for Environmental History of NYC. The class consisted of in-depth lecture and field trips to environmental sites in NYC. Really unique way of teaching, yet he was able to connect with everyone in the class. Lenient grading, approachable, and open to different viewpoints on topics.

Needham is hands down a really good professor and a very flexible one at that. My problem is that he is one of those professors that is too interested with the small details as opposed to the big ideas. Take him if you have a genuine interest in the minor details otherwise you will be bored out of your mind with irrelevant names and dates.

Needham's seminar was great. The readings were relevant and he did a good job leading discussions and getting the most out of his students. Very down to earth guy, approachable and understanding. He genuinely cares about students and their thought/opinions. Highly recommended.

Great lectures which are chock full of information. He's very smart and extremely thorough. Uses many different sources to teach the material: books, movies etc. The final paper is a **** though. 10-12 page research paper but he does a good job of helping you if you ask. Too bad the TA's do the grading and not him.

I had Prof. Needham as a lecturer and as my thesis advisor. He's great at both. He gives students the time they deserve. He listens well and helps you to sort out your own ideas about history. Very encouraging and thought-provoking.  In addition to all this, he is probably the most down to earth professor I've had at NYU.  I highly recommend him.

Needham is the best. Very enthusiastic and knows his stuff. Plus he actually cares about his students. The reading is a bit intense, but as long as you pay attention you can usually figure out what's going on. The people who complained about the class were the ones who weren't doing the work in the first place. It's a challenge, but it's worth it

Professor Needham is the best professor I ever had at NYU. The material of the course (US Hist. Since WW2) is extremely interesting, and I felt that all of the grading is far. The only way you could possibly do badly in his class is by being a bad student to begin with.

The professor is a nice enough guy, but the class is full of reading (300+ pages a week). The TAs run the class, and grading is ridiculous. Everyone gets a B on the midterm, and TA-professor continually screw students over. If you want to maintain a high GPA avoid this class at all costs. I dont even think the TAs could get an A the way they grade.

his lectures are well organized, and straightforward, but he's not afraid to deviate from them. he's into asking the students to respond to the material, which I like. in a fairly big class I felt very engaged. tons of reading though. attendance isnt taken, but I never wanted to skip, and when I did felt quite guilty. take his class you'll love it

My only complaint would be that he focused a bit too much on local history for a survey course.  Other than that, a really good professor and class.  Heavy emphasis on writing, critical thinking, and discussion. No rote memorization- all writing (including the final exam) is open-ended and subject to your interpretation. And he's a really nice guy.

The class can be a little nerve-wracking because participation matters and you get called on but overall it's pretty straight forward. The exams are super to the point and should be relatively easy/ do-able as long as you pay attention and do the work. The professor is kinda silly but really nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: These ratings are all so misleading. The professor was very clear and understanding and made the material very enjoyable. He gave 45 questions to study for the final (and spent a class reviewing it) and asked 20 of those exact questions as the final-nothing is a surprise in this class and he only tests on what he says he will. GREAT CLASS. (Lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super easy for a 4 credit class, if you don't mind looking at dead bodies and commuting 30 minutes to the hospital. The only hard part was that there weren't any other grades outside the midterm and the 10 question final. Super nice professor but his accent can be hard to understand. Homework and textbook were optional because he never checked them

Extremely disorganized in both lecture and lab. No teaching standards whatsoever. Final grade is entirely dependent on a single exam, with test material scattered and unpredictable. The cadaver lab exam is ONLY 10 questions.. How is this fair at all? This puts students at a severe disadvantage because one mistake can severely impact your grade.

Probably one of the worst professors I have had at NYU. Incredibly disorganized as we would never know what would be on our exams. I was extremely uncomfortable in his cadaver lab. Dr. Aqua did not make this environment any better for me and was blatantly rude towards me when I did not want to get near the dead body.

Wish I could take his class again x100. Aqua genuinely cares for each one of his students as humans, not just as bodies in a classroom. He's goofy sometimes, but he knows what he's talking about. Take good notes, be present and respectful in his classroom, and you'll have an amazing ally and mentor in a professor for the rest of your time at NYU.

I took two courses with Dr. Aqua and wish I could take a million more. He has taught me more than I ever thought I could learn. Hands down the best professor ever. He wants the best for all of his students and will do anything to help you out. His classes are hard but if you pay attention and study the right material you will do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Aqua is beyond amazing. NYU is a tough school and anatomy classes are tough but Dr. Aqua is the best that you will get. He is so inspiring and genuinely wants students to learn. Do the readings, take good notes, memorize key concepts and tell him when you need help. Dr. Aqua is the best there is, no one can convince me otherwise
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's awful. Worst teacher I've ever had at NYU. He expects you to memorize everything the entire human body in a week because he never talks about what actually is on the test for the entire year until a week before the exam. Then he throws up ten more units to learn yourself. He talks down to students and is awful to be around. Avoid this class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For a subject as difficult as anatomy, it's very frustrating that he doesn't teach it in a very linear and meaningful way. It often feels like you're learning random facts and therefore it's hard to see how all the parts of the body interrelate. Very unreasonable about his attendance policy and he did not make himself available for office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst teacher ever. Unclear, unorganized and hard to understand what in the world he is saying through that strong Nigerian accent.

If you have professor Aqua, I have news for you: you are in a difficult field! Get over it, or change majors. OF COURSE class is hard, the subject is hard! Professor Aqua is one of the BEST professor I have had in my 4 years at NYU. VERY clear, very approachable. Even remembered me on the street months after I had him. Beautiful eyes to boot! LOVE!
HARD class. very annoying man. did i mention that this class was hard? total gpa killer :(

Exams are pretty much just from his lecture notes. Reading the textbook helps also. Weekly quizzes which force you to keep up with the material and he tells you exactly what you need to know for the quizzes. Exams are very fair. Final is not cumulative. Overall great professor. I would strongly recommend this course.

If you are pre-med and need to take an anatomy class, you BETTER take Dr. Aqua's anatomy class. Yes, his class is difficult because, let me tell you, THE HUMAN BODY IS COMPLEX!!  If you are going into a healthcare field you better know the body inside and out.  Dr Aqua is the best and really wants all of his students to learn!!

You basically have to memorize everything. There is no homework so you have to keep up with the readings everyday. I had him 8am in the morning and attendance is mandatory. The exams were extremely specific. If you are pre-med and want to take an anatomy class, avoid him.

The best advisor EVER. She is actually so awesome. Has helped me with soo much so far in my academic career. From studying abroad to graduating earlier, from picking course classes, AND to helping me with situations with professors, Ashley is so supportive and caring. Also she responds so fast to emails and very quick to reach. She is a gem to MCC!

SHE IS THE BEST ADVISOR! 
i love her personality!!! my favourite person in all nyu!
She is the best, love her!!

Ashley is truly awesome! She's super kind, supportive, and makes every class fun. She answers emails quickly, offers flexible office hours, and always makes new students feel at home. Her TAs are fantastic too! This seminar made starting at NYU so much smoother for me. Such an amazing class and professor! Pick her as your advisor!

Ashley was a great professor. She made her expectations for the class very clear, which made it easy to do well in her class. If you want to learn how to excel in the professional world, you will not regret taking this class with Ashley.

Ashley is the best professor I have taken at NYU. Interviewing Strategies is a professional elective for my major, and I thought it was going to be a lot harder than it ended up being. Class was super chill, and Ashley is the reason I loved this class. Highly recommend, cannot recommend enough to those needing a 2 credit course

Ashley is so nice and approachable and she tries her best to make the class engaging. she respects everyone and supports us to achieve our professional goals. Always available in her office hours and she provides sweets if you go to her office. nice, caring, and amazing!
Hard class but if you keep up with communication and stay on top of things you'll be fine. Intense and helpful lectures - picture heavy. Get ready to take notes.

Zoned out entire lecture but her review sheets are helpful for midterms and finals (though it's just a whole list of vocab). I never read any of the required books and had a great recitation instructor. The professor is extremely knowledgeable but attending lecture felt like fighting sleep every time. So many essays oh lord, grading took forever.

Pros- easy lectures to follow, test questions entirely lecture based (no need to do readings for the most part)

Cons- totally inaccessible via email, takes forever to grade things, essay instructions not always clear and even if you write the essay entirely according to the instructions, she will still find ways to take off points

Professor Roth has had a very long career in Egyptology, which shines through in her lectures. However, she is hard to reach outside of class. I sent multiple emails requesting an extension on a paper and did not receive a response.

Horrible lecturer. Rambles on and on. Does not upload slides (slides are just pictures though). Unclear essay grading criteria although the "instructions" doc for each essay is 5 pages long. Thinks that your life revolves around her class. Avoid. Takes forever to grade too. Harsh curve (stern curve) in class as well.

Run. Lecture and reading heavy. Rambles on and on about one image on the slide during class and makes notes inaccessible to students. Takes 10 years to grade one paper. Takes another 10years to post midterm reviews. Only posts essay prompt a couple of days before it is due
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Roth is knowledgeable and passionate but, the class is disorganized. She takes a very long time to grade and is always behind on lectures. She gives reviews before exams but it's 500 slide images and keywords so it's not very helpful. You really must show up to class to do well. I would take this class only if you are really interested

She's very passionate and knowledgeable about the topic she teaches so if you enjoy it and find it interesting you will get a lot out of this class. That being said if you don't then the lectures are incredibly dry. Attendance matters and additionally the work load for this class was pretty high. Four essays + two exams + mandatory recitation

I loved Ancient Egyptian Art with Prof. Roth! I learned an incredible amount in one semester. A complaint I heard from students (Art History majors) was that she teaches "more like an egyptologist and archaeologist than an art historian." The fact is, ancient art in extricably linked to archaeology and thus its necessary to teach as such.

One of the most interesting courses I've taken. When she explained non-existence, it changed how I saw the whole course up to that point and the ways it was possible to envision the world as a whole. Memorizing some definitions is necessary, but completely doable even without doing every reading if listen to lectures & attend recitation

Professor Roth is kind and very obviously knowledgable about Ancient Egyptian Art and Egypt in general however this class was rather opaque. She uses a lot of jargon and throws a TON of information at you in one go. The content is fairly inaccessible, to be honest. It is very clear she is an Egyptologist before she is an Art Historian.

Was an ok class. Says that textbooks are mandatory but got away without buying nor using one for the entire semester so double check if you actually need the txtbook. harsh grader but is a little lenient when it is visible that you are trying. get ready to read and write

nice lady but a terrible teacher. Lectures were so disorganized that sometimes it felt like shes just spitting out whatever stuff that came to her mind. lots of papers to write but graded leniently. exams were easy. never did the readings and still got A-. overall relatively easy grade but terrible learning experience, would suggest not taking her.

I thought she was a decent prof--don't see why her ratings are so low. The subject matter of her lectures is interesting and she has a kind of dry wit I found funny. Pretty manageable workload (4 6-page papers and a midterm and final) and I found I didn't really need to do the readings if I paid attention in lectures. Slow grader though.

She's is amazing. She takes a while to grade essays but it was fairly easy to get an A on them. Tests are easy if you attend lecture, do like half the readings. There is a lot of vocab to learn, but she makes the fundamental concepts so clear and interesting that they are easy to learn in relation. Non-existence lecture was brilliant & eye-opening.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took cultures and context Egypt and all I have gotta say is... I would encourage you not to unless you are insanely educated beforehand regarding Egypt's mythology, geography, and every single cultural landmark, and I mean, every. single. one. Even if this is your last resort, it's not worth it. Please take another culture class next semester.

This class was super difficult. Her lectures are boring. Tests are ridiculous. Memorizing the whole map of Egypt with no dots and no word bank. Specific open ended questions on something she mentions once. Too many lengthy essays. Don't do the readings because they're completely useless. The notes you take in the lectures are what's on the test.

She's nice but the lectures are insanely dense. Tomorrow is the final and i have only received grades for essay one (worth 5%) and the midterm (15%). I never got feedback on a previous essay before i submitted another one so never knew how to improve. asked multiple times for feedback before the final, she didn't answer. really saddened by this.

She was nice and the class was easy as long as you payed attention in lecture. However, she is a strict grader when it comes to essays. 
Personally, the recitation for this class was completely unhelpful and a waste of my time.

The fing worst. You expect me to write 12 pages on a fragment of a fragment of a stela that has, like, 2 things  going on in it? It's like you don't even realize you ARE NOT THE CENTER OF NYU I HAVE OTHER HOMEWORK!

I LOVE Prof. Roth! This class was wonderful and her knowledge/experience is amazing. Two essays + a midterm & final (zero hw)... if you go to lecture and take notes you should be fine. All reading assigned is truly for supplemental purposes and I would have been fine without reading them. She is super accessible but does take long to grade things.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Egyptian Art, didn't know much about it going in, feel like a pro going out. You learn a lot, which has pros and cons. Definitely challenging, I take so many notes every class, and computers aren't allowed. There's a lot to memorize, so you have to put in the effort. If you do it's very rewarding, she's passionate and has great secret insights.

Phenomenal professor teaching a fascinating course. Prof. Roth doesn't just teach dry facts about Ancient Egypt, but gives really interesting lectures on the *worldview* behind their society (the "nonexistence" lecture was amazing). If you're looking for a professor whose enthusiasm towards the subject is infectious, this is the one!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she's pretty strict on things like attendance and deadlines but her lectures are incredible. class isn't easy by any means, but if you're really in it to learn i can't imagine a better professor. so, so knowledgeable and passionate with personal anecdotes about everything. occasionally goes on tangents but they're usually interesting.

I was in professor Roth's Culture & Context core class and I ended up loving it. There's barely any graded homework and the readings are relatively quick all you have to do is go to class and take notes. The lectures are heavy but I always came out feeling like I learned a lot. She knows her subject perfectly and you can see she is passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is very knowledgeable about the subject. Lectures can be hard to follow and hard to retain what is necessarily crucial to remember. 4 2000 word papers with hard deadlines and don't get grades back until end. Feedback is minuscule and can take a while to receive a response. Lots of readings before every class to be ready for class.

4 six-page papers, a midterm (with two essays), a final, and recitation writing assignments. lectures are crazy hard to follow and very disorganized. grading takes forever with very little meaningful feedback. so exhausting. would not take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Heavy class, but once you get a pattern you get lots from it. Professor is very, very intellectual and knowledgeable of the subject. Lecture heavy, but midterms and finals could be relatively easy-graded.

Professor Roth is one of the worst professors I have ever had. She assigned two quizzes, three papers, and a final exam for the semester and only ever got around to grading two quizzes and nothing else. She is lecture-heavy and tests on information that isn't discussed clearly. There is also a ton of reading. Don't take the class unless you have to
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: LECTURES VERY HEAVILY. But I'm a heavy lecture person so that's fine for me. Spends a lot of time to grade hw. I got my essay I turned in mid October in early Feb. Knowledgeable but a bit disorganized. Eager to help and approachable in person, but not email. Tests aren't hard but so many details to remember (my final study guide was 44 pgs)

Low commitment class that will have you write 4 papers and take two exams. For a core class, that isn't bad. The lectures are unstructured, but taking good notes is possible as long as you sit in the front so you can catch what she says. Posts study guides for exams but doesn't post powerpoints. Attendance sheet passed around see who is there.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Insane lecture style. Waffles all over the place and mixes stuff on the exam with personal asides. Not really textbook based and no handout notes. Does not publish the overheads. If you invest the time you can pass this but I would not take this again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Took Cultures and Contexts. Knowledgeable on the subject, doesn't necessarily translate to her being an good or even adequate professor. Goes off on tangents/shows up late, not to mention that she takes an extreme amount of time to grade work. inconsistent grading. Got my course grade a month and a half after the semester ended. DO NOT TAKE
Professor Roth is overly interested in the subject and is unclear as to what information is relevant and what is just her going off on tangents. Incredibly boring and lots of work.

I don't understand how she has such low ratings! I have to agree with some of the critiques about her lecture style - she's so enthusiastic about Egypt that, at times, she doesn't realize (or perhaps just doesn't care) when she's dragging on and on and on... However, she's extremely helpful and understanding, and I know that by experience.

Loves Egypt, but too much. Would rather hear her own voice than teach. Doesn't learn students names. Values her social life over class. Shows up late often. Takes months to grade papers that shouldn't take more than a week, two at most. Constantly changes due dates. Unorganized. Can't remember what she has/hasn't gone over.  Got tenure & gave up.
She gave interesting lectures (at 8am so it was hard to stay awake). Midterm and final were pretty straight forward. 4 papers to write, all straight forward. Grades fairly

I didn't know that Art History could be boring, until I had this professor.  Completely unhelpful.  Unclear.  Late on returning emails, assignments, posting reviews.  She may just need some more teacher training...

Roth is an organizational mess and always late. Essay grading is skewed; they have a strange system where your essays aren't graded by one person, but shuffled between Roth and the TAs. Essays were graded anally. Midterm easy. Attendance graded. Lectures unclear. Overall, not an easy or fun class. Take another Cultures and Contexts.

By far the WORST class I have ever taken. When grading essays, the professor and two instructors have completely different and subjective approaches leading to an incorrectly skewed grading curve of the class. Recitations were enjoyable but did not relate to lectures. Lectures were unorganized and incomprehensible. I HIGHLY regret taking this class

She was such a terrible and unorganized professor. It was really difficult to study for the final because the textbooks don't help. The lectures are disconnected, and the class fails to have an overarching theme. It just seems like a bunch of facts to learn. The TAs were somewhat nice but even they were pretty harsh in grading the essays.

This was the worst class I have ever taken. I signed up for it thinking that learning about ancient Egypt would be fascinating, but her dry lectures put me to sleep and studying was impossible as she NEVER teaches from the textbooks. I'd recommend this class if your life revolves around the Egyptian culture, much like hers does.
