I had her for Culture & Contexts: Egypt. The course was sort of interesting but really have to take good notes since she doesn't put up powerpoints. Points deducted for non-attendance so show up. Clear grading policy on how to get an A; just pay attention and do well on the final/midterm/2 essays

She is a wonderful teacher. Her lecture are sometimes confusing but if you are confused a visit to her office hours are very helpful. She has a wealth of information to share especially if you ask specific questions. Also, she is active on dig sites in Egypt giving her personal experience with the material she is teaching.

Easiest class I ever took, don't need to read, just pay attention to what she says in class. The stuff that's on the test is stuff she says over and over again. Tests were exactly like the study guides.
She's insane.  And rude.  The TA's are wonderful, though.

Lectures aren't bad as people say and the material is interesting but she refuses to post the power points. Tends to go over important ideas quickly while babbling about unimportant ones so you have to be attentive in class. Not easy A MAP course & lots of memorization required. Grade depends largely on your TA. A = good papers & knowledge of terms

unbelievably bad. massive amounts of reading which have often seem to be simply punishment (as they have no connection to tests and are far too long to actually be done). I feel rather sad that she is this obsessed with ancient egypt. just when i thought i knew the definition of boring there ol' macy roth goes beatin out my expectations!

i took her world cultures: ancient egypt and the near east class thinking it would be really interesting. no. there was an ungodly ammount of reading, and we mostly focused on the history-not the culture.

i took her Con West course my freshman year. utterly useless waste of time. she lectures straight from a powerpoint and conveniently references her own work throughout the class. recitation was almost as bad. worst class ever. only useful if, like her, egypt is your life. otherwise, avoid roth at all costs.

An unfortunate waste of money, time and "effort". I took the Archaeology of Ancient Egypt class... and though the material presented was interesting, Roth was incredibly unfocused, rude, and unhelpful. Her tests were very specific and unrelated to the material presented at lectures. Roth needs to go back to her dig site and let someone else teach.

I agree with all of the posts on this World Cultures class. I would never recommend it. It pretty much destroyed any further interest in the subject. Long boring lectures containing very little information except some art details. Absolutely unrelated and useless recitations. I don't think I ever dreaded a recitation more. I repeat, do not take.

Completely agree with the below post--makes a very interesting subject unbearably boring. Lectures are very unfocused and all over the place, so it's very hard to make any sense out of them. Tests are extremely specific, focusing on esoteric Egyptian terms. Don't take the class--it's awful, unhelpful, and a waste of time.

Professor Roth is very enthusiastic and excited about Egyptology. The lectures are sometimes interesting, but often she keeps talking monotonously whilst using powerpoint and I just fall asleep. Tests are nitpicky but not terribly hard if you study a lot. Recitation was a waste of time every time. Overall I do not recommend this class.

She knows so much about Egypt, which is incredible; however, the lectures can be boring because the lights are off and it is a powerpoint presentation every lecture. Tests were hard and the recitations didn't help one bit. In one recitation, we talked about Santa Claus. What a waste of time.

Poor lady, she's so fascinated by her own lectures... its a shame all the rest of us fall asleep as a result of boredom.  Lectures are all powerpoint pictures; nothing helpful.  Roth's a little on the disheveled side, doesn't return graded papers, constantly forgets to post assignments.  She makes the interesting subject unbearingly boring.
very knowledgable, her lectures/semesters are a little disorganized because there's so much information.  A very interesting class if you actually attend lectures and do the museum visits.

She clearly loves her subject (Egypt, that is, not the Near East), but wow. I never thought a class could be this painful to get through. Her Powerpoint slides are mainly like a home slideshow ("Here I am with some pyramids, here I am with the Sphinx..."), and the lectures give absolutely no info. My interest in the subject? Completely killed.
Amazing class, amazing teacher.  The only class I've ever taken at NYU where I never looked at the clock once during any lecture.  Very interesting material, tough but fair grader

Worst prof I have ever had. Very smart but lazy and apathetic about her students. Rude, late (everyday 15min). She did not hand our papers back for 2.5 months (a day before our second papers were due). She did not return our midterm for 2 months. Ridiculous waste of money. Beautiful topic but terrible prof. Only hard because she does not care.

She is in love with what she teaches which is amazing. If you love the subject, ancient egypt, then you will love the class. Its all lectures with slides, though and a final research paper.  Not hard if you pay attention. I loved it.

sweet guy. he kind of gets off topic compared to the slides at times. you might fall asleep during his 8 am lectures. basically zero homework though and he's a nice grader. you can get through this class easily and the projects are not too difficult, pretty interesting too.
Best professor

Very easy class, not too many homework. Exams were online with one group project. Attendance is not mandatory but you are expected to participate and participation grade is a big portion of your final grade, so you should show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: No homework. Attendance is not required, but it helps. One online midterm that you have the whole day to do. One final group project. He cares about learning and not tests. Must take.

Professor Ash was amazing! He grades very few assignments. He gives the class the option to do the midterm and final online or in person. Lectures can be boring. He doesn't take attendance, but I suggest still attending because he will notice if you're not there and won't be as lenient with you. Participation matters. Easy A and great connection!

Professor Ash is truly one of the best professors I had so far. His class is super easy and chill, lectures are super interesting, he's super knowledgeable. I'd definitely take him again. Midterm and quizzes were online, attendance is not taken but I still attended all of his 8am's because he's truly amazing.

Professor Kohli is one of the best Professors I've ever had. He is extremely encouraging, taking his time to understand and help each one of his students. His class structure and grading is clear, organized, and straightforward. He has inspired me to now pursue my master's in accounting. Would 10/10 recommend taking his class!

Professor Kohli is a very inspiring professor. The Course was clear, practical, and full of real-world cases. He encouraged me to push my limits, gave career advice, and his guidance helped me a lot when finding internships and a full-time role. He truly cares, motivates students to aim higher, and supports career growth. Highly recommend.

One of the best courses I took in undergrad! The classes are engaging, efficient, and the time honestly flies by. The professor makes the lessons interactive and is very approachable. He also helps with interview prep, resume building, and even offers personal mentorship if you reach out. Highly recommend if you are pursuing a career in finance!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best finance prof at Tandon. Kohli cares about students, helps with resumes and interviews, and preps you for IB or RE. Tests aren't bad, and he is generous in extra credit. Only teaches at NYU in the fall, so prep ahead of time to avoid D'Emic. Take advantage of his industry knowledge to get ahead in career stuff.

Fantastic professor! 
His lectures are truly inspiring, and his enthusiasm for teaching is infectious. He genuinely cares about the success of his students and offers excellent resources to help students prepare for a career in finance. 
I will take him again 100%.
Very unorganized, would not take this class again.

Pretty bad, seemingly the entire of this site knows. The moments of compassion for students number in the seconds. Then, boom! No help, actively rude. Kid was crying once. I asked for advice, got limited advice but did my best and then she had a go at me in front of the class. I barely could see this happening in a HS let alone a Uni.
I've taken two of her courses, and really appreciated her open minded style (all questions are welcome) and her conversational approach to guiding students through difficult material.

Extremely bad professor from all angles. Worst professor I had by far by how she treats students. Enjoys insulting students in front of everyone. Once as the class ended she intentionally started shouting AT me so others could hear it. Immature, Full of complex and misery. I genuinely wonder why the department still has her as a teacher. GG prof!

The whole class would get together after class ended to comfort whichever student she made cry that day. Prof Astrinaki clearly had stuff going on in her personal life and took it out on us. Once I was absent because I had to go to my grandmother's funeral and another student told me that she made fun of me in class and called me a liar. Disgusting

The only class I've taken at NYU where I truly learned nothing. She assigns TONS of busy work that is never graded and she never gives feedback. Lectures and class discussions were all over the place. Weekly readings from textbook were almost never relevant to the class discussion of the week. avoid avoid avoid
Totally different from any professor I've ever had, I wouldn't recommend. You are made to do a lot of useless work and the format for class discussions is horrible.

I've never had an instructor, in college or before, who went after students with such personal terms in front of the entire class, and so unreasonably. She is unclear in her assignments and then gets angrily upset when students don't meet her unknowable expectations. Avoid at all costs.
Does not give good feedback, very hard to know what you are doing wrong. Excessive amount of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took C&F and learned a TON. Online wasn't great but the content was fantastic, would recommend! Some films were very hard to watch (graphic holocaust depictions). The convos had a ton of structure which I found a bit limiting, but she was very kind and always offered office hours. Our time dif was definitely a bit rough too since she was in Greece.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Astrinaki is a very understanding person if you submit something late once or have trouble with an assignment but she will call you out in class if you're clearly not doing what she asked for. She is a caring person who wants the best for her students. She realizes she ask for a lot so she is more open to discussion.

She is lovely and always willing to help outside of class. The class is extremely interesting and not that difficult. She is very knowledgeable in the field. That being said, if you are rude in class (go on your phone/don't pay attention/don't do the readings) she will call you out on it, which I felt was completely valid.
Awesome and sweet lady! Seminar on modern greek culture was a very interesting class, I got to look at all forms of art. Just don't forget to cite sources in your papers.

She isn't a bad professor. Yes, the readings are challenging, and the lectures can be repetitive, but she actively seeks feedback and offers strategies to help. YOU have to advocate.Her readings are long and complex. She does a midterm paper which she breaks down the assignments. I wouldn't take the class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super lecture heavy class. Readings were frequent and dense but not super necessary for class. Prof. Tsaturyan was very passionate and seemed disappointed when people did not share that, especially in not participating. No exams but heavy weighted projects/papers

TA's grade your assignments and 2 papers total. It is lecture heavy, with small bits of partner/group discussions. Weekly units are tied in to readings, recommend you to skim them and take notes. Prof. can be a bit sassy at times but honestly wants the class to engage. Participation matters. First half is theory based, second on topics/culture wars
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're a lecture person, this course is not your choice, but if you're not, then this course is perfect for you. This prof can be boring and "passive-aggressive" when lecturing, but the midterm and final are not really related to what she talks about bc you can choose your own topics. And if you wanna participate in class, do the daily readings.

Ok, so you probably have noticed the ratings below that this prof is "passive-aggressive" during lectures, but actually her grading system isn't bad. My grades on the midterm and final papers are B and A-, respectively, and the prep assignments for the papers are graded for completion. Everything is graded by the TAs who are indeed a lot nicer.

Trust me it gets better in the second half of the semester(material-wise). She IS passionate about the subject but her sassiness at times is too much. I'd recommend you to skim the readings to get a general understanding, reads off script for lectures but values feedback. 2 papers, first is a culture war issue, second is an interview analysis
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Complete honesty. Lecture topics are interesting and prof is definitely knowledgable, not taking away from that. However, this class is genuinely boring in the way that its executed. The prof actually cares about the well-being of her students. She assigns work but this is college; she came from an ivy so she assigns actual work as opposed to 1/2 of the profs here. idk why ppl are acting like she's unaware of the class atmosphere. she has literally asked for our feedback-why don't these reviewers say it to her face

reviews.comment: Take these other reviews with a grain of salt! Yes, the homework & lectures can be somewhat repetitive-but its supposed to build up as the semester goes on. reviews.comment: Felt fine about her in the first few classes. She was passionate about teaching and the homework was OK overall. However, we discovered her issues after a few sessions. She pressures us when she doesn't think we participate enough and is kinda impatient and upset if we don't answer her questions. The classroom atmosphere is dull, cold, and passive.

She is the absolute worst professor. She's so rude & passive aggressive which makes people not want to participate, but she gets upset & makes sly comments when no one participates. This is NOT a safe space! Don't take this class if it's not required. 

She also doesn't like us looking at our computers during a discussion & when she's talking (???)

The course's readings and overall content are interesting, but she is by far the worst professor I've had in my three years at NYU. Passive aggressive, sarcastic (and not in a good way), and always has her ways to lower the energy in the room. I am always so discouraged to speak up in class by the way she teaches.

Passionate about the subject but not a qualified lecturer by any means. The content is not difficult and relatively interesting, but the lectures are so dull. There's a lot of cold calling in class and odd passive aggressiveness toward students. Feels like she is reading off a script instead of genuinely teaching from knowledge and experience :/
lovee her! she gives great feedback, is super sweet, and is very knowledgeable about econ. take her!
Very good prof, very accessible and tons of extra credit opportunities that will not only help your grade but also look good on your resume. Best prof I have had at NYU so far.
I love her

Good at explaining concepts and the course load was pretty easy. The final isn't cumulative, and both the midterm and final can be pretty easy as long as you to the homework and pay attention in her classes. If you don't, you can still do really well. I thought her lectures were great, but realized econ wasn't for me.

Literally the BEST professor at NYU by far. She is the most caring and sweetest person ever, and is very passionate about economics. I would take her every semester if I could. There are many extra credit opportunities and work load is very manageable.

The most caring and warm professor in NYU I've ever met, she's extremely knowledgable and passionate about economics, and she's easy to reach out. If you submit the homework she'll give you an A on these works, and the exams are not intimidating at all. Take her if you can!
She's the best. Definitely take her if you can. Sweetest human being god ever created

She is the best. Definitely take her!!! She is so understanding and accommodating, and it is clear that she is very passionate about economics. Tests are very easy and she is lenient with grading. She is just wonderful. There are many opportunities to improve your grade and she is very accessible via office hours and email.
Top top top. No one is better. Take her
Great professor and person, one of the best at NYU! Very kind and caring. Breaks down the material so it is easy to understand. Will not regret taking her.
Made econ such an enjoyable experience! Exam content was very related to practice quizzes and class notes. She's also so forgiving and caring, and really wants you to succeed.

A wonderful person who really cares about her students' success, sets up students well for midterm and final exams with great practice tests and questions, graded on those two exams + co-curricular activities and weekly assignments where you are guaranteed to do well. Learned a lot and highly recommend!

She is genuinely the sweetest professor EVER and she really cares about making sure her students understand economics. Tests are super straightforward (no trick questions or unnecessarily difficult questions), and the homework/extra activities are super easy as well. As long as you learn the material, the class should be amazing!
Great professor! Kind, gives good feedback, and makes difficult topics easy to understand.
Very good professor, very understanding and gives a lot of practice questions from which you can get the tests. Easy A
Incredible teacher. Makes concepts feel easy to understand.

Such a nice person. You can tell she really cares for her students and wants everyone to succeed. Her exams are not too bad, they are really similar to the practice exams she gives, so study those a lot. Otherwise, her lectures are pretty good and if you pay attention in class you can for sure get an A. Take her!!

Professor M simplifies macro enough so that you aren't completely confused on exams. You're graded on 2 exams (midterm/final), extracurricular activities (i.e. attending econ club meetings), online textbook assignments, and a group project. She grades really easily, even on exams, and wants everyone to do well. Take her
She was really nice and organized. Her assignments are generally easy, as well as the test.

Literally so chill, such a kind teacher - don't even know how someone this nice exists. Literally prayed for angels to watch over her she was that nice. Grade A with a little bit of focus. Full of love and curiosity. Even over zoom such a nice person. Refreshing to have a prof that actually cares about what they do and is kind and caring.

Super kind, super chill. You will get an A if you focus a lil, take some notes, and put some effort in on tests and assignments. Actually made economics interesting - one of those always happy teachers who seems too good to be true. It's hard to do online classes and this prof. completely understands that. One of the best teachers I've ever had!
You only need to attend classes, study what she covers, review handouts, do practices she posted, and you will get A very easily. She never test on complicated/ weird stuff.

One of the sweetest professors at NYU. Show up to class because she takes attendance every time and READ THE TEXTBOOK because that is exactly what the midterm and final are on. She is very understanding and genuinely cares for the well being of her students. She wants you to do well! I wish she taught more advanced Econ so I could take her again.

reviews.comment: Highly recommend. Concepts were explained well and in depth, classes were interesting. Encouraged interaction outside of class as well. Note that midterm and final exam comprise a large portion of final grade (over 50%)

The final and midterm are over 60% of your grade so beware of that. Very light homework load but she goes really fast in class because there is a lot of material to cover. Tests and quizzes aren't too hard as long as you study and do the homework.

reviews.comment: She's great, smart, caring and organized. You learn a lot but it's completely manageable by even the laziest person's standards.
She's one of the best professors in NYU. If you are in Liberal Studies, you should take her.
Great professor, you will come out of the class actually understanding and liking economics

She somehow makes me want to participate and get involved in class and drew me to become so interested in econ. Honestly loved her even though in the beginning she didn't really think I tried hard enough. She explained all the concepts very, very clearly.  Recommend taking her class.

Kind, caring teacher. She knows her discipline, yet manages to convey complex material in easy-to-understand fashion. Makes economics accessible to everyone and piques student interest in the subject.

She is the sweetest possibly lady, and knows her stuff. Chair of the LS Econ club. Econ, admittedly, I do not like. Ascension made coming to a painful subject pleasant. Tiny class, she tries hard to get everyone to participate. Must do extra participation out of class by going to Econ club (easy), doing forums, or presenting articles.
She's sweet, and her classes are very nicely organized, very helpful

I had amazing professors this semester, but she was the best of them. I wasn't particularly keen about studying Econ, but she is so enthusiastic about teaching that I fell in love with it and I want to major in it. I wish she taught at CAS/ more Econ courses, because if I could take her again I would. Fair grader, so helpful and just BRILLIANT

One of the best teachers I have had the opportunity to take in LSP. She is so passionate about her job and she truly loves to help students learn. She is the sweetest lady I have met in NY (and that's difficult) and she is so understanding. I can't imagine a better professor. Take her and fall in love!

The class is a lot more work than you'd expect at first, you get homework and quizzes regularly. But the material is crystal clear and you will know what you will be tested on, there really aren't any tricks. My favorite class this semester; Professor Mejorado makes Econ fun to learn.
very nice person, always available for help, gives pretty straightforward exams.

She's kind and helpful, but not a very good teacher. The tests and quizzes are somewhat straightforward, but she loves to throw in tricks (esp. questions on material we barely discussed in class!) It's by no means easy to get an A : if you score below an 84 on the midterm, you're already starting with an A-. No extra credit. Take Lieberman instead.

Fantastic professor who is highly energized and committed to teaching.  On the easier side, but ultimately very fair.  Basically she skips around the room, explaining her love of neo classical economics excitedly and is very happy at any class engagement or questions.  Highly recommended.

I failed Econ I and was afraid to take Econ II... This professor changed my view about Economics. DO TAKE HER. One of the best prof. She's easy and crystal clear on quizzes and tests. She makes ECON FUN. Do homework and read texts and you'll get an A. She's very reasonable and VERY ENERGETIC about her topic.

Might be the sweetest woman alive. The class and quizzes/exams are very easy if you do some reading and pay attention. Participating is not intimidating in the least bit, and even if you're shy, she gives you many alternative ways to participate.. Highly recommend. It's an easy course and you will learn a lot. She inspired me to major in economics.

helpful, caring, can listen to her, easy grader, what more can you ask. great teacher, don't fall behind though or else itll be hard to come back. but if you keep up with the material and do that aplia, you will get an A and actually learn something, unlike in many other GSP classes

Love her, she's an amazing teacher and such a sweet woman. The homework is annoying to do but it's helpful and she really just wants her students to do well. Her exams aren't hard but you definitely need to know the material very well. Read the textbook, pay attention in class and you will do well in the exam w/o having to study for much on yourown
Great teacher!!! Class is easy and makes you think. Somewhat useful and much better than other useless GSP classes
One of the best, nicest teachers i've ever had and i've had her twice. Enough said. Take her if you can. There is a substantial amount of busy work involved but it's easy enough
greatest teacher alive. sweetest women ever. she inspired me to be an economics major and is very clear in class. anyone who wants to take an econ class should take her.

Absolutely loved her!  After taking her class, I decided to major in economics.  She is one of the nicest professors I have had, and was truly interested in having her students understand the material.  One of my absolute favorite professors.
She is an amazing teacher, not a lot of work, cares about her students, very understanding, very knowledgeable. I def recommend her. You'll love her!!!
she is by far one of the best teachers i've had.... greatest

i luv this teacher. she is really good and is able to make students enter amazing and intersting debates. if hmwork late and genuine reason, she is very understanding. she wants students to understand, is is simply AMAZING
SHE IS SO SWEET AND NICE!!! her class isn't so hard. If you do hws you will totally be fine.
she genuinely cares about the students and really wants them to understand the material. I love her. She is the sweetest lady!
SHE IS GREAT!!!!!!!!!!!! TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! MAKES IT VERY EASY TO UNDERSTAND!!!!!! SHE IS DA BOMB diggity!

Mejorado is the greatest teacher.  Really nice, very understanding if homework is late.  Tests are very clear and easy if you study.  She makes it very easy to do well if you simply try.  Take her class
she is an amazing teacher who really wants to make the subject matter clear for her students.  shes also a really great person. take this class if you can!
Great teacher, very supportive, tries to explain everything so you will understand despite that her accent is a bit strong.
Easy class, can't understand a word she says though.
very easy class.. very nice teacher and helpful. has aslight accent which makes her hard to understand sometimes but not difficult at all u can def get at least a B plus or higher
This is a good class.  Professor is very enthusiastic about her subject, and she really wants for her students to understand the material.  I would recommend this class

Meg is super smart and passionate about the material. I really enjoyed her class!
You can mostly get away with skimming the reading, but class is a lot more interesting when you've read. I feel like you get out of her class what you put into it.
She's funny because her notes are really critical, but you'll still end up with a fine grade.

Definitely a stressful class. I struggled but learned more than other ITS classes. Agreeing with other comments, she gives a lot of hw and sometimes doesn't publish them until the night before which is agitating. Meg is very passionate about her lectures which is amazing but also makes her very particular so be weary of that for essays and tests.

She is a very sweet teacher but is definitely a yapper and harsh grader. For most theater students, ITS should be the least of their worries but this class gave me my heaviest work load. reviews.comment: Meg is very smart, I mean very very smart. Her lectures are well thought out and she is a really good person.

reviews.comment: A super kind, respectful, and helpful teacher. You have to keep up with the readings and complete discussion posts so that we could participate in class. You can't really be late with assignments, but the workload wasn't insane. I would 100% take a class with her again!

Really smartknows exactly what she's talking about. Kind and easy goingdon't be afraid to ask questions. Lots of reading homework, but she'll discuss it in depth during classyou can get by without reading (that's why it's so important to go to class). Class is mostly her talking. Exams are straightforward. Assignments very simple.

reviews.comment: I took a class about the Spanish Civil War with Prof Merjian. It was my first class about art history, and I truly enjoyed it. He is very knowledgeable about his material, and we can clearly see his passion for his work. Regarding grading, he's a fair grader. As long as you participate in class and do what's expected of you, it won't be difficult.

I thought Merjian was great, criteria is very clear, and what was expected of us was consistently communicated. For texts and ideas class, the amount of reading required was VERY light compared to other classes. Ara is very thorough and has a passion for what he teaches. Always posts slides, and no need to buy any books. He is a bit intense though
if your looking to basically not enjoy life for the remainder of the course, this class is for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Class was a bit different than other ones I have taken. There are daily readings but you do not have to read them to full detail to pass the class (As I freshman, I was the only one who did the readings and that was not very motivating) For the midterm and finals, focus on identification and general connecting ideas / themes for the essay.

Took along with Prof Vinakour.  Midterm and Final, easy group project, participation in recitation and two pop quizzes.  Information wasn't hard to grasp.  Exams were hard.  Reading is so much and is totally unnecessary apart from maybe some of the primary sources.  Was cool information and he was an ok lecturer.

Prof. Merjian cares so much about his students and the subject itself. He is always available for questions. The class itself is heavily reading based, but there are only 4 total tests during the semester and if you pay attention and take notes in class you'll be just fine. Wasn't super interested coming into the class but I learned a lot.

For Text and Ideas. Professor Merjian is an instructor who made history "story-like" rather than just memorizing facts. Although grades are concentrated on a few assignments, it's not bad. I got an A in the class without much studying and didn't do any of the assigned readings. Just don't skip class and participate, and you'll get an A.

Took his Expressive Cultures class on Fascism and Anti-Fascism in Art and Architecture. If you're interesting in the idea, take Merjian! He's passionate and knowledgeable, relatively approachable, and the workload is pretty light (aside from the reading, but that's par for the course in core classes).

Professors knowledge and passion for history & art are very visible in lectures that keep you entertained & interested (even over Zoom!). Welcomed questions, eager to get to know you (& your pets:), openly allowed practice for formal analysis skills. Lots of readings - helpful in lecture and recitation. I highly recommend Professor and his course!

Professor Merjian was the best professor I came across during my time at NYU. He was always understanding, compassionate, and had the student's best interest in mind. He made sure lectures were entertaining and engaging and would set aside time to meet and check in on us. Overall he cares more about the student than the grade.I loved him& the class

So Ara isn't the NICEST prof, and def wasn't lenient about cameras off during Zoom-U, but he's a fair grader and if you watch his lectures & take notes, you'll do just fine. The material is interesting; 1.5 papers, 1 midterm, 1 final. Like any CAS history core, recitation matters, and if you show your TA you try hard, you'll do just fine.

reviews.comment: Lots of readings! Be ready to pay attention in those lectures as well. Hard to get away without the lectures. The Professor was very interested in his work and thorough! Merjian is funny at times, and very engaged in his work. Lectures arent necessarily boring, but neither are they a breeze.

reviews.comment: Prof. Merjian is engaging and always available for advice. I appreciated the quality and clarity of his feedback. Highly recommended!

Merjian is a good lecturer and presents his material in a way that is easy to understand. Readings r short so do them or at least skim as they help bolster ur grade if u can use them in ur midterm. He can be a bit pretentious but the TA I had was great and they decide ur grade anyways. 3 written assignments, short, medium and long which are fine

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved Prof. Merjian. By the end of the class even students who'd never taken an art class before were able to analyze art. Very approachable and encouraged seminar discussions instead of lecturing and was flexible with final projects so that everyone was interested in their own topics. Never felt too intimidated to ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I chose this class because it was already late in the process, and was the only one open that would fit into my schedule. But I am so glad it was. Prof Merjian was very clear and taught the material in an extremely clear way, although it did get repetitive, but that made the tests easier anyway.

Very nice guy, extremely intelligent, very engaged with students, in and out of class, and is very willing to help. Has a good sense of humor, and is an overall great professor. He's really passionate about what he does, and yes, that does include memorizing a lot of art. But that's just what his class is about. One of my favorite professors.

Professor Kohli is an excellent teacher who combines strong knowledge with real care for students. His course was well-structured, with clear explanations and useful examples. He encouraged me to pursue grad school and new opportunities, giving confidence and direction beyond academics. Inspiring, supportive, and highly professional.

Professor Kohli is very helpful. He is good at teaching the class important skills for interview and future finance career. If you career goal is attending investment banking, I do believe you will get amazing information from him.
was very clear in lecture and inspirational professor. Gives instant feedback and tests are all lecture based - very straightforward professor and would love to take it again!

Professor Kohli is an exceptional professor and I only wish I had the opportunity to take more than one course with him. His lectures are interesting and very practical for jobs. Was also very understanding when it comes to not just asking for help on a topic, but also if I needed and extension on an assignment. Would highly recommend.

Took two classes with Professor Kohli, one of the most passionate professors you'll ever meet lifetime. His instructions are crystal clear, and genuinely loves interacting with students - whether it's over ping pong, coffee, or in class. Beyond academics, he generously invests in students' career development and personal growth. Truly exceptional

Ok professor but a good guy. I'm giving a 2 because his overly friendly approach didn't work for me. He treats everyone the same, even people who are pathological liars, and he doesn't seem to see it. His intentions are good, but it didn't work for me

Professor Kohli is an exceptional instructor who truly goes above and beyond for his students. His lectures are engaging, clear, and incredibly informative. He goes out of his way to provide extra materials to help students better understand accounting concepts and their real-world applications. He really helps students to succeed.

Strongly Recommended. Nice grader and patient for explaining. Truly care about student abt their lives or future careers. Everyone's favourite professor. He knows well abt finance and how to break into wall street with his industry experience. His finance course will be one of the few truly valuable course at NYU. Treasure of the BTM department.
Great professor, highly knowledgeable, and his courses are a must take if you plan on pursing a career in finance.

I had the pleasure of getting to learn from Professor Kohli throughout my time at NYU Tandon. I took his intro to accounting, finance, and advanced financial strategy courses. He was very approachable both inside and outside of class, and his mentorship throughout my years at NYU instrumental.

My second time taking a class with Professor Kohli. Not something I would have done if he was not so professional and nice to students. The group project is also meaningful, it adds a practical element to the course and allows for you to get to know your classmates. Overall, highly recommend.

Had an amazing experience with Professor Kohli in my accounting class. Not only is Prof. Kohli incredibly knowledgeable about the subject, but he is also super helpful and always willing to go the extra mile to ensure everyone understands the material. Truly appreciate his dedication to our learning! Highly recommend!

His lecture is engaging and inspiring. Great textbook and assignments to prepare for finance career. His willingness to assist made him an exceptional mentor. Truly cares about their students' success and creates a supportive learning environment.

The second course I took with the professor, he is really professional and nice to students. The group project is also meaningful, as it opens the door to real-life business and finance jobs. Participate in class, and you will get a good grade and more importantly useful knowledge for your future career.

reviews.comment: Great course, and the professor makes it even better. He cares about students' feelings and is really professional in the financial accounting field. Also keen on sharing his own career experience. If you are a freshman, he will be the man bringing you into the business and finance kingdom. Just participate in the course, work hard, and have fun.

I actually took Financial Strategy with Professor Kohli, but I couldn't find it under the listed course. Financial Strategy was not an easy course, but his lectures were really helpful and informative, and he tried to help us learn and improve. He was also very accessible outside of class via email.

reviews.comment: Taking IB/PE class with Prof. Kohli is one of my best experience in NYU! He always tries to help us and provides suggestions regarding career development. Great lecturer and the best professor ever! He's eager to teach and wants every student to learn. Definitely reach out to him if there are some problems come up, he always helps. I learned a lot with him.

reviews.comment: Got a very great experience in GC1200 class. Professor Ashish is very knowledgeable and engaging in class. He can provide lots of real-life examples that made comcepts easier to understand. Also, assignments were graded promptly, and all feedbacks were constructive.

Professor Kohli had the most significant impact on me throughout my entire college career. He took a lot of time to help me with both materials taught in the class and also helped me to find my career path in Finance. He was incredibly patient and never hesitated to help me apply for internships. He is great at teaching and is a fair grader.

He is the most caring professor I have ever met; he taught us all the financial models you need in financial strategy classes step by step, making sure that everyone understands it well. Besides textbook material, he also provided extra help on the technical questions you need for job interviews. Extremely grateful for his help in learning finance.

I took Professor Kohli's advanced corporate finance, and he was the best professor I met at NYU Tandon. His lecture covered all the finance knowledge you need for a level 3 class. Professor Kohli is a great teacher and a kind guy, he is always there for you when you need help. His lecture was informative and fun, you will not feel bored attending his lecture. Professor Kohli will never give you a hard time as long as you attend his lecture and interact during class. Will defiently take his course again!

Kohli is a seasoned investment banking professional. His courses combines practices and theories to help students learn the finance kowledge and its real world applications. He is an excellent finance professor.
Professor Kohli is really knowledgeable about career planning, especially in the finance industry. Make sure to take his class and let him help you with your career development.

Prof. Kohli is a very knowledgeable person, he has a very deep understanding of finance and his teaching experience is very rich as you can see from the lecture. I would like to take more of his classes if I have the chance, especially those related to investment banking. Don't hesitate to ask him questions, he will always explain to us patiently.

Prof Kohli is a really nice person, he spends a lot of time outside class to help students. He gives useful feedback on group and individual projects. He really cares for his student's success. He gives his books, Interviewing for Wall Street and Accounting for Wall Street, to class at no cost. I am looking forward to take more classes with him.

Great professor who goes above and beyond to make sure you understand the concepts. Cares about each student individually, with an specific emphasis on career growth. Great insights, as he has years of experience working in IB on Wall St.
Great at teaching and cares a lot about his students. Responds extremely fast to emails and mentors students.

reviews.comment: Professor Kohli is a wonderful professor who cares not only about the material which he is teaching, but also about the futures of the kids who sit in front of him. After his class, I gained not only invaluable skills in Finance and Accounting, but also a mentor.

By far the most interactive and most helpful professor Ive ever had. I took Professor Kohlis class for Private Equity, and I not only learned a lot about the subject itself, but also about other fields in the financial world. He made the class enjoyable and insightful. The books he wrote were given to us and described topics in a very easy way!

This guy was by far the most disorganized professor I've ever had. All he talked about was his professional career and he made racist remarks about Punjabi people. Furthermore, he often got extremely sidetracked, which led to him assigning the rest of the lecture as homework to read on your own. Tests were awful and made no sense. Avoid!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class is graded on four exams, but Professor Kohli really wants the class to succeed. He is helpful in what he teaches and is receptive to feedback. He also gives great feedback on the real world with his experience. The class is tough, so I would not recommend for electives, but if you're required to, this guy is the best you can get.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly feel like I learned so much in this class. He's clearly knowledgeable and a great lecturer. Wouldn't call this one an easy A just because it's graded mostly on the midterm and final, but still worth it in terms of material. I found it difficult to participate in this class because it felt slightly unwelcoming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an outstanding lecturer; keep in mind that what he teaches is based off select theories to explain extremely nuanced concepts. I learned lots but also disagree strongly with some of his teachings. Grading scale is arbitrary and you need a 95 to get an A. Base your exam answers off lectures and you don't need to do the readings; less is more.

Great professor and the lectures were super interesting. 10 simple pop quizzes based on readings and lecture. He really wants consistent participation which kept us paying attention. He's a generous grader despite exams being a little tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a fair but tough grader but it's an easy class if you read. Know your stuff. It's common sense. Think like a dictator. If you can't do that, good luck. Think outside the box, he likes that. 2 exams, a presentation, and final paper. Nothing special. No homework. Incredibly well versed and his lectures are outstanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are interesting and thought provoking. He does a good job of explaining difficult concepts. If you are curious about the subject, I would highly recommend taking his class. There were two exams and many pop quizzes. But the pop quizzes are incredibly easy if you do the reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly his lectures are interesting. But his grading scale is so arbitrary and he is very rude when explaining your grade.

Awful, conceited, and dismissive/rude towards students. I reached out for help improving my "midterm" grade as he grades based on his own arbitrary scale of what is considered "worthy participation." I raised my hand every 5 minutes in that class and still received a poor participation grade as well as a dismissive attitude from him.

The course is worth taking if you do the reading, participate a lot, and enjoy presentations. Prof enjoys confrontation and often makes backhanded comments at students. Students choose class topics but prof will often reject them with inconsistent reasoning (most IR topics). His personal opinions were obvious by topics rejected and his arguments

Chill dude. drop jokes at times and it worked well in keeping our attention with him. Just a final paper and a presentation to be graded, so the rest is participation (they draw HEAVILY from readings, so you need to show you have read and tried to understand the material). Otherwise, we had huge freedom in choosing our final topic. take if u can

Love love love Rozenas. Tough guy, *must* participate a lot & prepare to be cold called even if you do, so doing the reading *carefully* is mandatory. Otherwise, lectures are interesting, course is broken down well, lots of free range for the final paper, and he is a fun, passionate professor. Probably one of my favourite courses taken at NYU.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice/very knowledgeable prof. Easy grader. Hardly any work. Do the readings and be prepared to talk abt them. Talk more often than not to avoid cold calling. Easy A and interesting lectures/readings

do not take authoritarianism unless discussing polisci is your PASSION. took his class online and lectures were disorganized, random, and largely unrelated to readings. might be weakest nyu politics course. he's dry, argumentative, and impatient w/ students. course requirements aren't difficult and he grades easily, but an overall a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She gives a lot of resources to help you succeed, learn, and get a good grade by posting practice problems for all chapters, exams, and neat easy to read lecture notes. As long as you pay attention and study you will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I didn't like her at first because she pushes students to participate by answering questions. But over time I realized she's genuinely kind, fair, and supportive. Her exams are reasonable, and her grading is very fair. The class is manageable if you actually participate, and attendance isn't graded, but penalized if you miss too many lectures.

The best professor I've seen in Tandon for the past 3 years. Most beautiful notes I ever seen. Missed few classes but still catch up simply looking at notes. late for class is fine. HW harder but makes you study. practice exams given, do it you'll get 85+. Easy grader got avg 95+ on exams. Very kind and helpful. online OH provided. Overall 10/10

Exams are your whole grade. Great professor, clear notes and lectures, really good at explaining difficult concepts. Her tests are pretty straight forward, but only 3 q's per midterm & 4 q's on final. Go to office hours if you're confused. Homework is hard but it's only completion. I'd take her again. She's very very good. Does a review at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's very good if you struggle making it to class. Notes are very neat, making them easy to follow. Weekly homework tends to be much more difficult than exam questions. I recommend studying from the in-class problems given. She gives exam practice problems before each exam which basically guarantees you an 80% if you know how to do them.

The professor is extraordinary, for midterms and finals gives amazing resources. Literally sends out videos on how to do questions similar to what's going to be on the exam. Very difficult to fail because of the amount of resources. Would definitely take again and the notes are always posted, so you can always teach yourself the material. 10/10

One of my favorite classes from NYU. He changed my view on music composition a lot, and I just loved everything about this class. I feel like if you don't resonate, it won't be as fun, but if you get where he is coming from, an absolute goated class.

Arjomand is such an amazing professor. He is so caring, funny, and very engaging. This course has made me look at music theory and composition in a completely new light, and I am excited to use my knowledge from this course in my writing moving forward. If given the chance, I would absolutely take this class again.

He teaches music theory in a "self-actualization" way where you connect with yourself whilst connecting with the material. At times he gets kind of philosophical and complicates things through abstractions, generalizations, and theories that he has with the given subject, but it was a very engaging and thought provoking experience nonetheless.
he's just a chill guy who wants to discuss theory

Arjomand is very underrated. He might seem a little overwhelming at first since his lectures tend to be very philosophical, but it's just amazing how he always eventually gets to the essence of the topic. His classes are super engaging and thought-provoking. Definitely recommend taking him.

Cool professor, one of the best in the department at nyu. Have had him for theory multiple times and it honestly gets more interesting every time. Not the best student myself, but I didn't ever feel like I was ever being singled out or anything for not understanding. He won't exactly force you to participate but it def helps to do so.
Big time yapper but he's chill

Arjomand knows his stuffs. Very thought provoking and dense for a Theory 1 class, which is a good thing in my book. You learn so much more than your typical theory lectures. Keep an open mind about music, and please participate because that is pretty much all we do in class.

Arjomand is the best professor I have ever had. Every class has the most interesting discussion and after every class you wonder how is it going to get better and it just does. It is definetly helpful to know some theory before hand. The assignments are super easy but informative. I cannot reccomend his class enough. Beyond thought provoking.

Prof Arjomand's lecture is super inspirational. He helps students understand the essence of music theory in an easy way. His lecture sometimes seems abstract or philosophical but trust me it is super fruitful if you really pay attention and join the class discussion. Not many daily assignments but projects in midterm and final.

Arjomand is far and away the most brilliant instructor I've ever had. His discussion-based class format proved incredibly insightful and completely changed how I perceive Music Theory. From his unorthodox teaching style to his wit, I truly cannot say enough great things about him and his class. A real must-take!

I took him all the way from Theory 1-3. Unfortunately, he didn't teach Theory 4 otherwise I would've taken it with him. He is by far my favorite professor within MPAP. I remembered struggling with music theory but he made it so easy. His lectures are easy to understand and compound on the homework. All around great guy. Very highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Arjomand has a very unique way of approaching his classes and leaves you with a good impression of the days work. Through his lectures, I was able to gain a thorough understanding of the roots of music from the perspective of a musician rather than a textbook. I love him as a Professor and musician.

Arjomand is not only an incredible composer, but he also encourages a lot of discussion & diversity in approach. With Theory II, he encouraged compositional discussion, and often, you're allowed to break classical "rules" as long as you can justify why you did it. Definitely one of the smartest people I've ever met and one of my favorite professors

Had him for theory 2. Decent professor, but cares more about having you memorize specific part writing he does rather than learn the rules and how to do it on your own. If you don't memorize the specific way he part writes you wont do well at all.

I swear he just wants you to learn to the point where all the exams he made includes all the hard stuffs he explained in class. He can mark you wrong by the slightest error in your composition. Also if you skip class, you'll miss a lot of stuffs. Be ready to participate so hard and getting cold-called.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I had Ramin for Aural I and Music Theory II, and both were great choices. For theory, he really emphasized ways we can incorporate music theory into our own musical pursuits rather than just read from the book. He will like you even more when you participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you have any doubt in your theory skills I wouldnt recommend this class. Especially online, the only kids who are doing well are the kids whove had lots of theory experience before. Hes a tough grader and Lecture heavy so take at your own discretion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Arjomand was a fantastic choice for Aural I. Occasionally cold-called to sight-sing or dictate in class, but it helped to keep me engaged with the material. He definitely doesn't teach straight from the (required) textbook but does use it sometimes for in-class practice. Occasional short homework assignments, but grade is mostly exams.

As a student who got A's in all other theory classes, taking Arjomand's class was one of the biggest mistakes of my academic career. He is extremely knowledgable and a great composer but it seems like he wants to flex his theory knowledge more than actually teach it. He's a harsh grader and very full of himself. Way too much work for 2 credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I LOVE HIM! He made ear training seem so easy. His teaching methods are so amazing, and it really is analytical in the way he approaches this class. He doesnt like doing things the textbook way and I really feel that makes a massive difference. He helped me genuinely understand this class and I want to have him every semester.
Best theory professor I have ever had.

Fantastic professor! He teaches at a great pace and is always willing to give feedback on your work. Homework assignments are never graded; instead you just work through them as a class which I loved. Exams weren't bad either. Take his class!
Ramin Yasss!!! He is definitely one of the more difficult professors but you can really get much out from his class cuz he has high standards.

Very intelligent theory professor. Offers extra credit to students who might need it and wants to see all his students to succeed. One of the more difficult theory professors, so really pay attention and take good note of what he does in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Made me start liking classical music. Best Professor I've had.

Super super clear when he talks about the stuff in class. He definitely knows what he is doing. Very inspirational too, as he changed my way to think about music theory and compositions. Trust me, I have taken a couple theory professors, he is the best by far.
Arjomand rocks.  He cares so much about every individual student and explains things in ways that make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures were helpful, love the slides (very helpful). Gives 1 on 1 office hours if students didn't do so well on tests. 2 midterms and 1 final. Even gives funny stories so people focus

Lectures are so unclear and unorganized. Always had typos or glitches. He's pretty old school with a lot of stuff and good luck with the minitab, it barely worked for anyone, he didn't care he told us to figure it out... yet it was used on every HW. idk why he chose TA's that are undergrads themselves. I think they knew as much as we did.

Truly the worst class I've ever taken. I've had plenty of classes across disciplines (I've even taken stats before) but I've never been worried about passing a class until now. Shahmaei is rude, unwilling to help, and frankly the most disrespectful prof I've had. I don't even use RateMyProf but felt the need to share how awful I found him.

Always left guessing if this was one of his "typos" or "mistakes" again or something we genuinely had to know; the TA does not know anything and is not helpful as she also is just an undergrad student who has only taken this class once. The TA always avoids answering questions either because she doesn't know or doesn't want to take responsibility

Exams are worth a huge chunk of your grade and are pretty difficult. Professor Shahmaei was not a bad lecturer but if you've never taken a statistics class before you may find it challenging. He allowed students who did poorly on the midterms to meet with him one-one-one so he could explain clear concepts and see if they deserved more points.

Poor lecturer. I understand being inadequate with technology as he is old but that does not make him any less incompetent as a professor who has to teach as much as he can in 75 minutes. Instead of actually teaching the materials, he is only focused on teaching how to memorize to solve problems. With all due respect, he should consider retiring.

I'm harsh with my rating due to the TA's considering how rude, unhelpful and inaccessible they were it's really important to get closer with Professor in the beginning as the TA's ignore emails are unprofessional and don't speak coherent English. He is a funny and genuine guy but he should consider retiring as he doesn't know how to use any tech
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great personality unfortunately that's all I can say I enjoyed about his class. TA's for this class are very rude and uninformed and you could tell he was frustrated by their lack of effort to help. That being said I feel like this class is not too difficult but is dependent on how much your TA actually helps you which reflects my grade of mine.

Honestly the worst professor I had so far. Very inadequate with technology and his way of teaching depends on jumping back and forth between different topics within his powerpoint slides, making it extremely difficult to follow along. Acts like he cares about students but very rude when asked questions in class and office hours.
VERY UNCLEAR, he humiliates students in the class and makes some students cry, and too many assignments.

If you are willing to come to class and put in the effort, take him. Otherwise, don't. If you participate and put in the work you will get a good grade. He knows what he's doing and teaches well but he does expect you to come to class. He is super caring and will stop everything he's doing to answer your question if you don't understand something.

He often jumps around the slides in an unorganized way during the lectures which makes it hard and confusing to follow. Unless you're in the front row of the class, he will often ignore your hand in class. You can't talk to him after class because he's always in a rush to leave. In office hours, you can see that in his attitude with his impatience.
He's really sweet, exams are hard but he prepares you well, all lectures are recorded.

Funny and interesting old man with a funny accent, not in a bad way, an entertaining way. He knows what he's teaching about and will provide you with the easiest explanation to make sure you understand. Hes patient when it comes to asking silly questions and is willing to answer them in detail.

So glad I took him, he's so nice and funny. Great stats teacher. Homework is time-consuming. Lectures are very engaging. Available outside of class. Exams are tough. Get to class early and chit chat, hes the best!

Professor Shahmaei talks a lot about his story, but it makes the class more enjoyable. His tests are not that bad, usually around 1-2 trick questions, but the rest follow his practice exams. The final was a bit difficult compared to the other tests.

Amazing professor and human. Makes stats enjoyable which is a tough thing to do. Exams are exactly like the practice questions and he rarely ever tries to trick you with questions. Also overall a very understanding and caring person and genuinely wants to see everyone succeed. If you want an A in stats this is your best bet.

I'm sure he is a lovely and humorous person but sometimes he really needs to remember he is here to teach statistics, not his passion on Greek culture or a student's lunch schedule. Additionally his accent might take some getting used to and he talks as slow as he teaches (Three classes and we are still learning how to calculate mean and medians)

Great Professor for STAT-UB 103, the exams were similar to the homework and he taught in-person very well. Weekly HW that is not very hard, 2 midterms and a final exam. PPT Slides are clear and easy to study or take notes from. He made the class fun and interesting, which is hard to do with stats.

Hes such a sweet professor and cares about the students that give him the same positive energy in class. If you participate in class you will do great. It is sometimes hard to understand him and he makes mistakes on exams, but his heart is in the right place. Might be easier if you have some knowledge with stats, but in general a great professor!

Although Professor Shahmaei isn't very tech savvy, he tries his best to make lecture as smooth as possible. He is very accessible outside of class and is such a sweet man. He genuinely cares about his students. Definitely recommend this class but if you don't have patience, you might get frustrated with him. He's great!

terrible professor at least through zoom. speaks super slowly. 75 minutes of class only to teach 1 concept and do 1 practice problem. can't write a test to save his life. typos everywhere on midterm 1 and 2. final was a whole question too long. stingy with grading and blames students for his mistakes. look for a different stats prof.
He's funny and inspirational. Do take him.

A good, funny professor who goes out of his way to make sure his students understand the material. Provides printed out lecture slides and handouts for you to take notes, which is essentially the textbook for the course. Really really cares about attendance and timeliness. If you go to class, do the assignments, and pay attention, you will be fine.
great professor

I don't think I learned much from this class which may be due to my past experience with video/audio. It's a class where you get your equipment and are told to "go out and do it." He gives in-class critiques which can be nerve-wracking. It can get nitpicky which is a bit discouraging. He's strict with deadlines. I'm still waiting for a grade.
I feel like I didn't learn very much from t

He is great for getting a very good look at the multimedia journalism industry, and if you know nothing about multimedia before the class, you will learn so much. HOWEVER, be aware that he is the greatest strickler with deadlines I have ever met. No extensions, no changes, you have to do every assignment 36 hours before class otherwise it is a 0.

Prof. Chi'en is awesome, fosters a great community and really cares about students. He's very easily accessible outside of class. Lots of fun and creative assignments in different mediums. Heavy emphasis on coming up with unique ideas and building pitching skills. He is hilarious and offers insights into the industry that will help in job searches,

The class atmosphere was great, as the professor managed to form a community and ensured a safe space for building your pitching skills in the group. You get to explore audio, photo, and video formats covering the areas of your interest. Just do your work on time and put the effort in. We also got to build a portfolio website -- a pretty cool touch
VERY inspiring! Loved this class and Professor Chi'en, I recommend him to all my classmates
Chi'en is a down-to-earth person who cares a lot about his students. Also an experienced professional who knows the ins and the outs of his industry.

Professor Chi'en was wonderful! He puts a huge emphasis on learning technical skills. He's super passionate about local news and does a great job in keeping students up to date with current events. His feedback was great, instructions were easy to follow, and he was supportive throughout the semester. Take his class!

She is a good professor. BUT the graders are sucks. If you don't know what to do in the summer, taking her class is the choice never being wrong. By the way, the exam is open book, and participation is important, make sure you attend the ZOOM every week. Everything is about Pseudo code.
probably the best algos prof out there. homework is reasonable, exams are open book (but I also took the online class so I'm not sure about the in person ones)
Best Algo Professor for NYU students! Her exams follow the homework problems, and the homework problems follow the things she taught in the lecture. Really nice experience with her!
Take her class if possible. She was the best professor.
Prof. Ikram is vary vary nice and always open to students' questions! She is very accommodating and lenient!! She truely wants her student to understand the material and success!!!

If you have the opportunity to take a class with professor Ikram, do it! I've taken a handful of CS courses so far at NYU, and I have to say that professor Ikram is by far one of the best. She's very understanding and will listen to your "incorrect" answers to figure out why you may have done a problem a certain way and clarify. Very caring!
I took the class in summer 2021. One homework per week, clear grading, great curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved this class!
Take the class!
Loved this course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Solid class. Would take again
Good discussions and straightforward grading.
To my knowledge, most students left with an A. She gave us an opportunity to grade ourselves based on a rubric and actually went with the grade we gave ourselves. Good class.
I can't recommend this professor enough. Her class discussions are all interesting, and she's very helpful at giving feedback. You can improve your writing if you meet with her after hours.

There were a few freshmen in this class when I took the course so I can see the class material being a bit challenging for them. Personally, the conversational aspect of the class suited my learning style and helped me digest the complex readings. I recommend this class.

My writing and thoughts really developed in the class. Some students came in with a strong background on the subject we explored through writing. I liked that the professor offered them opportunities to share their knowledge so that we didn't just learn from her.
Received so much feedback on my writing in and out of class. The professor was always open to meeting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class
This class felt like a healing space compared to other classes. We did writing exercises outside and learned a lot of writing vocabulary.
I took this class as a form of writing therapy to help the healing process. She helped me clarify my degree, and essentially, who I am. I really enjoyed every class I attended.

I utilized a lot of the texts and concepts I learned here for my senior paper and I  titled my colloquium after this class. Would definitely take this professor again. I also participated in the mutual aid org she founded.
This was one of my favorite classes at NYU, and I am very grateful. Not only was I forced to think in critical way, this class exposed me to many ideas I wouldn't have otherwise know.
This course changed my life. We learned so much about writing from an interesting lens. If you don't do the readings, I can see you having a difficult time. Highly recommend!
Great professor! Caring. Very thorough syllabus. We had one of the best reading lists I've had at NYU.
Not a class for bigoted students. You will have thoughts challenged. Learned so much.
Great class. Would take again.
Terrible teacher, do not recommend.
She's unprofessional, always late to class, and treats students with no respect. Don't take her class for your own sake
The professor should be more open to fresh ideas.
This is a heavy literature class...not a creative writing class...

For this class, I would highly recommend taking detailed notes of what the professor and your classmates have to say about the works, and then using them to write your essays. She can come across very harsh, but she really cares about her students and is very passionate about what she teaches. Her class is very engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible!!!! Stay AWAYYYY
She asks her students if they have ever written an essay before as if they never did because of how specific she wants it. She always picks on specific students and get annoyed quickly.
Not Good

One of, if not the worst professors ever! She is a very tough grader and wants everything specific. She treats her students like middle schoolers and each assignment is worth 30%. She always accuses her students of things and does not care about anything about them. Please stay from her!

Arab Theater. She was disrespectful to many students. Usually the women. She asked if I ever written an essay before, yet she couldn't spell "enroll" and other words. Do not disagree with her. Students would analyze things differently and she would tell us we were wrong. If you dont write what she wants or how she wants it written, youre wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gender & Sex. in Arab Performance. One of the most knowledgeable, wise, & eloquent profs at NYU - truly a gem! All her readings + lectures were interesting, insightful, & thought-provoking. My favorite class at NYU yet! Aside from that, she's such a warm & kind person & makes you feel welcome. only 2 papers & a presentation on one of the reading s

Arab and Film. Mid-term and Final, but there are readings every class that can be really long. Take notes like crazy. Also if you don't write what she wants, you will fail. She is a tough grader. You can make it up but she will not allow you to explain yourself. She expects you to write/think the way she does, not only with writing but in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Naila is smart and passionate, but she is also a theatre professor. I took her class on Syrian culture and politics and I liked the materials and art we read and discussed, but she is disorganized and doesn't know how to lecture. I am not an arts major and I really wish it had more actual facts about Syrian politics, but its all about arts culture.

I love Naila so much! She's super understanding and passionate about the subject. I grew up in the Middle East and still learned so much more than I expected about Middle Eastern performance. She really cares about her students and is determined/ open to learning from them.

Naila is one of the most inspirational and intellectual professors I've ever had. This class was super informative and interesting. She is passionate and really wants to hear your opinions during discussions. She's also open to learning from her students and is constantly asking for input from them.

Syrian Culture & Pol. She is so sweet and incredible with so many personal stories about her time in Syria and she's truly passionate and sweet and a wonderful person to be able to learn from. She's a very understanding grader. You only have two papers be warned! But every reading is incredibly interesting and I always did them. Please take it!

He's a really caring teacher that wants you to do well. Responds to emails very fast and always open to office hours and post-class discussions. The class is all lectures, no interactive activities or group work, so if that's how you learn best it's great.

Best professor ever. Extremely chill and outgoing. He is also extremely caring and wants you to succeed and gives plenty of opportunity to do so. I took Real Estate Economics with him and it was a breeze, while I did learn a lot in this class. If you slack off, you can still score high, but you won't learn a lot.
Great Professor, I will take his class again! Pay attention in the class, and you will get A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great Professor and person but he grades like his admin is over his shoulder with a tazer. Also you cant miss class

In my opinion he is a very hard grader for a class that should be an easy A.  This class was not easy compared to other public speaking classes offered at Pace.  Exam was super hard.  Textbook is a must.  He is very deep and inspirational.

Professor Athanosios is a very open-minded and inspirational speaker.  His way of teaching and thinking is enlightening, which expands my thoughts and makes his students believe in our topics; therefore we are able to speak passionately and freely.  In this class, you will learn more than just public speaking.

I took his 7:25am class but it was so worth it. He's incredible and very intelligent! You will learn so much more than public speaking in his class. Just follow his requirements for your outlines and speak with passion. He also has a VERY STRICT policy on attendance and being on time. He was one of my favorite professors and I highly recommend him.

Professor Athanasios is a very chill guy who genuinely wants his kids to do well. This class is not an extremely easy class. You have to put in the effort and follow his instructions on the speech outlines or else he deducts points. Take his class if you really want to improve your public speaking skills.
Great Professor! Helped me over come my fears of public speaking. Has a fair grading system which allows you to do well if you follow the requirements.

Professor Athanasios is a great professor. He has a structured course that provides student's with the necessary foundation and skills to become a great public speaker. I recommend him to any student.
this professor is very old school, and his research field is also useless, he continued bragged about his old research in class and being condescending, as a latest news, he got fired from NYU

Prof. is a phenomenal professor and if you want to learn and push your knowledge to the next level he is the perfect person. I have him for VIP and I went in from knowing little to fully engulfed in this field of wearable technology. Great mentor and would recommend to anyone who is serious about learning and growing their skills in biotech.

It takes a while to get used to his lectures. He goes fast and is unapologetic about using heavy technical jargon. Homeworks and labs are heavyyyyyy. However, the grades were very generous. The TAs are very helpful in lab and office hours. Overall, it was overwhelming.

I took this course with very basic Matlab experience from a Mechanical Engineering background and really struggled my first month. I started attending office hours weekly and working with other students and learned so much in this course! I work in the surgical robotics field now and this class was my catalyst into the field.

+ Gaining extensive and valuable knowledge from the lecture and lab sessions 
+ appreciates any feedback and motivates the students to be honest about the lecture and lab sessions
+ very competent and kind professor
+ interdisciplinary content 
+ changed my field of interest and the course of my career

- lots of papers (interesting ones though)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is a main course offered in the field of medical robotics at Tandon School of Engineering. If you are a robotics student at Tandon, want to pursue your career in the field of medical robotics, I would highly recommend to take up this course.
