The course is quite tough, but it will be manageable even if you are not an expert on Matlab/simulink.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Farokh goes fast in his lectures but is kind enough to repeat the same material to ensure you understand. The class is lecture heavy. He is very well-versed with the content and loves answering questions. Pro tip: take notes in his class and copy everything he writes on the board

The assignment requires lots of research paper reading and systematic problem solving, which I think is a real master' level class instead of an extended undergrad course. 
Good for those who have interested in the related field and would like to cultivate their research ability. 
The workload is heavy but learning a lot. And the grade is kind.

Do not take this cousre under this professor. The curriculum is poorly structured. If you want to study the subject, there are so many online materials. He gives out his own research papers to read out for assignmnets. TAs will not conduct office hours.  Not recommended under this professor.

Great Content. Professor Atashzar takes you through the current technologies in medical robotics and the challenges that are faced to bring these technologies to use. His course focuses on telerobotics and is all based on state-of-the-art research. This is an excellent course for any area of medical robotics and the assignments make you think a lot

Heavy Lectures, the professor brags about his research a lot, tells us to read his own papers. Teaching Assistants are not at all helpful.His assignments are not even related to what he teaches in the class.

Most assignment is done in Matlab but doesn't teach enough knowledge to do the homework. The amount of homework is horrible and there is no TA to help. There is a chance that you won't get a response by emailing your teacher, and if you get a response, it's just asking you to read a few papers. The class is very long and there is no break.

Apart from providing the underlying math and concepts, Prof. Atashzar brings you to the field, explains the current-day challenges, walks you through state-of-the-art measures taken to overcome them, then challenges you to come up with the ideas behind those very measures. Best teaching philosophy and narrative in a course I've ever seen.

I took her in the summer for CS101. It was a very chill class and not very difficult. She doesn't hold your hand but the exams were easy. Just do some self-study (which is very easy to find some resources for an intro java course like this) and you'll be fine. Not the best CS professor (unorganized) I've had but I don't regret taking her at all.
Pretty bad at giving lectures, and the difficulty of tests varies a lot. Gives many extra credit opportunities and is a nice person though. Take her if you are a strong self learner.

Professor Ataman is a really nice person. If you need help, she is accessible. Also, she would adjust the difficulty of exams according to students' performance in the last exam. There are also extra credits in assignments.

Ineffective teacher. Could not express herself or teach clearly. I had to teach myself everything with the textbook. Very hard to access outside of class. Unwilling to help clarify anything and very rigid. 
I would avoid at all cost.

You might need to be self-taught a lot. Indeed, she does not teach so well during the lecture, but her quizzes are easy and despite that the exam is a bit hard, she gives a pretty good curve. Anyway, as long as you take it seriously, you can still get a good grade

Professor Ataman is new to teaching this course and she's still developing her teaching style. I respect that she made notable efforts to address student concerns and add more supplementary coding practice after hearing student feedback. She's very kind and accessible to students! If you read the textbook, lectures and practice, you will be fine.

She seems inexperienced and has no idea what she's talking about. The lecture is confusing so you'll end up pretty much teaching yourself everything. Some Homework Questions and first midterm are completely irrelevant from what she taught in class, and her PPT is not so helpful and sometimes has errors.
favourite professor so far :)
The class is pretty much just teaching yourself from the textbook, and then getting blindsided by the exams. Slow grader, so you won't get much feedback.
An intro java course is going to be pretty dry, so I can't really blame her for the class not being very exciting. She taught well and seemed nice. Sometimes would show up late to class though.

I'm giving 2 stars and not 1 because she seems like a nice person so it hurts to be too mean.  

However, you will end up teaching yourself Java. The grading criteria for the first midterm was ridiculous; 10 points for basically what was true/false and 5 points each for multiple choice. Don't take this class if you care about your mental health.

Takes a bit to get used to but is not a bad professor. She is new to teaching so she isn't going to be as good as some other professors. Goes a little fast but you can just watch a quick youtube video and you'll be caught up. Good examples in class and very short and simple homework assignments. Exams are very straightforward with a large curve.

It is very hard to get a decent grade in this class. The lectures are not helpful in understanding the course material and students can't get much coding experiences from class. The homework is fine but the exams are much harder. If you are not a strong self learner I definitely would not recommend you to take this class.
A very average experience. Straightforward lectures with decent examples mostly pulled from textbooks or online. She didn't add much flavor but wasn't bad by any means.

Panda is absolutely hilarious and hes very generous with his grading/curve. He really does care about teaching, go to office hours even if its just to say idk whats going on. Hes very intelligent but also down to earth. OS is a hard subject and theres nothing he can really do to change its difficulty but his explanations are very good.
Lectures are not organized and he is very picky on minor details. Although he does offer help during office hours especially for the labs, it may feel as though favoritism is involved. Questionable
Unclear and inefficient

This course definitely requires a passion for research, an interest in reading and thinking about papers, and a certain level of self-motivation. You will need to read a large number of papers, but in doing so, you will gain insights into how many classic systems work internally, rather than just learning how to use them.
The lectures are super helpful for me to understand distributed systems. And the selected papers are really good for a student without any background to get into the world.

Operating Systems is a difficult course by its nature, but Prof. Panda is an effective lecturer who adequately prepares students for the exam. Be prepared to struggle on the labs, but thats part of the process.

I attended every lecture, every textbook, attended office hours multiple times a week, had a 99% lab average for labs that took on average over 10 hours, and still got a 60 on the final. You can study and work hard in this class and still not do well. Prof himself doesn't like exams but they are 70% of your grade. How empathetic.
This course ended my CS career, farewell
Worst Decision In my Life... May the god bless you
Try to take other available sections if possible. Otherwise may the God bless you.

Labs are incredibly difficult, can take 10-30 hours. Unless you go to office hours multiple times, you will not finish them. Lectures are all over the place and are just messy whiteboarding. He will help you if you go to him though. He really helps you with your labs if you go to office hours. He's akward and not great, but not awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The best undergrad CS class I've taken at NYU. The labs are especially clear, with pages of step by step instructions to guide you along and a clear focus on the material being taught. Prof. Panda speaks clearly in lectures and is enthusiastic about the material. He's top notch.

Terrible professor. Messy lectures that are all over the place. Labs are ridulously long, take 10-20hrs and going multiple times to office hours. Overall too much work. He asked us to review him and the class, and after all of the overwhelming negative responses, he basically said he doesn't care and is not changing anything. How caring.

Panda's distributed systems class has so many papers to read, if you don't like doing paper readings, turn somewhere else for capstone. He is disrespectful outside the classroom and only favors the PhD students, and has some racial discrimination. If you decide to take the class, be extra careful when choosing project topic, you can't change topic.

His distributed system is great if you like to do research and think about the mathematical model of computer systems. The papers are not that hard to read (though time-consuming), considering it's a graduate course. Panda is very smart and explains things well. lecture assumed you already knew those stuff. So self-study is important.

He is a great professor in teaching, but his manner is disrespectful and snarky when you see him in person. If you try to search for help, he wouldn't help and try to convince to this is not your course if you can't catch up and you should drop it. Sometimes teases even he is an educator, he may be a great researcher, but definitely not great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A lot of the past reviews suggest that the professor can be strict, but I also think he's one of the best professors I've had at Courant. Incredibly dedicated and passionate, and you can tell from his lectures that he really cares about sharing knowledge. Absolutely want to take another class with him after Distributed Systems!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took his class back when remote learning first began. By far the least accommodating and understanding professor I had. He literally made record our hands and face while we took his exams and threaten students with what he described as a harder oral exam if our recording didnt meet his standards. Not friendly and lectures are very hard to follow

Prof. Panda's quite smart and incredibly organized - it's easy to follow along with lectures and he puts up notes pretty regularly. He gets a little snarky at times when things aren't going perfectly to plan and students veered lecture off-topic, but he's a good professor and you'll certainly work hard and learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The professor can be quite passive aggressive from time to time. Not really helpful outside of classroom.

This class is like the epitome of an easy A. You're graded on like three short essay "exams" and a small group presentation. Also, you don't really have to show up; attendance isn't taken, and all the test information is on the slides or online.
The guy gives everyone an A as long as you put .01% effort into the essays. The critical race theory could chill, but he's enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny and interesting guy. unconventional lectures for sure, approaches psychology though a very critical and unique lens which is refreshing and fascinating.
I adore Professor Ausch! His lectures are very interesting and he always brings some personality and humor to class which I really appreciate + I learned a lot so far! :)

His only graded assignments were 3 exams and a group presentation. All of the exams were written. Although his class didn't touch a lot on the psychology aspects until the final, I loved it. I found it boring at first but his class ended up being one of my favorites. His exams aren't too difficult, just reading heavy. Super caring and funny dude.

I know lectures may be at times off topic, but he is accessible via email and I would ask on topics I would be confused about during class before I thought about my groupwork and he would answer. He is cool.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Robert is a gem. A true national treasure.

Loved the class. Easy A if you just do the work. Skip the readings unless they interest you. Most people don't show up to lectures, but I'd say go for two reason: one he is SO funny and two when you do the tests, (open note), you won't have to search through readings to find answers, you can just use your notes. Learned lots and would take again.

lecture style is definitely odd, and will drift off a good amount. So it took me a while to get used to his teaching and get comfortable with the class but I'm pleasantly surprised. TA grades papers, and exams & project are simple but good amount of work to learn. Take the class, he can be intimating at first but he's sweet
Very enjoyable class. Pretty easy going professor. Easy A. He is hilarious, but says whatever he wants regardless if it's controversial or not.

Pretty easy to get an A. Doesn't care and doesn't seem like his field. Lectures are disorganized and confusing, but just watch the recordings you need to answer the midterm and final (tough but open note). A lot of reading, but you don't have to do it, and the TA's give out 100s for everything turned in on time. Don't take if you want to learn.

I can tell that he is a nice person (not mean or cold to students), but his lecture is not organized. Cognition is supposed to be a fun class but he makes it confusing and boring. I attended every lecture in the beginning the semester but found that watching the recordings was much more efficient as I could skip irrelevant discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really easy professor. Class is basically graded on completion, just do it all and you're good for the class. If you want to learn something I don't recommend it - mostly just an easy A. Really considerate guy and takes the time each class to ask his students how they are feeling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 80% of his class was asyn (him assigning random youtube videos that you have probably already seen). He gives out A like Oprah. I know people who turn in test a month late and gets full mark. For the presentation, he give you an A before you begin to speak. He is not a bad lecturer when he actually start teaching. But he's just too busy to do so.

An amazing professor. Our midterm was straight foward and the final was a take home which was essentially more difficult than the midterm. I was able to learn a lot through this class especially with my TA Samer.

I really liked this class and thought it was super interesting. It is more focused on philosophical or theoretical themes in cognitive psychology which made the midterm very difficult. But the TAs worked with students to improve their grades.

I wish there was a spot to rate the TA's because they are lovely. They did their absolute best to put up with him, and they all deserve the world. This guy, however, clearly doesn't care about this job at all and I genuinely don't know why he's here. Your grade is so heavily determined by one midterm with the world's most random questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very lazy and unorganized professor. This was his first time teaching cognition so he literally just used a syllabus and slides from other professors. His lectures have no structure and he goes off on random tangents the entire time. The first midterm we took essentially determined our grades for the rest of the class. Avoid if u value structure

Very hard course. Tests are extremely difficult and he does not test on the course material. He tests on the optional readings. Reading textbook is useless for the test. Lectures are boring, study guides are vague, scores are not curved.
Loved Group Dynamics. Really interesting material and he teaches it well! Hes genuinely a cool teacher - funny, easy going, not a hard grader, not a ton of work.

I took his Group Dynamics class this fall. Highly recommend taking this elective to APUG students who want to sharpen their critical thinking/writing skills. Unlike other psych electives, this class covers topics in sociology, history, and humanities, allowing you to explore many underlying problems in our society through a myriad of literature.

He contempts higher education and complains about its uselessness, yet he actively contributes to the problem. He has one of the most unorganized, useless classes in the entire school. He says that if the students don't vote for his preferred politician, they should forget to vote. If you cannot be a good teacher, at least try being a good person.
4 tests, the lowest one is dropped. His lectures are funny with personal anecdotes. No visual aids (presentations) so lectures help a lot.
great professor! Despite the lack of visuals, he made up for  it with his witty jokes and funny anecdotes. His lectures were always clear, concise, and specific.

Very interesting course that I would recommend to take. The downside is that there is no visual presentation to help you follow the lesson. Hence, you will need to attend recitation (optional) to go over the given topics. Course's grading breakdown is simple: 4 non-commulative exams and you're allowed to drop the lowest scored.
Humor's kind of dark, and is not nearly as hard a grader as he seems. Fun class. Interesting guy.

He is awesome! He is an affluent professor and gives a lot of space for students creative thinking. Does not "kills" independent opinions, treats everyone with respect. His teaching style is great. Has a little dark but really good sense of humor
He's the best, enjoyed going to his lectures, he's so passionate and easy to listen to. He's literally perfect. 10/10

AMAZING actually my favorite professor at NYU, take his class u will love him sooo much his mind is just pure genius shi, like at times it'll go quiet and then you'll hear the simultaneous clicking of all the pens in class because he had said something so profound that everyone rushes to write it down.

Professor Augst is a great professor! He is a good lecturer and shows genuine interest in the material. The grading is clear and the class is very fair. Overall he is a great choice for Literatures in English 3.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Augst is chill and a smart guy/fine lecturer but I did not enjoy this class. However, that is my own fault because I never did the reading: I couldn't stand reading excerpts from a textbook as opposed to actual books. Also I had beef with my TA. Whatever

I love Professor Augst! He is so knowledgeable (yet humble) and gives the best lectures. He is one of my favorite professors at NYU's English department, and certainly the best out of all the 'Literatures in English' courses. Grading was pretty difficult, but that depends on your TA. He offers a creative project for one of the assignments! Love him
He's just a really nice person. Show up, listen to what he has to say, and participate. It's a fun class.
He's such a great professor. You can tell he cares about his material and students. Do the reading even though it's a lot and you'll be fine

Tom is great! had him for Writing NY and he's a great lecturer- really passionate, the reading load is moderate, and he's so understanding with assignments and deadlines etc. The final project had a creative aspect to it so his classes are not just papers, and tests! Definitely would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Augst!! He was amazing. Inspiring, interesting, engaging-- would absolutely take again!

Augst is an okay professor. Long lectures on boring subject matter. Tries to engage the class, but it's hard to make the subject interesting. If you manage to get through the readings and write well enough, you'll pass. There aren't that many papers and they're pretty easy, but get ready for long, dry reading assignments.
Not very impressed. All lectures were politically charged and he frequently strayed off topic into sensitive areas.

Honestly my favorite professor at NYU. You can truly tell that he cares about his students. He makes the boring material a lot more interesting. Only thing is, there is a TON of reading, but he's pretty understanding, and you learn a lot!
Really clear, organized lectures. Makes even dry topics interesting.

Thomas Augst was a great professor! He gave me a whole new idea what literature really stands for. He's a really funny guy and tries to show the students that through American Lit we can better understand American Society. Highly recommended!

Started out good. I enjoyed the class, very interesting topic. But make sure that you actually clarify what he wants you to do paper-wise, otherwise you might unintentionally get on his bad side, which is bad.
Augst is the man! His lectures were always funny and engaging and informative. I learned an incredible amount from him but at the same time, didn't have to be bored out of my mind either.

Great prof.  Despite the sometimes dry subject matter, I never once fell asleep, and this was a 9:30 MW big lecture.  Highly recommend taking a class taught by him if at all possible.  Makes even the boring stuff intersting.
He is a brilliant lecturer, who breaths life into the material. Does a great job of explaining the three papers for the course and the exam formats.
Enjoyable classes and good topics for essays. Easy A if you do your work and the extra credit.

He is really nice in class and gives a lot of extra credit. He didn't grade your writing because of his grading contract. Everything is just completion grade. If you just go to class and do every homework with some extra credits, you can get an A easily.

Very nice and caring professor. Workload is manageable. One really good thing is that he doesn't grade your work on quality (unless you do really bad) and you can get an A just from attending class, doing bare minimum for assignments, and some extra credit assignments that add onto your overall average. Great professor overall.

dont even know why he doesnt have a 5. hes so understanding, funny. participate! he will love you. go to writing center? yea ur gonna get an A++. its literally so hard to get anything below A unless ur an idiot.  pls try though bc he deserves good students. just yap whatever u want he will always wanna listen and hear you and remembers his students

literally the goat. hes so kind, gives us very little assignments and GRADING IS SO LIGHT. HES A CUTIE PATOOTIE. and if u go to his office hours like hes the one u can just yap to. also hes so lienient w deadlines and if u dont finish everything like hes chill about it and he literallt says its fine.
Awesome professor, super funny and charismatic person. Do your work and you won't have any problems!

He was really nice, kind, and overall pretty good. His class was based on a grading contract and was relatively easy and reasonable to get a good grade in. He gave good feedback although he felt like he himself was unsure a lot. His class could be boring or tedious but it was because I didn't like the subject. I would 100% recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Kelley very good professor, and he creates an environment where you can try and test different ways of writing, and thanks to his grading contract, there was no risk of having anything under a B+. To get above a B+, all you had to do was an extra writing assignment or two, which varied from a semester reflection, to an essay revision.

This grade in this class was pretty much based on 3 essays and one presentation. It was an okay class but the professor graded very harshly on the essays and provided very subjective feedback. I revised one of my essays and was told it was very much improved, only to get a 1% increase after spending 5 hours on it.

Because it was online this semester, he expected microphone on. If your mic is broken, your gradell be a lil penalized ��. Essay feedback is a hit or miss, but you can still improve every assignment, go to WTC. If you miss a letter grade by even 1/4 a point, he wont round it up. Semi salty abt my grade but at least I learned how to write well ��
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a tough grader and made us read our essays to the whole class for peer review so its a bit of pressure not to embarrass yourself. There is always outlining/drafting before the final essays are due so you dont find yourself lost when the time comes to actually write. He is understanding and you can tell he wants to connect with his students.

Professor Kelley is a great teacher who genuinely wants you to learn and take something from his class. He is a tough grader, but will always let you know how you need to improve to be successful. He is an overall caring and funny guy who just wants the best for his students. I am happy to have had the opportunity to take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Honestly, an underrated professor. Everyone just wants an easy A, but he will actually help you grow as a writer. Gives very helpful conceptual advice rather than just editing your grammar. I am so glad I took his course, I can actually say I am a much better writer after him. He is a lenient grader.

Friendly and laid-back, easy to meet with outside class. Ambiguous with grading/feedback, but that's common in English classes. The texts he assigns can be difficult to read/understand and you won't get very far trying to write about an interpretation he disagrees with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy that gives useful feedbacks. I like him and would definitely take his class again if possible (although he grades hard).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He is a nice person and gives ok feedback. Accessible outside of class/easy to set up meetings. Write in the way he likes or you will fail. You never know how your grade is calculated, as of now I have received my official course grade, I still dont know my performance on my last essay. Grades way harder than teachers teaching the same class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a pretty very unbelievably tough grader. BE CAREFUL if you have the idea of spending little time on this course

He's really chill, as long as you do the work and act like you're paying attention, you'll be fine. Some of the topics in class are actually really interesting, and he gives students the chance to read each other's essays and improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Kelley was an excellent instructor and I would definitely take his class again. He gives great feedback and holds engaging lectures that you should definitely attend; he appreciates it if you participate.

Super engaging classes. He likes to be goofy, which lightens the mood. Gives reasonable amount of work. Isn't super strict as long as you do your work and show up. I've taken him two semesters in a row, and he's made EXPOS very enjoyable for what it was. Highly recommended!

I dreaded WTE (I normally HATE writing) but he made me love it! Yes you have to try - he's not an easy grader but not too bad you'll be fine if you try (best way is to actually try to enjoy what your doing, he notices and it comes out good!) He makes the class very interesting/ actually fun.

I'm probably the one person who will say this, but WTE was my favorite class this semester. Prof. Kelley is a great professor, he encourages you to push the boundaries of your writing and thinking. He is more than happy to meet with you outside of class, and he's a very fair grader. Take him!

Nice, funny guy. Extremely eager to help and never gets mad when the class hasn't done their hw (which will happen a lot, its boring). Definitely not a technical person who gives concrete feedback, but more holistic in his way of teaching and grading. Looks at the big picture. Meet with him as much as possible, its the most helpful.
Loves to help outside of class but is super unclear in what he wants in his papers.  He is artsy though.

A great professor who definitely wants to help students; he's always willing to meet after class. He is a bit ambiguous about expectations because he doesn't want to influence your writing. I really enjoyed his class.

Professor Kelley is an excellent professor. He really pushes you to focus on specifics, to be logically sound, and to advance your writing. The classes are interesting and I actually enjoyed going to them. Probably the best you can make a Writing the Essay class.  However, he is a fairly tough grader and you really need to put in effort.
super sweet guy & eager to help
Decent Teacher. Eager to help. Nice guy.
Don't hurt your gpa

Stefan is a great professor, and I learned a lot. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. Tests are straightforward, and the papers weren't too bad, but they require critical thinking. All of his assignments are reasonable. Highly recommend taking one of his classes. Super chill.

Professor Aune is one of the best professors I've ever had at NYU. Classes are made up of stimulating discussions related to readings (get ready to read A LOT). Research paper is made very approachable through smaller tasks throughout the semester. Provides clear feedback, returns grades super swiftly, and is super approachable and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: My favorite professor from my first sem. Very clear lectures, organized, use of many different sources, and timely feedback. Uploads slides and lectures. Overall a great guy. It was a very fulfilling course and I genuinely felt like I learned a lot.

Prof. Aune's class is extremely basic, understandable for being an introductory course, so it is not hard. In the two paper assignments, you need to include the primary sources he shares in class in your analysis, otherwise you'll get a low grade on the paper regardless of how good it is without them. More compassionate with that in Mid and Final.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He just reads off of powerpoints and doesn't teach. Take this class if your willing to self-teach yourself history, this class is such a waste of time and money.

His class was one of the only ones I was excited to attend. Very knowledgable. Class assignments throughout the semester were only two 3-page papers and short essay answer online midterm and final. We had basically 24 hours to complete the exams. Tip: Attend lecture! So much of what he mentions will help with all assignments. Love this professor!

reads fro his slides every class... IT's such an interesting topic that can be delivered in a way more intriguing way but he simply puts all the dates and names on the slides and reads from it why would i go to class if everything's on the slides Knowledgeable yes, wont give student a hard time yes, but boring

He's a great teacher. I learned a lot about World War II, beyond the obvious topics of The Holocaust and military progress. He had wonderfully detailed lectures, but still had a juicy amount of class discussions to stimulate thought and let students to ask questions. If you do the homework, it's easy to get an A, BUT the reading was battle heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really loved the professor and all the TAs. Took World War II class as an elective. Class wasn't mandatory to attend and grading wise, they were really good. Highly recommend it and he is really intelligent and fun to listen to. Thumbs up!
cool dude. super knowledgeable on the subject. pretty chill class.
She can be tough but she does it for a reason. Amazing professor, explains everything clearly and you can tell she truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed in Spanish.

Such a lovely and caring professor! She makes class super comfortable so it's not awkward or stressful at all. There's a good amount of work, and everything is pretty much required, but it pays off! Grading is extremely fair, and she gives very useful feedback. Profesora Augspach is the best, I wish she taught all levels of Spanish ;(

Love her. Hadn't taken Spanish in several years and she reminded me why I used to love it. She's a very sweet person, funny, extraordinarily patient and good at explaining things. I wish I could take her again.
Amazing professor!

Very easy A as long as you complete the assignments and put some effort in. She is a super helpful person but make sure to participate in class as she does keep track. Exams are all multiple choice and very simple. There was busy work (homework, projects etc), but as long as you get it done, you will be fine.

She was my first college Spanish professor so I was super nervous, but she's a great choice! She's kind and energetic and actually cares about her students. She's a fair grader too. Takes some effort, but if you do the work and participate in class, you'll get an A. Also, make sure you're early! She takes attendance the second class starts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Profesora really cares about your learning. She is always there for questions: email or office hours. Don't skip class as it does get difficult but manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Augspach is an incredible instructor who truly cares about her students. She is funny and probably the most patient person I have ever met, which is important in a language professor. Pay close attention in class, study in groups, and go to her when the class gets hard (and it will). Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Augspach is the best. She genuinely cares about your comprehension of the language and goes out of her way to teach you the fundamentals as well. I wish I could take her for all of my Spanish courses, or honestly just be her friend. She gives great feedback and authentically cares about how you're doing in her course. I 1000% recommend.

I really enjoyed Prof Augspach. She is so kind and very smart. Was willing to work with me during office hours and really help me out. She is the best Spanish teacher I have had. Really respect her and would recommend her if you need to finish the language req.

Professor Augspach is the best Spanish professor I have ever had! She is extremely enthusiastic and kind, and she is passionate about helping students learn. I never felt scared to make a mistake in her class, and I felt that my language skills truly improved while taking her class. Professor Augspach is accepting and very funny!

I'll preface this by saying I am horrible at language. That being said, Prof. Augspach is the best language professor I've ever had and has made me enjoy Spanish class. She always goes above and beyond with teaching and is patient. She made an app to help study for each test which is so awesome and helpful. I wish I could have her all four levels.

Absolutely amazing. Coming from the joke of a foreign language class at my high school, I felt unbelievably unprepared for Spanish III. But Profesora Augspach makes learning so easy, exciting, and engaging. She makes you speak in class, which you appreciate eventually, and has clever activities to make spanish more fun. What an incredible teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Elizabeth has been my favorite and most helpful Spanish professor. Although the homework was an average 30 minutes each night, if you keep up and stay engaged in class (don't be on your laptop!), you'll do well on tests and compositions. Very clear teaching style, especially regarding complex grammar structures. Definitely would recommend!

Elizabeth is the most wonderful person and an amazing teacher as well. I was so lucky to have her as my Spanish professor and I was definitely disappointed when I found out she wasn't teaching the next level class next semester. She gives homework but it is doable and doesn't take too much time. The tests are easy as long as you study. Take her!

Literally the best Spanish teacher I've ever had. Simple grammar things I didn't understand in high school suddenly became crystal clear. Some kids in my class struggled by I really clicked with her style of teaching. Definitely do the homework; there are lots of little assignments by they never took me more than twenty minutes total.
Going into college without having taken Spanish since sophomore year of high school, she made this class just as fun and interesting as it used to be. Amazing!

One of the best Spanish teachers I've ever had. She's extremely helpful and truly cares about her students and will make sure everyone understands everything. She is very understanding and accommodating and makes a conscious effort not to assign too much homework. Highly recommend her.

BEST EVER! she was extremely helpful, always organized, always pumped and willing to go out of her way for students. she somehow got me to be passionate for spanish, even though the class wasn't the most exciting thing she made it great. take her class!

Her tests are incredibly difficult but she's always willing to help. She makes all of the tests for all of the "elementary" classes in the Spanish department, so if you take any other teacher, the tests may not be so fair. If you plan to pursue Spanish, take her class. If not, stay far away.

I had this a while ago, but I remember that I LOVED her, but not so much the class. Grammar is a drag, be it in English or Spanish, but she really pumped the classes up and made them amazing. She's extremely helpful. I could never make office hours and she was always willing to take a few minutes after or before class to help me out. TAKE HER CLASS
had her class for only a day but she's great!

She's great! You can tell she has a passion for what she teaches, and she truly cares about her students. She is also very willing to help during office hours or make special appointments for her students. She'll help you in any way she can. Plus, she's very sweet and funny. I'm Junior and she's still the best professor I've ever had!
She tends to pick on the students she doesn't like as much and her tests are incredibly difficult.
SHE IS MY FAVORITE SPANISH TEACHER!!
She was AMAZING! The most hilarious and interactive teacher ever. She seems strict, but she really gets into it.
Really fun in a nutty kind of way. Very helpful and dedicated to teaching. Runs a lively class.
She rocked my world.
Amazing teacher, really dedicated and engaging

I am taking the machine learning with professor Cosse for this summer 2022. The overall content of the course is of medium difficulty but be aware that the hws are very hard and if you do not have previous experience in machine learning or strong mathematical backgrounds, you will definitely struggle. Exams are hard but the grading scale is loose.

Great material. Professor presents the material in a great way, he is good at explaining things. HW heavy, the coding HWs are challenging. He replies back within a day. Best Thing: Really really great material on the subject. Fantastic coverage of all topics in AI. Great slides and reading material as well.

Overall a kind instructor with solid maths background. Most slides and notes are available on the course website, and the exams are interviews (question list provided). Fair workload, quite flexible with HW ddls, but it'll be better if there are more feedback. Recitations can be better utilized. Recommended if you are confident with the maths part.

Probably one of the worst professors I have taken. She frequently has another teacher substitute for her or isn't there and she does tend to get her answers wrong a lot and have to fix it in her annotated notes later after class which is frustrating and hard to learn.

Prof. Avalos completely restructured QM from the last time she taught it. Course was more conceptual and less mathy. I thought this really made the content more tangible. Lectures were well-organized, thorough, and nicely complemented the TB reading. This course really made me appreciate the beauty of QM. Take prof. Avalos if you can!

In upper level chem courses you hope for knowledgeable professors. This however is farthest from the truth in this course. When your professor says "I don't know ill correct it in the notes after class" on numerous occasions, you feel your hopes of passing disappear. Coupled with a ridiculous grading scene, you are left with a nightmare of a class
boring and long classes/did not learn a lot from her classes.

boring classes, tough grader
she did not give any clear criteria for assigment
She is a sweet and caring teacher. Tries to make class fun and engaging. No clear grading rubric- very few assignments. Would take her again. Easy to get an A in this class

This class started off difficult and then got easier later on.The criteria for studying for the midterm was very broad and it was difficult because the questions were very specific and many bombed the midterm because of this. The essay assignment held very vague criteria; however Wallace understood that we had a difficult time and accommodated.

I don't even read the textbook unless I'm presenting a chapter. Lectures can be long but you cover the chapter twice so if you pay attention you don't even have to read the textbook. Doesn't give a lot of feedback or clear instructions but it's an easy A,  imo :/ She tries hard to be engaging but if you aren't interested, you aren't interested.

Had her MCC Intro, she's a sweet person but def pushes her own political agenda- it doesn't interfere with the class itself, but you'll pick up on it during discussions. Not necessary to do readings, but def take notes on what she mentions, that's what you'll be tested on. Fair/kinda tough grader, mainly bc she doesn't rly give u clear guidelines.

Aurora is a very nice lady but her lectures are really heavy and long. She is also a very tough grader but she doesn't provide clear guidelines, instructions, or good feedback on any assignments Took her at NYU Paris and she is the only Intro MCC teacher on that campus so you don't really have a choice :/
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't take her unless you have to. Not the best teacher to start with when learning about media and communications.

Wallace is a nice person but her lectures are mad boring (maybe its jus cuz of the material). The class is very easy but she doesn't give specific enough instructions on how to do well for papers and exams. Also felt kinda bad cuz barely any students turned on the cam and answered her questions in online lecture when she tried to make small talk :/
Not accessible and didn't learn much
Boring lectures. Harsh grader. I hate to say this... but for me, the worst ever.

Very boring class that is composed of boring lectures and just her playing movies for us in class. We've spent at least 11 hours this semester just watching films, with zero knowledge learned and zero academic interest sparked. Very vague comments on your essay and harsh grader. Don't waste your tuition over this class. Ain't worth the money.

Seriously boring lecturer, if you took one basic U.S history course & kinda know the progression of technology in America you'll be good to just sleep throughout what she says. Briefly did readings the night before tests & still got an A-. Completely unaccessible, she never answered a single email from me all semester so she must just not care.

Read just so you can make a few points in class. Participation is important. She likes when you say something kind of correct so she can hear herself say it better. She stresses the importance of the texts for the final but its all general questions, so you would have better luck just studying your lecture notes. BUT DO TAKE NOTES.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Aurora is fantastic! Really cares about our projects and makes an effort to support us towards creating a fantastic final work.

Aurora is a really great lecturer! The class was interesting and a delved into a variety of topics regarding modern media. You have to do the readings though and show up to lecture. Most of the material on the quiz is stuff she lectures on. TA's do all the grading as another review said. Overall, would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor and amazing lecturer. Class consisted mainly of quizzes and papers. TA's do most of the grading.

Took her for Crime, Media, Violence. Very charismatic and interesting. Funny dorky jokes propel the otherwise dull lectures. Very hard grader, doesn't really tell you what you did wrong/what to write on. Not the best, not the worst.
She was a great lecturer and engaging, particularly considering it is a large lecture environment.

I had her for two classes in one semester (Advertising & Society and Media History of NY). Definitely knows her stuff about advertising and increased my knowledge and interest in the subject. But she is a tough grader.

had her for advertising and society. extremely clear, knows what she's talking about. class was straight forward so there was no need to go to her to ask questions. definitely need to study for exams/tests but easily comprehensible material

Worst professor I've ever had. Refused to read my paper or answer my questions when I went to office hours and instead sent me to her TA. Absolutely thinks she's GOD and takes herself way too seriously. She's cold hearted and only cares about herself. I think she got pissed no one came to her lectures and failed everyone for the final out of spite.

Awful teacher. Incredibly boring. Would teach lectures and no one would show up. She would make sassy comments at people who did come. Very hard grader. Not a lot learned. You can take a lot better classes than this at NYU, do not do it.

Definately not the best at NYU, but she knows her material. Yet, she is so nerdy and laughs so much at her own dull jokes that her class is not really what you would call fun. Her quick facts are cool though.

I have Prof. Wallace for Advertising and Society, and I love her! She obviously knows a lot about the subject and has a lot of interesting, educated opinions (although she doesn't object to discussion). She has a lot of visuals (necessary for this kind of class) and plus, she's just adorable! But she doesn't take****, so don't give her any.
If you can take this course with someone else, do so. She takes herself too seriously. The lectures are dry and boring.

Boring class, boring material, monotonous lectures and cold atmosphere, I'd rather be giving blood.  I highly do NOT recommend this professor to anyone definitely take another professor even if it conflicts with your schedule you'll be VERY thankful trust me.
Professor wallace clearly knows what she is talking about and she always tries to make the class interesting. I HIGHLY recommend her as a professor for any subject within communications.
Most boring class ever.  If the material wasn't coma enducing enough, her monotonous voice should just about do it.
Aurora is the best professor NYU has to offer.
Great professor. Great class. Interesting subject matter. Pick a good TA, or the recitation is worthless. But, Aurora does a great job on her own. The people that complain are lazy.

Wallace is a pretty good professor.Her lectures were a bit dull esp at 9:30am,but the material is easy enough and as long as you read most of the txt and attend most of the lectures and RCT you shouldn't have any trouble.The hardest part about the class was finding the motivation to actually attend.

Her class is really interesting, and its sucks that its early in the morning because its easy to fall asleep...but her class is interesting and shes really funny. Her tests aren't that difficult if you keep up with your work.

She's really amazing, her lectures aren't as bad as everyone stresses them to be and her tests are really easy if you've kept up with the work. TA's grade papers so pick a good one, but she seems to be overall wonderful.

I enjoyed her lectures but exams were tough. The course itself covers a lot of material so missing even one lecture will cost you. TA's grade everything though, so as long as you pay attentoin in recitation it should be ok.
Her lectures are enjoyable and interesting, but grading really depends on the TA so make sure you sign up for a good recitation session.
Sheseems nice to me, but i havent taken a test yet
if there was ever such a thing  more boring than this class, I haven't experienced it
No Comments
Her lectures are so easy to follow which makes it so easy to take comprehensive notes.  And she actually makes the subject really interesting.

Aurora is a REALLY nice woman. Sure her voice can put someone to sleep, but if you work hard and pay attention you will do fine. I made an A, so I don't know what the last person was complaining about.
No Comments
No Comments
Difficult if you miss even a single class.  I would avoid taking a class with her if a TA is involved and she just handles the lectures.
Refuses to give an "A" - expectations unacceptable
BEST professor!
He is the best. Take him. Simple as that! Will have zero regrets. The GOAT.

Professor Patt is such a nice and good professor. I would deffinenetily recommend his Jewish Humor class if you if this is something that you are interested in. We had a few guest speakers over the semester and they were actually really interesting to listen to I would say compared to other guest speakers that I have had in past classes.

Professor Patt is the best! I went into this semester thinking, "Ok, I'm just taking a class on Jewish Humor, can't be too analytical." But I was presently surprised. He showed us how humor is so ingrained in the Jewish people, and how it is such a core part of our values. I would definitely recommend!
Great professor. Not too much workload. Two exams (midterm, final) memorization-based. A short paper. Would take again

Very interesting class. He is very well-versed in the department and makes heavy topics interesting. I learned a good amount in his class. There is a lot of reading and homework. My main issue was that more than a few classes getting changed to Zoom meetings. Probably wouldn't take it again because it is textbook-heavy, but very interesting prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is hands down the best, most kind professor I have ever had at NYU. The lectures are engaging and he respects his what his students  have to say so much. Everyone wants to participate and listen. Only two tests and barely any homework.
RUN!!! TONNNNNNNS of homework after every single class. LARGE AMOUNT OF HOMEWORK!!! If you are late for 1 minute, your attendance will be recorded as late. Homework grading is tough.
She is definitely the best writing professor.
The SWEETEST prof I ever met!!!! Take her class!

Kind and inspirational. Encourages us to step out of our comfort zone in writing and cultivates our critical thinking skills by offering us many useful writing techniques. This class was undoubtedly rewarding! However, you must work hard in this class, and participation (attendance) matters as the grading policy may be out of your expectations.
She is simply amazing

This professor is an absolute writing guru! She's incredibly inspiring and always willing to chat about your daily life. Plus, she's super patient and takes the time to review each of your papers. So, if you just put in the effort and complete the grade contract, you'll definitely succeed! Don't be a slacker, though!

Best writing professor I met that made me enjoy writing for the first time. She is so caring and gives constructive feedback that helps you grow as a writer. Make sure you get to class on time, don't slack off with the homework, and do the extra credits.
She is soooooooooooo sweet! Her lecture is amazing!
It is her that made me fall in love with writing!

Super nice and caring teacher. Gives good feedback and is very encouraging.
One of my favorite classes as a freshman. Go to class on time, finish your homework, and do the extra credits. You'll be fine!
She cares about students and teaches very well
The best writing professor

EXPOSUA4

The BEST prof I have ever met. 
She is accessible after class, truly cares about her students, and gives extremely helpful feedbacks. 
Taking her class is like winning the lottery, and I can't tell you how grateful I am.
She's very caring and knowledgeable- take this class if you want to take your writing to the next level. One of the best profs at NYU.

Great knowledgeable professor that pushes your critical thinking and writing to a new level. However, Lots of group work and talking to classmates.. not so great for introverts and weak writers. Sometimes long reading assignments and it can get really stressful especially when your workload from other classes pile up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
She cares alot!
 Listen to her feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's the best writing teacher I've ever had. She really cares about all her students and is also really funny. She does grade sort of tough but if you put in the work, you'll be good. Don't wait to do the homework until before class because the reading takes a while. You have to do the readings to write good essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Avia is a tough professor, but she will push you as a writer and you will produce some of your best work under her guidance. She is very strict about attendance and punctuality. Generally, she is also a harsh grader. However, very kind, approachable, and encourages participation.

I took WTE (as my first college writing course) and Prof Tadmor was wonderful. There's 3 essays, where a full draft is due a week in advance, but she gives all the feedback to improve + conferences. She pushes deadlines so you have enough time to write & revise. There are usually 2 readings per essay but they're easy. Make sure you're on time!

I had Professor Tadmor for Writing the Essay and she is simply the sweetest soul. Make sure you always put your best in the drafts because her feedback off off your drafts will be THE ONLY feedback you get, but if you use those changes you new guaranteed an A. She is super understanding and often gave us extensions for our 3 essays. Such a gem.

This was a very difficult class. Avia grades very hard. The three writing assignments were basically chosen for you (societal issues) which made the class dreadful and a drag to write any of the papers. She wants a final draft level paper a week before you submit it. She also is very strict with attendance and you have to arrive 5 minutes early.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Tadmor is honestly the best. It's clear that she really cares about her students and is extremely passionate about writing. She's super organized and really teaches her students how to get better at writing. Prof Tadmor is also really understanding when it comes to the classes workload and often times gives extensions on papers.

The writing professor everyone should have. She is incredibly sweet and caring (How is it possible for a human to be this nice?), and has a true passion for writing that shines through in her classes. She takes into account different previous experiences with writing and is always willing to talk your ideas out with you to help you grow as a writer

Was his first semester teaching forecasting time series and he did a great job. If you're interested in content/passion he will definitely deliver. Weekly HWs can be done in groups, and the 2 projects all follow a straightforward template and are pretty engaging. Downside is that it's a night class so will have to sacrifice a weekday evening 6-9pm.

Standard of the perf class to me so far. Giloni wrote live in OneNote the most important concepts w/ clear verbal explanations. No need to go to recitation unless you have q's abt hw. Textbook helps for hard concepts but not necessary. If u understand the hws you'll do well. Final is pretty hard tho so study well for the midterm.

So good at explaining the material.  Tests aren't too hard.  Definitely do good on the midterm because the final is harder.  Homework was graded on completion.  If you're exceptionally good at participating, he boosts your grade half a letter, so if that's you, take him.
He is chill just go to class

The professor is great. He is enthusiastic even at 8 AM. No attendance and post online recordings. However, the exams were difficult. The sample test is much easier than real exams and exams go much deeper than what you learn in class. Great professor but the exams were pretty hard. Still, the professor was one of the best professors I met.

I second the great ratings, Giloni is a great professor for 6 credit stats. Classes are recorded, and he goes through examples in class. Not too heavy of a workload but the concepts take some outside studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably best STATS-UB103 prof. His practice exams are really similar to actual exams and he boosts your grade if you've shown progress and effort. Show up to class, his lectures are really good and by the end of the course some people stop showing up, but that's a big mistake (material gets harder to comprehend). Highly recommend
Prof. Giloni is an excellent professor - it still baffles me of how passionate he is at literally 8 a.m.

Professor Giloni really cares about his students! His class is very organized, and he has office hours frequently. Tests are on the more challenging side but he teaches the content clearly and effectively. Group projects were a productive way to apply what was taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy, however he is quite disorganized and it is difficult to grasp concepts because he does not give worked examples. He throws formulas at you but does not apply them to a practical problem or model question therefore you kind of blindly go into practice papers and the exams.

Professor Giloni is amazing! He explains the concepts very clearly and offers many in-class practice to make sure we understand. Even though the class is usually big, asking questions is not a problem at all! Only comment I may say is beware of the curve. It can be pretty tough since a lot of people do really well in his class

Amazing professor. Lectures can go a little bit fast, but in general are pretty clear and he makes them interesting. Homework is pretty straightforward, although Minitab work can be a little tedious. Practice exams in general are representative of the actual midterms and final, and he allows cheat sheets during them. Please take him.

This course in general is not easy and I personally, did not understand a single thing. However, Professor Giloni made it bearable and most of the assignments and tests were pretty straightforward. You have to put in a bit of effort to earn a decent grade. If you're on the fence about statistics, take Giloni's class.

As long as you pay attention in class, you shouldn't have any problem understanding the concepts in his class. He's amazing at teaching the concepts in an easy way and his tests reflect the practice tests that he gives out.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As long as you watch the lecture recording/show up to class, do the homework, and prepare for the tests you would get an A. Lectures are always clear and concise. Definitely would take again.
Amazing professor and explains all contents in great details! Hugely recommend!

Professor Giloni was the best math instructor I've ever had. Not only is he a fun person to learn from (he even makes 8 am lectures fun), but he makes stats seem really easy. I would definitely recommend him if you want to learn (and get a good grade)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He teaches a tough subject, but he gives students benefit of doubt. Always answers class and asks students for questions and answers. Text book can only help you, doesnt quote it ever.

Giloni is very knowledgeable and is always willing to answer questions. His exams are relatively simple and you get to use cheat sheets on the midterms and your notes and book on the final. It's tough getting up for an 8 AM three times a week, but Giloni definitely makes it worth it. I'd take this class with him again.
His midterms and final are pretty much exactly as the samples he gives. If you pay attention and study a little, you'll do great.

The most brilliant stats professor you'll ever have. He makes the repetitive nature of stats seem more interesting than it is. He also never hesitates to help any student in need. His midterms are fair and he allows students to bring in 3 pages of notes into the midterms - much more than anyone really needs. he is truly amazing

very helpful. you can pretty much do anything you want in his class. i decided i did not want to take the midterm so i just left in the middle of it and made up some story which he eiter fell for or juss felt like being a nice guy. i ended up takin the test 5 weeks later. very cool.
nice guy, very passionate, very helpful!

Very nice teacher. Always willing to help and explain. Although he's an adjunct but he stays in the office substantially to answer your questions. He even has exam reviews over the weekend in his office. Makes a 8am stats class something I want to go to.
Very nice guy. I hated stat in high school and he made it my favorite class of freshman year.
Outstanding teacher. Very nice person. Very funny and helpful too. He's an adjunct, and we all know adjuncts kick butt! Big props to Prof. Giloni.

Professor Ronell is a treasure. She is just brilliant; her lectures will blow your mind and change the way you think. C&C Germany is the best class I've even taken at NYU, having had no Philosophy/German/Comp Lit background. Take her class!!!
A gift to this world. So smart, so caring. If I got anything from nyu, it's Avital. she's truly a gift

She was condescending towards several students when asked critical questions. I didn't like her insulting somebody just becase they're not familiar with extensive citations in her syllabus. I wouldn't recommend her.
Class is loose and casual.

This professors is what you dreamed of when u came to NYU: inspiring, well organized and brilliant but also she will recognize you and really support you. Don't believe any negative stuff u have heard - take the course for yourself and judge. She is dynamite and will bring out your own dynamite brain.
Take this course if you have a mind and want a better one. Prof Ronell is a phenomenal lecturer and though you have to work hard this is what u came to BUY for. Spectacular stuff  (and she is KIND)

So smart, so full of knowledge. Apparently she was part of some scandal a few years back - who knows what actually went down - don't let it put you off taking class with her, she's the best thing at NYU
This is why I came to NYU. This woman is everything you need to get your mind flying.

Professor Ronell delivers the most mind blowing performative lectures. Her readings of Kafka, Nietzsche, Derrida, Deleuze, Heidegger, Freud and others opened up a new world for me. She is kind, honorable, funny and caring. I highly recommend her classes.
If you like comparative lit, you'll love Avital.. She's inspiring, but she tends to talk in circles and goes off on tangents a lot. She doesn't allow computers in her lectures, though, so be warned.

She is not your usual type of professor, that's for sure. She literally PERFORMS her classes: every word that comes from her mouth is pure poetry/philosophy. Not everyone's cup of tea but I loved her!

Often misunderstood: In class, she is not only teaching the subject but also a very singular conception of "the professor" and of the philosophy of teaching, through a self-conceived postmodern performatic method, that makes use of facial gesture, body language, and vocal expression, plus sartorial and make-up props: A truly revolutionary method.

Often misunderstood: In class, she is not only teaching the subject but also a very singular conception of "the professor" and of the philosophy of teaching, through a self-conceived postmodern performatic method, that makes use of facial gesture, body language, and vocal expression, plus sartorial and make-up props: A truly revolutionary method.
So great. I loved watching her train of thought and went out of my way to take another class with her this semester. Youtube her, if you really want to know. She's on there.
shes great, smart, funny and very challenging.
just plain awesome. but never plain.
She is one of the most important scholar / thinker alive today, it is an honor to learn from her. She is an amazing teacher and someone who can teach you endlessly about yourself and the world.

I have to agree with some of the criticism here. Incredibly intelligent (seriously - very sharp), but if you want to witness an academic cult of personality at its most grovelling, take this class and watch how people who disagree with the professsor (there MUST be other poets than Holderlin and Rilke to examine) get eviscerated.
Anyone who brings their brain to her is lucky to be alive and at NYU.
Her class was teh best one I took at NYU.  She's brilliant and interesting, not at all just rote versions of theory.  She's original and interesting and helpful.  Take her class!!

Massimo is an amazing professor. His creative writing in Italian class helped me writing progress exponentially. So sad he is retiring, but I am thrilled for him to continue with his book and short story writings. Free plug! Check them out :)

So sad he's retiring now... truly the best professor I've had in all my years of schooling. He's genuinely so caring about all his students and wants nothing but success for all of them! Authored a few books as well which I'm more than excited to read now!
I love him so much :)... The assignments were kind of hard but that was because of the characteristic of my class.
Best prof ever!!! Loved his class so much, he is literally so funny and entertaining and he cares a lot about his students. I promise you will love coming to class if you take his Italian section.
Best Italian professor ever! You can tell he cares a lot about his students. Massimo makes learning Italian so fun, the semester was so enjoyable because of him.

He's such a teddy bear and was the best part of my semester at NYU Florence. His teaching style is incredibly chaotic but somehow it worked out really well and we all learned a ton. Everyone around campus loves Massimo.
Amazing professor, I learned a lot of Italian in his class and he was also very entertaining and one of a kind.
The nicest, empathetic and overall hilarious professor. He genuinely wants you to get a good grade and learn the material. Definitely study and pay attention before quizzes.

Massimo is the funniest professor, not because he cracks jokes but because he just is. I took his classes twice in a row. Classes can feel disorganized, but at the end of the day I learned Italian a lot. We get to talk a lot and not be too serious. His field trips were my favorite parts of being in Florence. Genuinely enjoyed attending the class.

Massimo doesn't know much English and that forces you to practice your Italian, which is a good thing. He is very passionate and a lovely person, but can be a little disorganized. His class goes very slowly. He makes you do a couple of presentations but it's totally fine if you try a little. Try to be his friend!
Massimo is an awessoommmeee teacher! His english isn't perfect, but he does a great job explaining things nonetheless. Best teacher in the department!

Class with Massimo is interesting to say the least. He doesn't speak perfect English, which means you have to be ready for him to be speaking Italian almost always. There isn't any structure to his class at all which is kind of annoying so definitely use the materials on his website.

Took his Israeli Politics class and really enjoyed it. Professor Shilon is a great professor and is very knowledgeable. Class is graded on a few short film review papers, class presentation, participation, and final paper. He is not a tough grader, and I would recommend anyone who wants to learn more about Israel to take his class!
Avi is a great professor who cares about his students and is always willing to help outside of class. Would recommend any class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Avi is always wanting to help the class, gives responses via email in a very efficient way. Absolutely would recommend this course.

Interesting class with connections to the present day. Clearly cares about students and what she teaches. Can come across as a little no-nonsense but she was warm by the end of the semester. She told us when most of the "pop quizzes" would happen lol. They're just simple check-ins that you should ace if you are reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: While professor Baltacioglu-Brammer is a skilled academic, and highly instructive as a professor of history, she can be old-fashioned in her teaching style. For example, she shamed a student who talked during class. She is not warm, to put it simply. She is sharp, and demands obedience, but you will learn a lot if you do the work.

I honestly loved this class. From the first day you could tell the professor really cares about what shes teaching and is knowledgeable in the class. Grade distribution is amazing, however there are pop-quizzes throughout but if you do the assigned readings you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Brammer is very understanding and engaging. If you skim readings, you'll be okay for the pop quizzes. Nothing surprising in assignments/exams. Interesting lectures, participation is important. Cares about her students, wants everyone to do well. Grade distribution is amazing as well; exams are not heavily weighted on the overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the best profs at nyu!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ayse is an amazing professor and this course was super interesting! No tech in the classroom and she really makes you work for an A. But be warned: you will be lost if you don't do the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: AMAZING. Tech-free and makes you WORK for it (do NOT turn in an assignment late), but it is SO. WORTH. IT! I have never been in a class with a better culture- everyone in the room got so close and studied tgthr outside of class. Ayse is a BRILLIANT historian and my only regret is taking her so late in my college career. 10/10!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: As long as you express interest in the subject and do the best, you will have a great time in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
If you are a vulnerable student who knows they would need some type of accommodation, do not take her classes. She will not comprehend what that entails & she doesn't have the empathy to deal with it. She might even crush your spirit if you are not too careful.
The class was boring & uninspiring. The discussions were too dry & she didn't offer much

Professor is very nice and provides great feedback. She does have a noticeable accent that makes certain lectures hard to understand. However, her slideshows will save the day. She basically only assigns writing and reading. Keep up on the reading she will ask you about it during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She sometimes disrespects other opinions especially if you try to come from a different perspective. She is too old school and therefore looks at cinema still in the olden days. My final grade in her class was very unsatisfactory but I had no choice.

Aviva's class on civil rights has changed my life. I don't understand her less than amazing reviews on here. She outlines what is expected of you on the first day of class. She really cares about her students. Meet with her for office hours so she is familiar with who you are. I wish I could go back in time, I would have taken all of her classes...

Aviva is a very kind woman who is passionate and extremely knowledgable about all things documentary. She loves to hear from students and is a very easy grader when it comes to papers-- she mostly just wants to see your thoughts.
Very engaged, kind, and a generous teacher. Willing to meet outside of class hours and discuss current projects. Creative, talented, and overwhelmingly great teacher!!
Aviva is a fantastic teacher and listener. She's highly engaged with her students and has a GREAT taste in documentary films!! She is very knowledgable about her craft and is a fantastic educator!!

I've taken two classes with Aviva and have loved both. She is a great person and a great teacher. You will get a lot out of her classes if you are willing to show up, pay attention, and do the work. She does not assign busy work. She wants her students to enjoy the class and to do well. She expects you to put forth your best effort.

Amazing teacher! Some sort of writing assignment every week, but the amount learned in and out of class is awesome! She has incredible industry and academic experience and her ideas and quotes are inspirational! Eye opening class.

Aviva is a great teacher. Attendance is mandatory (you're allowed to miss two classes) and you'll have homework almost every week, but there are no tests. Every writing assignment is simply a chance for you to form your own thoughts on the subject. As long as you're invested and bring ideas to the table, you'll do well. Would take again.

Extremely knowledgeable about the subject and always brought in great guests/films to share with the class. She's always eager to share her thoughts with hopeful filmmakers if you ask to meet with her. The weekly assignments aren't painful, but they can be annoying. All in all, great lady, great class.

Master class doc. I love Aviva. I'll admit, her personality takes some getting used to, but she's pretty fair. She only asks that you not be late and care about the subject. I did well in her class because I did the work, and it wasn't that hard. I learned a lot too, and she's well connected. Love this class.

Human Rights in Documentary was a great class. Each class is a film screening and sometimes guest speakers. The assignments are papers, and grading is simple. Aviva doesn't care about mla formatting, she cares more about the things that matter: understanding human rights, being engaged, getting something more out of a class than just a grade.

I've taken several classes with Aviva and she's amazing. She can be a hard grader at times because she expects a lot but if you love documentaries, you will love her and her classes. I promise. I've never received anything lower than an A- in any of her classes. Only because I did my work and I did it well. She won't let you slide with crap papers.

I took all three of Aviva's classes and was continually impressed both by the material covered and by Aviva's thoughtfulness. Aviva cares about each student and is always available to help them and listen. She was one of the best professors I had at NYU and I would encourage everyone to take a class from her.

Disrespects opinions (even her guests, sometimes). Addressed a format issue with my paper (she never spoke to me about) to whole class w/o naming me, but quoted a line from my paper.  Emailed question about final paper, called me irresponsible for starting it 2 days before due. Really? It got done, I got an A-, but I will NEVER take her class again

Prof Slesin is an amazing educator. She cares deeply about her students' ability to think critically about the world, & encourages them to look beyond the docs in class, to find their passion & then question everything. Those that aren't used to independent thinking & prefer the easy path of parroting the prof, will be frustrated in her classes.

Aviva believes each student will have their own viewpoint and seems to respect that until you get your paper back and her markings tend to only allude to the fact she doesn't agree, therefore, your grade reflects such.  Came to discuss with her which she blurted out before I said a word "I'm not discussing your grade. I don't even know why you came
Amazing professor! One of my favorite at NYU. She took a personal interest in each student!
Aviva's class taught me to love and appreciate documentaries. Aviva's insight to the films and their construction has helped me immensely as a filmmaker. Her passion for documentaries is contagious.

I switched into this class immediately after the first day because the professor. She takes documentary making and Human Rights seriously, but her goal is to spark each student's passion/interest.  Through the documentary lens was an eye-opening class and I would recommend this class and Professor to all my friends at NYU!You WILL LEARN A LOT!

She is very unprofessional. Throughout her course she told me that my papers were done well, until the last day of class in which she told me that I couldn't write at a college level and that she would pass me but nothing more.
