I attended all her classes and actively participated but still managed to be a horrible teacher and person.

Aviva's strengths are in the love she shows for doc films and the great (high-profile) guests she brings to class. Lots of in-class discussions, and there was a 3 page paper  each week on the film screened in class, as well as two 8 page papers. If you're interested in docs, or want to learn more about them, you can't go wrong with Aviva.

I was excited to take her course last year but unfortunately found her to be quite passive aggressive to certain students. She did not have a problem with me but her unrelentingness and tone towards a few other students made me feel a bit uncomfortable. I had a good time but can understand if someone else may find it a hostile environment
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Although Professor Ayers has made efforts to being nice and organize her classroom, it has not been entirely successful. The course content has been lengthy and unengaging. Her grading process has not been timely, which has added to my frustration. LOTS OF READINGS, which has made it challenging to maintain interest in the subject matter.

Elaine is such a caring professor--- not only does she care for all of her students but she's incredibly passionate/ wise regarding the work she's doing in & out of the classroom. She is also just an incredibly understanding human who knows how stressful school/ life can be and doesn't push too hard in her efforts to get the best work out of you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Ayers is a fantastic person who I would love to take another class with. She cares about the material and can answer the most tangential or difficult questions. Something I disliked was that it was easy for our class discussions to veer off course: one class we spent almost an hour looking for cafes on the Upper East Side. Overall, great!

She is a really talented teacher. She is always there to help her students. She is available in her office and through email. She is approachable and very understanding. But like the class requires, she does go by the textbook and attendance is required. I must say she ranks  number 1 on my list for teaching Japanese. She is awesome.
Just take her. She is an ideal lecturer. Super nice person, crystal clear - almost transparent - lectures.

At first, Matsushima seems very professional, but is very patient and helpful if you need anything inside or outside of class. In language classes, the easiest teachers don't always help you learn, and I'd rather have a prof w/ high expectations than not learn the language. She may seem demanding, but is understanding and never criticizes mistakes.

She's incredibly arrogant and strict.  She does not create a warm learning environment and my classmates and I agreed that we hated volunteering and answering questions when she was teaching the class.  I'm surprised at the good reviews, because I've had to deal with her cranky attitude for two semesters in a row.

Seems a little strict in class, but unlike other Japanese professors, never gets mad at you for struggling and always makes a genuine effort to help you. Very effective teaching style. Smolderingly hot as well.

Very helpful and fun.  She has a professional air and may seem strict, but is actually very nice in person.  The tests are ok, but there is a lot of homework.  She teaches out of the book so it's very easy to keep up.

She's a lot of fun to have a class with because of her youth and understanding of modern Japanese culture. You can tell her experience from teaching comes from enjoying the learning process, and you can tell her roots are very Japanese in nature. She's a lovely teacher and outside of class a respectable person all around.

she's insanely intelligent. can't expect a high grade without taking notes in class/reading + some questions in exams were obscure talking points you can only know if you pay attention. she was lenient with the grading. tbh, I learned so much in 8 weeks & didn't mind how dense/intense class was.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hope you like to read! Cause that's all you will be doing in this class. While the professor is extremely knowledgeable and seems to have endless to say about the Middle East, it is hard to keep up with the readings. Her lectures are scattered and not in chronological order which made it hard to follow. I do think she's incredible tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take this class unless you're ready to memorize the entire history of the Middle East. The prof is so knowledgeable but her lectures are dense and quick. She goes through points without much context. Her exams are extremely detailed pulling from things she mentioned for like 2 mins. Even memorizing all of the history isn't enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
If you've been relying on ChatGPT to get through university so far… run. Fast.

Professor Erbal is incredibly kind, well-read, and deeply knowledgeable. Be ready to read an entire book the day before an exam and still be tested on it. She's fantastic professor, but you need to actually do the work. No shortcuts here.

Incredibly intelligent professor, knows everything about everything its kind of insane.  Readings are very heavy and difficult, but as long as you put the necessary work in you will be fine.  Grading is very test heavy, but exams are graded pretty leniently.  Will learn A LOT.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the most intelligent and knowledgeable professors I've taken! Her lectures can appear scattered and disorganized, but if you do the readings and really listen to what she's saying you really retain so much, and the course was very interesting; she is very passionate about what she teaches and cares a lot about her students.

I really wanted to engage with this class but professor Erbal makes it IMPOSSIBLE. took this as a summer class and the workload was the same as a regular semester..Insane amount of reading, lectures are disorganized&hard to follow and exams are hard because it just feels like you've learned absolutely nothing even w/lectures... AVOID AT ALL COSTS!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her International Politics of the ME a was a very interesting and insightful class. You need to do the readings and take notes on them because in the lectures you won't get all the information off of the slides. We had midterm and final but it was open notes and the final was graded very generously and she bumped up everyone's grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This professor behaved as though COVID-19 was not happening in the worst months of the pandemic. I'll never forget how harsh she was with testing procedures and grading. Beyond that she demanded memory of an insane amount of info and expected you to come in with a lot of knowledge despite being an intro course. I Pass/Failed.
Easy if you do the immense amount of readings
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Erbal is extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter, and this is clearly conveyed in her lectures. Her classes can be a bit confusing and chaotic at times, however they should not be difficult to follow if you keep up with the readings! One of my favorite classes at NYU so far, don't let the workload stop you from taking this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Although very qualified, Professor Erbal gives way too many readings and if you do not form a study group it is impossible to follow. Graded on very few things, exams are very hard, get ready to work. Her lectures are long but interesting, if you are not interested in the subject, this is not for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Erbal is very knowledgable about the ME, however this didn't correlate to the material being taught well. The amt of readings is vast & the lectures are vague--making it hard to figure out what is important for the 2 midterms/final. COVID-19 made circumstances difficult for everyone, but Erbal was very unaccommodating in comparison to others.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Erbal is very smart and knowledgeable about the subject matter which she clearly is very passionate about. However her teaching style is very hard to follow and there is an insurmountable amount of reading that you can't get away without doing. Tough grader and you will be responsible for insane amounts of information.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pros: One of the smartest profs I've met at NYU. Incredibly well-informed on politics and political history. Cares a lot about her students. Cons: Way too much reading assigned. She often lectures too quickly and throws out too much information at once. Can be difficult to keep up.

Erbal is the most disorganized professor I've had. While she is undoubtedly competent in her field, I frankly did not find her lectures to be necessarily insightful given the insurmountable amount of readings she assigns and weight placed on uncharitably graded essays. I looked forward to this class initially but unfortunately did not learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take her, she is very mean on grades, want you to read a lot but with so much disorganization, and above all, won't be available when it comes to recommendation.

Prof. Erbal is incredible! She beautifully facilitated diverse class discussions & She is BEYOND brilliant; I learned so much about history & the world even in tangents. Sometimes class was a bit disorganized, & there's a TON of readings. But you'll learn SO MUCH & it's so eye-opening-- if you work hard, you'll do well. No regrets!!! She's amazin

Ayda is nothing short of one of the most brilliant professors NYU has to offer. Her readings are fascinating, lectures make you so engaged and fascinated on the subject matter. She's a legend and has an amazing heart. Take all of her classes.
Ayda Erbal is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. Her teaching style is not for everyone, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Honestly, she's really great, and I would take her again  but it's the hardest I've ever worked for a single class ever, period. She assigns an obscene amount of reading, and didn't do a lot of draw connections between them - but after the class, I understand all the readings pretty well, and it was hard material. Would take again, if I feel brave
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take any other class. literally any other one. take a tisch class. take american constitution. do not take ayda erbal. her grading is the so extreme, it doesnt matter how much you study. worst and hardest professor i've had at nyu. i cant save myself but theres still time for you
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE. SO DIFFICULT. THE WORKLOAD IS JUST INSANE. if you're interested in the topic, then read about it on your own time. don't subject yourself to this class. everyone i talked to regretted taking it. i'm just saying
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's deeply insightful and really cares about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ayda is clearly very intelligent but the class is way too much. The amount of reading assigned is overwhelming, which is obvious since she only is able to cover about 50% of it during class lectures. Your entire grade is based off basically just the final and midterm; the grading for those is insane. The class is super informative but at what cost
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ayda is not very organized, but she is one of the greatest professors I've had at NYU yet, and her classes are extremely enlightening. If you're looking for an easy course to fulfill a politics/humanities requirement, this isn't it. But if you're looking to really learn about politics and have your mind expanded, she is the choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Ayda is extremely knowledgable about what she teaches,  but can often be incoherent and extremely disorganized.  She was constantly behind on the syllabus and didn't upload a missing lecture until the night before the midterm.  Wish she could get herself together a little more because she has a lot of knowledge to share.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took Democracy and Dictatorship as well as International Politics of the Middle East. Ayda is a crazy genious but she will be as demanding to you as she is to herself. She is caring and her classes are the most interesting you will ever take. However, dont think for a second she will write you a recommendation letter -  she's so unreliable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Democracy, Dictatorship, & Globalization as a senior, and it was the most interesting politics course I've taken at NYU. Ayda's no nonsense, but she really cares about her students. She's a tough grader (your final grade is based on 2 exams and a group project), and assigned 200+ pages/week of reading. Also, no attendance requirement.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ayda is an absolutely brilliant professor who really knows her stuff. She can be very disorganized and her class can be a little painful because of the disorganization but I still strongly recommend her because of the interesting readings and her erudition. I just wish she had office hours. She needs to have set office hours in the future.

Ayda is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've taken at NYU. She can be scattered during lectures, and a bit disorganized, but every class she dropped a major chunk of knowledge on us and she really made me grow intellectually because of it. I cannot recommend taking her DDG class enough. Truly amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff, but she's really disorganized and doesn't ever really cover  what she intends to in class a lot of the time. Also, her accent sometimes makes it hard to understand but it's not too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: At first I really identified with the criticisms of Professor Erbal on here already, but halfway through the semester I realized I needed to change tactics to do well in her class. I started taking notes by hand, and reading more regularly and really paying attention in lecture and her class became a really interesting, and a pretty fun breeze!

The class is interesting, but the material seems a little scattered sometimes. There's a lot of reading (which you have to do) and the exams are VERY VERY VERY long and are a big part of your grade. She's very disorganized and we're always behind and rushing to get through the material.  Fulfilling class but painful.

VERY interesting class, but VERY disorganized professor. Readings were awesome, topics, were awesome, but she was not (nice person but a bad professor). Classes were pretty pointless - you leave the class more confused than when you walk in, but are good as she gives away exam questions. If she would be more organized, the class would be perfect.

Really great teacher, was nervous about the reported workload. The truth is the grading is very fair and most of the readings are very interesting. Doing the readings helps on the exams because it gives a solid background that the lectures sometimes lack..
She has a lot of insightful knowledge into current events. However if you miss class or don't do the readings you will end up lost.

Really great class! She is one of the best professors at NYU. She is very knowledgeable and you will definitely learn a lot. The work load may be overwhelming for some people but if you're interest in the topic, definitely take the class.

Ayda is a very talented professor. I have found that the course is confusing until the final few weeks when the different themes become intertwined. Definitely do the reading week to week. It will make exam studying much easier. I highly recommend taking her!

Professor Erbal is scary smart and really knows her stuff on Middle Eastern politics.  The class isn't easy, and there are A LOT of dense readings (most of which you do need to do).  Her explanations of the readings were a little incoherent at times, but she was always willing to answer questions when students had them.

This is the second class that I take with Ayda and I can confirm it has not disappointed. She teaches very objectively and tries her hardest to remain impartial when addressing sensitive issues. She's not a difficult grader and while she assigns many readings they are well picked and engaging.

One of the best professors at NYU! Although I do have to say people tend to love or hate her. Her exams are a bit difficult but just remember to always mention the author and works in the essay and vocab. There is a lot of reading, but you can get away with not reading, so long as you focus on the major events.

I did enjoy this course.  The readings are very interesting.   However, there are a ton of readings and you really need to know all of them for the midterm, so I would say get a study group, or you're going to have a hard time.  For me, the lectures were useless.  But the grading was fair and, though Ayda can be intimidating, she does care.

(Intl Pol ME) DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Erbal is w/out doubt the worst prof i've had at NYU. Lectures are incoherent. She knows a lot but is totally incapable of presenting the info in a structured way. Tries to get through an insane amount of material and shows no respect for anyone's time, holding Sat class. Jan. 13 and still no final grade
I absolutely loved this class and professor. If you have a passion for Middle Eastern studies you will likely enjoy Professor Erbal's lectures as I did.

Brilliant woman. Indulged the crazies in her class a bit too much for my taste (a small sector in the back corner attended just to shout ill-informed arguments at her), but a very good experience overall.

Passionate, knowledgeable witty, insightful and critical. Despite some extreme visions she will broaden your perspective on world issues.Classes are high paced and sometimes disorganized but if you are interested in the field of study your focus will not shift. Intellectually challenging yet fair grader. I highly recommend her !

I love Ayda! She has to be THE BEST professor I have ever had at NYU. You will learn so much in this class and your perceptions about the Middle East will change greatly. My only criticism about this class is that I don't know if I would call it a politics course. She teaches a lot of history.

At first, I thought she was a HOT mess. However, as the semester progressed, she slowed down the lectures and became more approachable. The grading is not tough; but there is A LOT of reading. I'm not going to lie, I didn't read it all. But I went to most lectures and ended up doing pretty well.

The MOST readings of any NYU Politics course. Your time is not respected although you are expected to respect hers- if you have a job, other courses, etc, you will struggle to keep up w/ this class (this coming from a 3.7 GPA student). Lectures detract from the material. Discussions are overrun by idiotic students who like to hear their own voices.

lots of reading so pretty tough but very interesting; annoying that some readings are about the same thing but in the end it makes it easier for material to stick in your head; midterm was hard but she went easy on us so everyone ended up doing well; taking notes on reading also helps a lot. she definitely knows her stuff! recommend her class!!

Ayda is extremely knowledgable about the subject. That is also part of the problem. This semester she tried to fit so much into the lectures that we are now way behind schedule and taking notes is quite a challenge. There is tons of reading too. If you're interested try her if theres no better alternative you know of. If you arent interested avoid!

I had Erbal for two classes; Democracy and Dictatorship and IPME. Both were extremely interesting and I can honestly say that I learned a great deal, which is not always the case. She is a challenge, but trust me it is worth the undertaking ;0

Aydas awesome, supersmart and personable (after class, less so during) and if you can synthesize the class notes (attendance mandatory) w/the readings (also mandatory), you'll do very well. I got an A- and worked my butt off but it was worth it because she not only teaches ME politics, you learn the history - great overall experience w/her, fun,too

Ayda summarizes the readings in a very incoherent way. Thus, I found attending class to be more detrimental than helpful. Some of the readings are dense and could use clarification but instead, her classes often ended up in never-ending arguments. Worst prof I had at NYU. Big disappointment in the class.

She basically just went over the readings during class instead of having the readings as supplementary material to class lecture. She was very disorganized and half of the classes ended up being a discussion/arguement between her and one or two other students.

At least this year she's an easy A- grader, not an easy A. You don't really need to participate that much, but she did cold calls. Easy to reach out after class, but the grading criteria were really confusing. Never comment clearly on all the writings. Really cares more about Chicago style than what you wrote. don't take her if u are international

I actually enjoyed this class. Lectures were boring, but I learned a good deal. I never did any of the required readings, just a quick summary. If you dont contribute, she'll cold call, but if you participate at least once per class, she will like you. I put the least effort into this class out of all mine and still got an A. Cares about students.

Had a hard time trying to get an A in her class, grading criteria isn't clear. Class is easy because the lectures are just her speaking. Take this class with her if there are no other good professors left.

Clear on expectations about class work, considerate of others, and easy to reach at all times. 
Easy grader and good feedback on the two papers. There are two exams, but the professor gives a well-prepared study guide upfront.
Take her and get an A.

SUPER easy - she WILL give you A's on assignments if you try. She's very kind. However, it is truly the most boring class you will ever take. She drones on for 90 minutes (always goes over time), and her lectures are abominably dull. You can get by with just the summary of each reading. easy A, but less will to live. I fell asleep every time.

Okay here's the thing, very sweet lady and clearly passionate. She's an expert in her field. However, this will be the most boring hour and fifteen minutes of your life. reviews.comment: a lot of papers and nitpicky. not as bad as some are describing her but her reasoning for taking a point off were silly, like the formatting of Chicago style. was understanding though, just really boring and went over the class time often.

Prof Kola is a super reasonable and knowledgeable professor. I'm not sure why people are giving her bad reviews.. if you do the work you should be able to get an A unless you don't know how to read a syllabus or able to follow basic instructions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

The most caring person!

Inspirational classes
Best professor at the IR department

She is lazy, unimaginative, and doesn't give proper feedback to your papers. She yawns in class and has limited knowledge about world politics. You wouldn't get anything out of her classes that you couldn't get from reading a newspaper. My advice: If you value your time at NYU, don't take her class. Seriously.

I really like Habib! He truly cares about his students and he wants them to make their best work! He's a very nice guy and he knows his stuff. genuinely the goat

reviews.comment: Nice person BUT lecture is unstructured. He doesn't follow schedule and went really fast through any important topics. You wouldn't know what's gona be on the exam until you saw the homework and start self teaching.

He explains concepts very clearly and sets clear expectations for assignments and exams. The grading is fair and reasonable, and the rules are explained in advance. The course is challenging but well structured, and effort is rewarded. Overall a very positive learning experience.

He explains complex concepts very clearly and makes sure students understand both the intuition and design trade-offs. The grading policy is explained clearly, and expectations for homework and exams are transparent. The course is very fair, and the evaluations accurately reflect the material taught. Highly recommended for students.

The course is challenging but well organized. He explains CMOS and circuit concepts clearly, focusing on intuition and design trade-offs rather than just formulas. Homework and exams are tough but fair and closely match the lectures. You will learn a lot if you keep up with the material. Highly recommended for students interested in IC design.

Prof Azeez is one of the best profs I have seen so far at NYU. reviews.comment: One of the best profs at NYU. Completely understands the students perspective. Whatever your concern is, you'd be able to easily communicate with the professor. always late to class....doesnt put that much effort so you have to learn by yoruself alot. Getting good grades isnt that dificult in his class but his assignment is confusing and takes a huge amount of time

Professor Azeez Bhavnagarwala cares deeply about his students, adjusting assignments and exam schedules flexibly based on their academic progress. He also provides access to information about opportunities for industry internships outside of class.

put little to minimal effort to teaching and it shows. always late to class, confusing and wrong answer keys and questions. I'm certain people with poor reviews on his teaching don't attend his classes. Barely 10-15 come when the total strength is 150+. He is a great professor and actually likes what he teaches. Overall a good professor who is an expert in his field with a lot of industry knowledge. Course content is kind of hard but he gives very good grades.
Relatively easy exams. Homework can be a lot at times but the problems appear again on exams. One of the best professors at Tandon.

This man is lowkey the GOAT of the century. He genuinely cares about student feedback and the exams are not that difficult, especially since it is open notes. Definitely would recommend taking this class. As long as you submit all the work on time this an A is possible.

This class is super easy. He tells you exactly what to expect on the exam. Lots of extra credit. Azeez is also a very nice guy, and he is very laid back. Always 15 minutes late to lectures and exams and cracks jokes about how he makes the exams 10 minutes before we take it; He really lives life like we are on a floating rock.

Prof Azeez is an incredibly patient and a kind teacher. One of the few professors who would pace his lectures so that no one gets left behind. No matter what level you are on, he will work with the class to ensure that you understand the material as you go. Very accessible in and outside the class. Always happy to wait back and resolve your doubts!

Terrible professor for student who would like to learn, but wonderful for those just want GPA. reviews.comment: The lectures, homework assignments and group projects were insightful and helped us understand advanced concepts on RISC V.

Prof. Azeez gives students a clear structure of designing flow of a chip through the term project. The project requires students to use Synopsys tools to design a BIST memory system from RTL code to GDS which was very helpful.

The class covered a broad range of topics - from Verilog constructs to the design of logic and memory components from RTL to GDS - their synthesis, verification, static timing analysis and timing closure using tools from Synopsys. Professor Azeez provided insights that helped us design SRAM BIST engines for the term project.

Did not cover anything that was mentioned in the course description. More than half of the classes were cancelled by the prof for some or other reason. Does not have any technical knowledge required for the class. All the labs were setup by two fellow classmates and they had a better understanding of the class and tools than him. Boasts too much.

reviews.comment: Knows EVERYTHING about NYC. He's so explorative and engaging in his teaching. Sometimes lectures can be boring, but it's all great overall.

He is definitely one of the best professors at NYU. He really cares about your feelings and is always very patient with your projects. He is extremely passionate when giving lectures. I took his J-term, a three-hour course every day, and I never felt bored.
Scott is the best, easy class but so fun and the material was super interesting. If you are interested in learning about art in NYC pls take the class!
Scott was an amazing professor! So engaging, caring and knows what he is talking about! If you get the chance to take his class please do
Scott was an AMAZING professor. So kind, genui

reviews.comment: Everyone must experience a class with Fatiha you have not lived until you have. She is the sweetest, most caring soul on this planet. Just trust me. Take her. You will do well. No need for a long comment. Just trust me.

She is so unbelievably sweet, and such an amazing professor. I cannot stand language classes but I enjoyed and was excited to learn French. The class is a lot of work for sure but you will learn French. Cannot recommend enough.

She's the best French professor at NYU. If you can, take her! Intensive courses can be bit much in terms of the course load but she is extremely understanding and somehow makes you look forward to morning classes. Attendance matters A LOT so be present and on time, it all counts for participation.
I love Professor Bali's class! She makes it so interactive and fun! Highly recommend for anyone who is looking to improve their French and learn more in a caring environment.

Professor Bali has been my favorite professor my entire time at NYU. She is so sweet and always goes the extra mile. She is always there to help and is very understanding. She wants you to do well and I want to do well in French because I want her to be proud. J'adore le professeur Bali et à cause d'elle, j'adore le français. Take her if you can.

Prof. Bali is the best!! If you struggle in French- take her class. She genuinely wants you to do well, so just show up and ask for help when you need it. She is very kind and wants to help you learn French. I enjoyed her class and actually improved in French, without google translate.

One of my fav profs ever. I never liked taking foreign language classes in hs and was never good at learning a language but prof bali makes me want to become fluent in french. I wish I took her earlier in college bc then I would 100% major in french.
An actual queen. So caring, cool, and dedicated. Everyone in the class loves her.

I took Fatihas class in the first semester of my college life and she was just AMAZING! Nothing seemed to be hard as long as she teaches me. If I have the chance I would definitely take her classes again. I miss this wonderful teacher and her class so much.
I loved having Fatiha as my French prof. She truly helped me enjoy learning the language and often cracked jokes or played funny videos to keep us entertained. So sweet and so caring, she is amazing!

Professor Bali is an amazing professor. I had the class 2x a week for 2 hrs but it was never a burden! The class is super chill. When I had it it was in Lipton lounge and she would bring in croissants/pastries when we had exams. She is super understanding and you can email her about anything!!

I love Fatiha so much!!!! She is literally the best professor. Soooo understanding and really wants her students to do well. She brings us croissants on test days and is just an ANGEL. She really does an amazing job teaching french to students who are struggling and helping those who need it

Croissants on test days, SNL videos at the end of class, and a teacher who will make you laugh. She uses the textbook in class but also writes extra on the board for tougher grammar. Favorite class of the semester.

reviews.comment: Intensive Elementary French with Fatiha Bali was my favorite class of the semester. She genuinely cares about her students and makes hard French concepts easy to learn. She makes an effort to make classes enjoyable (and usually brings croissants on test days). AMAZING PROFESSOR

Fatiha was by far my favorite french teacher ever. She made learning fun and would encourage everyone to participate. Everyone should take this class! on quiz days she brought croissants for the class !

The nicest, most understanding and helpful professor I have ever had. During the hardest semester of my life she was the only teacher who showed any hint of understanding and that I really felt wanted me to do well. You do have to put in work to do well but the tests & assignments are all reasonable. I learned a lot and I will miss her :)

Easy core class. Easy A. Take his class if you are good at memorizing things. Make sure you get a nice TA and show up to all the labs, then you will get an easy A. He's an easy grader and tests are pretty standard and easy as well. The class is extremely applicable and interesting. Loved his lectures :)

The Brain: A user's guide was SO disorganized and pretty difficult for a core, non-major class. The professor tends to ramble and isn't very interesting to listen to. He puts most people to sleep. The class has a ton of neuroscience jargon that is confusing. The TAs are helpful if you get a good one, but the prof is very okayish.

Honestly one of the most caring professors I have ever had in terms of material. He is straight up and down to earth and is truly knowledgable about his subject matter. It is a shame many students are unable to handle a real professors and need to be coddled in their time at college. Shame.

Dr. Azmitia is an excellent professor and lecturer. Be sure that you attend all lectures and lab sessions, and that you are highly familiar with the powerpoints. You will be tested monthly. If you have an average of "A" in his class (labs, papers, and tests combined), you will be exempt from taking the final exam. 4 tests, 2 papers, lab every week.
Professor is a good, caring man, but the class is very disorganized. Lots of tests based on the PowerPoints, and no textbook. TAs were very cool.

His lectures were very disorganized and he can be rather confusing. The questions on the tests are taken directly from the powerpoints but the powerpoints often were out of context and didn't really make any sense. The tests always had mistakes on them which reflects how some of the TA's really didn't care. Overall, I regret taking this class.

What a horrible class.  Disorganized lectures--incompatible exams.  TA's made the exams w/o the prof ever looking at them, when he reviewed the test w/ the class afterwards, he realized he would have gotten many questions wrong.  An awful and stressful class for a student.  I learned absolutely nothing--sad thing is that I love the subject area

Not your typical MAP class. Consists of 4 tests in the semester, of which your top 3 count for 40% of your grade. Final (30%) is pretty much all repeated questions from those tests. Labs + 2 papers which count for 30% in all are a joke. The tests are really annoying, but not having to study for a final is nice. Graded fairly. Prob easiest NatSci II

His lectures were pretty disorganized, but he's a very sweet man. The grading is very fair. The review sessions set up by the TAs (Shyam!!!) are incredibly helpful--necessary to go. The class does require work, but I found it all fun and interesting. Azmitia is a very nice man who really cares about his students.

NAT SCI II - The Brain: A User's Guide - Like many others said before he is a bit unorganized, but he really cares for his students & he is very approachable. If you have no interest in science or if it is not your strong point, I don't suggest you take the class. He curves all the tests and allows you to drop one. I got 3 Bs & 1 A and I got an A.

He is an easy and understanding professor. It may not be easy to get an A is the class but all you have to do is try. His final is all questions from previous test and he curves his tests like crazy. If you get a 50 ish test grade, he'll curve it to a B. He may be a bit disorganized, but the TA's are the best.

His lectures are terribly unorganized and just ramblings. His tests are all multiple choice/True or False, which you would think should be easy, but it's not when the lectures suck. Although I passed this class only because of the amazing TAs, it's still apparent that he cares about his students - hence the crazy curves on the tests.

This man is absolutely useless. The lectures are rambling, and he tests you on things that aren't discussed in class. The lack of a text book makes it impossible to study for the tests. Worst of all, the man is incredibly insensitive while dealing with very serious issues such as gender and depression. HE THINKS GENDER AND SEX ARE THE SAME THING.

Absolutely terrible! The worst class ever! I strongly recommend you to avoid his class (I feel terrible for saying this about his lecture) but it is true that he is just NOT good at teaching. The lectures are disorganized and he does not clarify what to study and what not to. I felt like he was rambling throughout the lectures. Don't take his class

This was the most disorganized class I've ever taken. Take a different NatSci class. Incredibly random and incoherent lectures. Slides come directly from Google images. Under-qualified TAs. Nearly impossible to get an A.

I took NatSciII The Brain: A User's Guide. Lectures were disorganized and difficult to follow. Offered students opporutnity to print out slides pre-lecture but often changed slides right before class. TAs communicated poorly. Take a different NatSci class or Intro to Psych if you want the same (better organized and better thought-out) material.

Nat Sci brain: the users guide.  Lectures and exams were extremely disorganized.  Poor communication among TAs and prof.  Exams were easy but you have to study and be present at lecture.  Azmitia is a fair grader and willing to work with you.  He tries to get you the best grade possible.  Interesting class.
Great Professor!! Passionate about Neuroscience! Truly cares about his students education and success!

Awful class for competitive liberal arts students. An absurd curve gives nearly everyone a B, making it impossible to get a higher grade without prior knowledge or insane amounts of studying. Good if you want to get a B w/ minimal work, bad if you care about your GPA and hate bio.
I took The Serotonin System with him over 12 years ago. I learned a lot.
No Comments
Professor Azmitia is a great guy and his class The Brain: A User's Guide is really not difficult. Just do well on the tests. The final is optional.

I entered this class hating it. But i really like it now, even though I don't care about the Brain at all. If you do above the average on tests, you're fine. Lab is easy. There is almost NO homework. Azmitia is HILARIOUS. I make a point of never missing class, though because there is no text book. Class is fun. Take it.
In the beginning the class is a bit scary but it turns out awesome. He is brilliant and hilarious. Attendance is not mandatory and the tests really aren't that bad. Azmitia is just hilarious.

He makes no sense, makes no effort to explain, the test are hard but subjected to an absurd curve in which 65-90 is a B, and it is impossible to get more than that. He spelled the same word 3 different ways in the same sentence. I have no words to describe what a failure at teaching this man is. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS FOR NATSCI II,it was a mistake
im so bored

this class was sososo awesome - azmitia is really nice, sarcastic often which is hilarious - quizes are crazy easy b/c he lets u retake them again the following week - i dont think he even read the term paper lol - easy A as long as u study his slides and do the work - azmitia is so cool and nice and a GENIUS.. take the class!!

Intimidating at first b/c he's this great scientist, but you find out that he's just a really friendly, FUNNY guy. VERY laid back on quizzes and book reports and ALMOST anything goes. His lectures were VERY boring at times and VERY VERY interesting and enlightening during others. However, to REALLY know about 5HT, you study the topic on your own.

Lots of negativity among other reviews, which I think are unwarranted and unhelpful. Dr. Bassler is a knowledgeable and effective lecturer. However, she occasionally cancels lectures, which leads to either pivoting in assignments or the lecture schedulei tself. I did not feel that she did this intentionally, and she clearly communicated.

She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She will make sure that everyone gets the material. She does tend to cancel class quite a bit, but it's usually due to health issues which aren't her fault. If you want a professor that is genuinely passionate about what she's teaching, this is the one.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bassler works very hard to improve your skills in aural skills AND music theory. We do a majority of sight singing, but it is very helpful to know what you need to improve on. She is very kind and cares about what you think and feel. If you need help she is very accessible and wants to make sure you understand the content.

Dr. Bassler stood out among the boring aural skills/theory professors who made no attempt to connect with they're students. Anyone who gave her a bad rating probably doesn't know what their talking about...
This teacher is awesome I love her. Very friendly learning environment and she actually cares about the development of her students
Goes on a lot of really interesting tangents and I think she got a cool vibe
she is really bad

Honestly I didn't learn a thing but Dr. Bassler is very funny and tries to be engaging. She would cancel all the time, often last minute and yap the entire time when we did have class. The homework assignments and quizzes weren't too bad as long has you somewhat knew the material beforehand. Lot's of dictation and unrelated conversation.

Bassler is so confusing. It was supposedly an easy course, but it turned into hard labor. The midterm was absolutely terrible. She gave us a 2-hour bring-home online test, turned out to be a 5+ hour test with 20+ essay questions that she expected us to finish. It's ridiculous. She is so easily distracted in class and always makes things awkward.
Bassler is the definition of just OK. You won't learn a thing though.
yaps too much
DO NOT take Bassler if you value your own education. This is not even about grades. You actually learn nothing in this class. Plus she's mad annoying

The workload she assigns is egregious for a 2-credit course. I have four credit courses where I don't even get half the assignments. The midterms require you to write 20 essays that are around 500-words each. She strays off topic so much that we end up learning nothing in class. Everything I learned in class I learned by doing my own research.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her midterms are absurd. Although it's a take-home exam and online, that midterm has around 20 essays to write. It took me around 3 hours to complete, as I did it fast, but it would've taken 4 to 5 hours if I had taken my time. After all this, though, they graded my exams in less than 3 hours of submission, which is ridiculous.

I know that Bassler is a good person but she is def not a good teacher. She is not very great at explaining things very clearly which leads to a lot of confusion during assignments. She also gets distracted a lot which makes classes very unproductive. Def wouldn't recommend taking this class.
Bassler is funny and engaging! Take her class!

I'm never taking a class from her again. She gets way too political and emotional, once she spent the entire class talking about the presidential debate. I am all for small talk and having fun, but if you're going to be talking about it for 90 straight minutes, why not just teach politics? I actually don't feel like I've learned anything valuable.
Dr. Bassler is a great professor. She really cares that her students do well and she is willing to work with you to get there. She is bubbly and animated in class and is a joy to learn from.

Look. I'm gonna be real with you: Dr. Bassler is sweet and funny, but she is not a good instructor. She has an incredibly rigid mindset about music that is often more reductive than it is helpful. She's fun, but she missed a TON of classes during the semester. Nice person... but my least favorite class last semester :(

Professor Bassler is a great person but as a teacher she set me back. I took 3 courses with her my first year at NYU because they were the only ones available once my selection time was up. Honestly dont waste your time, you wont learn much and she refuses to give clarity when you ask her for help.
She is caring, such a cool person. Just too passionate and I took for an elective course so... yeah

Dr. Bassler is extremely accommodating and understanding of whatever you might be going through; she's one of the best professors I've had in that regard. That said, she cancels class all the time, which really derailed my enjoyment of this course. It's hard to feel motivated to learn when weeks pass without a proper in-person class meeting.

Speaking of being a teacher, she is the textbook of average: she is not bad at teaching not so good at it either. Yet, she is an extremely caring and nice person. I was in a different time zone so she opened new zone-meeting time slots specially for me and I didn't have to stay up late for meet-ups. I will recommend her.

I took her Musicianship II class online. Her lectures are the definition of OKAY: she just doesn't have much efficiency with the content but she does teach not bad. Personally speaking, she is a really lovely person----easy-going, patient, and welcoming to explaining anything----for her personality, I would take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Thought it was a good class since my friend told me exams are online. However, this class is not worth it, it does not make sense how this 1-credit Aural class gave so much work every week, even more than my 1-credit Engineering class. Attendance mandatory. Grading for midterm and finals is not clear. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. DEF NOT A ONE CREDIT CLASS.

Had her for aural comp 1. I didnt learn much. I taught myself everything. When I ask her for help its always just practice or youll get it eventually which wasnt helpful. Shes very energetic which is a good thing but not at 8am. Personally, if you really need help with ear training or you never did it before then dont take her please.

The class as a whole was pretty meh. It was really heavy in assigned reading and the online lectures were boring but you have to be there with camera on to get participation. Professor Bassler is always very enthusiastic about what is being discussed in class which is refreshing. I'm not sure if I actually learned anything though...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Bassler means well, but her online class is really boring. And all the writing you have to do at the end of the semester is lethal. She's also an inconsistent grader. Sometimes she just passes out As and sometimes she randomly grades really tough. Depends on the week I guess. Overall not that bad but really boring material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Bassler was super flexible and class was very engaging. She is very playful and fun and is very hip. We had a week after due dates to complete work which was super amazing and she makes the material, which is usually boring, super fun to learn. I took Music History II

Absolutely fantastic!! Workload is a lot but she is very understanding and extremely caring Professor. Bassler is really funny and energetic!! Office hours are amazing!! By far the best theory professor ever!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: she. is. the. BEST!! I have had Prof. Bassler two years in a row now and am currently in 3 of her classes. she is one of THE best teachers and people I have ever known. she is endlessly patient. when I was placed in her class, which was the level above what I was supposed to be in, she completely tailored the whole thing to me and helped me.

One of the best professor during my college career. Very knowledgeable, caring, and accessible. She is strict but I think this is beneficial for learning, which would be good for you unless you just want to take a easy course. Also a teacher that had very important education on me, very lucky for the experience of studying with Banks.
Took the class 2-3 yrs ago, I love her so much. She is a very caring professor.

3 years after graduating college I came back to write this review for professor Banks. If there was one professor through my entire schooling career I actually remember, it's her. She's caring but more than anything her teaching style and overall content has been truly impactful in my life after college. I think of her often & hope she is well!!

3 papers and 1 group project. for my class: paper 1 was imitating the writing style of an author we studied in class paper 2 was an academic essay paper 3 was a personal essay. group project was to introduce a painting at a museum. project was super easy, pretty chill grader, hates tardiness, try to participate but lowkey it doesn't affect grade
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved Danis. Despite me being a pretty eccentric person and quite the yapper, she always listened and actually cared, and was willing to respond and give advice too. Now since I do have dyslexia, reading is a bit of a challenge for me, and when I told her she kept it in mind, not calling me out on reading in class. I love her so so so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: a nice person but grades harsh imo. weird writing prompts that take over a page to explain and one mistake can tank your grade entirely.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE HER! She is honestly the best professor I had this semester. Only 3 essays and a fun group project. Super caring and will give extensions for valid reasons if you ask prior to the due date. Couple readings every week but they are short and some are actually fun. Easy A if you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great time, solid professor

She actually cares about her students. Very strict on attendance and participation. Beware of a pop quiz in the middle of the semester. Write good papers and show up to class. Office hours encouraged.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Danis is a great teacher with a participation, discussion heavy class format. 3 essays during the semester, with drafts for each of them and clear feedback on how to improve. However, most feedback is grammar based and often overpowers the writing itself, leading to a somewhat lack of improvement by the end. Overall, very sweet and approachable.
tough grader, strange grading criteria, not recommend, run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is just a Karen who only gives feedback on grammatical errors without constructive advice. TOUGH GRADER. I hate her. She is ruining my college experience. I wish that I had dropped this class the first day. Don't be deceived by the overall rating.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Her class was super interesting and she grades fairly. A lot of opportunities to get a good grade on essays because there are a lot of drafts prior to final submission. One final group project and presentation at the end of the semester was not difficult. Final paper counts as final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Banks is an overall good professor. Her class features a special theme so you'll explore more deeply into this aspect. There will be readings, and get ready for in-class writing. Papers are graded according to her expectation so follow her advice. Three papers, one group project, and some easy quizzes in class. Go to OH, she is ready to help.

Amazing professor to improve your writing! 
Highly recommended for those who want to get good grades and improve your writing at the same time!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Banks is amazing!! Literally the best writing professor I ever met. She is always accessible outside the class and is ready to give you really detailed and helpful feedback. She allows you to have courses via Zoom when needed, so she is pretty flexible. I learned a lot in her classes. If you want to improve your writing, choose her!

She gives incredible feedback that allowed me to actually like writing and at the same time to grow as a writer.  She is very lively and doesn't do what I think of as a traditional lecture. What she does instead talks about the text, analyze it, and point out some writing technique used. I 100% recommend her.

This class was pretty hard for me as I'm not that big of a writer, but Danis is really encouraging and made me want to try hard in that class! She gives amazing feed back, which is rare so if you want to improve as a writer you should def give her a shot

Danis is such a great professor to have if you want to develop your writing abilities. She gives you good feedback and her essay prompts are very introspective. Her readings aren't always the easiest, but they're diverse and many are super interesting and pulled from The New Yorker. She's also very understanding and there to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Danis is a tough professor and has tough readings, but she will give you feedback on papers that tell you exactly what she's looking for and is reasonable when it comes to grading. The readings are heavy, but you have to do them for class discussion. Overall, a good, but challenging class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She offers good insight and really practical advice. She's different from the hundreds of other writing professors in my opinion, she actually cares and helps you dramatically improve your writing. Took her online last semester and it was great

She's actually an awesome professor if you have the chance to take her you should. She doesn't grade too harshly, however she does give good feedback. Her class completely changed my writing and thats the only class I can say such thing about. Def take her!

My favorite professor! She's so nice and understanding and the material she teachers is really interesting. There's always a reading to do for class, but they're usually short, She is tough on grammatical errors, but gives really clear and helpful, feedback on papers. Take her!

She is just the sweetest and sometimes corny. The readings are very light but theres always a reading due so keep that in mind. Her in class assignments and papers usually have a clear prompt and it shouldnt be too hard to get a high grade as long as you stick to the guidelines. Shes my favorite professor bc she was very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The major papers tend to get longer as the semester progresses, but she gives you insightful comments and practical advice. You will have to put the work in if you want the A, but if you humbly accept her comments you should get a decent grade. She's very defensive about her opinions and tends to stick with it, so you may have arguments about it.

Really great freshmen writing professor, she sets you up to understand how to write good papers for later in college. She cares about her students but in a tough-love kind of way. Def not an easy A class bc to her, there's always something you can improve on (which I think is a good quality in a prof) Lots of reading and class discussions

Professor Banks is one the most kind and caring professors at NYU. She really cares about making her students better thinkers and writers. Participate and share your opinions in her class. Definitely take her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Banks is the most legit prof I've ever had. Gives good and helpful feedback on papers without overpenalizing because she truly wants to help, which is amazing. Also uses peer review a lot. Her lectures are awesome and always interesting but can get boring if you don't like to participate because they're mostly discussion-based
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor! I enjoyed her class. She's grammar-heavy, but her criticism will definitely help you become a better writer. You do have to work in her class, so I'd recommend taking her if you're into getting your work done on time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She was fantastic! Some said she was a tough grader, but I think she was just fair. You learn a lot and are pushed to speak your opinions! 10/10 Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Good professor for writing. She gives thoughtful comments on your essays. Very tough on grammar and sentence structure. Would recommend if you're a capable writer. If you're looking for perfect grades every time leave. Participation is IMPORTANT
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Amazing woman! Tries to make class enjoyable, CARES, and is usually available for office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I don't understand why all the reviews are bad; Prof Banks is amazing! She helped improve my writing skills tremendously; her social awkwardness is what makes her quirky and she tries her best to fill in any awkwardness in the class; and her readings, which can often contain films, are eye-opening. Perhaps the others just don't like the work load.

reviews.comment: Don't expect to contribute, only to have her opinions shoved down your throat. Her Crippling social awkwardness makes for an uncomfortable learning environment. Sometimes just so obviously blatantly wrong. Not nyu material. Extremely focused on grammar. gives random articles from the new yorker as if that was good literature.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She's so horrible. So opinionated and refuses to listen to any different ideas. Also very mean. NEVER TAKE HER!
Always being sarcastic in classes. LOTS OF READING. TOUGH GRADER.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: amazing course!
Open-book tests, that's all you need to know, but actually put in the effort; I low-key failed on that.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely love this professor!! He is the best professor I have had. I loved his classes and how he connected psych topics to pop references. His exams are not hard, but extremely specific, so you have to make good notes for your exams, which takes time. But I'd do it again if I had to.

Im pre med taking orgo and phys and somehow this class was my lowest grade. His exams are in person open note which sounds easy but like half the exam is ultra specific questions that require a niche understanding of something mentioned once during a lecture. On our third midterm he asked questions about a 10 minute ted talk he played one time?????

Great professor! Although classes are online, he makes it very engaging and explains concepts throughly. 3 exams, 1 optional final that is cumulative but can replace an exam grade. You can bring any paper material you want to the exams which is helpful. Very nice and knowledgeable, lectures are all recorded too.

I don't think it's worth taking this professor for Intro to Psych. Exams make up 90% of the grade, and the essay portion makes an A unlikely. First two exams had low average. There are other Intro Psych courses at NYU that are easier for earning high grades. im. a math major and this might be my lowest grade which is insane, DUMB GRADING AVOID!

Great Professor overall, but class is test havy 3 midterms and 1 final  account for 90% of your final grade and The final is optional if you do well on all 3 midterms. The average for the first midterm was an 80, so basically impossible to get an A? He says he will curve if the average is too low, but not sure how that is going to work out
Even though this course is online, he makes it super engaging. He is very nice and knowledgable. The content is easy to follow!

Dr.Bavel was a great professor, his lectures are extremely engaging and catered toward his students so that we fully understand the content. The class is tests heavy so it is important to review lecture and readings but regardless he is very accessible and so are the TA's
Amazing lectures given by doctor Jay, a truly inspirational course for student like me major in engineering.

You have little contact with him due to the large number of students in the class. However, he is one of the best lecturers that I have ever seen. His lectures are extremely engaging and have sparked my interest in psych. I am so thankful for this course and Dr. Van Bavel. There are 3 mandatory exams and 1 optional final. He gives extra credit!!

One of the few professors that make getting an A, or overall high grade accessible to all students. His lectures are engaging even though not mandatory, but you have the ability to watch on your own time through zoom. Tests are straightforward and easy as long as you use the study guide to review. Also, recitation assignments are easy grade boosts.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Van Bavel is such a nice person. While you have little contact with him, his lectures are great and really reflect the tests. The tests are application based and are tricky so be careful and use the study guides. Do not let that steer you away from incredible lectures and an amazing psych class.
Amazing professor. Great lectures and awesome personality. Would 100% recommend if interested in psych.

Very caring and nice professor. He makes his lectures easy to understand and interesting. Exams are open-book and easy (as long as you study and understand the concepts & study guides will be given for each exam). Highly recommend.
Amazing intro to psychology professor that makes lectures fun and entertaining. Very kind and accommodating to students. Take his course!!!

Best professor I have ever met at NYU. I took intro to psych without any former psych knowledge and this course is surprisingly fun! Now I decide to minor in psych and that is all because Dr. Jay's lectures make me so interested in psych. Exams are open-book this semester and not so hard if you take notes and review during the lectures.

Love Dr. Jay's class & would take again. Tests covered textbook reading and lectures. Lectures were very interesting and easy to understand. Downside was that test questions were extremely specific and if you missed one detail from lect. or readings then you would get it wrong. Graded on 4 tests and some things for participation grade.

This class is definitely not as easy as some people are saying as many of you cheated lol. Yes, this class is easy if you take the exams together, which obviously it's harder to catch people doing that online. It's not a hard class. Just saying a lot of people cheated hardcore since the tests aren't proctored.

First of all, this professor gets extra points for teaching a lecture while trapped in an elevator! That is dedication. He has great lectures, and always ties in pop culture references for humor. His class is 90% test, and there are 3 mandatory ones. So it's important to study! Overall, I loved professor Jay and his class! I highly recommend him.
super easy and interesting intro psych professor. definitely an easy A if you just look over the slides and fill in the study sheet that's provided. highly recommend

Jay really is a great prof, just a really nice guy and was very accommodating. Compared to other profs, he makes online lectures so much more interesting. Exams are easy if you study a week before. Really upset this class is ending, but it's made me strongly consider about pursuing a minor in psych. If u have Jay as a prof, you won't regret it!

I took Intro to Psych just to try out a psych class for once in my life and thanks to Jay, it will certainly not be my last!! His passion for psychology is highly contagious. He has also made the online learning experience a lot less difficult by making lectures very engaging and fun. If you get the chance, take his class, you won't regret it!!!

Absolutely loved Dr. Jay! Seriously he is the best prof I have ever taken in my entire academic career, I am so sad this class is ending! He is extremely accommodating and truly cares about students' well being. Don't even think twice about it, HE IS THE BEST!!

Jay is the GOAT, and he is an amazing person and lecturer. Made exams open book b/c of COVID, made every lecture really interesting so students were able to engage with the material. As long as you study for exams 5-7 days beforehand and use the study guide, you'll ace the exams. Never missed a class, and it was always the only class I enjoyed.

I really appreciated having Dr. Jay as a professor this semester. His lectures were always interesting, and he was very knowledgable on the topics we discussed. He also seemed to genuinely care about the students, and he was flexible given the pandemic. If you have the opportunity, please take his class. Readings were not necessary, lectures were.

Great psych lecturer. Lectures aren't mandatory but go anyway because his exams are based on his lectures. Exams are easy A's if you attend lectures, do assignments, and study a week b4. Attend class as an optimist. I find it better sitting in the front. I tend to pay more attention. Also, attend recitation and start research participation earlier.

Professor JVB is excellent and his lectures feel like ted talks. He seems humble as he admits he's not sure on an area of study. In addition, he teaches his lectures using psychological principles. For example, he asks questions relating to a concept in order for students to actively recall the concept, enforcing the material in an effective way.

90% of the grade is based on midterms, however, they are very fair exams. His lectures are always extremely engaging and made me want to go to class. Makes funny jokes here and there. Can't really asks questions, but makes the class very interesting with real-world examples.

Super cool prof- funny, efficient, understanding. He gets that school is hard so he makes it super easy to pass. no attendance, but I never skipped b/c the lectures actually made me laugh and I still learned ! Definitely take his class if you're interested at all in anything psych! For real adding psych to my major b/c I was so inspired

Really great professor. He makes classes interesting and funny (you won't want to skip which is crazy)! It's hard not to do well in his class; he drops your lowest - and one of the tests is ALL multiple choice! He gives you literally everything you need to know in the study guides; he wants you to do well and gets that school is stressful. 10/10!!

Best Teacher Ever !! Seriously take his class if you have any interest in Psychology. 4 exams (including the final, which is cumulative) and one is dropped. Super chill guy and amazing professor, one of the best (if not the best) at NYU
Gives amazing lectures and is thoroughly engaging. The tests aren't too difficult, just make sure you go over your recitation notes clearly and examples used in class.

AMAZING PROF., so far the first class that I actually wanted to go to. He makes his lectures as engaging as possible, he's pretty funny & very knowledgable. If you go to his lectures/look at his slides (he writes his script on PP presenter notes) you'll be fine, but you will study a lot since each exam covers a bunch of content

Professor Van Bavel gives clear, entertaining lectures that prepare you well for the exams. The exams are relatively easy if you go to every lecture, take notes, and skim the class readings. He posts the lecture powerpoint after class which is helpful if you missed anything during. I highly recommend him for Intro to Psych.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: amazing professor. His lectures are interesting and entertaining. Exams can be challenging but if you attend his lectures you already did half of the job. Strongly recommended.

Today was my last day of class, and I honestly have never been so sad for a class to end. Van Bavel is one of the most engaging and interesting professors I've ever had. He truly know what he is talking about, and presents the information in such an easy to understand and entertaining way. He makes his students eager to learn and retain info.

This class was really interesting and his lectures were fun to attend.  However I felt that his assignments and exams were poorly reflective of class discussions.  He's really easy-going in lectures, but has really, really difficult exams that he does not curve.  So prepare to study hard for those midterms/finals.

He's structured the class as a graduate course to prepare people for other graduate courses but is clear and helpful enough to make this possible. He is engaging and makes an honest effort at creating a discourse and exchange with the class. He not only knows the material very well but he understands how it comes across and what can be difficult.

If you like Social Psych, this class is a more in-depth version of that. It can be tricky- tests are short answer and essays, and have an hour time limit. There is also a lot of reading, and a fairly tricky paper. But Jay really knows his stuff, and his classes are engaging. He is also really open to helping out of class. Also pretty cute...
Super nice teacher. Haven't finished the class yet, but she explains all the material very well so far. No complaints!

she was okay. attendance didn't matter and the lectures were online and recorded. felt bad because not a lot of people responded during zooms, but also the class was boring and a bit disorganized. Felt like lectures didn't help too much, it was mainly my TA and practice problems that helped me on exams. she did not know much about the exams at all
No curve at all throughout the semester and extremely difficult final. She's kind of mediocre, a bit disorganized. Lots of practices and self study needed to get a good grade.

She is very disorganized and doesn't know much about the tests being given. Attendence isn't needed but if you've never taken calc this class will be kinda hard. I just took it for my calc requirement for the bio major and struggled a lot. No curve was given either
maybe the most unorganized person ever. do not take her if you are already not an A+ student in math. run

It would be difficult to take this class if you've never taken calc before, because the lectures were taught in a way that felt as though you should already know key calculus concepts. Even though I took calculus in high school, I found the course challenging and relied on lots of information I learned in high school.
She was my 8 am, slept through most of her (online) classes, still passed.

lectures and notes could be confusing, but she posted recordings and digital notes which helped. problems on homework and exams were harder than those reviewed in class, but the final was not as hard as the exams before it. there were weekly quizzes, but some were dropped

Very tough class. I had to get tutoring throughtout the entire semester. I had taken AP calc which prepared me a little, but if you haven't taken calc before then I would not take. Her teaching style is quite confusing and there is little instruction. The only things that saved my grade were the curve for the final and all the online homework.
Professor Stepp is an amazing Professor. She cares greatly for her students, and her online lectures are awesome. Don't hesitate to take her class.

Prof. Stepp is a great person, but I don't think she is the best at teaching. She assumes that most people already have knowledge about probability/statistics, which sucks if you don't. Her notes are a bit of a mess but they are not too bad. 1 midterm and 1 final, no curve. She's hilarious though, and shows us her cats all the time.

Do not take her. Especially if you are taking another stem course alongside. everyone does badly on the midterms and there is no curve. lectures are based on her knowledge not the book. Had to self-teach myself and at the end i wasn't willing to get a C on my transcript so i withdrew. Asked her for help and she was not helpful and even rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: kind of the goat tbh, super nice and explains concepts clearly w lots of examples. i personally didnt find her notes confusing and she was pretty okay about recording lectures. exams were way harder than the material taught in the lectures tho, mid 70s avgs on both midterms so far, no EC. long hws and webassigns but shes still a great prof imo
prof stepp's notes are disorganized and her explanations are always unclear and difficult to comprehend
i gotta run, but, to whom it may concern: do not tak
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Made the online class interactive and encouraged participation. Will definitely be on her good side if you go to all the lectures and make an effort to participate. Go to class because notes can be confusing at times and lecture recordings are not guaranteed! Weekly hws but they prepared you for the tests + quizzes so definitely do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Stepp was decent at teaching concepts, but her notes could be confusing on times. I mostly just focused on doing the homework and it was similar to the tests. For the midterms, the first one was difficult, but the final and the 2nd midterm were not too bad. She is really helpful if you ask her questions and the quizzes were really easy.

To be fairly honest, I didn't think that Stepp taught very well. Her lectures were merely useless and disorganized since she just based everything from her own knowledge instead of actual textbook-based material. First two midterms were mediocre (given no curve) and the final was just horrific. She curved everyone's average at the end.

solid explanations, answers questions over zoom. doesn't interact much with her campuswire. test wording can be oddly tricky. there was extra credit for the second midterm, and the final was optional. my biggest con was that her notes were a little disorganized (they were just all one one giant page). really nice and casual/chill tho. uncurved.

reviews.comment: She was overall a great teacher, she is very patient and kind. She is very nice and patient. But indeed a lot of HW.
Be prepared to face a huge amount of work and hard exam that does not look like the actual ones at all.
Study hard, then a B+ or A- wouldn't be a prob!

Prof. Stepp was great for the data analysis course and had good lectures. She was always available in office hours to answer questions and was very good at explaining concepts. Overall a great professor for math.

Dr. Stepp is really sweet and cares for her students. She will take the time to explain concepts if you need them. She likes questions! Her explanations are clear, and she is engaging. She adapted to the pandemic well and really cared for her students' wellbeing and success in the class. if you can, you must take Stepp!! She's literally the best professor I've ever had in college. Her lectures are actually amusing and she welcomes all questions without any judgement. Elizabeth Stepp is one of the best math professors I've ever had. I had Professor Stepp over 10 years ago, she has a genuine interest in the student's learning and success. Professor Stepp is super nice and caring, she's always available outside class and responds to emails fairly quickly. The examples she does in class are almost always on the exams. She really wants you to understand and do well. Definitely recommend taking her class.

Professor Step is the most caring professor I've ever had. She is always accessible during office hours and after class and does her best to help her students. She also asks for students' opinions on how they want to spend class time before exams, and adjusts to their needs.

Professor Stepp is the best math teach I have ever had. You are extremely luck if you get her. She is a hilarious person and an even better professor.
