reviews.comment: JUST DON'T. Textbook was used, but none of the questions on the textbook was related to exam questions. Theory heavy lectures with messy notes that couldn't be understood.

Avoid! Honestly ruined my stats experience. His lectures were unreasonably hard and covers a lot of theoretical concepts that couldn't be understood. Exams were hard too and graded harshly. It was not possible to succeed in this class with his unreadable notes and difficult exams, and you will learn almost nothing about stats.

Highly recommend for those whos serious about econ. He teaches the formula and focuses on intuition, which can be conceptual, theoretical, but AMAZING. He doesnt care about math. As long as you UNDERSTAND it, math doesnt matter (quoted). Exam is graded on procedures, and lose grading. One of my best decisions at NYU, very thankful.
Hes the most terrible one you can have for university. Guys, just dont ��

Tbh the worst prof I have had here. He seems fun and an interesting person, but he's ridiculously bad at teaching. His lectures are SUPER difficult, he uses advanced topics to explain introductory material, no examples. Everything is dry theory but at the exam he asks things he never told us. No one I asked understands him. Ruined my term really
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures may feel a little confusing, but they're actually very interesting. The exams are honestly easier than lecture. Do the weekly homework and the exams will be fine. Listen to your TA's grading criteria and attend recitation. He was fairly understanding of the corona situation too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice guy. But, he doesn't really know how to teach statistics outside of the abstract. Expect theory heavy classes that don't deal with numbers whatsoever. His lectures are confusing and not structured at all; there is no textbook so your only solace is to attend recitations. If you don't attend recitations, you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly not an easy A class, but amazing lectures. His class is helpful in a way that he really requires us to understand the material instead of merely how to solve the problem. The class may seem confusing at first, but you will likely find the class interesting when you get to know his style and understand his words.

Bisin is probably a good researcher but he really doesn't know how to teach undergraduate students who are new to statistics. He is terrible at math so he leaves everything to the conceptual level. His lectures are very confusing, sometimes he gets himself lost. It is possible to ace the exams but you need to self study a lot of materials!

Bisin overall is OKAY I would say. Very nice guy, funny and cares about students learning. Make sure you go to class and write down every word because he doesn't go by the book and will test you on what you did in class. If you have Seher Gupta for recitation, you're lucky and make sure you GO FOR ALL OF THEM. She is amazing and taught me everythin

Do not take his class. He is a very nice person and genuinely cares about your LEARNING. But that results in him not caring about your grade. He is extremely vague about his exams and tests and won't tell you ANYTHING. You'll have maybe 2-3 questions for the entire midtermfinal and they'll be mad hard. Just do yourself favor and avoid him.

I'm still not entirely sure why NYU has such great Intro teachers but not one decent Intermediate one. Bisin is a good guy, but he WILL challenge you and make you work hard. He thinks spending 5-6 hours on a problem set (which you'll get every week) is the norm and you SHOULD be stuck and have to think it over. The structure of the class is weird

Curriculum is poorly constructed, involving jumping from topic to topic without much depth or explanation. Lectures are unclear. Bisin frequently goes entire lectures without explaining even the basic concepts behind each problem, leaving even the most interested students lost. However, he is a funny and interesting guy.

He has no book for the class. This is not an Introductory class, but instead, an advanced and quickly moving survey of microeconomic principles and topics.  I don't understand how he is still teaching aside from tenure and research contributions. Arrogant and comes off as unhelpful.

I pay attention in class yet learn little. He skips multiple steps and often tells you more about what you will learn rather than actually teach it. You don't know what is important and things are taught in random order. When I look at homework sets, I don't know what I'm even supposed to do. He's a cool/smart guy, but not a great teacher.

Bisin gives off the charts interesting lectures, they are not always directly related to the material but they are very engaging and entertaining. He is very kind and helpful to students who approach him. He can come off as a bit intimidating at first but he is a great guy. Incredibly helpful to students who make an effort in the class and with him

Bisin is not a great communicator or teacher, making the material difficult to understand. There seemed to be no structure to the class, and many people seemed lost. He asks little of his students, though, making it easy enough to get a good grade without truly comprehending the material.
Bisin moves fast, very fast. Classes seem scattered and material can seem difficult at times, but it makes sense if you can keep up with it. Make sure you're interested in the subject beforehand
Class is in dire need of a real textbook.  Prof's notes are whimsical, unpolished, and not nearly comprehensive enough.  Basically, if you ever don't get something, you're screwed.

Bisin is a brilliant economist, but not that great of a teacher.  He knows and understands the material in his own mind and in his own language (Italian) but struggles to convey the principles simply to his students.  However, he would be a much better teacher if he asked more of his students (i.e. its possible to get by without doing any work).

The class is a difficult one - don't take it if you're not sure about whether you can deal with the amount of mathematics in it. I changed to the Policy track after it. He's a really knowledgeable guy, and he loves what he's doing - but he's not particularly into an easy approach, dives right into it assuming everybody's going to be following him.

Okay everyone who keeps complaining that microeconomics should be a prerequisite obviously never took microecon, therefore has no grounds to say it should be a prereq. Its not for a reason, if your good at math you will do well in this class regardless of prior econ knowledge.
Very intense, not much help if you don't have a background of the course.

You should know principles well and you should be familiar with basic calc. The economic intuition is explained in class, but it might go over your head if you have no econ background and don't spend time reading outside materials (try varian, he puts suggested books on the syllabus for a reason)...he's not the greatest teacher, but you don't really have a choice!

very unorganized but interesting class. very little homework (3 problem sets) doesnt really matter how you do on the tests and problem sets because he gives everyone a B+ unless he knows who you are and he likes you

Extremely interesting class... material is well presented and challenging. He uses good examples and always explains the intuition behind the math. Most of the other people commenting are, uh, lets say "sissies", and should take a econ principles class, or just go back to high school.
He can not teach, he can not even speak, does not even reply the e-mails. You can not learn anything from the lectures, he is not prepared at all!
requires calc 3 and micro. not an intor. with otu a good TA dont even bother taking this class. You might get an A, but you will learn little int he lectures.
No Comments

Nice guy with a good sense of humor, but this class is impossible. It is NOT an introductory class and should not be listed as one--it definitely requires prior knowledge of microeconomics and that should be a prerequisite.
Can barely speak english

Bisin is a cool guy.  He obviously cares about what he's teaching.  The class is indeed hard as ****, but there is a big curve and he does a lot to help grades.  The subject material is a little abstract...  but if you stay with it its fine
Bisin's a good enough teacher. The class and material is just hard as****, half the class dropped after the 1st midterm. Noticeable Italian accent, but actually pretty funny.

She's really unorganized, late to classes several times, and I know it was specific to our class, but she also cancelled 3ish classes due to her own schedule. Considering how much we pay for each class, it was very disappointing.

Professor Blakeman is the best! She is full of stories from working in the music industry in multiple different areas, and is always down to give advice. You end up working in groups a lot for quizzes/the final project, and it was really fun. Her lectures go by quickly and are fascinating. Highly highly recommend taking her for Music Publishing.

Prof. Blakeman is one of the best at NYU. She is super insightful about the industry and helps her students get involved with industry professionals. I enjoyed her classes. The lectures were super data-heavy, though workable. All the quizzes are teamwork-based, so they will be easy. The final was super easy, too. You must take her class!

One of the best professors at NYU and the reason why I stayed in my major. She is so sweet, humble, yet has so much experience in the industry, both as an artist and executive. Definitely take her class! She will make you love Music Publishing!

Blakeman's class has been the most enjoyable Music Business class I've had. She's very knowledgeable about the industry and encourages students to discuss their opinions. She's very open-minded and actually listens to suggestions. The class itself is pretty easy; there's a lot of group projects though.

blau is super chill, very accessible outside of class (MCBGroup). everything for MCB1 is clearly laid out, and as long as you watch the pre-class videos (normally 5-30min), do the quizzes, do your homework, and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. there's a growth bonus if you improve over the course of the class, and extra credit.
Overall a great lecturer and interesting classes! The exams are very long and a bit challenging, but a good reflection of the lecture content. The British accent also makes it more interesting
I could listen to him talk for days on end. What a great guy!!!!!!

i absolutely loved blau. i'm so glad i took mcb1 (not required for me) bc of him. his lectures are so helpful and i learned so much from him. mcb1 was also one of the most helpful class for me (with biochem 1). he makes it very possible to get an A with practice exams and homework. nothing but praise for this british man.

blau is a great professor, he's clearly there to help you and will make it so you can improve. even if you do poorly on exams, there are ways to help save your grade. this class is difficult and his tests are hard but if you put in the work you can do well. you will need to put in a lot of work though.
really good at encouraging discussion using poll everywhere. slides are relatively good. show up to class.

Never showed up to a lecture and this guy is still my favorite professor lol. Every lecture is recorded and he clearly states everything you need to do in order to succeed in the class. As long as you take the time to watch his recordings and do the practice problems he gives you will do fine. Overall, a great guy who wants his students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: loved loved loved his class. expectations and assignments are very straightforward. if you understand the main concepts taught in class, you should have no problem doing well. exams are very similar to practice exams and homework problems. growth bonus can help your grade if you are stuggling. basically, just take him !
As a person who got an B- on POB1 and still managed to get an A on MCB1, he is one of the best professors you can find at NYU.

Really cares about students doing well in the class, has lots of resources available outside of lecture and super easy to approach. Made learning mcb very enjoyable, exams are pretty fair and the growth bonus also gives the opportunity to raise your grade even if you start out poorly. Definitely take him if you can!

LOVED Prof. Blau. Such a nice person, good lecturer, and very willing to help students succeed. His dedication to teaching is so evident and the amount of work he puts into helping students outside of class is inspiring. Super approachable and will explain anything without making you feel stupid. Highly recommend this class I've learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Adorable intelligent British man with humor. Blau takes advantage of active learning over passive learning. He's truly fantastic. If you want an A, my biggest tip is to prime yourself before each lecture by going through slides and understanding them just enough so you are never in the dark during lecture, and you can feel apart of the story.

Decent lecturer, lenient grading, HWs and practice exams are very good prep for the exams. I just wish he would type out concepts & explanations on the slides instead of just having diagrams and a slide title. When you're sitting in a giant lecture hall early in the morning, it's pretty easy to zone out and lose track of what he's talking about.
he's my glorious king.

This man is the goat. Whoever is complaining is wrong. Tests are reflective of homework and lectures. It is exactly what you did for homework. Grading is very fair. Do well on the homeworks and it boosts your grade by a lot.

Definitely not a tough grader, so much partial points given, even to the point where just plain getting the answer wrong could be 50% points given. Very caring and respectful, just put in the time and effort to understand and it will show

Great professor, entertaining, makes you feel like you want to learn, has good attitude which is important. Course isn't easiest but isn't hardest, if you're in research since freshman year you'll have a very easy time. Easier than orgo IMO, great professor, lecture heavy but what isn't, definitely doable and very possible to get A

Overall really great guy. MCB1 concepts can be difficult but he's super dedicated to helping his students understand. Would recommend taking advantage of all the different resources like OH and MCB group. You're graded on many different things so it's possible to end with an A even if you mess up on an exam

Prof Blau is such an amazing and caring professor. If you're struggling I highly recommend going to OH, MCB group or even talking to him after class. He's really patient and will explain everything until you understand it. I noticed my understanding of MCB improved so much after making use of office hours and MCB group, would def recommend going.

For Blau's part of MCB, be sure to pay close attention to his lectures. The pre-recorded videos go over techniques of molecular biology, and the lecture is about a topic in which that technique is applied and proves how/why that topic was discovered using the technique. Application and conceptualization heavy for exams. Good professor though.

the content is hard, but he tries his best to explain it. review and consistent studying is necessary to pass. He truly want his student to be successful. his style of teaching is experiment heavy and there really isn't content, just a bunch of tests to prove something. Would recommend taking him if you are interested in doing bio research

The material wasn't hard, but Blau doesn't know what a flipped classroom means. At least half of the information being tested on the exam was taught in class instead of in videos, which was annoying because I almost always had to rewatch the lectures to take better notes even if I went in person.

Even after going to class, was heavily confused about content. Prepare to take notes and toggle between post and pre slides. Study practice problems, he will repeat similar question on exams and test you on understanding of lecture content. Go to your TA's office hours and ask question in MCB group.

Hes a really good professor and I highly recommend his behavior class. Hes very good at explaining things and makes sure his students understand the material. There is a decent amount of work but it is not too difficult and it is a reasonable amount. Highly recommend.
Dr. Blau is all about being a chairman and forgets what is the purpose of a student pursuing a degree.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Blau was definitely my favorite of the MCB 1 lecturers. His slides were clearer and he generally helped me to understand better. Make sure you don't skip lecture and study often. There was a generous curve but that doesn't fix everything. Go to review and make sure you do well in rect. (completely separate from lecture but helps your grade)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Excellent prof!  Prof Blau really tries to get people involved in thinking, so he asks a lot of questions.  Tests aren't too difficult if you study his lectures.  He's very helpful during office hours.  Overall it's a really interesting, fun class taught by an equally interesting professor.  I highly recommend him and Nat Sci Human Genetics!
justin was a great prof, very clear and organized. interesting class and helpful labs. definitely recommend!

HWs are nothing like the exams (I wish they were more similar). Be sure to focus on edge cases when studying. Practice exams are outdated and nothing like the current exams. The big file of examples is a good representation of what will be on the quizzes/exams, but the actual questions that will show up can throw you off.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dont take this professor unless you want to rethink your whole life and major decisions. I would not wish this class upon my worst enemy. Messed up my first semester at uni and my mental health.

Hws are not at all similar to exams, but they weren't bad; autograded and free resubmits. Goes quickly in class, talking abt stuff not on slides, and doesn't have recordings, so you def miss stuff. Exams are tricky even w/ cheatsheets, but he (slightly) adjusts grades to make up for it. Said he had harder exams last sem, hence some earlier reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teaches concepts well, makes time for you outside of class, and is passionate about what he teaches. However, the homework doesn't sequentially reflect the midterm/quiz content. Exams are reasonable for what he has taught, but they are a time crunch and reflect the more difficult end of problems. If you put in a lot of effort, you will learn a lot.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He is accessible outside of class and gives good feedback, but if you haven't taken java in high school, I WOULD STAY FAR FAR AWAY FROM HIS CLASS!!! His homework assignments are so far off from the exams its not even funny and he does not curve them no matter what. More than half the class ends up dropping. RUN PLEASE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: run run run run

He is a nice professor, good teacher for concepts, and is very willing to provide extra help with outside sessions. But for an intro class he is very very tough, homework does not help too much with very hard exams.

Teacher is hard, straightforward but nice, class is extensive and hard but it prepares you for the real world struggle. He expects you to know things and no one asks questions. But he is really willing to help and will make 1-1 time for you if you ask. The class has a lot of math references, and is based on coding syntax not mcq.

While the lectures are very in depth and he does a good job of teaching CS concepts. His tests are extremely difficult and grading system unfair. On Midterm 2 the class average was a 41% and no curve was provided. It almost seems as though he is trying to fail as many students as possible. Definitely much more difficult than other CS101 classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework has nothing to do with exams
Great professor but really hard and tricky tests.

Fascinating class. Very clear that Professor Block is an EXPERT in his field. Brings in concepts from cs, cog sci, neuroscience, etc which makes the class more interesting but also difficult. LOTS of reading so don't try to cram. Wish slides were more informative with less pictures and more text. Essays are hard so be specific and start early!
If you are interested in philmind, just take his class. It's not easy to get a A but u will definitely learned a lot.

He's very experienced, knowledgeable, and incredibly well-read on contemporary developments in psychology, neuroscience, and even deep learning. He's passionate and engaged in office hours, and he shows genuine interest in interacting with students in and outside of class. There's lots of concepts, and you do have to understand some deeply.
You have to take one classes from professor Block if you are a phil major! Lecture is super fun learned a lot about mind.

Philosophy of Mind: Philosophy part is not difficult. However, Biology and Psychology are unexpectedly difficult. Recommend not to take his class unless you are highly interested in Biology and Neuroscience.

Ned Block is a respected professor, and he is top in his field. Nonetheless, it doesn't deter him from teaching a boring class. Avoid his class if you actually want to learn something because everything is explained better in the reading material.

Consciousness is NOT for you if you do not have any psychology or neuroscience background. The philosophical aspect of this class is not hard, but the scientific terms and experiments are very complicated. Yet you have to get them straight to completely understand this course. If you are humanity-orientated, this course is gonna be a struggle.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredible professor! Incredible class! Loved having the opportunity to take a class with Block. It is incredibly an incredibly dense class and at times, lectures and readings are hard to get through. However, if you stay on top of the subjects and pay attention you'll learn a lot.

I agree with the other comments here. Essays are definitely pretty hard to get a solid A on, but as long as you're thorough with your answers you should do fine. A big part of your grade also comes from attendance and the final, so as long as you put in reasonable effort you'll do fine.

Block's lectures are non-mandatory but you DEFINITELY want to turn up, because this man is not only a snappy dresser but he genuinely does his best to make the already engaging course material interesting. This class really is graded by a few things, since 60% of your grade is distributed evenly across 3 essays. Essays are tough but graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures alternate between fascinating, mind-numbingly dense, and both at the same time.  He knows a breathtaking amount about his field, and has written a lot of influential papers  in it.  That being said, his explanations and assigned readings are not always very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Block is the type of professor who makes being on a college campus so invigorating. Although some of the material is complex (esp. for an intro class), Block does his best to allow for questions/discussion during lectures. He is easily at the top of his field and absolutely worth taking. Also... as other noted he has an amazing sense of style.
good professor, interesting ideas
The only assignments for class were the weekly readings (which admittedly sucked), and three 3-5 page papers. Plus a final. Such an easy class and it was extremely interesting.

Professor Block is the nicest guy. He's incredibly passionate about consciousness and is always asking students what they are not understanding, so he can work with them until they get it. Gives you all sides of the debate (though not shy of course about where he stands). Lots of reading, but assignments are just reading comprehension questions.
brilliant teacher at the top of the consciousness field. has no qualms about arguing his own ideas against the material he teaches, specifically his nemesis dennett. also a snazzy dresser woo hoo!

took his class "minds and machines" when he visited harvard.  fantastic. led me not only to study philosophy but to try to pursue it professionally.  only gripe is that he didn't accept harvard's offer...
No Comments
Brilliant man.

Dr. Blaney was a phenomenal professor this semester! Her lectures are clear and easy to follow, with detailed slides and many opportunities for questions or clarification. The homework assignments and tests were all straightforward with review sessions in class. Her office hours were also very helpful, so do go if you take her class!

Dr. Blaney is INCREDIBLE. I loved every lecture & left with lots of knowledge & interest in epidemiology. Her slides and lecturing are straightforward & she always stopped for questions. She dedicated class time for test review. Manageable workload (some homework assignments, a group project, online textbook.) I wish I could take this class again!

Her lectures and slides are detailed - don't need to read the materials assigned. She is caring and you can go to her to talk about anything. She has study slides for 2 exams and 1 midterm. There was like 3 hw assignments and one easy final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Blaney was the sweetest and kindest Professor I met at NYU. She listens when we express that the TAs might have graded something too harshly. I didn't do any readings because her lectures covered all the materials anyways. She has study slides for all exams and there's was't much hw (maybe 4 max). Very accessible and ready to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: great professor, her class is good
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Participation matters. Also read the books!!
A great professor!!! Classes were always fun and challenging. She rocks!!!!

this is a great class. dopico black is excellent and knows a ton about the subject. sometimes we went off topic a little but it was always related and interesting. the grading is very fair. good to speak up in class.
This is one of the best classes I've ever taken and one of the best books I've ever read. GDB is amazing.
Awesome prof. Awesome class. Take it!
No Comments
No Comments

Never hated writing more, and I came to school for it. Unclear feedback and convoluted instructions. If you are a straight and to the point person communicating with her is difficult. Do not take if you value your creative liberties.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I wished I liked this class better, but if you are a writer for film/narrative/non-fiction, especially if your major requires it, taking this her class will not help you. Lessons become tangential and she talks herself in circles. Feedback is redundant and your essays will be boring and by the book, but with no prior expectation set by her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Blag is kind. That comes to grading as well. If you put effort in and participate you'll be good. Zoom when you can, she likes the effort. She doesn't explain what she is looking for in the essays so she'll likely always have you completely change your essay. She gets off topic during class. Use the class to get other work done but pay attention.

Puts more restrictions on topics than pretty much all other teachers, but deeply invested in her students' success. Your papers will be fine as long as you do not go to her for feedback (she will twist your essay into something you don't recognize). Good excursions outside of class!!

You have to write what Blag wants you to write, which goes against the entire principle of Tisch WTE. I received A's on all 3 of my papers this semester because I took no liberties, and my papers were honestly worse for it. She's good if you're not a writer and want to be told exactly what to do in this class. If you're a writer, don't take her.

Absolutely loved her as a person. However, there was never a night without homework. Often long prompts and had extremely tough grading. She would give feedback but it was very obscure. There are fun outside-of-class activities that she offered extra credit for, in the form of excusing absences.

Blagovesta is a nice and sweet person, but not the greatest professor. Her feedback makes little sense, and she'll assign loads of homework for short periods of time. On my 1st progression, she told me that I need to start over with a whole new idea way too close to the deadline. She cares for her students but it's hard to succeed in this class.

Blagovesta is genuinely great, however, her homework's often seem like busy work and more or less ridiculous. Exercises only made sense and were clearly connectible to the progression during the 3rd essay. Her feedback will need follow up, but she wants you to succeed so do it if you want to learn with carefully crafted questions. Also hilarious.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I liked her, but her class was just so confusing and overwhelming. Clarity and workload are her biggest issues. Feedback is also not great. She's one of those teachers who says "think deeper" and won't tell you how or why.

This professor's requirements for her assignment are extremely hard to understand. She doesn't articulate her ideas well and something the class thinks she just saying things to say things. She a lovely persona and has the biggest heart. It's just hard to do her assignments because of her requirements/prompts.

This class was extremely taxing. Not very helpful but assigns tons of work regardless. Criticisms can be very harsh and almost impossible to accomodate for. Papers have to be written so specifically to how she wants it, leaving no room for creativity. She's also not very accomodating for lateness, absenses, or late work and makes no effort to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Awful class. My previous writing the essay class was amazing but this one is just awful. The professor gives elusive feedback, is a very tough grader and has a set essay formula in mind which she expects everyone to follow. We learn nothing in class and she assigns plenty of complicated readings wich we never discuss or even mention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The amount of work is ridiculously small compared to other teachers. If you need free time to work on other things, this is the right teacher. She is very nice, and gives good advice.

Like all of the other reviews, she is a very nice person; however, the class itself is not enjoyable. The course load is heavy for the amount of time we have in a semester. The same amount of work due Wednesday from the Monday class as is due Monday from the Wednesday class. She checks everything! Very caring lady- just be ready to work!

Very nice and caring. However, as a professor, you don't learn much and is a complete waste of your time. Her online classes are ineffective. Every class she wastes a lot of time and we don't learn much at all. Her responses in class are very abstract and hard to understand. She also gives lots of homework too with not so useful comments on essays

Caring person, but this course as an online class is absolutely terrible. Her feedback is elusive. Zoom meetings are inefficient so far. She often spends twenty to thirty minutes addressing logistical issues. The purposes of the assignments are questionable. I don't know about how she is in-person, but don't take this class if you're going online!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Really nice and friendly, a great person for no doubt. However, not so much as a professor. Her homework are meaningless and classes are disorganized: she lets students chat randomly for an entire class. She gives a lot of hw and has a very harsh yet equally ambitious grading criteria. Don't take her if you want to learn something from this course.

WTE is kinda an awful course anyways, but she really tries to make it interesting. She can be a bit confusing bc she usually has very specific opinions, so if you're wrong you're wrong. Also she has a tendency to go on tangents in class which is kinda fun because then suddenly you're 45 minutes into the class and you're still talking about birds.
She does not know how to write or grade. She is not helpful. I want to cry.

I absolutely love this woman as a person. However, as a teacher she is not the best. We spend most classes talking about completely random topics that having nothing to do with the lesson. As a result, there is a lot of work to do outside of class. Chill class time, but it leaves you with lots of work to do. Unclear with directions and tough grader

She's the most homely and fun teacher you'll find on campus. While grading is not too easy, classes are breeze and full of interesting discussions. She is an amazing person whose class I would absolutely love to take again. 10/10 recommend.

Blagovesta is a Bulgarian angel. WTE is inherently an awful idea, as the class varies drastically depending on who teaches it, but you really are saved if you choose this prof! She assigns about 2 pages of writing outside of class which may sound like a lot, but these "exercises" end up making up the body of your essay, so drafting is a breeze!

Blagovesta was my favorite freshman year teacher and if I could take her class again, I would. She didn't stress me out, but still motivated me to do my best and I am really proud of the work I did in her class. If you can, take her!

He gave good feedback on essays and was a pretty easy grader. He made the class interesting even if the readings were boring. He was really chill and I felt like I learned a lot. I absolutely loved my class with Joe! He's a great lecturer but the class isn't lecture-heavy and involves a lot of work in discussion groups which I personally enjoyed. There's a lot of reading, some of it boring, but very few other assignments besides the midterm and final. Overall a fun and interesting professor!

Jo is the best! He made the class very engaging even though some of the topics seemed boring at first sight. He is really passionate about what he teaches which made the class more interesting. Not a lot of papers. Just a take-home midterm, a discussion post, a research paper and final. We also had a class trip to the MET! TAKE HIM!
Love the teaching style

I truly enjoyed his class. From the beginning (which was on zoom), he managed to make a highly interactive classroom. He has extensive command of marketing and I loved that he ended each class asking us what we learned and what/where we had questions. Brought in guests speakers and I feel his projects are very similar to what we'll do IRL.

Always ending class 30 minutes ahead of schedule. Tuition wasted. Strict on tardiness. Being 5 minutes late is called "super disturbing". This is NYC. Subway delays and traffic jams are part of daily life.
Avoid. Nitpick every detail in homework assignments.

Unclear grading criteria -allow subjective report structures but may not align w/ his preferences. Demands excessive detail,strict adherence to professional report standards in HW, when in reality HW is a way to show comprehension. If you're busy w/ internships, this class may not suit. As a high-achiever, a B on paper was incredibly disappointing.

Prof. Meyerson is great, loved the jokes he'd crack in class. The grading was very tough, but he did give pretty good feedback (especially during the one-on-one meetings), which helped me improve my writing tremendously. Honestly, just participate A LOT during class and put in the effort because it'll pay off for sure!

Amazing professor who will improve your writing ability. Fun in class and during one-on-one meetings, and is a joy to talk to about any random topic. The class grading can be harsh because his standards are high but participation will help a lot.

He's a really amazing guy overall. He can be harsh on grading essays, but make sure to really put effort into them and think deeper than you are used to. His classes are very interesting if you take initiative and participate. Once you know how he grades, you can adjust your essays as needed.
Syllabus doesn't matter. Only 3 essays. Poor feedback on writings.

Prof Meyerson cares a lot for his students and wants them to succeed. I learned so much in his class and opened my eyes to many different perspectives. Tough grader but gives a lot of feedback for improvement. I didn't think I would get a good grade because of that but ended up getting an A. If you put in the work, you'll definitely see results.

B&S is a terribly structured class, but Meyerson makes it actually useful. Amazing, discussion-led lectures that cause you to genuinely think about the course content, and the class revolutionized my understanding of society. Grading criteria is clear and he gives great feedback. I never got an A on an essay, but still got an A in the class.
He was a really good guy, fun to be around. Grading (in this course in general) is rough-ish but aside from not "great" feebacl, hes overall a really nice guy

Best professor I've had at NYU! Took his Commerce and Culture as well as Business and Society. Genuinely cares about his students. Take advantage of how open he is to giving feedback and apply it to the papers. Morning classes are never fun but he makes them quite enjoyable if you participate. Couldn't recommend him enough!

LOVE HIM! One of my favorite classes I've taken so far. Felt like I really improved on my writing. He's a tough grader for sure but effort, time, and participation all really help. Makes morning classes funny, keeps classes interesting. Cares a lot about his students.

A lot of ppl r saying that Meyerson is a harsh grader due to his emphasis conciseness but I wanted to point out that I got the lowest score on the rubric for conciseness on my 1st essay and still got an A-. He's also willing to give feedback on essay content before u submit it so it is not hard to see what resonates with him and what doesnt.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I honestly really liked Professor Meyerson. Yes, he is a tough grader, but so is most if not all other professors for B&S. He has slides that guide his lectures and there is a fair amount of time where he talks to us, but there is also times that there is discussion. I am not the best at discussion based classes and I was still comfortable.

Class is entirely based on in class conversations and some slide shows. Class is extremely enjoyable if you have knowledgable peers that engage in conversation. Tough grader but once you understand how he grades and what he looks for. Took him two semesters in a row, your relationship with him matters and he will make you a better writer.
he is absolutely horrible... it's beyond me

Professor Meyerson is very caring and makes class interesting, but he is a tough grader. I took him for Commerce & Culture and again for Business & Society; once you understand what he is looking for in the papers, it's not too bad. 

If you genuinely pay attention to what he wants and participate in class, he'll like you and you will be just fine.
Pls don't take this prof unless you have to. Toughest grader in NYU.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Appreciates good writing. Be sure to speak often and with high quality remarks, not just dribble--argue against other classmates, if you must. But participation is important, because although he really liked my writing, I didn't speak enough in class to warrant an A. He makes a 7-hour class bearable, and I talked to him for two hours outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't anyone who got an A in his class, it seems like he tanked everyone's grade and no one knows why. On top of that, his classes got really repetitive and boring. No matter what you're looking for this guy's class probably isn't for you
Did not care about the students

"You're the best class I ever had!" Thanks Prof! Why'd every single person get an A- then? Everyone? Everyone. You clearly care about the quantity, not quality of what we said. Take this to heart, dear reader. What you write doesn't matter at all. Neither is what you say during the mind-numbing sessions. It's how often you say it. Thanks Prof.

I had professor Meyerson for my B&S intensive and he was one of the first professors who made me feel seen and heard both in and out of class. He gives everyone a fair chance to speak and remains engaged even during 7hr classes! I loved his stories, especially the one about Costco! Really hope to bump into him in the hallway sometime.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I didn't have Professor Meyerson in an online format, but I can tell you that he is one of the best professors I've had at Stern. As long as you put in the effort to work on your writing (and meet with him outside of class), you will learn a lot and rewarded accordingly. Professor Meyerson made B&S an engaging and insightful course.

Watch out for Meyerson. His classes are very lecture-based, and these lectures are boring. Other Business and Society classes are far more engaging. On top of that, he's a harsh grader. Very few people get As, and that hasn't changed in the pandemic. It's not a terrible class, but I didn't learn much beyond his stories about trips to Costco.

Professor Meyerson is overall a great teacher. He's kind and caring and wants the best for his students. However, he is quite a tough grader, pretty tough to be honest. But, if you want some help, he'll always be here.

Look, I appreciate Bruce's lectures and the fact that he is a relatively engaging professor that seems to care about his students. HOWEVER, there's one thing he doesn't care about, and that's your GPA. He will absolutely wreck you if you don't either adhere to his exact style of writing. Honestly not worth the work, he gives NO A's, barely A-'s

He cares more about style than the analysis. There is no world in an english class where someone should be getting a B- when there are no comments about the analysis and the only comments are all personal style points. Save yourself the effort and unnecessary stress. Don't take this guy. Hes great outside of grading and feedback, only GPA matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You are graded on 3 essays. He hands them back after the draft of the next essay is due, even though there is a MONTH to read the essays and grade them. He is SO nitpicky and if he does not like your style, he will give you a b- or lower. Its not just passive voice, its delete all adjectives, no extra words, just write in the style he wants.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would like to think that Meyerson has a war on a good fraction of the English language; his stylistic conventions are eccentric, and he makes a point of doing away with some form of grammar or syntax at the beginning of each session. He will prioritize writing over analysis, and he has a very particular style of writing which has to be followed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly I thought he was going to be a good professor, and he is funny in class, but PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. YOUR GRADE WILL MESS YOU UP. YOUR GPA WILL THANK YOU DONT TAKE. There is no clear grading criteria and if you do not write PRECISELY AS HE WANTS (despite saying we should have own writing), you will fail.
Fantastic Professor. Had from for IEPT writing portion. difficult, more so than others, yet will help develop writing skills.
Meyerson was a really great professor! Super nice, funny, and helpful. I looked forward to his classes.    He really went out of his way to help people succeed.

Bruce Meyerson is a Stern legend. Had to take him two semesters, and my writing skills have improved exponentially. He's also an amazing person, and he really wants to help you improve by answering to questions in person or via e-mail directly and quickly.

Professor Meyerson actually makes sure that, by the end of his class, you actually know how to write well.  Because of this, he is one of my favorite teachers to date.  People who do not do well in the class usually do not utilizing the teacher more; Meyerson is always available to discuss your essay and how to improve it.
Terrible Grader
Funny, Helpful, and smart. Can be a tough grader, but he's fair and he can definitely help you improve your grade - and make you a better writer
Sarcastic, funny, chill, helpful
Unorganized

Be prepared to do a lot of self-study. The class is not where you first learn the basic concepts of the material. If you don't read the material ahead, you may have difficulty understanding the lecture. The class is held with the expectation you've already read and understood the material beforehand. So the lecture may seem somewhat unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: if taking during the summer, it is really fast paced. try to get everything done ASAP. At times she is not clear in the things she says. follow the syllabus and you will be ok

I don't understand why she gets so many negative comments.
She is a caring and smart professor. I learned a lot. Maybe it's because I'm in the small group at the doctorate level with her.
Disrespectful and awful!
She did not seem to follow research updates for decades.

She is really demanding or difficult to work with. Demanding work is one thing, it's completely unacceptable for her to be disrespectful or irresponsible for students in the nursing research class. Further, some of her faculty instructor are even worse. Awful experience. Never wanna take it again.

It's condensed to 6 weeks and the turn around time for assignments is extremely short. Mostly group work and one to two people end up doing all work. The class is poorly designed. Professor Bruno lacks organization. It is the most inconsiderate graduate classes and made me question the value of the program and the price tag. Do better.
She has a gift at keeping you engaged, very enthusiastic and just an overall pleasure to work with and listen to. Highly recommended professor.
Fantastic professor,

Professor really cares about her students, but is not the best teacher. There are quizzes every week but just study the slides before hand. She accommodates everyones situation, but sometimes gets off track with what we are learning. Did not necessarily learn a lot, but easy A.
Very enthusiastic prof. There are quiz every week but as long as you do your weekly homework and read the slides after class you'll probably be fine. Very understanding
Great teacher!!! Everybody take her stats class!
he is the most lovely man ever. best best best best best and easiest class ever.
This is an amazing class - really makes you think about your college experience.  Lots of great guest speakers/ Prof. Dom is approachable and funny.  Take this class!
Awesome class - interesting content.  Super organized.  Great professor!
i love this professor
pretty much graded on completion. essays are fun and TAs are mostly chill. Dom is super nice and gives everyone extensions for pretty much as long as you need

Designs the class so it's easy to get an A, i.e. 5 DB that are pass/fail, five quizzes where you get ten open book attempts, and two papers. TAs are lowk useless and may grade oddly, but if you just do the quizzes and discussion boards, it is very easy to get an A in this class. Very interesting content as well.

All the students complaining about the CAs/graders are being SUPER petty, especially in a course where the grading is straightforward and generous (put in the work and you will get a decent grade!). This class i thought provoking and fun.  Prof Dom is accesible and wants you to succeed.  Take this if you want flexibility and a caring Prof.
Just don't understand why some of the TAs grade so hard.
This course is really good
You grades depend on TAs, and some of them are unreasonably strict.

Literally the easiest class I've taken so far. If you're looking for an easy A, then this is the perfect class for you. Aside from that, this class was actually so interesting and fun! Despite going through the U.S education system myself, I still learned so much that really put a lot of things into perspective. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: TA's did all the grading. It was an online course, which I do not love, but Prof. Brewer did his best. The readings were interesting, but lectures I just put on my computer while I did other works. Essays all based off readings, so lectures were not really helpful.

The professor was AMAZING! However, it is possible to get a B or lower because some of the TAs are very strict in their grading, which is quite unreasonable. Here's a kind message: ask someone who has taken this class about the course assistance the professor has assigned to you.

Nice professor! Online lecture of 400 ppl. Daily reading assignments that are not strictly checked. A discussion and an online quiz every month. You can take the quiz up to 10 times for a perfect grade. The only graded assignments are 3 papers graded by the CAs. As long as you put enough effort into them, you are good to get an A in this class!

Brewer is the best! Really interesting course, and is open to feedback. Tons of accommodation, the syllabus literally is so detailed and tells you everything. Class is about historical and contemporary issues of the U.S. Education system. 3 papers in this class, at least during Fall 2024. He provides the textbook in brightspace! 100% easy and fun!!
Super nice guy and made class interesting even if it was online.

honestly as close to an easy A as you can get, as long as you upload your discussion forum posts and dedicate some time to ask your TA's for advice on your papers. classes are online, attendance isn't mandatory, and you get 10 tries on quizzes to get a perfect score. 10/10 would recommend if you put in a little bit of effort.

This class is super fun and the course material is very interesting. Dom is super knowledgeable on the subject matter and his TAs are equally as great. He brings in the best guest lecturers as well. As long as you put a fair amount of time and effort into the essays, you will get an A

This class is super fun and interesting as Dom brings in the best guest lecturers, and he is also one of the best lecturers I have had. As long as you put the time and effort into the papers, the class is an easy A

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR. Half the classes are asynchronous, synchronous ones take one participation question for attendance. A couple papers with super clear instructions, and a few easy open-note quizzes. Really interesting material too. Take this class especially in a harder semester.
Prof. Brewer is awesome and this class is amazing! His TAs are also very helpful and he's very accessible outside of class. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dom is the best!! If you need an easy and want to take a very interesting course on the history of American Education, I HIGHLY recommend this course. Dom wants you to succeed, there are infinite retakes on open note quizzes, 3 essays and some homework readings. You will get out of this course what you want to receive. I can't recommend it enough.
A lot of readings but the material and assignments are really manageable. The TA's are very helpful too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Brewer is a super sweet man. His lectures are pretty interesting in my opinion and he's a super easy grader! He really wants his students to succeed. The only part that I struggled in a little was with the readings. There's a lot of them and I wouldn't consider myself  the strongest reader. Anyway, 10/10 would recommend though!

Kind professor. All lecture based some asynch. Kind of boring sometimes but class set up & respect for students makes up for it. 3 papers, quizzes, & discussion posts. Late papers no penalty, ask for reopen quizzes or discussion posts. Quizzes can be taken several times & the highest grade gets put in. Very cool person & CAs are equally as kind.
Really informative class. He's a great lecturer and I learned A LOT!

Why does college cost so much course. Very easy A. Two papers which you must just put effort into. Several quizzes which you can do as many times as you want - only highest take counts. Several simple forum posts.
Professor Dom is an excellent professor! whole grade is based on three papers, a few quizzes that can be retaken, and discussion forums. Would definitely take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Brewer made this class really engaging despite being completely online. Lots of readings, but not too long. Classes were split between lectures, small groups, and asynchronous work. There are quizzes throughout the semester (10 tries per quiz), 3 essays (4-5 pgs each), and discussion forums. Overall, definitely recommend for an easy A!

Prof Brewer has 5 TA's who do all the grading, usually 4 essays and 5 quizzes (but it's an easy A). Essays are usually based on reading, which can be skimmed but on personal opinion and the grading isn't strict. Extensions were given on everything but use your time wisely. Take this class if you need credit and an easy A (with some effort)!

This is the class that made me realize I want to minor in education, thanks to Prof. Brewer. He is very passionate and inspirational, and clearly always knows what he's doing. Over Brightspace, it was an easy A because 40% of the grade was quizzes that you can take 10 times (easy 100%) and 60% was papers that you can't really go wrong with.

Really have a taste and opinion. Sensitive when you are using your device in class. I really don't understand how everyone is getting an A. She's nice, but you really have to be her favorite student, or she won't give you a good grade. Yes, I didn't get a boom on mine. I received an A on each of my quizzes but ended up having an A-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: There was a decent amount of reading, but Professor Brosh made it pretty easy to understand. Pop quizzes, but she always hinted to them the class before. Really cares about being on time and participation, if you do both she will love you.

She is an amazing and kind professor. Make sure to do all of the reading and come prepared for class and you will be on her good side. Also, pop quizzes are quite frequent-- so yes, reading the material really matters! If you are a good participant, that will really help too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Brosh's class. I think she makes very interesting claims about different literature. No midterm; instead 6 pop quizzes and the lowest one gets dropped. Should be easy to get an A or A- on quizzes if you read. If you write about an opinion she disagrees with, it'll be reflected in your grade. I asked for a slight bump and she got me an A.

THE WORST EVER DO NOT TAKE!!! She caught someone internet browsing on their laptop and literally snatched it out of their hands and held it for the rest of class. Two months into the semester she called me the wrong name like twice when I participated everyday. Was always late to class. Gave the worst pop quizzes. Easy A, but at what cost...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not the best but not the worst. If you miss more than 4 classes your participation grade goes down a whole letter. About 2 pop quizzes per book, one essay, midterm, one art project, and hard final but if your study for a long time you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Brosh was a pretty easy professor if you do the readings and participate in class. Get on her good side because she does pick favorites! She's very picky about her students having the exact translations of every text, and she gives reading quizzes almost every week. She's also very old school and rude sometimes, but occasionally funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading and there can be pop quizzes. But if you did read and participate, you will find this class easy. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Brosh is an interesting professor. Class is super boring but if you do the reading and the work on time and speak here and there she will like you and give you a good grade. it's not a hard class if you put in some work and get on her good side.

This is among one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Despite the fact that this is an ENTRY LEVEL class, it's treated like a weed out course. She constantly breaks university code, and she has a new excuse for why something is the student's fault and not her own every week. It's a curse that she hasn't been fired yet.

Honestly I thought she was so funny and kept engaged—cause if I was typing on my computer she'd call me out lol. She's an easy grader and lowkey hints at pop quizzes but like you have to read a little to bs your way out of that. Final took a lot of studying but overall an easy A if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's... something. As a person, she's not very nice. As a grader, it's mixed. I don't know how hard the professors here can be in terms of grading, but if you're okay with getting your feelings hurt or jabbed at, take it. If you're like me and you're sensitive and start crying in the shower because of what people say a week ago, don't.

Her assignments weren't hard but she was so unclear with what she expected out of us. not really understanding and nit picks everything. not interactive with students and you can tell when does not fw you. smh. would never take again. pop quizzes out of no where too so beware!

definitely have to read thoroughly for class due to pop quizzes, the final, and discussions. grading is based on what she wants to hear/read..it is known she rarely gives A's. she is slightly biased in that you can tell who her favorites are right from the start.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Pop quizzes around 5 times during the semester, where she expects you to memorize everything. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is a very unreasonable grader. There is no logic in how she grades her assignments and she is very inconsistent. the worst ever

"I don't care about your grade"

reviews.comment: tough grader

The worst professor I've ever had. She's super mean and loves giving ppl Fs on pop quizzes. Its all abt her bias. I didn't learn anything from this class.
Just RUN

Brosh is one of the best professors I've had. She is very clear about how she grades and what she's looking for in assignments. She gives so much leeway with assignments and is such an easy grader. Her final exam is challenging, however it is so easy to get an A in her class if you put in the work. She is accommodating and very sweet to talk with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Brosh is passionate about the subjects she teaches, but it is critical that students participate in class and do the readings. reviews.comment: Professor Brosh analyzes texts in depth and gives everyone a chance to participate. The readings excessive and you're expected to remember all the details. A lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of the funniest and coolest professors I've ever had.

Brosh is such a good professor, especially for this class. She helps you understand the texts you read and helps you with any questions you may have on your assignments. This class has 2 papers, a final and a presentation but she's an easy grader if you put in the work. I really recommend her and this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Brosh is so passionate about what she teaches. She is very thoughtful and much sweeter than she initially seems. Final was tricky, but if you study thoroughly you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Brosh can seem a little intimidating at first, but she's truly a great professor. She's smart and passionate about the material. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She can seem cold/intimidating at first. Still, she is always fair and only wants her students to engage and perform their best. If you pay attention to her instructions, do the readings (very light, few chapters or less each lecture) and share thoughts at least once each lecture you will do well :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took her both semesters, and honestly as long as do the readings (not too long, interesting books) and participate in class (literally just say any analysis): youre golden. She is very nice and gives a lot of warnings in regards to pop quizzes, and the assignments are straightforward. Just read and offer "interesting" text opinions and youre good

I was pretty anxious about her classes at first so I put lots of works and time into this class. It turned out my efforts were paid back! She is so caring! The art history part is difficult but she did a great job of explaining it!

She is very caring and very inspirational in class. She makes you want to know arts more. People here give her bad ratings because she is not that kind of professor who gives an easy A to everyone. You need to read the readings for discussion. This is one of my favorite classes throughout the whole year (yes I took her for a year).

Bottom line is if you read and participate you are golden. She is very fair when it comes to grading and loves talking about the literature and art she teaches. She also gives out study guides for the readings and most likely than not one of those questions is going to be your quiz question on that text. She is intimidating at first.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Brosh was very rude in class and created an uncomfortable environment. She did offer extra credit, though, and was understandable about some things. However, I don't think her attitude in class was worth it. Plus, the readings were hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shes awful, I got a 55/100 on the art history part of her final. The assignments are mostly repetitive, which dropped the motivations for me most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's very enthusiastic about the course and cares for students. But gets more strict since online classes. Lots of quizzes instead of a midterm. A final paper and final exam on everything, but graded easily. LOTs of reading, though it was quite fun. So take her if you want to learn authentically.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is very into literature, but not so interested in teaching about art, which is a disaster for me. Although she will always inform us before she gives out quizzes, they are not very easy because she gives out tons of readings for every class. Still, she seems like an easy grader, because I think I screwed lots of pop quizzes but still gets an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Caring, do not take her class because: 1) weekly quizzes, class discussions, at least two reaction papers, an art presentation, one 1500 words min final paper, a hard final exam (two versions of unfair, unequal difficulty) while your peers have only weekly response paper and discussion 2) grading is harsh 3) disorganized professor who goes offtrack
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Brosh can seem a bit discombobulated, but she knows what she's doing. Though she can be a bit of a savage, she's really just playing devil's advocate to make you really think about the material. Easy if you do the reading and participate. I had her during the corona semester and she really worked to make online classes as good as possible. Caring
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Brosh is a nice enough person as she is but definitely plays by her own rulebook. She does not allow ANY questions outside of what the lecture is on and if you bring in another idea during the lecture, she will glaze over you. There's a lot of reading every class, and lots of pop quizzes. Take her class if you want to learn authentically.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Brosh is my favorite professor ever! I'm sorry, but she's not here to give you an easy A (she makes you work for it, but it is definitely doable). You have to do the readings in order to succeed, which is how it should be. I've learned so much for her and cannot recommend enough. I love her. If you like learning, you will love her.

A professor who brings immense passion and expertise. Classes can become a little dreary, as she bans technology and tends to lecture more. Be prepared to complete the readings, as she often doles out pop quizzes. However, quizzes come instead of a midterm, which is a benefit. Expect to earn a good grade if you do the work and participate actively.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who is very kind, subject matter can be kind of dull sometimes but her class discussions liven things up and can be interesting. She's been nothing but the best to me and I can tell that my participation made a difference in my learning of the subject matter and on my grade. Very kind professor who genuinely cares about her students
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: You actually have to READ and ANNOTATE and review your annotations. Expect quizzes often, quizzes are obscure/ from random parts of the text, be as detailed as possible in any work you submit. If you participate in class (every class) and go to office hours (one on one) you may be okay. Show up to class because you cant make up anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: if it wasnt daily, it was weekly quizzes. need to read in order to pass. discussions are very analytical on her part but too boring. cnt use technology; must take notes by hand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I feel she's the pro you'll love or hate and I absolutely love her! she's intellectual, articulate, and sweet. she's thoughtful and values ideas so take her if you have any lol! I would admit she appeared intimidating in the beginning but once we got to know each other she's ever so kind and sweet!

Looking back, this class was a solid choice. There's a lot of readings and you have to make and effort to keep up with them otherwise Finals season is going to hit you way harder than it should. The pop quizzes are "OK", if you read you won't have a problem. She's a nice person, make sure she knows your name (participation is important). Good luck!

I LOVE Professor Brosh. Great teacher with a vast knowledge of the required texts. She has a genuine interest in the course material and expects you to share that same interest. While reading is often pretty heavy, every text is interesting. She is a very caring person that will help you along the way. 10/10. Already planning to take her again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a caring, sweet person. Very easy grader. Says she gives "pop quizzes", but will tell you when shes gonna give them and they're not difficult, just one written response question. And the quizzes are your midterm grade, so no midterm :) Classes are mostly discussion based, but heads up, they are so so boring. Overall, is a pretty okay teacher

Solid professor, tends to lecture a lot before allowing students to participate. Clearly states criteria for assignments and grading. Quite lenient when grading, you can get a high grade by reiterating points she made herself in class. For someone who is otherwise disinterested in the course material, she's a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: prof brosh is rly chill. grades REALLY leniently. assigns easy reading w homework, but v easy/ cushions your grade. never received anything lower than an A- in her class, bc most things are context. chose interesting but old books, lectures get pretty boring but she's just doing her job going through course material. Would take her again fo sho.

Very nice person, but with very minimal knowledge of the material she teaches. She will act as though you've made an incredibly insightful point as long as it's something she agrees with. Gives pop quizzes but they're in substitution for a midterm. Very easy A, but if you're passionate about literature and/or art, I'd go with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gave a poor review and came back to give her 5stars cause she's dat good! Did so much work and really worked hard. But it pays off. She gave the best fee back of all time and makes you want to work even more harder! 10/10 love! Will give extra credit work to help you upgrade the letter. TAKE HER! So many student got a letter up bc they tried
my fav bbb professor Broshie luv her guys
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lecture is like poetry. Carefully planned, skilfully executed, from the heart. I miss this lovely lady. Students: Don't expect an easy A just because you paid the fees. Put some effort !!

Very adamant on having things being seen from her point of view. Makes inappropriate comments on others in class (comments on frat life, drinking habits, etc.) Disorganized at times. Seems genuinely passionate though- I admire that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I like her in the beginning, but as time goes on she still doesn't know my name as I am one of the most active one in class. My name is foreign, I will take it even if she pronounces it wrong but she's not even trying! It is for sure not a problem if she doesn't know like the others too. But it is a SMALL CLASS and she remembers all the others.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Brosh is one of those professors that you will love or hate. Personally, I loved her but that is not without putting in way too much effort. On the midterm she gives out there was one 100 and the next highest grade was a 90 obtained by at most three people. Her midterm and final identification sections are extremely hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very nice professor, her lectures were very clear and interesting. Exams can be hard, especially the passages can be confusing; however, if you actually take notes and read the required texts you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A wonderful professor! Dr. Brosh is strict about grading, attendance, and homework, but very reasonable. I have learned literally so much in her class and took her for both CFI and CFII.  She picks great works and engages her students. She also offers ample extra credit and it is not hard to get an A if you put in the wokr
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: My favorite professor in liberal studies! I took both CF1 and 2 with her, and I absolutely love her. She is strict about her assignment policy and attendance policy, yet she is super nice and a generous grader as long as you finish all the works she gave out. She doesn't expect perfect answer, but if you argue reasonable she gives you fair grade.
absolutely terrible, do yourself a huge favor by not taking this class. Expects perfect answers on things she doesnt even teach in class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Do your readings, DON'T MISS  CLASSES (automatic F for any missed quizzes, no makeup), hand in all study questions, always be ready for pop quizzes, participate actively in class. Makes it extremely clear what she wants & makes u work for ur grade. Really nice person but very stern about class ethics. Tests are pretty difficult but easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Great person and great teacher hands down!! Nearly every class there is a reading assignment, possible quiz, and then a discussion of information. She makes it clear what she expects. Just know that the course gets easier towards the end of the semester and she becomes more lenient. Read and show up. You'll do just fine. :-) Liora is awesome!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Do the readings, show up, do the study questions, participate, and you'll get an easy A. This class is literally high school, as she includes pop quizzes and homework roughly equivalent to midterms and finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Brosh is a nice person. She gave me an A-, but I had to work for it. HARD. She relies heavily on class participation to carry discussions, and will call randomly on you. A nice person and gives you second chances on papers if you show that you care. But honestly, I dreaded her class. Even looking back on it, I still wouldn't take again. Mixed...

I love Dr. Brosh, i took her twice. She gives a lot of reading but if you actively read and participate in class, you will get an A. 50% of the class is pop quizzes on the HW so read, take notes on what you're reading so you can bring it up in class. The final is HARD but if you actually read you should be kind of ok.. i got a 90 on it somehow.
Straightforward, informative, never dull. She is not a hard grader but she still expects for you to read and do your work well. Take her if you want to learn new things AND get a decent grade.

This Professor is honestly one of the most straight-forward professors I encountered within my freshman year. Even though she seems to be a bit intimidating in the beginning and gives of the impression that she isn't very approachable, if you read everything you're supposed to and participate in class, you will be perfectly fine.

Extremely disorganized (she was ALWAYS late to our class). She is also not open to other interpretations of the text- she is adamant in having the text seen in her point of view only. An easy A though if you do the reading. During the days she was actually early for class, there would be pop quizzes.

Extremely kind, understanding, and compassionate. As long as you participate and do the reading (emphasis on doing the fking reading), then you will 99% get an A. It's that simple. Do what you are supposed to do and you will be rewarded. However, if you don't, then gluck!

You will learn a lot if you take Professor Brosh!! Professional, informative, and enthusiastic, Professor Brosh will motivate you to work hard and get as much out of the class as possible. There is a lot of reading, but that's just the nature of the course. Also know that she offers plenty of extra credit, and is a fair grader. I'd take her again.

Very good, structured class. A lot of reading but we always discuss the reading in class. Pop quiz on reading most classes. She likes people who participate. If you don't do the reading you will fail, if you do, you'll get an A

Professor Brosh is a passionate, helpful, and instructive professor. She comes to every class very prepared, and is always willing to be a great instructor. She is also a very kind lady, and she creates an entertaining class environment. I could not say anything bad about her or her class. You will love her!!!!!

Although the class would sometimes be put to sleep during her lectures, she also gives the class time to participate. She does get flustered easily when it comes to technology, but she is a nice person. She likes those who participate. There is a lot of reading, and she expects you to do all of it.
