Sometimes she gives quizzes based on the readings.

Professor Brosh is very intense but also a very sweet lady. She's stressed a lot, but she is always willing to help. She tends to get flustered, but seriously she is so passionate about teaching and about the material it's amazing and she is willing to work with you. Don't even think about using your phone or cheating. She will catch you.

She is THE BEST professor at NYU I've ever had the pleasure of meeting. She is always smiling and is ready to help! Show you're interested in the class and she will love you. Do the reading, participate in class and you will get an A. Do the reading it's sooo interesting and engage in discussion, you will learn so much!  Take her!

She chose good texts. At first, listen to the discussions and learn the type of analysis she likes. Then analyze the subsequent works in that manner.  Not a hard grader, if you follow directions. Lecture is based on class participation so be sure to get your word in there. As a person, she is kind and patient. I would take her for CFIII if I could.

Prof. Brosh is the sweetest woman. She is very helpful and she understands that you have other classes. Mora than once she extended our due dates, which was great. I recommend getting yourself a buddy to keep you updated if you miss class. Other than that, she is great. She taught me how to analyze tets on a deeper level. I recommend her highly.

Best teacher I've had so far in NYU. She inspired me to take interest in something I was previously not and made my experience with the subject all the better. She is a very FAIR grader, holds interesting discussions in class, and is a very nice lady. She may assign homeworks after every class but they are really helpful for the final.

One of the best teachers I've had so far.  She really wants the students to do well in the class and is very helpful with essays.  Her assignments are not that demanding.  You just have to do the reading and the questions.

Prof. Brosh showed a considerable lack of consideration for the students. She was late 90% of the time and has very little interpersonal skills. Unless if you want to be pointed at and called "you" when you raise your hand because your prof. can't learn 20 names don't take her.

Brosh is very interested in and knowledgeable about her subject, but she is often a little too excited. She is late to class more often than not and doesn't know how to use a computer well. She doesn't stick to the syllabus either. She's rather scatterbrained, but her class is easy. If you have her, MAKE FRIENDS(!) in case you miss class.

Incredibly condescending. His essay prompts are a little unclear and it takes a minute to understand. But, the things that make my rating a 1/5 are his consistent general digs at college students' work, his cursing far past the amount that is considered humorous from a professor, and his hostile, personally disrespectful feedback.
He is cute like a rabbit, he is understanding, tho sometimes he may not be offering you enough feedback as he is busy with his children.

bro is SOOOOOOOOO passionate abt writing. like idek. I had some brain cells revived ong. but his rubric is very thought out and clear and all you have to do is just put one ounce of effort in. he's funny. if you take him in the fall or spring you'll enjoy his class a lot if you take it after lunch or something. very entertaining.
His lectures are a lot of fun. He's a humorous and engaging professor who respects students and shows empathy toward international students who come from diverse backgrounds.

Awesome writing professor! Doesn't give much daily homework. I love his daily reading assignments that interest int'l students a lot. Like other expos professors, he uses the labor-based grading system, meaning that you need to do a challenge option each progression to receive a final A in the course. Only two progressions (essays).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor, he uses labor-based grading (doesn't grade each essay individually) so as long as you complete all the work with effort you will receive an A. Don't be late because that will impact your grade. He allows 4 absences without impacting your grade but do go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He clearly cares of international students as he provides many materials based on students's nationality, which gives you clear sense how to write a paper based on materials he provides. No strict grading policy on paper and you can get A just by making some videos and extra work. So you dont have to dying for writing a perfect paper for A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's pretty chill, the class felt pretty rushed just because it was a summer course, but he managed to make three hours go on pretty seamlessly. It did feel repetitive to keep reading sample essays during class, but his feedback helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Butler is a decent grader, but his classes weren't very engaging. He tries to fit in with the rest of the class, but it just makes him more like a boomer. He slams his hands on the board, and would sometimes talk very loud. For ACE there was a total of 2 progressions, and you could revise the first one. Overall not an ez A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
He is the best ACE Prof!
- Teaching style -> lectures + discussions -> material is engaging
- Homework -> MINIMAL (1 writing tasks per week + 1 reading) 
- Lenient with deadlines
- 2 essays in total and a few small graded activities 
- Conferences were helpful --> Prof would make direct edits --> gives good feedback (PLS show him a full draft tho)
Tough grader

Butler is an engaging lecturer and fairly easy grader. Really understanding person too. He would come off as a bit pretentious sometimes (he reaaallly loves classic literature) which made him seem a little inaccessible. If you participate and do all the assignments, you'll be good. Overall I enjoyed the class.
Decently easy grader and helpful in individual feedback sessions, but his classes aren't that engaging. He bangs his hands against the board to make a point which is eh. Also has boomer energy.

My favorite writing prof at NYU so far. Very understanding of personal circumstances but remember to clearly communicate your concerns. Will not be on your case if rough drafts are not fully completed in time, but a good grade requires effort. If feedback is unclear, ASK HIM! Really likes talking during class but content is interesting. Minimal hw

Favorite Writing Professor at NYU. He is so warm and helpful, held individual meetings with you to discuss your papers, and I think he grade fairly while carefully at the same time. Really MINIMAL homework. Recommend!

He is by far the best professor I've had at NYU. Very clear about the criteria and explain things explicitly in class. Individual meetings are extremely helpful and detailed, some of my classmates say he is better than the writing center. Also super understanding and caring, respects the different time zones students could be in.

As an international student, I do believe Prof Butler cares about his students. I learned meaningful writing skills from him, true. And his class is pretty fun. Indeed, receiving an A requires quite a lot of effort. However, LISTEN to his feedbacks in the video conference because they are helpful! Overall, he will be a good choice for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is such a mean person. The most unfortunate thing in this semester is taking his class. He never replies to email nor give helpful feedbacks. Once I was sick and had 5000 words papers. I politely asked for his extension. He didn't reply until four hours later I finished. I said: please ignore this. He immediately replied: ignored. Really hurt.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Butler is the most interesting professor I had in the writing courses. He is really supportive of creative ideas and he tends to give a lot of choices for students to write about, so I ended up enjoying the writing process. Still, get a good grade requires a lot of effort, and he is pretty loud. Btw: I'd suggest stir away from political questions.

I wouldn't say he's a bad professor and I understand that some profs think B's a really good score, but he just grades too toughly (comparing to everyone else's sessions) that it really affects my GPA (which s kinda important). Caring and inspirational. Generally good. But sometimes he wouldn't answer afterclass questions as "it s unfair to others"

Nobody really wants to take expository writing, but Professor Butler is a really great choice. He cares and really tries to make the class interesting and insightful. I can honestly say I am a much better writer after taking this course. One thing to note is that he is quite a difficult grader and was not specific in his feedback.

Amazing professor who really cares about his students. He gives great feedback and is always willing to help. I advise reaching out to him outside of class either through email or after class. Very tough class in general but you definitely learn a lot and become a much better writer. Don't expect to get an A, maybe an A- if you really work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: No one in this class likes this professor. He talks just to hear himself talk and won't listen to any perspectives other than his own. Of course ACE and Writing the Essay aren't the best classes to begin with but he makes ACE HELL.

Butler is fantastic! This class is tough no matter what but he really will make you a better writer by the end of it. He's always willing to help students and classes are engaging. Put a little effort into your papers and he'll like you.
Helpful, tough grader, not clear

Expository writing courses are no joke at NYU. Professor Butler makes sure that students understand the importance of these courses. He may seem intimidating at first, but he's one of the nicest professors I've had. As long as you do all your homework and show that you're putting genuine effort, you should be fine. He is somewhat of a tough grader.
Great professor! Very helpful and makes class entertaining. Not easy workload or grading-wise, but definitely one of the best WTE professors and made me a much better writer.

Great professor, really helped me improve my writing. Readings were not too bad if you actually bothered to read. In-class discussions were heavily dependent on readings and very helpful. Grading contract makes it quite easy to get an A as long as you put some effort. Attendance policies are quite strict, and affects your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Bujnowski's Writing as Inquiry class. She was very encouraging and never judged a student's writing. Rather, she gave helpful feedback to help you improve. Grading criteria is fair, if you do all your work you get a B, and if you want an A you need to complete 3 bonus options, which were interesting and fairly simple to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I enjoyed her class, and it significantly improved my writing skills. The professor provided very detailed and meaningful comments on the essay, but it took several weeks to receive the feedback. I would recommend taking her lecture if you want to improve your writing, but don't want to get stressed by the endless assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bujnowski changed my entire relationship to writing. I started the class feeling totally unprepared and scared, but she was so encouraging and took time to check in with me. The classes/homework break down the process for each essay and her feedback and conferences really helped….she's constructive without being harsh. So glad I got her!

The course felt extremely smooth and interesting. I liked the way professor Ali encourages students and she's very caring.The class has a friendly environment and would not bore anyone. I look forward to this class every week. Though there might be work to do in the class, not all will be extremely tiring, instead, it is fairly enjoyable.

BEST. PROFESSOR. EVER! Ali totally transforms how you think about writing. I didn't expect to enjoy this class as much as I did. She breaks down the writing process and makes it feel manageable. Sometimes challenging, but in a way that makes you grow as a writer and thinker. 10/10 recommend. TAKE HER IF YOU CAN. 🌟
a lot of readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor B is absolutely the best professor you could ask for. She does give a lot of homework but they are very helpful. She is very accessible through email and office hours, or even just after class. She genuinely cares about us and brings us snacks occasionally.
lots of home work, grading criteria is not clear and her opinions towards your paper changes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. B is amazing and so nice! She really created a supportive and engaging class experience. The homework exercises and lessons prepare you to write the essays and overall I've grown so much as a writer. Sign up for conferences and to talk to her! She's super accessible and will offer ideas and suggestions to help you with your essays.
heavy homework and really confusing and strict, you will spend almost 10 hours each week on her course
I spend my whole weekend working on her homework
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ali is so nice and will work with you to make sure you are keeping up and was so easy to meet with outside of class. Her feedback was insightful and, overall, gave a huge boost to my writing. There was a lot of required reading, but the majority was quite interesting. Take her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Ali's seriously the best. She's a tough but fair grader and really pushes you to do your best. It's obvious how much she cares about her students and wants them to grow and succeed. She's the kind of professor I came to NYU for. Also, go to the writing center, getting the right tutor can make a world of a difference in this class.

I found Professor Ali to be a lenient grader, as she is caring and understanding about deadlines. She encourages  participation.  It was the best writing class I've ever taken. Her clear accent makes her easy to understand, and she is the professor I admire the most.

Definitely one of the nicest professors you can meet at NYU. She is so kind and caring:) She made my first semester of college much easier and more comfortable. Regardless, you have homework almost every day, but that homework ultimately helps you to guide your final paper per each progression.

Take her! She may appear crazy in the beginning, but trust me she may be the kindest person you've ever meet. A lot of weekly homework that may need a few hours. Her feedback is always shaky and she mentions stuff when she submits your grade that you've never heard before. She's giving older sister vibes and always asks us how our weekends were.

Professor Bujnowski was one of my first teachers at NYU, and she really made my transition into college very pleasant. She cares deeply about each of her students' success, and it shows. Even though my class was at 8am and everyone was tired, she managed to peak my interest in the topics of discussion. Thank you so much Professor!!
Super caring teacher!

You can really tell that Ali cares about her students. She's not exactly an easy grader, but you can definitely manage an A- as long as you ask her for feedback on your essays. She gives good advice on your writing and it helps a lot to have specific questions in mind before conferences. Didn't do them, but she also offers revisions at the end.

Ali is a really caring professor who just wants to see you improve as a writer. Reading the long homework assignments will help in the long run, and the more you participate the better because then she will be more helpful to you on your drafts. If you do your work, and put in a bit of effort Ali will make this class very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Bujnowski might be the best professor I have ever had. I wasn't too excited about taking a writing class and it ended up being my favorite course. She is caring, comprehensive, and incredibly dedicated. I learned more than I ever thought I would. She inspires you to work hard for your essays and grades fairly. Take her class if you can!

Ali is one of the most amazing teachers I've ever had. Puts in the time to make sure the class is up to speed. It is clear she cares about her students. Offers amazing insight into how you can strengthen your essays. Completely successful at transforming your writing and taking your essays to the next level. Allows revisions on certain essays.

Ali is the best! She knows WTE is a challenge but shes super approachable and will help you a ton. She gives lots of targeted feedback on drafts so you know exactly how to improve and I really did become a better writer because of her. The readings and assignments were relatable and interesting, and yeah, theres hw but its manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Ali loves getting her students involved in classes and is constantly making writing topics relevant to us. However, her commentary is extremely confusing and contradictory. Every essay I wrote she would wait and decide she didn't like my argument during my final draft and my grade would suffer. If you want an easy A do not take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ali is the best that WTE has to offer. With her class, you get what you give. She does her part to make class interested (Wes Anderson days are the BEST), and she expects you to do your part (i.e. reading the assigned essays, fully investing yourself in drafting, participating in class). She is brilliant, genuinely cares, and is gorgeous. Love her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Ali is great. She really is the best you can get. However, don't go there expecting an awesome grade if you are not the best writer out there. While she does value effort and commitment, it is very hard to go above the B if you are a 'normal' writer. Homework is heavy but it does help build your essay in steps which helps. Also, she is BEAUTIFUL

Ali was the best writing the essay professor I could ever ask for. Classes and guidelines were very structured which WTE easier to understand. Though her grading is tough, she's so willing to help and gives opportunities to revise that if you put in the effort you can bring your grade up to as high as you try. An incredible and caring professor.

I'm absolutely in love with her. Ali is not only a great professor, but also a genuine person. I learned something from every class and she was very clear on what needed to be improved. I took her class for both WTE and ACE and I do not regret waking up early to take her 9:30 AM class. If you want to learn how to write, she should be your go-to.

Amazing WTE Professor, but grades are a struggle. Coming from a mediocre writer, she made me understand exactly where I was lacking, and expected me to adapt to her expectations. Tonnnnnes of homework, but that's WTE for you. Take her! Very lucid, and no WTE is really an easy A.
Despite the fact that WTE is a huge pain, Ali made it pretty fun. She's very chill and definitely knows her stuff. If I could take a class with her again, I would.

Ali Bujnowski is kind, intelligent, respectful, and fair.  I started off hating her just because of the sheer work involved in Writing the Essay.  However, now that I understand that this workload is common amongst all professors in this class, I have grown to see the value of her assignments.  I would take a class taught by her again.

Ali is a great teacher! I didn't think I would like WTE at the beginning, but she's made it one of my favorite classes this year & I always look forward to it. She's approachable but professional, intelligent, and really engages us with the material. Would definitely recommend her.

Ali was very helpful, and genuinely tried to make us all better writers. This being said, the fact that we had "Writing the Essay" made everything a real pain, but I doubt that it could have been better without Ali. If I ever have to take another writing course, I'll definitely try my best to get Ali again

She is passionate about the subject and likes to have discussions with the class. She is respectful, kind, helpful, and reasonable. However she tries to hold your hand every step of the way which is suffocating, and the amount of work (2 papers a week) got tiring(all writing 101 classes are like this though). Overall I'm happy I got her.

Amazing professor; Writing the Essay is by nature an extremely annoying, tedious,  and somewhat pointless class, but she makes it enjoyable. The actual classes with her are really fun and engaging, but the homework and everything is still as abundant and time-consuming as any other WTE class's is.

Ali is hands down one of the best writing instructors in her department. (I've been to the writing center many times) Her class is well-organized and she engages her students in exciting conceptual discussions. If you have any problems, schedule office hours and conferences with her; they are extremely helpful. All in all, she made WTE enjoyable!

I don't consider myself a writer, and I really dreaded WTE coming into it. The class was certainly a lot of work, but Ali is awesome. Her teaching is really engaging and fun. Schedule a conference with her for each essay because she is so helpful and provides a lot of insight. Her grading is fair and she rewards hard work. Definitely recommend her!
I have her as a writing the essay professor and I really like her teaching. I just wish I actually enjoyed writing. Even still, she is very reasonable and helpful. I would highly recommend her.

Ali is an amazing professor.  Her classes are interesting, she brings in photographs, art, and movies to help get you to understand the writing process.  She is clear in her feedback on exercises and essays.  The more you participate and put in effort, the better grade you'll get (as long as your work is good) Ali is a fair grader and great overall
yes,it's true that policy changed since fall2025
he doesn't know what he is teaching & the grading is super bad and no room for discussion on hws and quizzes grade. make us desperate
Just to let you know that I got C+ and three of my friends got C+ too. Don't say he is easy grader. I am pretty sure I work a lot and do everything he told on class. More than 50 percent got below B.
very harsh grader for fall 2025. don't take his. overall a range less than 15 percent. Fierce competition. I withdrew.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Minimal workload, open book tests. Final project worth 50% of the grade. Nobody got below an A- in it. Pretty sure 100% of the class had A- and up. Easy grader. Gives you an opportunity to build something cool for the final project and gives great suggestions in office hours. Go for the prof, maybe not for the content as it is a bit scattered.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Loved the class! You'll learn a lot, from bioinformatics to graph theory and cryptography. Professor really cares about students' learning!
The biggest joke of a class in the CS department. Take this iff you want to put minimal effort into getting an A.
Informative but 0 structure. Doesnt seem to care if you learn anything.
barely learn anything, quizzes not related to lectures, most of grade is on hw and final project
you will learn nothing from this course. easy A but not worth it

After the midterm grade for the course was released, he wasted an entire lecture going over every single piece of negative feedback he received on the midterm course evaluations one by one, trying to convince us that they were incorrect. His classes are aimless, and homework is not related to what is discussed at all.

Worst professor ever. Told us quizzes only counted for less than 10% of the grade, made them count for 30% of the grade in the end, and threatened to lower my grade when I pointed this out. Quizzes have no bearing on anything (we were asked about Angelina Jolie's risk of breast cancer), website is never updated. Seems friendly, do not fall for it.

Very nice guy but horrible as a professor. No structure to class whatsoever, no way to check your grades. Quizzes have NOTHING to do with anything, will instead test pop culture knowledge. Never updates website. Expects you to have an idea for final project on Day 1. Really weird guy overall. Probably an easy A, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Bud is a nice man but you learn nothing and there is no transparency with how you are graded. You are not given like a guidebook to what your grades look like online. He doesn't use NYU Classes nor does he have any online way to let you know how your grade is looking. Very confusing and no structure don't recommend.
Great class!
Don't think I learned anything in this class

biggest joke of a class. no tests, no exams, hardly any hw, quizzes are riddles, probably the easiest class to get an A in with minimal effort. feel ripped off taking this class, did not learn anything either. put in more effort into 1 algo hw assignment than in the entirety of this class. avoid if you want to learn. take if you want easy A.
the way he puts words together makes things hard to be understood
I wish I could take more courses taught by him!
Awesome professor!
First day in and he already seems snobby and rude. Heavily considering dropping this class

his lecutres r skippable. hes a smart guy and is sometimes interesting but the lectures are extremely boring and useless. paper criteria is weird. midterm and final r rly difficult but its nicely curved. this class made me switch out of the poli sci major

4 two-page papers are 50% of your grade. Extremely forgiving curve on the midterm -- almost unfair to people who scored well. Exams are very similar to practice exams. Go to recitation; game theory learned there is not taught in lecture. Prof is very interesting. If you have something meaningful to contribute to class he won't belittle you.

very intelligent and accomplished man, though arguably not the BEST professor: is pretty harsh to students that try to participate in lecture which i'm sure is good for overall development of politics students but some of it seems unnecessary, and didn't do too well with pacing units and lecture slides were rough to look at. but overall recommend!

Encourages students to answer questions and belittles them when they respond incorrectly, despite having several degrees and decades more experience. 

Your TAs don't grade your material! It's all random, so don't stress whoever you end up taking for recitation. They're also quite flexible about just attending other sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Encourages people to ask questions then belittles them when they don't agree with his views. Has very strong ideas of international politics and is not open to students who question him about some biased facts he says during lectures. You don't have to do the readings, everything on the midterm is based on the midterm review and the past midterms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awesome professor would take him again!

Fascinating guy who pioneered the IR field. Goes on tangents a lot, and the pacing was too slow in the beginning and possibly too fast near the end. Attending recitation is important because it equips you with the necessary quantitative skills to succeed. Would recommend, I have learned a lot about IR from this class.

extremely interesting lectures, except theyre pretty info-heavy and its easy to get lost in the content so make sure you keep up. funny and cool and tries to engage with his students. graded on few things so its not an easy A at all. but its a very valuable course. make sure you actually are interested in int pol though and youll like this

He is a good professor but he doesn't take a lot of time to explain things in a way that makes sense without prior game theory knowledge. I took this course as a freshman, but I would recommend waiting until at least your sophomore year and you'll be fine! (He is a funny dude)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very inspiring professor; his lectures are incredibly captivating. This class was just game theory 101, you'll need to be comfortable with some math. There are 4 short papers graded by the TAs, a midterm, and a final. The exams were almost identical to the practice exams. Readings are not necessary, what you learn in recitation will carry you.

BDM is a icon, he is so smart, funny, and edifying to have as a professor. he made international politics super interesting to learn about. however, TA's can vary so select carefully, some are incredibly difficult and like to flex their statistical/game theoretical knowledge j to confuse us. def look at BDM's youtube videos online before tests!

The material for this class is not easy so you will have to do a lot of independent studying. The review problems that are released before the exams are very similar, if not nearly the same, as the exam that you take so do the review problems
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture and recitation material hardly overlap, and the content is explained poorly. Part of the grade is also based on essays, graded somewhat subjectively by the TAs. Luckily, the midterm and final exams are very similar to what is on the review guides, but you have to teach yourself the game theory/math because it's not discussed in class.

He could do a little better in explaining concepts, but he makes practical applications very clear + the midterm and final were almost exact copies of the study guides he gives you. Very little reading required and the course is designed so just paying attention in lectures and recitations is enough to pass

Bruce is a good professor. Lectures can be a little slow at times, but the material itself was pretty interesting. No homework, just four 2-page papers that are worth 50% total. There are readings, but nothing too crazy. Make sure to attend recitations, since the midterm and final are based on concepts you go over there. All in all, a fair class.

Your experience in this class really depends on the TA you get since they'll be the one grading the 2 page current event papers. Mine was a harsh grader but it got easier once I figured out what they wanted. The readings are quite dense but you can manage without reading everything. The tests don't exactly mirror recitation practice though.

The exams can be difficult and he will actually warn you about it. He curved our two exams but I was quite upset until he informed us about the curve. Doing the readings is necessary as he will test you about the readings, and I will also suggest going to the recitations if you want to do well in this class.

Took his game theory class. Does not go over your assignments carefully. Written comments/feedback were useless, had to go to office hours to figure things out. Rude to students who disagree with his thoughts.

He's an erudite professor who teaches his own compelling theories. Lectures involve basic math; nothing too challenging. He sticks around after class to answer questions, though sometimes his answers are a bit complex. Going to both recitations and lectures is crucial - topics often differ, and both are on exams. No need to spend time on readings.

hands down the most inspiring and also difficult intro politics I've taken. has a fair amount of algebra that you don't normally see in politics classes, that's where most ppl were struggling. That being said it's an interesting class that changed my opinions about politics. readings r hard & unhelpful. recommend read his book dictator's handbook

tbh not as bad as everyone in my class made him out to be. not that much math as it's mostly just plugging in middle school algebra equations that you usually dont have to memorize as long as you understand the basics. TAs pretty much write and grade everything so def go to recitations. his lectures are interesting but hes a bit egotistical.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of math and equations out of nowhere. The final was horrible. TA's did not give an answer key to the practice problems for it. Most of the topics were interesting (P.S lots of content and concepts to learn) but most of the time I didn't understand a thing of what he was saying as well. I fell asleep in all of his lectures.

Do not take this class. The midterm review was nothing like the midterm. The final was worse as my TA only went over 3/7 questions and then all the TAs refused to post the answer key/help as you should've "been in recitation" (when they didn't cover it). As an A student with a 4.0 GPA, I had to make this class p/f. Interesting topic, horrible class

DO NOT take this class. More than an international politics class, this is a calc course. The professor has really interesting ideas and theories, he created most of the material and that's really cool and interesting BUT he comes up with a non sense equation for everything. Neither lecture nor recitation prepare you for the exams (50% of grade)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: More of a lecturer than a professor. Not the most open when you ask questions and often answers as if you should already know it. Cool that most of the stuff we learn was created by him, but there are sometimes shortcomings of his theories that he fails to mention which makes things confusing.

Do not take this class unless you are interested in the game theory behind International Politics. For an intro class we were learning very complex game theory, and the class average for the midterm was curved 20 points to a 60. Most of the exam is from the recitations and 1/3 is from lectures. Take another core class/ try a different professor.

Comes up with a stupid formula/diagram every single class to explain qualitative principles which makes no sense. Horrible class. Like girl, I did not sign up to be a Politics major so I could memorize 10 different stupid formulas that he literally pulled out of his ass, that i'll never have to use in another class ever.
AVERAGE

I do feel the people who take this class need to get luck with their TA because the exams are highly dependent on the content that are covered on recitation. It was not a great experience since that some of the practice problem answers are just the opposite of what in the slides. So it is perplexing.

I did not enjoy his teaching style. He is kind of arrogant in his knowledge/experience in politics and talks down to students. He teaches really abstract concepts that are hard to apply to real life. I understand he is a well-known and respected professional but that doesn't make someone a good teacher. Relied 100% on TA's to get through.

respected poliscientist, expert in his field (wrote textbook); organized lectures with lots of advanced content, but you will do well on exams by understanding the basic logic, which he truly wants you to learn, so he provides huge curves on both midterm and final, but I still suggest studying outside of class. three easy HWs. great politics class.

You really have to get lucky with your TA, as Bruce does not have anything to do with the grading for the class. However, he has had a very interesting career and gave great lectures with cool real world applications he has experienced.

3 problem sets, midterm, and final make up your final grade. Lectures are optional but very educational and entertaining, but most if not all test material comes from the recitations and textbook. The textbook is very clear/interesting (he wrote it himself) and reading it along with knowing game theory should have you covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most inspiring and knowledgeable lecturers and his class would be worth taking for that simple reason. However, he does go off on tangents quite often and it makes it hard at first to figure out what to jot down. His tests expect understanding rather than raw learning. No need to show up to recitation, they're not graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best lecturers that gives you amazing insight into politics and power struggles. The only downside is the grading. It is very tough and one sometimes ambiguous topics briefly described in class or hidden in a random bullet in the powerpoint. The curve should take care of it though, so don't miss out on this class for fear of a bad grade.

Great material, but grading is unfair and unrepresentative of what is covered in lecture. The final is 50% of the grade. It doesn't test major concepts and ideas as much as very abstract concepts that you cannot find a direct answer to anywhere. There was a no-partial credit MC on it worth 10% of that final, or 5% of YOUR ENTIRE GRADE! Absurd!

Gives a bunch of abstract concepts, explains them without clarity, doesn't give you chances to practice applying these abstract concepts and then tests you on them on exams that are weighted super heavily. One question can be worth a bunch of points, for example, circling a multiple choice question wrong can get you up to 10 points off.
Bruce is great to listen to in lecture, but what he says doesn't matter much on the exams. To get an A, you need to go to recitation and learn the math of IR. Easy class overall.

Only take if interested in Politics or IR majors. Teaches IR through math. It is easy to get distracted in class as Bruce does tend to gloss over a lot of things. Recitation is your BFF- if you have a good TA (KJ, Harsh or Pedro). TA matters for your grade, not prof. Go to office hrs. Textbook is useless, got A without opening it, but studied a lot

You cannot graduate NYU without taking a class with Professor Bueno de Mesquita. This guy know's his stuff & presents thoughts and arguments, based strictly on logically induced positive thinking.  The best professor ever!

Great professor!! Most of the class revolves around material he researched with his colleagues. Must attend lectures and recitations. He gives a new perspective to international relations and politics. Only thing that could be difficult is game theory, but they teach it well and clearly.

International Politics is a fantastic course and very interesting. Bruce can be a bit confusing in class, but recitation usually clears up all confusion. Attendance to lectures is not mandatory, but I highly recommend going because Bruce is THE expert in the field. Reading the text is assigned, but it is not essential for a good grade. Take!

The guy knows what he is talking about. Everything he says in class is word for word from the textbook (which he authored). The lecture is more so necessary to understand IR applications rather than just succeed grade wise in the class. The class if basic algebra and logical reasoning, so test shouldn't be that hard if your prepared.

He is really an amazing professor. Great researcher and great mentor. He introduced rational choice into IR and has made it essential part of IR. Ignore negative comments. You should experience one of the greatest professor in history of IR before leaving NYU.

Amazing professor, really knows his stuff and is engaging. He is, however, a bit of an egomaniac and thinks the world of himself. Still, this should not hinder your learning experience, just give you something to laugh at.

(Solving Foriegn Crises)Anyone writing negative comments just doesn't get it.  Take any of his classes, audit... whatever... you MUST experience him before you leave NYU.  You will simply have your mind blown every class.  You will mature as a thinker due to his rigorous methods of examining IR.  His teaching is life-changing.
Disregard all previous comments.  He is a narcissist who just wants his students to buy his book!

While he is enthusiastic about his subject and has a wicked sense of humor, he is not the one to determine your grade but the TAs.  The class is usually 200+ people so make sure you have a helpful TA who is lenient. Despite how much he says the class is like "9th grade algebra".. it's NOT. It's like chemistry... memorization.

i LOVE Bueno De Mesquita.  He may be well past his sexual prime.  But my god, the man gets me all hot and bothered.  I want him to talk nerdy to me. ALL. NIGHT. LONG. <3 .  He knows his stuff, he knows the material, he's incredibly enthusiastic and he wants to challenge you to really understand the topic.  He is BRILLIANT!  One of the best! <3 him!

Prof. Bueno de Mesquita is probably the most amazing professor you will ever have at NYU. I took his Intl Pol class and learned alot. Intl pol is not what you think is, it's highly mathematical. But that's reality; this man speaks the truth. He is highly intelligent and his teaching method is eccentric, yet logical. He is a modern-day Nostradamus.

He told us he hadn't taught the course since the 1970s.  While everything he had to say was always interesting, it wasn't always relevant.  Do all of the reading and understand it BEFORE the lecture, otherwise you'll be lost with him.  Digressions are either wonderful or terrible.
AN IR GOD.
I like International/world politics. Dr. Bruce is intelligent and well-connected but difficult to follow in class.

The very first classes are hard to understand and it might seem like the game theory is going nowhere. However, I was suprised that it all made sense in the end. Great Class!! Very smart man! I loved it!

Heavy on game theory and equations, uses interesting and facinating case-studies, great sense of humor, engaging with students. Highly recommended for for political science and international relations students.
great teacher. Incredibly intelligent on politics and many other subjects. A little hard to understand sometimes, but overall, you'll learn a lot from her.
Hottie 4 eva! Needs to improve teaching skills... i daydream in that class.

I took Professor Busa in the Fall of 25 for her CAMS 147 - Love Actually class. She loves teaching this class, and you can tell. She teaches directly off the slides and from the readings; however, this does not mean skip class. This class has two professors, and she was clearly the favorite. She does teach fast, but it is very comprehensible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took Love Actually with Jeremy and Sam. She is fun and relatable, but tends to rush through content sometimes. Midterm was unfairly difficult, which she warned us about (?), but the final was easy. Lots of reading, which I didn't do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Sam is a very relaxed, down to earth professor! She really just wants participation in discussion and on forums, but makes it easy to. The final exam was hard but shes not wholly in charge of what goes on the test - all the Love Actually course instructors give the same exam. She is super quick at responding to emails (never on weekends though).
Took her class "Love Actually" and LOVED it. She's a fun professor and was great about facilitating discussion. Easy grader and takes feedback into consideration.

Great CAMS teacher! She gives you every opportunity to succeed by dropping lowest response and test grades. The lectures are informative and generate great discussion. Some weeks are heavier than others on reading, but they are integral to fully understanding the class. She is very understanding about participation and workload, would take again!

Professor Burgos is a true gem at silver. She cares for her students. PARTICIPATE !!! Show commitment to the material, she doesn't like people to be on your screens. Email is very reliable when communicating with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Burgos was amazing! If you really care about the course and the topics you will find each class incredibly engaging and powerful. Do NOT be late to class, her expectations are very clear. No going on phones or computers while she speaks-- participation matters. Overall a funny, kind, knowledgeable and well respected woman!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE HER! She is very caring and smart and passionate about social work! I just enjoyed the class so much. You will learn a lot! If you just listen and participate you'll have no problem! She teaches from the heart and not just reads off the slides. I love her!

She's the best teacher I've ever had. Society and social welfare is the reason I want to be a social worker. She's hysterical and sweet and everyone loves her. most understanding person. I will miss her. Easy A but definitely pay attention, she has so much incredible knowledge, its stupid to miss out.
Professor Buhler skillfully synthesizes a collection of interconnected and important methods in applied mathematics with artistry. Highly recommended.

Prof Buhler is the best math prof I have ever met!! He's nice and caring in his office hour. Although the course is extremely hard (do not expect to understand everything in the lectures), the homeworks and exams are moderate.

Hope this time when Professor Butler browses this webpage, he won't be heartbreaking haha. He really has a good sense of humor. To be honest, among the 20-ish lectures, I only understood one lecture which was about particle paths. However, his office hours helped a lot, though I always asked stupid questions:))
The best prof I had this semester, very inspiring lecture!! Love him!!

Professor Buhler is AWESOME!! He genuinely cares about his students, holds regular office hours, delivers inspiring lectures and encourages critical thinking. The semester was truly exceptional, and I have gained far more than I initially anticipated when I began with professor Buhler. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

I seldom leave a comment for professor but professor Buhler is an exception. He is such a nice person who really care about his student. He hosts 2 hours OH each weeks and willing to schedule extra meeting with you even he has a busy schedule. Very encouraging and knowledgable. I would definitiely take his course in the future if he will teach.
Tough professor but worth it! Exams are based on homework and manageable if you study. He is a great professor, highly recommend

Great professor. Fast-paced lectures with no notes posted. So make sure you don't miss any of them since the homework would be pretty difficult without the lecture material. The difficulty of the midterm and final is at the same level of the homework, so if you take the homework seriously, it shouldn't be hard to get an A.

Professor Buhler is a gem. His lectures are very condensed and he has the ability to convey challenging mathematical concepts fairly smoothly. Learning from him is a great opportunity but make sure not to miss any lecture and to go to his office hours.
Don't understand the negative reviews. Prof Buhler is the GOAT !
Best Prof EVER !!!!!!
Best class ever!
One of my favorite classes Ive taken! Dr. Buhler is clear and willing to help. Tough class but if you study the material properly then you will be fine. Highly recommend taking his class!
Avoid him at all costs. Seriously. Run. No solutions provided for HWs, and then he based the entire midterm on homework. Even if you go to his office hours, you will still come out confused.

Be sure to avoid this prof. Promised to give exam similar to homework problems, which are already hard enough and no answers are provided, and gave a totally different thing in the exam. Be ready to learn by urself and dont expect his lecture could help anything. Always finishes his lec earlier, but why not use the time for more examples?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tara is passionate about linguistics + understands how to explain complex topics to non-linguistics majors. Lectures are very long + info heavy, but all notes/slides are posted online. Expect to have a mandatory 6-question quiz once a week + homework due every week. Tests are not hard, just a lot of info to study prior. Provides many office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Science of Language was a pretty difficult class, and actually very boring at times. There's A LOT of memorization so be prepared. The class is very organized but the material is pretty difficult especially if it's your first time taking linguistics. There were a couple complaints about this class so beware. Studying a ton I only managed to get A-

Tara isnt a bad professor, shes very knowledgable about the field and her lectures are informative. But this is a REALLY hard class. Theres A LOT of work and the material is not by any means easy. If you're taking this to fulfill a NATSCI requirement either take it pass fail or take another class. Our class avg was a B- so yeah. Definitely regret.

There was a quiz schedule that was given at the beginning of the semester. Prof. Byun keeps all her information slides & study guides on NYU Classes which is REALLY helpful. It makes for easy & organized studying. Her class is clear and recitation with Emily was great and informative! Loved it. Also,  just rent the textbook from Amazon for cheap!

I love this Spanish professor. As long as you participate in class and do the homework, this class is basically guaranteed an A. However, he gives 10 pop quizzes in the semester, so make sure you do the homework carefully, especially the readings, podcasts, and videos (series & movies). Lots of fun discussions in the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Goat professor, love him

Professor Burgos is a delight. He's incredibly funny and only speaks Spanish in class (at least for intermediate II idk his rules for other levels); however, during grammar lessons, he speaks English to be extra clear. Also side note he has a very relaxing voice, and he always tells stories and it's been really great for listening comprehension.

Felix is truly the best! The class has quite a lot of work (VHL hw, quizzes, presentations, 3 exams) but he makes it so enjoyable. His classes are very engaging and he's very funny. I'd highly recommend his class.

Incredible professor. Funny, understanding, and incredibly nice. 
He is not afraid to call you out on things and it is guaranteed that he will call on you at-least once per class, so you definitely cannot skip on his homework.
I love this guy. He's so funny and chill, but at the same time such a simple human being. Gracias!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Super easy class if you've taken Spanish prior. To receive an A in the class make sure you complete all your MindTap assignments, which is an easy A and practice vocabulary. One way I practiced was making by making my own Quizlet cards. Felix was a really caring professor and super understanding. His classes are comical and honestly fun to attend.

If you need to complete Spanish 1, take him! Mr. Burgos is one of the best professors at NYU; you can tell he cares so much about the language, and helping everyone learn it at their own pace. He does pop quizzes, but if you complete the homework, you should get a good grade on them! There's a lot of work too, but he's very fair with grading :)

Felix is one of the best professors I've had and made me care about Spanish. He made class engaging, which really helps with learning Spanish. He's extremely understanding and a really nice guy. There's a lot to learn but he grades very fairly. The pop quizzes are fine if you're paying attention and doing the homework. Take this class with him.

The class moves pretty fast, and you'll be speaking Spanish from day one. Most of the stuff is done in pairs or groups, so you end up making friends. Burgos has a great voice and is super easy to understand. He brings a lot of energy and makes sure everyone gets involved. There are pop quizzes, but they're chill as long as you do the homework.
Very easy class. Feels a bit like high school though because it's Spanish 1, freshman, terrible Spanish accents, and tons of forced participating in a circle.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awesome teacher, would totally take again, always found a way to keep the content interesting and light even though the readings were dense. Personally not a fan of the final project but loved his teaching style, would def take again!

He's awesome. The homework load is not bad at all and generally straight forward. 3 tests, 3 writing assignments, & 1 final project (have to go & talk to spanish speakers). SUPER nice guy tho, very funny & relaxed. But get ready for pop quizzes (usually when you learn new verbs).

His class is very interesting and himself is very enthusiastic. He's fun and patient. The workload is moderate. Personally speaking, the quizzes and exams are not hard and if preview is well done, then you can get a high score. The grade is very fair.

He makes learning Spanish easy and fun. I looked forward to coming to class everyday. Nobody in our class had a single complaint about him. The class will be an easy A if you come to class, participate, and do the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Went into class thinking that Spanish was my least favorite class but it ended up being my favorite.  He actually made me want to learn the language and apply it outside of the classroom.  He is everything and more 10/10
Really friendly, patient, and easygoing professor! Still friends and greet him when we meet in campus
Great lectures. Very patient during classes and always ready to help

Definitely a solid and respectable Professor overall. Super chill, well organized, and I have no complaints. Love him as a person too. Take him if you can. Spanish classes require practice and a lot of work, but put in effort and it isn't difficult to get an A. Everything is laid out in the syllabus.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The whole NYU Spanish department is known to be great, and Burgos really exemplifies that. He is very kind to his students and mindful of their situations, and his lessons are generally planned out perfectly. The Spanish department all follows the same material. Spanish classes are work, but Burgos made it bearable and engaging despite Zoom fatigue
I love him. He's hilarious and he makes classes super fun, you become friends with everyone in class. But he does make you talk to random people to practice.
Felix is my hero loved him as a person more than as a professor.

Professor Burgos is an angel. He made my experience this semester so much better. Hes super funny & class is always fun (you play games like Kahoot), youll make friends in the class because hes always pairing up students for activities. Work load is manageable as long as you stay on top of online HW & writing prompts. Definitely recommend!
nice guy, great voice and amazing beard
Honestly he's my president, great teacher great man
Loves Macchio Picchu
nice guy, great voice and beard

What an amazing, amazing professor and man. He's intimidatingly intelligent, caring, and funny. He genuinely wants his students to learn and develop their Spanish skills, and his passion is evident throughout each class. He appreciates improvement and participation, and workload is very manageable, especially because he follows the syllabus to a T.

He's such a great man!  I've definitely improved in this class and he had great methods of teaching. Make sure you actually try here,  these new concepts aren't that easy. Speak to him if you need any help and he will try to help you. This is a class where you will improve your fluency and knowledge about latin american politics.

Professor Burgos is awesome! He's very patient and willing to help students. The class covers a lot of material, but he manages to explain it well. There are lot of conversation activities, so be ready to talk in Spanish. Highly recommended!

Besides the fact that we had to buy a book we only used like once or twice, Felix is fantastic! The class was small and pretty chill and relaxed. He is very clear during lectures and his presentations are mega helpful. He also always has funny stories to share. He is truly a great professor! Te lo recomiendo!! Es el mejor!

Felix is young-ish, is very clear (both in speaking and in assignmentsgrading), patient, and helpful. He also has funny stories. The homework and assignments were not very difficult, just appropriate for the class. He connects well with students. Would recommend.
Felix is a great Spanish professor. He explains clearly the grammar and has fun stories. The prezi presentations are very helpful, if you ask, he will email them to you

Absolutely loved taking Advanced Grammar with him. He is one of the funniest teachers I have had. Very energetic and clear. Ask him for the Prezi presentations before the exams and he will email them to the class.
I am using this professor's Textbook for my class and it's one of the most useless and vague texts I've ever had the displeasure of using in my education.

Professor Cabral is not a good teacher. The textbook you use is written by him and includes so much useless information. The useful parts are written in a very confusing matter. In lectures he just reads off the textbook and really doesn't explain much. His tests are really not that bad if you force yourself to read the textbook, but this is hard.

Lectures were highly ineffective. Even if you attend every lecture that does not guarantee you will do good in the class, as the tests rely heavily on the textbook. The lectures and problem sets are very different and have little to no correlation with one another. Thankfully, problem sets are graded based on effort, but are ultimately ineffective.

Although sometimes you will not be clear about the course content by only listening to the lecture, the course is manageable if you spend some time reading the textbook. The course is analytics/writing heavy so make sure you understand each topic very well!

Prof Cabral is a nice person and likely great high-level econ prof, but terrible for an entry course. He wrote the textbook, which is more real-world examples than econ concepts. Graded debates which don't help you understand econ better. Tests either impossibly hard or so easy you're Stern curved down heavily. Cross your fingers for a good TA.
PLEASE RUN AWAY FROM HIM, THIS GUY IS TERRIBLE, PLEASE RUN AWAY FROM HIM AT ALL COST
Memorize the textbook and hope that the stern curve will save you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Stern curve saves it all because everyone fails in this class. You need to do the discussion forum although you participated - so if you're a tedious monster who wants to get an A that bad, check the discussion forum every day. Exams are weirdly theoretical heavy, read the book. I repeat READ HIS 500 PAGE BOOK AND MEMORIZE!

He's the BEST professor EVER at Stern. Have no idea why so many people said bad things about him. It doesn't matter how hard the exam is since everything is CURVED at Stern. The slides are clear and the lectures were interesting. He was good at using econ concepts to explain real-world examples, which is the best part of the course.

His lectures are literally a regurgitation of the textbook (which is SO DRY). His tests are hard and when I went to his office hour, he didn't even make an effort to explain the concepts in a new/helpful way.

Professor Cabral is a really nice person but he simply cant teach. His lectures are just him giving his opinions on economic concepts and less of him actually teaching. Youll have to teach yourself most of the material either with the textbook or your own sources. The textbook can be useful at times but is poorly written.
He's a nice person. But be ready to read the textbook to prep quizzes and exams.
Great professor! Please take his class if possible!

Honestly not that bad if you pay attention in class and read the textbook. The quizzes are very similar to the homework. The examples he gives are interesting if you are into economics. A lot of people dont show up to the lectures

He lowered my grade AFTER he released a different grade on Albert. Terrible communication, unclear grading criteria, unclear course material, lectures are useless because everything is taught out of a textbook HE wrote.
Simply. Cannot. Teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are impossible to focus in, and even if you manage to pay attention, nothing he says will appear on any homework, test, or quiz. His textbook is unreadable, covers basically none of the math and equations required for the assessments, and is chock full of useless 'real-life' examples that confuse you more than they help. Horrible class.
Respected professor. But he cant teach!

Lectures is ALL OVER THE PLACE, if I haven't studied myself I would for sure fail this class. At the same time, the textbook of this class is his own task book,which is packed with content but HARD TO READ. He is a genuinely nice guy but there so much room for improvement for the lectures.

Bad professor plain and simple. Cant teach at all very confusing. If your TA isint good your grade is down the drain cuz thats the only way most people managed to pass the tests. He taught for maybe 30 minutes and had these useless speakers in our class who talked abt random stuff i didnt even pay attention. Avoid the class you wont learn anything.

Homework consists of weekly problem sets (2-3 hours). 2 quizzes, a midterm and final; all similar in difficulty to homework problems/ practice tests. Nice person, answers all your questions, but doesn't really teach and instead, invites a lot of guest speakers to take up class time. Essentially have to self study entire course by reading textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice man, but terrible professor. Uses his own textbook for the class, which is not bad at all, but his lectures are all over the place and literally seem like they're for a completely different class. Lots of guest speakers with no relevance to course at all. Tough grading on exams and quizzes. Avoid if you can.

He changed his syllabus this year and used his own textbook which had mistakes in it (making students even more confused). he never really taught in class but just had guest lectures and for HW we were meant to read the textbook and take notes from it. ur TA will literally save you, go for office hours otherwise it can be challenging
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The whole class is a glorified textbook reading session
Textbook is of no use. Quizzes have no clear answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cabral is a nice guy. But unfortunately, being a nice guy doesn't help one cope with the unironically dozens of hours of self-teaching this course requires. He doesn't teach in class in the slightest. All learning is expected to be done independent from his own textbook, which has more pages of errors/typos than not. It's convoluted.

This class will not be as difficult if you've taken AP micro in high school. If not, this will probably be the worst class you take at Stern. He assumes the students have a lot of prior knowledge in the subject and tends to skip a lot of important/fundamental concepts. He only talks about real-world applications that aren't on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He changed the class so that it's entirely theoretical, no math involved. TAs are tough graders and only give full points for including every example, definition/term, and graph in the notes, even if your answer is right. Make sure to read the lecture notes and do all the practice problems he gives!
He never teach you anything but give you hard test. He grades students only on two tests, which is ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hes a great guy, but doesnt teach the material thats on the tests and quizzes. He goes off on tangent a lot. I recommend going to office hours if you need help.

Professor Cabral is probably a great guy. However, he is not that great of a teacher. He often goes off on tangents about random stuff like cod and drones which very little to do with Economics. His questions on homeworks/quizzes/tests usually either have nothing to do with the material or include include information we haven't learned yet.

It is definitely a tough course for freshmen, and for this prof especially, you need to do a lot of self-studying. if you do, you'll be relatively fine, but if you just listen in class and go to tests, you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He was a nice professor but I found he just didn't focus on the right topics during lecture. The course involved a lot of self-study because he would glaze over the more important topics and ramble on real-life applications. Maybe that was appreciated by some students, but the majority of what was covered in lecture did not ever appear on exams.
He's good. Homework and quizzes are easy, but the final is pretty hard.

Taking Sight & Sound Film with Catherine was amazing! I was lucky to have a good crew, which definitely helped, but she's super caring and her lectures were always interesting. She also invited lots of great guest speakers. Class was very much about collaboration and giving your classmates feedback. Highly recommend!

Lectures can be long but she always tries to let us go early. She's really nice and caring, unintentionally hilarious too. Class was a wonderful space and she was a truly kind person and attentive professor. Not a harsh grader and you have lots of freedom
Wasn't lecture heavy. Wasn't the greatest professor but good person overall. For context pick good crews before you decide to blame the teacher

Had Catherine for S&S Doc. She's AWESOME. She will show you docs currently in the industry, she will push you to make your films happen. Getting feedback from her each time made me grow, and with 5 docs in one semester, you grow fast! can't thank her enough for what she's taught me.

Catherine is straight to the point. She gives really helpful, clear feedback and her class is a fun environment. I really appreciate her comments. Although they can sometimes seem harsh if you're not used to that sort of feedback, it'll help you grow in the long run. Would definitely recommend! One of my favorite classes I've taken at NYU so far.

As long as you follow the prompt, there is quite a lot of freedom. Class structure is loose. Lectures are not too rich but luckily are rare. Gives critiques. A bit of an oldhead- will mention the Godfather. Ultimately allows the class to be about collaboration and practice, which is great.

I had Catherine for both Documentary and Filmmaking S&S. While I'd definitely recommend her more for documentary, she was one of my favorite professors at NYU. If you take the time to get to know her she has such a big heart and also gives super valuable critique. She makes you work towards and recognize your strengths.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. She barely knew anything about the topic she was teaching and would sometimes "teach" us things that were untrue. She was also hostile to anyone who disagreed with her. Ruined what could have been a great class.

Catherine has a lot of knowledge and admiration for the medium and shares it with you. She's also very nurturing and open-minded, providing you with room to roam free with your ideas. Don't take her for granted. She's also honest with criticsm, but presents it tenderly. The class is somewhat loose structurally, but it certainly didn't bother me.

I enjoyed Catherine's class. She wasn't the best lecturer but she's a sweet lady that just wants to see her students succeed. If you come to class (she really doesn't like when students miss class if it isn't for a good reason) and participate in the group critiques and submit everything, you'll get an A.
Canary rawdogs his lectures but his practice worksheets are good, he isn't that bad of a teacher and offered the most extra credit which you can't really complain about.

Not the best but not the worst. 

Pros:
- Well organized slides which rly helped when learning and reviewing the material
- Gave extra credit that boosted my grade by 5%

Cons:
- Unclear teaching, made mistakes during lecture that i didnt realize until i reviewed the material myself
- Not enough practice material (can get from other profs tho)

This professor has gotten a lot of hate for his teaching, but I will say that he put in lots of effort and clearly wants his students to succeed. Recorded lectures, gave extra credit that no one else did & gave us plenty of practice worksheets and old exams. This is a hard class that needs lots of outside practice. You honestly get what you give.

at first he wasn't the best professor, but he quickly improved. He gives extra credit at the end of each lecture and holds extra office hours during finals. He posts plenty of practice problems that are helpful and made sure the exams were fair. He often gives hints about whats on the exams. his quizzes were much more difficult than other prof tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall an ok lecturer, but the notes and bits of info were somewhat disorganized. Exams(and quizzes) were on the challenging side, especially compared to the other sections
The course was incredibly disorganized, and you end up doing seven times the work just to keep pace with students in other sections, who consistently perform much better.
He writes his own exams, his class still has the lowest average.

Professor Canary is such a kind professor and wants his students to succeed in orgo.  He is a little outdated when it comes to technology, but his knowledge regarding organic chemistry is unmatched and he hosts amazing office hours where you can ask him anything.  He stays over his office hour limit everytime to help students who are having trouble
Good luck, on your second attempt.

Not sure why everyone's praising him for giving extra credit..he kind of had to when his class average was consistently A LOT lower than other sections for a standardized test. Means it's his fault.  Even then, it didn't amount to how much he should've gave.

I didn't attend lectures since 8am for something that YouTube can teach better isn't worth it. There is extra credit for showing up and taking a quiz though. I don't think Canary is too bad but def not the best of the options. The course itself is difficult so just don't fall behind cause procrastination won't work…. Unless you want C ……………

His lectures are a mess but he managed to explain most things at a surface level. With orgo you must read the textbook and grind practice regardless of how good a lecturer you have, so Canary is getting a worse rap than deserved. He gave so much extra credit that we thought it was a mistake and hosts okay office hours. Go to SLGs and grind the book

Yall are being too harsh, its Orgo not intro to finance. His lectures are pretty bad and you have to work hella outside of class, it's like a full time job. Canary gives insane amounts of extra credit compared to other professors (5.5% vs 1.5%). Take him if you can grind on your own, go to the SLG's and watch youtube videos and READ THE TEXTBOOK.
There's no way he is seriously here to teach students. If you need to wait a semester, a year, two years, to avoid taking organic chemistry with James Canary, do it.
He's the next Maitland Jones. Look him up.

He would tell his students explicitly to know certain material for the exam. When students in other sections would ask their professors if that material would be covered on the standardized exam that all sections receive, they would say no. Low and behold, that material would not show up on the exam.

He would tell his explicitly students to know material for an exam. Students in other sections would ask their professors do we need to know this ? They would say no. Low and behold the very difficult
I could watch a Chads prep video and teach the class the concept better than him

Not accessible outside of class if u need help . Not understanding. If u ask a question during lecture he will be so annoyed and just stare at u like did u really just ask that and he won't answer the question either

There's a reason his lecture was the only one open. If you have to take orgo off track or whatever literally do anything else but unless u want to self teach urself the entirety of orgo and somehow pass the very difficult recitation quizzes, do not take his class. I literally wish I delayed taking it

He once told us he would  do something  , something that is very common  in America in schools recently happened at brown university   (writing this so the review is posted) us if we made a specific mistake in a reaction. Nothing funny about that. He in a later lecture made the same ” mistake.

Don't listen to anyone saying he's funny or sweet. He's not. He tries to make corny jokes but nothing is funny at 8am when I can't even read what he writing and u can't even follow ur own work, are making mistakes, aren't teaching properly, and the averages for ur exams are in the 50s while every other section is doing better.

His section always had the lowest average for every single exam. He also gives the hardest quizzes for recitation. Writing during lectures is illegible and constantly makes mistakes. If he can't even teach us Orgo 1 at a PHD level, how does he expect us to do good on tests?
Avoid at all costs
He comes to lecture a little unprepared, messing up some of his own examples. He's used to teaching majors orgo so his worksheets are good but lectures aren't amazing. Do the textbook questions

Literally the worse class i have ever had. I am 1000% sure if his quizzes were easier and if he actually taught during lectures I would understand whats going on. DO NOT TAKE this class if you actually want to understand whats going on in orgo. I recommend to take another professor like Angelo.

He's a very nice person, but not an effective teacher. His handwriting is difficult to read, and he largely leaves students to learn organic chemistry on their own through the textbook. His quizzes are harder than those of other professors, and our section typically performs the worst. I wouldn't recommend taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very cute old man, not very cute lectures... His "Canary scratch" does not help with the fact lecture is @ 8AM and orgo is a very visual class. Get ready to interpret hieroglyphics. He quizzes us harder than other sections even tho he is the worst of 3 sections @ explaining (rushed + makes lots of mistakes!) We r always the lowest scoring section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: tbh the only good thing about him was extra credit. his handwriting is so bad u cant even read his notes & his lectures aren't very clear

He's a fine lecturer, but not the best. Over complicates things. Makes very difficult recitation quizzes, should not be teaching undergrads. Gave more work than other orgo professors. Avoid if you can- that being said he is a very nice guy. Very accessible outside of class. But get ready to read and make orgo your entire life.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He moves very quickly through the material and often rushes his explanations. The extra credit he offers (0.25 points each class) is definitely helpful, but overall he isn't a very effective instructor. His recitation quizzes are consistently more difficult compared to those given by other professors.
Professor Canary is so slay. He is one of the best teachers I have ever had.

This is a difficult class which can be quite intimidating, but Canary does his best to help his students succeed. I would strongly advise going to his office hours to get the help you need because he is so willing to help and guide his students. He's very funny, very kind, and a great professor! I thoroughly enjoyed his class and would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Canary is truly an amazing professor and chemist. He is always kind and helpful and he is very funny! Tests are difficult, but he seems to care much more that students understand and are interested in chemistry than any test grade. Don't believe the bad reviews, Canary is a great guy and a great teacher

Professor Canary is easily one of the best professors at NYU- he is extremely caring and genuinely wants his students to learn. He would sit with us in office hours for hours at a time discussing random topics and helping us with problems, which really shows how dedicated he is to teaching and to his students! Love this man!!

Cannot deliver a coherent lecture. Feels like the last time he saw the material he is teaching was 10 years ago. Skips concepts and comes back and leaves many gaps in knowledge. Calculation errors. Gets bored of what he is teaching and moves on to next topic. Teaches like topic is review and not the first time learning. Tests are straightforward.
