Canary doesn't have an ability to teach at all. It always seems it's his first time using the slides, he makes so many computational mistakes. He misleads students on what to study for exams. Lab questions are taken verbatim and put on exams, yet TA's don't give them back. They send passive-aggressive emails about kids who ask about it

Midterm I was a disaster with more than 50% of the class getting a C or below and Midterm II was worse despite 'assurances' that exams would mirror the HW's. Poor professor + Poor course design  Poor evaluation. As a department chair treat your students and TAs with more respect. Absolute madness for a CORE class with no curve!

Prof. Canary's Energy and the Environment class has been the worst class I have ever taken at NYU. Not only does he seem unprepared to teach, but his lectures are boring, and his tests are much harder than they need to be. Do not take!!!

Professor Canary is one of the worst professors I've had. He cannot explain concepts whatsoever, isn't clear on what he's looking for on exams and has made an introductory course much much more difficult and stressful than necessary. You're better off skipping class and studying yourself. Do better NYU!

Stay away from this class at all costs. Professor speaks in monotone, struggles at explaining concepts, and make learning chemistry a lot harder than it needs to be. Labs are equally as bad. Expect to teach or re-teach yourself chemistry on your own as this professor and your TA wont be helping you much.

Prof Canary is absolutely horrendous. He is a terrible lecturer, doesn't understand what he is teaching, and makes the class really hard. Tests are impossible. Labs are boring. Terrible class. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Take Canary over Jones. Seriously. He will teach you all you need to know for the MCAT and your GPA will thank you. I took Jones first semester and had to sacrifice any studying for other classes just for a B. Took Canary, studied the normal few hours a day one should for Orgo, and made an A (and the tests are still challenging!). Great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Canary was an excellent lecturer and a great professor overall. He followed the textbook closely so it was easy to get ahead by reading the assigned chapters. His exams were moderate to challenging, but working through his exams from previous years helpsed.
Extremely clear and helpful, made orgo easy to understand
Very insightful and passionate teacher. You will learn a lot if you pay attention. He also has a very good sense of humor. Exams are a bit hard, but they are all based on what has been taught.

Seems like a smart guy, but he isn't the greatest teacher. Exams were hard, answers to practice exams were illegible, and he often forgot things in class that an organic chemist shouldn't forget. His jokes will make you laugh though!

hard prof. weekly timed quizzes (usu. 30 min long) given on Blackboard & no retakes are allowed unless you get a quiz grade lower than 5. grading for lab reports are inconsistent & there's a pg limit of 4-6 single-spaced typed pgs. final was hard. if you want to do well, definitely don't type lab reports at last min, review all labs for final!

CB was a wonderful professor! The range of topics covered in his class was so extensive, and I feel like food as I know it has been given all this dimension to it than ever before. Was supportive of every voice in the classroom, and just overall a funny and honest dude who loves the work he does. I had a great time participating in his class!

Discussion-based class and CB makes it very engaging. He gives out pop quizzes but if you do the readings you will be fine, mostly articles and videos, which are quite interesting and fun to read and watch anyways. No midterm just one final with written response questions. Take this class!
His personality is alright and I can see why students here gave him a 5-star rating. However, it is a participation matters class but he never calls on me.

CB is such a nice guy. He is so generous and always gives the extra credit. No midterm, only the final project/exam (you can choose by yourself). There are only 6-8 pop quizzes which is quite easy if you read the material. He is so great!!! You definitely need to take him!!!

CB is a great professor. He's extremely chill, easy to get ahold of, and hilarious. The work is pretty light, and he doesn't really require using highly academic writing in papers, which makes them really easy and fun to write. If you show up, do the readings, and participate in the discussions, you'll do well. Make use of the extra credit opps!

There are four reading responses for the class as well as four in-class quizzes. CB gives out lots of extra credit opportunities. The course is very inspiring as well, heavily based on current issues and innovations. Learned so much about food and the industry.

If you care about your GPA do not take her class. She is very strict with things outside of the quality of people's work, like participation, talking to your friend in class, being late… it will significantly affect your grade even when your works are strong.  Very unclear about grading criteria.

Not creative as an art teacher. Not much freedom for projects. Being too strict on attendance and phone use and no music during studio time. Better follow the rules and finish things on time. Not much critical thinking or discussions. But learned technical sculpture skills, if that's your priority in freshmen, recommend.

She is fine. I don't think I learned that much from this class. Although I got a good grade not many people were happy with their grade. She gives little time with the projects. Once she only gave us a day to finish our work, had to stay extra hours. BE ON TIME that is crucial. Also she doesn't let you use your phone.

A lot of work... be prepared to work 3+ hours outside of class. She is kinder than you might think though, and really cares for her students. Does give strict guidelines and makes you follow a clear set of rules when working on your projects. Do not take this class if you like to create art on your own terms, as you may find it hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Callihan is a really good writing professor that allows you to interpret her prompts through your own lens. Shows lots of love

She is an excellent professor, and I was very grateful to have her last semester. While expectations can feel open-ended at times, she is very willing to guide students who seek feedback and ask questions. She grades rigorously, but her comments help point you in the right direction and encourage improvement over time.

Professor Callihan came back to teach this semester and I could not have been more grateful. Use her comments and advice when writing, they are very helpful. The work can take a while but is meaningful and fun. Also, please talk during lecture, it gets very awkward when people just sit there. She is very accessible outside of class in her office

I am a good writer but the professor is incredible. She is so supportive in all aspects even let us out of class if we had an exam that followed her class. She understands that this is class is one of our lowest priorities but she expects you to show up and try your best. Always participate that helped me increase my grade.
Amazing Prof!!!! Love her. She's literally the sweetest and is so helpful. Thank you for a wonderful semester.
She is truly one of the best expos professors. Her feedback made me a better writer.
She is an angel. She is very inspiring and supportive. She is the best. You will be grateful if you can take her course.

Took Nicole's class for two semesters (Expos-UA 4/ 9). I'm not a great writer, but Nicole helped me improve by a mile. Gives great feedback and cares a lot about her students. Very accessible during office hours & can talk to about anything even if not class-related. I'm a STEM major, but writing the essay w/ Nicole was the highlight of freshman yr

Amazing professor with a marvelous sense of humor. Extremely enthusiastic about the material and made me genuinely excited to come to class. The course is structured very creatively, from presentations to pitching Op-Eds. She's very encouraging and gives excellent feedback to help you improve as a writer.

Nicole is a really sweet person. She cares her students, understand them, and most importantly she prepared class material and revise essays really carefully. Can't think of any professor better than her!

I would take her again if it fit in my schedule. Shes really sweet and caring. I would definitely recommend her. In my opinion she could be a LITTLE unclear in what she wants you to right about but she explains it if you dont get it. Professor Callihans class isnt terribly difficult. If you can, id say take her class!
Thank you for being my teacher.

Incredible lady. Super sweet, knowledgeable, and just wants everyone to learn and be happy. Great experience in the course, which was a total 180 from last semester. The environment is happy, supportive, and I've learned so much more from her than I did last semester.

Professor Callihan is an amazing Expository Writing teacher who cares for her students. Not only is she understanding of your situation but also she really wants you to improve your writing skills. I have always found her critiques clear! She also offers many one-to-one conferences.

Professor Callihan is the perfect EXPOS instructor if you are an intellectually curious person who wants to explore the surrounding world. She always has such a profound presence in the class and her ideas are extraordinary. Truly inspiring!
Professor Callihan is always so nice and full of amazing ideas. She inspires her students a lot and really cares and listens to her students. EXPOS will be fun with her, I promise.

reviews.comment: Prof. Callihan is definitely a nice lady, but if you've struggled with English and writing in high school, I don't think her class would be the best for you. Her style of teaching and grading was very difficult for me, so the class was a bit overwhelming and a tad unenjoyable since I was never a great writer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. She's very kind and energetic. I looked forward to her class and when it comes to conferences, she gives useful feedback and advice with how to write your essay. She makes writing enjoyable and she is such a wonderful person! I definitely recommend to take her class!

Professor Callihan is a great professor. She really cares about you and wants you to succeed so if you're having trouble all you have to do is go visit her and she will try and guide you. Professor Callihan is a great writing professor and she knows that we are engineering students so she does a lot for her students.

Not only is she an outstanding teacher, Prof. Callihan is a very nice person in and out of the classroom. She is always willing to help out, as long as you go to class. There's no reason to miss her class: you will always learn something and have a great time! And someday she might even bring cookies/madeleines.
Wonderful teacher; she is  helpful, friendly and pretty good at explaining things.
LOVE professor callihan. She's a star! tough grader, but she wants you to do well and tries her best to get you on the right track. And she brings cupcakes to class sometimes!

She is so smart and nice. Her lectures were engaging and interesting. She cares about her students and spent a class period teaching us how to use linked in. She understands that to study public health we need to understand how to make connections in the real world and gave us many opportunities to do so! AMAZING! take her.

reviews.comment: her class is super interesting, her class is packed with knowledge, and the vibe is immaculate!

Take her!!! She genuinely cares about her students and her lectures are so engaging and interesting. Time definitely flies in this class. All the projects and the midterm/final are take home, and the grading criteria is clear. As long as you do your work and stay engaged, you're set! Best professor I've ever taken, honestly.
I really enjoy the ways her lectures are creative keeps me alert and I find myself interested in stuff I didnt expect to be. Also, really nice!

Avoid this teacher at all costs. I cannot believe she has lasted at the university for this long. She talks down to her students and will not budge if you try to reason reason with her. Her lectures are all over 150 slides and she does not even teach them. Oh, and she provides no study guides for exams. It upsets me that my money is going to her.

Lectures are confusing b/c info keeps repeating. Powerpoints are like 150+ slides and she edits them w/out posting the updated version. Tests are LONG (90 question final). During the midterm she made everyone get up and stretch which is distracting and frustrating. Its hard to do bad b/c of all the extra credit she offers and she is condescending

Dr. Stewart is genuinely invested in her students understanding the material. The way she conducts class aims to promote reasoning and asking the right questions. This makes the class difficult. You need to come to class prepared.

Terrible all around. Condescending even if you are a hard worker. Does not explain things clearly. Mistakes in slides, which are extremely disorganized. When people ask her questions, she tries to shut them up so she does not have to answer them, and makes you feel bad about it on top of it.  Any other professor but her. Ugh.

I liked this professor in the beginning, but then I learned how unflexible she is. She always talks in this soft voice, so it can seem like she is being nice, but actually she is talking down to you. Her lectures are disorganized and hard to follow (and boring). The only good thing is that she wrote the book, so its like a repeat of the lecture.

Agree with everyone else. She is very spacey/disorganized/unclear and it's a drag to sit through her class. She can patronize and disrespect you all while smiling and speaking softy (my guess is she is always trying to reduce her vocal effort, but still wanting to take jabs at you).
she is one of the worst teachers i have ever had.  she is totally unorganized, patronizing, and downright bizarre. she is not helpful and is mean spirited.

unorganized, unhelpful, unfair, mean, makes a lot of mistakes and will never admit to them. on a test, if you wrote something from your notes and she marks them as wrong, but you show her it was what she mentioned in class, points will not be rewarded. total ****

She really wants you to learn the material, which is great, but she doesn't know how to teach it.  She will make errors all over her notes and worksheets, but will never admit to them and will expect you to know what's write and wrong.
Took his class a few years back. He is a super caring professor and genuinely led me to make up mind to do a major in Spanish. Highly recommend.
He was easily the best Spanish professor I have had. He is completely understanding of any problems you may have.

He is the best Spanish professor at NYU 100%. He is so understanding of your work load for other classes and does his best to accommodate any issues. He genuinely cares about his students and wants us all to do well. He is a king!
super super sweet & generous with grading - homework can be boring but syllabus easy to understand and know what's due!

sooooo kind and understanding-- i needed to change the day of a presentation and asked a couple days before and he was so nice about it. although the class is quite work heavy, he's such a great teacher too, really passionate and clearly cares about everyone in the class! would very highly recommend.
So understanding. He sees your effort and rewards you for it. Love him!

reviews.comment: Michelle is amazing. I would definitely recommend her as a TA for Intro to Soc. She's very laid-back and really knows how to foster a productive conversation. You can also ask her anything and get a good response, unlike a lot of TAs who just regurgitate the textbook at you. Grading-wise, she's pretty chill. The curve is like 60% get an A.
Michelle is super kind - complements what is learned in the lecture w/ really relevant info - very understanding! Def take her rec section
Michelle is the best TA in NYU. Provides solid feedback for your essay and replies email within a day. Defenitly take her session since soc1 is graded by TA.

Michelle was super sweet, caring, and always made an effort to make class fun and easier. She is always available for help and gives really good feedback on papers so you know exactly what you need to do for a good grade. Definitely take her if you can!

The best TA I ever had! She is very caring and inspirational. She doesn't curve grade and give students a second chance to edit their essay. If you have any problems, just talk to her, she is always willing to help. I would definitely take her course again!

Took this class a few years back. Awful TA: no kindness, no tailoring of the material to students' backgrounds, and most of all, exceptionally rigid in her teaching. There was no room for discussion and most students felt extremely scared of asking questions because the responses we'd get were so condescending and mean.
GOAT!

all i have to say is dont take it

Great instructor, she really cares about her students. Difficult coding lectures and labs for beginners but she provides solid help to get over the initial struggles. Remote instruction didn't make this course easy but I think she really tried her best.
Great prof! loved the lectures, intense but super responsive and helpful. i really feel like i learned a lot, from the basics up

If you're looking for an inspiring professor, DO NOT take class with her. Every lecture was mind-numbing, just her reading straight off slides she refused to post. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class, for an online class in the middle of two crises in America, was horrible. Her online quizzes were almost impossible to get a good grade on, and her attitude was unsympathetic to the status of the world. There were some quizzes, 1 paper, and 2 Tests. She read off her slides mostly, and one class legit just read a research paper outloud.

Paola does not care about students and her grading is just based on whether she likes you or not. Not only that, 20% of her grading was for participation but the only way to participate in the course is to interrupt the lecture and ask questions. It was completely subjective. Her quizzes were really difficult for a core class filled with non majors

She is tough and demanding, you need to put in the work and show that you make an effort. She has little patience for students that don't care, but her lectures actually got me genuinely interested and then I realized that she is beyond helpful, patient and knowledgeable. I learned much more from her labs than from lecture! She is amazing!!!

She is without a doubt the rudest professor/TA I have had at NYU. When you ask her a question, she always gives an answer in a condescending manner. I never ask questions on labs, because I know she is just going to give a nasty response. Great class, but choose a different TA.

At first a bad impression: very strict and demanding. In reality super caring and knowledgable. Yes, you need to work hard otherwise you won't pass. Very fair grader. A tough hard working woman - if you like anthropology she is amazing and inspiring!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a great TA, and I really got inspired during her lectures to learn more about the topic. However, sometimes she does not really have a lot of patience if you don't understand immediately what she is talking about. She is super knowledgable but other people are not necessarily anthro majors! She is very helpful though and always available!

Paola is an amazing TA, the best I've had at NYU. She is really passionate about anthropology and really wants her students to do well! I'm not an ANTH major, but if she was to teach a class of her own I would take it!

Hands down one of the best TAs I've had. Super knowledgable, funny and interesting. The subject is at times dry and boring but you can tell she tries to make the best of it in her labs. Tough grader and NOT flexible with deadlines, but if you are on top of things you will be fine. Bonus: she's super hot so you really want to pay attention.

Professor Cerfon has done a phenomenal job! He's lecture notes are wonderful, and he gives amazing lectures! Prof. Cerfon is very caring of his student, very assecible (though he's busy), and relly trying to let his students understand the material well. Definitely choose him! He is the GOAT!
The best math prof at NYU
My math sucks but professor Antoine teaches so well that makes me feel I have to come here and give him a rating.

Great Professor and is dedicated toward teaching. Tests/ HWs are extremely difficult so that you will run out of time easily during the exams. Take it if you have significant amount of time to spend on this course.

Took grad complex var with Prof Cerfon as an undergrad. Presented the materials in a palatable manner, cared about his students, and had flexible in grading. He was passionate about the subject and willing to help you solve the hard hw problems during office hours. Exams will be fair if you study hard and understand the hws. DEF TAKE HIM!

Antoine is easily one of the BEST Math professors you can find here at Courant. He cares about students' progress and would meticulously explain anything should anyone comes to questions on it during class. Also has a great sense of humor. Could recommend 11/10

Professor Cerfon is an excellent math professor, he really tries to explain the concepts carefully, gives multiple ways to solve the problems, and is really open to questions both after class and in office hours. He was even willing to talk to me about how I'd learned the material in the past to better teach in the future. Nice review sessions too!

A brilliant Professor. Clear and helpful lectures complemented by his own notes. Exams are not unreasonable and he bundles weekly quizzes together so you only have to deal with them every month or so. Really great guy!

Cerfon is a really good professor. He explains abstract concepts well, and provides very detailed lecture notes (and he tells funny math-jokes in almost every lecture).  Homework is really, really, really hard, but he would help you solve them if you come to his office hours. And he curves the grade pretty generous. Really RECOMMEND his course!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cerfon is a very good professor in many ways. He explains the material well, and he understands how difficult the material is for students. At the end of the semester, he bumps your entire course grade by 1 letter grade if he sees that you have demonstrated excellent effort. Homework is insanely difficult, but his lecture notes should help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: This course was a really difficult course, I had to study like crazy. Prof Cerfon is a pretty average teacher by NYU standards (which, in my opinion, is pretty good!) He wasn't outstanding, but he was fairly energetic, which is necessary in a nearly 2 hr math lecture. Overall, I'd recommend taking him.

Pádraig was my best prof in all of undergrad. He truly gets to know you as a person, is incredibly understanding when personal problems pop up that take precedence, and he cared far more about our passion for the Irish language than our short term retention - he lit a fire in my that will last for a long, long time. Go raibh maith agat a Mhúinteoir

Padraig is the cool Irish dude you never knew you needed in your life. As others have said, he wants you to do well. I forgot what a question word meant on my oral exam, and he skipped the question. Just put in a little effort, and have a little fun. Also, enjoy all the singing. (He does take attendance).
No Comments
No Comments

He seemed like a good professor in freshman year, for intro to programming. However, he is very biased, even though this class is for beginners, he expects you to have an understanding of coding already, and favors students who peeks his interest. He failed a few students in my year because we didn't understand coding fast enough.

Took his Game Studies class, Charles is a great professor who clearly knows what he's talking about, very knowledgeable and passionate, answers questions inside and outside of classroom. His advice might sound redundant at times but his feedback will help you improve on your writing. Take him if you can.

reviews.comment: One of my favoutie course this year! ! If you do not have a lot of programming background this course might be challenging. There is a weekly quiz for the first 5 weeks(if you do not like exams this is hard) and a weekly hw project for the whole semester, so do expect to spend a lot of time and learn a lot. Mr Pratt is super helpful and accessible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's okay. Pretty passive aggressive at times. The class is easier if you have prior coding knowledge. The lectures he gives have basic info, so if you really want to make your project nice then you have to do a lot of your own research. Felt a bit anxious attending his class sometimes due to his critiques but he acted like that toward most people.

He is a good lecture speaker, charismastic even, yet, he uses his personality to get away with working with every group and spends ALL of his time in his favorite, while neglecting others. A lot of people struggled for his favoritism. He also gaslights groups of mostly females into changing their genre to narrative. Not sure why he is still here.

The course itself is coding-heavy so don't expect easy A or easy hw. Weekly lecture video and weekly programing hw would be assigned. The class only met once per week and it was for reviewing your hw code. The course would be a bit easier if you have previous coding experience.

He should teach philosophy not game design

reviews.comment: The lectures are entertaining, especially if you care about games. You have to go, as there's a quiz guide that answers all the questions that you'll be asked in recitation. Some of the speakers don't do too well and some of the lectures aren't very entertaining (ancient board games). The weekly writing isn't hard once you know what they want.

Games 101 Great Class. Note: Don't take if you have trouble with memorization and you're not an avid gamer. Because you'll probably fail or get a low grade. Lectures vary because lecturers vary. Notes can be difficult because of that. But you need notes! But he's very helpful and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Charles is easily my favourite professor I've had at NYU. Great lecturer, fair grader, and just an interesting guy overall. Really liked the course.

Class was straightforward game history. Lots of memorization. Was flexible on midterm by for final you need to know every detail. The TAs are the people you go to with most questions. Overall seemed like a nice guy. No textbook. Hw was to play specific games and write analysis. The games are provided in the game library.

This class is great, this professor is great, this material is great. Probably the best class I've taken in college so far due mostly to the material covered and recitations. If you go to lectures and recitations, do the weekly reports, study maybe 5-10 minutes for each quiz, you're on track to an A. I loved his class and highly recommend it.

I've had Charles for three classes now. He's a great professor, always willing to engage with students. He is rather hardheaded about his views, but he does have the evidence to back them up, and invites a good debate.  I've never had someone lecture better than him.

Make no mistake, games 101 is hard. It sounds like a joke but each exam will have you memorize the gameplay, history, precedents, designers, platform, and year of release of 60 games + other lecture topics. Additionally, you have to be able to identify these from a picture. I was told this is to fight "grade inflation."
Charles is the best!
lectures can be kind of boring but she is very nice

Professor Ciftci is one of the most incredible professors I have taken. She cares about her students SO much, inside and outside of the classroom. I would absolutely take her again. I loved walking in and seeing her smiling face welcoming us. She also gives a lot of help when needed. 10/10 professor.

Dr. Ciftci is a fantastic professor! I've taken two of her classes and had the best learning experience. Her grading is very clear and her door is always open for feedback and improvement. If you put in the effort, getting an A in her class is very doable. Her lectures teach you a lot, and she will always support you in and out of the classroom!

Definitely A high school teacher. LOL

The GOAT. Her lectures are exceptionally well-structured, interactive, engaging, and inspiring. The course itself is extremely practical and useful. The workload is very reasonable. Super chill, kind, accessible, and genuinely cares about her students. One of the best professors I've had!

I took this class with Prof. Chiu two years ago. She is truly a great professor and very knowledgable in her field. The content are well organized and engaging, I also find that the coursework greatly helped me in my internship performance afterwards. Take her if you can! You won't regret it.
Her class is engaging. I would say she is the best professor I met this year. She is truly encouraging and supportive. The class content is well organized in a clear manner. Highly recommend.

Professor Cipani is knowledgable and very passionate about his subject. His texts and ideas class was fascinating, and if you pay attention you can get a lot out of it-highly reccomend!! What a great guy and what a great class! Enough Said.

This professor is the best; at first, I was a bit lost since it's not a typical class where you will typically understand the reading at first, which is okay since during your recitation, you and the TA will go over it together and it's going to help. Looooved his class. Really fun recitations and the papers weren't too hard! I liked what we learned too.
enjoyed his class. engaging and informative.

One of the meanest and most confusing professors Ive had here. Very unclear with his feedback and what he wants out of students, and is an unnecessarily tough grader even when he sees students are trying. Demeaning as well. Would NOT take this professor ever again.

Best Italian prof I've ever had! Nicola is very passionate and knowledgable about his subject. Fun classes/discussions, not a lot of work, and you can get by doing only half the reading. Beneficial if you know something about linguistics, but if not, you'll still be fine. Participate in class and he'll love you.
he's one of the best prof I've had from Italian department. Very caring, his class is rather challenging, but really helpful tho. I am in love with him. period.
very clear, helpful and knows his stuff (obviously-he's f.o.b.) ... and i want his babies
great class - the professor was very helpful, concerned and encouraging
Great professor - thorough, challenging, friendly.
excellent instructor. class is fun and very informative
the instructor is a lot of fun and very helpful. highly recommended.

Great teacher! I would definitely reccomend him.  His classes are usually small, and he gets to know his students on a comfortable level.  He is a great guy.  His quizzes are a little tough, but if you study the material and go to class you will do fine.

Nicola made me love to learn Italian. He kept the class engaged, we all loved him and he is a funny guy. One thing you should know: he tends to come to class late, sometimes as late as 30 to 45 minutes. This gets really old after a while, but no one in the
so ****ing funny.  molto buono!
He's pretty funny.  Challenging though, expects a lot out of students.

I love Nicola! He's super fun/funny, not the easiest teacher, but you'll learn a lot and have a good time with it....except on the days when he comes to class in a bad mood...that happens, and then the party's kind of over...but he's awesome

Interesting, but lot of notes and information to keep up on. Genuine person and clearly wants to improve the best that he can, as he looks for feedback after every class. There were only two assignments he gave and harshly grades with no chance of extra credit. There's also lecture questions at the start of each class (all on exam which was easy).

MPAVP-UE - 1152 
Professor Citera is such a genuine person. He will seem a little cringy at first, but then you quickly start to realize that his teaching style really works (at least for most people). There was a lot of work for this class, however, that's simply because it's very important information. His call outs are very helpful for me. LOVE!
Long lectures, and random call on questions at the beginning of each week

The worst psychology class I've ever taken. He explained things fast (although NOT in depth) and therefore tended to overgeneralize. Confusing wordings of exam questions, never encouraged students to think beyond the lectures (or to raise questions). Not willing to have discussions after class, even when he was obliged to. Plus real bad TA.

Solid prof! Concise and digestible slides, zoom vids are posted so you can watch whenever on 2x speed. He posts straightforward review sheets for each exam, and exams have a 3-day period to complete, which is a lifesaver. I didn't find the textbook useful for the exams, but still interesting (and free) to read

His lectures are honestly really boring and dense. When he explains things, he tends to overcomplicate. His tests are easy, once you understand how he writes them. His wording can be confusing. But an A is easily achievable. Loved that it was online. He records every lecture so you can go back to it. Talks super fast though.

I had Professor Cimpian for Intro psych, and given that it was online, I still had a good experience. He lectures are very clear, sometimes a bit fast, so be prepared to take good notes to really help with the exams. He does offer an extra credit opportunity and is always willing to answer questions. Great class, and definitely recommend it.
Class was easy but not interesting. I wish it had been in person.

Great Professor!! He is apparently an extra qualified teacher who I guess have utilized knowledge in cognitive psychology to make the exams the fairest for students. He knows how students can really mess things up if they are nervous and how simply memorizing things is meaningless, and had probably structured his exams to avoid these problems.

LOVED Professor Cimipian for Intro to Psych. Lectures are super clear, interesting, and easy to follow. There are no notes on his slides, so be prepared to take notes. He does go too fast, allows for questions and makes sure everyone is engaged. Literally one of the best professor I have had to far at NYU, never had to worry about  his class.
I took him for Intro to Psych. I would definitely recommend his class. Tests were always fair, and the TAs were great.

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. It is very inspirational to talk to him, as when you say something that you think is correct but is actually silly, he would still treat it as if it is a serious theory but would then propose a little objection which makes you soon realize that it is wrong. Anyway, it is a pleasure to take his course.

Fantastic Professor. When you say something that seems to be correct but is actually silly, Professor Dorr would still treat it as if it is a serious theory, and then propose a little objection that makes you realize you are absolutely wrong. It is very inspirational to talk to him and be taught by him.

knows a lot about his subject, but cannot teach to save his life. Office hours are unhelpful, slides are unhelpful, readings are disconnected from material, extremely not approachable at office hours.
EXTREMELY difficult for philosophy students who don't have much previous knowledge of Math. Don't come

Amazing professor, extremely smart and knowledgeable in his field. Open to questions and gives amazing answers. During office hours you can expect to know a lot more beyond the class materials, which is great for any philosophy majors who want to dig deeper into the topics. Very adorable and friendly.
Confusing and not focused

It's been almost a year since I took Cindy's class and I am so glad I got her early on because not many people know how to teach writing. I had some bad profs since her, so now I can say I appreciate her more now then I did back then. At the time I thought she was giving us too much to do and being too picky; now I know why that was so important.

Teaches by "socratic" method; would have prefered to be taught by her- the person with real world experience. Very nice woman though; cares about students a lot; Her edits on papers were the most helpful thing, although she fell behind on those. Good class to get a overview of the journalistic method.
Take her class! She's awesome.

This was a tough class. Lots of writing and rewriting. I thought I was a good writer and came to realize I have a lot to learn about journalistic writing. But I feel I learned a lot in this class. She made us create blogs and I am happy with the way mine came out. I have a nice portfolio now, which I will build on.

She's tough. The class started out easy and then became harder. Just when I thought I was getting the hang of it, Cindy (she lets her call her by her first name) pushed us to do more. We created cool news blogs and I'm proud of the work I did in the class. Looking back, I'm really glad I took her section. So much better than the other ones.

I love Cindy and her class! She is one of the best professors I've ever had.  The class is a lot of work and the papers can get frustrating, but Cindy is so helpful and accessible.  We've had some great guest speakers and my writing has definitely improved.
I've learned a lot about good writing. It's not a conventional class. Her's is more workshop than lecture which works well because to get better you have to do it, not talk about it.
Vry nice and accomodating.  Not very demanding in terms of quantity but values quality.  Guest speakers ere always pretty interesting and very varied in their experiences.

Had her for Inquiry. She takes some getting used to, since she doesn't really stick to the syllabus, but she's a really nice person. Brought us pizza because she was happy with our rewrites. She's interested in our progress and wants to see us succeed. I like her way of giving us three big stories, instead of one every week.

Professor Rodriguez really worked us hard. Lots of rewriting of our stories, but the assignments were fun and just like she predicted my writing improved 100 percent. She's not like other professors who haven't been in a newsroom in years. She has a ton of experience and it shows in the way she conducts the class.

Eugene was a pretty cool professor. He did give a lot of readings, however they were all really interesting and gave different perspectives on environmental thought. I would definitely recommend taking his class!

Definitely a good man who is passionate about the subject, he just is not very open to others people ideas and does not make it clear what he is looking for in his papers. reviews.comment: Only take him if you are truly interested in learning more about Darwin/ evolution otherwise this class will probably bore you. This class is heavy reading but lectures are low stress. He requires blog posts which are not graded but will hurt your grade if you do not do them. I feel like he was a fair grader and he gave good feedback on essays.

Eugene is a really kind professor. He obviously is knowledgeable about ecological and environmental history. He connects a lot of the material to his own life, which isn't a bad thing. I enjoyed the range of readings he offered and the class atmosphere. While he grades a bit tougher on papers than other professors I've had, he's still fair.

I wish somebody warned me about Professor Cittadino, probably the worst professor I have had at NYU. His lectures were boring, reading assignments were ridiculously long, and the homework were extremely time consuming. He is a strict and tough grader. He will take off points if he doesn't like your idea and does not allow revisions. Do not take!!!
Recommend !

Second time taking MFE III after a bad experience. Prof Chikhany is a savior! Everything ins so clear and manageable. Perfect lectures, only 6 homework assignments and 6 quizzes, midterm and final the same as additional exercises and recitation problems! He is very smart and I love the economic applications he gave. Take him!
MFE II is really well organized, and professor is a great help. The exams are similar to quizzes and homework and recitation worksheets.
I dont know how can he got this score at rmp

Professor Ralph is one of the best math professors I've had in college. His lectures are clear, well-structured, and make even the most abstract concepts much easier to understand. It's obvious that he has a complete mastery of the material and genuinely cares about our learning. The course is challenging but manageable with him!

Fantastic professor. Made me excited to show up to an 8am math class. Made very abstract concepts easy to understand. Workload is very manageable if you stay on top of it and exams are similar to homework and lecture problems.

Take him!! Exams are very similar to homework/quiz/recitation questions. Attending lectures and recitations matters. TAs were great. Lowk disappointed I didn't get an A, but I might've bombed the final. His curve is pretty decent. He's very accessible outside of class and responds to DMs quickly. One of the sweetest professors I've had! Take him!!!
great prof and course is not bad just abstract

I seriously can't recommend this dude enough. He's one of those rare professors who genuinely cares about his jobs and students. This was my second time taking MFE III and the difference in professors made all the difference.

Really knows how to teach.

good prof but the midterms and final are like 70% of your grade alone (and they are so so so hard). he curved all the grades up by one whole letter though so idk but it's a hard class so beware.........
FINAL is way too hard
tuff. wouldnt suggest

reviews.comment: Professor Chikhany teaches with the clarity and care you wish every math professor had. He explains concepts precisely and always offers extra guidance. this diva is sassy... homeworks are difficult, long, hard. exams are brutal but not as bad as mfe1. would study basically every night to tweak about a random integral/matrix. exams are somewhat fair, not always similar to given examples. HOWEVER compared to the rest of the evil present in the math department he is an angel sent from heaven.
hes great. The course materials are tough, thats just how it is. but he explains them super clearly. you get some credits just by doing hw and going to class. tbh best math prof so far.

Exams were unlike HWs, Recitations or Quizzes. Expects you to do just as good as HWs or he will think you are not doing it on your own and using other resources. His lectures are just him doing example questions and the questions on the exams don't look like them either.

Professor Chikhany was awesome for MFE II. He explained everything clearly so it actually made sense, and he's always there to help. His classes are chill but still organized, and he cares a lot about how we're doing. He also gave a generous extra credit quiz after the midterm.

Took MFE2 with him this summer and he is awesome. Great at explaining difficult topics in a simpler manner and gives assignments that match up with the exam content. Really fair and caring---recommend him for any class.
Only 5 HW and 5 Quizzes over the summer with a midterm and a final. His lectures are very clear, and the exams are similar to what is seen in class. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Professor Chikhany for Discrete math. He is very fantastic teacher. His lectures are very clear and easy to understand. HWs and lecture notes are so helpful when reviewing for exams. Best prof in the math department!

Very organized and understandable discrete class. Emphasizes proof-writing ability which may be tricky for many but ultimately useful and rewarding later. Accessible outside of class and appreciates students taking effort, participating, etc. Decently forgiving grading and clear guidelines and grading practices.

MFE 2 had harder material but Chikhany explains/teaches the material in a much more organized and clear way. Tests were similar to examples in class and fair as long as you studied. Didn't have in person office hours but very accessible via Campuswire and responds quick!

Best math professor ever. Very clear and structured lectures and notes. Although the homework may take some time, but his grading is fair. Very organized and clear, and pretty strict. Harsh grading on exams, wish he has in person office hours

Discrete Math is a tough class with a lot of homework but he makes the course manageable. Polished proofs are really annoying as expectations keep getting more demanding. Professor Ralph is available a lot on Campuswire and answers all questions in class. Definitely take his classes!

Chikhany's lectures, organized course and enthusiasm in the classroom prepared me for a lot of future courses. I wish he taught econometrics as well, I am sure I have had a better experience if he did. Chikhany is undoubtedly one of the best professors ever.
Professor Chikhany makes stats a breeze. His clear lectures with relatable examples make the material easy to grasp. unstuckstudy was a game-changer for exam prep - highly recommend!
Great class. Clear and organized lectures with videos to help study. Curves a lot.

reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

This course is really hard but the professor is so caring. The quizzes and the problem sets are also hard. But the exams are nice.

The best math class I've taken at nyu so far. The materials are super structured, and he made his stuff so clear to follow. The summer session really has a tight schedule, but he made me a solid foundation in linear algebra.

FRIENDLY!!!
HE IS THE BEST!!!
I really hope that all of my math classes will be taught by him.

Good class; Professor Chikhany was very understanding, gave clear lectures, and was available to answer questions on Campuswire. The course wasn't too challenging (in my opinion), though it was probably shortened a bit for the summer session.

100% take professor chikhany if you can, he is a fantastic professor. he has no sympathy for his students and complains over the pettiest things. Exams were very difficult and lectures consisted of him doing problems over and over again with barely any explanation. Like we get it, you know how to do it, stop showing us, and actually TEACH us!
difficult to communicate with

Great lectures, explains really well! Also gives lots of resources on Brightspace, information is very organized. Nice guy and replies fast to students' questions on Campuswire. Material was difficult but you can definitely do well with effort.

Linear Algebra is a really hard class but he made it so clear. Attending lecture is important even though the notes have a lot of details. I wish he recorded lectures but a very solid choice, serious but fun class and prof.

I have taken Prof Chikhany for 3 courses and he has, once again, made his class fun, informative, and clear. lectures are well organized and well explained. guidelines are explained clearly. weekly recitations with quizzes, and three exams. this course specifically was curved, but that's not always the case. best best econ math/stats prof. def take him if you can. Everything is super organized, ALWAYS respond to campuswide within 24 hours with very helpful answers. Tests and midterms are super fair- just study hard.
Amazing professor, really clear notes and lectures. Super accessible during and outside of class and makes lectures very fun. Definitely take him!

my favorite Prof at NYU for math. He's organized and caring for every student in his class.

Discrete was amazing with Dr. Chikhany. Lectures were very well organized, even when the material was hard or he made mistakes and fun of himself! He is very enthusiastic and caring. Good lectures and everything is clearly explained, it's just a lot of work with the assignments due every week. Pretty decent class overall.

MFE1 is definitely a lot of work, but as long as you keep up with the work, the exams/class won't be a problem. The class is super structured and Prof. Chikhany is super helpful, definitely go to office hours!
