reviews.comment: He's a caring teacher. He appears to be passively aggressive sometimes but if you ever had office hours with him you know he's a friendly dude. The WebAssign and Gradescope assignments are totally manageable. It's a reasonable amount of workload.

Ralph Chikhany is a great professor. His ability to break-down complex concepts is second to none. But his tests & quizzes are extremely challenging. Even after putting hours to study, complete homework and work on quizzes, I wasn't able to do well on exams as there was never enough time.

workload is heavy. two Psets & a quiz every week. grading is nitpicky and very specific. tests are extremely tough w/no curve & very different from lecture. very conceptual, if you dont think w/numbers, avoid. good teacher & very accessible, but material/grading is more difficult than it needs to be. feels like an 8 unit class, wouldnt take again

Standard math teach. Adheres closely to textbooks. Grading is way too specific, though: docked points if they don't like how your graph looks, if your paragraph-length explanations aren't long/'good' enough, etc. Very accessible.

They assign a significant amount of homework, but more importantly, the quizzes and tests are much more challenging than the homework and you're given little time to complete them. Don't take the class unless you're willing to commit lots of time to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professors at lectures. He gives an absurd amount of workload. His tests are significantly harder than the homework and gives you minimal time to complete them. If you can I would try to avoid this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Chikhany was amazing. There is weekly homework and quizzes but they are very similar to class work. Recorded lectures are detailed and enough to study for the tests. Exams are similar to class. He is funny and tried to make class inclusive by using pronouns and dedicated time to talk about transgender week, no other prof did. A true gem!

The course itself has a lot of work so cannot blame him for the homework and quizzes. He is very caring and is always available to clear doubts. He explains the concepts very well and if you ask him to explain it again he will do so. The midterm was not very difficult if you practice and come, the final was long but not very difficult.

The homework took forever and it seemed like I had never done calculus before (and I usually get high grades in math). Any NYU class giving a final gives 1 hr 50 min to complete it. He decides to shave off 10 min not even 24 hr before. He repeatedly said in class it'd be 1:50, so this caused lots of unnecessary stress. Avoid him at all costs!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You will work VERY hard in this class (I spent a minimum of 5 hrs/week on homework- and that's on an easy week!), but he is SO great at teaching! His lectures are in depth and make sense, the problems he goes over are very useful for hw and exams, office hours are helpful, and he is always open to questions (no matter how dumb you think it is ;)

Professor Chikhany is a good lecturer and can explain ideas very clearly. He is very accessible outside class and willing to answer any questions you have. There are quizzes every week. Those quizzes are not hard but the time limits are very short. Exams are easy if you understand all the ideas in class.

Prof. Chikhany is a great lecturer. He was very accessible outside of class, especially via Campuswire and office hours. My main struggle in this class were the quizzes and large exams (midterm, final). It took me a WHILE getting used to finishing quizzes on time. My advice: BE CAREFUL OF TIME, be a fast test taker in general to pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Harder than expected. Nice professor.

Professor Chikhany is fantastic. He lectures very well and I genuinely learned a lot from his course, even with my astounding hatred for mathematics. His homeworks are long and much more difficult than his lectures or quizzes. Final and midterms are unfortunately the same, with no curves (significant ones, at least) to help. Slow workers, careful!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is super kind, relatable, easily accessible outside of class and made my first remote semester very easy. Lectures and course are insanely organized. I really can't think of anything negative... except if you don't want to work hard, then don't take his class. I think I learned a lot, not only math wise, but also about how to succeed in college.
Amazing professor, guide me through MFE1. Accessible outside of class, reply to every message I sent him on CampusWire. Also he lets you drop 3 lowest quizzes, hw, very generous. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I worked very hard on quizzes and homework and got A for both sections, but the midterm and final are incomparably difficult to what he gave for quizzes and homework. It's especially unrealistic to do so much work in a limited time. He does give great lectures, but they won't save you from a failing final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Chikhany gives great lectures, and he really cares about students!!! I got an A on midterm but not sure about the final. Just take his class. The lectures are so clear.

Prof. Chikhany is admittedly scattershot: sometimes the class feels unprepared, and the recitations sometimes conflict the lectures. But hes super nice, caring, frequently funny during class, and is a natural lecturer. Getting an A requires some work, but if you do the homeworks and quizzes youll be fine.
Professor Chikhany is a great person and professor. Although the workload may be challenging, he tries to help as best as he can. If you get the chance of taking him, take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is super diligent and nice. He is always funny and also very helpful in any time! Of course there are lots of homework but I ask the other class and they have the same amount of HW as us. HE IS A REAL GEM . Straightforward, do actually help the students instead of giving vague answer. And also a fair grader ! If u study, tests are doable.
Nice professor for MFE I. Clear lectures, engaging materials. Accessible and friendly. Word hard and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The best professor in NYU. I love his class! It's so clear and well-organized. And he is kind and helpful. Homework is easy and sometimes challenging. I definitely recommend his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Chikhany is one of the best math teachers I've ever had. Work can be tough, but it is manageable if you pay attention in class and ask questions whenever you can. Very accessible outside of class, always answering questions on Campuswire, cares about every student and wants them to succeed. Highly recommended if you're willing to work!
Unreal teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His explanations are very clear - especially his asynchronous lectures - and he's always available to answer questions, he won't give you the answers but will point you in the right direction. He uses technology well and has adapted well to an online mode of teaching. The homework is time-taking but good practice. I would definitely recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Practice is essential to Math learners, and I think the weekly homework is important also. Keep up his pace and you will be fine.

Prof. Chikhany is a great guy. Lectures and materials are clearly organized. Class contents are well explained. He responses to every question on campuswire. Dropping policies are very generous. Highly recommended.

Professor Chikhany is a nice guy. However, the material is really hard, and his tests are difficult. He gives out tough homework assignments every week, and he's a fairly strict grader. Overall, he's a great person who cares about his students, but I hope he will be nicer to his future students.
Dr. Chikhany is a well-guiding professor and would take his classes again. He is very helpful with interesting homework that make you think beyond the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a great professor. Very guiding and would surely take one of his classes again. He is responsive, he makes you work for it, something that I appreciated as this is a math class--and not a history, politics or same kind of class that you only learn things by heart. He has a fixed schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think Dr. Chikhany is a great professor and is always very quick to respond. His responses can be vague, but he usually points you in the right direction. The class is tough with one of the weekly homeworks taking a very long time to complete (usually several hours), but it is nice to have a weekly schedule that you can rely and plan on.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Incredibly difficult class. Professor is a nice guy, but I wouldn't take his class ever again. The homework assignments, due every week, were incredibly time consuming and so different as to not be related to the course videos themselves. Choose another professor or test out. Don't take his class unless you want to stain your textbook with tears.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Chikany is a great and caring person but I definitely would not take his class again. The course is heavily application based and even though I took calculus already, I felt very underprepared. The class is very time consuming as well. Dr. Chikany is very considerate, though, and will help you throughout the course.

The class is very engaging but Prof Chikhany made it so organized and easy to follow. His video lectures are very clear and funny and he is always taking feedback in consideration. He always answers questions on Campuswire too. I highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Chikhany seems like a great guy, but he treated our class like a "guinea pig" class: it's clear he figures things out as he goes long. He gave us a quiz that almost everyone failed so he had to offer a retake (so not everyone would get a 2/10). He only has one midterm and it counts for a lot which also sucks. He's pretty engaging, though.
Amazing professor, extremely passionate and cares deeply about her student's success
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My god if only I knew what I was getting myself into! The class was overall fine, but the reading is quite hefty! The readings averaged around 300-400 pages a week, missed my Halloween. The reading is long and a bit boring with occasional times piquing my interests. The writing is fine and fun because you can choose your topics.
changed my life, let her change yours
idk about understanding, but she's definitely a person who teaches a class about writing

The semester started off rocky because the workload was difficult for the class to keep up with. But once she could tell that was happening, she cut it all in more than half. She was sweet and understanding throughout the semester, and was passionate about nurturing her students as writers. I honestly couldn't have asked for a better professor.
Great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Read the book. Don't leave your essays till the day before. And engage in the Proust. Marcelle genuinely cares about your learning, but also about you. She'll read every word you put up on the blog, and rewards you for your hard work. Writing essays on Proust is hard, but your motivation should be the fact that you don't want to disappoint her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She is extremely helpful. But read the book, for god's sake.
This semester is not over yet but I just wanna say that Marcelle is amazing. She could be extremely helpful if you follow all her instructions and read the book.

If you love to read and write, TAKE HER CLASS. She is amazing in every way; amazing feedback, involved and passionate about what she teaches, interested in your growth as a student, and a very very fair grader (there's no reason you shouldn't be getting an A with her guidance if you use her resources to your advantage.)

This year (2013-14) Marcelle was voted one of the best professors in CAS. There is no doubt in my mind that she deserved it. Proust is hard to read, especially for college freshmen, but Marcelle makes it worth it. Come to class, participate (both in class and online), and for the love of god, do the reading, and this class will be rewarding.
I am a creative writing minor, and if I could I would take all four of my classes with Marcelle. She is passionate and amazing. TAKE HER! no two ways about it.

Marcelle is FANTASTIC. She is completely dedicated to helping every student improve his/her writing, and she gives her students lots of individual attention. I learned SO MUCH from her--you have a write and read a lot, but it's totally worth it. She will without a doubt make you a better writer. She is definitely the CWP's best kept secret.

I loved taking a class with Marcelle. She is so friendly and warm and she really makes you write a lot so you get better. I didn't even see my progress till she showed it to me! She is really good! Takeee her!

Absolutely the best creative writing teacher I have had at NYU. If you can take her fiction class--or any class that she teaches, for that matter--take it. She completely cares about her students and makes that clear every day.

Marcelle is the best ever. She is such a great teacher and such a hilarious person; so smart, so sweet, so fun to be around. Take anything she teaches. I'd take computer science if she taught it. I love her.
there are a few people in a lifetime that have a dramatic impact on who you become as a person. Marcelle has the potential to be one of those few.
Interesting, passionate, old-world writer.  I want to be her.
Marcelle makes great snacks and likes to invite students to her home.  She also knows a lot about Proust and has all sorts of older lady class.
Take other courses if you want to learn industrial skills.

Prof. Clayton was wonderful! He gives really good lectures and engages students with the material very well. His homeworks are very helpful for learning and fun to do even though some of them can be a bit long. He allows cheatsheets on all exams, and everything comes from his lectures.

Professor Clayton was very kind and knowledgeable. The class consists of lectures where you watch videos beforehand and workshops where you work on coding project. The midterm and final are harder than you'd expect- the final especially was a lot harder and ruined my A in the class so beware. Besides that, very great class, I highly recommend!
prof clayton is a great professor. exams are fairly simple if you learn the class material & use the practice materials. i learned a lot and it was a fun class! def recommend if you need to take ICP.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Clear guidelines and easy tests like the practice exam.
Clayton's class is really easy.  But he's still entertaining and a good guy.

Love this professor! He is super friendly, explains the material well, and is open to helping students. Midterm and final are a bit tougher than you might expect, so study well. Otherwise, the class is pretty easy since he drops lowest homework, quiz grade, and will weigh the final more if you do better on that than the midterm.

Very enthusiastic professor with engaging lectures. All of the homework had very clear grading criteria and never too time consuming. The midterm and final were very straightforward and open note. Highly recommend this professor.
Easy exams and easy A if you don't cheat in homework. Nice professor.

This class requires you to understand coding so be ready to study by yourself. Lectures go through really fast and hard to catch up every single words he said. Homework videos are not enough for study the material because they missed many details you need to know. However the NYU's learning website and its YouTube videos can be really helpful.
Nice guy, but everything is really slow.  Anyone can skip this course with a couple weekends of self-study.

Very caring and dedicated prof. Teaches really well but exams (pen & paper) make up 60% and these exams are out of 40 or 45 and brought up to 100, which means that the % you get will always seem considerably lower than your performance, demotivating. Course seems easy but picks up quick. No curves or round ups, your final grade is your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy. Explains things super clearly and wants everyone to succeed. Weekly homework assignments but they really do help with learning the content. I went in to CS101 feeling super prepared.
Super nice and patient.

The assignments were doable but were time consuming, but the exams were harder than the practice problems he gave us. He told us the midterm review problems would be a bit more challenging than the actual midterm itself, but the midterm turned out to be harder, as did the final.
Great professor. Workload can be handled, as there's only one homework per week or two weeks. Professor is always accessible by email. Learn a lot of fun techniques about web using Js

Take Prof Clayton!! Weekly learning modules/online quizzes plus his lectures were both helpful and organized. Assignments were straightforward but took hours each week to do if you get stuck. Midterm was harder than he said it would be which brought down my grade... but besides that he was a great teacher!!! Super nice and always excited to there.

Good professor. Him and his assistant were always accessible. If you do the learning modules and know how to do the assignments without cheating you'll be good. Just make sure to proof check your code for any sort of errors. The midterm and final weren't very hard if you know how to do the assignments.

I took Intro to Programming with Professor Clayton, he is an awesome professor. His lectures were well-organized and helpful. The assignments are engaging and not hard to do. He is helpful both inside and outside of class. Taking his course with him helped me build a solid foundation for my further study in CS. Really appreciated his teaching.

1. The midterm is not easy, instead, it is hard
2. He teach. He is a good teacher and everything in his class is meaningful
3. If you finish the assignment by yourself and do the module and quiz every time. A- at least can be guaranteed.
You are dedicated, you get the grade. I love him very much! Overall a good teacher!

Excellent professor. Lectures are well-designed & taught, and homework assignments & quizzes are beyond manageable. Certainly understanding and respectable. Exams may be a bit more difficult than expected, but if you want to take an introductory-level course for programming, he is definitely the person to choose.

Amazing professor. He gives great feedback and is very available outside of class. If you do the learning modules you'll be mostly set, so missing a class or two isn't the end of the world. Coding assignments take at least 3 or 4 hours to complete, but are pretty fun and help with the concepts tremendously.
Great professor who cares and accommodates for his students. Keeps lectures engaging and motivational. Just be wary of midterm and final and you'll have a great semester.

Professor Clayton is very knowledgeable and encouraging. He inspired us with useful examples and encouraged us to create things out of our own interests by applying knowledge in class. The class is arranged with care, and every project leaves us a huge space to create and practice. There was only one exam, and it was not that hard.

Intro to Programming was one of my favorite courses and was really fun! Professor Clayton makes the lectures very clear and is available to answer any questions. There were weekly workshops that allowed us to start the homework in groups, and the assignments were helpful and engaging. I recommend starting homework early and attending exam review.

I took Professor Clayton's Drawing on the Web class. I really learned a lot about the potential of web pages, like using them as a place holder for 3D models. I actually got a research assistant job because of this class. Professor Clayton is definitely very knowledgeable in his field. He is also one of my favorite professors in the cs department!

super nice dude. its kinda annoying how we have an assignment each week without any grace days or having one of them dropped at the end of the semester because they do pile up. also, the tests were HARD. like, study all u want but like there will be questions you've never heard of/seen before.

As long as you read the modules before class, you will be able to understand the concepts. However, his exam questions aim to confuse you rather than to test understanding. All exam questions are marked on a right or wrong basis, no opportunity for you to show your work. I came out of this class knowing how to code, but the tests do not reflect it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Hated the homework. The midterm was fine. The final exam felt very unfair.

Dont let the negative reviews stop you from taking Clayton. He is my favorite of all CS professors Ive had. Failed my final (somewere in 50s or 60s) and still managed to end with an A-. That goes to show how accommodating he is. Work hard, have fun, take him! And Clayton, please teach higher level CS courses I BEG YOU!!!

overall great professor, but very hard final/midterm (no curve, completely unrealistic time limit) especially for a "no prior experience" class. weekly coding assignments were pretty time consuming but really helpful

This semester was virtual, so I didn't attend many classes, but his notes were so well written it didn't matter! The weekly homework assignments include hours worth of various programs, but they were manageable as long as you start them ahead instead of the night before. Gives practice questions before midterm that was similar to it. Great course!

Such a nice professor. I honestly thought I was going to fail the class because of how time-consuming the assignments were but ended up passing. His midterm was fair. His final was hard because of the time limit the amount of questions, but overall the class was worth it.
Awesome guy

Weekly coding assignments that take 3-5 hours to complete. Grading for homework is a bit tough as you get deducted points for minor errors. Midterm is easy but final was much harder. A lot of self studying from modules before class and lectures are brief summaries of what was covered in the pre-lecture module videos/articles. Prof is nice though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Professor! His lectures are extremely clear, organized, and easy to follow. He is always happy to clarify any doubts and seems to be a nice person. His weekly homework was quite time-consuming and the final exam was not easy by any means. That said, you should certainly take him, you won't regret it!
He's the nicest guy ever, and made the material clear and easy to understand.
He's just so great. Made web design so much more approachable and he cares so much about providing an engaging class environment. Can't reccomend him enough.

He's such a nice guy, makes the lectures really fun which is hard to do when teaching coding. This dude will brighten ur day everytime you see him. 100% recommend even for non-compsci majors his class is fun, interesting, and useful too.

Honest Review: Good:Clayton and the class are stellar, I'll leave that to other reviews Bad:Exams Really hard, not enough practice material AT ALL Keep in mind:Missed assignments  Lots of points off Advice:Do EVERY assignment, watch every lecture, do every quiz. Points from these will save you from what feels like an exam you can't prepare for

Love professor Clayton - generous in personality and help and accommodating of all learning needs. The lectures for Web Dev are a delight as each lesson features relevant, exciting content that can be immediately applied. Clayton is knowledgeable of the most recent web dev trends and teaches a strong intro level class.

Intro to web design with clayton got me more interested in pursuing web development. It's a great entry point and he really exposes you to more creative applications of programming. Well-organized and 50% of your grade is based on homework and a final project which is nice. Two lectures a week, one of which was asynchronous.
Very clear, very cool guy. Loves to teach and makes everything so simple.
Prof. Clayton is honestly the best professor I've ever had at NYU. He's very accessible outside the classroom, and he's very clear and understanding when teaching. I loved being in his class!

He is the best professor I have ever had in my whole life. He is so accessible, nice, knowledgeable, well-organized, and clear!! He always has a smile on his face. He made me fall in love with programming. As long as you put effort in it, you will get an A.
Midterm and Final are worth 60% in total, and theyre sorta difficult if you don't pay attention in lectures. Assignments are fairly straightforward and Prof Clayton is a realy nice guy. Reccomend him

Great guy. Class is difficult though for those who have never coded before. A lot of learning is on your own. A lot of information can hit you at once. Definitely need to put in hours outside of class to understand the information. Does not give extra credit. Does not curve. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. Most of the learning is on your own; he assigns weekly online modules to read, which you take mini quizzes on at home (easy), and writing your own programs based on the modules (a bit challenging). He has tutors in class to help you and he is accessible outside of class. Tests are very straightforward. Great class overall!

He's very caring, makes things clear and understandable, and always willing to help. Weekly assignments, but not too bad however he is very nit picky in grading so do everything exactly as it should be done. Test are relatively fair and gives you study guide beforehand. Definitley an excellent teacher! Highly reccomend!

Prof. Clayton is easily one of the best professors I've ever had in NYU. Not only is he a great person, he is also a wonderful teacher who explains all relevant concepts with helpful examples and lectures. In addition to that, he is also very accessible outside the classroom. Would highly recommend.
Fantastic professor. Very organized and clear teaching style. Very approachable and knowledgeable guy. I would recommend anyone take this class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Clayton outlines the goals of the class clearly from day one. He is a fair grader and as long as you communicate he may give an extension. He does put slides online but it is very important to go to class to see the examples he does.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Always a wonderful professor. He will take the time out to explain things to you if you express that youre confused about something. Very approachable. Hes my favorite professor at NYU.
One of the best professor I've ever met in NYU. Clear lectures and approachable.

Took him for Web Design for my minor. I absolutely love him. His grading policy is very clear cut. He gave extra credit on each assignment after the midterm. The exams are quite easy, as long as you study, you will be fine. He is very reachable and understanding. He'll give you tips on any outside projects you have going on. Taking him next sem too
The nicest guy! Really love the way he teaches. Really learned a lot from his class. Definitely gonna take him again.

Had him for intro to computer programming, and loved him and the class. Very approachable, and willing to help over email of in his office. Prepares you for the exams with review sessions and many practice problems. Take him even if you know  no programming, its actually fun.
Joshua is very helpful and clear. Got an A without much trouble. Do your homework once he assigns them so the info from the lecture is still fresh in your mind, either that or during class.

Very clear lectures, and goes through information several times to make sure everyone understands. Homework is super easy. Midterm was all multiple choice. Definitely not difficult to get an A in this class if you have even the slightest knowledge of web design.

Professor Clayton is the one professor you need to take at least once while at NYU. His lectures are extremely clear and he's always willing to help. He's also pretty funny which is nice during lectures.

FANTASTIC. I went to every lecture not because I had to, but because I wanted to. Granted, I was very interested in programming before this class, but his teaching only strengthened my interest. His teaching is so clear and he is mindful that not everyone has programming experience. He also posts class notes online to refer back to. Take him!
GREAT PROFESSOR

He is literally one of the nicest professors I have ever had. So helpful and always available to make sure you understand something. Tests are also pretty easy and straightforward. No tricks. The class is a gentle intro to programming and as a person with ZERO experience whatsoever, I loved it. :)
Really great easy Professor.
So helpful and nice! Take him!!!
Extremely helpful, very nice, and generally a great professor overall. Would kill to take his class again.
This guy can teach like a boss.  He is really comprehensive, but takes the time to thoroughly go through his reasoning.

Clayton is awesome! He makes the class very interesting and fun. He's an extremely nice guy, very helpful in class and over email, and goes through everything at a good pace. It's not much work and the exams are straightforward. The class is an easy A. I highly recommend him; he's an excellent professor and a terrific person.

For a writing class, there was way too much reading. He was really sweet and genuinely cared about his students, but we didn't get much practice writing. There were only 2 writing projects the entire semester (one being the final, which he didn't even grade). The class environment was nice, but not the best professor for writing.
Super chill!! Great and laid-back professor. Lots of reading, and every class is entirely discussion-based. You will not learn a lot, but it is an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is nice & funny, but cold calls constantly, which gets annoying and makes me anxious. If you dont do the readings you will sound stupid when he calls on you. He assigns way too much reading, sometimes multiple at once, often over 25 pages, so the workload gets hectic. Also the readings just don't make sense half of the time, doesn't explain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Wills! He is funny and caring, and he makes the class very insightful and interesting. He is very understanding of outside circumstances and understands the efforts that students take. He sparked a new interest in the subject of Public Health for me!

Definitely not a difficult professor if you're just looking for a good grade, He's nice, and offers availability. However, his class will not teach you very much, both with feedback on papers, and just day-to-day in classes. Every class is pretty much just reading aloud a reading.
Dr. Wills is the best. He is so funny and caring. He is a light grader and takes into account any issues you may have. He always provides help and is awesome.

Dr. Wills is a very sweet and nice professor who cares about his students. However, I wish that care also went into the course content. The classes were very boring and even though it is a writing seminar don't expect to learn anything about writing. I don't know why I put effort into the papers the grade was based just on grammar and spelling.
Can't understand
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really like him! He's very smart but very VERY intimidating and pretty impatient when he thinks you're d*mb. You just have to soldier through because the ideas he presents are very valuable and he cares a lot about what he teaches.

The class itself is interesting, but as a professor, he tends to play favorites and is rather blunt against students at times. The grading criteria feels all over the place, especially as it doesn't seem as if there were plans for the finals/major assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The content of this class is relevant and stimulating. The way it is taught is a different story. Clementi is a kind person, but he struggles to present material clearly, which makes lectures confusing. There is also no room for challenging his way of thinking. Finally, the grading criteria are unclear, with little transparency about expectations.

reviews.comment: If I were a fish, I would describe myself as British Fish and Chips (so fried). I can't focus because of his heavy accent. This amazing professor also likes to talk about random things that come to mind, even if they have nothing to do with the final exam. Please RUN!

literally the worst class I have ever taken at stern. be prepared to work every week doing work that is useless to education and learning anything about economics other than letting him take half of the week off

Never published the syllabus after changing it, assigns extremely long readings, and randomly pivots in topics. Still have not received a final grade, and it's spring sem already.

unpopular opinion he wasn't that bad!!! yes the final exam had little to nothing to do with his lectures but some concepts we learned in class were applicable to understanding the reading on the exam. he can be intense but just don't ask dumb questions to make yourself look smarter and it'll be fine

The lectures themselves are interesting, but he goes off on tangents on topics that arent relevant at all to the class. The tests are not related to any of the course material, and are impossible to study for. Participation is almost impossible to do well in. Not a mean person, just an atrocious teacher.

His lectures felt like some kind of fever dream. Changed the syllabus halfway through the semester. Final exam had absolutely nothing to do with in-class content or readings. Gave absolutely no information about the grading criteria or structure of the final. His classes are interesting, to say the least.

I don't really know what to say. He's nice but his exams have nothing to do with the content he teaches. His debates are so convoluted and he will start arguing with you mid-sentence. He knows what he wants he just won't tell you what it is. He's a sweet guy but be warned. Good luck BPEers.

Honestly not a bad prof, just has a bad temper sometimes but he explains the concepts in a relatively clear manner and can sometimes be nice

Very difficult and stressful class as the lectures didn't align well with homework or tests. chill guy, encourages students to ask questions and get help, but the content seems way harder than it needs to be. very lecture heavy. the weekly homework takes several hours to get through, and some of the questions are unclear and unnecessarily difficult. the exam is formatted similar to the HW.

reviews.comment: This class made me hate waking up. Everyday, he drones on and on at 930 am and gets pissed if you ask any dumb question. Zero effort in making things understandable, just trying to flex his intellectual superiority in concepts that will never matter. Homeworks are stupidly long, and the Stern curve makes the midterm and final your entire grade.

Would give a 0 if possible. He teaches too quickly, gets annoyed at students who ask clarifying questions, and makes exams/HW extremely hard. TLDR: AVOID HIM.

Quite possibly one of the worst professors I've ever seen. He's not a bad person but he cannot teach if his life depended on it and the tests are based on what he teaches. Lectures are useless and half of us are fighting not to fall asleep. Speaking of halves, half the auditorium is empty bc so many people dropped after the first midterm. HW seems alright bc he lets us do it in groups, but we've sat in the 3rd floor stern room for over five hours losing our minds over externalities and absurd numbers, its insane.

Buddy straight-up sucks at teaching. Couldn't find a textbook that was an appropriate level for the course so just gave us 3 and uses a mix like that makes any sense at all. Lectures don't really help. Homeworks take hours to complete even in groups. Averages on tests are abysmal and most kids withdraw from the class. Turned an intro to Econ class into an extremely theoretical and math-heavy PhD-level economics course.

Clementi's lectures go fast and can be hard to understand, but it is reasonable given the amount of content he has to cover. The first week of lectures and homework are the hardest so don't be too afraid if the material seems overwhelming at first. Definitely a significant weekly time commitment. There is a lot of coursework, there are also pop quizzes and exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Really awesome professor. Keeps everyone engaged during class time, and offers great out of class support. Mindtap / Brightspace Homework for each class, but wasn't difficult. Exams were tough, but as long as you study, you'll be fine. She also gives comprehensive study guides to help you! Definitely recommend!!
Love her! Aside from being so sweet and understanding, she has great taste in literature :) Love the Spanish department at NYU, and she's a fantastic part of it!

So understanding and kind! There's a lot of homework in the class but you'll get to learn a lot. Just participate in class and she'll like you. It's a fun class and an easy A if you do the homework and talk.

Claudia is genuinely one of the nicest professors I've ever had at NYU. You can tell that she's really passionate about teaching and she is pretty clear with her material. There is a fair amount of work for a 6 credit class and the pacing is not too fast. She is very understanding and tries hard to make sure you understand everything.

Claudia is so wonderful. She constantly made our whole class laugh, and before anything, she wanted us to be good friends, learn and have fun. All assignments in Intermediate Spanish I were easy, straightforward and she always had a rubric and clear grading criteria. Online workbook is decent too. Having a Cuban Spanish prof. is the best.

Claudia is absolutely one of the best professors at NYU. It is so clear that she genuinely cares about teaching and her students. It's a 6-credit course and there's a fair amount of work but she makes it as enjoyable as it can be and makes sure you understand. She is so understanding and I wish she taught more classes. 10/10 pls take her class.

I took Claudia for SPAN-UA 10 and SPAN-UA 20. She has by far been my favorite professor at NYU. She genuinely cares about all her students. She will make sure you do well in her class as long as you try. She takes time to make sure everything is clear.  She does a great job at explaining concepts and keeping a good pace. PLS TAKE HER!!!

I usually like to focus on the positive things when writing these reviews but like some other reviews, he is unfortunately not a good lecturer. He does ramble a lot and it is quite hard to keep up in order to take notes. He is very knowledgeable by all means, just wish he would switch up his lecture style for the future.

He's so difficult to understand it's like each class is a competition for him to see how much jargon he could pack into it. His slides are literally blank except for poorly labeled diagrams. Had him for PSYCH UA 25, cogneuro, hes clearly really passionate about what he teaches, but shouldnt teach. he goes on rambles and his slides are only pictures. 2/10 run

Good professor, but don't take this course if you don't care about cognitive neuro and just want to fill the requirement. Boring af

You could succeed if you pay attention to classes, but I will steer away from this course unless you're good at memorization.

I wouldn't take this class again if Clayton taught it. The material is extremely interesting but he is not a good professor. The slides are difficult to follow. His exam questions are tricky or ask minute details that were not stressed. If you take his class, memorize the slides from the TA reviews on the first 2 exams. There is no 3rd review.
Nice guy but grade too harshly. Curving, yes, but it barely improves your grade. Whether you want to learn something real or just get credits, he is not the professor you want.

Ridiculous class and ridiculous professor. Nice guy, but is not accessible outside of class at all, and neither are the TAs. He seems plenty competent in cog neuro but he's not the best teacher. His slide decks are some of the worst I've seen, mostly just pictures and random text. You don't need to read the textbook to succeed or be premed. Go to the TA reviews, they saved my life. If you're good at memorizing info the class is easy.

Very unforgiving professor, not accessible outside of class whatsoever. TAs also had no idea what was going on making it hard to do well in the class. unless you absolutely have to do not take his class

TAs very helpful, utilize them for the paper!

So if you're not enthusiastic about this area or confident with your ability, think twice.

reviews.comment: Curtis was a great professor! Although, his voice is monotonous he does crack jokes here and there to keep everyone engaged. The lectures were always very interesting and you need to go for note taking because the slides don't explain everything. There was one small paper and 3 quizzes (drops lowest) and a final. Not an easy A, but you can get one.

Cogneuro is a difficult subject, especially because most people taking the class have very little experience with the topic aside from Intro Psych, and even that doesn't really prepare u unless u were really paying attention during the brain biology part. But you'll be fine as long as u study to learn the basics. Curtis is a good prof & is helpful

No need to ever read the book -- the PDF's online anyways, btw. Make sure to be on top of the 1 paper. Know every author of every recitation paper, every researcher in every study, and the differences between each. GO TO LECTURE or seriously, don't take the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is very friendly and an interesting guy. reviews.comment: THE WORST
Not only is he the rudest professor I have ever dealt with, his class is unnecessarily difficult and he refuses to be of any help.

Prof. Curtis is a pretty smart guy, but his tests are tough and literature critiques are hard. In the test he also includes some details in the textbook which you have to pay attention to. If you are not really enthusiastic about this field you might consider taking someone else.
THE WORST. TESTS ON IRRELEVANT DETAILS. AVOID HIM, TAKE PASCAL. TURN BACK WHILE YOU STILL CAN!!

The textbook is useless and only supplements some lectures. Clay's lectures are extremely long, loaded with information and he is extremely repetitive. He often goes off on tangents and you end up typing the same information again and again. You have to record lectures unless you can write down everything he says. This class is a ton of work.

Brilliant guy, but possibly the worst professor ever. He goes off on useless tangents, claims his tests are based off only the "broad concepts" and then goes onto ask specific, minute details. It's not fair how difficult his class is considering the other cogneuro professor gives open book tests and an optional final. TLDR: Avoid him!

Curtis is a kind, funny, and knowledgable guy, unfortunately, as a freshman with little background in biology, CogNeuro was extremely difficult. The lectures were long and information packed, and although he is a pleasant lecturer, I felt like I couldn't space out for a second without missing a ton of information. Good class for memorizers

His lectures were pretty loaded with information, and although he definitely knows a lot about his field and knows what he's talking about, he's not very good at explaining coherently. I appreciated his funky humor, and he's very nice, but that's not really enough. You're basically on your own in this class, but if you work hard, you can get an A.

Just focus on what you learn from lecture and recitation. The book is completely useless. And make sure you understand the research articles well. He's an excellent lecturer and explains concepts very well. Very nice guy too. The literature critique is a little tough, but it's important. TAs were also excellent and laid back.

Attend his lectures; Bring a recorder with you. His tests are solely based on lecture material. Don't bother with the textbook (a poorly written one btw) Overall, a very good course to take with a very good professor. The T.A's are very helpful and the articles you need to read for recitations are probably the more challenging part of the course.

Take his course! His tests are really straightforward! Focus on his lectures and powerpoints for studying, NOT the textbook! He is a fair grader and a great lecturer! Be sure to attend class every time because his tests are based on his lectures!

This class is hard and you must put in a lot of work and time but if you try your best you should be okay. Go to lecture!!! Its a must! You may read the textbook to clarify things but the textbook is not really necessary. My TA was awesome, the professor is funny, nice, helpful, and loves neuroscience! Just be prepared to work hard!

He's a really nice guy and can be funny at times. His lectures are very informative so go to his lectures! The topics are very interesting. The T.A.'s are great! Recitation articles are interesting and helpful! Focus on his lecture notes when studying for his tests. Tests are very understandable with no tricks and grading is very fair. Take this!

Although this is a very challenging class, I learned an incredible amount of information that helps me in every psych class I've taken since. Professor Curtis is so nice and funny and his lectures are very helpful. Worth taking if you're willing to learn and listen.

The book is nice to have but you will not be tested on anything in the book that he does not discuss in class. The tests are not hard if you study for them. The TA's grading can be subjective on the essay part of the "quizzes" so make sure you fight for the points if u deserve them. Overall a great class !

I expected this to be a difficult class and it lived up to that expectation. You MUST attend every class and take excellent notes--that's what the tests are based on. I found the paper difficult-but doable, just start early and consult your TA often on it. Professor Curtis does a pretty good job making this class survivable.

Clay teaches the most wonderful aspect of the psych discipline, and you will learn A LOT. While not the easiest of the cores, I highly recommend it for the value of the class. You will learn how to really understand current research papers--a rare omission from 99% of undergrad classes. Side note: you will never be tested on the textbook.

Clayton is the man.  I was hesitant because of the comments on here, but had him this past semester and learned a ton of interesting material.  He's a great lecturer and I actually looked forward to class.  The readings are pretty peripheral and the tests are straight-up fair.  Just be sure to put the effort forth and his class will be rewarding.
WARNING TO NYU STUDENTS: AVOID AT ALLLL COSTS.

Hard and not in the "but I learned a lot" way. He expects you to know all about the topic before you take his intro to cogneuro course. Also, if I ever hear the phrase "frontal eye fields" again, I will scream. You will learn more about the most boring aspects of the discipline than you thought possible. Did I mention that the tests are impossible?

Classes were clear and interesting, however textbook sucked (glossed over complex lingo and said, "we'll discuss what this actually means in chapter 17"). Also, grading was inconsistent and hard, but that had more to do with TAs than prof Curtis. I could never be mad at his cute, bald, Texan self.
very hot, well spoken, knows what he is talking about, a pioneer in his field at a relatively young age.
he dresses very well i must say
he was a good teacher but he is very hard!! i think the tests are difficult!!

I loved this class!! for a nonscience person i thought it was great! the classes were all on power point and the quizes werent too bad, and you get to drop one of the three. The articles for RCT are kind of hard but you dont really need to know them for the test, just the basic idea of them, The paper was difficult but do-able. Loved this class.
No Comments
This was a great class and the prof was cool.  He made the class challenging but overall it was fair.  Made me switch from wanting to go to med school to grad school (well, at least for now).

I took cog neuro fall 2004. I thought it was an alright course. He is pretty funny, he has the notes on power point, and there are articles to read and go over in resitation. Over all I think he was a good professor and taught clearly, with out any overload of assignments.

Very Subjective.She favors certain game genres, and when uninterested, her feedback often focuses on criticism with a dismissive tone, rather than constructive suggestions. 

In our case, she only engaged with 20% of our work before giving a negative evaluation. Although we responded to clarify her questions, she didn't seem open to discussion.
Worst professor ever .
Extremely subjective grader. No grading criteria. If you have any other choice, don't take her course.
Clara is a tough grader but you'll be fine if you try your best. As an Asian, I had Clara for two courses but never felt discriminated. She was very nice(at least to me) and I got pretty good grades.

She is very flattering to native English speakers and very discriminating against Asians.
If you're an Asian, run! Never take her class! She gave all Asians really low marks.
The specific way she discriminates is: ignore.
You will feel very disrespected in her class.

Clara's a tough grader but she knows the specific parameters she wants students to adhere to, and gives clear concise feedback that genuinely helps improve the games you're making. She's accessible outside of class and is genuinely passionate about what she teaches.
Subjective Tough Grader

One of my least favorite professors I've had. Her class is not particularly difficult so I won't say you absolutely shouldn't take it but I do not like her as a person and her feedback was often phrased in a rude way. (and if *I* think she's rude you know it's bad...)

I loved her classes. I felt challenged but pushed beneficially. Content was inspirational and so relevant. Her input and knowledge are so worthwhile. Even if it is a high effort, time-consuming course, I would take it again.

de Obaldia is certainly versed and intelligent. However, she is not a very good professor, and her feedback is more times than not directionless. Her paper prompts are also either completely uninteresting or asinine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: GET READY TO READ!! Will read a lot in this class she comes in class expecting all readings to be completed prior and will drill hard on the reading content. She grades very hard, so if you want to challenge your writing skills, feel free to take the class, but she will give honest (sometimes even rude) feedback on your paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you show up to class, do the readings, participate, and submit the homework on time, you will be golden. Genuinely cares about student's progress and lives and doesn't take BS. Super smart and well-read and really knows what she's talking about. Dr. Obaldia will only have an issue with you if you are a bad student.

French and Expatriate Literature -- Dr. de Obaldia is a sarcastic bully who gaslit me into thinking I couldn't write papers. Several other students noticed that her behavior towards me differed from the rest of the class. Her feedback was limited and unhelpful. Quel dommage !
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Had her for Writing the Essay and the content itself was boring and Obaldia was well aware. This teacher is sarcastic and her presence is intimidating (though her intentions are good). Feedback can be vague sometimes, and sometimes it's hard to understand how to improve my work. essay prompts give you lots of freedom to choose what to write about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had her for EXPOS-UA 9001. She's a very sweet woman, cares about her students + appreciates perspectives/ideas of all kinds. Sometimes the content during class was unnecessary/didn't help develop my essay. Pretty tough grader, but she def is accessible & provides helpful feedback, so if use what's available + ask questions, you'll be okay for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think Prof. de Obaldia's teaching style is not for everyone. She is a really tough grader but if she sees that you put the effort into the class you should be fine. Really go to her after class or during office hours to see what the prompts really mean because they can be hard to understand what she wants you to write about.
just dont. save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment:
She is HANDS DOWN the best Spanish teacher I've ever had, both at NYU and throughout my life. There is clearly a reason why she is the director of the intensive Spanish courses. If you have the ability to take her, do it.

Sincerely, 
Someone who has taken Spanish since 7th grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Look, you are taking intensive spanish, its going to be hard, but she brings her dog to class, is very kind, goes over stuff that dosnt make sense the first time, and isnt too tough on grading. you have to try though, if you dont try why are you taking this class. but she is the best, litterly amazballs.
do not take her elementary intensive spanish...

Wilmiriam is literally one of the sweetest and best Spanish professors! She is always willing to help if you are struggling and makes it so exciting to come to class each day. She is also a fair and easy grader and is super patient and caring. Her dog is also so cute!! Definitely take her if you have the chance :)

I've had four Spanish professors at NYU and she is definitely my favorite. She is so caring & kind, no matter how I'm feeling when I come into class I always leave smiling. She is very helpful, encouraging, and understanding. My Spanish has definitely improved with her as a teacher. If I have the opportunity to take a class with again I will!

Very nice and fun in class. The curriculum is standard among classes so there are a lot of hw/projects but all profs give the same. She is helpful in class and office hours. Would definitely take again! and her dog is really cute.

Professor Cotto is one of my favorite professors at NYU! She cares a lot about her students and is always ready to help with understanding concepts in and outside of class. Would definitely recommend taking her class if you genuinely want to learn Spanish.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class. It was easy, probably because I did badly on the placement test because I'm bad at multiple choice. She was a really good teacher and always made sure we understood the material. All the tests were multiple choice which wasn't my favorite. I would definitely recommend her.
Loved her! She was so nice, and class was always fun! Definitely take her!
really really nice lady but really really boring lectures, 2 essays + 2 open-note exams, easy A if you pay attention sometimes and know what the readings are about
Good! Worthwhile.

Easy A overall. The class can feel a bit dull and lectures can be hard to follow, but she is very kind and understanding toward students. Exams are open-notes; as long as you attend class consistently and keep up with the work, the course is very manageable.

Correm is a very good professor if you want an easy A. She's very nice and cares about what she's teaching but her lectures can be boring. If you focus sometimes and do some of the readings you can get an A. Shes very understanding about attendance as long as you dont overdo it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really nice and sweet woman. Her grading is fairly easy and the workload from the class is pretty chill. Midterm and final are open notes and the two papers in the class were easy to write. Most people ended with an A.
She's great she's so chill please take her. She's an easy A. Yes her lectures might be boring but if you show up and participate you'll do great.
good professor

Lectures whole class except for 15-20 minutes. Chill teacher, extremely well versed in the subject and knowledgable. Pretty caring I think. Lectures quite boring. Reading by the end of the year becomes quite hard and long. Definitely learned some stuff though. Midterm is short answer + MCQ, final is a paper (compare contrast). Two critical essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't expect useful feedback. Perfectly fine, nice enough person but not great at teaching.

she clearly knows what she's talking about but her lectures are so boring. assignments are really easy and she's an easy grader. she loves to hear other perspectives and clearly likes teaching but it's so hard to pay attention to her

She's very nice and values participation, which in my class was severely lacking. Her powerpoints go over historical context of readings extensively, very informational overall. One discussion post per unit and midterm and final essay. Pretty easy class, just would have been more fun if the class participated more and if she had encouraged it more.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awesome professor! She is really kind and caring. I highly recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: i love her. she's super understanding. even tho her lectures were boring and i never verbally participated, i still did extra work by posting more weekly discussion posts and got an A in her class. 1 midterm essay, 1 final group project + final essay at the end. easy paper topics. takes forever to grade/give feedback tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Correm is amazing. Her lectures are thorough and well organized. Always willing to help you out. Do participate and read beforehand - this will help you enjoy the lecture so much more. Loads of time to complete assignments and very clear grading criteria. She knows what she is doing, would not disappoint as a professor.

Prof Correm is the Queen of Philosophy! She cares for students and will explain all concepts carefully after class and during office hours. Whether you are interested in Philosophy, Take Her! Midterms and Finals are Take-Home!
although the lecture maybe a little boring, but not that much homework, and essays for midterm and final. esay for A
I took GWM-201 last semester. Tal Correm is an awesome professor. Just remember to participate the course then you will get an A.

Professor Correm was great! Take her if you enjoy lectures with some group discussions. Readings can get long, but she covers their themes and topics during class. There is a group project, although you receive a lot of time to work on it. You also have the midterm, final, and weekly online discussion posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Amazing. Chill lectures with only a couple essays + group presentation. She is super kind and teaches well. Easy A. Would 10/10 recommend.

The professor is very kind, but her lectures were too dry for my taste. Sure, we read a lot, but none of it stuck with me. The class is very participation heavy, which would lead to very awkward silences when only two people read the reading. She also doesn't provide a lot of feedback but her assignments are pretty easy.

Professor Correm is so amazing! She doesn't assign too much work, she explains everything well, and you can tell she's really passionate and knows a lot about what she's talking about. She outlines what she expects from her students very clearly, so you know exactly what you need to do to get an A.
Nice lady, but lectures are too dry. Approachable and accessible. You gotta speak in class.

Take her class! Dr. Correm doesn't assign a lot of homework & reading. The lectures are helpful because she explains the concepts of the textbook readings well. She gives feedback with each major writing assignment and she's open for office hours.
Really nice person and a great professor! take her

I LOVE professor correm! She is so kind and she will look over all of your assignments if you schedule a meeting with her- if you do this, you will get an A. She assigns a medium amount of work, but it's super easy if you pay attention. When her class is on zoom, she doesn't require you to turn your camera on. The midterm + final is take home.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: COVID-19 semester. Really solid professor. She's very caring of her students and the work is very organized. Participation matters but as long as you do the readings, you'll do fine. Short assignments for homework every other week and a couple of essays. Take her!

Really organized and provides additional resources in each unit to help you better understand the texts. Caring and accessible outside class. Just follow each lecture and take each assignment seriously you'll be good
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved this class and her. Don't take it if you don't care about the material and don't want to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: loves hearing herself talk, very lecture heavy but slides are not useful for studying. she is inconsiderate of her students, not flexible or understanding even in the case of illness. get ready to study everything on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took three classes with Prof. Connelly and loved all of them. If you are not willing to put in the work to memorize, study, and research, you may not like her class. The amount that I learned from her in only two semesters is mindboggling. I learned SO much. Genuinely. If you pay attention in class and follow directions, you will be successful.

brilliant woman and somehow has a complete blind spot for basic ideas of learning and teaching. Her lectures are word vomits with attached dates. Convinced she became a professor to dedicate more time to listening to her own voice. 70% of the class failed the first quiz, she blamed us for not memorizing/developing 10 different essays. run away!

class was more about her accomplishments than archaeology. just talks the whole class. no "required" reading or hw, just a 1 hr presentation + 10 pg paper (80% of ur grade!) disorganized/confusing class structure. she just stops teaching & students present their reports the rest of the semester. seems like someone who became a prof just cause

JBC is the only archeology professor at NYU. Therefore you might encounter her, however, try to take the archeology credit at CUNY (or anywhere else). The warnings about her are true: she's sexist, self-absorbed, combatant (will fight you) not constructive, unavailable, not liked in the department by her peers and hates philologists.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This isn't so much an art history class as it is an archaeology class. She makes you buy her textbook which gives you all the info you need. Loves to talk about the people she's worked for and her own achievements. She expects you to memorize a LOT of information/details, thinks her class is "fun". Nice lady, but with high expectations
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I know more about her career than about the material. No attempt to connect any of the concepts this "seminar" was supposed to cover. Half flipping through slides, writing down info word for word, half her telling us about her accolades. Made us buy books we never talked about. No meaningful discussions took place. This isn't how you teach art :(

I love this professor. She is my favorite that I've had at NYU and I consider myself fortunate to have the opportunity to have formed a personal bond with her rooted in intellectual discussions. However, if you are a bad student I would recommend avoiding her class. She expects you to be able to memorize and read, which not everyone found doable...

Professor Connelly is brilliant and clearly an expert in the topic. However, much of the lectures are concerned with her personal experiences and accomplishments. The grade is based on two exams (which are both extremely difficult) and one paper. She is one of the most sought after professors at NYU, but is also disliked by many students.
Best class ever !
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you love yourself do not go on the Yeronisos trip. I'm posting this now because I know this is that time of year when she comes a-hunting for impressionable students to indenture. Besides her being awful, it will end up costing you a lot more money than you might expect. Stay away!

The six weeks I spent in Yeronisos was some of the happiest times in my life! The western coast of Cyprus is a magical place. I made lasting friendships. We worked hard, played hard. The food was amazing. I felt accomplished. It can be a bit like bootcamp, given that you have to wake up at 5am daily, but if you're committed, you'll be rewarded!

Few of my professors possessed Dr. Connelly's ability to weave an absorbing, humane narrative from art historical interpretation. She helps students see familiar subjects differently by asking productive, revelatory questions. Her guidance during my research project was meticulous, and demonstrated what it means to be an authority in one's field.

Prof. Connelly is fascinating, articulate and caring. Her Greek vase painting class far exceeded my expectations, in the sense that she made it incredibly fun. I will never look at them the same now, plus I'll never lack the ability to show off in the Greek and Roman art section of museums now.

Professor Connelly's class was one of the best I took in college. She is an excellent speaker who has a deep understanding for Greek Art and Archaeology. She will also go the extra mile for students who care to learn as much as they can.
do not go on the cyprus trip you have been warned
This class was wonderful!  Made me want to study Greek and Latin as well.  Also, this class made me want to take her Parthenon class.

I took The Parthenon and its perception. Professor Connelly was very helpful throughout the semester and she was always available to answer questions. Her knowledge Of the material is superb and she was very clear when she explained it. I have to admit I had a great time and if you are really interested in Ancient greek art you should take it.

A wonderful professor- she is a great lecturer, a caring person, and she is up for the task of actually teaching students.  The coursework is much like any art history course with the added benefit of learning from an archaeological viewpoint.  Take this class if you are serious and dedicated to learning because what she offers is knowledge.

She clearly isn't hear to teach students.  She spends half of the lecture talking about her accomplishments than actual archaeology. Seriously avoid this teacher.  She doesn't care for the students and when she does engage the students, it is usually to speak down to them and discourage them. Her class was one of my worst experiences at NYU.
Professor Connelly is an excellent professor who wants you to do well. She is very entertaining and knowledgeable but don't expect her to actually meet with you during office hours.

Connelly is a terrific professor: engaging, clearly fascinated by the material, and personable. Great anecdotes. Literally wrote the book on the Parthenon and Greek priestesses. She expects a lot, but delivers back in kind. Would take her again, no question.

Professor Connelly was my first professor in the art history department.  She was my professor for Western Art I, Ancient Greek Art, and Ancient Art at Risk.  I highly recommend her- she is extremely knowledgeable and will definitely inspire you to continue your studies in the field of ancient art.

THE best professor I have ever had. She is so much fun and always has an exciting/funny story to add to each lecture. She is incredibly smart and knows what she is talking about. She will inspire you and make you want to learn more about what she teaches. I learned so much in her courses and loved meeting with her one-on-one.

A student is extremely lucky to have taken a class with Professor Connelly. Not only is she an incredibly inspiring and informative teacher, but she will even devote time to each individual. Overall, she is a dynamic, dedicated, and knowledgeable professor from whom all students should try to take a class.

Prof. Connelly is a rare find in a university known for its unapproachable teachers; she was friendly and worked with me when I needed extra help outside class. There is always a long line to see her during her office hours, not because she limits her time with students, but because she is one of the most popular professors at NYU, and it shows. A+

This prof.'s arrogant and unhelpful attitude deterred me taking a course I had high hopes for. In the two class meetings I went to, she said "I don't have time for that" in response to legit questions/concerns more than five times. She also told us she would only respond to emails if they concerned work she was trying to publish.  Selfish.

Only 2 office hours a week, which have an average wait of one and a half hours (according to my visits and those I've talked to) before seeing her. She provides help when needed but is somewhat difficult to get a hold of. Also, took 6 weeks to grade the midterm and waited until the latest possible date to turn in final grades.

My favorite professor at NYU!Really makes an effort to know her students! She is incredibly helpful and insightful whether you are consulting her about ancient art or life in general. Her stories in class are more than entertaining...they actually helped me remember a lot of images and pieces we learned about even after the final.
Prof Connelly is a great professor. Her classes are really interesting and she is a helpful professor.

Professor Connelly is probably the best teacher I've had at NYU.  Her lectures are extremely engaging, she really keeps you awake and excited about the material.  She's also very helpful if you make an effort and show interest.

Prof. Connelly was amazing - enthusiastic, extremely intelligent, and dedicated. And her lectures were enlightening. Even with her busy schedule, she was happy to sit and talk with me about me papers, presentations, life in general. And was great at encouraging me to come up with new ideas and thoughts.

One of the most popular professors at NYU. Her courses are challenging, but she always teaches ancient art with a humanistic touch. She's also one of the most genuinely generous profs at NYU. She spends personal time and energy helping students who come to her for help. One gains back the effort one invests in her classes.
She's kind as a professor. Tests can get hard only if you don't study for them. But, if you do, then you're good to go and you'll learn a lot. She's soooo funnnyyyy.

she is the greatest professor in nyu. she is published everywhere and knows so many people. she does like to talk about herself a lot, but i guess can. i cant think of a better introductory professor into history of western art. totally recommend her.

This professor is an odd mix of amazing and nice with horrible and mean. If she sees something in you then she will use you, if not you are nothing. She is only out for her own glorification. Although extremely intelligent, she cares more for the stuff she teaches than the students she is teaching. You are not important, its what you can do for her
Awesome, interesting lectures, really cares about individual students.  Also, very famous and well-published, lucky to have an introductory level class with such an outstanding prof.

so annoying. this woman drives me crazy. thinks she's amazing and all-knowing but really just likes to hear herself talk. do not take any class with her unless  you like that type of person. super easy class though. don't have to show up for her lectures.

Engrossing lecturer, smart, funny, caring, and engaging. When I screwed up on a presentation, she personally told me how disspointed she was and gave me one-on-one help with the next presentation. How many professors (nevermind @ NYU where you're lucky if they make ever even eye contact with you) does that anymore?

A good teacher who lectures well and knows her stuff.  However, she's mean spirited, extremely defensive, and downright rude to her students, especially if you try to ask for help or clarification about a test.  This isn't just me: she has a reputation among archaeologists and historians of being nasty (I asked around).  Not recommended at all.

awesome professor!  she really knows everything about western art (and the parthenon in particular).  intelligent and funny lectures.  she also seems to have connections to just about every one in every corner of the globe, which is pretty cool.  also, she has great insights into important, current issues.

Grades depend on three exams with three questions, so no time constraint. The exams are very similar to the optional practice questions, so do them! The only downside is that because the exams are a bit easier, the econ curve is competitive. Also, going to class is a must because he explains the concepts clearly.
A humorous guy and a lovely professor. No homework, and hard work pays off.
Very good professor, explaining everything clearly and providing an inspirational approach in combining theories and reality.

The professor is a funny guy and presented the materials in a clear way. The slides he provided are well-designed and the lectures were inspirational. If you come to the lecture and finish the practice questions he provides with, you will get a solid A. The exams are quite similar to the practice questions.

Explains everything in detail. Class is very straightforward. Exams are graded harshly so understand the methodology for every concept, and explain your economic intuition clearly. No hws, however practice problems given every week, which you must do for the exams. Also, there was no curve down and the TAs are very helpful.
Horrible person. TA's even worse.

When I took this course there was no curve down – maybe things have changed from before. Professor Cogley is a really nice guy (also really funny) who is happy to explain stuff outside of class or in office hours. The concepts aren't unbearable, it just requires some practice. Overall this class was definitely enjoyable and quite interesting.
The woooooooooooooooooooorst professor!!!!!!!!
Do your research before enrolling his course. If you want a surprising curve down you should take his course.

Professor is OK despite the confusing method of calculating the final grade, which leads to a curve down. TAs are just horrible. They don't know what they are doing, won't reply to emails, mumble over homework and exam questions, and can't explain why points are deducted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would say he is one of the worst professors in the Econ Department. If you have to take macro analysis, take it with Prof. Virgiliu Midrigan. You will learn something useful.
AVOID!

He makes everything difficult. I spent too much to get an A. The 2 TAs are interesting. You do not know how they would grade since they are not experts. So you have to overprepare, which is totally unnecessary.
I do not think he is too bad. But he is indeed not caring. But he is an old man. How much can you expect from a senior?
The class is easy. But the grading is surprisingly bad. I was expecting a solid A and the professor shocked me with a B+. He uses some mysterious method to curve down the grades. Not so fair.
Do you want to ruin your GPA? Do you want to experience despair? Do you want to learn nothing useful? Come to his class.
Red Alert: AVOID AT ALL COST!!!
