The grading is ridiculous. He gives easy exams but with unbelievable stupid graders. They do not even major in economics. The graders deducted points for no legit reasons. They don't know economics. It is difficult to handle those people.
He is not so caring. He failed to provide help to students who need them. He is slow in responding to any emails. I don't understand why NYU would hire such a professor.
He teaches nothing useful. Don't bother taking macro analysis. Stick with Interm Macro. He is a horrible person by the way.
One of the worst professors in the world. He does not know how to teach. You will never know what will be on his tests

Easy test, but absolutely the worst grade curve i have ever met in my entire life. His curve down is absolutely unbelievable. Even u get above average 10 points or more, he curves down two letter grades. Never take his course! Unless you are such a good ass future economist.

He was genuinely such an amazing professor and person. It's really easy to just talk to him about anything during classes. He is really lenient to getting assignments in on time and won't really take points off.

Conor is the best. Gives lots of reading and takes some time to give feedback but is really understanding of deadlines and gives you an A if he sees effort/improvement throughout your drafts. He's just a funny nice Irish guy and I learned a lot in his class.

I found Conor to be a very chill and kind professor. He clearly cared about your work and wanted to help you personally improve as a writer. His feedback was often helpful and specific, while also respecting how personal most essays could be. I found some of the readings to feel a little useless and random, but overall enjoyed coming to his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Conor is very patient and understanding of deadlines, and he is also a very engaged teacher. He pulls from different mediums of art and gives you choices of what to write about.
He's chill
Great professor! Chose great readings and gave very helpful feedback.

Conor is a sweet and quirky man, very flexible for deadlines. Take him if you want to become a better writer, otherwise it's too much work for the uninterested-i found it quite rigorous for a required course. His feedback is vague yet demanding, the other reviews are accurate. His teachings ended up being fundamental for all my writing since then

Prof Creaney was the best. I never liked writing but he made his class super fun and made me actually excited about the essays I was writing. He gives lots of feedback, gives you extensions, and lets you rewrite essays for a better grade. i ended with a good grade and think he made me a better writer.
Lot's of readings, unorganized class, harsh grader

He's pretty nice but the class gets awkward sometimes. Some of the stuff we did in class was unnecessary; I felt that I didn't learn much from the class. We just read a bunch of articles that he gave as inspiration for our papers and the lessons didn't have much structure. He also doesn't give that much feedback.

It's just a lot of reading about random topics. He thinks by reading New York Times Articles that means that we'll be able to write like that. Harsh grader and doesn't give feedback to anything. He doesn't pace the semester or projects well. It's just reading and then randomly the full essay due in a week. But he is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, but the classes dragged on forever. Like someone else said, I was always watching the clock. The homework assignments were frequent and required a lot of unnecessary work. The class was very participation based, but no one raised their hand so it was just very awkward and dead. Wouldn't advise taking his class if you don't have to.

Conor is the best. It's an essay writing class that is a requirement and I am not a big reader/writer. Going in I was unsure of how I would like the class however it quickly became one of my favorite classes to go to. Conor is hilarious and just made the class great!! He was always understanding if you needed extra time and you could redo essays.

Your standard introductory writing course. Do ALL assignments given, turn in essays on time (if not granted an extension), and show that you care about the quality of your work*** (e.g., office hours) and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Conor Creaney is a nice guy, but his classes are very boring. I watch the clock every time I go to his class. He takes your phone away from you & gives you a ton of things to read for hw. His essay topics are not clearly structured and when students asked him to be more clear about the prompt he was not helpful at all. He's a tough grader as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Conor was an amazing professor. I had him during the CAS Summer in Dublin program, which is a gem in and of itself. I loved all of his required course texts. Conor is very flexible and willing to listen to and work with students, and his accent is great, too. Lots of good craic.

Conor is the best. WTE is hard but Conor was so willing to meet with me outside of class and help me through essays that I was extremely worried about. He really listens to his students and lets us speak our minds and complain about the class to him. He brought us cookies on the last day. As far as WTE goes, it doesn't get better than Conor.

I have never had more work in my life for a required English course. If I were in AP English in high school maybe I would understand why there is so much work. But, the students he is teaching already have so much to do in their respective Tisch programs & he fails to understand this. He is a cool guy but the workload makes the class not worth it.

Conor made the biweekly workshop classes incredibly interesting. He brought in many readings and materials to broaden our horizons and inspire our own essays. Conor is laid-back in class but does take his work seriously and gives very good feedback. He has a unique, insightful view of the world. I feel like a stronger writer because of his class.
Sets expectations high, but his exercises really got my ideas rolling and my essays really improved. Gives great feedback and is not condescending at all. Students really respect him for that.

Creaney's a really nice guy, but he can be a bit dry or ambiguous sometimes. He also hates technology for some reason. He really makes you think your papers through, and is big on "exploring your ideas on the page." I liked him, though personally I think WTE as a class is BS.

As a person, he's a really nice guy who is genuinely interested in teaching you something new and learning something new from you. As a teacher, he's okay. His ambiguity in everything he says is what keeps him from being a GREAT teacher. He's not as straight forward as you'd like him to be, but he has some good advice to give.

Expects a lot and pushes his students but it's definitely worth it. Great guy and I really improved as a writer. Take his comments seriously because he knows what he's talking about. He's Irish and runs the Dublin summer study abroad - he won't let you forget that.

Conor can be strict with readings and he has expectations that you do them, and understand them. He can be a bit ambiguous sometimes but I think that that may be due to the nature of the subject. He is, however, a very cool teacher and Irish!

He made Writing the Essay my favorite class and I wish there was a major specifically for this kind of writing. He's a very hard grader but if you want to know more about yourself as an artist and about art theory then this is the right class. Be prepared to write and rewrite a lot. At the end, you'll have grown so much. Mildly in love with him...

Conor is an excellent teacher who is clearly passionate about the material. He is eager to help and readily available. He always leads really great discussions and tries to make the class as interactive as possible. I had him in Dublin, and he made the experience so fun and really educational. I learned a lot under his tutelage.

Conor is a good professor to take if you really want to learn a lot about art, interpreting art, and writing about art. He is really passionate about the subject and has a lot of interesting stuff to share. He is very helpful with the assignments as well. recommend for people serious about Writing the Essay.

Conor is very creative when it comes to teaching and this aspect of him makes the learning experience a lot more interesting. One day, he brought glitters into class and we talked and wrote about glitters for the entire class. He is very open to students and is willing to help even if it means that he would have to dedicate his own personal time.

Conor is a really great professor, who devotes his time and efforts into helping you improve your writing. With conor you not only to learn how to write good essays, but also to discover your own reasoning and artistic criticisms. He's always willing to have long discussions about your writing, and is a really good guy overall

Conor is a fabulous teacher, for he both encourages and challenges his students. In class he was always prepared with interesting lesson plans. After each one-on-one meeting, my essays always improved. He made Writing the Essay one of my favorite classes at NYU.

Conor is one of the greatest professors I've ever had. He's also one of the smartest people with whom I've had the privilege of conversing. My writing improved as a result of his teaching, as did my general critical and artistic approach to thinking. He is always engaged with both his material and yours, and keeps class an enjoyable place to be.
Class is lots of fun (it's possible for writing the essay!). Conor is engaging and helpful - a very good writer =)

Conor was the best teacher I had so far at NYU. He actually cares about the students and takes an extensive amount of time out  of his life to help ensure that his students get the best education possible. For every single paper, he was willing to meet outside of class for questions and further help. His class was very challenging, but rewarding.

Conor make WTE not only bearable but also enjoyable. My writing clear, nuanced, and interesting. The reading that Conor assigned I still talk about today. I wanted to work hard to get better and that was because of Conor.
Great professor! Always came with tons of external videos and articles.

He's a great professor, and if you care about what you're writing about he's going to try his best to help you think through it. Other comments here are very untrue and seem that the people weren't really trying to produce good work. He's always around, and understanding when you have to turn some stuff in late.

Conor's a really nice guy and makes WTE a lot better than it otherwise would be. However, I consistently felt like Conor was grading us harder than other teachers. I always found myself surprised at what my friends in other sections were getting A's for when comparing it to my essays and the essays of other people in my class.

He was a difficult grader (not necessarily a bad thing, but...), not a very nice person in general (so nothing redeeming there), and totally unclear. It would've been one thing had I felt like I was learning a ton, but that wasn't the case. He expected you to read his mind and shot down other people's opinions. Not ideal.

Apart from Writing the Essay being an utter waste of time, he's okay. Can be pretty unclear about what he wants from his assignments. Says a lot of vague things. The class felt random and thrown together. He's a nice guy, and he cares, but he's an inconsistent grader and the class can be dull. (HOT accent.)
totally awesome teacher.  knows his stuff. funny and open minded
He's very chill and understanding.
Conor has helped me to become a better writer. In his class you will write a lot, but also learn a lot.
his accent is amazing. end of story, hot.
good teacher. very cool. he's from ireland
No Comments

Took Boundaries and Transgressions, the workload wasn't overwhelming, the topics covered by the course were compelling, getting a good grade is realistic so long as you complete the readings and attend class. However, Marie would commonly arrive to class 10-15 minutes late, wasn't very accessible via email, and grading often wasn't very clear.

Loved Prof. Marie Cruz Soto! Definitely thought the readings were unexpected at first but it all came together in the end. Definitely reccomend, part of you grade comes from attendance and particiaption but there are no tests! But the main part of the class is just how interesting the the discussions are.

Boundaries and transgressions IDSEM- definitely not what the description said. Nice professor but goes off on tangents a lot and doesn't really accept another viewpoint other than her own. Some readings are confusing but it's not that hard to participate in class if you do the readings. Very discussion based, one project, no papers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I love Professor Marie Cruz Soto. Her mind is so powerful and beautiful. Expect to read a lot because that is the only way you will learn. What you put in is what you get out of the class.

Coming from a public school, most of the concepts discussed, such as Jacques Lacan's mirror stage and the abject in reference to Kristeva, were challenging and difficult to grasp at first. But Professor Cruz Soto is very engaging, understanding, and informative. As long as you do most of the readings and add to class discussions, you will be fine.

She is my favorite professor I've taken at NYU. Really cares about knowledge, makes space for students. Take this class. She wants to teach and be there, and carries such a strong message of hope and empowerment for students!!

Professor Cruz-Soto is genuinely passionate about the seminars that she teaches, and encourages the same passion in her students. Be prepared to talk in class - it is entirely necessary to succeed. Readings are dense but if you pay attention in class, not impossible to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Cruz-Soto is a gem. I feel fortunate to have learned from her. Do yourself a favor and take her class if you get a chance! Be prepared to engage and READ.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Absolutely fantastic professor. I loved her class, would definitely recommend taking Boundaries and Transgressions. I have never met a teacher with so much passion for a subject. The subject is fairly difficult to grasp and there are a lot of dense readings, but discussions really help in understanding.

Looks nice, but give you a final grade LOWER than your expectation without any reasons or response even you did a great interaction/conversation with her during the semester. Also, she seldom checks email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take him if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The best professor I have took this semester. Clear and organized tutorial structure for the whole semester, and the writing plan for the course is carefully planned. From exploring yourself to the whole society, three essays are very helpful. Professor Corcoran is very nice, the vibe of the class is chilling and comments for essays are useful.

Professor Corcoran deserves all the 5/5 he can get!! If you have the chance, PLEASE TAKE HIM!!! Only 3 essays for the whole semester, with workshops within the classes. The readings he gave were all so interesting and I never felt bored in that class at all. Participation was 25% of the overall grade. Wish I could take him again!! Such a sweet guy!

GOAT of LS writing profs. Literally all you have to do is turn in 3 essays, plus sit there for 3 hours each week without going on your phone. If you can do that, you WILL get an A. His stories are also super cool and he is just a genuine and kind guy. Can't recommend him enough tbh
I would vehemently defend professor Corcoran against any potential 4/5 rating, he deserves every single 5/5. A caring, warm-hearted professor you should take, an easy A but you learn so much too!
An excellent professor. Please take him if you have the chance.
No Finals/Midterm. Only grades on 3 big papers. Amazing Professor.

Professor Corcoran is amazing, he's rated 5/5 so many times for a reason. There were only 3 big essays in this class and a few short papers that we wrote in class. There is reading due every class, but it consists of interesting articles and leads to stimulating in-class discussions. He is chill, just make sure you get to class on time!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Be in the classroom on time, participate the discussion actively, and write every essay by yourself, then you can get an A. A really nice man!

This professor is just amazing you barely have teachers like him.He is always caring and passionate about teaching. He loves helping out his fellow students in a manner that not only helps you as a student but the entire class. He is flexible with office hours and is there to help you. Definitely recommend if want an easy A but just put in the work

AMAZING PROF!! i took him last year and he was always giving great feedback on essays. he also made sure everyone felt comfortable in class and was super engaging. even though it was an 8 am, i always looked forward to class bc he's so fun to be around. i'd rate him a 100/5 if i could. definitely take him, he's one of the best profs in LS.

Might actually the best prof in NYU. No exageration, it has to be somebody and I think it very well may be him. An absolute legend. Can't think of a reason why I wouldn't take him. Nice, caring, NORMAL, actually understand  AND PRACTICES the idea that his students are managing 3 other courses and adjust accordingly. Good dude. would give him a 6/5

He is the best professor I have ever met at NYU. Always passionate in class even if it is 8am. Helps everyone to get involved in the class and make friends with each other. Enjoy his class the most. Best!!!!!

I took him back during COVID, and despite many of the freshman like myself having a miserable start to NYU I have fond memories of his class. I think he made the transition to college a lot better for all of us. He made me unafraid to express myself through writing, and I wrote stuff I'll never forget. Not stressful at all.

TAKE HIM! The class is very easy, but you will be surprised on how much you learn. He is such a fun and amazing guy. There are three essays, low-stake readings (very short), and peer reviews. Just turn everything in on time and participate and you will get an A. Get ready for your essay to be read and discussed in class by everyone.
Easy A but he takes attendance so you have to show up in class! Amazing professor

It is amazing how you can get an A easily and learn a lot at the same time! Professor Corcoran is the best professor I met in LS. He's so knowledgeable and gives reeeeeeally useful feedback. Nearly zero workload except for the three essays. Take him if you can!

Professor Corcoran has been my favorite professor at NYU so far and it's very clear he's super passionate about helping us get out of our boxes and become better writers. The workload is very manageable especially because he gives us so much creative freedom to write about whatever really speaks to us.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: TAKE HM! Even though the class is not that difficult, I definitely improved my writing skills. Though it was an 8 a.m. class, every day I looked forward to it! Just three essays to submit during the semester that I really enjoyed writing! His lectures were amazing and the readings he chose were very interesting! 1000/10

Professor Corcoran's class's a super fair grader, all you have to do in the class is participate and do your work. The content he has you read is super interesting, and even though the class isn't hard, I definitely improved my writing skills. The class is really engaging; definitely one of my favorite classes this semester.

If you have the change, absolutely take Professor Corcoran. Never have I felt more inspired to write, and I love writing as a rule. Definitely also take him for the second part of the LS writing sequence.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: BEST PROF! If you have the chance, please take his class. I signed up for his 8am WREX class and had pretty low hopes to start, but I ended up looking forward to his class every morning. He turned me into someone who despises writing to someone who genuinely loves it. Only three papers throughout the semester. Genuinely miss his class already.

I had Prof Corcoran for an 8am class, but he was so positive and interesting that the early time didn't matter. He assigned 3 essays with two workshops for each. He provides lots of feedback and asks that the other students do the same. He was very attentive to our well being and always emailed us after class to see how we were. Truly a great man!!

Prof Corcoran was the highlight of my semester!! Grading is based solely on effort and participation, so as long as you are trying on the essays and leaving comments/giving feedback during workshops you're good. He was incredibly nice and friendly as well!!

THE BEST PROF!! I had him fully in person for Spring and I have ZERO regrets! Literally the only class I would look forward to going to was his. He is very caring and understanding. As long as you participate and attend class you'll get an A!

My favorite professor at NYU so far. He really encouraged you to work hard not only for a good grade, but for the integrity of your writing. All our homework was super interesting and my writing improved a TON learning from him. I wish he was teaching next semester because I would take him a million times if I could! Take this class!

Professor Corcoran is a great writing teacher and provides wonderful feedback, participation is key in this class, make sure you read your peers essays/give feedback to talk about in class. He also gives us short readings that surround the topic of what we are writing to discuss in class as well to give ideas on techniques and what to write about

The only Camera 1 professor to take if you are serious about learning about cinematography. Unbelievably knowledgeable about the physics, technology, and craft of cinematography down to the minutia, but does not expect you to know ALL of it to get an A. Incredibly hardworking, dedicated, and passionate. An honor to learn from him!

Crawford is extremely helpful, nice and ridiculously intelligent. He is a great lecturer, and explains things clearly and is always willing to stop and clarify should any questions arise. He tries to give everybody as much hands-on time as possible. He's got a good sense of humour but will not tolerate people who don't worktry.
By far the standout professor in the Tisch film program. His class is the only one where I've ever gotten my tuition's worth.

John Crawford is one of the 3 best professors I had during my time at NYU. He was one of the only teachers to ever really challenge me and my fellow Tisch students, and he knows EVERYTHING. Really and truly a fabulous teacher.

Had him for Camera 1 and I learned more in his class than any other class at NYU so far. He is so intelligent and in my opinion, hilarious. My roommate thinks I'm in love with him (I probably am) because I'm always telling her how amazing he is.

Simply the best!!! THE BEST TEACHER IN FILM... you will learn more than in all your other classes combined. (I saw that nobody had rated him in a while and thought it needed to be said that he has maintained his awesomeness over the years)
He is so intelligent and helpful!!!
John Crawford is the nicest guy on earth. He is also amazingly smart and accomodating. I love him and you will too, take his class!
AMAZING AMAZING!  so knowledgable and interesting- goes out of his way to help
i had john for tech theory and camera II. he is the best - knowledgable, willing to help, very involved with his students. there are none better.

John is an exceptional film theory professor.  His knowledge of the medium of film is extensive and he's very willing to help you outside of class.  I have gone to him several times for assistance with projects and he's answered my questions every time.

John Crawford is not only incredibly smart, but he is also very interesting. John Crawford taught me more in one marathon lesson than I had ever learned before about the tech of film. Also, he looks like Jesus and has the same initials.

Professor Beltrán was amazing! I would highly recommend her class if you have not taken Cultures and Context. The exams were extremely straight forward, which she gives an extremely helpful review sheet for. The content was very interesting and despite the class size being large, she facilitates casual discussion during class to hear our thoughts.

she's very sweet and likes when people participate. the class is easy, but a lot of reading. you can easily get away with looking over the slides and studying by going back to specific parts of the reading, I do recommend reading since it just makes it easier (just skim it). The tests are super easy and she gives you the test questions beforehand.

great professor!!! content was so interesting and engaged the class, also enjoyed the recitations. midterms and final were very easy because she gives you the a list of potential questions before the exam and an easy final project too. defo recommend.

3 Exams + Oral Final

Gives study guide with exact questions that will be on tests, just memorize your answers.

Exams have a time crunch only because of hand written answers that require 1-3 blue book pages.

You don't need to read anything imo, very chill class. Lovely teacher but class is super slow if people don't talk. Moderately interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, the class is fine.  Exams are easy since she provides a word-for-word exam study guide. Lots of reading but you can get by by skimming, going to lecture, and using the slides. Lectures could get a bit long and stale but its not terrible. Beltran is very nice and caring. Downsides: no tech during lectures (notes) and mandatory attendance

Just a ridiculous amount of reading—around 90 pages a week and they are dense. And all she does is go over the same readings in class. Easy tests but it's unreasonable to expect students to be able to do all of it in 4 days when you have other classes. Also she is extremely politically biased—even for me who actually agrees with her points

So so so so much reading. Exams are super easy but reading is kind of ridiculous and for me, the lectures are boring as she just speaks to us for 75 mins about the reading which took so much time in the first place. Attendance strict and mandatory. Meh class overall

What a gem! If you don't take at least one class with Cristina you've missed out on one heck of brilliant professor! During my undergraduate work I took Contemporary Latino Cultures, Race and the American Right, and an American Studies Seminar in graduate school. She's adored and an inspiration to many!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Beltran is a very great professor in the sense that she gives great lectures. However, this class, "Contemporary Latino Cultures" is VERY reading heavy and all readings are mandatory. You will have roughly 8-10 readings per week. Nonetheless, Beltran is very nice and accessible outside of class hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: easily one of the best professors at NYU. her lectures are very informing and interesting, and not boring where you want to fall asleep. attendance is mandatory and laptops are not allowed but the impact isnt really felt. the ta's are amazing as well and funny. the exams are easy since the questions are the same as the study guide
I cannot say enough amazing things about this professor. She is a treasure. A pillar in the social and cultural analysis dept.
Really easy exams. Easygoing and love to communicate and help students.
Bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Midterms + finals are easy. Beltran provides study questions that will appear the same on the exams. 2 written essays (graded harshly), but she helps students review the essays and give feedback. Beltran provides extra-credit to students but it doesn't count a lot toward our grades. There's a lot of readings that you don't have to do. No daily HW.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams could not be easier. The essays were a little tougher considering the rubric wasn't available to the students but they were also graded very generously. Engaging lectures and lots of readings.

She is an amazing teacher with great TAs. She gives the test questions a week or so before so you can prepare. The writing isn't bad at all and the tests are easy. I loved the class and it was pretty interesting as well. If you are in Stern definitely take this class to fulfill your culture class requirement

Attendance is taken every lecture. Attending lecture is WORTH IT as she does not record. Take notes and you won't have to read. Participation is graded. Just ask like one question every recitation and you're good. Study guide given for the exams! She is very passionate, and her Contemporary Latino Cultures is more aimed towards political science.

Reductive, myopic, faddish thinking promulgated without any dissenting views allowed. Not able to engage with race in an intelligible way. Not interested in freedom of expression. Parrot back to this professor her views, and you will get an A--it's that simple.

beltrán is the best prof/class I have taken at nyu in 3 years. the worse reviews below are by those who didn't agree with a female, progressive prof who teaches respect, equality, and inclusivity in her historical analysis. she's a genius lecturer/writer; brilliant in conducting discussions; hardworking TAs. class is an absolute GEM and an easy A!

would recommend to anyone who is either eager to learn or wants an A. Classes are informative but not difficult. As long as u put in some effort in ur weekly response papers (only like 500-700 words) and if you show up to class you'll get a good grade. There is lots of reading but u do not need it all, just pick some quotes and write. Easy A.

She's nice, but the content is delivered from an unbelievably one-sided perspective. If you enjoy critical thinking, this is not your class. Lectures sound more like therapy sessions and rants than actual two-sided discussions. I don't necessarily disagree with the professor's views, but there is zero attempt to even understand "the other side".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Beltran is interesting and engaging and I have definitely learned a lot about Latino history and culture. There is a ton of reading, although I find I can get away by scimming for the weekly responses (2 pgs). Partipation is 40% , including attendance, participation, and forum posts. A final paper is 20% and everything is graded by your TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A real gem of a CORE class. I dreaded the science Cores and was excited for this one, so take that with a grain of salt, but I think she does an amazing job of lecturing and engaging a huge class made up of a lot of students who dont care about the material or have any context for it without alienating the rest. Amazing reading list. Easy exams.

I wish I could do this class justice in this short summary. Class is definitely reading-heavy, but every single reading is well worthwhile. Lecture is inspirational and eye-opening, and Prof. Beltran is sarcastic, entertaining, and very intelligent. I loved SCA101 so much, and Prof. Beltran is to thank for that. I think everyone should take this.

Prof. Beltran assigned interesting readings but had difficulty managing discussion in an large lecture-style class. She has a habit of cutting off students and twisting their words to make the fit into the message she's trying to convey. Easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Readings were boring, spent the entirety of the lecture just analyzing the reading to the point that actually doing the assigned reading felt like a waste of time. Tried to encourage discussion in a class with 80+ students, didn't learn a thing in her class. On the bright side, she's really approachable and super available to come to for extra help

Prof. Beltrán was great! For cultures + contexts, you can't do better than her class. She is friendly and well-spoken, and cares a lot about both her subject and her students. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities, and as long as you put in minimal effort, it's easy both to get a good grade and to learn something. Loved it!

Prof Beltrán assigns weekly reading (that you don't necessarily have to do, but are necessary for the essays and exams). There are 3 essays, and 2 exams. For both exams you are given the questions ahead of time, and the essays aren't too bad. Your TA grades all of your stuff. There is a weekly recitation that, along with the lectures, is mandatory
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I was wary of taking this class because I had no interest in Latino Cultures. But Professor Beltran  saved this class for me. There is a reading for every class and she lectures about the reading. Most of the readings were interesting and an easy read. For midterm and final, she gives you the questions beforehand and chooses from those questions.

Cristina Beltran is the best! Her lectures were engaging, funny, and promoted discourse on current issues and events. I was not expecting this from a Cultures & Context course. I would love to take her again!

Professor Beltrán's passion for the subject matter was very contagious, sadly that did not translate to the TA's. Your grade depends solely on if the TA feels you have a deep understanding of the material as opposed to how hard you tried and the amount of effort you put into your work. Great class, better with the right TA!

Beltran is absolutely amazing. She will help you expand your mind through each lecture and makes all the information relevant and relatable. Super approachable and keeps lectures light. Enjoys hearing from students and always validates people's thoughts. Assigns a lot of reading but it's always interesting and worth it. Read and participate!

Prof Beltrán is one of the most fascinating scholars and professors I've had at NYU. She is hilarious, and a truly personal and approachable individual. Her knowledge on Latinoa Studies and insight into Latino Politics will make you fall in love with the field -- at least it did for me. Lectures are amazing. Absolutely take this class if you can!

Prof. Beltran is equally passionate about the subject matter and the students. While she sometimes talks too quickly in lectures, she presents the information in an engaging way. Facilitates dynamic class discussion, even in a large lecture hall. Essays were difficult, but reasonably graded. Midterm and final exams extremely fair. Lots of reading.

Compared to other Cultures and Context courses, this one has the most clarity and is probably the most interesting. I would recommend doing all the readings, if not to pass the class, but also for life knowledge. The TA's are great and you can tell Professor Beltran loves what she does, and that makes it all the more beautiful. Take this class.
Very accommodating and understanding professor. She genuinely wants you to succeed in her courses and in the field, she is an absolute gem.

super easy A impossible to get below an A- to be honest, but very boring and you do not learn anything. her classes are mandatory for the csd major so consider them a grade booster but I have never see anyone really pay attention to her lectures.

Professor Crus has truly been the best professor I've had at NYU so far. Her lectures are very straightforward. Once you get to know her, she is very caring and funny. You can tell she wants you to do well in the class. The exams and quizzes are super easy, but still make sure you study. It would take a lot of effort to do bad in her class.

Prof. Cruz was incredible! Such a sweet and caring professor that was also very knowledgeable. She really wanted her students to succeed and gave a lot of opportunities for extra credit. There are a lot of quizzes/tests/assignments, but she offers generous deadlines and gives you good guidance on what material to study for. TAKE HER CLASS!
This professor is fantastic! Her class is super engaging, even though the material can be tough. She's really good at explaining things, and she'll help you understand the material better.

OMG, I love Professor Cruz, I would take the class again just because I like her so much, She has so many funny stories and she truly loves what she does, the class itself was not bad at all, mostly online quizzes and interesting lectures. I'd pick her as my favorite professor, if you get her you're lucky

One of my favorite teachers at NYU, Professor Cruz is very caring and has some of the best stories. This class is centered around participation all semester long with a final portfolio due at the end, accounting for most of your grade. It is a great class to prepare for grad school and explore the field of speech-language pathology.
Her classes are super interesting, and she'll take your grades into account, so she makes sure to explain things clearly.
Best professor I've had so far! Really interesting class.
Pretty nice professor! Both the professor and the TA helps me a lot.

I had her for CSD2109 and she was wonderful.  Very understanding that the class was pretty boring but still made it so that we understood the importance of research in our field.  She also extended and altered deadlines so that everyone felt accommodated.  Would love to have her again for a class i'm genuinely interested in

I can't believe no one has left a review yet. Dr. Cruz is a saint, she was incredibly understanding regarding each student's situation, esp w observations. Her passion for CSD is apparent in every lecture, and she highly values and emphasizes the diversity of students in her class and in the field. Had her for both this class and CSCD-UE 101.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I learned a lot from this APA cultures course, the content is incredibly important and interesting. Graded by a wide variety of assessment formats including papers, worksheets, class participation, group work, discussions. This course demanded a lot of my time, must stay on top of readings and lectures because of random comprehension checks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super sweet, quite understanding, but class is kinda hard to follow: we jump around quite a bit from culture to culture/timelines with no through line, makes it hard to memorize info. Lecture is fine, readings are lengthy but skimmable (you'll do fine on exams even without reading, w/ study guide). recitations are boring and unnecessary imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Parikh is an incredibly engaging, adorable, and all-around amazing professor. Would take again 10000%
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would like to take her class 1000 times

I've heard she's great for her other courses, but I have absolutely hated this class. It may be because this was her first time teaching it. It is an enormous amount of reading per week and a skim over them in lectures. In her lecture she shows how intelligent she is, but she rambles and never finishes a sentence and I always leave feeling confused
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most disorganized prof I have ever had. She speaks at a million miles per minute with no clear direction. She often interrupts her own thought with a different thought and never finishes a sentence. I use to go to every class but I stopped going altogether, as you can never decipher what she's saying. What's the point? Should not be a professor

not the worst teacher ive ever had, but i hate going to her class, so i usually dont. she speaks so fast its hard to keep up with what she's saying. taught in a lecture which is a horrible choice for philosophy. readings are impractically long and boring and not thoroughly explained in class. unnecessary recitation/amount of reading. do not take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Parikh is kind, caring, and funny. She makes a point to learn her students names. She is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the subject. Her class (Reading Race and Representation) is well-organized and reading heavy. However, she does not have absurd expectations and the class is manageable. There are about 6 essays, and a final.

Took her for "Reading Race & Representation," by far best class taken at NYU,wishing it could be mandatory so that everyone could learn more about today's critical racial issues. Extremely intelligent, adorable, generous and will always have you leaving the classroom with something essential to know about our society, culturally speaking.

the most down-to-earth prof. i've had at nyu.  distills theoretical texts to their bare components so that the concepts are understandable.  great syllabus -- both "lit." and theory were interesting and relevant.  prof. parikh is both smart and approachable.  definitely take her!
Took Reading Race and Representation with her. Great class! Relatively easy grading and work load. Very friendly.

She is a great professor that taught me more about writing in one sem than all four years of high school. Readings and essay prompts are intimidating but she does a great job at making them approachable. The writing workshops are so helpful and she really expands the way you think about writing. She challenges you but in a way that you learn from.

There are a lot of readings, but as long as you read it a bit and participate, you should be fine. The essays are pretty straightforward, and she is a generous grader. Overall a very kind and amazing professor :)

Cris is an absolutely phenomenal professor. The self is a very intimate class and she was very good at making it a safe space. She is dedicated to every student, actively responds to emails, and will definitely help you grow as a writer. She's also not afraid to let a tangent go which makes every class feel better than the last.

I adore Professor Beam! She is so kind and welcoming and treats everyone like writers. Super non intimidating and really improved my writing. Grading wasn't harsh which allowed room to really work on just becoming a better writer. It may take a second to realize her genius, but once you do the class really grows on you! Recommend this class.

She said I did really well in the class but when I asked her to write 1 small paragraph of a reference for a scholarship application I desperately needed, she had 1 week to do it and said no, it wasn't enough time. I went to another professor and staff and they both did within the hr bc it was so short. She wrote a book on empathy but lacks it.

Definitely one of my favorite professors of all time. As the other reviews state; sharp, fun, inspiring, and knows her stuff. Super available to students. Wants to see you succeed. Had her for book and magazine editing. Will be taking her again for creative non fiction. William Paterson University.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Cris is the best writing professor I've had. She's sharp, fun, inspiring, and she knows her stuff. Really helps break down the writing process for you and make it your own.

Cris is the best professor I've had at NYU. Fair, understanding, smart, clear in her comments back and helpful in actually improving your writing. She created a great atmosphere for workshops and genuinely made me excited to get to class.
Excellent professor. No complaints whatsoever. Her grading is fair and workshops were the best I've had at NYU.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER!!! He's pretty chill and isn't a strict grader. I'm not sure why he's rated a 4 instead of a 5. For the last class, he ordered pizza to celebrate the previous day, and for other classes, he tried his best not to make the class boring. He's a 10/10!

reviews.comment:
He is a great great great professor!!!!Awesome!!!!

Select him!

he is just so kind that you couldn't bare being not engaged in his class

the course was hard, but professor Cregar is quite chill. There were a lot of readings after every class, sometimes you might feel overwhelmed, but his grading was generous as long as you follow the instruction. Sometimes his homework requirements was confused, but no need to worry a lot, you'll just be fine.

reviews.comment: he is mean and give pretty subjective feedbacks.
Very unclear and ambiguous instructions for each assignment.
So nice
Great professor, even have free snacks for us every lesson
A good professor. He can teach you a lot, and you can get a good grade easily.
If you work hard and ask more questions, you can get A. Sometimes ambiguous feedback but overall a good professor.

He is nice but he grades strictly. He gives very confusing feedback that you don't understand and you never know what he wants in the essay. He also changes his idea constantly and you may need to redo the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I am an international student. I was unconfident in my English writing until I met David. He is very inspirational and always gives me constructive feedback. During breaks in classes, he also brings us some snacks.

1. Bad time management in conferences. Its delayed by about 20minutes every time. 2. Unclear instructions and doesnt really give any constructive feedback. 3. Passive. If you talk about your progress and ideas about your essay he would just nod. No feedback for drafts except the first one. 4. Expect a B+.
Gives very constructive advice for essay drafts And he is really nice and chill too
Amazing teacher, he will help you as much as he can for you to be able to succeed

Professor Cregar's assignments are quite vague. He usually gives u only a direction and that's pretty much it. He taught me more how to think as a writer than how to write well and he taught students a lot of useful tools. He is accessible outside classroom and is not a tough grader as long as you figure out what he wants( which is not easy.
David is a greater writing teacher who is always chill. Workload is not heavy, efforts get payoff. Will indeed take his class again if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Extremely Inspiring Teacher. Never thought I would enjoy a writing class. Encourage you to think a lot and respect international students. He can be unclear sometimes but his unclearness somehow gives me more chance to expand my way of thinking. Love his Lectures.

The only thing that made his class even bearable was the hot girl sitting next to me. Unless you have lots of oxy to get high on during his class, you would probably want to hang yourself during his class

Professor Cregar is very understanding and respectful to all students during class. His comments toward essays and assignment prompts tend to be very unclear. I wouldn't say that his grading is severely harsh, but there's no guarantee of getting a high grade just by working hard in his class.
Very unclear about what he wants. His classes are interesting, but he never gives clear answers in feedback. Respects students but not an easy grader.
Not recommended. He's unclear about what he wants. Tough grader. Boring class.
He is super clear about what he want, explained everything in a way for everyone to understand. And hes always willing to help and adjust for the group. Highly recommend!
Learned a lot from him but that does not guarantee a good grade. He is very clear about the assignments and helpful. Nice person but does have preference of students.
David Cregar was an interesting professor. He is an easy grader and answer questions if a student is confused. He is also willingly to help after class.
Awesome professor. Never thought I'd enjoy WTE, but I actually did. Learned a lot.
fun fun fun. never enjoyed writing itself, but enjoyed the course over all
good but grading not fair.
He tought a course at Montclair State University during the summer and it was the most writing i ever did in my life, but it was also the most I've ever learned in any writing class.

Dave is a total badass. You'll be lucky to have him for WTE. He's extremely helpful and does whatever he can for you to do your best. That doesn't mean you don't have to work, it just means he's an awesome teacher and you'll learn a lot if you listen to him and put the work in.

Cregar is an amazing WTE professor, especially when compared to all the horror stories I heard from various friends.  He is definitely willing to give high grades, is a very fair grader and tells us what he's looking for, and he is SUPER helpful.  Just beware he does tend to run 5 minutes late.  Talks a lot, haha.
Definitely reccomend Dave as one of the better WTE teachers.  You are safe to take it with him, and he into music and cool like that.

Dave is an AWESOME professor!!! He is an extremely nice guy who gave me helpful constructive criticism for drafts of each essay. He really wants you to do well in his class, and he is a really fair grader (essay is not a reflection of who you are as a person).
He managed to make a subject I find tedious fairly interesting, and in a group of freshmen I was usually one of the few people who didn't complain about my writing the essay teacher.

From what I have heard from many other freshmen, Dave is the BEST WTE professor that you can get. Totally cool and really caring about his students (and always available for help). You will actually enjoy WTE if you take it with Dave, even though his class is still challenging.
hes good
great teacher. Really helpful and fair. Actually cares about the students and their performance in his class. Highly recommended for writing the essay.
Great enthusistic instructor.

LOVED his class. He's very helpful and made his class enjoyable. and we all know that MAP courses can be EXTREMELY boring.. but he was very fair when grading (easy as long as u show effort) and made his class fun!! i recommend everyone to take his class!
So funny and cares a lot about her students. She genuinely wants you to succeed. So funny and smart, I don't have a bad thing to say about this woman.

I loved taking Chiara Curtoni for Intermediate Italian 1. She is great at explaining concepts and knows when people are struggling and how to make it clearer for them while creating on-the-spot problems and examples. She is really sweet and at the end of the semester the class feels like a fam. She wants you to succeed and to learn.

Loved Professoressa Curtoni! She's great. I took her for Advanced Review. Her class was not overly difficult, but she was a bit harder on the grading for essays, but nothing crazy. Would def recommend!!

She definitely has high expectations, but also wants her students to succeed. While this class was one of the more difficult classes I've taken at NYU, I learned a lot and improved my Italian immensely. Class is fun and engaging, with lots of discussion. Not an easy class, but a very rewarding one if you have the time for it.

She is the best professor I've had. Makes learning Spanish really easy and she is super understanding. For an Intensive Class, she surely made it a really easy class. There is a lot of homework, but she is really understanding when it comes to deadlines or lateness. It is better to take Spanish Intensive then Intermediate 3.

Barbara is the best!! Learning a language is hard in itself and your success is reflected by the amount of work you put in. Needless to say, she was an amazing professor. She graded very leniently and I looked forward to going to this class even though it was at 9:30 a.m. every day.
Barbara was so nice!!! I will say that there are a lot of graded tasks, but if you stay focused and participate in class it will be pretty easy to get through and still get a good grade.

The course is hard because of the work load and level. But professor Curiel is an amazing teacher. She was always accessible, timely with feedback and created a very inviting atmosphere for us to participate. She genuinely helped us learn the hard concepts and was always open to questions. She is the best teacher to have for difficult subjects.

she's so sweet and fun and very understanding!! grade is based on 3 tests, 2 in-class essays (which you can re-write for a higher grade), vhl homework, oral assessment, and participation. the coursework is not that hard and the tests are exactly like the practice tests.

Very personable professor who makes learning Spanish engaging and fun. Everyone was participating because it made the class better, and she was always encouraging and inspiring us to understand the concepts. Highly recommend taking her class if you can!

Intensive summer course over zoom, still very enjoyable despite the two hours in front of the screen. Very interesting class and readings and brought up a lot of theoretical and historical perspectives I had never heard before. A lot to read but prof was understanding when we couldn't finish everything and would work with us from there
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's a really nice and understanding proff. she seems rlly knowledgable about her subject and gives interesting lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Barbara is great! I would love to take her again. As long as you show a little effort to speak in class (and she isn't even too harsh about the no English thing), and do the simple and quick daily assignments, you'll get an A.
Amazing prof, amazingly comfortable class environment!

Very good lectures and one on one advice. She cares a lot about her students and gives great feedback. Definitely doesn't give away As but she will give you one if you take the work seriously and make a real effort.
She's definitely a really good TA, and you can tell she cares about her. But I also heard that for C&C Spain, the other TAs are much easier graders than her... so take that as you will.
Fun, caring, and great at explaining difficult topics.
Working with Bárbara was such a privilege. Her course was fun and illuminating, and her feedback on written work was particularly helpful.

A good teacher who clearly cares about her students but her guidelines and expectations for assignments can often be unclear or unspoken causing mistakes. She allows you to self-assess yourself but the grade she gives you can be influenced by the tiniest of things you don't remember. She is very passionate and engaging but her grading can be weird.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A great teacher who provides detailed feedback and is always available outside of class to offer additional comments and guidance for revising essays. She is knowledgeable about writing and goes above and beyond to help her students improve. The journaling activities she assigns are helpful for developing writing skills and self-reflection.

I thoroughly enjoyed Mrs. Cuddeback's ACA course. Mrs. Cuddeback is a thoughtful and supportive teacher who provides detailed, constructive feedback to help you refine your work and create the best possible paper. Her dedication to her students' success made the experience incredibly rewarding. Would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Cuddeback is my favorite teacher in NYU Florence. she's a chill teacher, she allow us to do the self evaluation for our midterm and final grade. I really enjoy our class discussions, which are open and encourage us to express our thoughts freely, while she skillfully expands on our ideas. she also really care about student, shes brilliant

I took Nicole for my mythology class at FSU (idk why it doesn't have it available on here). She was awesome, it was literally like something out of the Dead Poets Society, but about mythology. She cares for her students deeply and is passionate about the material. She also is lowkey a genius. Pretty easy class, you just have to read a lot of myths.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading in this class. I took her for Arts and Cultures. This is majority a student lead class, which is okay but gets boring at times. She gets really excited and just starts talking. More than 93 percent of the time we got out of class late because she was just talking. Overall it was an okay class, and she was wonderful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Anyone who has made a living writing in Florence, Italy is worth your time. She helped us all explore our personalities through writing, in a creative workshop, and then we sat together to discuss contributions on a blanket in the grass beneath the most beautiful architecture in Europe. Perhaps I even carried some Chianti in my backpack.

reviews.comment: I took her class in 2009 at Florence, Italy. I tried hard on my essay homework, I got B. Therefore i asked a revision from my friend in Harvard, still got B. I asked a revision from Harvard Newspaper editor, still got B. I asked a revision from Harvard writing professor, still got B. I found out Most of Asians got B. Still cant forget her name.

Doesn't prepare anything for class- requires students to write dozens of pages of things she will never read in a physical journal. If you enjoy writing endlessly for no apparent purpose and then counting your own pages like counting prison days, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Really good, she gives you a lot of feedback and goes through a lot of drafts with you, would definitely recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: We did a lot of free writing and useless peer reviews. She is a tough grader and if she doesn't like your style of writing she will try to make you change it to cater to her taste. Really wants DETAILS. In class discussions are good but she assigns way more out of class homework than the other profs.
A great teacher! She's very patient and made me interested in writing!
She is not an easy grader, do not take her if you really want higher GPA. she also has favorites so i don't know for those who are her favorites, but i sure wasn't. do not take her. trust mee
Very nice and patient woman. Her readings are always thought provoking.
IF you want to get a good GPA, do not take her. Since there is no specific answer, she gives grade whatever she wants. Please do not trash your money on her.

International students, do not take her. Seriously. I submitted my final essay that was revised from Harvard Univ. newspaper editor, and i got B while other native american students got A..s. I still don't understand how Harvard editor gets inferior grade than NYU LSP students.

I took IB English Higher Level in high school, so coming here and having Cuddeback was like going back to the 7th grade. She constantly forgets what she's talking about and the subject material is well below college level.

This professor talks waaay too much. For the whole class, she will not stop talking. She breaks things down too much, I felt like I was in middle school. However, some of the reading we did was interesting and I did feel like my writing skills improved a little. She does not have a lesson plan and simply relies on students expression their opinion.
i had her for my writing i and ii, and i loved her. she was great, very helpful and considerate, and most of the time lets you choose what to write about.

The girl def has some stupid assignments and stupid readings. Its true you can write an great piece and not get the grade 4 it or (show her) that you try har on a bad piece and get an A. In her class A is for "effort" not "quality" so start off by a slacking off on ur first draft then, make all the changes SHE told u to make and Voila : A!

I had to remind myself that I was in University and not in High School when it came to this class. A case of putting effort into your work rather than writing something amazing which gets the grade. At times she came across as juvenile which got on everyone's nerves. But at least she cared about the students and their work. Kudos on the cat comment

She should have been my 9th grade english teacher, but her class was a nice break from the rest. Her assignments are incredibly easy and she is easy to suck up to. Just bs your interest in her class and do the easy assignments and you will do well. Very nice though, but def has cats on her wall.
she's a terrible writer--the kind of woman who has pictures of cats in her wallet. lack of self-esteem seems to get in the  way of her teaching.
I doubt her own writing skills.  She's a bit ditzy.
take this for intensive, lots of work but thats all the intensive courses, very good professor and caring

Such an understanding and lenient professor, easy grader if you show up and participate, and the class has so many assignments that it's hard to genuinely get a bad grade. If you have to take intensive Spanish, take her class!

reviews.comment: I loved having him! He's really big on class engagement, but he honestly makes it really easy to participate. You're literally given the discussion questions beforehand so that you can prepare. We were assigned 4 essays, each worth 20% of our grade. He's pretty fair with grading, but feel free to visit his office hours for help. Would recommend!

Really nice guy but sometimes he makes comments that translate very poorly or can be distasteful. Lectures are engaging, with lots of art and literature analysis. TAKE NOTES!!!! Essays are based on things he says explicitly in class. However, essays have no rubric, so go to office hours for help or questions because he will help!
Prof. Culver gives great lectures. You can learn a lot about arts and cultures stuff. He is encouraging for in class participation. Work on your essays.

Overall seems to be a nice person but can give off icky vibes sometimes. if you are an active listener and participant during class you'll have no problem. class could get boring. he also makes you read stuff that he wrote himself.
Great Professor - TAKE HIM! He is nice and extremely knowledgeable. A little hard to reach via email but his course load is fairly manageable.

reviews.comment: He's passionate about the subject but can be condescending with how he teaches. Midterm/final essay prompts are convoluted and his grading criteria is a bit unclear, so make sure you understand. As long as you take notes in class you will have plenty of material for the papers.

I mean, he's my favorite professor so far at nyu. His class is not that easy, needs you to give your own opinions. You'll get a lot as long as you participate in this class and think, he really made it interesting with his knowledge
hes kinda racist
if you got other teachers just take their class. dont waste your time here.

He expects us to do so much when he's just standing there in front of the classroom, swearing half of the time. I hated it. He's so boring, too. reviews.comment: Chill guy. His lectures are very engaging. Takes notes and you'll do well on the essays.

Professor Culver is very knowledgable and you will learn a lot from taking his class. The class itself is interesting and a good combination of lecture and discussion. If you participate, pay attention, and use what he says in class for your four essays then you will do well. Go to office hours for help with the essay assignments.
lowkey do not take him

Amazing professor, i wish I could take Culver's class next term! he is so engaging and excited to teach arts and cultures! on top of being my favorite teacher this term, he has an encyclopedic knowledge of page numbers and quotes and leads the class discussion SO smoothly.

reviews.comment: While Culver was an okay professor, he does not have a clear grading criteria and grades harshly. He does not give any sample essay examples leading students to not know how they should write their papers. If he is your only option it is fine, but try to steer clear.

Despite asking the silliest questions on class, he graded papers very harshly by making deductions for super minor details that he has never clarified when assigning them. Very rude during office hours and replying emails.  Maybe your grade heavily depends on whether he likes you.

It's my first time rating. It was a fun class overall and he explains materials quite clear. BUT he's VERY RUDE outside the class and not understandable at all. VERY HARSH in essays grading, the reasons he gave are elusive and changing each time. No rubric in grading at all. His feedbacks are mostly negative, but not helpful for your work as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Four essays across the class... I got a B+ for the first paper, but once u start taking notes and using what he says in class in ur essays, it definitely becomes doable! Participation matters. Culver is always friendly and bright in class! What a wholesome guy

Lectures are pretty engaging, workwise there are only 4 essays which you get a reasonable amount of time to complete. He's a really nice guy and as long as you show up, pay attention, participate now and then, atleast skim over the class readings and understand the material being explained you'll be fine.

Attendance not mandatory but participation is huge part of your grade. Tries to keep energy up @8am but not a great lecturer/unfriendly person esp outside class, If he likes you (at random) you will be fine, if not, good luck. Essays graded harshly (no rubric, little to no guidelines) Genuinely an unpleasant professor, take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: pretty easy class since its just essay work. however, his grading can be a bit harsh. he is funny though but also slightly intimidating because he is somewhat strict about the contents of the essay

culver is not a professor you should take if you want an easy class, contrary to these other reviews. he gave us four essays and they all could make or break your grade, stressful especially because the last essay he gave us THREE days to write. he is not understanding and he can be quite ignorant to student circumstances.

he's funny sometimes and to his credit he makes lectures interesting, but he can be a bit much. also didn't respond to a lot of my emails which is annoying. grading scheme is 20% per essay (there are four, including the final which he gave us four days to complete) and participation is worth another 20% so definitely go to class and participate.
He is super chill, his lectures are always fun. I can see that he loves what he teaches. You don't get a lot of work--just 3 essays and that is it.

super nice and understanding. i always went to office hours and he was great. but in class he asks us the dumbest questions about the readings. but he makes it so easy to participate which is good. papers are quite long but not hard at all. write more than required! pay attention in class & TAKE NOTES! would def take again bc it was an easy class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great attention to detail, lots of reading, but if you pay attention in class, you'll be fine. Both final and midterm are papers. Your thesis needs to be supported by lots of evidence and details. Be sure to go to his office hours, it is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly if you don't do a single reading all semester you'll be just fine as long as you pay attention in lecture. He's always trying to draw connections to different time periods/genres so take notes on those ideas specifically and especially. Culver is AWESOME and actually a really fun guy to be around. Makes things interesting all the time!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Culver is very insightful and knowledgeable regarding the arts; His lectures are unparalleled. As long as you take notes in class and participate you'll be fine. He is a very tough grader regarding his essay's but thats why I like him. Additionally he'll answer any questions you have if you show up to his office hours.

This class isn't too hard, but the class time is pretty mind-numbing. It's challenging to stay awake, but Dr.Culver tries to keep things engaging. He's a good choice to get your ACM requirement out of the way
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Culver is one of the few LS professors who actually has a lecture planned with slides. His class is quite engaging. However, be warned he is not as easy as he seems from these reviews. His grading of papers is unpredictable, so try to go to office hours as much as u can
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Culver is great honestly. Love when he sings in class. His expectations are very clear and so are his readings. If you just pay attention in class and participate (participation questions are easy) you will do well. He is very passionate about the material and his lectures can be very entertaining.

Professor Culver is super clear with what he wants from his class. Lectures are based of the his readings that he assigns or the text at hand. The things he wants you to get from this class, he will walk you through. With papers, which make up the majority of your grade, he has super clear guidelines of what the outline should look like.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Culver is the sweetest prof you'll meet at NYU I swear. Even in an online course he's so lovable, funny, and all around such a nice guy. Really clear on what he wants from essays, gives plenty of time to go over the assignment sheets, and is always willing to answer questions. Really great class environment
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Culver is the ideal prof. Not too many assignments, clear grading criteria/expectations, not too much HW or reading usually, gives plenty of time to do papers, and is highly accessible + gives great feedback. He's super nice, funny, passionate, and encouraging. He clearly knows his stuff but allows students to give their own opinions

Prof Culver has been one of my favorite teachers during my time at NYU. He is extremely passionate about his class and is also very organized. Attendance is not mandatory, yet if you do not go you can be a bit lost. He also has a great selection of readings!
He's very nice and helpful, actually makes me interested in works that I wouldn't understand if I read it by myself. He tries to make sure you understand what's going on in his class.

One of the best teachers hands down, he really tries to be mindful of people with different viewpoints and doesn't just support one. You should definitely take, he gives out the final before and other than that it's mainly 3 essays and they're very interesting to write about and easy to get done in the time he gives to work on them.

Prof Culver is very knowledgable on the subject and his discussion concerning art was interesting, opportunity to learn a lot. He tries to explain everything very carefully and likes to make sure you understand everything. I think great for people whose first language isn't english (like me). The class isn't really hard and you learn A LOT!

He's super boring and seems like the easiest A ever, yet he might unpleasantly surprise you at the end of the semester with the grade he gives you. In the beginning, it wasn't that bad, but through the course of the semester, the quality of his lecturing was deteriorating. To be fair, his essays are actually extremely easy.

Culver is very enthusiastic and passionate about what he teaches. He has a good sense of humor which adds a lot of color to otherwise boring course material. His assignments are pretty run of the mill, a couple of essays and a final exam, to which he grades without bias. He makes it very clear what you need to do, I will be taking him again soon.

Professor Culver is really nice, but boring. Write all your essays couple days before the assignments and bring to his office hours - he will correct everything and you will get an easy A. Take home midterm and essay for the final.

He's so nice! Will make sure you thoroughly understand the work and will make occasional jokes that lighten things up. He lets you know two to three weeks advance about a paper and will try his best to help you. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Sweet but boring. Culver looks like santa claus in a grey blazer, talking to students like they are his elves. Although he is passionate about the topics discussed, his classes aren't really engaging or specifically interesting. Grades are a mystery as there is no clear grading criteria. Just take him if there is no better option.
Literally the most demeaning, horrible teacher I have ever had. Would give back papers with low grades with no apparent reason. If you don't agree, with him, you're wrong. STAY AWAY!

If you want an easy class this is it. You have to show up but participating is easy.  No tests expect final with you get the prompt for before hand. Three essays that are pretty easy. Didn't read a single book in two semesters i took CF I and II and i got an A- so its a pretty good class. I actually learned a lot in this class.

He's alright. He's enthusiastic about his lectures, but you don't have to try hard in this class. No one does the reading or questions he assigns, since he tells you everything during class. Essays are a bit harder, but if you do the bare minimum of an essay's requirements, you'll get a good grade.

Really just an awful class. Horribly boring and the man is pretty annoying. Talks to us as if we are children. It's easy to participate, but the essay grading, unlike stated in the previous comments is much worse. Don't trust his grading; I went in spoke with him once about a grade, and turns out he missed an entire paragraph.

Professor Culver is a great teacher. His classes were interesting and engaging . The love he had for the subject he teaches is infectious and makes you love the class that much more. Participate a lot (which is easy to do his questions are there on a silver platter) and you will get an A.

Definitely a knowledgeable teacher.  He assigns basically all essays--2 open-ended ones and 2 "exam"-type essays.  He is very clear on what he wants in the prompt and is looking to see that you are responding to what he is trying to teach you.  His jokes might be lame, but I thought they were hilarious! Office hours don't hurt!

His class is boringly easy. He talks to his students like they are 5 years old and expects you to finish every single dumb sentence he says, but nobody ever feels like it because the questions aren't even real questions. And he'll ask the same questions and say the same obvious things over and over again. Easy class, boring if you actually care

Culvz is the man. Actually love him and his green sweater so much. Has such an amazing voice, should try out for American Idol. Not hard, sit in front, participate, and he might call you Satan but gotta love him.

I took this class because of all the previous "easy A" comments, but I don't know if he had a change of heart or what. He is INSANELY strict with attendance, even when I was 2 minutes late ONCE he said that it would affect my grade. His papers are also incredibly long, and gives very vague prompts so you don't know what he wants. Would not take.

Do not be fooled. This guy is no easy A. He has 3 essays and one final. He basically won't give you an A like ever. And his instructions are confusing and unclear. I worked for hours on the last essay and got a B. He tries to be so helpful, but he only makes things more confusing. Be warned

NOT AN EASY A. People obviously do not know the definition of an EASY A. Take Salemi if you want an easy A. VERY focused on music, sings in class, gets very boring. You tell him what you think but ultimately his opinion is more valid and basically tells  you that there is no wrong answer but then acts like you say the dumbest things.

Tells you exactly what he wants from you. Really cares about you doing well. Go see him with drafts of your papers before they're due and participate a lot and you'll do well. Can be a little boring at times, but that's the nature of the material. Does a great job of making it interesting. Highly recommend him for cultural courses!

Really fun class. Interesting course material. Focuses on art & music. Loved the way he linked the 2. Very easy. Only complaint is that his interpretation of material is all that matters. He will listen to your opinion but ultimately, he is right. Go with it and you'll do well. No tests, just essays.

Culver is one of the best professors I've ever had.  He's extremely interesting to listen to (and I didn't like art at all before his class).  Always willing to help, not a hard grader if you just follow his structure.  Participate in class and he'll love you.

Culver is a genuinely nice guy who is incredibly interested in the subject. Reading isn't required as it's never brought up in detail. Four papers and no exams.
