Class participation is really big, but just 1 comment each class keeps him satisfied. Easy A if you see him about papers beforehand. Take him!!

Extremely solid guy, really picks up on the little things in the curriculum that make you laugh. His jokes will help you remember all you need. No midterm exam just a paper. Most of the time you don't even need to do the readings he rehearses it in class on his own. Very kind-hearted dude, doesn't call anyone out. "Doesn't like surprises".

I liked Culver's class at the time, but now I especially appreciate it after having taken II and III. Culver is obviously interested in his topic, never thinks a question/ answer is stupid, and is overall very nice. I found his class very clear so I never went, but he definitely seemed as if he would be more than happy to help someone outside class

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HATE ART AND MUSIC!!! Boring class and whatever you learn during class is basically useless for the final. He does assign the one essay Final exam before the exam but it is extremely subjective. The essay questions are very vague and subjective. I chose his class because he was apparently easy but it regret it.

Prof. Culver's class was great. I learned a lot about what "modern" means. We listened to some very interesting music and read some fantastic literature. The art discussions were a tad broad, but I can see them being very rewarding for someone looking for a crash course in modern art (1700's-Today). Very easy class if you listen, speak, and write.

BORING but easy.  He greatly appreciates participation it since awkward silences happen after every Q and it helps boost your grade. there were 3 essays & 1 final exam. final was an in-class essay & he gave the Qs ahead of time.  His essay Qs were always kinda confusing so go to him so u can figure out what he wants. sparknotes helps. got an A-
A great professor who explains everything crystal clear. Make sure to always do the response papers and read and you'll be guaranteed a pretty good grade. :)

If you dislike learning about art or music: describing it, comparing it, and recognizing it. DO NOT TAKE THE CLASS. The majority of the class deals with art or music. Culver is quite passionate about the subject material and seemed to be pretty helpful. However, the class is not easy, and there is a ton of reading.

What's great about Culver's class is his tireless enthusiasm about the generally boring subject matter. All you have to do regularly is look at his reading questions and participate (he loves it). He's also ALWAYS very willing to help and clarify. My one criticism is that sometimes it felt like he was talking down to us, which can be frustrating.

Agreeing with everyone else, Culver is SUPER SWEET and enthusiastic about his class, but that enthusiasm couldn't compensate for the boring material. Go see him for papers if you want an A, and speak up in class, participation is big, and easy. Overall, nice teacher, boring (sometimes painfully boring) material.
His class is boring. He's not an easy grader.

very smart professor. culver is all about class participation. make sure you do the reading and say something in class. he is a hard grader. there was 3 papers. 1 counted as a midterm. and the final is an inclass paper. dont expect an easy A.

He is really nice and all that but he does not give out As to everybody. He actually is a pretty hard grader. A LOT of READING and CLASS PARTICIPATION is CRUCIAL. His tests are not too hard but he rarely gives out anything better than B+ and A-... Don't take if you want to get A for sure.

Really nice guy and loves his subject. The class is very structured. The workload is not unreasonable. You will write two papers, and both the midterm and final are essays that you write in class (gives you the prompt ahead of time). He emphasizes discussion, so do the reading and speak up in class.

Lovely man, but a bit boring at times. You can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. As long as you do the responses (easy but annoying) and raise your hand once a week, you have yourself an A. The reading list starts out crappy but the last few books are amazing. Not a bad class at all. I recommend it!

Culver is a great guy, great prof. Just like others have said, read the material, go to class, raise your hand. He will never say you're wrong and really takes your thoughts into consideration. He doesn't force his opinions on you, lets you think for yourself. Exams let you tell him what you've learned rather than what you don't know. Great class.

He's nice, but so BORING. It feels like you're in kindergarten. People raise their hands and say stupid stuff, and feel like geniuses because he makes you feel that way even if you say dumb stuff. You don't actually have to do the reading, but as long as you pretend you care, and write what he says, it's an easy A.

Class is a complete waste of time, he repeats the same basic concepts over and over again, class after class. Lots of quoting from the textbook. Everything is said with a knowing smirk, as if  we're privileged to have his great wisdom imparted upon us. Very smug. Doesn't want you to think for yourself, easy A if you just repeat what he says.

Do the readings (and response papers), go to class and raise your hand once or twice and you have yourself a B+ or better. I actually loved his lectures as he really knows his material. My favorite GSP professor by far, wish I knew about him before my last semester.. Great reading list too, Godot and the Modern Art lectures were AWESOME!
Great class. Great professor. Culver is extremely organized, a major plus. As long as you read and raise your hand a lot, he'll like you. Exams are not that difficult as long as you read.
he is a really nice guy, and he'll help you out with whatever you need... but i felt like i was in kindergarten in this class.  it was so boring and so easy that it almost wasn't worth it.
Culver's class is great. He's a super nice guy, boring, but it can be interesting. Not hard if you read what he assigns, really easy midterm and final.

He is a nice and easy going guy.  But unless your truly into the topic, his lectures are extremely boring.  I find myself playing my phone or sudoku most of the classes.  He is easy going and not much work is need for him.  So ask yourself, if you want an easy grade and suffer his lectures, it's up to you.
His monotone lecture=a Great lullaby!

this man is the biggest idiot i have ever met. he has no idea what he is talking about and he analyzes books the way most people did in middle school. if you want to be bored to tears and leave each class feeling more stupid, take him. AWFUL!!

This class was sooooooooo easy!!! You just raise your hands, say watever...anything...his questions themselves are a joke. the books are fun to read...and the responses are about 14 in all..and only 1-2 pgs.  he showed us our final a week before we actually took it so we knew exactly wat was on the exam.  Raise your hand, hand in ur responses = A!

hes a good professor. he knows his stuff and has a great way in teaching it. some days may be boring, others fun. u really learn and get a true aspect in meaning of art and what ur learning. just has 2 papers and he gives u the final and midterm a class before, which is great cus u know what to write. hes a fair grader and i took him twice. def tak

The Topics class for Modern Culture: Modernism in America is a great class.  Some of the books are actually fun to read.  You have to hand in informal responses that are like 1-2 pgs and can be filled with b.s.  If you raise your hand (you don't even have to say anything smart)...you'll get an A. VERY EASY
the most boring class ever, but pretty easy
Culver is a very sweet man and a fair grader..the class was boring at times but probabaley bc i learned alot of it in high school.  I recommend taking this class!

Prof. Culver is obviously an intelligent person who knows his stuff but he addresses the class like he is lecturing a group of five year olds. He's a good guy and gives decent grades, but he teaches college students classic literature like he's teaching toddlers the alphabet. If you've ever had any of the material before his class will annoy you.

I didn't enjoy the first few weeks, but I think it's mainly because I don't enjoy art history and analyzing art. He's really nice, though. Intelligent and (at times) even funny. Read the texts so you can have something to talk about during class... otherwise everyone is just sitting there twiddling their thumbs. He likes it when you talk

This man is REALLY nice; easy-going class, not a lot of demanding work.  You can never be right or wrong in his class; papers are not bad; he likes art & music a lot.  Sometimes there are down periods in class - just do a little of the work so you'll be able to talk (he likes it when you talk).
Lots of music and art. He is so nice. Pretty easy, but I learned a lot too. He's a great teacher.

He is the nicest man... and his class is very fun! not much work to do at all but he discusses many interesting points dealing with modernism. if you like modern art..music.. then this class is the way to go... its an easy A.

Overall, I really enjoyed his class.  At times it was a little boring, but then again it could have just been the material we were studying.  He is very clear and fair.  As long as you work hard you will do well. I really recommend his class.

One of the most confusing classes I've taken. Assignments and grading standards weren't clearly explained, so it was hard to know how to do well. Attendance was enforced harshly, which added constant pressure.

Professor will randomly pick your grade after not returning any assignments, then when asked for clarification fails to have records of any specific assignment grade. Also chooses to follow the stern curve even though its an elective grad course. Not afraid to fail people. None of this would be a problem if the course material wasn't super easy.

Disorganized course with unclear expectations. The syllabus lacked detail on grading, and criteria were never clearly explained. Attendance is strictly enforced, and missing one class can seriously hurt your grade. Heavy reliance on a curve made grading feel opaque and stressful.
grade is like a box of chocolates, u never know what you're gonna get from cyrus. Most subjectively graded course i've ever taken

Great experience with Cyrus, very caring prof. Will take time to listen to you, re explain lectures and answer questions even mid lecture. He requires participation and attendance but fair grading and does everything he can to help you succeed. Cyrus is also pretty funny and laid back, he is easy to talk to and sympathetic.

The class is tough, but Cyrus is anything but. He is caring, funny, and engaging. He tries to make the material relevant and easy to understand, especially for those who aren't familiar with it. He's clear with grading and provides ample opportunities to learn and reach out if you're struggling. Would definitely take again!
Cyrus condescending attitude can create a challenging learning environment, overshadowing their professional capabilities. Questionable ways of talking to students.

Cyrus is caring and wants his students to succeed. He takes the time to explain difficult concepts and invites speakers to present examples of their real-life applications. Participation is important, and homework is assigned occasionally. Overall, he made this class not only enriching but also genuinely enjoyable.

Cyrus is a great professor. He is firm attendance, writing unit of measure on homework and exams, and rounding, but he teaches the exam and there are no surprises if you study. He holds study sessions before exams and offers extra credit if you don't do well on the midterm. He loves teaching and cares about the success of his students.

I had a poor experience with Cyrus. He lectures quickly and his writing is fast and sloppy which makes it very hard to follow. In my experience communicating one-on-one with him, he was unempathetic, rude, and condescending. This was a very poor first impression of the Stern MBA. To be honest, his class makes me question the quality of Stern.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: wouldn't give you ten cents for his course- major Ahole
One word describes Mohebbi: conceited.

Took her the last semester of my undergraduate. The least I can say is that she severely stressed me out. Her guidelines were very unclear, her syllabus was a mess, and it seemed like she was just winging it every class. She was not open to feedback and would always blame everyone else instead of taking accountability.
Please get fired. Or quit.
run or zone out to stay sane

Genuinely THE WORST professor I've ever had. She makes constant changes to the syllabus about IMPORTANT things and DON'T TELL US, only telling one student and expecting it to trickle down. No accountability, heavy victim mentality, and overall pretentious mess that can dish but can't take. NYU needs to be held accountable; paying for THIS is wild.

Did not learn anything this entire semester. I wouldn't even call her a nice person because she's a typical white woman asserting her savior complex on the educational narrative. Once asked how to handle gang fighting in schools, she avoided my question entirely. Focused on saying environments dont shape kids, they shape who they are, even as teens

(pt.2) She literally used AI to write her emails to us. She didn't know how mass emailing worked and blamed it on us. She trauma dumps anytime the class is upset with her teaching and scheduling style. Frankly, she needs to be fired. She committed a micro-agression the first day she saw me. Oh, she also used AI to write her books...we had 2 read it
Like 20% of the work in this class actually correlates to the subject. The rest will in no way benefit our future careers. It's also unfortunate that these are core classes; no avoiding her.

I don't even know what to say. Her pedagogy makes no sense and every lecture feels like an incomplete thought. I do feel for her; I do believe she has a vision of her own, but I just don't think it's relevant for our classroom and the current climate.

Her homework is just a bunch of links to 5 minute youtube videos which are very elementary and kind of infantilizing. My only advice if you have to take this professor is to just let your eyes glaze over and try to mentally check out before every class so that you dont get any permanent brain damage
Me when I'm probably tenured so I don't have to gaf anymore

Worst professor I've had. She heavily encourages AI use & admitted multiple times her inability to complete basic tasks without it. Does not teach in the slightest. She just leaves you in groups the entirety of class to discuss middle school level youtube videos or her projects, which are poorly explained & assigned with extremely tight turnaround.

Like others said, group discussion learning style worked for me, but thats a misleading rep of her as a prof. Yes my group was great, but taking offense to a student asking for clarification is ironic + disappointing for an intro to education class. Very uncommunicative, says she feels "attacked" when students expressed concerns, her words not mine

I chose the 'hilarious' tag because it's hilarious how bad she is. Is she even trying? The entire semester was just a bunch of youtube links to 5 minute videos of random topics. Maybe she just wanted to talk about herself or something idk but I can't imagine she actually believes her teaching style is effective.

The professor spends most of the alloted time each lesson with students in group discussions; her reading materials included a 40-page booklet she wrote, and a host of videos by a group that advocates for "unschooling", a form of homeschooling that has statistically been shown to be less effective than even normal homeschooling.
Great teacher, learned a lot. Lots of discussions and collaborations that are student led and worked for me personally.

Professor McCallister is very knowledgable, but her teaching style is extremely hands-off to the point where one cannot help but wonder why classroom attendance is even required. Class is largely small-group discussions about the copious material required to be read before each class. Regrettably, I did not learn much from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor McCallister is truly a kind and well knowledgeable professor in Education. The class is very heavy in group discussions and she will pop in and out of tables to hear the conversations. She isn't very tech savvy so  what you see on BrightSpace might not always be true, always double check with her either in-person or through email.

McCallister is VERY kindhearted and knowledgeable! That being said, her hands-off style (read then discuss w/peers while she observes) was not effective for me, and not to the fault of my groupmates. Frequent confusion about assignment expectations and hosts a very tense, awkward classroom environment. With all due respect, I did not learn much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Cynthia is a really nice professor. But, she does not know how to handle the students and gives too much reading. You are put into groups and have to respond to each week's readings together which is hard if your group sucks. If you tell her about the group, she'll tell you to figure it out yourself. Super not helpful and I didn't learn anything.

Cynthia obviously knows what she's talking about, but had trouble conveying it to the class.  There was often mass confusion over the assignments and I didn't feel like I learned anything from the class.  She's very nice and available outside of class, but not my kind of professor
No personal boundaries

I have to be honest, cynthia is a really nice professor and she means well. However, I think that the course work can be pretty dated for a new media class, and the topics discussed stay very surface area. As a student in this class, I would have liked to learn more and stay concentrated on more relevant topics.

She is my adviser and my professor, and I think she's fantastic. In her "Digital Art & New Media" class we learn about all kinds of cool stuff and go to really cool and informative things around the city. She is kind, funny, and very interested in the subjects. There is regular homework, but it's more than manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you are into comics this is a must take. Cynthia is very flexible, fun and helpful. She is a great teacher.

Digital New Media class.  Class was interesting, cool field trips.  Must do readings and blog about them, but we never spoke about them in class. Blogging was annoying but class is easy and interesting.

digital new media; lectures very little, shows short movies and brings in lecturers a lot (professionals from the field). has lots of connections; takes us to the galleries in soho/chelsea. the only work you have to do outside of class is keep a blog about the class & some dinky timeline, which is really easy. class is long, though but also easy.
No Comments

Whoever rated this guy 5 stars must love reading. I have never been in a more difficult class in my life. This man does not seem to understand what is reasonable amount of work to assign full-time student. 1 complicated book a week + addtl readings, one quiz on the book at the top of class, weekly assignments, tri-weekly essays, films 🤦🏻
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor has very high expectations of his students, and grades accordingly. Compared to other professors in the Text and Ideas department, he assigns significantly more work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took him last semester for Technophilia and Its Discontents (Texts & Ideas) and I literally wish I could take the class again. I have never attended lectures for a class that were more interesting and worth listening to than his. Honestly the best class I've taken here at NYU and I miss it so bad.

If you can understand what he says then you might as well consider not doing college entirely. I have not met a professor who is so unclear in his speech, yet so proud in it. 

I think he has some trauma from being an immigrant and never quite fitting in during English class. Believe me, I am one too.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took his Global Shakespeare class. It took me a while to warm up to Patell just because of how we were kind of thrown into the course with having to read one Shakespeare play a week and submit responses to them. Its also a really discussion driven class. Final project was actually a ton of fun, though the 8 page final paper was not as fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Took Professor Patell for Texts & Ideas and I loved his class! Probably my favorite one among the classes I was taking for the semester. His lectures are so interesting to listen to. Lots of film-watching and reading (which, to be fair, is a given already considering that it's a Texts & Ideas class)

Cyrus is my academic mentor and lit professor. His phenomenal classes on the epic and drama traditions give you the cultural foundation to appreciate art and life more critically. That being said, the workload for his class is quite heavy; 100+ pages reading/ class, submitted 100+ pages of notes + two 10-paged essays for the sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I hate this guy. Pompous, arrogant, and useless. His lectures are boring and he think his own opinion is the only one that matters. A lot of reading, and quizzes that you will fail regardless of whether you read or not. TA's are really hard on essays. AVOID THIS GUY.

Patell is self-centered and tries to shove his opinion down the students' throats.  His lectures are soo arrogant and boring.  The class basically was not fun AT ALL but the topics could have been more interesting if the students were allowed to voice their opinions more.

Professor Patell is a joy to watch in lecture. For someone constantly preaching about "cosmopolitanism", he doesn't seem open to listening to other perspectives and definitely gives the impression that he thinks he's better than everyone else. Generally really interesting lectures though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Patell is a sweet and funny guy who clearly cares about what he is teaching. I took Cosmopolitan Imagination, for a core class, It was quite difficult. The context was very philosophical and required 100+ pages of reading every night.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Took his American Literature: From the Beginnings to the Civil War online when I was yr 11 in high school. Lots of reading, but great sense of humor, great insights, and overall great professor.
Dynamic and interesting but not always clear. Had him for AmLit I - he managed to hold my attention on a topic I hated, which I thank him for, but he still didn't make the class worthwhile for me.

My favorite teacher at NYU. I've had him for both Am Lit & ConWest, and want to take him for WritNY too. I was only intimidated by him bc of his incredible intellect, but once you visit office hours, he's very helpful. Much more reading than you will have for any other class, but his lectures are all worth it.  Take CYRUS!

There is a lot of reading, and attendance is mandatory, and this is not the easiest way to fulfill the con west requirement-grading is hard. BUT if you like literature viewed from a semi-anthropological perspective this class is interesting.  if that sounds boring, definitely don't!  also get a good TA and you'll be fine (they do all the grading).

Professor Patell is so interesting to listen to, never boring and so intelligent. He is very too and always engaging in lectures. A LOT of reading (books due every class) but the class is so worth it. He always draws connections through out the course, and you feel so smart afterward. Take his class!

One of the most intelligent, interesting, engaging and funny profs I've had. A ton of reading and in-depth analysis, but it's worth it. He makes even the boring material interesting and nuanced, and integrates modern media into class in a fun way. His lectures are well-structured and coherent. I recommend to all English majors!

There is an insane amount of reading, but Cyrus does an amazing job of unpacking the material and drawing parallels across subjects. He is well prepared, organized, funny, and interesting. He made reading Moby **** extremely interesting. This was my favorite class that semester. The TAs are smart and great as well.

I think he's great! There was a lot of reading for his class-like two books every week.  It was really hard to stay up to date on the reading, but you have to becasue he gives quizes on the reading every lecture.  Plus he's kinda really cute.  I really enjoyed his lectures! He's so freakin smart and a great teacher!
Very hard.  Not approachable.  Boring books.  INSANE amounts of reading.  Too high of expectations.

Patel is passionate about what he teaches and wants to engage his students with the topic at hand through modern parallels.  He's not for the work-shy and those adverse to sarcasm, but he really isn't unapproachable or unwilling to listen, he just likes to say it how it is.  I absolutely loves learning from him.
He cares about attendence sheet more than his students. He believes that everybody should be an English major and had read Bible and Moby **** 10 times.

Nice professors and good TA's. Knows what he's talking about and approachable but not very interesting, maybe it was due to the subject matter. He doesn't mind you sleeping in class but attendance is mandatory
Great class, and he and Prof. Waterman are the perfect pair to teach it. Always really passionate, insightful, interesting and funny. I love going to class.
Passionate and verbose

I've had Professor Patell for both ConWest and Writing NY. Though I found him incredibly intimidating for a time, a meeting with him during office hours completely changed my view. He is consistently brilliant, an engaging and passionate lecturer, a fair grader, and an unrelenting advocate of discourse.  Highly recommended!  Hope to have him again!
He is a good lecturer but he gives a lot of work and is a harsh grader.
He is rather arrogant, dismissive, and, what's worse, he underestimates the intelligence and independence of his students.
He is a great lecturer and i was never bored in his class even though i had him @ 8 in the morning. he is a fair grader and is very approachable.  He made even Moby Dick exciting and fun.
Good guy!  He might seem unapproachable and narcissistic, but in actuality he is extremely helpful and kind.  Don't be intimidated!

I've had Patel for ConWest and Writing NY. Star Wars nut, could be very funny. Lots and lots of work. Grading was pretty fair. A true academic, knows his stuff, but would do well to clarify what he's saying. I found him very approachable, visited him in office hours very often, explained things. Still, wouldn't recommend him to non-English majors.

Professor Patell is a hard grader and there will be a ton of reading in class. That said, I am really enjoying his class. He keeps the classes interesting, and knows a lot about the subject he's teaching. He's one of the best english teachers I've had and would recommend him to anyone who is interested in Am lit or needs to take it.

horrible.. and horribledon't know how he won an excellent teacher award, the committe who awarded it must have been on crack. He's arrogant, rude, and dismissive. He should pack his stuff back to Harvard.

Good lecturer, covers the material, but try not to get wowed by that.  Adjectives to describe him should include unapproachable, unhelpful, narcisistic, condescending, and closed-minded.  Not respectful of serious students.  Additionally, a seemingly deep-rooted authoritarian streak seems to cloud judgment and basic knowledge of NYU policies.

Ridiculous workload. Prepare to read 200 pages of the bible in one night. Brilliant man, but has difficulty conveying his thoughts to the class. Very egotistical and unapproachable. Take a different section of conwest, his class is not worth the stress.
cyrus.
heavy course load, but really great lectures; interseting as well as well organized.  not really very friendly outside of class though.

He's an absolutely amazing teacher. He uses all sorts of media (Star wars clips, anyone?) to explain difficult concepts. Every day as class starts he plays music associated with that day's lecture. He makes learning entertaining. I can't count how many times we all cracked up in his class. Not that it isn't hard- the homework load is insane (2 days to read a novel..) but it's worth it to have him as a teacher. A+++

I don't know why this man wins awards.  he is an awful advisor and all the others hate him.  He knows a lot, but he has no compassion or care for his students.  Stick to reasearch and leave us alone!  I don't know why people want him as a professor, rather

one of the best professors at nyu. work load is ridiculous but well worth it. he uses many kinds of media to demonstrate ideas. lectures are so interesting that you might even want to wake up for them. he can be intimidating to talk to.
Even though I almost never went to his class, I thought Professor Patel was one of the best teachers I'd ever had. I only wish I was together enough that semester to really get something out of it.
A genius. Made me fall in love with NYU's English program. A real professor, with new and exciting outlooks on relatively stale literary texts. But be prepared to work your ass off.
An outstanding lecturer, but the syllabus was far too overloaded. Get ready to read Uncle Tom's Cabin and Moby Dick in less than two weeks.

This man is brilliant. His lectures will amaze you. He's down to earth and funny which can be intimidating but he's incredibly helpful and knowledgeable on many things - not just literature. he's a pop culture buff.

Class is a little disorganized and unclear. You are graded by about three essays (lot of freedom with prompt), a quick group presentation, many forum posts, and a brief journal (15 entries). Do not expect to get 95% of your grades and feedback until the semester is well over. Participation is required. Otherwise, nice professor and very easy class

I'm writing this the day before our last class, and at this exact moment, we have NONE of our essays graded. The first one was due 2 months ago and she STILL has not graded it, along w other assignments. Tomorrow is our last class ever and I have no idea what my grade is. We have only met up for 11 (out of 28) classes this sem. V irresponsible

She's always late for classes, and she canceled classes frequently. She either tells us an hour before the class or after class. There was at least one time that we waited for her for half an hour in the room and she didn't show up. Our class is 8 AM! Never get feedback from her. Only had two writing assignments so far. Lots of forums and readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Please do not mistake my rating for a 1. It is actually a zero. The reviews on this page are so misleading it's criminal. She literally never shows up to class, so imagine our disappointment waking up for an 8 am, going to class, and then just leaving 30 minutes later. Work is brainless. Learned nothing. Avoid her class at all costs. Waste of money

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! She didn't show up to four classes in a row in person, and even when we went online (bc of corona), she was still 35 minutes late. She doesn't tell you in advance when she doesn't show up either, so she completely wastes your time. Her essay topics aren't that interesting. She also brags about herself a lot too
She had an easy course, and she is very inspirational with writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Such a sweet lady. The readings to prep before class are short and always interesting. Assigns fun and easy mini assignments that are a great grade boost (one was to go to a historical pub, another a very interesting and lesser known museum). She's super caring and always will help with essays if you need it. Let me rewrite one I did not do well on

She gives feedback to everything you write. I think it was an easy A for me because I was able to freely write how I felt. Writing about how the readings make you feel are a definite plus especially in all the writing she assigns you!

Her class is honestly super interesting. We have amazing readings and great discussions. She loves when you participate and attendance is mandatory. Super helpful if you visit her during office hours with your paper. She also lets you do multiple drafts if you didn't do so hot the first time. Genuinely wants to help you!
Prepare you write in your journal every week. Reading required. Easy class to pass. Really enjoyed it. Allows you to explore your own writing methods.

If I'm being honest avoid at all costs. gives very vague assignments with very vague feedback and expects perfection. office hours confuse me more. she always suddenly throws a big assignment at you and makes it due the next day. also always late to class herself, but if you show up late, she marks you tardy

I loved her. She is a tough grader when it comes to essays but she allows you to turn in as many drafts as you want. You will walk out of this class a much better writer. There's a lot of work in it when it comes to re-editing, reading, and writing forums but its all worth it in the end. Great class, and an excellent professor!

Absolutely loved her! She's so nice and really has a passion for what she's teaching. Super easy to reach out to. If you need anything just email her or ask her in class she'll help you out. Her paper topics were actually very interesting and challenged you just enough to make you dig deeper. Very fair grader and really cares about her students.

Very kind and helpful.  I never thought her grading was tough, just follow directions and ask for help if you need it.  Most of her essays involve imitating the style of things read in class, so just pay attention and you'll be fine.  Highly recommend.  :)
She is an amazing professor, and her personality alone makes me want to take her for Writing 2.  Her instruction and ability to relate our material to life is uncanny.  She won't disappoint.

Super nice and entertaining!  I personally don't think she's a tough grader, just follow directions on assignments and you'll get an A.  Sometimes vague, but you still do some fun and interesting stuff in class.  Definitely recommend.

The professor was terrible. She yelled at you for asking students next to you for help during class. She posts homework assign. online every so often, but doesn't inform you. Good luck checking everyday to realize no homework is due til the one day you miss and it's past due. She doesn't teach much. Interview final midterm homework and class part.
I knew more spanish before this course than I do now.

Worst teacher I have ever had. Showed up to every class, participated like crazy, tried as hard as I could. When she gave me a C for my final grade, she told me I put no effort into the class. Ugh. Plus she never teaches. She just reads out of a book. I'm posting this just so no one else has to suffer through an awful semester with this teacher.

He lectures like he's gossiping, but the gossip is history. He makes amazing connections that genuinely engage the class. He doesn't just assign readings but also podcasts and videos too. I wish I had more chances to take his classes.
I wish I could have him teach every class. He has the most random facts stored in his brain, yet they all somehow correlate to the topic of discussion. Take his class!

gosh robert davis is such a delight, and a must have at nyu. he so clearly knows what hes talking about and his assignments are very open where you can do whatever. theres even a minecraft assignment that i loved. his lectures are also very fun and open to all students so it feels more like a discussion. would love to have him again.

It's very clear that Professor Davis cares about sharing his knowledge and passion for theater and history with his students! He is very knowledgable and is willing to open up class discussions on any topics relating to the course which students are curious about, his classroom always had a welcoming environment full of participation.

I took Fairs Museums Sideshows for J term. Robert is the best teacher at NYU.  I took his Astor place class and wrote a review then too. He's so funny and made J-term bearable. He does love his chalk board and Im more of a whiteboard kind of guy but to each their own. I asked if we could see an extra museum and he graciously allowed us too.  10/10

Robert is an amazing professor. After taking two classes with him I can confidently say that he is by far the best professor I have had at NYU. His classes are always interesting and engaging. His assignments are very manageable and he is very understanding and flexible with due dates. Please take one of his classes if you can!

Prof Davis is really nice and caring. He always gives a super clear instruction on his assignments and grades them generously. The lectures are interesting and inspirational. Just take his classes if you can!

Such a nice guy super funny and cares about his students. I took the Astor Place riot class and it was super interesting. I got covid and emailed him if i could get an extension he responded right away(always responds right away) and he said i could wait till i got better to turn it in. One of the best professors I've had at NYU
So funny, relatable, passionate, and caring. Incredibly knowledgeable and a great professor

Robert is one of the best professors Ive had during my college career. Incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the class subject, assigns useful readings, super woke, funny, relatable, really cares about his students, and is obsessed with TV which is always a fun tangent to go off on! If you have a chance to take a class with Robert, do it.

Prof Davis is extremely approachable and down to earth, clearly passionate about what he teaches, and overall a good time. He teaches in a style that is easily understandable and very conversational, and is extremely open and encouraging of any questions. The class is always kept interesting. The best theatre studies professor you could ask for!

He demystifies the notion of "professor" and is super down-to-earth and incredibly knowledgable in an accessible way. Phenomenal. Would recommend. Honestly even if the subject doesn't really interest you.

Would 100% take another one of his classes. He's engaging, hilarious, & knows how to present the material in a way that makes it easier for students to understand w/o dumbing it down. There's a decent amount of reading & while you may be able to pass  w/o doing all of it you'll get so much more out of the class if you do.

He is a great and entertaining teacher. He really talks with the class, which leads to a lot of interesting tangents. He is EXTREMELY knowledgeable about the 19th century. There was a lot of reading we had to do, but it's mostly just reading plays, and you can get away with not doing it. I strongly recommend this class.

Dr. Robert Davis is an AWESOME teacher. He's really knowledgable about the subject and makes it fun and interesting to learn. I'm so glad I took this class with him and I'm sad it was only for a J-Term. Take his classes if you can!
Very humane professor. A true pleasure to learn from. Witty, open to questions, and very learned. Made theater theory palatable. Not an  easy deed.

Really cool teacher who tries to make the class interesting and relevant. Very relatable person - funny. Readings for every class but most are short enough and at least semi-interesting. Good class discussions - never boring. Highly recommend. Def. taking a class of his again
Super interesting, fun class, not bogged down with assignments, totally recommend him

Robert is a great teacher, he's clearly passionate about theatre history and it's hard not to catch the bug. He makes every lecture interesting, especially with his sometimes lengthy off-topic rants. Would take any of his other classes in a heartbeat.

Took Theatre in Ancient Greece with him.  He's great!  Knows more about the subject than maybe anyone else alive and is a genuinely funny, smart, caring guy.  Has a performance project which is awesome, and is incredibly quick to respond to emails etc.

I have no idea who wrote those positive comments, maybe himself.  6 essay tasks, extremely boring lecture, for the feedback you get from essays you are going to see a question mark on every paragraph. 

If you are interested into "liberal studies", then yes go take his class, maybe you will find it interesting. 

If you simply want easy A, AVOID!
BY FARRRRRR BEST TEACHER I've had at NYU. you will benefit from his class very much.

Dr. Paliwoda is definitely interesting. He's unlike any professor I've had here so far, but with that being said, PLEASE TAKE HIM!! Oh my god he's so good. His lectures are so insightful, and I left every class questioning what I already know about the world. He can be a little intimidating, but if you get to know him and talk to him, he's amazing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor who genuinely wants to see you learn. He's also very passionate about his class. I struggled at the beginning but he let me revise my work which was really nice. Lecture driven, not too much reading. He assigns a lot of papers though, but its generally not too demanding. Fav prof this semester, maybe so far in my time at NYU.

Professor Paliwoda is so sweet and genuinely such an amazing professor. His class is about War, something he is very passionate about, and he makes his lectures very interesting. He is big on participation, and there are 6 "papers" but some are only 2 pages minimum so it is not that bad. Do take this class, it is so interesting and not very hard!

Paliwoda gives great lectures and puts a lot of effort into each one. All about war btw. He gives a bunch of papers tho (7). Way more than any other professor for this kind of class. His grading and feedback is very unclear. He write the same things on each of my papers and I feel like he would just come up with a grade for them outta thin air.
Big yapper but nice guy

You can really tell he cares about the content he teaches with all his heart. He is so inspirational. The whole class is based on the topic of war, so if this is something that may be triggering or upsetting, would not recommend. I learned a lot. Participate and share your thoughts because he cares! All tests out of class. Not the easiest grader.

He is a very passionate lecturer and clearly cares about what he teaches and his students. His grading criteria aren't too clear but he is very accessible outside of class (via Zoom meetings whenever he is available) and always answers emails very promptly.
Definitely would take again.

Amazing passionate professor. If you genuinely want to learn this is the professor for you. He will give amazing lectures and he deserves students who want to engage. You *can* take him if you just want a nice relatively easy professor but if you just want to just sit on your laptop the whole time (not that you couldn't) Id pick a different proff.

Dr. Paliwoda is my favorite LS professor! He is genuinely passionate about what he teaches that it makes you want to actively listen. Our class only focused on war and the inhumanity/humanity of it, so be careful if this is a sensitive topic for you (or if you're more interested in the format of other AC classes where it's mostly literature based)

Professor Paliwoda is a lovely professor who is willing to talk to you even on weekend if needed and takes care of the students. His class does have a lot of writing (all the grade comes from writing). However, if you go to class, and listen to his lecture, you will be fine. Attendance is not required. Overall recommended
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A pretty good prof who is very interested and well versed in his class topic; however, his class topic, war, is pretty depressing. So be warned if you don't want to learn about the horrors of war pls do not take this class
Overall pretty good and patient

I just wanted to warn other ls students that this class is only about war. Every artwork and lecture revolves around its horrors. I sincerely wish that  would have sent us an email or something ahead of time instead of waiting till the first day to reveal this. Me and many others are now scrambling to find another acm class when most are closed

Great professor with heart in the right place. Can ramble a bit too much sometimes, but that's only because he's passionate. Very understanding and a fairly easy grader. Requires a lot of introspective work so prepare for that. The only downside: he's pretty set on his topics and does not give one much room to choose, but I guess that's college.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have ever had. Caring, passionate, professional. He has a lot of stories waiting for you to discover. Take his class and talk to him after class. He will be a great mentor for life if you can bond with him.
Professor Paliwoda is certainly passionate about his studies and will lead you into that mood. The class was great but I think he is not an easy grader. Need to work hard to get an A.

Dr. Paliwoda was an incredibly caring professor whose course was quirky and inspiring, connecting often to the city. His homework is minimal but interesting, and his grading is clear and fair. He was also very accessible outside of class and office hours were always very helpful. Essays were personal and the topics broad enough to allow creativity.
The class is all about war, so it can be a bit depressing. However, I learned a lot and was exposed to a lot of new things. There are next to no tests/quizzes, besides the final, and only two papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: He is an easy grader but his lectures are boring and sometimes depressing
His lecture is usually boring but he's chill about late assignments. He takes attendance sometimes

subject material was really interesting, but the classes got a bit repetitive sometimes. He's really nice, and if you hand in your paper a bit late he's chill about it. Lots of papers though, most of them short (1/2 pages) but a couple long . but he's an easy grader, i got an A on my first paper. also  guest speaker. Def participate he loves it
Professor Paliwoda is not exactly inspiring, but an easy A. We watched some interesting movies in class. If you answer questions in class, he'll like you. Easy grader.

Prof. Paliwoda was an exceptional Writing I professor. The course theme of Hope and Cynicism was hugely interesting and offered flexibility in terms of paper topics. There are readings for each class, but they are light and interesting. I went to office hours before each paper was due and always got super helpful feedback. Very much recommend.
Good class, if you do your homework, it helps prepare you for your exams. Almost everyone get passing grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easier than other fundamental algorithms courses at courant. He curves the grade. Doing his assignments on your own is the key to an A in this course, if u do your assignments , your exam becomes way easier.

Extremely boring monotone voice, fought myself to stay awake. HWs are okay, definitely prep you for exams. Coding assignments are fine just make sure to check your code runs through terminal as standard. Exams were okay, he's a very fair grader. You're expected to read the content before class which will help you understand concepts thoroughly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor who gives clear lectures about AI. Around 8 theory-based problem sets and 4 coding assignments. Discussed many topics throughout the semester. Also, there are a lot of questions during the midterm and final. If you do the HWs carefully, you can do very well through exams and get a good grade

Not the best prof I met but definitely a good choice for an online class. Clear slides, useful assignments and lecture recordings help a lot with study. Ernie himself is quite helpful and responds to emails pretty quickly. The curve was awesome when we had an a** prof Canziani who made the final average to be 55. Take his course without Canziani!

I think his is a really good professor, who knows how to teach students. His slides are very detailed and he goes in depth with the examples. He also takes his time to repeat information when it's not clear or understandable. The information itself can be a little confusing but if you rewatch the lecture and the reread the notes you'll do well.

Clear lectures, super accessible, and great assignments, Ernie is beyond perfect. the only thing he has done wrong in this whole semester was letting Alfredo Canziani teach the second half of the course
Well taught lectures and well crafted assignments.
Ernest, we miss you! Please come back for us
Bettern than Alfredo Canziani!!!
Clear lectures/lecture slides & fairly easy assignments. Graded homework in a timely fashion & stayed responsive on Campuswire. Wish he taught the entire course rather than just the first half.
Nice professor, respond very quick.
His lectures are clear, although his handwriting can be incomprehensible. The assignments and exams are relatively easy compared to other FA professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Prof. Davis focuses more on ideas behind algs rather than formal proof of correctness or time complexity.
Workload is light. Some probs are tricky but he and TAs are willing to help you. 
He provides clear notes on the website.
Mid is easy, while final is hard. But no question is harder than the most difficult one in hwk. He will curve the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Highly recommend AI with Professor Ernest. He explains every concept very clearly with examples and his lectures are easy to follow. He cares more about your learning than giving hard homework or exams. Most of students in my class got very good grades. Take it if you are even remotely curious about AI!

Davis is a great teacher. I felt very confident entering his exams based on my understanding of the hw and lectures. However, his exams are long and arduous. Since 40% of your grade is hw, you can succeed but only if you are very committed to the hw.

Excellent lecture slides that he uploads. Best pseudocode I've ever seen, very straightforward to understand and easily translatable to actual code. He's not the bubbliest prof, but definitely smart and thoughtful in his teaching. Reasonable workload that ensures you learn how to apply your knowledge. One of the better ones at NYU for CS.
Everything easy to understand. Average amount of homework. No strict mathematics.

One of the best professors I've ever had at NYU. His lectures are super easy to understand. The course is well balanced, lecture slides are clear and concise. Homeworks are not hard, takes only a decent amount of work. Documents for programming assignments are super clear and always come with lots of sample outputs which is great. 10 out of 10!
Lectures may get boring. But he gives good homework, and is always ready to help outside class.
Proficient in his domain, but boring teaching and terrible hand writting. He teaches fast as if you have already understood the algorithm like kim.

Prof Davis is very knowledgeable and entertains all your questions no matter how many times you bother him. Unfortunately his lectures are not to the point. He does not teach very well. What he teaches in class is not at all exam oriented. The course is very tough so are the assignments and final exam. Your grade depends on the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: AI with Prof. Davis was fine. Lectures can be a bit dry at times, but the order of topics makes sense and Prof. Davis describes most topics pretty clearly. The problem sets and programming assignments are not too bad, the latter might take some time depending. The final was ok, the class is more of a survey though. Don't expect heavy math.

Lectures are boring but clear. His online lecture notes are amazing! If you miss something in lecture, almost always in his notes. You can turn in homework a week late and still get 90% which makes time management easier. He doesn't mind if you ask questions.
Professor Davis is one of the nicest professors I've ever met. He is also very responsive if you have any questions.
I took his data structures class. The tests were very easy and the grading was incredibley lenient. Unfortunately, he is not a very good teacher, so be prepared to teach yourself.

Professor Davis's smart and easygoing, but a terrible teacher. His lectures aren't clear and won't help you satisfactorily understand the basic code you'll need to create data structures. The assigned textbook is also poorly written, making it harder to understand some otherwise understandable data structures concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't clear and don't help with learning the material. You would do better to skip class and just read the notes on the course website. He assigns weekly homeworks (4-5 short problems) and bi-weekly programming assignments (more in-depth). Exams are of average difficulty. It's manageable, but I definitely wouldn't take his class again

He is among the most boring professors I've ever had to endure. While the course is not hard, his teaching style makes it dense and dull. The textbook he prescribes is almost unintelligible. Standoffish on emails, though he does respond promptly. Overall, avoid if you can.

I took Fundamental Algorithms with him during the summer. His lecture style is pretty dry and he's all business and focuses only on the material at hand. He's not really a jovial type of professor even during office hours. However, he does make himself available to answer any questions and one-on-one I found him easier to understand.
Clear, interesting lectures. Very smart and informative. Interesting assignments and very clear expectations.

This guy sure knows how to make a roomful of people drowsy. Attendance is not taken for lecture or recitation. Davis seems like a funny, sort of sarcastic guy, but he clearly has a hard time lecturing a room full of students. He's mostly talking to himself up there. Avoid.

Avoid at all costs, no idea how to teach. Nice guy, but talks to himself, doesn't answer questions, but does reply to emails quick. If you are not 100percent confident coming into this class, do not take it

Responds to emails quickly, posts clear online notes for each lecture, allows makeup exams for schedule conflicts, provides lots of visuals. He doesn't try to "spice up" his classes with jokes or anecdotes, so if you don't like programming, you probably won't like him, but I felt he made the subject itself interesting and always enjoyed class.
I really love this professor, if you have to take spanish please take him he is the best

Enrique was such a nice professor, he genuinely cares about his students and tries to teach in a fun way. There were 3 exams a few papers with homework assignments and a presentation. The class was not hard, just had to put in some work in. There are going to be 3 classes per week so a little bit more workload.
Fun teacher, interactive class, participation heavy, 3 exams, 2 presentations (10 minutes), few and easy hw assignments

Cool guy! He has a thick Cuban accent but you'll get used to it. He cares about his students and wants to see them succeed. Prepare yourself for full language immersion. He doesn't speak English but can understand it. There is a lot of homework. It's not necessarily hard, but you will have homework and readings three times a week. Vale la Pena!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Enrique is so funny and kind. We just go to class and talk about things. It's a super chill class, I'd highly recommend.
Professor Del Risco is unmatched. He is so funny and truly cares about all of his students. I looked foward to his class every week! Take him for any Spanish class trust me he's the absolute best.

Had him for a native speakers class and enjoyed his teaching. He is very caring, funny, and understanding, and tries to make sure each student learns something in his class. Some have trouble with his accent, but you can ask him nearly anything and he'll respond, so if you have trouble understanding, don't be shy. Looked forward to class every day.

My favorite professor EVER. You can tell that he makes an effort to teach material that is engaging, thoughtful, and entertaining. He really wants his students to learn and will make every effort to ensure that you do. You'll never be bored in his class. Definitely take a course with him if you ever get the chance!

If ur looking for a prof to get Spanish out of the way like I did, def take Del Risco. Funny guy and treated everyone like he was their good friend. Doesn't check attendance, basically gives you full credit on hw's if u just do them, and gives good grades for essays, projects, and participation. Doing the bare minimum is good enough for this class.

Enrique is an amazing guy, he treats you like a friend. He loves everything related to history and Latin America, he is really passionate about it. Lots of HW, and projects, but hey this is a course for natives. Do the projects and participate, don't worry much about HW, but READ ALL the texts from the syllabus. He is pretty clear on what he wants.

If you just want to be done with your foreign language requirement, Enrique is amazing. I never understood his accent, didn't go for 80% of the classes, or submit my project, and basically gave up halfway through the semester. But Enrique understands, and Enrique saves your freaking hide. Not the hero I deserved, but boy was he the hero I needed.

If you need 1 more Spanish class for the language requirement, TAKE ENRIQUE. He doesn't check HW, doesn't take attendance, gives good participation grades even if you don't participate. He is the easiest Spanish prof at NYU, but he is also a cool guy as well. He appreciates if you participate, but really doesn't penalize your grade if you don't.

Great great great professor. Really knows his stuff and makes the class incredibly fun. This was the only class that I actually enjoyed going to. Doesn't really require that you do the homework or go to every class,

Great teacher. Class work is fairly simple. He really wants the students to step out of their comfort zone and think. Makes the subject much more interesting. Just go to class. LOVED the cuban accent.

Enrique is by far the greatest spanish prof. ever. He's ridiculously easy and really helpful. He's always got great stories to tell, you never get bored, and he's an easy grader. Homework: not really required. For those of you taking spanish because its required, he knows you're there for that and doesn't give you ****.

Let's face it. Intm2 Spanish sucks, no matter who you get. But getting Enrique helps! Sure, he is really hard to understand. I actually never understood a word out of his mouth. But we didn't follow the syllabus, I skipped class all the time, and I didn't really learn anything. And I got an A- and I'm done with Spanish forever. Take Enrique!

While he is a nice guy that jokes around a lot, he was not always in touch with the syllabus/what was required of the class, making assignments confusing. A little more sensitivity to non-native speakers would have been appreciated.

Enrique Del Risco is a very nice guy who really does have your best interest at heart, but he has a Cuban accent and speaks so fast that it's really hard to understand him. His class isn't fabulous, but it certainly isn't horrible. To get the best out of it ASK QUESTIONS
He is a little pretentious but clearly smart.

Extremely rigorous and demanding course, but also one of the most intellectually rewarding classes I've taken. If a negative review is based solely on strict grading, I don't think that's a fair reason. I didn't do well in this class, but that does not take away from the fact that Professor Ray is a truly dedicated and thoughtful instructor.
eye-opening course but very difficult. problem sets and exams are difficult, one of the harder courses I have taken at nyu
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good at explaining

Tough class, but the Professor is a great lecturer and makes complex topics easy to understand. The problem sets are quite difficult, but are important to understand for the exams. Accessible outside of class. I missed an exam due to a personal issue and he was very helpful in trying to accommodate me on a short notice.

I was the worst student in his class. Missed the first midterm, did poorly on the 2nd, did ok on the finals, and somehow he still gave me a passing grade. For people who show up to class, he always try to make sure we understand before moving on. Course material is definitely hard, but the negative reviews about his character are not justifiable.

One of the best econ professors I've had. Homeworks are hard and so are the exams. But he teaches very well and if you study hard, you'll understand the concepts. Also, go to office hours. It definitely helped me.
Debraj is a brilliant professor, and he has a very deep understanding of economic theory in Development Economics.

Not an easy class but looking back, I really learned a lot of useful tools from it. He explains all the math in class so people who commented about him not explaining anything probably didn't go to his lectures to start with. TA is also really helpful. I would recommend it to people who want to learn.
beware nonmales

He is a very caring professor and provides lots of feedbacks if you go to his office hours. This class is not easy but if you put in your work and really understands the material, you'll be fine. also, his lectures are really fun and organized. He explains the concepts very clearly, all the math are explained in class, not in the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
11% of A.
Hw question are extremely difficult.
Lecture is tough and sometime bland but not entirely his fault

Lecture heavy homework HEAVIER, and he bombs you with emails all the time. He never teach the math in his exams and homework, and TA grades harshly. Also his questions contain math models that are not convincing at all. His class is for those who ONLY take one class per semester. Also too many Econometrics there, which I don't understand why.
24 queschuns over break is he ffr
0gr3 h3 !$ :PPP

Good person and good teaching. But the content is very difficult and abstract; he does not use econ grading so it's possible for everyone to get an A/C. It all depends on the problem sets (grading very harshly) and three exams (also very difficult). Choose him if you don't care that much about getting a good grade.

Good professor, but not an easy course so don't have too high expectations on good grades. Grader is very tough. His lecture are funny so if you really like development econ and likes theorists, 323 would be a good class. But it's not very practical and most concepts are very abstract. He is a very nice person.

Hands down my favorite Econ professor at NYU! While lectures aren't mandatory, they're incredibly informative and inspiring. He genuinely cares for his students and is super supportive even outside of class. The course is math heavy and not at all an easy A, but still a really wonderful experience overall!

If you love expressive, kind and funny professor, you will love Ray. The class is very difficult but not impossible if you are truly interested in the condition of developing countries. Math matters, but econ intuition matters more. He write his own textbook, which is actually quite good. I swear he is a comedian in disguise also. Great experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easily one of the most passionate, knowledgable, caring NYU Econ professor but EXTREMELY difficult problem sets & exams (which are the only graded components). Attendance isn't mandatory but lectures are crucial to understanding the seriously math-heavy material. This class is def meant for Econ Theory and not Policy, so take the class to learn

Prof Ray is extremely intelligent, approachable, and delightful. The class is theory- and math-heavy. However, Debraj is wonderful at explaining the concepts and makes a conscious effort to answer all doubts. Homework and exams are not easy and require some serious effort. I learnt a lot from the class and Debraj himself. A wonderful class overall!

Explains very well, is engaging and accessible, but has tough problem sets and expects you to work in order to learn. Fair grader, reasonable tests. Overall, the best econ class and econ prof I've had at NYU.
Favorite prof in my first semester in NYU. She is so nice, and help me a lot with my intellectual thinking process .

A very nice professor. I like her very much. The deadline she posted on the syllabus is not the final deadline. She may change the deadline after she reads our essay. She also gives recommendations to our drafts, so we can make it better.
Professor Martone is the best!!!

She is soooooo nice! Professor Martone is the reason I want to stay in NYU. She gave her students Christmas gift & candy in the last class at Fall semester. I really want to become friends with her. Helpful & Friendly ! so lucky to meet her as a freshman

Really really good professor. Very accessible outside class, caring and inspiring. She helps me a lot during one to one conferences. Really nice professor. Not a hard grader. If you put effort in writing, you will get a pretty good feedback. Would definitely take her class again if possible!
She is super nice and caring! Definitely take her if you can. She is not a hard grader

Actually if I had another chance I would want to try another professor, but Dr. Martone is definitely a good professor. She really inspired me during classes. She has a really high standard, so prepare to see some unpleasant grades.

I would recommend her class, had her for International Writing 1, instructions are usually lengthy but most are unclear. But she wants to help everyone and knows what she is doing. She takes time to meet with every student and gives good feedback. grading i think is okay. try not to miss class but if you do miss a few times it will be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She's great. By far the best writing teacher here. She is VERY helpful, she will meet with you to discuss your writing if you think you need it. If she thought we were working hard and still couldn't get it, she extended the deadline of the final essays (by more than a week sometimes). She's not a hard grader.
really helpful. as an international students whose english is rather poor. she offered me a lot of help and improve my writing. with a great sense of responsibility  ps. her office is awesome.

She is very approachable and easygoing though she sometimes leaves a first impression of sternness...She is not strict on deadlines which is rather important in courses like writing the essay. Try to be nice with her and she will show her nice part. A good friend.

Very helpful teacher who is really interested in seeing her students grow as writers. She is flexible with deadlines and understanding if work is submitted late or we are unable to attend classes due to valid reasons. I've spoken to her about stuffs outside of class and she is just like a friend who is rather approachable.

She is a very inspiring teacher, her teaching methods vary from photos, movies,artwork,  textbooks but her goal is very clear. She enjoys meeting her students and is very patient in hearing your opinion; she also do art walk to gallery after class. Great Professor. Director of the program so she has a good understanding of the goal of the program.
Really helped in improving my writing. She works with us throughout the essays so we know what needs to be done yet we have the creative freedom to reach the goal through our own vista.

Denice is the co-chair of the expository writing department, knows what she's doing. She compiled the Business and its Publics book this year. I've always found her to be very specific about what she wants in her essays and if you can do that and do it well, you get an A.
Kind, respectful, passionate. A great example of how competent nyu tisch teachers can be.

Christina is so amazing! You receive so many invaluable resources from her Producing a Short Screenplay class. She's easily accessible outside of class and just a very kind and caring person.

The lectures were all so helpful and informative and the projects actually help you learn. Highly recommend taking her if you get the chance!
Maybe the sweetest professor alive. So knowledgeable and caring. LOVE HER!

She gives you resources you will use for life! Im producing a film because she allows students to pitch their ideas. The film I'm producing for is no longer taking her class and still uses her google drive! LOVE HER! CANNOT RECOMMEND MORE

If you hate this woman you are probably a psychopath, because she is honestly the sweetest person ever. I've never met a better professor than Christina. She is EXTREMELY organized, always on top of things, gives thorough feedbacks and has organized so many resources for us to utilize for the rest of our lives. AND she genuinely cares about us.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very organized and inspirational professor. Some lectures can get to feel a little dull, but the amount of information and resources she provides are invaluable.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She can share a lot of experiences as a producer in the industry. She is very kind and fun. The homework is quite useful for students to practice what learned in the class. She is quite helpful on keeping student on track. She gives detail feedbacks. The class is quite informational and will make you learn a lot if you are a beginner.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The second week of class I had an emergency and missed a  hands-on unit. At office hours, she reserved a conference room for me  for a Zoom call and spent 90 minutes going over the entire unit and assignment, stopping any time I had questions. She truly cares about her students and teaching and it shows with her compassionate-yet-productive matter.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Christina might be one of the best professors I have had during my years at NYU. Both she and her classes are amazing.
Her producing class is so informative and crucial for the film world, everyone should take it, even if they don't want to produce.
She is so supportive, understanding, caring and experienced. She is a gem. Take her class!

Christina's Producing the Short Screenplay class should be mandatory for all ftv students. Her class folder is so valuable, and her lectures are so informative and clear. She teaches you everything you need to know about producing and gives you DETAILED feedback on every assignment. She's also the nicest person and can give you very good advice.

Christina is a fantastic professor. Her lectures actually teach you things that you'll use in a career in the film industry. She also is willing to give you advice for projects that have nothing to do with class, and gives amazing feedback on the assignments. Her class is the best I have taken at Tisch so far.

Christina is the best. She is extremely helpful and gives great advice. She responds to emails very fast and has folders with all the information you could ever need for producing. Incredible professor, very kind and thoughtful. If you can take her, do it.

I came to this class not knowing anything about production, and Professor Dehaven has helped/inspired me learn so much! I would definitely take her again and I really wish she taught some other classes too. She also gives amazing feedback on your assignments!

Professor DeHaven was extremely helpful and brought a lot of personal experience to class discussion. She also provided many helpful materials and guest lecturers which could not be found outside of class.
She should be thankful we're not allowed access to the balconies. Memorize 988 before having her as a professor.

I took Prof. Williams's class last semester and enjoyed it! We were usually assigned under 10 pages to read per class. She expected everyone to come prepared to participate, but since the readings were short it felt very manageable. Overall class discussions were really fun and engaging. We only had 3 essays, and I thought she graded very fairly.
quite stubborn.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor provides unclear instructions, grades extremely based off of subjectiveness, and is extremely stubborn. Would not ever take again, please don't take this writing course, choose someone else if they are avaliable. Not to mention the amount of essays you have to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: DO. NOT. TAKE. She won't agree w any opinion that doesn't align w her own & refuses debate against her opinions. She gives extremely bad feedback trying to get u to rewrite ur paper to align with her ideas. I've never met a prof w such an active interest in verbally diminishing her own students. if u value ur mental health at all do NOT take her.

DO NOT TAKE. My commons had been removed 3 times, yet I am still here to common. DO NOT TAKE. She is trying to implant her ideology into you, and if you don't accept it, you end up with bad grades and attitudes. Grading also doesn't make sense. I was fooled by the high rate of commons to take her class. Please trust me, DO NOT TAKE

To all of those thinking about taking Professor Williams: If you feel that you are an extremely strong writer, take her. I got an A in this class because I am a very good writer, but I still had to put a lot of work in to get an A. The class period itself is fine, you just talk about the reading. If you aren't an incredible writer take someone else

Extreme subjective grading. My essays are degraded into a B or B- simply because she didn't agree with my ideas. While the feedbacks are not instructions to improve your writing, it is just a guideline to write in her favor. Do Not Take, trust me, I don't know why there are so many 5's.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Grading is very subjective. You don't know what she wants to see. If you happen to match her ideas, the score will be high, but if not, you will get the lowest score. That doesn't happen if you put the same effort in other professor's class. If you have to take her class, you should talk to her more to guess what opinions she wants to see.

This professor is unnecessarily harsh and makes grading feel more like a punishment than an evaluation of learning. Expectations are vague. If you're looking for a class where effort is appreciated, this is NOT it. Would not recommend unless you like frustration and unfair grading.

Criteria are extremely vague—three lines of text, leaving you unsure of what she wants. She offers chances for revisions, but her feedback only consists of marking everything as "unclear and confusing." Even if you revise and clarify everything she suggests, the shockingly low grade—unlike anything you've received in other classes—doesn't improve…
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally love Professor Williams. She is beyond prepared to teach freshmans at nyu and she will 200% improve your writing skills as long as you put in the effort. I love her teaching style and she is very personable. Get to know her as a person outside of the academic environment! She is 100%  miss world wide, practically been everywhere :)

I can't recommend this professor enough. Her class discussions are all interesting, and she's very helpful at giving feedback on papers. In total there were 3 essays over the semester and she really helps you revise each one. This class certainly isn't an easy A but the workload is very manageable and the class is overall very rewarding.

My favorite professor! She is genuienly the best. She also somehow creates an environment in which you start to build friendships and get really comfortable in her class and with the people in it. LOVE HER!! Also she taught in NYU Abu Dhabi which makes her so fascinating, she brings in so many writing pieces from different cultures.

One of my favorite LS professors EVER! So caring and tries to be funny. Discussion posts for homework and we discuss readings in class, so be prepared to read and participate. Readings are actually fun and interesting. Allows paper resubmissions for a better grade. Easy A as long as you do the work, and try. TAKE HER YOU WILL NOT REGRET!!!

The best professor. learned so much from her. Looked forward to every class. would take it over and over again. There were three essays and they were all so much fun to writeI would write my first draft, go to her office hours, She would help me make it better, and I would finish it myself. She's ] smart and has a lot to share. Take if you can!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The goat

A very intelligent professor who actually stimulates your brain. Tough grader but she forces you to be a better writer. There's no way you come out of this class without learning something. Very funny and didn't give too much hw.
