You can tell she genuinely acres about her students. Great lectures and great readings. There are three papers (six pages each minimum) and there are discussion posts. Would overall recommend her to anyone looking for a professor to make their time at NYU worth awhile.

Professor Williams is the nicest professor I've taken. Although stern at times, overall she is a great professor and an even better person. Her readings were engaging, prompting great discussions in class, and feedback on papers and smaller assignments was unmatched. Workload isn't the worst, with short written responses to readings and 3 papers.

She's probably my favorite prof from freshman year. :) Williams forces you to better your writing. Her comments and instructions for papers are tough, but she wants your final papers to be amazing! You must put a lot of reading and work into the assignments, but with her help, your writing becomes succint/clear. I wish I could take her class again!

I learned so much from Williams this semester. She teaches you to truly write like a college student. Short weekly writing assignments and 2 big research papers. She makes you work hard for an A but she's so worth it. Always willing to meet and discuss papers. Shes super nice and down to earth.

She is an amazing Professor. She is funny and manages to keep you interesting throughout the entire class and semester.  You do have to do the readings, but she gives Dracula and Frankenstein to read which is amazing.

My experience is unfortunately fully in line with the other review here.
I attended the Risk and Change Management course at NYU. There was no textbook, no hand-outs, and no PowerPoints. The lack of materials made the course seem very unstructured, and it made studying for exams extremely difficult.
worst instructor I've ever encountered

Never understood what she wanted. She expects students to know words and phrases that she should be teaching. Her classes are all over the place. She constantly has students learn concepts themselves & then present them. I understand she tried to make the class Agile, but I don't think it worked. Probably one of my most infuriating professors

Never, never take her class! All course materials were sent via email and she always needed to correct herself several times. Poor PPTs -- some words are even placed out of the page and when she sent the pdf to me, I can't even see those words. No homework feedbacks, only grades. And the phrase she most often says is 'do not send me the email!!!'

Incredible professor who genuinely cares about her students and their future success. She consistently makes herself available, takes time to support each student, and creates an environment where you feel encouraged to grow. Assignments are thoughtful and highly applicable to real-world, which makes the work feel meaningful rather than busywork.

Dr. Dina is truly my favorite professor at NYU! She's engaging, knows her stuff, gives great feedback and above all else, actually cares about her students. She wants us to do well and gain something from our education. She's one of the few that makes me feel like the amount we pay per credit is worth it. 100/10 would recommend taking her classes!

She teaches nothing. And there are a lot of readings and videos to watch. It sometimes feels as though students are being treated more like employees facing potential legal consequences, and the tone of the emails can come across as somewhat intimidating.

Too many mandatory group meetings and theres a group project. Directions to projects are unclear and if you get a bad partner in the group- dont think she'll help out. I am usually an A+ student and I was unfortunate to have a bad group member and even though she was informed we received a C- because that person did not carry their own weight,
A lot of feedbacks on essays, very specific. She's very nice.
Professir Dent seems to be wired or mean at the first class, but actually she does not perform that way. Overall she is friendly while the load of hw is kinda heavy.
Terrible professor and rude person

Her homework is quite messy, and she can't let you go to the bathroom during class. Attendance is mandatory, including sick leave.But she's very caring outside the class, but I don't think I can learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Dent is responsible and warm. She gives clear feedback and is willing to help you with your personal life problems. She listens to students' suggestions and gives clear rubrics for every grading item. Participation and attendance matter, however. Be sure you contact her each time you are going to be late and be active in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: very hard! RUNNNNNN!
IDK why there are lots of good grade. The hard workflow doesn't mean learn a lot.
DO NOT HERITATE TO RUN
Such difficult class
She was not respectful for all students and her office hour is mandatory. She suspects others plagiarism and then give really low graders. not a good professor . very mean.

The only thing the prof did was show an extreme lack of respect for students, their time, and their agency. Unnecessarily difficult experience that did not improve my writing skills or my academic journey in any way. Did learn one thing: streer clear from this professor.
I made a big progress through her class.
Helpful but arrogant. AND SHE GIVES TONS OF HOMEWORK.

Subpar teaching, wildly unpleasant person and not someone you'd want to guide you in terms of writing. Speaks to her students with a degree of arrogance that is absolutely shameful and takes pride in putting others down. Many other classes in this university where you can improve your writing skills without dealing with this condescending behavior

Every writing class in NYU is hard so that's probably why most people here are leaving bad reviews, but honestly Prof. Dent really helped my writing!  If you put effort it and you genuinely want to improve your writing you will do good! I like her feedbacks and her grading criteria is clear, however I wish she gives feedback on the assignments.

reviews.comment:
AVOID her. 

- changes the wording of her prompt every class, and doesn't know how to divide time between 3 writing assignments. 
 - takes 2 months to give feedback for the first of three writing assignments. 
- gives horrible writing advice and nonsubstantive feedback for assignments. I don't think I've learned anything new about writing from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Dent is caring but a tough grader. The workload is pretty heavy, but you can learn a lot!!! She is reachable outside of the classroom. She always gives extensions and opportunities to revise your essay.

I learn little from this class. The class is boring and its purpose is unclear. It's better not to take her EXPOS-UA 4 class if you are a first year international student, because her tasks will be very difficult and take a lot of time although sometimes her tasks aren't so many.
Nothing to say. I learn nothing. Everything is hard to understood, the hw prompt or rubric.. Even the lecture itself. (Yeah, time wasting
R!U!N!! rude, impatient, unorganized classes, late feedback and arrogant. tough grader.

Professor Dent is a good person. She's very friendly. She extends deadline for her students. If you take her class, you will have a huge improvement in both your writing and reading skills. Listen carefully on her classes--its definitely not enough to just look at the feedback without listening to the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The professor is very nice and helpful! You can have 2 conference with her, one is one on one and the other is group review. She may also extend the deadline. For my course, she extended twice and each for 4-5 days which is pretty awesome and give extra time to revise my essay.

Only a few homework or assignments during the semester would be graded. She would clearly tell you what will be graded. She would give you a second chance to revise your paper after a graded assignment is returned although you typically wouldn't get an A for the first time unless you are really good at writing in English. She's a tough grader!

Prof Dent, though being friendly, can be extremely tough on grading. You should only write things she likes, or you get a C. Classes are boring with no value, she only asks you to read your essays awkwardly in front of all your classmates instead of analyzing the words she assigned. Tons of assignments. Don't take her class!

It's true that there is a lot of homework. To receive good grades, you need to work really really hard. She won't teach you much during lectures. However, the professor provides good feedback during additional conferences. You will learn a lot and make a big progress after a semester.

She assigned us too many exercises, forced us to submit them on time, and never graded them or given any feedbacks. It took her one moth to return the feedback of progression 1. I sacrificed so much time in this course for only B+. I was really disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Dent is a very friendly person, but her homework and grading are not so friendly (I need to spend more time on it than on the rest three classes in total!!!). But if you can bear that, it's a good idea to take her class.

heavy workload, we have writing homework for every class and she is very old school. You have to print the hw and bring it to class. No excuse for any absence. her grading is very personal, if she likes you then you are fine. and she could be mean sometimes. But I have to say her class is helpful for future writing and inspirational.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her class is extremely stressful. She never provides insights about the sources. Lots of writing assignments. She has clear political inclination and you will not get a good grade if you take a different political stance in your essay. Tough grader and ambiguous calculation in grading. She was caring though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Only give abstract and useless theories instead of providing you with practical writing strategies. Very stubborn and wanted your interpretation to satisfy her expectations. Does give you a lot of feedback but you are only going to receive then when everything is done.

First of all, I have to say that professor Dent's class is really tough. She has very high standards, but she is very INSPIRATIONAL and her criticism is really you become a better reader and more importantly, a better thinker. I finish every class with new takeaways. Take her if u wanna become a better writer. Avoid her if u just want easy A.
Tough grader. Would control heavily on your idea. Giving guideline after you finish your writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The professor is a mean woman and she will say oh you are maturing and making a lot of progress and still gives a B, which you got before. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!!

She is definately caring and inspirational, but if this is your first semester freshman year, and you're an international student, I would advice you to choose someone else. Her class was definately a challenging one, but won't lie, I learned bunch about writing.
Amy Hosig is definitely one of the best professors in WTE, take her class instead of this teacher
To get a good grade you have to show improvement in your papers over the course of the year. Learned a lot about how to write and the course itself was pretty fun.

Hard greader, grades are only in a range between D and B. Expect A LOT OF HOMEWORK from her class. She gives a lot of feed backs but sometimes it's hard to understand. If you know her style of writing I'm pretty sure you will get around a C in the class

Attendance is mandatory. She expects us to be on time and prepared for class. Absences will result in lower grade. Her classes are well-structure and helpful. She has very good insights to all the essays in the Brooklyn readers. She gives really good feedbacks and comments. Sometimes, her essay prompts are hard to understand but she explains well.

Acts like your best friend, and is very into getting engineering students to be more social - we did group work almost every day. Seemed a little high school-y in her methods at times, with the no electronics/calling you out when you used them, and her love of "active listening" and journal entries. She's great during conferences though.

She is very strict regarding class manners. Never be late to class, don't ditch classes, do your work on time, and don't fall asleep in class. If you get on her good side, expect a wonderful, fun class for the rest of the semester; But if you get on her bad side.. well, say good bye to your A, and you will have to endure her death glares every day.
Very good writing teacher. If you get a good grade with her you can be positive that you did a great job. Gives plenty of opportunities to revise and resubmit the graded essays.

She is very passionate about writing. Like some people said, she can be vague about certain instruction, but she tries her best to make her students understand a concept. If you put your time and effort into it, you will be able to grasp and take something valuable from the class experience.

She really makes you do the work when it comes to grasping ideas/drawing conclusions; looking back she really helped me prepare to think like a college student. I found the course itself pretty useless, but it was a good freshman experience. I've done better in humanities courses after having her, because I expect the worst.

She may be tough, but she has great overall intentions. She is also willing to take the time to meet with you one-on-one, which can prove very helpful. And the crescendo concept was a very good idea and makes a lot of sense.

Michelle is an intelligent teacher, and she understands writing really well. Problem communicating some of the concepts but possibly intentional vagueness. Didn't feel like she cared as much for my writing as she did for her teaching.
Challenging and edgy, dedicated to her students and their writing.  Tough, yes, but so what?  Intro to New York-level thinking.

If you are too stubborn to listen then yes, you will get a bad grade. but if you do listen to what she says about your writing, you will learn a lot and hopefully get a good grade. most people write crap the night before and dont wanna admit it. its not an easy class.
Get down with  your bad self and take this class....home fry...
she IS difficult and I'm glad. I spend a lot of money to go to NYU, and unlike most of my classmates, I would like to learn something for my $$$

I don't think Michelle's that bad of a prof. We're doing Writing the Essay right now and she has actually helped me a lot. Condescending at times tho. If you write well, you'll do well, if not, learn to write well because that's what college is all about.
Excellent Professor, she is very accessible and caring. She is extremely flexible and cares about her students. This was a great class. I loved it.

Dr. Hughes cares a lot about her work, and it's easy to get a good grade in her class because there's a lot of extra credit. However, her class is often disorganized and a lot of the homework is busywork that feels like it doesn't have a clear purpose.

I really liked her Community Psychology class and the way she teaches it. She clearly cares about the subject and her students, is super understanding of our time and is aware that we're dealing with so much more outside of class. She always has extra credit options for us to take and her grading system makes it easy to get a good grade. Highly rec
Learn much than book

The class often begins with rapid-fire questioning at 8 a.m., when many students are still waking up and adjusting. The chain of “why this?” and “why that?” questions can feel overwhelming. It often feels as though we are expected to guess the exact answer she has in mind. This makes participation feel stressful rather than constructive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment:
A fashion THEORY class and not what people usually picture when they imagine a fashion class. The class itself was sorta drag to get through but she's very intelligent. She cares deeply about her students but not many make an effort to reach out so not many people know that. 

Big exams were online, pop quizzes were annoying but manageable.

I loved what I learned, but compared to other discussion-based classes, classmates agreed she wasn't great at facilitating conversation, especially for ppl new to the vernacular of fashion and already nervous about voicing their opinion. She's probably a great fit for grad students, but not great for an undergrad elective. Never replied to emails..

This professor really opened my eyes on how I view the world in so many ways. Her inquiry seminar class on fashion was very interesting and she as a professor inspired me so much as a person. I pride her on being so honest and open with the class. Not many professors are like her. Definitely pick her if you want to grow.

Clearly very engaged in her topics but this might not necessarily translate well for an undergraduate class. She's not afraid to call you out for slacking off. This class is very rewarding if you actively participate and do the work--don't do the bare minimum if you want an enjoyable experience. Her lectures can get very off topic very quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Definitely not the easiest course, but she values effort and participation very much. Go to class, give your input, show that you are learning and at the end of the semester you will realize that everything was worth it! I grew so much through the course.

This class was incredibly engaging and offered fresh perspectives on the fashion world. It taught me to analyze and approach topics in ways I wouldn't have considered before. I now think more deeply about certain issues, and the course helped me develop a broader understanding of the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Yangzom initially intimidated me with her directness and no-nonsense approach, which made me uncomfortable at times. However, it's clear that she genuinely cares about her students and is committed to helping us succeed in life.

This course has been really enjoyable overall. While the readings can be time-consuming, I find the content to be engaging and well-structured. The class discussions are always interesting, and I look forward to them, often finding myself listening attentively because I genuinely enjoy the conversations we have.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Harsh Grader. Group work - no exams but get ready to read. Repetitive classes and got bored easily. Participation matters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Learned a lot in her media, communication, and culture course on fashion. Recommend her class. Class was always interesting and fun.

Great professor. She touches on many aspects of a topic in such fascinating ways. She's very easy to talk to and is sensitive when dealing with heated topics. As long as you do the reading, you are fine.

Seriously wish I'd taken this class sooner! Don't let the haters scare you off. This class is mind-bending, and the teacher's legit. If you're about learning, not a teacher liking you, then go for it! Your life will change for the better!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Yangzom motivates us to excel academically and personally. She's compassionate, witty, and committed to our success. Her class is a standout - engaging and enriching. If you're into fashion or great discussions, don't miss it!
Feel sorry for those who will take her class next semester. she will definitely kill your GPA and leave a disastrous impression by grading Fs and Ds for you projects. Good luck guys.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: I've never written a review before but for this teacher, I had to write one. whatever you do do NOT take this class. It was the biggest waste of time and credits ever...  I've never had a professor this bad before. Her directions make no sense, the readings are not interesting at all, and her attitude is the cherry on top. Take anything else.

She is a brilliant woman, but an awful professor. She is very unclear about what expects, grades things harshly with bad feedback, misses class, but gets mad and does not listen to any extenuating circumstances. She blames her RMP rating on her students not being able to "handle the harsh truth," but she needs to listen to her feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fashion and Power with Professor Yangzom was my least favorite class I took during my four years at NYU. The professor was dismissive, mean, and very unpredictable. At the end of the semester she asked us to leave high evaluations for her on RMP. The course caused me severe stress and was genuinely the worst experience during my time at NYU

Prof.Yangzom is incredibly unprofessional, after taking her course with almost no support from her, she asked our entire class to give her good reviews on RMP.  She does not offer support to her students, misses meetings and class A LOT, likes to humiliate her students and she has favorites. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.She should not be allowed to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Yangzom challenged and pushed me, and my other classmates, to be better students and people. She is compassionate, smart, funny, and will meet with you because she wants all her students to succeed. Easily one of my favorite courses I have ever taken. I recommend that anyone who is interested in fashion or just amazing discussions, take this class!

I was a bit nervous seeing the reviews for Professor Yangzom but I am so happy I ending up taking her class and judging for myself. I learned so much about the sociology in fashion, and the readings for this course were genuinely interesting. Professor Yangzom is passionate about teaching and her lectures were engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She can be really intimidating but I learned a lot. I recommend doing the reading thoroughly and working on the discussion posts intentionally. You won't get away with not doing the reading, so don't do this class if you don't want to read. She was very demanding but I think I grew a lot.

Professor Yangzom is a professor who believes in the significance of fashion education, and I really appreciate that. She changes her teaching style every semester. No quizzes/exams. Graded on reading responses and a final project, hard to get an idea of your grade. Doesn't always reply to emails. But you can certainly learn a lot from her lecture.

My favorite class this semester. The readings can be challenging but she is good at explaining complex ideas in a simple way. I enjoyed that she does not lecture much. Most of the class is discussion based. Will definitely take another class with Professor Yangzom!

She made a few classes online so students could work on finals She teaches her students to debate question and research. She is honest & vulnerable which made her approachable & relatable. Readings, in the beginning, are dense but the modules cover every aspect of fashion so there are some really fun sources. Little disorganized but overall nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Yangzom is intimidating at first but as you get to know her, you can see she really cares. The readings are sometimes dense but she makes sure to balance it with field trips, films and lots of discussion. This course has challenged me to critically understand the world. One of the best classes I have taken at NYU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Yangzom's teaching is not for everyone (esp. if you like 'easy' professors). She is very straightforward & never sugar coats. I respect her honesty & vulnerable moments she shared with us. She expects alot from her students & really challenges you. Sometimes a bit disorganized & sporadically answers emails. But I truly enjoyed this class.

I was hesitant enrolling in F&P due to previous negative ratings but glad I did. Reading assigned = average
Graded on 2 weekly discussion posts and final research paper
May come off stern @ first but makes class personal by connecting her experiences to readings
Challenged my thoughts making me view topics through a different lens
Fav class so far

Fashion and Power was my favorite class I've ever taken at NYU. Dicky is so intelligent, passionate, and a great professor. She really cares. If you are willing to put in the work, which I really suggest you do, you will take away so much from her. Changed the way I think about so many issues and topics. Would take again!

Only have good things to say about Professor Yangzom - she's intelligent which inspired me to do well in the course. I think her reviews are polarized because she challenges you. This motivated me to work, and I feel you have to work smart not hard in this course. Very doable. I felt accomplished by the end, and sad the course had to end.
She may be forward, but it's all in good fun. Cares deeply about really offering a true learning experience.

Professor Yangzom changed the way I perceive the world around me, something I cannot say of many professors. Do your readings. Sit in the front of the class. Professor Yangzom is undoubtedly entitled to having high expectations. She has a lot to offer.

Do not take this class. I was recommended by my advisor not to take it because of all the bad reviews she has received but I was interested in the course material so I decided to anyways. Huge mistake. She is not a good teacher, she is not a nice person. From the first day of class the energy in the classroom is incredibly hostile from her end.

This was by far the worst class and worst way to end my undergraduate career. The workload is far too much, she gives little to no feedback, expectations are not laid out clearly, and the professor is extremely inconsiderate even when you speak with her about particular situations. She has her favorites and it shows. I would NOT recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is interesting but shes very rude & doesn't flesh out lessons well... she talks for most of the class and then acts surprised when there is no time left. Never responds to emails, doesn't give clear instructions or rubrics but is a hard grader. Also gave us criticism on our presentations live in front of the rest of the class... stay far away
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Incredible teacher and even more incredible course. Her approach to teaching the subject matter was so insightful and helpful. Her background is phenomenal, and her support as a teacher has been so great in the remote learning environment! She really cares for her students and she is genuinely passionate about her work.

When I first started F&P I was definitely intimidated because there are a TON of readings and Prof. Yangzom has some scary reviews, but in the end I loved her class SO much!! She is such a caring professor and the class really pushes you to think in new ways, almost every session we went over because we wanted to continue talking! DEFF take this!!!

If you had asked me to review this class 3-4 weeks in, I'd tell you to run. But in the end, Prof. Y has taught me more than any other prof and she truly cares about her students. She's adapted the courseload and class material to fit the ongoing pandemic, she's understanding, and gives super helpful feedback. Lots of reading but SO SO worth it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I had Professor Yangzom for my Fashion, History, and Society class in the fall of 2019. I must say with her credentials of graduating from Yale University, I was a bit intimated. However, Yangzom is an inspiration. She doesn't just teach the class she challenge you to think actively and go more in depth of the different topics. Great person!

I read the reviews before taking her class and was honestly preparing for a hard class. However as I learned this past semester, Prof. Yangzom may not teach the easiest class but she taught probably the most thought-provoking I have ever taken. Prof Yangzom is incredibly passionate and that definitely shows in her teaching and is 100% underrated.

Professor Yangzom is amazing. The reviews on this site are written by those who do not take criticism well. Professor Yangzom is incredibly knowledgable and genuinely wants her students to succeed. She gives several opportunities for extra credit (possible +5 pts on your final grade each), and gives excellent feedback. BEST professor I've had.

Prof. Yangzom is unapproachable, standoffish, and oftentimes just rude to students who just want feedback on assignments or elaboration on class topics. She is a sociologist, so the class is like a sociology course rather than a media comm / fashion class. Not at all what I was looking for. Assigned dozens of textbooks we had to purchase or rent.

I wish someone had written this because I was honestly terrified of going into the class. The reviews and attacks of her character are all completely false. This class is challenging/thought-provoking. She truly wants her students to see fashion in a different light. I highly recommend if your sense of character isn't based on a teacher liking you.

She is truly just rude. There is no other way to put it. She spent 30 minutes of our class telling us how stupid we are and how bad our papers were but the only actual advice she gave us to do better was that we should google how to do a proper citation. Instead of teaching you stuff she just calls you stupid for not already knowing it
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is the most absurd course I have ever taken in my life. Not only does this "Professor" expect nothing less than perfection, but when you ask for help or show that you need it she uses the time to passive aggressively criticize your lack of understanding of her DENSE DATED WORDY TEXTS. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. SAVE YOURSELF.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't know what's her grading criteria, didn't get our first grade back until the week before final, gives you extra credit opportunity but obviously would forget to count that into the final grade, has absolutely no filter and will troll you in class. Prof. Yangzom knows her stuff, but she's just way too far above the undergrad level.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: F&P is a sociology course that barely talks about fashion. sadly prof. yangzom doesn't focus most subjects surrounding contemporary fashion or related issues around the world we're living in now until the last 2 lectures when she'll about sustainability whatsoever. what is "the system"??? Agreeing to the point that she is extremely unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: LOTS of reading--she'll want you to read 300 page books for homework. The texts she assigns us have the potential to be interesting, but they are very dense texts and she does little in class to help us understand them. She's also extremely standoffish. Don't enroll in this class if you think you can get by by doing the bare minimum.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes, but not hard to do well

Professor Landa is a knowledgeable professor, though he might go off track a bit when he's lecturing. He assigned us weekly closed-book essays, which might sound scary but are actually a fantastic way to learn the material. The TAs are super nice and grade the tests and essays clearly and leniently. However, the required book costs 80 dollars!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dimitri was an okay professor. The class itself isn't difficult; rather his lecture style and his ramblings make some topics more confusing. The reading itself was a lot, but I found it enjoyable. I found that my TA just did not give clear feedback on assignments, which made it hard to improve. Dimitri is fine, but I would avoid to be honest.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I have to say some of the really negative reviews of Landa simply aren't true. He's a pretty awkward guy but you can tell he really cares about the subject. Has a tendency to ramble and go on tangents; the lectures aren't NECESSARY but they were still worth going to (I went to every lecture). Your TA makes or breaks the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Landa made the lectures easy to comprehend and tied them to our homework readings, which helped me understand the material better. I had to make a last minute request for an accomodation for the final exam and Professor Landa helped me find a solution which was greatly appreciated. Great Professor!

A lot of people have complained about this professor, but I seriously loved his class. You aren't allowed to use technology, so it forces you to use notebooks, which is honestly helpful. The class is super interesting, and he's very passionate, funny, and caring. He definitely has a "European teaching style," which I appreciate and would recommend.

Dimitri Landa is genuinely one of most EMBARASSING Professors in existence. 
I don't care how many fancy words he uses, he simply does not know how to get to the POINT. 
Additionally, he seems to enjoy punishing students that perform well on assessments, because he curved us down. 
Do not take this guy, he's PATHETIC!

Here's what you really need to know: you dont need to go to class. U also dont need to read anything. Attendance isn't taken, there's weekly "quizzes" but honestly it takes 2 seconds of online "research" to figure out exactly what ur supposed to write about. Unless u have a really awful recitation teacher, this is probably the best politics class.

I don't get the hate on Professor Landa, the class is very lecture heavy and a lot of readings, but he tries his best to make it fun. Honestly, it's better to not do most of the readings as everything is covered in lecture anyway. No tech policy and weekly quizzes in recitation, but if you have a nice TA they are very easy.

Terribly boring. Prepare to fall asleep in lecture. The no tech policy is annoying. There are weekly quizzes during recitation- not too hard. Rob was my TA and he was truly the only good part about this class. Class material itself is not difficult.
Easy class, tons of reading, but you can just use ChatGPT most before your weekly quizzes. The lectures are beyond boring, though, so fair note. (Attendance not mandatory, take this class.)

RUN. 
Professor Landa does NOT post slides, and you have to take notes ON PAPER. You also have to complete WEEKLY QUIZZES, and Midterm was down-graded. He tried to make the class funny and sometimes it is, but it is still a hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course itself wasn't too difficult but I did not enjoy the professor, he was condescending and made lectures pretty boring. Attendance technically not mandatory but if you don't have a friend in the class to send you notes, you have to go because he doesn't post the slides. Also no tech policy, so handwritten notes.

Very smart, sometimes goes off on tangents, but that can give you time to process and think about the material. Also, every once in a while, one of his tangents was exactly what I needed to make sense of everything, or provided me with a thought-provoking example to sit with for the next few days. Not a life-changing teacher, but very good.

I went to him once with a question and he accused me of trying to get ahead in the class and I was like umm yeah I want to do well. He doesn't know how to connect with people and engage with the students. he is also just so boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a hard class. Prof's no tech policy sucks. Don't bother doing all the readings, just go to lecture and look up main ideas. Weekly quizzes in recitation (easy quote interpretation but don't forget your book). 2 term papers graded easily. Midterm and Final are not too bad as long as you study. Not the worst intro class and not too hard.

Lectures were essentially just summaries/explanations of whatever reading we had to have completed, though sometimes Professor Landa explained things in a way that just made topics more confusing. The readings are all very well known writings on political philosophy, so it's easy to find resources online to help with understanding. TAs do grading.

Professor Landa fosters genuine love for Political Theory. Attendance isn't mandatory but highly recommended if you value eccentricity and different approaches to interpreting text. Only two essays, and questions are thought provoking and interesting. Enough time spent understanding and discussing each text, and recitations were especially helpful.

unnecessarily tough grading (you can miss a minor point in your essay and receive like a third of the credit off) no slides posted, no computers allowed, and no taking pictures of slides either. papers were due throughout the semester and graded after classes were over.
terrible. no lecture slides given no grading criteria no nothing

Many readings are assigned so keep an eye out for that. He doesn't send the lecture slides out either so you kind of have to take notes, and devices are not allowed in class, too. He takes too long to answer students questions during the lecture, taking away from the actual class. If you need help, you have better luck turning to the TAs.
Very hard class

The biggest complaint I have about him is how condescending he can be. I went to office hours to clarify my understanding (the text is very dense) and he was incredibly rude throughout the session. Rather than actually explaining the content, he spent the entire time belittling me.

I did not enjoy this professor. He does not take attendance, but he doesn't post the lecture slides online or record the lectures so you have to be there. There is a lot of reading and note taking that you have to do in order to understand what is going on in class. He doesn't help his students and relies on his TA's instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The material itself isn't the challenge, it is Professor Landa himself who ruins courses. As noted by another reviewer, this man is indeed, very bad at his job. He also engages in biased and capricious grading when he believes he can get away with it. His class was simply a disgusting experience in every way.

His lectures were clear, informative, and quite dense, but attending and taking good notes is all you need to get an A. Weekly recitation quizzes on readings, but they were super easy + if I didn't have the time to do the actual reading I'd skim through a Sparknotes summary/my lecture notes, and would always get a perfect score. Easy & interesting!

Avoid this class with Landa. He was didn't communicate well. He would take days to answer his emails, and if you approached him after class he would respond "Just email me". His tests were extremely difficult and vague. He would not grade anything, and his TA's were not on the same page, so the grading was super confusing to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: IDK if I was doing something wrong but I was told this class was easy but it wasn't for me. The professor talks about how if you do the readings you will do great and how all the people that did bad never showed up but I came to every class and actually read the book (which is something I never do) and I got a 74 on the midterm. also no tech policy
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Landa is the funniest, most genuine political theory professor. He makes lectures fun by including real-life examples and many jokes. There are weekly quizzes that ensure you read, but he does a great job of covering the key arguments in his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's very boring and not the most lenient guy. He is very unaccommodating even in a literal pandemic. He doesn't record his lectures, doesn't provide lecture notes, but expects you to retain all the information he blabs out. He has a good heart but his teaching style is not it. Be aware of a lot of reading and weekly quizzes. Easy tests though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So here's the catch, take him after you've taken reading heavy and writing heavy courses. I loved his class because I knew how to balance reading and writing. A lot of people who come into his class don't and feel bad as a result. If you listen to his lectures and then do the readings you'll do fine! But he isn't an easy A.

He's really bad at his job. Class isn't too hard, I never bought the textbook or did any of the readings because I had already read some of them in prior classes. He does manage to make some of the most interesting and important foundational texts in human history seem boring and mediocre. try and do the readings and it shouldn't be too difficult.

The lectures are very boring. Professor Landa does not post the slides online yet both midterms and a final exam are comprised of 60% of specific terms you need to define. Recitations are too very boring and there are reading quizzes you need to take almost every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Landa is a very mediocre professor. His class is introductory in nature. The class is not very difficult. There are recitations that take attendance and have quizzes.

One of the worst classes that I have ever taken. The readings are preposterous and the content is not taught well. They do not take attendance for the lectures but they do at the recitations, even though the recitations do not really help with understanding the topics and the class. Hands-down one of the worst classes that I have taken. 1/10
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Terrible. Would not take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's so boring and he assigns papers on a Friday and makes them due on a Monday. He must assume that NYU students spend their weekends twiddling their fingers, while the reality is that many students need weekends to work jobs to afford living at NYU, and preventing us from working on the papers on weekdays while working isn't fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The lectures are extremely boring and you are not allowed to have any electronic devices out. The class is too abstract and subjective and he talks intellectually which is annoying. I dread the class because it is so boring. You got quizzes (graded subjectively), papers and exams, a lot of work and its not interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A little dry in lectures occasionally, but overall a very interesting class. Can definitely get by without doing the readings if you go to the lectures. Pretty easy class and a nice professor, funny guy and approachable. Recitations must be attended and they give pop quizzes! (just explaining a quote from reading)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Landa was a good professor and brought a lot of humour to a subject that is typically taught in a dry way. His lectures covered all the highlights of the readings, but they did go quite quickly. A lot depends on your recitation TA to go in depth into the arguments. Can sometimes be hard to follow in lecture without further clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: My favorite class. Professor Landa presents the arguments and concepts in a very clear and understandable way. If you are into politics, this class will be both interesting and easy. I did all of the (heavy) readings, but I had friends who did not and still got an A-, being that his lectures cover all the important points from the readings.

A rather dry course and lecture. There are quite a bit of reading to do for this course but you don't have to read everything to get by. Lecture is not mandatory but is highly encouraged that you do since a lot his tests are based on what he says in lecture. Also his lecture helps you understand the reading better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: His intro to pol theory class can be boring, and he assigns a ton of reading. However, as long as you know the basic arguments of all the political theorists, you dont even have to do the readings. I didnt do any of the readings and got an A-. He is intelligent but can be hard to follow and confusing at times. HIs exams were easy, from the notes
Out of the 28 or so lectures we had, I slept through at least half.

This is an essential intro to politics class. There's a ton of reading, and a couple of harshly-graded papers, but the things you learn are the basis of government in general. I found it fascinating, but be prepared to do a lot of reading if you want to be of any real use in recitation.

The professor takes very interesting material and makes it unpalatable. Lectures are boring. Recitation sections are even worse. You are better off just reading the books on your own. You will get more out of them and won't have to constantly worry about having to take one of Landa's infamous "pop-quizzes".

I am currently sitting in this class, bored out of my mind and frustrated. I entered NYU wanting to be a political science major, but because of this class, I am changing my major. There are a lot of boring readings, there are impossible pop-quizzes, and the lectures would put anyone to sleep. Save your soul and do not take this class.
Extremely boring, barely discusses political theory in modern context. Extremely slow - will ensure that you lose interest in the class by the second week. Do not recommend you take him.
He's not wonderful, but he's not horrible. The lectures are pretty clear and he's got a sense of humor. The tests aren't bad if you study the readings and notes.
Everything is from a powerpoint, but is coherent.  If you go to recitation then you should be fine.  Open textbook midterm and final and 2 short essays.  Overall I would recommend him

Great teacher, is knowledgeable on the subject and speaks clearly. He makes plenty of great jokes and keeps every class interesting. Also provides plenty of room for discussion. Overall, recommended professor

material was somewhat interesting.  however - beware, the TAs will try to avoid having to meet with you during office hours to help you.  they also grade extremely harshly.  by no means an easy class to get an A in

He is decent and articulates lectures very well. He puts everything on slides and the tests are pulled directly from those. The midterm was riducculously easy and the two response papers were okay. The TA's grade harshly so be prepared. The final however, was a hot mess and CAME OUT OF NO WHERE! The terms were random and I almost crapped myself.

Probably the easiest of the Politics cores. MUST go to class; tests are directly from lecture notes and are easy if you go to class and take good notes (reading not necessary to get good grade). Mike Kates was the best TA ive ever had, made everything crystal clear. lectures do get boring but all lectures do. take notes and youll be fine.

At least it hit the expectations of going through the big political theorists. However, Landa has horrible lectures and completely focuses on the wrong things. He ignores the important stuff and focuses on little things that don't matter, so you need the notes. No reading is necessary since summaries are enough. Poor political theory class.

lectures in the beginning are pretty interesting, but eventually they get extremely boring, recitations are engaging though. The readings are very dense but you dont have to read all of it.Take excellent notes and you should be able to easily get a good grade; its pretty hard to get an A though bc all the T.As are prety tough graders...

The content of the class was boring sometimes, as was Landa, but he definitely knows his stuff and is pretty chill as far as professors go.  Definitely attend lectures and take notes if you want to do well on the tests because the readings are hella long and pretty challenging.
This professor lectured about Jackie's pen  every single time. He was awful. Do yourself a favor: do not take his Political Theory course!
This is a great introductory course. Professor Landa is interesting, and very thought provoking. The tests come right from lecture notes, and you will learn alot.

Professor Landa is a great teacher. He truly cares about his work, and does a very good job summarizing the readings. Grading is a bit tough, so getting an A is pretty much out of the question, but if you dont mind getting an A-/B+, and actually learning something, take this class. TAs were very knowledgeable and helpful as well.

I like Landa a lot. I heard some people complain that his lectures were unclear, but I thought they were really thought-provoking. The workload can be a lot. Seems like you'd have to work really hard to get a straight A. But if you're happy with A-/B+/B and a really good professor who really knows his stuff, I reccommend him. Mike was a great TA.

Not a very difficult class, but an engaging one at that.  A lot of reading, but you don't have to do it because the exams are from lecture notes.  The second half of the semester is much more difficult than the first.  He starts to move quicker and lectures become confusing and tedious. But he provides a solid/extenive background of Pol. Theory.

A lot of reading, but going to rec and class helps.  Gives 2 essays, midterm and final.  all graded by TA.  Mid and Final are MUCH easier than essays. Essays are difficult but manageable. not a bad class!

No suprises here,  a very straightforward survery course. Lectures can be tedious sometimes because he lets student questions dominate, but he's witty and spoon feeds you everything (which gets annoying, but makes for easy exams). Exams are IDS and an essay: the bulk of the IDS are straight from lecture notes.
humorous, patient about answering questions, you learn a lot and you actually end up liking it - didn't hear a lot (if any) complaints about him or the class from other students
I wasn't extremely interested in the material, but DL made it fun. The class is hard in that there are a lot of dense readings, but the tests are pretty easy if you go to class and take notes.

He's a pretty decent professor. Cracks some pretty funny jokes from time to time. Go to class definitely most of his test is on his class lectures. Readings are a bit much if you have a lot on your plate like I did this semester but otherwise I would definitely recommend this class.
RUNNNNNNNNNNNNNNN

I think Professor Dietschi is a good professor in terms of her feedback and knowledge. My biggest issue in this class, though, is the lack of transparency and clear guidance in the grading rubrics. Communications is a very subjective course in and of itself, and the grading in this class heavily reflected that.

Avoid taking her class if possible. While she may seem nice initially, her grading is exceptionally harsh and lacks transparency. She provides no details on participation grades (which heavily impact your final score), and leaves you completely in the dark about your progress. If your goal is an A, choose a different professor.

Very chill professor. Her grading criteria isn't super clear sometimes and she takes points off for random stuff on presentations. However, she is willing to help outside of class and values participation. The class is graded by 2 individual writing assignments and 3 group projects. Overall, a solid choice for Org Comm.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not take this class if you care about your grade because everyone is getting a b for their presentation and the rest of the grade is up to participation and whatnot, which she does not explain well

Professor Dietschi is very kind and cares about her students. My only issue is that the grading feels abstract, and it's hard to know where you stand throughout the semester. Even with extra credit, it's tough to tell how much it helps. Great professor, but the grading could be better. I really tried my best :(
she is a literal robot. does not care about her students. avoid at all costs
Super tough grader. Save yourself the stress and take someone else!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: her grading is so random you will never know how you are doing in the class but at least you can just chatgpt everything and do just as well as everyone else. group projects are so useless and if your teammate doesn't do anything, tough luck bc she doesn't care and everyone in the team will get the same grade. her lectures make me regret waking up.

He is such a hard grader and legit will say one thing pulled your grade down and bump you down a whole letter grade. Super harsh and even if you go to office hours and talk to him about things he wont give you a good grade. Mid term and final are so hard you have to like idenitfy quotes he selected out of past reading and explain. DO NOT PICK
Prof Diamond was very nice, though I did find it hard to engage in his class at times. He's also a bit of a strict grader, but his lectures were planned out well. I would go to his office hours!
patient person, very kind

Very nice guy, sweet older man, but definitely more of a traditional style of teaching. Extensive readings, although this whole course is heavy on it. My main complaint is that his grading scheme is very confusing, and apparently he starts all students' participation grades out at a B, but doesn't tell you that unless you ask
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Content in Diamonds classes is the content discussed the most later that day. Thought provoking! Superb classes
Extremely boring and a harsh grader!

He was the worst for Global Works. He absolutely killed my interest in the field of philosophy. He's an EXTREMELY harsh grader and has no good things to say about you. His class was not enjoyable what so ever, as it was the same boring format every day. He makes you feel like an idiot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Best professor i've ever had

Professor Diamond is a great guy. He does assign a lot of reading and a lot of essays. But most of his readings can be understood from his lectures, so his essays are manageable. The most important thing is to participate in any way possible.

4 essays, 4 assignments, plus readings and participation grade. Professor diamond grades quickly and gives helpful feedback. He is extremely knowledgeable and connects ancient texts to modern life. If you are interested in philosophy and/or political science take him. This class is what you put into it, and you can come out of it with a lot learned
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Diamond is extremely knowledgeable. His lectures are guided by organized, informative slideshows. Participation opportunities are key, but usually limited. He does, however, assign a LOT of homework, both reading and writing. He is very quiet and monotone, making it hard to understand him (and to stay awake for the duration of class).

Class is relatively easy if you do the readings but be prepared to do a lot of writing. You can tell he is passionate about what he teaches but his lectures drag and you will fall asleep. He does give a lot of feedback but he can be very unclear.

Professor Diamond is a really great teacher and the material he teachers is super interesting. The feedback he gives on papers is very insightful and he is always open to new ideas during and after class. Would definitely recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Excellent professor and kind person. 3 papers, a midterm, and a finalfor the papers, really go deep. He likes to critically analyze what you say/write, so be ready to defend your views (in a good way). Not too harsh a grader, but he can def tell if you're trying. Participate and you're golden. If you have trouble, go to office hours for sure.

I love prof diamond, so caring and kind. Very organized syllabus and a decent amount of homework. The reading may get a little bit heavy if you're a freshman, but I managed to get through. Three 5 pages essays based on what you learned and read; easy if you read and listen to the lecture.

It's evidenteven in a remote classthat Professor Diamond is incredibly knowledgeable and cares about what he's teaching. I love how his class is set up on NYU classes and he gives very clear instructions for assignments. There's a decent amount of reading, but it's not bad if you manage your time well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Prof. Diamond is a very nice Professor. He is knowledgeable and always tries to connect the texts with the modern world. Class discussions are fun and insightful. Very caring and understanding. 5 papers per semester, he always gives detailed feedback on your work. Fast and fair grader

Good guy, super intelligent but sometimes hard to follow due to monotone. He's awesome but it is a LOT OF WORK that's expected, and he definitely knows who has and hasn't done the readings. No final exam though, but very few grades to bring it up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is great. Facilitates students to higher levels of discussion and drives you to participate for a good effort grade. Know your stuff.

This class is more work than it should be. More than anything Diamond just wants people to talk. I definitely didn't read/understand anything but he kept giving me B+s. His lectures are super boring and he assigns A LOT of papers (5 total). Just talk and sparknotes the books.

Not recommended. Classes are extremely boring and its easy to lose focus. He just goes on and on about whatever the subject is for the day, writes nothing on the board, and just finds random excerpts from the book. You must read the rather long readings and raise your hand all the time to like the class in any way. 4 papers, not the easiest grader

He's very boring. The papers are incredibly easy, though the guidelines for his "Athenian Assembly Game" are very vague and it's hard to get a good grade. You might as well not try for a participation grade because everyone gets a B.

Diamond is a kind man who is passionate about teaching, but his style is dry and yawn-worthy. His assignments are straightforward, but he grades with bias because he knows so much that any opinion that strays is wrong in his mind. Don't try to sound like you know what you're talking about, even if you do, because he will always protest question.

I agree with most people on here- PDids is a sweetheart.  He is very kind and understanding about absences and very patient in general.  I suppose his class is a bit drab if youre not interested in the subject, but if you try to participate and do the reading its really interesting and goes by quick.  I would highly reccommend his class to anyone!

Participate from the first day of class and participate every day. Go to his office hours about papers. Using wikipedia was more useful than reading the books. Class can get a bit boring but overall great course. He is passionate about what he teaches.
Took two classes with him, great guy.  Extremely interesting and tells you from day one what to expect.  Participate, write a few papers, and enjoy!

Just signed up for his Social Foundations for the 3rd semester. Great professor and most intelligent man! He is full of great ideas - i have learned so much in his class. He relates everything to current day events. His voice is really soothing so sometimes you feel the need to fall asleep but just wake up and enjoy his insight! 100% recommend!

Pretty chill professor- not extremely interesting nor boring. Still, there are the boring days. Fair grader. The game was interesting and competitive- good way to boost up grades... I advise him only because if you want to be safe and not venture out to try new teachers, Diamond is good.

AWESOME TEACHER!!!!! not super hard but not super easy.....we play this game where we are all members of the national assembly during the french revolution and it i sooooo amazing....def take this class

He's a really nice guy, really interactive but you have to love participating if you want to enjoy the class. He is a pretty fair grader and expects you to do the reading. But he is really a smart man and he made Plato understandable. Take him!

He is an awesome teacher. We played this awesome game which has you become an Athenian in the Assembly of Athen. It was really cool. He is also really interesting and you don't need to do too much beyond listening in class to maintain a B
He's a pretty fair grader. There are 2 required papers and 2 during a pointless game he makes us play. Besides the game, just plain, boring lecture. You get a B if you don't want to participate.
Professor Diamond is pretty boring but if you truly listen to what he has to say it's really very interesting.  He's really brilliant and helpful, so just take a lot of notes and read the material.

Diamond is SO SMART. He really knows what he is teaching and is he enthusiastic about the material. While not always the most engaging, he loves to hear students' views and opinion. Take his nation building class if you have any opinion on the US' war in Iraq whatsoever!

So boring...follows the same structure every day, class is open discussion but extremely dull if you aren't passionate about Nation Building.  Don't take this class without lots of background knowledge about global politics or you will be out of the loop.  Voice is like Tim Gunn--it will put you to sleep.
This man is very nice, but so dull. It's a pretty easy B if you don't really try. Nice guy, monotonous voice.

So boring.  You never have to participate if you don't want to, and you'll still get a B in participation.  Go to class, take some notes.  Midterms and Finals are kind of impossible to study for but also not that difficult.  Really helpful when it comes to papers.  Email it to him and he'll edit.  Boring boring boring but an easy class.

This guy is smart. By taking his class, I just felt a lot smarter sitting in that chair and listening to him. Only important caution is that his voice can occasionally put you to bed. But other than that, the class was insightful.
No Comments
Great class, he's smart and helpful, and very interactive, but doesn't pick on you if you don't wanna talk.  Very clear on what he wants, but still flexible.
Good professor and excellent lectures. Always made sure to explain things well and ensure student understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is hard as it tackles a lot of content and new concepts, but the professor makes an effort to be accessible out of class and explain as good as he can. THe class is hard in concept and exercises canbe tricky, but he really does his best to help.

The course requires a heavy amount of content, so it can sometimes feel rushed, but he is accessible outside of class.
He cares about his students and their understanding. He managed to move my final exam date and was okay when I declined. TLDR, he is a good professor teaching a hard class.

Unless you are really smart or want to spend tons of time on this course, run :(
The first half was easy but second half is really confusing and requires lots of time to understand.
Run!!!!
Get ready to learn by yourself
Bad professor. After midterm2, 10%-20% student withdraw from his class
Enjoy taking this course with professor Erik. He is very nice and accessible. He would be patient and provides you a lot of examples if you don't understand the concept

I took him in the summer during covid for MFE and basically never came to class, watching the recorded lecture when I am confused on homework. He did not in fact make my GPA Dies, but I can't say whether that will happen to you in the present day.

I heard from my friend that he was very strict in grading and that he was terrible at teaching last semester(fall 2023) so I came to this class without high expectation. I have to say that Professor Dies has changed a lot! The exam was not hard and he assigned sample exam in which some of the questions appeared on the final!

This professor was assigned to this course at the very last minute before the start of this semester. So it seems like he does not know what he is teaching. You need to depend on reading the textbook and self-studying in order to pass the exam because his lectures are basically picking some random contents from the book and read it for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very considerate, generous and caring guy. He's very knowledgeable about the content. Though the course is extremely difficult and abstract as a stats class, and the exams are very tough, he gives very very generous curve!!! Just go to class, read the book, do your homework. You are certainly going to make an A in this class.
Dies is a brilliant professor. Math is hard and Prof Dies explains the concepts and also stimulates invigorating conversations and Rick illustrative examples. Great prof if you are good at math.

Good professor overall but I find it so hard to keep track on courses, everything is perfect except he's extremely monotoned and lectures are rlly boring, its hard to focus on material 100% of the time, and no sample exam at all. Slow grading. but remember everything else is good, I just wanna talk bout what I'm struggling with.

Summer 2021. Pretty standard as a math professor, textbook material is converted and summarized into readily understandable handwritten pdf notes, and the exam is not difficult at all, given very sufficient time. There's a lot of homework tho.

Spr 2020. Very robotic and basically reads the textbook word by word. That being said, he is helpful and friendly if you ask in or outside of class for him to explain a concept. Quiz every class, forces you to stay on track. Exams were moderate-easy for someone with good maths skills. Occasionally cracks a joke, pretty funny guy.
He is somewhat robotic but is very knowledgable on the material.

He has a talent for being able to explain and teach concepts well, not everyone can do that. I don't how how true it is but I get the feeling that he actually cares about students succeeding, not just doing his job teaching and moving on with his life.

Dies is a very solid teacher. He's difficult, but it seems appropriate given the class. Very good lecturer who can explain confusing topics with precision and care. Caring. The daily quizzes are good to keep you on track and can boost your grade. Show up to class, read the book if you don't (it's a good book), and you're in good shape. Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the best professor ever. Work hard and you will get an A. If you are struggling he will do his best to give you a respectable grade. He genuinely wants to see everyone move on to the next course. He is the best person I ever met
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Go to class, but his lectures aren't great if you aren't the best at calc or visualizing math. He mostly just goes through examples from the book. I needed a lot of extra help understanding concepts. I struggled in his class but he is very kind. not an L if you get him but there are probably better options.

He's a good lecturer, clear and concise and willing to help with problems. He tries his best to make you understand why things work the way they do. Exam was easier than the midterm, and he curves everyone below a certain grade. Solid teacher, would take again for future math classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pretty fair tests although I've heard he's harder than other professors for Discrete. Was rough for an 8am but make the effort to go to classes and he'll reward you (gave a random pop quiz that was to write your favorite number down). Would take again! Very clear and great clear voice
Good lecture, but he makes the homework harder than other instructor, as far as I know other two sections doesn't have that much homework, nor hard exam.
took it over the summer and he had no office hours. Unclear grading criteria but nbd. Would take again if he has office hours.
Very interesting and clear teacher.  Helped me break down my assignments into simple logical progressions.  Respects his students.
He is a great teacher. His lectures are very clear cut and really knows his material and how to explain it. . Always there to help. Tests are pretty standard  GREAT TEACHER! I RECOMMEND
I took it over the summer and he had no office hours.
Uses real examples in homework. Requires programming not in course description (in syllabus, though).
Fair, not great. Teach from the book, but give inspiring homework. Good voice.
His lectures are very helpful. He is a very great professor. He helped me towards an a in the class.
Dies is an overall great professor. He has a great sense of humor.
Helpful.

Erik is hands down the best lecturer you can possibly have for a Math class. He begins each class with an organized, concise review of the previous class. He is very approachable if you're missing a concept and he gives very strong hints as to what he'll put on the exam. He makes hard Math subjects bearable.

Erik is a fantastic communicator who likes to do mini review sessions of prior material at the start of each class. This is helpful come exam time as well as for quiz preparation. His midterm was very easy as was his final exam. Do all the HWs and ace one of the two exams and you'll receive an A.

Great lecturer, took him for Calculus 2.  He really made the topics we covered clear.  Always open to questions from students and speaks CLEAR English (Which is definitely important for a math class)  Take him if you can

Overall, I wouldn't say the class was particularly difficult in terms of content. While kind and approachable, is a meticulous grader who focuses on specific aspects of the work. The midterm, mostly from the slides and a few questions from books, proved manageable. The final project can be confusing, ask questions in person rather than  emails.

She was nice in class. However, the instructions she gave about assignments are not clear enough. There were a lot of papers during the semester, and she did not provide rubrics for some assignments. She was a tough grader, and it is almost impossible for someone to get an A. Choose someone else if you want to receive an A for this course.

Worst professor Ive ever had. She manages to make an otherwise interesting and important subject nauseatingly boring. She reads off of slides for almost 3 hours and gives zero indication as to what well have to actually know. Please avoid this professor and her class at all costs. NYU, please make her stick to her day job.

You will not learn anything.

reviews.comment: Goes through lecture way too fast, only meet once per week and she goes through like 80-100 slides at a time. reviews.comment: Doesn't reply to emails, not so good with tech as the others have said, quizzes have no study guides, tough quizzes for no reason.

sometimes funny but will call out tech use and "bad" answers to questions. lectures are boring and tangential; if content is interesting, manages to make it uninteresting. most annoyingly: she doesn't provide checklist for artworks to memorize so you're taking each test blind, hoping you studied the right material. heavy but cool readings

Most boring and undecipherable lectures in the world. I genuinely felt myself slip into REM sleep in that lecture hall. SO to HL for being the best TA, she ever should've been teaching this godforsaken class.

reviews.comment: Her lectures are useless. Quizzes are based off of naming artworks and the heavy readings assigned before every class. Grading is tough and there isn't enough time on the quizzes to do the 2 full essays and 4 short essays. Overall this is not a good class at all, I don't recommend but it's unfortunately a required course for Art History majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Heavy readings; need to remember all of them, including the names of each artwork and its artists, to prepare for quizzes. Limited office hour slots, only four 15-minute office hour slots every week. No review session before the quiz. Strong accent.

This class harvested my soul. I was literally sitting in class today and thinking "GET ME OUT OF HERE". Her lectures are so incredibly boring and hard to follow, I swear half the time I have no idea what she is yapping on about. Just straight ahh. The only thing that is keeping me going is my goated TA. Shout out H.L.
just don't.
this class turned me to a history major I hate art history
